146::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.4.0
147::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 2.1.0
148::CODE;;If the parameter ``widget`` is None, all animated widgets will be
149::CODE;;the target and cancelled. If ``largs`` is also given, animation of
150::CODE;;these properties will be canceled for all animated widgets.
151::CODE;;'''
152::CODE;;if widget is None:
153::CODE;;if largs:
154::CODE;;for animation in Animation._instances.copy():
155::CODE;;for info in tuple(animation._widgets.values()):
156::CODE;;widget = info['widget']
157::CODE;;for x in largs:
158::CODE;;animation.cancel_property(widget, x)
159::CODE;;else:
160::CODE;;for animation in Animation._instances:
161::CODE;;animation._widgets.clear()
162::CODE;;animation._clock_uninstall()
163::CODE;;Animation._instances.clear()
164::CODE;;return
165::CODE;;if len(largs):
166::CODE;;for animation in list(Animation._instances):
167::CODE;;for x in largs:
168::CODE;;animation.cancel_property(widget, x)
169::CODE;;else:
170::CODE;;for animation in set(Animation._instances):
171::CODE;;animation.cancel(widget)
172::CODE;;def start(self, widget):
173::CODE;;'''Start the animation on a widget.
174::CODE;;'''
175::CODE;;self.stop(widget)
176::CODE;;self._initialize(widget)
177::CODE;;self._register()
178::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_start', widget)
179::CODE;;def stop(self, widget):
180::CODE;;'''Stop the animation previously applied to a widget, triggering the
181::CODE;;`on_complete` event.'''
182::CODE;;props = self._widgets.pop(widget.uid, None)
183::CODE;;if props:
184::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_complete', widget)
185::CODE;;self.cancel(widget)
186::CODE;;def cancel(self, widget):
187::CODE;;'''Cancel the animation previously applied to a widget. Same
188::CODE;;effect as :attr:`stop`, except the `on_complete` event will
189::CODE;;*not* be triggered!
190::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.4.0
191::CODE;;'''
192::CODE;;self._widgets.pop(widget.uid, None)
193::CODE;;self._clock_uninstall()
194::CODE;;if not self._widgets:
195::CODE;;self._unregister()
196::CODE;;def stop_property(self, widget, prop):
197::CODE;;'''Even if an animation is running, remove a property. It will not be
198::CODE;;animated further. If it was the only/last property being animated,
199::CODE;;the animation will be stopped (see :attr:`stop`).
200::CODE;;'''
201::CODE;;props = self._widgets.get(widget.uid, None)
202::CODE;;if not props:
203::CODE;;return
204::CODE;;props['properties'].pop(prop, None)
206::CODE;;if not props['properties']:
207::CODE;;self.stop(widget)
208::CODE;;def cancel_property(self, widget, prop):
209::CODE;;'''Even if an animation is running, remove a property. It will not be
210::CODE;;animated further. If it was the only/last property being animated,
211::CODE;;the animation will be canceled (see :attr:`cancel`)
212::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.4.0
213::CODE;;'''
214::CODE;;props = self._widgets.get(widget.uid, None)
215::CODE;;if not props:
216::CODE;;return
217::CODE;;props['properties'].pop(prop, None)
219::CODE;;if not props['properties']:
220::CODE;;self.cancel(widget)
221::CODE;;def have_properties_to_animate(self, widget):
222::CODE;;'''Return True if a widget still has properties to animate.
223::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.8.0
224::CODE;;'''
225::CODE;;props = self._widgets.get(widget.uid, None)
226::CODE;;if props and props['properties']:
227::CODE;;return True
231::CODE;;def _register(self):
232::CODE;;Animation._instances.add(self)
233::CODE;;def _unregister(self):
234::CODE;;Animation._instances.discard(self)
235::CODE;;def _initialize(self, widget):
236::CODE;;d = self._widgets[widget.uid] = {
237::CODE;;'widget': widget,
238::CODE;;'properties': {},
239::CODE;;'time': None}
241::CODE;;p = d['properties']
242::CODE;;for key, value in self._animated_properties.items():
243::CODE;;original_value = getattr(widget, key)
244::CODE;;if isinstance(original_value, (tuple, list)):
245::CODE;;original_value = original_value[:]
246::CODE;;elif isinstance(original_value, dict):
247::CODE;;original_value = original_value.copy()
248::CODE;;p[key] = (original_value, value)
250::CODE;;self._clock_install()
251::CODE;;def _clock_install(self):
252::CODE;;if self._clock_installed:
253::CODE;;return
254::CODE;;self._update_ev = Clock.schedule_interval(self._update, self._step)
255::CODE;;self._clock_installed = True
256::CODE;;def _clock_uninstall(self):
257::CODE;;if self._widgets or not self._clock_installed:
258::CODE;;return
259::CODE;;self._clock_installed = False
260::CODE;;if self._update_ev is not None:
261::CODE;;self._update_ev.cancel()
262::CODE;;self._update_ev = None
263::CODE;;def _update(self, dt):
264::CODE;;widgets = self._widgets
265::CODE;;transition = self._transition
266::CODE;;calculate = self._calculate
267::CODE;;for uid in list(widgets.keys()):
268::CODE;;anim = widgets[uid]
269::CODE;;widget = anim['widget']
270::CODE;;if isinstance(widget, WeakProxy) and not len(dir(widget)):
272::CODE;;self._widgets.pop(uid, None)
273::CODE;;self._clock_uninstall()
274::CODE;;if not self._widgets:
275::CODE;;self._unregister()
276::CODE;;continue
277::CODE;;if anim['time'] is None:
278::CODE;;anim['time'] = 0.
279::CODE;;else:
280::CODE;;anim['time'] += dt
282::CODE;;if self._duration:
283::CODE;;progress = min(1., anim['time'] / self._duration)
284::CODE;;else:
285::CODE;;progress = 1
286::CODE;;t = transition(progress)
288::CODE;;for key, values in anim['properties'].items():
289::CODE;;a, b = values
290::CODE;;value = calculate(a, b, t)
291::CODE;;setattr(widget, key, value)
292::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_progress', widget, progress)
294::CODE;;if progress >= 1.:
295::CODE;;self.stop(widget)
296::CODE;;def _calculate(self, a, b, t):
297::CODE;;_calculate = self._calculate
298::CODE;;if isinstance(a, list) or isinstance(a, tuple):
299::CODE;;if isinstance(a, list):
300::CODE;;tp = list
301::CODE;;else:
302::CODE;;tp = tuple
303::CODE;;return tp([_calculate(a[x], b[x], t) for x in range(len(a))])
304::CODE;;elif isinstance(a, dict):
305::CODE;;d = {}
306::CODE;;for x in a.keys():
307::CODE;;if x not in b:
310::CODE;;d[x] = a[x]
311::CODE;;else:
312::CODE;;d[x] = _calculate(a[x], b[x], t)
313::CODE;;return d
314::CODE;;else:
315::CODE;;return (a * (1. - t)) + (b * t)
319::CODE;;def on_start(self, widget):
320::CODE;;pass
321::CODE;;def on_progress(self, widget, progress):
322::CODE;;pass
323::CODE;;def on_complete(self, widget):
324::CODE;;pass
325::CODE;;def __add__(self, animation):
326::CODE;;return Sequence(self, animation)
327::CODE;;def __and__(self, animation):
328::CODE;;return Parallel(self, animation)
329::CODE;;class CompoundAnimation(Animation):
330::CODE;;def stop_property(self, widget, prop):
331::CODE;;self.anim1.stop_property(widget, prop)
332::CODE;;self.anim2.stop_property(widget, prop)
333::CODE;;if (not self.anim1.have_properties_to_animate(widget) and
334::CODE;;not self.anim2.have_properties_to_animate(widget)):
335::CODE;;self.stop(widget)
336::CODE;;def cancel(self, widget):
337::CODE;;self.anim1.cancel(widget)
338::CODE;;self.anim2.cancel(widget)
339::CODE;;super().cancel(widget)
340::CODE;;def cancel_property(self, widget, prop):
341::CODE;;'''Even if an animation is running, remove a property. It will not be
342::CODE;;animated further. If it was the only/last property being animated,
343::CODE;;the animation will be canceled (see :attr:`cancel`)
344::CODE;;This method overrides `:class:kivy.animation.Animation`'s
345::CODE;;version, to cancel it on all animations of the Sequence.
346::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.10.0
347::CODE;;'''
348::CODE;;self.anim1.cancel_property(widget, prop)
349::CODE;;self.anim2.cancel_property(widget, prop)
350::CODE;;if (not self.anim1.have_properties_to_animate(widget) and
351::CODE;;not self.anim2.have_properties_to_animate(widget)):
352::CODE;;self.cancel(widget)
353::CODE;;def have_properties_to_animate(self, widget):
354::CODE;;return (self.anim1.have_properties_to_animate(widget) or
355::CODE;;self.anim2.have_properties_to_animate(widget))
356::CODE;;@property
357::CODE;;def animated_properties(self):
358::CODE;;return ChainMap({},
359::CODE;;self.anim2.animated_properties,
360::CODE;;self.anim1.animated_properties)
361::CODE;;@property
362::CODE;;def transition(self):
364::CODE;;raise AttributeError(
365::CODE;;"Can't lookup transition attribute of a CompoundAnimation")
366::CODE;;class Sequence(CompoundAnimation):
367::CODE;;def __init__(self, anim1, anim2):
368::CODE;;super().__init__()
371::CODE;;self.repeat = False
372::CODE;;self.anim1 = anim1
373::CODE;;self.anim2 = anim2
374::CODE;;self.anim1.bind(on_complete=self.on_anim1_complete,
375::CODE;;on_progress=self.on_anim1_progress)
376::CODE;;self.anim2.bind(on_complete=self.on_anim2_complete,
377::CODE;;on_progress=self.on_anim2_progress)
378::CODE;;@property
379::CODE;;def duration(self):
380::CODE;;return self.anim1.duration + self.anim2.duration
381::CODE;;def stop(self, widget):
382::CODE;;props = self._widgets.pop(widget.uid, None)
383::CODE;;self.anim1.stop(widget)
384::CODE;;self.anim2.stop(widget)
385::CODE;;if props:
386::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_complete', widget)
387::CODE;;super().cancel(widget)
388::CODE;;def start(self, widget):
389::CODE;;self.stop(widget)
390::CODE;;self._widgets[widget.uid] = True
391::CODE;;self._register()
392::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_start', widget)
393::CODE;;self.anim1.start(widget)
394::CODE;;def on_anim1_complete(self, instance, widget):
395::CODE;;if widget.uid not in self._widgets:
396::CODE;;return
397::CODE;;self.anim2.start(widget)
398::CODE;;def on_anim1_progress(self, instance, widget, progress):
399::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_progress', widget, progress / 2.)
400::CODE;;def on_anim2_complete(self, instance, widget):
401::CODE;;'''Repeating logic used with boolean variable "repeat".
402::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.7.1
403::CODE;;'''
404::CODE;;if widget.uid not in self._widgets:
405::CODE;;return
406::CODE;;if self.repeat:
407::CODE;;self.anim1.start(widget)
408::CODE;;else:
409::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_complete', widget)
410::CODE;;self.cancel(widget)
411::CODE;;def on_anim2_progress(self, instance, widget, progress):
412::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_progress', widget, .5 + progress / 2.)
413::CODE;;class Parallel(CompoundAnimation):
414::CODE;;def __init__(self, anim1, anim2):
415::CODE;;super().__init__()
416::CODE;;self.anim1 = anim1
417::CODE;;self.anim2 = anim2
418::CODE;;self.anim1.bind(on_complete=self.on_anim_complete)
419::CODE;;self.anim2.bind(on_complete=self.on_anim_complete)
420::CODE;;@property
421::CODE;;def duration(self):
422::CODE;;return max(self.anim1.duration, self.anim2.duration)
423::CODE;;def stop(self, widget):
424::CODE;;self.anim1.stop(widget)
425::CODE;;self.anim2.stop(widget)
426::CODE;;if self._widgets.pop(widget.uid, None):
427::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_complete', widget)
428::CODE;;super().cancel(widget)
429::CODE;;def start(self, widget):
430::CODE;;self.stop(widget)
431::CODE;;self.anim1.start(widget)
432::CODE;;self.anim2.start(widget)
433::CODE;;self._widgets[widget.uid] = {'complete': 0}
434::CODE;;self._register()
435::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_start', widget)
436::CODE;;def on_anim_complete(self, instance, widget):
437::CODE;;self._widgets[widget.uid]['complete'] += 1
438::CODE;;if self._widgets[widget.uid]['complete'] == 2:
439::CODE;;self.stop(widget)
440::CODE;;class AnimationTransition:
441::CODE;;'''Collection of animation functions to be used with the Animation object.
442::CODE;;Easing Functions ported to Kivy from the Clutter Project
443::CODE;;https://developer.gnome.org/clutter/stable/ClutterAlpha.html
444::CODE;;The `progress` parameter in each animation function is in the range 0-1.
445::CODE;;'''
446::CODE;;@staticmethod
447::CODE;;def linear(progress):
448::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_linear.png'''
449::CODE;;return progress
450::CODE;;@staticmethod
451::CODE;;def in_quad(progress):
452::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_in_quad.png
453::CODE;;'''
454::CODE;;return progress * progress
455::CODE;;@staticmethod
456::CODE;;def out_quad(progress):
457::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_out_quad.png
458::CODE;;'''
459::CODE;;return -1.0 * progress * (progress - 2.0)
460::CODE;;@staticmethod
461::CODE;;def in_out_quad(progress):
462::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_in_out_quad.png
463::CODE;;'''
464::CODE;;p = progress * 2
465::CODE;;if p < 1:
466::CODE;;return 0.5 * p * p
467::CODE;;p -= 1.0
468::CODE;;return -0.5 * (p * (p - 2.0) - 1.0)
469::CODE;;@staticmethod
470::CODE;;def in_cubic(progress):
471::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_in_cubic.png
472::CODE;;'''
473::CODE;;return progress * progress * progress
474::CODE;;@staticmethod
475::CODE;;def out_cubic(progress):
476::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_out_cubic.png
477::CODE;;'''
478::CODE;;p = progress - 1.0
479::CODE;;return p * p * p + 1.0
480::CODE;;@staticmethod
481::CODE;;def in_out_cubic(progress):
482::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_in_out_cubic.png
483::CODE;;'''
484::CODE;;p = progress * 2
485::CODE;;if p < 1:
486::CODE;;return 0.5 * p * p * p
487::CODE;;p -= 2
488::CODE;;return 0.5 * (p * p * p + 2.0)
489::CODE;;@staticmethod
490::CODE;;def in_quart(progress):
491::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_in_quart.png
492::CODE;;'''
493::CODE;;return progress * progress * progress * progress
494::CODE;;@staticmethod
495::CODE;;def out_quart(progress):
496::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_out_quart.png
497::CODE;;'''
498::CODE;;p = progress - 1.0
499::CODE;;return -1.0 * (p * p * p * p - 1.0)
500::CODE;;@staticmethod
501::CODE;;def in_out_quart(progress):
502::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_in_out_quart.png
503::CODE;;'''
504::CODE;;p = progress * 2
505::CODE;;if p < 1:
506::CODE;;return 0.5 * p * p * p * p
507::CODE;;p -= 2
508::CODE;;return -0.5 * (p * p * p * p - 2.0)
509::CODE;;@staticmethod
510::CODE;;def in_quint(progress):
511::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_in_quint.png
512::CODE;;'''
513::CODE;;return progress * progress * progress * progress * progress
514::CODE;;@staticmethod
515::CODE;;def out_quint(progress):
516::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_out_quint.png
517::CODE;;'''
518::CODE;;p = progress - 1.0
519::CODE;;return p * p * p * p * p + 1.0
520::CODE;;@staticmethod
521::CODE;;def in_out_quint(progress):
522::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_in_out_quint.png
523::CODE;;'''
524::CODE;;p = progress * 2
525::CODE;;if p < 1:
526::CODE;;return 0.5 * p * p * p * p * p
527::CODE;;p -= 2.0
528::CODE;;return 0.5 * (p * p * p * p * p + 2.0)
529::CODE;;@staticmethod
530::CODE;;def in_sine(progress):
531::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_in_sine.png
532::CODE;;'''
533::CODE;;return -1.0 * cos(progress * (pi / 2.0)) + 1.0
534::CODE;;@staticmethod
535::CODE;;def out_sine(progress):
536::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_out_sine.png
537::CODE;;'''
538::CODE;;return sin(progress * (pi / 2.0))
539::CODE;;@staticmethod
540::CODE;;def in_out_sine(progress):
541::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_in_out_sine.png
542::CODE;;'''
543::CODE;;return -0.5 * (cos(pi * progress) - 1.0)
544::CODE;;@staticmethod
545::CODE;;def in_expo(progress):
546::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_in_expo.png
547::CODE;;'''
548::CODE;;if progress == 0:
549::CODE;;return 0.0
550::CODE;;return pow(2, 10 * (progress - 1.0))
551::CODE;;@staticmethod
552::CODE;;def out_expo(progress):
553::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_out_expo.png
554::CODE;;'''
555::CODE;;if progress == 1.0:
556::CODE;;return 1.0
557::CODE;;return -pow(2, -10 * progress) + 1.0
558::CODE;;@staticmethod
559::CODE;;def in_out_expo(progress):
560::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_in_out_expo.png
561::CODE;;'''
562::CODE;;if progress == 0:
563::CODE;;return 0.0
564::CODE;;if progress == 1.:
565::CODE;;return 1.0
566::CODE;;p = progress * 2
567::CODE;;if p < 1:
568::CODE;;return 0.5 * pow(2, 10 * (p - 1.0))
569::CODE;;p -= 1.0
570::CODE;;return 0.5 * (-pow(2, -10 * p) + 2.0)
571::CODE;;@staticmethod
572::CODE;;def in_circ(progress):
573::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_in_circ.png
574::CODE;;'''
575::CODE;;return -1.0 * (sqrt(1.0 - progress * progress) - 1.0)
576::CODE;;@staticmethod
577::CODE;;def out_circ(progress):
578::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_out_circ.png
579::CODE;;'''
580::CODE;;p = progress - 1.0
581::CODE;;return sqrt(1.0 - p * p)
582::CODE;;@staticmethod
583::CODE;;def in_out_circ(progress):
584::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_in_out_circ.png
585::CODE;;'''
586::CODE;;p = progress * 2
587::CODE;;if p < 1:
588::CODE;;return -0.5 * (sqrt(1.0 - p * p) - 1.0)
589::CODE;;p -= 2.0
590::CODE;;return 0.5 * (sqrt(1.0 - p * p) + 1.0)
591::CODE;;@staticmethod
592::CODE;;def in_elastic(progress):
593::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_in_elastic.png
594::CODE;;'''
595::CODE;;p = .3
596::CODE;;s = p / 4.0
597::CODE;;q = progress
598::CODE;;if q == 1:
599::CODE;;return 1.0
600::CODE;;q -= 1.0
601::CODE;;return -(pow(2, 10 * q) * sin((q - s) * (2 * pi) / p))
602::CODE;;@staticmethod
603::CODE;;def out_elastic(progress):
604::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_out_elastic.png
605::CODE;;'''
606::CODE;;p = .3
607::CODE;;s = p / 4.0
608::CODE;;q = progress
609::CODE;;if q == 1:
610::CODE;;return 1.0
611::CODE;;return pow(2, -10 * q) * sin((q - s) * (2 * pi) / p) + 1.0
612::CODE;;@staticmethod
613::CODE;;def in_out_elastic(progress):
614::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_in_out_elastic.png
615::CODE;;'''
616::CODE;;p = .3 * 1.5
617::CODE;;s = p / 4.0
618::CODE;;q = progress * 2
619::CODE;;if q == 2:
620::CODE;;return 1.0
621::CODE;;if q < 1:
622::CODE;;q -= 1.0
623::CODE;;return -.5 * (pow(2, 10 * q) * sin((q - s) * (2.0 * pi) / p))
624::CODE;;else:
625::CODE;;q -= 1.0
626::CODE;;return pow(2, -10 * q) * sin((q - s) * (2.0 * pi) / p) * .5 + 1.0
627::CODE;;@staticmethod
628::CODE;;def in_back(progress):
629::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_in_back.png
630::CODE;;'''
631::CODE;;return progress * progress * ((1.70158 + 1.0) * progress - 1.70158)
632::CODE;;@staticmethod
633::CODE;;def out_back(progress):
634::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_out_back.png
635::CODE;;'''
636::CODE;;p = progress - 1.0
637::CODE;;return p * p * ((1.70158 + 1) * p + 1.70158) + 1.0
638::CODE;;@staticmethod
639::CODE;;def in_out_back(progress):
640::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_in_out_back.png
641::CODE;;'''
642::CODE;;p = progress * 2.
643::CODE;;s = 1.70158 * 1.525
644::CODE;;if p < 1:
645::CODE;;return 0.5 * (p * p * ((s + 1.0) * p - s))
646::CODE;;p -= 2.0
647::CODE;;return 0.5 * (p * p * ((s + 1.0) * p + s) + 2.0)
648::CODE;;@staticmethod
649::CODE;;def _out_bounce_internal(t, d):
650::CODE;;p = t / d
651::CODE;;if p < (1.0 / 2.75):
652::CODE;;return 7.5625 * p * p
653::CODE;;elif p < (2.0 / 2.75):
654::CODE;;p -= (1.5 / 2.75)
655::CODE;;return 7.5625 * p * p + .75
656::CODE;;elif p < (2.5 / 2.75):
657::CODE;;p -= (2.25 / 2.75)
658::CODE;;return 7.5625 * p * p + .9375
659::CODE;;else:
660::CODE;;p -= (2.625 / 2.75)
661::CODE;;return 7.5625 * p * p + .984375
662::CODE;;@staticmethod
663::CODE;;def _in_bounce_internal(t, d):
664::CODE;;return 1.0 - AnimationTransition._out_bounce_internal(d - t, d)
665::CODE;;@staticmethod
666::CODE;;def in_bounce(progress):
667::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_in_bounce.png
668::CODE;;'''
669::CODE;;return AnimationTransition._in_bounce_internal(progress, 1.)
670::CODE;;@staticmethod
671::CODE;;def out_bounce(progress):
672::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_out_bounce.png
673::CODE;;'''
674::CODE;;return AnimationTransition._out_bounce_internal(progress, 1.)
675::CODE;;@staticmethod
676::CODE;;def in_out_bounce(progress):
677::CODE;;'''.. image:: images/anim_in_out_bounce.png
678::CODE;;'''
679::CODE;;p = progress * 2.
680::CODE;;if p < 1.:
681::CODE;;return AnimationTransition._in_bounce_internal(p, 1.) * .5
682::CODE;;return AnimationTransition._out_bounce_internal(p - 1., 1.) * .5 + .5
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Application
3::CODE;;===========
4::CODE;;The :class:`App` class is the base for creating Kivy applications.
5::CODE;;Think of it as your main entry point into the Kivy run loop. In most
6::CODE;;cases, you subclass this class and make your own app. You create an
7::CODE;;instance of your specific app class and then, when you are ready to
8::CODE;;start the application's life cycle, you call your instance's
9::CODE;;:meth:`App.run` method.
10::CODE;;Creating an Application
11::CODE;;-----------------------
12::CODE;;Method using build() override
13::CODE;;~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
14::CODE;;To initialize your app with a widget tree, override the :meth:`~App.build`
15::CODE;;method in your app class and return the widget tree you constructed.
16::CODE;;Here's an example of a very simple application that just shows a button:
17::CODE;;.. include:: ../../examples/application/app_with_build.py
18::CODE;;:literal:
19::CODE;;The file is also available in the examples folder at
20::CODE;;:file:`kivy/examples/application/app_with_build.py`.
21::CODE;;Here, no widget tree was constructed (or if you will, a tree with only
22::CODE;;the root node).
23::CODE;;Method using kv file
24::CODE;;~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
25::CODE;;You can also use the :doc:`api-kivy.lang` for creating applications. The
26::CODE;;.kv can contain rules and root widget definitions at the same time. Here
27::CODE;;is the same example as the Button one in a kv file.
28::CODE;;Contents of 'test.kv':
29::CODE;;.. include:: ../../examples/application/test.kv
30::CODE;;:literal:
31::CODE;;Contents of 'main.py':
32::CODE;;.. include:: ../../examples/application/app_with_kv.py
33::CODE;;:literal:
34::CODE;;See :file:`kivy/examples/application/app_with_kv.py`.
35::CODE;;The relationship between main.py and test.kv is explained in
36::CODE;;:meth:`App.load_kv`.
37::CODE;;.. _Application configuration:
38::CODE;;Application configuration
39::CODE;;-------------------------
40::CODE;;Use the configuration file
41::CODE;;~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
42::CODE;;Your application might need its own configuration file. The
43::CODE;;:class:`App` class handles 'ini' files automatically if you add
44::CODE;;the section key-value pair to the :meth:`App.build_config` method using the
45::CODE;;`config` parameter (an instance of :class:`~kivy.config.ConfigParser`)::
46::CODE;;class TestApp(App):
47::CODE;;def build_config(self, config):
48::CODE;;config.setdefaults('section1', {
49::CODE;;'key1': 'value1',
50::CODE;;'key2': '42'
51::CODE;;})
52::CODE;;As soon as you add one section to the config, a file is created on the
53::CODE;;disk (see :attr:`~App.get_application_config` for its location) and
54::CODE;;named based your class name. "TestApp" will give a config file named
55::CODE;;"test.ini" with the content::
56::CODE;;[section1]
57::CODE;;key1 = value1
58::CODE;;key2 = 42
59::CODE;;The "test.ini" will be automatically loaded at runtime and you can access the
60::CODE;;configuration in your :meth:`App.build` method::
61::CODE;;class TestApp(App):
62::CODE;;def build_config(self, config):
63::CODE;;config.setdefaults('section1', {
64::CODE;;'key1': 'value1',
65::CODE;;'key2': '42'
66::CODE;;})
67::CODE;;def build(self):
68::CODE;;config = self.config
69::CODE;;return Label(text='key1 is %s and key2 is %d' % (
70::CODE;;config.get('section1', 'key1'),
71::CODE;;config.getint('section1', 'key2')))

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Atlas
3::CODE;;=====
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.1.0
5::CODE;;Atlas manages texture atlases: packing multiple textures into
6::CODE;;one. With it, you reduce the number of images loaded and speedup the
7::CODE;;application loading. This module contains both the Atlas class and command line
8::CODE;;processing for creating an atlas from a set of individual PNG files. The
9::CODE;;command line section requires the Pillow library, or the defunct Python Imaging
10::CODE;;Library (PIL), to be installed.
11::CODE;;An Atlas is composed of 2 or more files:
12::CODE;;- a json file (.atlas) that contains the image file names and texture
13::CODE;;locations of the atlas.
14::CODE;;- one or multiple image files containing textures referenced by the .atlas
15::CODE;;file.
16::CODE;;Definition of .atlas files
17::CODE;;--------------------------
18::CODE;;A file with ``<basename>.atlas`` is a json file formatted like this::
19::CODE;;{
20::CODE;;"<basename>-<index>.png": {
21::CODE;;"id1": [ <x>, <y>, <width>, <height> ],
22::CODE;;"id2": [ <x>, <y>, <width>, <height> ],
24::CODE;;},
26::CODE;;}
27::CODE;;Example from the Kivy ``data/images/defaulttheme.atlas``::
28::CODE;;{
29::CODE;;"defaulttheme-0.png": {
30::CODE;;"progressbar_background": [431, 224, 59, 24],
31::CODE;;"image-missing": [253, 344, 48, 48],
32::CODE;;"filechooser_selected": [1, 207, 118, 118],
33::CODE;;"bubble_btn": [83, 174, 32, 32],
35::CODE;;}
36::CODE;;}
37::CODE;;In this example, "defaulttheme-0.png" is a large image, with the pixels in the
38::CODE;;rectangle from (431, 224) to (431 + 59, 224 + 24) usable as
39::CODE;;``atlas://data/images/defaulttheme/progressbar_background`` in
40::CODE;;any image parameter.
41::CODE;;How to create an Atlas
42::CODE;;----------------------
43::CODE;;.. warning::
44::CODE;;The atlas creation requires the Pillow library (or the defunct Imaging/PIL
45::CODE;;library). This requirement will be removed in the future when the Kivy core
46::CODE;;Image is able to support loading, blitting, and saving operations.
47::CODE;;You can directly use this module to create atlas files with this command::
48::CODE;;$ python -m kivy.atlas <basename> <size> <list of images...>
49::CODE;;Let's say you have a list of images that you want to put into an Atlas. The
50::CODE;;directory is named ``images`` with lots of 64x64 png files inside::
51::CODE;;$ ls
52::CODE;;images
53::CODE;;$ cd images
54::CODE;;$ ls
55::CODE;;bubble.png bubble-red.png button.png button-down.png
56::CODE;;You can combine all the png's into one and generate the atlas file with::
57::CODE;;$ python -m kivy.atlas myatlas 256x256 *.png
58::CODE;;Atlas created at myatlas.atlas
59::CODE;;1 image has been created
60::CODE;;$ ls
61::CODE;;bubble.png bubble-red.png button.png button-down.png myatlas.atlas
62::CODE;;myatlas-0.png
63::CODE;;As you can see, we get 2 new files: ``myatlas.atlas`` and ``myatlas-0.png``.
64::CODE;;``myatlas-0.png`` is a new 256x256 .png composed of all your images. If the
65::CODE;;size you specify is not large enough to fit all of the source images, more
66::CODE;;atlas images will be created as required e.g. ``myatlas-1.png``,
67::CODE;;``myatlas-2.png`` etc.
68::CODE;;.. note::
69::CODE;;When using this script, the ids referenced in the atlas are the base names
70::CODE;;of the images without the extension. So, if you are going to name a file
71::CODE;;``../images/button.png``, the id for this image will be ``button``.
72::CODE;;If you need path information included, you should include ``use_path`` as
73::CODE;;follows::
74::CODE;;$ python -m kivy.atlas -- --use_path myatlas 256 *.png
75::CODE;;In which case the id for ``../images/button.png`` will be ``images_button``
76::CODE;;How to use an Atlas
77::CODE;;-------------------
78::CODE;;Usually, you would specify the images by supplying the path::
79::CODE;;a = Button(background_normal='images/button.png',
80::CODE;;background_down='images/button_down.png')
81::CODE;;In our previous example, we have created the atlas containing both images and
82::CODE;;put them in ``images/myatlas.atlas``. You can use url notation to reference
83::CODE;;them::
84::CODE;;a = Button(background_normal='atlas://images/myatlas/button',
85::CODE;;background_down='atlas://images/myatlas/button_down')
86::CODE;;In other words, the path to the images is replaced by::
87::CODE;;atlas://path/to/myatlas/id
89::CODE;;.. note::
90::CODE;;In the atlas url, there is no need to add the ``.atlas`` extension. It will
91::CODE;;be automatically append to the filename.
92::CODE;;Manual usage of the Atlas
93::CODE;;-------------------------
94::CODE;;::
95::CODE;;>>> from kivy.atlas import Atlas
96::CODE;;>>> atlas = Atlas('path/to/myatlas.atlas')
97::CODE;;>>> print(atlas.textures.keys())
98::CODE;;['bubble', 'bubble-red', 'button', 'button-down']
99::CODE;;>>> print(atlas['button'])
100::CODE;;<kivy.graphics.texture.TextureRegion object at 0x2404d10>
101::CODE;;'''
102::CODE;;__all__ = ('Atlas', )
103::CODE;;import json
104::CODE;;from os.path import basename, dirname, join, splitext
105::CODE;;from kivy.event import EventDispatcher
106::CODE;;from kivy.logger import Logger
107::CODE;;from kivy.properties import AliasProperty, DictProperty, ListProperty
108::CODE;;import os
110::CODE;;CoreImage = None
111::CODE;;class Atlas(EventDispatcher):
112::CODE;;'''Manage texture atlas. See module documentation for more information.
113::CODE;;'''
114::CODE;;original_textures = ListProperty([])
115::CODE;;'''List of original atlas textures (which contain the :attr:`textures`).
116::CODE;;:attr:`original_textures` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.ListProperty` and
117::CODE;;defaults to [].
118::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.9.1
119::CODE;;'''
120::CODE;;textures = DictProperty({})
121::CODE;;'''List of available textures within the atlas.
122::CODE;;:attr:`textures` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.DictProperty` and defaults
123::CODE;;to {}.
124::CODE;;'''
125::CODE;;def _get_filename(self):
126::CODE;;return self._filename
127::CODE;;filename = AliasProperty(_get_filename, None)
128::CODE;;'''Filename of the current Atlas.
129::CODE;;:attr:`filename` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.AliasProperty` and defaults
130::CODE;;to None.
131::CODE;;'''
132::CODE;;def __init__(self, filename):
133::CODE;;self._filename = filename
134::CODE;;super(Atlas, self).__init__()
135::CODE;;self._load()
136::CODE;;def __getitem__(self, key):
137::CODE;;return self.textures[key]
138::CODE;;def _load(self):
140::CODE;;global CoreImage
141::CODE;;if CoreImage is None:
142::CODE;;from kivy.core.image import Image as CoreImage
144::CODE;;filename = self._filename
145::CODE;;assert filename.endswith('.atlas')
146::CODE;;filename = filename.replace('/', os.sep)
147::CODE;;Logger.debug('Atlas: Load <%s>' % filename)
148::CODE;;with open(filename, 'r') as fd:
149::CODE;;meta = json.load(fd)
150::CODE;;Logger.debug('Atlas: Need to load %d images' % len(meta))
151::CODE;;d = dirname(filename)
152::CODE;;textures = {}
153::CODE;;for subfilename, ids in meta.items():
154::CODE;;subfilename = join(d, subfilename)
155::CODE;;Logger.debug('Atlas: Load <%s>' % subfilename)
157::CODE;;ci = CoreImage(subfilename)
158::CODE;;atlas_texture = ci.texture
159::CODE;;self.original_textures.append(atlas_texture)
162::CODE;;for meta_id, meta_coords in ids.items():
163::CODE;;x, y, w, h = meta_coords
164::CODE;;textures[meta_id] = atlas_texture.get_region(*meta_coords)
165::CODE;;self.textures = textures
166::CODE;;@staticmethod
167::CODE;;def create(outname, filenames, size, padding=2, use_path=False):
168::CODE;;'''This method can be used to create an atlas manually from a set of
169::CODE;;images.
170::CODE;;:Parameters:
171::CODE;;`outname`: str
172::CODE;;Basename to use for ``.atlas`` creation and ``-<idx>.png``
173::CODE;;associated images.
174::CODE;;`filenames`: list
175::CODE;;List of filenames to put in the atlas.
176::CODE;;`size`: int or list (width, height)
177::CODE;;Size of the atlas image. If the size is not large enough to
178::CODE;;fit all of the source images, more atlas images will created
179::CODE;;as required.
180::CODE;;`padding`: int, defaults to 2
181::CODE;;Padding to put around each image.
182::CODE;;Be careful. If you're using a padding < 2, you might have
183::CODE;;issues with the borders of the images. Because of the OpenGL
184::CODE;;linearization, it might use the pixels of the adjacent image.
185::CODE;;If you're using a padding >= 2, we'll automatically generate a
186::CODE;;"border" of 1px around your image. If you look at
187::CODE;;the result, don't be scared if the image inside is not
188::CODE;;exactly the same as yours :).
189::CODE;;`use_path`: bool, defaults to False
190::CODE;;If True, the relative path of the source png
191::CODE;;file names will be included in the atlas ids rather
192::CODE;;that just in the file names. Leading dots and slashes will be
193::CODE;;excluded and all other slashes in the path will be replaced
194::CODE;;with underscores. For example, if `use_path` is False
195::CODE;;(the default) and the file name is
196::CODE;;``../data/tiles/green_grass.png``, the id will be
197::CODE;;``green_grass``. If `use_path` is True, it will be
198::CODE;;``data_tiles_green_grass``.
199::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.8.0
200::CODE;;Parameter use_path added
201::CODE;;'''
205::CODE;;try:
206::CODE;;from PIL import Image
207::CODE;;except ImportError:
208::CODE;;Logger.critical('Atlas: Imaging/PIL are missing')
209::CODE;;raise
210::CODE;;if isinstance(size, (tuple, list)):
211::CODE;;size_w, size_h = list(map(int, size))
212::CODE;;else:
213::CODE;;size_w = size_h = int(size)
215::CODE;;ims = list()
216::CODE;;for f in filenames:
217::CODE;;fp = open(f, 'rb')
218::CODE;;im = Image.open(fp)
219::CODE;;im.load()
220::CODE;;fp.close()
221::CODE;;ims.append((f, im))
223::CODE;;ims = sorted(ims, key=lambda im: im[1].size[0] * im[1].size[1],
224::CODE;;reverse=True)
227::CODE;;freeboxes = [(0, 0, 0, size_w, size_h)]
228::CODE;;numoutimages = 1
231::CODE;;fullboxes = []
234::CODE;;for imageinfo in ims:
235::CODE;;im = imageinfo[1]
236::CODE;;imw, imh = im.size
237::CODE;;imw += padding
238::CODE;;imh += padding
239::CODE;;if imw > size_w or imh > size_h:
240::CODE;;Logger.error(
241::CODE;;'Atlas: image %s (%d by %d) is larger than the atlas size!'
242::CODE;;% (imageinfo[0], imw, imh))
243::CODE;;return
244::CODE;;inserted = False
245::CODE;;while not inserted:
246::CODE;;for idx, fb in enumerate(freeboxes):
248::CODE;;if fb[3] >= imw and fb[4] >= imh:
252::CODE;;del freeboxes[idx]
253::CODE;;if fb[3] > imw:
254::CODE;;freeboxes.append((
255::CODE;;fb[0], fb[1] + imw, fb[2],
256::CODE;;fb[3] - imw, imh))
257::CODE;;if fb[4] > imh:
258::CODE;;freeboxes.append((
259::CODE;;fb[0], fb[1], fb[2] + imh,
260::CODE;;fb[3], fb[4] - imh))
262::CODE;;freeboxes = sorted(freeboxes,
263::CODE;;key=lambda fb: fb[3] * fb[4])
264::CODE;;fullboxes.append((im,
265::CODE;;fb[0], fb[1] + padding,
266::CODE;;fb[2] + padding, imw - padding,
267::CODE;;imh - padding, imageinfo[0]))
268::CODE;;inserted = True
269::CODE;;break
270::CODE;;if not inserted:
273::CODE;;freeboxes.append((numoutimages, 0, 0, size_w, size_h))
274::CODE;;numoutimages += 1
277::CODE;;Logger.info('Atlas: create an {0}x{1} rgba image'.format(size_w,
278::CODE;;size_h))
279::CODE;;outimages = [Image.new('RGBA', (size_w, size_h))
280::CODE;;for i in range(0, int(numoutimages))]
281::CODE;;for fb in fullboxes:
282::CODE;;x, y = fb[2], fb[3]
283::CODE;;out = outimages[fb[1]]
284::CODE;;out.paste(fb[0], (fb[2], fb[3]))
285::CODE;;w, h = fb[0].size
286::CODE;;if padding > 1:
287::CODE;;out.paste(fb[0].crop((0, 0, w, 1)), (x, y - 1))
288::CODE;;out.paste(fb[0].crop((0, h - 1, w, h)), (x, y + h))
289::CODE;;out.paste(fb[0].crop((0, 0, 1, h)), (x - 1, y))
290::CODE;;out.paste(fb[0].crop((w - 1, 0, w, h)), (x + w, y))
292::CODE;;for idx, outimage in enumerate(outimages):
293::CODE;;outimage.save('%s-%d.png' % (outname, idx))
295::CODE;;meta = {}
296::CODE;;for fb in fullboxes:
297::CODE;;fn = '%s-%d.png' % (basename(outname), fb[1])
298::CODE;;if fn not in meta:
299::CODE;;d = meta[fn] = {}
300::CODE;;else:
301::CODE;;d = meta[fn]
303::CODE;;if use_path:
307::CODE;;uid = splitext(fb[6])[0]
309::CODE;;uid = uid.lstrip('./\\')
311::CODE;;uid = uid.replace('/', '_').replace('\\', '_')
312::CODE;;else:
315::CODE;;uid = splitext(basename(fb[6]))[0]
316::CODE;;x, y, w, h = fb[2:6]
317::CODE;;d[uid] = x, size_h - y - h, w, h
318::CODE;;outfn = '%s.atlas' % outname
319::CODE;;with open(outfn, 'w') as fd:
320::CODE;;json.dump(meta, fd)
321::CODE;;return outfn, meta
322::CODE;;if __name__ == '__main__':
325::CODE;;import sys
326::CODE;;from glob import glob
327::CODE;;argv = sys.argv[1:]
330::CODE;;if len(argv) < 3:
331::CODE;;print('Usage: python -m kivy.atlas [-- [--use-path] '
332::CODE;;'[--padding=2]] <outname> '
333::CODE;;'<size|512x256> <img1.png> [<img2.png>, ...]')
334::CODE;;sys.exit(1)
335::CODE;;options = {'use_path': False}
336::CODE;;while True:
337::CODE;;option = argv[0]
338::CODE;;if option == '--use-path':
339::CODE;;options['use_path'] = True
340::CODE;;elif option.startswith('--padding='):
341::CODE;;options['padding'] = int(option.split('=', 1)[-1])
342::CODE;;elif option[:2] == '--':
343::CODE;;print('Unknown option {}'.format(option))
344::CODE;;sys.exit(1)
345::CODE;;else:
346::CODE;;break
347::CODE;;argv = argv[1:]
348::CODE;;outname = argv[0]
349::CODE;;try:
350::CODE;;if 'x' in argv[1]:
351::CODE;;size = list(map(int, argv[1].split('x', 1)))
352::CODE;;else:
353::CODE;;size = int(argv[1])
354::CODE;;except ValueError:
355::CODE;;print('Error: size must be an integer or <integer>x<integer>')
356::CODE;;sys.exit(1)
357::CODE;;filenames = [fname for fnames in argv[2:] for fname in glob(fnames)]
358::CODE;;ret = Atlas.create(outname, filenames, size, **options)
359::CODE;;if not ret:
360::CODE;;print('Error while creating atlas!')
361::CODE;;sys.exit(1)
362::CODE;;fn, meta = ret
363::CODE;;print('Atlas created at', fn)
364::CODE;;print('%d image%s been created' % (len(meta),
365::CODE;;'s have' if len(meta) > 1 else ' has'))

31::CODE;;class ExceptionHandler(object):
32::CODE;;'''Base handler that catches exceptions in :func:`runTouchApp`.
33::CODE;;You can subclass and extend it as follows::
34::CODE;;class E(ExceptionHandler):
35::CODE;;def handle_exception(self, inst):
36::CODE;;Logger.exception('Exception caught by ExceptionHandler')
37::CODE;;return ExceptionManager.PASS
38::CODE;;ExceptionManager.add_handler(E())
39::CODE;;Then, all exceptions will be set to PASS, and logged to the console!
40::CODE;;'''
41::CODE;;def handle_exception(self, exception):
42::CODE;;'''Called by :class:`ExceptionManagerBase` to handle a exception.
43::CODE;;Defaults to returning :attr:`ExceptionManager.RAISE` that re-raises the
44::CODE;;exception. Return :attr:`ExceptionManager.PASS` to indicate that the
45::CODE;;exception was handled and should be ignored.
46::CODE;;This may be called multiple times with the same exception, if
47::CODE;;:attr:`ExceptionManager.RAISE` is returned as the exception bubbles
48::CODE;;through multiple kivy exception handling levels.
49::CODE;;'''
50::CODE;;return ExceptionManager.RAISE
51::CODE;;class ExceptionManagerBase:
52::CODE;;'''ExceptionManager manages exceptions handlers.'''
53::CODE;;RAISE = 0
56::CODE;;PASS = 1
59::CODE;;def __init__(self):
60::CODE;;self.handlers = []
61::CODE;;self.policy = ExceptionManagerBase.RAISE
62::CODE;;def add_handler(self, cls):
63::CODE;;'''Add a new exception handler to the stack.'''
64::CODE;;if cls not in self.handlers:
65::CODE;;self.handlers.append(cls)
66::CODE;;def remove_handler(self, cls):
67::CODE;;'''Remove the exception handler from the stack.'''
68::CODE;;if cls in self.handlers:
69::CODE;;self.handlers.remove(cls)
70::CODE;;def handle_exception(self, inst):
71::CODE;;'''Called when an exception occurred in the :func:`runTouchApp`
72::CODE;;main loop.'''
73::CODE;;ret = self.policy
74::CODE;;for handler in self.handlers:
75::CODE;;r = handler.handle_exception(inst)
76::CODE;;if r == ExceptionManagerBase.PASS:
77::CODE;;ret = r
78::CODE;;return ret
80::CODE;;ExceptionManager: ExceptionManagerBase = register_context(
81::CODE;;'ExceptionManager', ExceptionManagerBase)

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Cache manager
3::CODE;;=============
4::CODE;;The cache manager can be used to store python objects attached to a unique
5::CODE;;key. The cache can be controlled in two ways: with a object limit or a
6::CODE;;timeout.
7::CODE;;For example, we can create a new cache with a limit of 10 objects and a
8::CODE;;timeout of 5 seconds::
10::CODE;;Cache.register('mycache', limit=10, timeout=5)
12::CODE;;key = 'objectid'
13::CODE;;instance = Label(text=text)
14::CODE;;Cache.append('mycache', key, instance)
16::CODE;;instance = Cache.get('mycache', key)
17::CODE;;If the instance is NULL, the cache may have trashed it because you've
18::CODE;;not used the label for 5 seconds and you've reach the limit.
19::CODE;;'''
20::CODE;;from os import environ
21::CODE;;from kivy.logger import Logger
22::CODE;;from kivy.clock import Clock
23::CODE;;__all__ = ('Cache', )
24::CODE;;class Cache(object):
25::CODE;;'''See module documentation for more information.
26::CODE;;'''
27::CODE;;_categories = {}
28::CODE;;_objects = {}
29::CODE;;@staticmethod
30::CODE;;def register(category, limit=None, timeout=None):
31::CODE;;'''Register a new category in the cache with the specified limit.
32::CODE;;:Parameters:
33::CODE;;`category`: str
34::CODE;;Identifier of the category.
35::CODE;;`limit`: int (optional)
36::CODE;;Maximum number of objects allowed in the cache.
37::CODE;;If None, no limit is applied.
38::CODE;;`timeout`: double (optional)
39::CODE;;Time after which to delete the object if it has not been used.
40::CODE;;If None, no timeout is applied.
41::CODE;;'''
42::CODE;;Cache._categories[category] = {
43::CODE;;'limit': limit,
44::CODE;;'timeout': timeout}
45::CODE;;Cache._objects[category] = {}
46::CODE;;Logger.debug(
47::CODE;;'Cache: register <%s> with limit=%s, timeout=%s' %
48::CODE;;(category, str(limit), str(timeout)))
49::CODE;;@staticmethod
50::CODE;;def append(category, key, obj, timeout=None):
51::CODE;;'''Add a new object to the cache.
52::CODE;;:Parameters:
53::CODE;;`category`: str
54::CODE;;Identifier of the category.
55::CODE;;`key`: str
56::CODE;;Unique identifier of the object to store.
57::CODE;;`obj`: object
58::CODE;;Object to store in cache.
59::CODE;;`timeout`: double (optional)
60::CODE;;Time after which to delete the object if it has not been used.
61::CODE;;If None, no timeout is applied.
62::CODE;;:raises:
63::CODE;;`ValueError`: If `None` is used as `key`.
64::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 2.0.0
65::CODE;;Raises `ValueError` if `None` is used as `key`.
66::CODE;;'''
68::CODE;;if getattr(obj, '_nocache', False):
69::CODE;;return
70::CODE;;if key is None:
77::CODE;;raise ValueError('"None" cannot be used as key in Cache')
78::CODE;;try:
79::CODE;;cat = Cache._categories[category]
80::CODE;;except KeyError:
81::CODE;;Logger.warning('Cache: category <%s> does not exist' % category)
82::CODE;;return
83::CODE;;timeout = timeout or cat['timeout']
84::CODE;;limit = cat['limit']
85::CODE;;if limit is not None and len(Cache._objects[category]) >= limit:
86::CODE;;Cache._purge_oldest(category)
87::CODE;;Cache._objects[category][key] = {
88::CODE;;'object': obj,
89::CODE;;'timeout': timeout,
90::CODE;;'lastaccess': Clock.get_time(),
91::CODE;;'timestamp': Clock.get_time()}
92::CODE;;@staticmethod
93::CODE;;def get(category, key, default=None):
94::CODE;;'''Get a object from the cache.
95::CODE;;:Parameters:
96::CODE;;`category`: str
97::CODE;;Identifier of the category.
98::CODE;;`key`: str
99::CODE;;Unique identifier of the object in the store.
100::CODE;;`default`: anything, defaults to None
101::CODE;;Default value to be returned if the key is not found.
102::CODE;;'''
103::CODE;;try:
104::CODE;;Cache._objects[category][key]['lastaccess'] = Clock.get_time()
105::CODE;;return Cache._objects[category][key]['object']
106::CODE;;except Exception:
107::CODE;;return default
108::CODE;;@staticmethod
109::CODE;;def get_timestamp(category, key, default=None):
110::CODE;;'''Get the object timestamp in the cache.
111::CODE;;:Parameters:
112::CODE;;`category`: str
113::CODE;;Identifier of the category.
114::CODE;;`key`: str
115::CODE;;Unique identifier of the object in the store.
116::CODE;;`default`: anything, defaults to None
117::CODE;;Default value to be returned if the key is not found.
118::CODE;;'''
119::CODE;;try:
120::CODE;;return Cache._objects[category][key]['timestamp']
121::CODE;;except Exception:
122::CODE;;return default
123::CODE;;@staticmethod
124::CODE;;def get_lastaccess(category, key, default=None):
125::CODE;;'''Get the objects last access time in the cache.
126::CODE;;:Parameters:
127::CODE;;`category`: str
128::CODE;;Identifier of the category.
129::CODE;;`key`: str
130::CODE;;Unique identifier of the object in the store.
131::CODE;;`default`: anything, defaults to None
132::CODE;;Default value to be returned if the key is not found.
133::CODE;;'''
134::CODE;;try:
135::CODE;;return Cache._objects[category][key]['lastaccess']
136::CODE;;except Exception:
137::CODE;;return default
138::CODE;;@staticmethod
139::CODE;;def remove(category, key=None):
140::CODE;;'''Purge the cache.
141::CODE;;:Parameters:
142::CODE;;`category`: str
143::CODE;;Identifier of the category.
144::CODE;;`key`: str (optional)
145::CODE;;Unique identifier of the object in the store. If this
146::CODE;;argument is not supplied, the entire category will be purged.
147::CODE;;'''
148::CODE;;try:
149::CODE;;if key is not None:
150::CODE;;del Cache._objects[category][key]
151::CODE;;Logger.trace('Cache: Removed %s:%s from cache' %
152::CODE;;(category, key))
153::CODE;;else:
154::CODE;;Cache._objects[category] = {}
155::CODE;;Logger.trace('Cache: Flushed category %s from cache' %
156::CODE;;category)
157::CODE;;except Exception:
158::CODE;;pass
159::CODE;;@staticmethod
160::CODE;;def _purge_oldest(category, maxpurge=1):
161::CODE;;Logger.trace('Cache: Remove oldest in %s' % category)
162::CODE;;import heapq
163::CODE;;time = Clock.get_time()
164::CODE;;heap_list = []
165::CODE;;for key in list(Cache._objects[category]):
166::CODE;;obj = Cache._objects[category][key]
167::CODE;;if obj['lastaccess'] == obj['timestamp'] == time:
168::CODE;;continue
169::CODE;;heapq.heappush(heap_list, (obj['lastaccess'], key))
170::CODE;;Logger.trace('Cache: <<< %f' % obj['lastaccess'])
171::CODE;;n = 0
172::CODE;;while n <= maxpurge:
173::CODE;;try:
174::CODE;;n += 1
175::CODE;;lastaccess, key = heapq.heappop(heap_list)
176::CODE;;Logger.trace('Cache: %d => %s %f %f' %
177::CODE;;(n, key, lastaccess, Clock.get_time()))
178::CODE;;except Exception:
179::CODE;;return
180::CODE;;Cache.remove(category, key)
181::CODE;;@staticmethod
182::CODE;;def _purge_by_timeout(dt):
183::CODE;;curtime = Clock.get_time()
184::CODE;;for category in Cache._objects:
185::CODE;;if category not in Cache._categories:
186::CODE;;continue
187::CODE;;timeout = Cache._categories[category]['timeout']
188::CODE;;if timeout is not None and dt > timeout:
194::CODE;;timeout *= 2
195::CODE;;Cache._categories[category]['timeout'] = timeout
196::CODE;;continue
197::CODE;;for key in list(Cache._objects[category].keys()):
198::CODE;;lastaccess = Cache._objects[category][key]['lastaccess']
199::CODE;;objtimeout = Cache._objects[category][key]['timeout']
201::CODE;;if objtimeout is not None:
202::CODE;;timeout = objtimeout
204::CODE;;if timeout is None:
205::CODE;;continue
206::CODE;;if curtime - lastaccess > timeout:
207::CODE;;Logger.trace('Cache: Removed %s:%s from cache due to '
208::CODE;;'timeout' % (category, key))
209::CODE;;Cache.remove(category, key)
210::CODE;;@staticmethod
211::CODE;;def print_usage():
212::CODE;;'''Print the cache usage to the console.'''
213::CODE;;print('Cache usage :')
214::CODE;;for category in Cache._categories:
215::CODE;;print(' * %s : %d / %s, timeout=%s' % (
216::CODE;;category.capitalize(),
217::CODE;;len(Cache._objects[category]),
218::CODE;;str(Cache._categories[category]['limit']),
219::CODE;;str(Cache._categories[category]['timeout'])))
220::CODE;;if 'KIVY_DOC_INCLUDE' not in environ:
222::CODE;;Clock.schedule_interval(Cache._purge_by_timeout, 1)
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Clock object
3::CODE;;============
4::CODE;;The :class:`Clock` object allows you to schedule a function call in the
5::CODE;;future; once or repeatedly at specified intervals. You can get the time
6::CODE;;elapsed between the scheduling and the calling of the callback via the
7::CODE;;`dt` argument::
9::CODE;;def my_callback(dt):
10::CODE;;pass
12::CODE;;Clock.schedule_interval(my_callback, 0.5)
14::CODE;;Clock.schedule_once(my_callback, 5)
16::CODE;;Clock.schedule_once(my_callback)
17::CODE;;.. note::
18::CODE;;If the callback returns False, the schedule will be canceled and won't
19::CODE;;repeat.
20::CODE;;If you want to schedule a function to call with default arguments, you can use
21::CODE;;the `functools.partial
23::CODE;;module::
24::CODE;;from functools import partial
25::CODE;;def my_callback(value, key, *largs):
26::CODE;;pass
27::CODE;;Clock.schedule_interval(partial(my_callback, 'my value', 'my key'), 0.5)
28::CODE;;Conversely, if you want to schedule a function that doesn't accept the dt
29::CODE;;argument, you can use a `lambda
31::CODE;;to write a short function that does accept dt. For Example::
32::CODE;;def no_args_func():
33::CODE;;print("I accept no arguments, so don't schedule me in the clock")
34::CODE;;Clock.schedule_once(lambda dt: no_args_func(), 0.5)
35::CODE;;.. note::
36::CODE;;You cannot unschedule an anonymous function unless you keep a
37::CODE;;reference to it. It's better to add \\*args to your function
38::CODE;;definition so that it can be called with an arbitrary number of
39::CODE;;parameters.
40::CODE;;.. important::
41::CODE;;The class method callback is weak-referenced: you are responsible for
42::CODE;;keeping a reference to your original object/callback. If you don't keep a
43::CODE;;reference, the ClockBase will never execute your callback. For
44::CODE;;example::
45::CODE;;class Foo(object):
46::CODE;;def start(self):
47::CODE;;Clock.schedule_interval(self.callback, 0.5)
48::CODE;;def callback(self, dt):
49::CODE;;print('In callback')
54::CODE;;Foo().start()
57::CODE;;foo = Foo()
58::CODE;;foo.start()
59::CODE;;.. _schedule-before-frame:
60::CODE;;Schedule before frame
61::CODE;;---------------------
62::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.5
63::CODE;;Sometimes you need to schedule a callback BEFORE the next frame. Starting
64::CODE;;from 1.0.5, you can use a timeout of -1::
67::CODE;;The Clock will execute all the callbacks with a timeout of -1 before the
68::CODE;;next frame even if you add a new callback with -1 from a running
69::CODE;;callback. However, :class:`Clock` has an iteration limit for these
70::CODE;;callbacks: it defaults to 10.
71::CODE;;If you schedule a callback that schedules a callback that schedules a ... etc
72::CODE;;more than 10 times, it will leave the loop and send a warning to the console,
73::CODE;;then continue after the next frame. This is implemented to prevent bugs from
74::CODE;;hanging or crashing the application.
75::CODE;;If you need to increase the limit, set the :attr:`max_iteration` property::
76::CODE;;from kivy.clock import Clock
77::CODE;;Clock.max_iteration = 20
78::CODE;;.. _triggered-events:
79::CODE;;Triggered Events
80::CODE;;----------------
81::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.5
82::CODE;;:meth:`CyClockBase.create_trigger` is an advanced method way to defer a
83::CODE;;callback. It functions exactly like :meth:`CyClockBase.schedule_once` and
84::CODE;;:meth:`CyClockBase.schedule_interval` except that it doesn't immediately
85::CODE;;schedule the callback. Instead, one schedules the callback using the
86::CODE;;:class:`ClockEvent` returned by it. This ensures that you can call the event
87::CODE;;multiple times but it won't be scheduled more than once. This is not the case
88::CODE;;with :meth:`CyClockBase.schedule_once`::
90::CODE;;Clock.schedule_once(my_callback)
91::CODE;;Clock.schedule_once(my_callback)
93::CODE;;event = Clock.create_trigger(my_callback)
94::CODE;;event()
95::CODE;;event()
99::CODE;;event()
100::CODE;;In addition, it is more convenient to create and bind to
101::CODE;;the triggered event than using :meth:`CyClockBase.schedule_once` in a
102::CODE;;function::
103::CODE;;from kivy.clock import Clock
104::CODE;;from kivy.uix.widget import Widget
105::CODE;;class Sample(Widget):
106::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
107::CODE;;self._trigger = Clock.create_trigger(self.cb)
108::CODE;;super(Sample, self).__init__(**kwargs)
109::CODE;;self.bind(x=self._trigger, y=self._trigger)
110::CODE;;def cb(self, *largs):
111::CODE;;pass
112::CODE;;Even if x and y changes within one frame, the callback is only run once.
113::CODE;;Unscheduling
114::CODE;;-------------
115::CODE;;An event scheduled with :meth:`CyClockBase.schedule_once`,
116::CODE;;:meth:`CyClockBase.schedule_interval`, or with
117::CODE;;:meth:`CyClockBase.create_trigger` and then triggered can be unscheduled in
118::CODE;;multiple ways. E.g::
119::CODE;;def my_callback(dt):
120::CODE;;pass
122::CODE;;event = Clock.schedule_interval(my_callback, 0.5)
124::CODE;;event2 = Clock.schedule_once(my_callback, 5)
125::CODE;;event_trig = Clock.create_trigger(my_callback, 5)
126::CODE;;event_trig()
128::CODE;;event.cancel()
130::CODE;;Clock.unschedule(event2)
133::CODE;;Clock.unschedule(my_callback)
134::CODE;;The best way to unschedule a callback is with :meth:`ClockEvent.cancel`.
135::CODE;;:meth:`CyClockBase.unschedule` is mainly an alias for that for that function.
136::CODE;;However, if the original callback itself is passed to
137::CODE;;:meth:`CyClockBase.unschedule`, it'll unschedule all instances of that
138::CODE;;callback (provided ``all`` is True, the default, otherwise only the first match
139::CODE;;is removed).
140::CODE;;Calling :meth:`CyClockBase.unschedule` on the original callback is highly
141::CODE;;discouraged because it's significantly slower than when using the event.
142::CODE;;Clock Lifecycle
143::CODE;;---------------
144::CODE;;Kivy's clock has a lifecycle. By default, scheduling a callback after the Clock
145::CODE;;has ended will not raise an error, even though the callback may never be
146::CODE;;called. That's because most callbacks are like services, e.g. responding to a
147::CODE;;user button press - if the app is running the callbacks need to service the app
148::CODE;;and respond to the input, but once the app has stopped or is stopping, we can
149::CODE;;safely not process these events.
150::CODE;;Other events always need to be processed. E.g. another thread may request a
151::CODE;;callback in kivy's thread and then process some result. If the event is not
152::CODE;;processed in Kivy's thread because the app stopped, the second thread may
153::CODE;;block forever hanging the application as it exits.
154::CODE;;Consequently, we provide a API
155::CODE;;(:meth:`CyClockBase.create_lifecycle_aware_trigger`) for scheduling callbacks
156::CODE;;that raise a :class:`ClockNotRunningError` if the clock has stopped. If the
157::CODE;;scheduling succeeded it guarantees that one of its callbacks will be called.
158::CODE;;I.e. the new :meth:`CyClockBase.create_lifecycle_aware_trigger` accepts an
159::CODE;;additional ``clock_ended_callback`` parameter. Normally, ``callback`` will be
160::CODE;;called when the event is processed. But, if the clock is stopped before it can
161::CODE;;be processed, if the application exited normally (and the app was started) and
162::CODE;;the event wasn't canceled, and the callbacks are not garbage collected, then
163::CODE;;``clock_ended_callback`` will be called instead when the clock is stopped.
164::CODE;;That is, given these conditions, if :class:`ClockNotRunningError` was not
165::CODE;;raised when the event was scheduled, then one of these callbacks will be
166::CODE;;called - either ``callback`` if the event executed normally, or
167::CODE;;``clock_ended_callback`` if the clock is stopped while the event is scheduled.
168::CODE;;By default, events can be scheduled before the clock is started because it is
169::CODE;;assumed the clock will eventually be started when the app starts. I.e.
170::CODE;;calling :meth:`CyClockBase.create_lifecycle_aware_trigger` before the clock
171::CODE;;and application starts will succeed. But if the app never actually starts, then
172::CODE;;neither of the callbacks may be executed.
173::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 2.0.0
174::CODE;;The lifecycle was added in 2.0.0
175::CODE;;Exception Handling
176::CODE;;------------------
177::CODE;;Kivy provides a exception handling manager,
178::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.base.ExceptionManager`, to handle its internal exceptions
179::CODE;;including exceptions raised by clock callbacks, without crashing the
180::CODE;;application. By default when an exception is raised, the app will crash.
181::CODE;;But, if a handler is registered with the exception manager and the handler
182::CODE;;handles the exception, the app will not crash and will continue as normal.::
183::CODE;;from kivy.base import ExceptionHandler, ExceptionManager
184::CODE;;class MyHandler(ExceptionHandler):
185::CODE;;def handle_exception(self, inst):
186::CODE;;if isinstance(inst, ValueError):
187::CODE;;Logger.exception('ValueError caught by MyHandler')
188::CODE;;return ExceptionManager.PASS
189::CODE;;return ExceptionManager.RAISE
190::CODE;;ExceptionManager.add_handler(MyHandler())
191::CODE;;Then, all ValueError exceptions will be logged to the console and ignored.
192::CODE;;Similarly, if a scheduled clock callback raises a ValueError, other clock
193::CODE;;events will still be processed normally.
194::CODE;;If an event's callback raises an exception, before the exception handler is
195::CODE;;executed, the callback is immediately canceled.
196::CODE;;It still is possible for the app to be corrupted if kivy itself is the source
197::CODE;;of the exception. I.e. even with a handler that ignores exceptions and doesn't
198::CODE;;crash, the app may be in a corrupted state if the error originates from within
199::CODE;;Kivy itself. However, the exception handler can help protect the app from
200::CODE;;crashing and can help protect against user callbacks crashing the app.
201::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 2.0.0
202::CODE;;Prior to Kivy 2.0.0, an exception raised in a event's callback would
203::CODE;;cause the clock to crash and subsequent events may or may not be executed.
204::CODE;;Even if the exception was handled by an
205::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.base.ExceptionHandler`, there was no guarantee that some
206::CODE;;scheduled events would not be skipped.
207::CODE;;From 2.0.0 onward, if a event's exception is handled by an
208::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.base.ExceptionHandler`, other events will be shielded from
209::CODE;;the exception and will execute normally.
210::CODE;;Scheduling from ``__del__``
211::CODE;;---------------------------
212::CODE;;It is not safe to schedule Clock events from a object's ``__del__`` or
213::CODE;;``__dealloc__`` method. If you must schedule a Clock call from this method, use
214::CODE;;:meth:`CyClockBase.schedule_del_safe` or
215::CODE;;:meth:`CyClockBase.schedule_lifecycle_aware_del_safe` instead.
216::CODE;;Threading and Callback Order
217::CODE;;-----------------------------
218::CODE;;Beginning with 1.10.0, all the events scheduled for the same frame, e.g.
219::CODE;;all the events scheduled in the same frame with a ``timeout`` of ``0``,
220::CODE;;well be executed in the order they were scheduled.
221::CODE;;Also, all the scheduling and canceling methods are fully thread safe and
222::CODE;;can be safely used from external threads.
223::CODE;;As a consequence, calling :meth:`CyClockBase.unschedule` with the original
224::CODE;;callback is now significantly slower and highly discouraged. Instead, the
225::CODE;;returned events should be used to cancel. As a tradeoff, all the other methods
226::CODE;;are now significantly faster than before.
227::CODE;;Advanced Clock Details
228::CODE;;-----------------------
229::CODE;;The following section goes into the internal kivy clock details as well
230::CODE;;as the various clock options. It is meant only for advanced users.
231::CODE;;Fundamentally, the Kivy clock attempts to execute any scheduled callback
232::CODE;;rhythmically as determined by the specified fps (frame per second, see
233::CODE;;``maxfps`` in :mod:`~kivy.config`). That is, ideally, given e.g. a desired fps
234::CODE;;of 30, the clock will execute the callbacks at intervals of 1 / 30 seconds, or
235::CODE;;every 33.33 ms. All the callbacks in a frame are given the same timestamp,
236::CODE;;i.e. the ``dt`` passed to the callback are all the same and it's the difference
237::CODE;;in time between the start of this and the previous frame.
238::CODE;;Because of inherent indeterminism, the frames do not actually occur exactly
239::CODE;;at intervals of the fps and ``dt`` may be under or over the desired fps.
240::CODE;;Also, once the timeout is "close enough" to the desired timeout, as determined
241::CODE;;internally, Kivy will execute the callback in the current frame even when the
242::CODE;;"actual time" has not elapsed the ``timeout`` amount.
243::CODE;;Kivy offers now, since ``1.10.0``, multiple clocks with different behaviors.
244::CODE;;Default Clock
245::CODE;;^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
246::CODE;;The default clock (``default``) behaves as described above. When a callback
247::CODE;;with a timeout of zero or non-zero is scheduled, they are executed at the frame
248::CODE;;that is near the timeout, which is a function of the fps. So a timeout of zero
249::CODE;;would still result in a delay of one frame or about 1 / fps, typically a bit
250::CODE;;less but sometimes more depending on the CPU usage of the other events
251::CODE;;scheduled for that frame.
252::CODE;;In a test using a fps of 30, a callback with a timeout of 0, 0.001, and 0.05,
253::CODE;;resulted in a mean callback delay of 0.02487, 0.02488, and 0.05011 seconds,
254::CODE;;respectively. When tested with a fps of 600 the delay for 0.05 was similar,
255::CODE;;except the standard deviation was reduced resulting in overall better accuracy.
256::CODE;;Interruptible Clock
257::CODE;;^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
258::CODE;;The default clock suffers from the quantization problem, as frames occur only
259::CODE;;on intervals and any scheduled timeouts will not be able to occur during an
260::CODE;;interval. For example, with the timeout of 0.05, while the mean was 0.05011,
261::CODE;;its values ranged between 0.02548 - 0.07348 and a standard deviation of 0.002.
262::CODE;;Also, there's the minimum timeout of about 0.02487.
263::CODE;;The interruptible clock (``interrupt``) will execute timeouts even during a
264::CODE;;frame. So a timeout of zero will execute as quickly as possible and similarly
265::CODE;;a non-zero timeout will be executed even during the interval.
266::CODE;;This clock, and all the clocks described after this have an option,
267::CODE;;:attr:`ClockBaseInterruptBehavior.interupt_next_only`. When True, any of the
268::CODE;;behavior new behavior will only apply to the callbacks with a timeout of
269::CODE;;zero. Non-zero timeouts will behave like in the default clock. E.g. for this
270::CODE;;clock when True, only zero timeouts will execute during the interval.
271::CODE;;In a test using a fps of 30, a callback with a timeout of 0, 0.001, and 0.05,
272::CODE;;resulted in a mean callback delay of 0.00013, 0.00013, and 0.04120 seconds,
273::CODE;;respectively when :attr:`ClockBaseInterruptBehavior.interupt_next_only` was
274::CODE;;False. Also, compared to the default clock the standard deviation was reduced.
275::CODE;;When :attr:`ClockBaseInterruptBehavior.interupt_next_only` was True, the values
276::CODE;;were 0.00010, 0.02414, and 0.05034, respectively.
277::CODE;;Free Clock
278::CODE;;^^^^^^^^^^^
279::CODE;;The interruptible clock may not be ideal for all cases because all the events
280::CODE;;are executed during the intervals and events are not executed anymore
281::CODE;;rhythmically as multiples of the fps. For example, there may not be any benefit
282::CODE;;for the graphics to update in a sub-interval, so the additional accuracy
283::CODE;;wastes CPU.
284::CODE;;The Free clock (``free_all``) solves this by having ``Clock.xxx_free`` versions
285::CODE;;of all the Clock scheduling methods. By free, we mean the event is free from
286::CODE;;the fps because it's not fps limited. E.g.
287::CODE;;:meth:`CyClockBaseFree.create_trigger_free` corresponds to
288::CODE;;:meth:`CyClockBase.create_trigger`. Only when an event scheduled using the
289::CODE;;``Clock.xxx_free`` methods is present will the clock interrupt and execute
290::CODE;;the events during the interval. So, if no ``free`` event is present the clock
291::CODE;;behaves like the ``default`` clock, otherwise it behaves like the ``interrupt``
292::CODE;;clock.
293::CODE;;In a test using a fps of 30, a callback with a timeout of 0s, 0.001s, and
294::CODE;;0.05s, resulted in a mean callback delay of 0.00012s, 0.00017s, and 0.04121s
295::CODE;;seconds, respectively when it was a free event and 0.02403s, 0.02405s, and
296::CODE;;0.04829s, respectively when it wasn't.
297::CODE;;Free Only Clock
298::CODE;;^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
299::CODE;;The Free clock executes all events when a free event was scheduled. This
300::CODE;;results in normal events also being execute in the middle of the interval
301::CODE;;when a free event is scheduled. For example, above, when a free event was
302::CODE;;absent, a normal event with a 0.001s timeout was delayed for 0.02405s. However,
303::CODE;;if a free event happened to be also scheduled, the normal event was only
304::CODE;;delayed 0.00014s, which may be undesirable.
305::CODE;;The Free only clock (``free_only``) solves it by only executing free events
306::CODE;;during the interval and normal events are always executed like with the
307::CODE;;default clock. For example, in the presence of a free event, a normal event
308::CODE;;with a timeout of 0.001s still had a delay of 0.02406. So this clock,
309::CODE;;treats free and normal events independently, with normal events always being
310::CODE;;fps limited, but never the free events.
311::CODE;;Summary
312::CODE;;^^^^^^^^
313::CODE;;The kivy clock type to use can be set with the ``kivy_clock`` option the
314::CODE;;:mod:`~kivy.config`. If ``KIVY_CLOCK`` is present in the environment it
315::CODE;;overwrites the config selection. Its possible values are as follows:
316::CODE;;* When ``kivy_clock`` is ``default``, the normal clock, :class:`ClockBase`,
317::CODE;;which limits callbacks to the maxfps quantization - is used.
318::CODE;;* When ``kivy_clock`` is ``interrupt``, a interruptible clock,
319::CODE;;:class:`ClockBaseInterrupt`, which doesn't limit any callbacks to the
320::CODE;;maxfps - is used. Callbacks will be executed at any time.
321::CODE;;* When ``kivy_clock`` is ``free_all``, a interruptible clock,
322::CODE;;:class:`ClockBaseFreeInterruptAll`, which doesn't limit any callbacks to the
323::CODE;;maxfps in the presence of free events, but in their absence it limits events
324::CODE;;to the fps quantization interval - is used.
325::CODE;;* When ``kivy_clock`` is ``free_only``, a interruptible clock,
326::CODE;;:class:`ClockBaseFreeInterruptAll`, which treats free and normal events
327::CODE;;independently; normal events are fps limited while free events are not - is
328::CODE;;used.
329::CODE;;Async clock support
330::CODE;;-------------------
331::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 2.0.0
332::CODE;;Experimental async support has been added in 2.0.0. The Clock now has a
333::CODE;;:meth:`ClockBaseBehavior.async_tick` and :meth:`ClockBaseBehavior.async_idle`
334::CODE;;coroutine method which is used by the kivy EventLoop when the kivy EventLoop is
335::CODE;;executed in a asynchronous manner. When used, the kivy clock does not
336::CODE;;block while idling.
337::CODE;;The async library to use is selected with the `KIVY_EVENTLOOP` environmental
338::CODE;;variable or by calling :meth:`~kivy.clock.ClockBaseBehavior.init_async_lib`
339::CODE;;directly. The library can be one of `"asyncio"` when the standard library
340::CODE;;`asyncio` should be used, or `"trio"` if the trio library
341::CODE;;should be used. If not set it defaults to `"asyncio"`.
342::CODE;;See :mod:`~kivy.app` for example usage.
343::CODE;;'''

870::CODE;;def triggered(timeout=0, interval=False):
871::CODE;;'''Decorator that will trigger the call of the function at the specified
872::CODE;;timeout, through the method :meth:`CyClockBase.create_trigger`. Subsequent
873::CODE;;calls to the decorated function (while the timeout is active) are ignored.
874::CODE;;It can be helpful when an expensive function (i.e. call to a server) can be
875::CODE;;triggered by different methods. Setting a proper timeout will delay the
876::CODE;;calling and only one of them will be triggered.
877::CODE;;@triggered(timeout, interval=False)
878::CODE;;def callback(id):
879::CODE;;print('The callback has been called with id=%d' % id)
880::CODE;;>> callback(id=1)
881::CODE;;>> callback(id=2)
882::CODE;;The callback has been called with id=2
883::CODE;;The decorated callback can also be unscheduled using:
884::CODE;;>> callback.cancel()

886::CODE;;'''

889::CODE;;fun = timeout
