1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Configuration object
3::CODE;;====================
4::CODE;;The :class:`Config` object is an instance of a modified Python ConfigParser.
5::CODE;;See the `ConfigParser documentation
6::CODE;;<http://docs.python.org/library/configparser.html>`_ for more information.
7::CODE;;Kivy has a configuration file which determines the default settings. In
8::CODE;;order to change these settings, you can alter this file manually or use
9::CODE;;the Config object. Please see the :ref:`Configure Kivy` section for more
10::CODE;;information.
11::CODE;;Applying configurations
12::CODE;;-----------------------
13::CODE;;Configuration options control the initialization of the :class:`~kivy.app.App`.
14::CODE;;In order to avoid situations where the config settings do not work or are not
15::CODE;;applied before window creation (like setting an initial window size),
16::CODE;;:meth:`Config.set <kivy.config.ConfigParser.set>` should be used before
17::CODE;;importing any other Kivy modules. Ideally, this means setting them right at
18::CODE;;the start of your main.py script.
19::CODE;;Alternatively, you can save these settings permanently using
20::CODE;;:meth:`Config.set <ConfigParser.set>` then
21::CODE;;:meth:`Config.write <ConfigParser.write>`. In this case, you will need to
22::CODE;;restart the app for the changes to take effect. Note that this approach will
23::CODE;;effect all Kivy apps system wide.
24::CODE;;Please note that no underscores (`_`) are allowed in the section name.
25::CODE;;Usage of the Config object
26::CODE;;--------------------------
27::CODE;;To read a configuration token from a particular section::
28::CODE;;>>> from kivy.config import Config
29::CODE;;>>> Config.getint('kivy', 'show_fps')
30::CODE;;0
31::CODE;;Change the configuration and save it::
32::CODE;;>>> Config.set('postproc', 'retain_time', '50')
33::CODE;;>>> Config.write()
34::CODE;;For information on configuring your :class:`~kivy.app.App`, please see the
35::CODE;;:ref:`Application configuration` section.
36::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.7.1
37::CODE;;The ConfigParser should work correctly with utf-8 now. The values are
38::CODE;;converted from ascii to unicode only when needed. The method get() returns
39::CODE;;utf-8 strings.
40::CODE;;Changing configuration with environment variables
41::CODE;;-------------------------------------------------
42::CODE;;Since 1.11.0, it is now possible to change the configuration using
43::CODE;;environment variables. They take precedence on the loaded config.ini.
44::CODE;;The format is::
45::CODE;;KCFG_<section>_<key> = <value>
46::CODE;;For example:
47::CODE;;KCFG_GRAPHICS_FULLSCREEN=auto ...
48::CODE;;KCFG_KIVY_LOG_LEVEL=warning ...
49::CODE;;Or in your file before any kivy import:
50::CODE;;import os
51::CODE;;os.environ["KCFG_KIVY_LOG_LEVEL"] = "warning"
52::CODE;;If you don't want to map any environment variables, you can disable
53::CODE;;the behavior::
54::CODE;;os.environ["KIVY_NO_ENV_CONFIG"] = "1"
55::CODE;;.. _configuration-tokens:
56::CODE;;Available configuration tokens
57::CODE;;------------------------------
58::CODE;;.. |log_levels| replace::
59::CODE;;'trace', 'debug', 'info', 'warning', 'error' or 'critical'
60::CODE;;:kivy:
61::CODE;;`default_font`: list
62::CODE;;Default fonts used for widgets displaying any text. It defaults to
63::CODE;;['Roboto', 'data/fonts/Roboto-Regular.ttf',
64::CODE;;'data/fonts/Roboto-Italic.ttf', 'data/fonts/Roboto-Bold.ttf',
65::CODE;;'data/fonts/Roboto-BoldItalic.ttf'].
66::CODE;;`desktop`: int, 0 or 1
67::CODE;;This option controls desktop OS specific features, such as enabling
68::CODE;;drag-able scroll-bar in scroll views, disabling of bubbles in
69::CODE;;TextInput etc. 0 is disabled, 1 is enabled.
70::CODE;;`exit_on_escape`: int, 0 or 1
71::CODE;;Enables exiting kivy when escape is pressed.
72::CODE;;0 is disabled, 1 is enabled.
73::CODE;;`pause_on_minimize`: int, 0 or 1
74::CODE;;If set to `1`, the main loop is paused and the `on_pause` event
75::CODE;;is dispatched when the window is minimized. This option is intended
76::CODE;;for desktop use only. Defaults to `0`.
77::CODE;;`keyboard_layout`: string
78::CODE;;Identifier of the layout to use.
79::CODE;;`keyboard_mode`: string
80::CODE;;Specifies the keyboard mode to use. If can be one of the following:
81::CODE;;* '' - Let Kivy choose the best option for your current platform.
82::CODE;;* 'system' - real keyboard.
83::CODE;;* 'dock' - one virtual keyboard docked to a screen side.
84::CODE;;* 'multi' - one virtual keyboard for every widget request.
85::CODE;;* 'systemanddock' - virtual docked keyboard plus input from real
86::CODE;;keyboard.
87::CODE;;* 'systemandmulti' - analogous.
88::CODE;;`kivy_clock`: one of `default`, `interrupt`, `free_all`, `free_only`
89::CODE;;The clock type to use with kivy. See :mod:`kivy.clock`.
90::CODE;;`log_dir`: string
91::CODE;;Path of log directory.
92::CODE;;`log_enable`: int, 0 or 1
93::CODE;;Activate file logging. 0 is disabled, 1 is enabled.
94::CODE;;.. note::
95::CODE;;Logging output can also be controlled by the environment variables
96::CODE;;``KIVY_LOG_MODE``, ``KIVY_NO_FILELOG`` and ``KIVY_NO_CONSOLELOG``.
97::CODE;;More information is provided in the :mod:`kivy.logger` module.
98::CODE;;`log_level`: string, one of |log_levels|
99::CODE;;Set the minimum log level to use.
100::CODE;;`log_name`: string
101::CODE;;Format string to use for the filename of log file.
102::CODE;;`log_maxfiles`: int
103::CODE;;Keep log_maxfiles recent logfiles while purging the log directory. Set
104::CODE;;'log_maxfiles' to -1 to disable logfile purging (eg keep all logfiles).
105::CODE;;.. note::
106::CODE;;You end up with 'log_maxfiles + 1' logfiles because the logger
107::CODE;;adds a new one after purging.
108::CODE;;`window_icon`: string
109::CODE;;Path of the window icon. Use this if you want to replace the default
110::CODE;;icon.
111::CODE;;`window_shape`: str (default: '')
112::CODE;;Specifies the default path to an image file that defines the window shape.
113::CODE;;To change the window shape after initialization, use the
114::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.core.window.WindowBase.shape_image` attribute.
115::CODE;;.. warning::
116::CODE;;This option takes effect only if the `shaped` setting in the `[graphics]`
117::CODE;;configuration section is set to `1`.
118::CODE;;.. warning::
119::CODE;;The image file must meet the requirements outlined in
120::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.core.window.WindowBase.shape_image`.
121::CODE;;:postproc:
122::CODE;;`double_tap_distance`: float
123::CODE;;Maximum distance allowed for a double tap, normalized inside the range
124::CODE;;0 - 1000.
125::CODE;;`double_tap_time`: int
126::CODE;;Time allowed for the detection of double tap, in milliseconds.
127::CODE;;`ignore`: list of tuples
128::CODE;;List of regions where new touches are ignored.
129::CODE;;This configuration token can be used to resolve hotspot problems
130::CODE;;with DIY hardware. The format of the list must be::
131::CODE;;ignore = [(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax), ...]
132::CODE;;All the values must be inside the range 0 - 1.
133::CODE;;`jitter_distance`: int
134::CODE;;Maximum distance for jitter detection, normalized inside the range 0
135::CODE;;- 1000.
136::CODE;;`jitter_ignore_devices`: string, separated with commas
137::CODE;;List of devices to ignore from jitter detection.
138::CODE;;`retain_distance`: int
139::CODE;;If the touch moves more than is indicated by retain_distance, it will
140::CODE;;not be retained. Argument should be an int between 0 and 1000.
141::CODE;;`retain_time`: int
142::CODE;;Time allowed for a retain touch, in milliseconds.
143::CODE;;`triple_tap_distance`: float
144::CODE;;Maximum distance allowed for a triple tap, normalized inside the range
145::CODE;;0 - 1000.
146::CODE;;`triple_tap_time`: int
147::CODE;;Time allowed for the detection of triple tap, in milliseconds.
148::CODE;;:graphics:
149::CODE;;`borderless`: int, one of 0 or 1
150::CODE;;If set to `1`, removes the window border/decoration. Window resizing
151::CODE;;must also be disabled to hide the resizing border.
152::CODE;;`custom_titlebar`: int, one of 0 or 1
153::CODE;;If set to `1`, removes the window border and allows user to set a Widget
154::CODE;;as a titlebar
155::CODE;;see :meth:`~kivy.core.window.WindowBase.set_custom_titlebar`
156::CODE;;for detailed usage
157::CODE;;`custom_titlebar_border`: int, defaults to 5
158::CODE;;sets the how many pixles off the border should be used as the
159::CODE;;rezising frame
160::CODE;;`window_state`: string , one of 'visible', 'hidden', 'maximized'
161::CODE;;or 'minimized'
162::CODE;;Sets the window state, defaults to 'visible'. This option is available
163::CODE;;only for the SDL3 window provider and it should be used on desktop
164::CODE;;OSes.
165::CODE;;`fbo`: string, one of 'hardware', 'software' or 'force-hardware'
166::CODE;;Selects the FBO backend to use.
167::CODE;;`fullscreen`: int or string, one of 0, 1, 'fake' or 'auto'
168::CODE;;Activate fullscreen. If set to `1`, a resolution of `width`
169::CODE;;times `height` pixels will be used.
170::CODE;;If set to `auto`, your current display's resolution will be
171::CODE;;used instead. This is most likely what you want.
172::CODE;;If you want to place the window in another display,
173::CODE;;use `fake`, or set the `borderless` option from the graphics section,
174::CODE;;then adjust `width`, `height`, `top` and `left`.
175::CODE;;`height`: int
176::CODE;;Height of the :class:`~kivy.core.window.Window`, not used if
177::CODE;;`fullscreen` is set to `auto`.
178::CODE;;`left`: int
179::CODE;;Left position of the :class:`~kivy.core.window.Window`.
180::CODE;;`maxfps`: int, defaults to 60
181::CODE;;Maximum FPS allowed.
182::CODE;;.. warning::
183::CODE;;Setting maxfps to 0 will lead to max CPU usage.
184::CODE;;'multisamples': int, defaults to 2
185::CODE;;Sets the `MultiSample Anti-Aliasing (MSAA)
186::CODE;;<http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multisample_anti-aliasing>`_ level.
187::CODE;;Increasing this value results in smoother graphics but at the cost of
188::CODE;;processing time.
189::CODE;;.. note::
190::CODE;;This feature is limited by device hardware support and will have no
191::CODE;;effect on devices which do not support the level of MSAA requested.
192::CODE;;`position`: string, one of 'auto' or 'custom'
193::CODE;;Position of the window on your display. If `auto` is used, you have no
194::CODE;;control of the initial position: `top` and `left` are ignored.
195::CODE;;`show_cursor`: int, one of 0 or 1
196::CODE;;Set whether or not the cursor is shown on the window.
197::CODE;;`top`: int
198::CODE;;Top position of the :class:`~kivy.core.window.Window`.
199::CODE;;`resizable`: int, one of 0 or 1
200::CODE;;If 0, the window will have a fixed size. If 1, the window will be
201::CODE;;resizable.
202::CODE;;`rotation`: int, one of 0, 90, 180 or 270
203::CODE;;Rotation of the :class:`~kivy.core.window.Window`.
204::CODE;;`width`: int

206::CODE;;`fullscreen` is set to `auto`.

210::CODE;;Minimum height to restrict the window to. (sdl3 only)
211::CODE;;`min_state_time`: float, defaults to .035
212::CODE;;Minimum time for widgets to display a given visual state.
213::CODE;;This attrib is currently used by widgets like
214::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.dropdown.DropDown` &
215::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.buttonbehavior.ButtonBehavior` to
216::CODE;;make sure they display their current visual state for the given
217::CODE;;time.

219::CODE;;When enabled, the window will be brought to the front and will keep
220::CODE;;the window above the rest. Only works for the sdl3 window provider.
221::CODE;;``0`` is disabled, ``1`` is enabled.
222::CODE;;`show_taskbar_icon`: int, one of ``0`` or ``1``, defaults to ``1``
223::CODE;;Determines whether the app's icon will be added to the taskbar. Only
224::CODE;;applicable for the SDL3 window provider.
225::CODE;;``0`` means the icon will not be shown in the taskbar and ``1`` means
226::CODE;;it will.
227::CODE;;`allow_screensaver`: int, one of 0 or 1, defaults to 1
228::CODE;;Allow the device to show a screen saver, or to go to sleep
229::CODE;;on mobile devices. Only works for the sdl3 window provider.
230::CODE;;`vsync`: `none`, empty value, or integers
231::CODE;;Whether vsync is enabled, currently only used with sdl3 window.
232::CODE;;Possible values are `none` or empty value -- leaves it unchanged,
233::CODE;;``0`` -- disables vsync, ``1`` or larger -- sets vsync interval,
234::CODE;;``-1`` sets adaptive vsync. It falls back to 1 if setting to ``2+``
235::CODE;;or ``-1`` failed. See ``SDL_GL_SetSwapInterval``.
236::CODE;;`verify_gl_main_thread`: int, 1 or 0, defaults to 1

239::CODE;;`shaped`: int, 0 or 1 (default: 0)
240::CODE;;If set to `1`, the system will attempt to initialize the window as shapable.
241::CODE;;However, whether the window is actually shapable depends on the
242::CODE;;platform and implementation. To check if shaping is supported, inspect
243::CODE;;the window object's `shapable` property.
244::CODE;;.. warning::

246::CODE;;`Window.clearcolor` to `(0, 0, 0, 0)`.
247::CODE;;`alpha_size: int (default: 0 on the Raspberry Pi and 8 on all other platforms)
248::CODE;;Specifies the minimum number of bits for the alpha channel of the color buffer.
249::CODE;;Set this to 0, so SDL3 works without X11.
250::CODE;;Only applicable for the SDL3 window provider.
251::CODE;;:input:

256::CODE;;default = tuio,127.0.0.1:3333

356::CODE;;'''The default Kivy configuration object. This is a :class:`ConfigParser`
357::CODE;;instance with the :attr:`~kivy.config.ConfigParser.name` set to 'kivy'.
358::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
359::CODE;;Config = ConfigParser(name='kivy')
360::CODE;;'''
361::CODE;;class ConfigParser(PythonConfigParser, object):
362::CODE;;'''Enhanced ConfigParser class that supports the addition of default
363::CODE;;sections and default values.
364::CODE;;By default, the kivy ConfigParser instance, :attr:`~kivy.config.Config`,
365::CODE;;is named `'kivy'` and the ConfigParser instance used by the
366::CODE;;:meth:`App.build_settings <~kivy.app.App.build_settings>` method is named
367::CODE;;`'app'`.
368::CODE;;:Parameters:
369::CODE;;`name`: string
370::CODE;;The name of the instance. See :attr:`name`. Defaults to `''`.
371::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.9.0
372::CODE;;Each ConfigParser can now be :attr:`named <name>`. You can get the
373::CODE;;ConfigParser associated with a name using :meth:`get_configparser`.
374::CODE;;In addition, you can now control the config values with
375::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.properties.ConfigParserProperty`.
376::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.7
377::CODE;;'''
378::CODE;;def __init__(self, name='', **kwargs):
379::CODE;;PythonConfigParser.__init__(self, **kwargs)
380::CODE;;self._sections = OrderedDict()
381::CODE;;self.filename = None
382::CODE;;self._callbacks = []
383::CODE;;self.name = name
384::CODE;;def add_callback(self, callback, section=None, key=None):
385::CODE;;'''Add a callback to be called when a specific section or key has
386::CODE;;changed. If you don't specify a section or key, it will call the
387::CODE;;callback for all section/key changes.
388::CODE;;Callbacks will receive 3 arguments: the section, key and value.
389::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.4.1
390::CODE;;'''
391::CODE;;if section is None and key is not None:
392::CODE;;raise Exception('You cannot specify a key without a section')
393::CODE;;self._callbacks.append((callback, section, key))
394::CODE;;def remove_callback(self, callback, section=None, key=None):
395::CODE;;'''Removes a callback added with :meth:`add_callback`.
396::CODE;;:meth:`remove_callback` must be called with the same parameters as
397::CODE;;:meth:`add_callback`.
398::CODE;;Raises a `ValueError` if not found.
399::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.9.0
400::CODE;;'''
401::CODE;;self._callbacks.remove((callback, section, key))
402::CODE;;def _do_callbacks(self, section, key, value):
403::CODE;;for callback, csection, ckey in self._callbacks:
404::CODE;;if csection is not None and csection != section:
405::CODE;;continue
406::CODE;;elif ckey is not None and ckey != key:
407::CODE;;continue
408::CODE;;callback(section, key, value)
409::CODE;;def read(self, filename):
410::CODE;;'''Read only one filename. In contrast to the original ConfigParser of
411::CODE;;Python, this one is able to read only one file at a time. The last
412::CODE;;read file will be used for the :meth:`write` method.
413::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.9.0
414::CODE;;:meth:`read` now calls the callbacks if read changed any values.
415::CODE;;'''
416::CODE;;if not isinstance(filename, str):
417::CODE;;raise Exception('Only one filename is accepted (str)')
418::CODE;;self.filename = filename
428::CODE;;old_vals = {sect: {k: v for k, v in self.items(sect)} for sect in
429::CODE;;self.sections()}
430::CODE;;PythonConfigParser.read(self, filename, encoding="utf-8-sig")
432::CODE;;f = self._do_callbacks
433::CODE;;for section in self.sections():
435::CODE;;for k, v in self.items(section):
436::CODE;;f(section, k, v)
437::CODE;;continue
438::CODE;;old_keys = old_vals[section]
440::CODE;;if k not in old_keys or v != old_keys[k]:
441::CODE;;f(section, k, v)
442::CODE;;def set(self, section, option, value):
443::CODE;;'''Functions similarly to PythonConfigParser's set method, except that
444::CODE;;the value is implicitly converted to a string.
445::CODE;;'''
446::CODE;;e_value = value
447::CODE;;if not isinstance(value, str):
449::CODE;;e_value = str(value)
450::CODE;;ret = PythonConfigParser.set(self, section, option, e_value)
451::CODE;;self._do_callbacks(section, option, value)
452::CODE;;return ret
453::CODE;;def setall(self, section, keyvalues):
454::CODE;;'''Sets multiple key-value pairs in a section. keyvalues should be a
455::CODE;;dictionary containing the key-value pairs to be set.
456::CODE;;'''
457::CODE;;for key, value in keyvalues.items():
458::CODE;;self.set(section, key, value)
459::CODE;;def get(self, section, option, **kwargs):
460::CODE;;value = PythonConfigParser.get(self, section, option, **kwargs)
461::CODE;;return value
462::CODE;;def setdefaults(self, section, keyvalues):
463::CODE;;'''Set multiple key-value defaults in a section. keyvalues should be
464::CODE;;a dictionary containing the new key-value defaults.
465::CODE;;'''
466::CODE;;self.adddefaultsection(section)
467::CODE;;for key, value in keyvalues.items():
468::CODE;;self.setdefault(section, key, value)
469::CODE;;def setdefault(self, section, option, value):
470::CODE;;'''Set the default value for an option in the specified section.
471::CODE;;'''
472::CODE;;if self.has_option(section, option):
473::CODE;;return
474::CODE;;self.set(section, option, value)
475::CODE;;def getdefault(self, section, option, defaultvalue):
476::CODE;;'''Get the value of an option in the specified section. If not found,
477::CODE;;it will return the default value.
478::CODE;;'''
479::CODE;;if not self.has_section(section):
480::CODE;;return defaultvalue
481::CODE;;if not self.has_option(section, option):
482::CODE;;return defaultvalue
483::CODE;;return self.get(section, option)
484::CODE;;def getdefaultint(self, section, option, defaultvalue):
485::CODE;;'''Get the value of an option in the specified section. If not found,
486::CODE;;it will return the default value. The value will always be
487::CODE;;returned as an integer.
488::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.6.0
489::CODE;;'''
490::CODE;;return int(self.getdefault(section, option, defaultvalue))
491::CODE;;def adddefaultsection(self, section):
492::CODE;;'''Add a section if the section is missing.
493::CODE;;'''
494::CODE;;assert "_" not in section
495::CODE;;if self.has_section(section):
496::CODE;;return
497::CODE;;self.add_section(section)
498::CODE;;def write(self):
499::CODE;;'''Write the configuration to the last file opened using the
500::CODE;;:meth:`read` method.
501::CODE;;Return True if the write finished successfully, False otherwise.
502::CODE;;'''
503::CODE;;if self.filename is None:
504::CODE;;return False
505::CODE;;try:
506::CODE;;with open(self.filename, 'w', encoding="utf-8") as fd:
507::CODE;;PythonConfigParser.write(self, fd)
508::CODE;;except IOError:
509::CODE;;Logger.exception('Unable to write the config <%s>' % self.filename)
510::CODE;;return False
511::CODE;;return True
512::CODE;;def update_config(self, filename, overwrite=False):
513::CODE;;'''Upgrade the configuration based on a new default config file.
514::CODE;;Overwrite any existing values if overwrite is True.
515::CODE;;'''
516::CODE;;pcp = PythonConfigParser()
517::CODE;;pcp.read(filename)
518::CODE;;confset = self.setall if overwrite else self.setdefaults
519::CODE;;for section in pcp.sections():
520::CODE;;confset(section, dict(pcp.items(section)))
521::CODE;;self.write()
522::CODE;;@staticmethod
523::CODE;;def _register_named_property(name, widget_ref, *largs):
524::CODE;;''' Called by the ConfigParserProperty to register a property which
525::CODE;;was created with a config name instead of a config object.
526::CODE;;When a ConfigParser with this name is later created, the properties
527::CODE;;are then notified that this parser now exists so they can use it.
528::CODE;;If the parser already exists, the property is notified here. See
529::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.properties.ConfigParserProperty.set_config`.
530::CODE;;:Parameters:
531::CODE;;`name`: a non-empty string
532::CODE;;The name of the ConfigParser that is associated with the
533::CODE;;property. See :attr:`name`.
534::CODE;;`widget_ref`: 2-tuple.
535::CODE;;The first element is a reference to the widget containing the
536::CODE;;property, the second element is the name of the property. E.g.:
537::CODE;;class House(Widget):
538::CODE;;address = ConfigParserProperty('', 'info', 'street',
539::CODE;;'directory')
540::CODE;;Then, the first element is a ref to a House instance, and the
541::CODE;;second is `'address'`.
542::CODE;;'''
543::CODE;;configs = ConfigParser._named_configs
544::CODE;;try:
545::CODE;;config, props = configs[name]
546::CODE;;except KeyError:
547::CODE;;configs[name] = (None, [widget_ref])
548::CODE;;return
549::CODE;;props.append(widget_ref)
550::CODE;;if config:
551::CODE;;config = config()
552::CODE;;widget = widget_ref[0]()
554::CODE;;widget.property(widget_ref[1]).set_config(config)
555::CODE;;@staticmethod
556::CODE;;def get_configparser(name):
557::CODE;;'''Returns the :class:`ConfigParser` instance whose name is `name`, or
558::CODE;;None if not found.
559::CODE;;:Parameters:
560::CODE;;`name`: string
561::CODE;;The name of the :class:`ConfigParser` instance to return.
562::CODE;;'''
563::CODE;;try:
564::CODE;;config = ConfigParser._named_configs[name][0]
565::CODE;;if config is not None:
566::CODE;;config = config()
567::CODE;;if config is not None:
568::CODE;;return config
569::CODE;;del ConfigParser._named_configs[name]
570::CODE;;except KeyError:
571::CODE;;return None
574::CODE;;_named_configs = {}

580::CODE;;When a ConfigParser is given a name, that config object can be

586::CODE;;`ValueError`.

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Context
3::CODE;;=======
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.8.0
5::CODE;;.. warning::
6::CODE;;This is experimental and subject to change as long as this warning notice
7::CODE;;is present.
8::CODE;;Kivy has a few "global" instances that are used directly by many pieces of the
9::CODE;;framework: `Cache`, `Builder`, `Clock`.
10::CODE;;TODO: document this module.
11::CODE;;'''
12::CODE;;__all__ = ('Context', 'ProxyContext', 'register_context',
13::CODE;;'get_current_context')
14::CODE;;_contexts = {}
15::CODE;;_default_context = None
16::CODE;;_context_stack = []
17::CODE;;class ProxyContext(object):
18::CODE;;__slots__ = ['_obj']
19::CODE;;def __init__(self, obj):
20::CODE;;object.__init__(self)
21::CODE;;object.__setattr__(self, '_obj', obj)
22::CODE;;def __getattribute__(self, name):
23::CODE;;return getattr(object.__getattribute__(self, '_obj'), name)
24::CODE;;def __delattr__(self, name):
25::CODE;;delattr(object.__getattribute__(self, '_obj'), name)
26::CODE;;def __setattr__(self, name, value):
27::CODE;;setattr(object.__getattribute__(self, '_obj'), name, value)
28::CODE;;def __bool__(self):
29::CODE;;return bool(object.__getattribute__(self, '_obj'))
30::CODE;;def __str__(self):
31::CODE;;return str(object.__getattribute__(self, '_obj'))
32::CODE;;def __repr__(self):
33::CODE;;return repr(object.__getattribute__(self, '_obj'))
34::CODE;;class Context(dict):
35::CODE;;def __init__(self, init=False):
36::CODE;;dict.__init__(self)
37::CODE;;self.sandbox = None
38::CODE;;if not init:
39::CODE;;return
40::CODE;;for name, context in _contexts.items():
41::CODE;;self[name] = context['cls'](*context['args'], **context['kwargs'])
42::CODE;;def push(self):
43::CODE;;_context_stack.append(self)
44::CODE;;for name, instance in self.items():
45::CODE;;object.__setattr__(_contexts[name]['proxy'], '_obj', instance)
46::CODE;;def pop(self):
49::CODE;;_context_stack.pop(-1)
50::CODE;;for name, instance in get_current_context().items():
51::CODE;;object.__setattr__(_contexts[name]['proxy'], '_obj', instance)
52::CODE;;def register_context(name, cls, *args, **kwargs):
53::CODE;;'''Register a new context.
54::CODE;;'''
55::CODE;;instance = cls(*args, **kwargs)
56::CODE;;proxy = ProxyContext(instance)
57::CODE;;_contexts[name] = {
58::CODE;;'cls': cls,
59::CODE;;'args': args,
60::CODE;;'kwargs': kwargs,
61::CODE;;'proxy': proxy}
62::CODE;;_default_context[name] = instance
63::CODE;;return proxy
64::CODE;;def get_current_context():
65::CODE;;'''Return the current context.
66::CODE;;'''
67::CODE;;if not _context_stack:
68::CODE;;return _default_context
69::CODE;;return _context_stack[-1]
70::CODE;;_default_context = Context(init=False)
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Core Abstraction
3::CODE;;================
4::CODE;;This module defines the abstraction layers for our core providers and their
5::CODE;;implementations. For further information, please refer to
6::CODE;;:ref:`architecture` and the :ref:`providers` section of the documentation.
7::CODE;;In most cases, you shouldn't directly use a library that's already covered
8::CODE;;by the core abstraction. Always try to use our providers first.
9::CODE;;In case we are missing a feature or method, please let us know by
10::CODE;;opening a new Bug report instead of relying on your library.
11::CODE;;.. warning::
12::CODE;;These are **not** widgets! These are just abstractions of the respective
13::CODE;;functionality. For example, you cannot add a core image to your window.
14::CODE;;You have to use the image **widget** class instead. If you're really
15::CODE;;looking for widgets, please refer to :mod:`kivy.uix` instead.
16::CODE;;'''
17::CODE;;import os
18::CODE;;import sysconfig
19::CODE;;import sys
20::CODE;;import traceback
21::CODE;;import tempfile
22::CODE;;import subprocess
23::CODE;;import importlib
24::CODE;;import kivy
25::CODE;;from kivy.logger import Logger
26::CODE;;class CoreCriticalException(Exception):
27::CODE;;pass
28::CODE;;def core_select_lib(category, llist, create_instance=False,
29::CODE;;base='kivy.core', basemodule=None):
30::CODE;;if 'KIVY_DOC' in os.environ:
31::CODE;;return
32::CODE;;category = category.lower()
33::CODE;;basemodule = basemodule or category
34::CODE;;libs_ignored = []
35::CODE;;errs = []
36::CODE;;for option, modulename, classname in llist:
37::CODE;;try:
39::CODE;;try:
40::CODE;;if option not in kivy.kivy_options[category]:
41::CODE;;libs_ignored.append(modulename)
42::CODE;;Logger.debug(
43::CODE;;'{0}: Provider <{1}> ignored by config'.format(
44::CODE;;category.capitalize(), option))
45::CODE;;continue
46::CODE;;except KeyError:
47::CODE;;pass
49::CODE;;mod = importlib.__import__(name='{2}.{0}.{1}'.format(
50::CODE;;basemodule, modulename, base),
51::CODE;;globals=globals(),
52::CODE;;locals=locals(),
53::CODE;;fromlist=[modulename], level=0)
54::CODE;;cls = mod.__getattribute__(classname)
56::CODE;;Logger.info('{0}: Provider: {1}{2}'.format(
57::CODE;;category.capitalize(), option,
58::CODE;;'({0} ignored)'.format(libs_ignored) if libs_ignored else ''))
59::CODE;;if create_instance:
60::CODE;;cls = cls()
61::CODE;;return cls
62::CODE;;except ImportError as e:
63::CODE;;errs.append((option, e, sys.exc_info()[2]))
64::CODE;;libs_ignored.append(modulename)
65::CODE;;Logger.debug('{0}: Ignored <{1}> (import error)'.format(
66::CODE;;category.capitalize(), option))
67::CODE;;Logger.trace('', exc_info=e)
68::CODE;;except CoreCriticalException as e:
69::CODE;;errs.append((option, e, sys.exc_info()[2]))
70::CODE;;Logger.error('{0}: Unable to use {1}'.format(
71::CODE;;category.capitalize(), option))
72::CODE;;Logger.error(
73::CODE;;'{0}: The module raised an important error: {1!r}'.format(
74::CODE;;category.capitalize(), e.message))
75::CODE;;raise
76::CODE;;except Exception as e:
77::CODE;;errs.append((option, e, sys.exc_info()[2]))
78::CODE;;libs_ignored.append(modulename)
79::CODE;;Logger.trace('{0}: Unable to use {1}'.format(
80::CODE;;category.capitalize(), option))
81::CODE;;Logger.trace('', exc_info=e)
82::CODE;;err = '\n'.join(['{} - {}: {}\n{}'.format(opt, e.__class__.__name__, e,
83::CODE;;''.join(traceback.format_tb(tb))) for opt, e, tb in errs])
84::CODE;;Logger.critical(
85::CODE;;'{0}: Unable to find any valuable {0} provider. Please enable '
86::CODE;;'debug logging (e.g. add -d if running from the command line, or '
87::CODE;;'change the log level in the config) and re-run your app to '
88::CODE;;'identify potential causes\n{1}'.format(category.capitalize(), err))
89::CODE;;def core_register_libs(category, libs, base='kivy.core'):
90::CODE;;if 'KIVY_DOC' in os.environ:
91::CODE;;return
92::CODE;;category = category.lower()
93::CODE;;kivy_options = kivy.kivy_options[category]
94::CODE;;libs_loadable = {}
95::CODE;;libs_ignored = []
96::CODE;;for option, lib in libs:
98::CODE;;if option not in kivy_options:
99::CODE;;Logger.debug('{0}: option <{1}> ignored by config'.format(
100::CODE;;category.capitalize(), option))
101::CODE;;libs_ignored.append(lib)
102::CODE;;continue
103::CODE;;libs_loadable[option] = lib
104::CODE;;libs_loaded = []
105::CODE;;for item in kivy_options:
106::CODE;;try:
108::CODE;;try:
109::CODE;;lib = libs_loadable[item]
110::CODE;;except KeyError:
111::CODE;;continue
112::CODE;;importlib.__import__(name='{2}.{0}.{1}'.format(category, lib, base),
113::CODE;;globals=globals(),
114::CODE;;locals=locals(),
115::CODE;;fromlist=[lib],
116::CODE;;level=0)
117::CODE;;libs_loaded.append(lib)
118::CODE;;except Exception as e:
119::CODE;;Logger.trace('{0}: Unable to use <{1}> as loader!'.format(
120::CODE;;category.capitalize(), option))
121::CODE;;Logger.trace('', exc_info=e)
122::CODE;;libs_ignored.append(lib)
123::CODE;;Logger.info('{0}: Providers: {1} {2}'.format(
124::CODE;;category.capitalize(),
125::CODE;;', '.join(libs_loaded),
126::CODE;;'({0} ignored)'.format(
127::CODE;;', '.join(libs_ignored)) if libs_ignored else ''))
128::CODE;;return libs_loaded
129::CODE;;def handle_win_lib_import_error(category, provider, mod_name):
130::CODE;;if sys.platform != 'win32':
131::CODE;;return
132::CODE;;assert mod_name.startswith('kivy.')
133::CODE;;kivy_root = os.path.dirname(kivy.__file__)
134::CODE;;dirs = mod_name[5:].split('.')
135::CODE;;mod_path = os.path.join(kivy_root, *dirs)
140::CODE;;mod_path += '._d'
141::CODE;;mod_path += '.cp{}{}-{}.pyd'.format(
142::CODE;;sys.version_info.major, sys.version_info.minor,
143::CODE;;sysconfig.get_platform().replace('-', '_'))
145::CODE;;if not os.path.exists(mod_path):
146::CODE;;Logger.debug(
147::CODE;;'{}: Failed trying to import "{}" for provider {}. Compiled file '
148::CODE;;'does not exist. Have you perhaps forgotten to compile Kivy, or '
149::CODE;;'did not install all required dependencies?'.format(
150::CODE;;category, provider, mod_path))
151::CODE;;return
153::CODE;;env_var = 'KIVY_{}_DEPENDENCY_WALKER'.format(provider.upper())
154::CODE;;if env_var not in os.environ:
155::CODE;;Logger.debug(
156::CODE;;'{0}: Failed trying to import the "{1}" provider from "{2}". '
157::CODE;;'This error is often encountered when a dependency is missing,'
158::CODE;;' or if there are multiple copies of the same dependency dll on '

160::CODE;;'This can occur if you are mixing installations (such as different'
161::CODE;;' python installations, like anaconda python and a system python) '
162::CODE;;'or if another unrelated program added its directory to the PATH. '
163::CODE;;'Please examine your PATH and python installation for potential '
164::CODE;;'issues. To further troubleshoot a "DLL load failed" error, '
165::CODE;;'please download '
166::CODE;;'"Dependency Walker" (64 or 32 bit version - matching your python '
167::CODE;;'bitness) from dependencywalker.com and set the environment '
168::CODE;;'variable {3} to the full path of the downloaded depends.exe file '
169::CODE;;'and rerun your application to generate an error report'.
170::CODE;;format(category, provider, mod_path, env_var))
171::CODE;;return
172::CODE;;depends_bin = os.environ[env_var]
173::CODE;;if not os.path.exists(depends_bin):
174::CODE;;raise ValueError('"{}" provided in {} does not exist'.format(
175::CODE;;depends_bin, env_var))
177::CODE;;fd, temp_file = tempfile.mkstemp(
178::CODE;;suffix='.dwi', prefix='kivy_depends_{}_log_'.format(provider),
179::CODE;;dir=os.path.expanduser('~/'))
180::CODE;;os.close(fd)
181::CODE;;Logger.info(
182::CODE;;'{}: Running dependency walker "{}" on "{}" to generate '
183::CODE;;'troubleshooting log. Please wait for it to complete'.format(
184::CODE;;category, depends_bin, mod_path))
185::CODE;;Logger.debug(
186::CODE;;'{}: Dependency walker command is "{}"'.format(
187::CODE;;category,
188::CODE;;[depends_bin, '/c', '/od:{}'.format(temp_file), mod_path]))
189::CODE;;try:
190::CODE;;subprocess.check_output([
191::CODE;;depends_bin, '/c', '/od:{}'.format(temp_file), mod_path])
192::CODE;;except subprocess.CalledProcessError as exc:
193::CODE;;if exc.returncode >= 0x00010000:
194::CODE;;Logger.error(
195::CODE;;'{}: Dependency walker failed with error code "{}". No '
196::CODE;;'error report was generated'.
197::CODE;;format(category, exc.returncode))
198::CODE;;return
199::CODE;;Logger.info(
200::CODE;;'{}: dependency walker generated "{}" containing troubleshooting '
201::CODE;;'information about provider {} and its failing file "{} ({})". You '
202::CODE;;'can open the file in dependency walker to view any potential issues '
203::CODE;;'and troubleshoot it yourself. '
204::CODE;;'To share the file with the Kivy developers and request support, '
205::CODE;;'please contact us at our support channels '
206::CODE;;'https://kivy.org/doc/master/contact.html (not on github, unless '
207::CODE;;'it\'s truly a bug). Make sure to provide the generated file as well '
208::CODE;;'as the *complete* Kivy log being printed here. Keep in mind the '
209::CODE;;'generated dependency walker log file contains paths to dlls on your '
210::CODE;;'system used by kivy or its dependencies to help troubleshoot them, '
211::CODE;;'and these paths may include your name in them. Please view the '
212::CODE;;'log file in dependency walker before sharing to ensure you are not '
213::CODE;;'sharing sensitive paths'.format(
214::CODE;;category, temp_file, provider, mod_name, mod_path))
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Audio Output
3::CODE;;=====
4::CODE;;Load an audio sound and play it with::
5::CODE;;from kivy.core.audio_output import SoundLoader
6::CODE;;sound = SoundLoader.load('mytest.wav')
7::CODE;;if sound:
8::CODE;;print("Sound found at %s" % sound.source)
9::CODE;;print("Sound is %.3f seconds" % sound.length)
10::CODE;;sound.play()
11::CODE;;You should not use the Sound class directly. The class returned by
12::CODE;;:func:`SoundLoader.load` will be the best sound provider for that particular
13::CODE;;file type, so it might return different Sound classes depending the file type.
14::CODE;;Event dispatching and state changes
15::CODE;;-----------------------------------
16::CODE;;Audio is often processed in parallel to your code. This means you often need to
17::CODE;;enter the Kivy :func:`eventloop <kivy.base.EventLoopBase>` in order to allow
18::CODE;;events and state changes to be dispatched correctly.
19::CODE;;You seldom need to worry about this as Kivy apps typically always
20::CODE;;require this event loop for the GUI to remain responsive, but it is good to
21::CODE;;keep this in mind when debugging or running in a
22::CODE;;`REPL <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Read%E2%80%93eval%E2%80%93print_loop>`_
23::CODE;;(Read-eval-print loop).
24::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.10.0
25::CODE;;The pygst and gi providers have been removed.
26::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.8.0
27::CODE;;There are now 2 distinct Gstreamer implementations: one using Gi/Gst
28::CODE;;working for both Python 2+3 with Gstreamer 1.0, and one using PyGST
29::CODE;;working only for Python 2 + Gstreamer 0.10.
30::CODE;;.. note::
31::CODE;;The core audio library does not support recording audio. If you require
32::CODE;;this functionality, please refer to the
33::CODE;;`audiostream <https://github.com/kivy/audiostream>`_ extension.
34::CODE;;'''
35::CODE;;__all__ = ('Sound', 'SoundLoader')
36::CODE;;from kivy.logger import Logger
37::CODE;;from kivy.event import EventDispatcher
38::CODE;;from kivy.core import core_register_libs
39::CODE;;from kivy.resources import resource_find
40::CODE;;from kivy.properties import StringProperty, NumericProperty, OptionProperty, \
41::CODE;;AliasProperty, BooleanProperty, BoundedNumericProperty
42::CODE;;from kivy.utils import platform
43::CODE;;from kivy.setupconfig import USE_SDL3
44::CODE;;from sys import float_info
45::CODE;;class SoundLoader:
46::CODE;;'''Load a sound, using the best loader for the given file type.
47::CODE;;'''
48::CODE;;_classes = []
49::CODE;;@staticmethod
50::CODE;;def register(classobj):
51::CODE;;'''Register a new class to load the sound.'''
52::CODE;;Logger.debug('Audio: register %s' % classobj.__name__)
53::CODE;;SoundLoader._classes.append(classobj)
54::CODE;;@staticmethod
55::CODE;;def load(filename) -> "Sound":
56::CODE;;'''Load a sound, and return a Sound() instance.'''
57::CODE;;rfn = resource_find(filename)
58::CODE;;if rfn is not None:
59::CODE;;filename = rfn
60::CODE;;ext = filename.split('.')[-1].lower()
61::CODE;;if '?' in ext:
62::CODE;;ext = ext.split('?')[0]
63::CODE;;for classobj in SoundLoader._classes:
64::CODE;;if ext in classobj.extensions():
65::CODE;;return classobj(source=filename)
66::CODE;;Logger.warning('Audio: Unable to find a loader for <%s>' %
67::CODE;;filename)
68::CODE;;return None
69::CODE;;class Sound(EventDispatcher):
70::CODE;;'''Represents a sound to play. This class is abstract, and cannot be used
71::CODE;;directly.
72::CODE;;Use SoundLoader to load a sound.
73::CODE;;:Events:
74::CODE;;`on_play`: None
75::CODE;;Fired when the sound is played.
76::CODE;;`on_stop`: None
77::CODE;;Fired when the sound is stopped.
78::CODE;;'''
79::CODE;;source = StringProperty(None)
80::CODE;;'''Filename / source of your audio file.
81::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.3.0
82::CODE;;:attr:`source` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.StringProperty` that defaults
83::CODE;;to None and is read-only. Use the :meth:`SoundLoader.load` for loading
84::CODE;;audio.
85::CODE;;'''
86::CODE;;volume = NumericProperty(1.)
87::CODE;;'''Volume, in the range 0-1. 1 means full volume, 0 means mute.
88::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.3.0
89::CODE;;:attr:`volume` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and defaults
90::CODE;;to 1.
91::CODE;;'''
92::CODE;;pitch = BoundedNumericProperty(1., min=float_info.epsilon)
93::CODE;;'''Pitch of a sound. 2 is an octave higher, .5 one below. This is only
94::CODE;;implemented for SDL3 audio provider yet.
95::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.10.0
96::CODE;;:attr:`pitch` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and defaults
97::CODE;;to 1.
98::CODE;;'''
99::CODE;;state = OptionProperty('stop', options=('stop', 'play'))
100::CODE;;'''State of the sound, one of 'stop' or 'play'.
101::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.3.0
102::CODE;;:attr:`state` is a read-only :class:`~kivy.properties.OptionProperty`.'''
103::CODE;;loop = BooleanProperty(False)
104::CODE;;'''Set to True if the sound should automatically loop when it finishes.
105::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.8.0
106::CODE;;:attr:`loop` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty` and defaults to
107::CODE;;False.'''
108::CODE;;__events__ = ('on_play', 'on_stop')
109::CODE;;def on_source(self, instance, filename):
110::CODE;;self.unload()
111::CODE;;if filename is None:
112::CODE;;return
113::CODE;;self.load()
114::CODE;;def get_pos(self):
115::CODE;;'''
116::CODE;;Returns the current position of the audio file.
117::CODE;;Returns 0 if not playing.
118::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.4.1
119::CODE;;'''
120::CODE;;return 0
121::CODE;;def _get_length(self):
122::CODE;;return 0
123::CODE;;length = property(lambda self: self._get_length(),
124::CODE;;doc='Get length of the sound (in seconds).')
125::CODE;;def load(self):
126::CODE;;'''Load the file into memory.'''
127::CODE;;pass
128::CODE;;def unload(self):
129::CODE;;'''Unload the file from memory.'''
130::CODE;;pass
131::CODE;;def play(self):
132::CODE;;'''Play the file.'''
133::CODE;;self.state = 'play'
134::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_play')
135::CODE;;def stop(self):
136::CODE;;'''Stop playback.'''

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;FFmpeg based audio player
3::CODE;;=========================
4::CODE;;To use, you need to install ffpyplayer and have a compiled ffmpeg shared
5::CODE;;library.
6::CODE;;https://github.com/matham/ffpyplayer
7::CODE;;The docs there describe how to set this up. But briefly, first you need to
8::CODE;;compile ffmpeg using the shared flags while disabling the static flags (you'll
9::CODE;;probably have to set the fPIC flag, e.g. CFLAGS=-fPIC). Here's some
10::CODE;;instructions: https://trac.ffmpeg.org/wiki/CompilationGuide. For Windows, you
11::CODE;;can download compiled GPL binaries from http://ffmpeg.zeranoe.com/builds/.
12::CODE;;Similarly, you should download SDL.
13::CODE;;Now, you should a ffmpeg and sdl directory. In each, you should have a include,
14::CODE;;bin, and lib directory, where e.g. for Windows, lib contains the .dll.a files,
15::CODE;;while bin contains the actual dlls. The include directory holds the headers.
16::CODE;;The bin directory is only needed if the shared libraries are not already on
17::CODE;;the path. In the environment define FFMPEG_ROOT and SDL_ROOT, each pointing to
18::CODE;;the ffmpeg, and SDL directories, respectively. (If you're using SDL3,
19::CODE;;the include directory will contain a directory called SDL3, which then holds
20::CODE;;the headers).
21::CODE;;Once defined, download the ffpyplayer git and run
22::CODE;;python setup.py build_ext --inplace
23::CODE;;Finally, before running you need to ensure that ffpyplayer is in python's path.
24::CODE;;..Note::
25::CODE;;When kivy exits by closing the window while the audio is playing,
26::CODE;;it appears that the __del__method of SoundFFPy
27::CODE;;is not called. Because of this the SoundFFPy object is not
28::CODE;;properly deleted when kivy exits. The consequence is that because
29::CODE;;MediaPlayer creates internal threads which do not have their daemon
30::CODE;;flag set, when the main threads exists it'll hang and wait for the other
31::CODE;;MediaPlayer threads to exit. But since __del__ is not called to delete the
32::CODE;;MediaPlayer object, those threads will remain alive hanging kivy. What this
33::CODE;;means is that you have to be sure to delete the MediaPlayer object before
34::CODE;;kivy exits by setting it to None.
35::CODE;;'''
36::CODE;;__all__ = ('SoundFFPy', )
37::CODE;;try:
38::CODE;;import ffpyplayer

41::CODE;;except:
42::CODE;;raise

61::CODE;;elif video_src == 'dc1394src':
62::CODE;;video_src += ' camera-number=%d' % self._index

64::CODE;;caps = ('video/x-raw-rgb,red_mask=(int)0xff0000,'
65::CODE;;'green_mask=(int)0x00ff00,blue_mask=(int)0x0000ff')

67::CODE;;'appsink name=camerasink emit-signals=True caps={}')

71::CODE;;'name=camerasink emit-signals=True caps={}'

75::CODE;;self._decodebin = self._pipeline.get_by_name('decoder')

77::CODE;;self.start()

93::CODE;;return False

100::CODE;;def unload(self):
101::CODE;;self._pipeline.set_state(Gst.State.NULL)
102::CODE;;def _update(self, dt):
103::CODE;;sample, self._sample = self._sample, None
104::CODE;;if sample is None:
105::CODE;;return
106::CODE;;if self._texture is None and self._texturesize is not None:
107::CODE;;self._texture = Texture.create(
108::CODE;;size=self._texturesize, colorfmt='rgb')
109::CODE;;self._texture.flip_vertical()

113::CODE;;try:

121::CODE;;addr = mapinfo.__hash__()

125::CODE;;self._copy_to_gpu()

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Image
3::CODE;;=====
4::CODE;;Core classes for loading images and converting them to a
5::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.graphics.texture.Texture`. The raw image data can be keep in
6::CODE;;memory for further access.
7::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.11.0
8::CODE;;Add support for argb and abgr image data
9::CODE;;In-memory image loading
10::CODE;;-----------------------
11::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.9.0
12::CODE;;Official support for in-memory loading. Not all the providers support it,
13::CODE;;but currently SDL3, pil and imageio work.
14::CODE;;To load an image with a filename, you would usually do::
15::CODE;;from kivy.core.image import Image as CoreImage
16::CODE;;im = CoreImage("image.png")
17::CODE;;You can also load the image data directly from a memory block. Instead of
18::CODE;;passing the filename, you'll need to pass the data as a BytesIO object
19::CODE;;together with an "ext" parameter. Both are mandatory::
20::CODE;;import io
21::CODE;;from kivy.core.image import Image as CoreImage
22::CODE;;data = io.BytesIO(open("image.png", "rb").read())
23::CODE;;im = CoreImage(data, ext="png")
24::CODE;;By default, the image will not be cached as our internal cache requires a
25::CODE;;filename. If you want caching, add a filename that represents your file (it
26::CODE;;will be used only for caching)::
27::CODE;;import io
28::CODE;;from kivy.core.image import Image as CoreImage
29::CODE;;data = io.BytesIO(open("image.png", "rb").read())
30::CODE;;im = CoreImage(data, ext="png", filename="image.png")
31::CODE;;Saving an image
32::CODE;;---------------
33::CODE;;A CoreImage can be saved to a file::
34::CODE;;from kivy.core.image import Image as CoreImage
35::CODE;;image = CoreImage(...)
36::CODE;;image.save("/tmp/test.png")
37::CODE;;Or you can get the bytes (new in `1.11.0`):
38::CODE;;import io
39::CODE;;from kivy.core.image import Image as CoreImage
40::CODE;;data = io.BytesIO()
41::CODE;;image = CoreImage(...)
42::CODE;;image.save(data, fmt="png")
43::CODE;;png_bytes = data.read()
44::CODE;;'''
45::CODE;;import re
46::CODE;;from base64 import b64decode

669::CODE;;def save(self, filename, flipped=False, fmt=None):
670::CODE;;'''Save image texture to file.
671::CODE;;The filename should have the '.png' extension because the texture data
672::CODE;;read from the GPU is in the RGBA format. '.jpg' might work but has not
673::CODE;;been heavily tested so some providers might break when using it.
674::CODE;;Any other extensions are not officially supported.
675::CODE;;The flipped parameter flips the saved image vertically, and
676::CODE;;defaults to False.
677::CODE;;Example::
679::CODE;;from kivy.core.image import Image
680::CODE;;img = Image('hello.png')
681::CODE;;img.save('hello2.png')
683::CODE;;texture = Texture.create(...)
684::CODE;;img = Image(texture)
685::CODE;;img.save('hello3.png')
686::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.7.0
687::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.8.0
688::CODE;;Parameter `flipped` added to flip the image before saving, default
689::CODE;;to False.
690::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.11.0
691::CODE;;Parameter `fmt` added to force the output format of the file
692::CODE;;Filename can now be a BytesIO object.
693::CODE;;'''
694::CODE;;is_bytesio_like = False
695::CODE;;if callable(getattr(filename, 'read', None)):
697::CODE;;is_bytesio_like = True
698::CODE;;if not fmt:
699::CODE;;raise Exception(
700::CODE;;"You must specify a format to save into a BytesIO like object")
701::CODE;;elif fmt is None:
702::CODE;;fmt = self._find_format_from_filename(filename)
703::CODE;;pixels = None
704::CODE;;size = None
705::CODE;;loaders = [
706::CODE;;x for x in ImageLoader.loaders
707::CODE;;if x.can_save(fmt, is_bytesio_like=is_bytesio_like)
708::CODE;;]
709::CODE;;if not loaders:
710::CODE;;return False
711::CODE;;loader = loaders[0]
712::CODE;;if self.image:
714::CODE;;data = self.image._data[0]
715::CODE;;if data.data is not None:
716::CODE;;if data.fmt in ('rgba', 'rgb'):
718::CODE;;size = data.width, data.height
719::CODE;;pixels = data.data
720::CODE;;else:

726::CODE;;size = self._texture.size
727::CODE;;pixels = self._texture.pixels
728::CODE;;if pixels is None:
729::CODE;;return False
730::CODE;;l_pixels = len(pixels)
731::CODE;;if l_pixels == size[0] * size[1] * 3:
732::CODE;;pixelfmt = 'rgb'
733::CODE;;elif l_pixels == size[0] * size[1] * 4:
734::CODE;;pixelfmt = 'rgba'
735::CODE;;else:

750::CODE;;def read_pixel(self, x, y):

763::CODE;;'''
764::CODE;;data = self.image._data[0]
766::CODE;;if data.data is None:
767::CODE;;raise EOFError('Image data is missing, make sure that image is'
768::CODE;;'loaded with keep_data=True keyword.')
770::CODE;;x, y = int(x), int(y)
771::CODE;;if not (0 <= x < data.width and 0 <= y < data.height):
772::CODE;;raise IndexError(f'Position ({x:d}, {y:d}) is out of range.')
773::CODE;;assert data.fmt in ImageData._supported_fmts
774::CODE;;size = 3 if data.fmt in ('rgb', 'bgr') else 4
775::CODE;;index = y * data.width * size + x * size
776::CODE;;raw = bytearray(data.data[index:index + size])
777::CODE;;color = [c / 255.0 for c in raw]
778::CODE;;bgr_flag = False
779::CODE;;if data.fmt == 'argb':
781::CODE;;bgr_flag = True
782::CODE;;elif data.fmt == 'abgr':
785::CODE;;if bgr_flag or data.fmt in ('bgr', 'bgra'):
786::CODE;;color[0], color[2] = color[2], color[0]
787::CODE;;return color
788::CODE;;def load(filename):
789::CODE;;'''Load an image'''
790::CODE;;return Image.load(filename)
792::CODE;;image_libs = []
793::CODE;;if platform in ('macosx', 'ios'):
794::CODE;;image_libs += [('imageio', 'img_imageio')]
795::CODE;;image_libs += [
796::CODE;;('tex', 'img_tex'),
797::CODE;;('dds', 'img_dds')]
798::CODE;;if USE_SDL3:
799::CODE;;image_libs += [('sdl3', 'img_sdl3')]
800::CODE;;image_libs += [
801::CODE;;('ffpy', 'img_ffpyplayer'),
802::CODE;;('pil', 'img_pil')]
803::CODE;;libs_loaded = core_register_libs('image', image_libs)
804::CODE;;from os import environ
805::CODE;;if 'KIVY_DOC' not in environ and not libs_loaded:
806::CODE;;import sys
807::CODE;;Logger.critical('App: Unable to get any Image provider, abort.')
808::CODE;;sys.exit(1)

9::CODE;;from kivy.core.image import ImageLoaderBase, ImageData, ImageLoader

12::CODE;;'fatal': Logger.critical, 'error': Logger.error,
13::CODE;;'warning': Logger.warning, 'info': Logger.info,
14::CODE;;'verbose': Logger.debug, 'debug': Logger.debug}

16::CODE;;message = message.strip()
17::CODE;;if message:
18::CODE;;logger_func[level]('ffpyplayer: {}'.format(message))
19::CODE;;if not get_log_callback():
20::CODE;;set_log_callback(_log_callback)
21::CODE;;class ImageLoaderFFPy(ImageLoaderBase):
22::CODE;;'''Image loader based on the ffpyplayer library.
23::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.9.0
24::CODE;;.. note:
25::CODE;;This provider may support more formats than what is listed in
26::CODE;;:meth:`extensions`.
27::CODE;;'''
28::CODE;;@staticmethod
29::CODE;;def extensions():
30::CODE;;'''Return accepted extensions for this loader'''
32::CODE;;return ('bmp', 'dpx', 'exr', 'gif', 'ico', 'jpeg', 'jpg2000', 'jpg',
33::CODE;;'jls', 'pam', 'pbm', 'pcx', 'pgm', 'pgmyuv', 'pic', 'png',
34::CODE;;'ppm', 'ptx', 'sgi', 'ras', 'tga', 'tiff', 'webp', 'xbm',
35::CODE;;'xface', 'xwd')
36::CODE;;def load(self, filename):
37::CODE;;try:
38::CODE;;loader = ffImageLoader(filename)
39::CODE;;except:
40::CODE;;Logger.warning('Image: Unable to load image <%s>' % filename)
41::CODE;;raise
43::CODE;;self.filename = filename
44::CODE;;images = []
45::CODE;;while True:
46::CODE;;frame, t = loader.next_frame()
47::CODE;;if frame is None:
48::CODE;;break
49::CODE;;images.append(frame)
50::CODE;;if not len(images):
51::CODE;;raise Exception('No image found in {}'.format(filename))
52::CODE;;w, h = images[0].get_size()
53::CODE;;ifmt = images[0].get_pixel_format()
54::CODE;;if ifmt != 'rgba' and ifmt != 'rgb24':
55::CODE;;fmt = 'rgba'
56::CODE;;sws = SWScale(w, h, ifmt, ofmt=fmt)
57::CODE;;for i, image in enumerate(images):
58::CODE;;images[i] = sws.scale(image)
59::CODE;;else:
60::CODE;;fmt = ifmt if ifmt == 'rgba' else 'rgb'
61::CODE;;return [ImageData(w, h, fmt, img.to_memoryview()[0], source_image=img)
62::CODE;;for img in images]

3::CODE;;'''
4::CODE;;__all__ = ('ImageLoaderPIL', )
5::CODE;;try:
6::CODE;;import Image as PILImage
7::CODE;;except ImportError:
9::CODE;;from PIL import Image as PILImage
10::CODE;;from kivy.logger import Logger
11::CODE;;from kivy.core.image import ImageLoaderBase, ImageData, ImageLoader
12::CODE;;try:

20::CODE;;PILImage.frombytes = PILImage.frombuffer

22::CODE;;class ImageLoaderPIL(ImageLoaderBase):
23::CODE;;'''Image loader based on the PIL library.
24::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.8
25::CODE;;Support for GIF animation added.
26::CODE;;Gif animation has a lot of issues(transparency/color depths... etc).
27::CODE;;In order to keep it simple, what is implemented here is what is
28::CODE;;natively supported by the PIL library.
29::CODE;;As a general rule, try to use gifs that have no transparency.
30::CODE;;Gif's with transparency will work but be prepared for some
31::CODE;;artifacts until transparency support is improved.
32::CODE;;'''
33::CODE;;@staticmethod
34::CODE;;def can_save(fmt, is_bytesio_like):
35::CODE;;if is_bytesio_like:
36::CODE;;return False
37::CODE;;return fmt in ImageLoaderPIL.extensions()
38::CODE;;@staticmethod
39::CODE;;def can_load_memory():
40::CODE;;return True
41::CODE;;@staticmethod
42::CODE;;def extensions():
43::CODE;;'''Return accepted extensions for this loader'''
44::CODE;;PILImage.init()
45::CODE;;return tuple((ext_with_dot[1:] for ext_with_dot in PILImage.EXTENSION))
46::CODE;;def _img_correct(self, _img_tmp):
47::CODE;;'''Convert image to the correct format and orientation.
48::CODE;;'''
50::CODE;;if _img_tmp.mode.lower() not in ('rgb', 'rgba'):
51::CODE;;try:
52::CODE;;imc = _img_tmp.convert('RGBA')
53::CODE;;except:
54::CODE;;Logger.warning(
55::CODE;;'Image: Unable to convert image to rgba (was %s)' %
56::CODE;;(_img_tmp.mode.lower()))
57::CODE;;raise
58::CODE;;_img_tmp = imc
59::CODE;;return _img_tmp
60::CODE;;def _img_read(self, im):
61::CODE;;'''Read images from an animated file.
62::CODE;;'''
63::CODE;;im.seek(0)
65::CODE;;try:
66::CODE;;img_ol = None
67::CODE;;while True:
68::CODE;;img_tmp = im
69::CODE;;img_tmp = self._img_correct(img_tmp)
70::CODE;;if img_ol and (hasattr(im, 'dispose') and not im.dispose):
73::CODE;;img_ol.paste(img_tmp, (0, 0), img_tmp)
74::CODE;;img_tmp = img_ol
75::CODE;;img_ol = img_tmp
76::CODE;;yield ImageData(img_tmp.size[0], img_tmp.size[1],
77::CODE;;img_tmp.mode.lower(), img_tmp.tobytes())
78::CODE;;im.seek(im.tell() + 1)
79::CODE;;except EOFError:
80::CODE;;pass
81::CODE;;def load(self, filename):
82::CODE;;try:
83::CODE;;im = PILImage.open(filename)
84::CODE;;except:
85::CODE;;Logger.warning('Image: Unable to load image <%s>' % filename)
86::CODE;;raise
88::CODE;;if not self._inline:
89::CODE;;self.filename = filename
91::CODE;;return list(self._img_read(im))
92::CODE;;@staticmethod
93::CODE;;def save(filename, width, height, pixelfmt, pixels, flipped=False,
94::CODE;;imagefmt=None):
95::CODE;;image = PILImage.frombytes(pixelfmt.upper(), (width, height), pixels)
96::CODE;;if flipped:
97::CODE;;image = image.transpose(PILImage.FLIP_TOP_BOTTOM)
98::CODE;;image.save(filename)
99::CODE;;return True
101::CODE;;ImageLoader.register(ImageLoaderPIL)

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Spelling
3::CODE;;========
4::CODE;;Provides abstracted access to a range of spellchecking backends as well as
5::CODE;;word suggestions. The API is inspired by enchant but other backends can be
6::CODE;;added that implement the same API.
7::CODE;;Spelling currently requires `python-enchant` for all platforms except
8::CODE;;OSX, where a native implementation exists.
9::CODE;;::
10::CODE;;>>> from kivy.core.spelling import Spelling
11::CODE;;>>> s = Spelling()
12::CODE;;>>> s.list_languages()
13::CODE;;['en', 'en_CA', 'en_GB', 'en_US']
14::CODE;;>>> s.select_language('en_US')
15::CODE;;>>> s.suggest('helo')
16::CODE;;[u'hole', u'help', u'helot', u'hello', u'halo', u'hero', u'hell', u'held',
17::CODE;;u'helm', u'he-lo']
18::CODE;;'''
19::CODE;;__all__ = ('Spelling', 'SpellingBase', 'NoSuchLangError',
20::CODE;;'NoLanguageSelectedError')
21::CODE;;import sys
22::CODE;;from kivy.core import core_select_lib
23::CODE;;class NoSuchLangError(Exception):
24::CODE;;'''
25::CODE;;Exception to be raised when a specific language could not be found.
26::CODE;;'''
27::CODE;;pass
28::CODE;;class NoLanguageSelectedError(Exception):
29::CODE;;'''
30::CODE;;Exception to be raised when a language-using method is called but no
31::CODE;;language was selected prior to the call.
32::CODE;;'''
33::CODE;;pass
34::CODE;;class SpellingBase(object):
35::CODE;;'''
36::CODE;;Base class for all spelling providers.
37::CODE;;Supports some abstract methods for checking words and getting suggestions.
38::CODE;;'''
39::CODE;;def __init__(self, language=None):
40::CODE;;'''
41::CODE;;If a `language` identifier (such as 'en_US') is provided and a matching
42::CODE;;language exists, it is selected. If an identifier is provided and no
43::CODE;;matching language exists, a NoSuchLangError exception is raised by
44::CODE;;self.select_language().
45::CODE;;If no `language` identifier is provided, we just fall back to the first
46::CODE;;one that is available.
47::CODE;;:Parameters:
48::CODE;;`language`: str, defaults to None
49::CODE;;If provided, indicates the language to be used. This needs
50::CODE;;to be a language identifier understood by select_language(),
51::CODE;;i.e. one of the options returned by list_languages().
52::CODE;;If nothing is provided, the first available language is used.
53::CODE;;If no language is available, NoLanguageSelectedError is raised.
54::CODE;;'''
55::CODE;;langs = self.list_languages()
56::CODE;;try:
59::CODE;;fallback_lang = langs[0]
60::CODE;;except IndexError:
61::CODE;;raise NoLanguageSelectedError("No languages available!")
62::CODE;;self.select_language(language or fallback_lang)
63::CODE;;def select_language(self, language):
64::CODE;;'''
65::CODE;;From the set of registered languages, select the first language
66::CODE;;for `language`.
67::CODE;;:Parameters:
68::CODE;;`language`: str
69::CODE;;Language identifier. Needs to be one of the options returned by
70::CODE;;list_languages(). Sets the language used for spell checking and
71::CODE;;word suggestions.
72::CODE;;'''
73::CODE;;raise NotImplementedError('select_language() method not implemented '
74::CODE;;'by abstract spelling base class!')
75::CODE;;def list_languages(self):
76::CODE;;'''
77::CODE;;Return a list of all supported languages.
78::CODE;;E.g. ['en', 'en_GB', 'en_US', 'de', ...]
79::CODE;;'''
80::CODE;;raise NotImplementedError('list_languages() is not implemented '
81::CODE;;'by abstract spelling base class!')
82::CODE;;def check(self, word):
83::CODE;;'''
84::CODE;;If `word` is a valid word in `self._language` (the currently active
85::CODE;;language), returns True. If the word shouldn't be checked, returns
86::CODE;;None (e.g. for ''). If it is not a valid word in `self._language`,
87::CODE;;return False.
88::CODE;;:Parameters:
89::CODE;;`word`: str
90::CODE;;The word to check.
91::CODE;;'''
92::CODE;;raise NotImplementedError('check() not implemented by abstract ' +
93::CODE;;'spelling base class!')
94::CODE;;def suggest(self, fragment):
95::CODE;;'''
96::CODE;;For a given `fragment` (i.e. part of a word or a word by itself),
97::CODE;;provide corrections (`fragment` may be misspelled) or completions
98::CODE;;as a list of strings.
99::CODE;;:Parameters:
100::CODE;;`fragment`: str
101::CODE;;The word fragment to get suggestions/corrections for.
102::CODE;;E.g. 'foo' might become 'of', 'food' or 'foot'.
103::CODE;;'''
104::CODE;;raise NotImplementedError('suggest() not implemented by abstract ' +
105::CODE;;'spelling base class!')
106::CODE;;_libs = (('enchant', 'spelling_enchant', 'SpellingEnchant'), )
107::CODE;;if sys.platform == 'darwin':
108::CODE;;_libs += (('osxappkit', 'spelling_osxappkit', 'SpellingOSXAppKit'), )
109::CODE;;Spelling: SpellingBase = core_select_lib('spelling', _libs)
1::CODE;;'''

3::CODE;;================
4::CODE;;Implementation spelling backend based on enchant.

7::CODE;;'''
8::CODE;;import enchant

10::CODE;;class SpellingEnchant(SpellingBase):

12::CODE;;Spelling backend based on the enchant library.
13::CODE;;'''
14::CODE;;def __init__(self, language=None):

16::CODE;;super(SpellingEnchant, self).__init__(language)
17::CODE;;def select_language(self, language):
18::CODE;;try:
19::CODE;;self._language = enchant.Dict(language)
20::CODE;;except enchant.DictNotFoundError:
21::CODE;;err = 'Enchant Backend: No language for "%s"' % (language, )
22::CODE;;raise NoSuchLangError(err)
23::CODE;;def list_languages(self):
26::CODE;;return enchant.list_languages()

28::CODE;;if not word:
29::CODE;;return None
30::CODE;;return self._language.check(word)
31::CODE;;def suggest(self, fragment):
32::CODE;;suggestions = self._language.suggest(fragment)
34::CODE;;suggestions = [s for s in suggestions if self.check(s)]
35::CODE;;return suggestions

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Text
3::CODE;;====
4::CODE;;An abstraction of text creation. Depending of the selected backend, the
5::CODE;;accuracy of text rendering may vary.
6::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.10.1
7::CODE;;:meth:`LabelBase.find_base_direction` added.
8::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.5.0
9::CODE;;:attr:`LabelBase.line_height` added.
10::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.0.7
11::CODE;;The :class:`LabelBase` does not generate any texture if the text has a
12::CODE;;width <= 1.
13::CODE;;This is the backend layer for rendering text with different text providers,
14::CODE;;you should only be using this directly if your needs aren't fulfilled by the
15::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.label.Label`.
16::CODE;;Usage example::
17::CODE;;from kivy.core.text import Label as CoreLabel
18::CODE;;...
19::CODE;;...
20::CODE;;my_label = CoreLabel()
21::CODE;;my_label.text = 'hello'
23::CODE;;my_label.refresh()
26::CODE;;hello_texture = my_label.texture
27::CODE;;Font Context Manager
28::CODE;;====================
29::CODE;;A font context is a namespace where multiple fonts are loaded; if a font is
30::CODE;;missing a glyph needed to render text, it can fall back to a different font in
31::CODE;;the same context. The font context manager can be used to query and manipulate
32::CODE;;the state of font contexts when using the Pango text provider (no other
33::CODE;;provider currently implements it).
34::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.11.0
35::CODE;;.. warning:: This feature requires the Pango text provider.
36::CODE;;Font contexts can be created automatically by :class:`kivy.uix.label.Label` or
37::CODE;;:class:`kivy.uix.textinput.TextInput`; if a non-existent context is used in
38::CODE;;one of these classes, it will be created automatically, or if a font file is
39::CODE;;specified without a context (this creates an isolated context, without
40::CODE;;support for fallback).
41::CODE;;Usage example::
42::CODE;;from kivy.uix.label import Label
43::CODE;;from kivy.core.text import FontContextManager as FCM
45::CODE;;FCM.create('system://myapp')
46::CODE;;family = FCM.add_font('/path/to/file.ttf')
48::CODE;;lbl1 = Label(font_context='system://myapp', family_name=family)
49::CODE;;lbl2 = Label(font_context='system://myapp', font_name='/path/to/file.ttf')
52::CODE;;lbl3 = Label(font_context='system://myapp', family_name='Arial')
53::CODE;;'''
54::CODE;;__all__ = ('LabelBase', 'Label',
55::CODE;;'FontContextManagerBase', 'FontContextManager')

80::CODE;;class LabelBase(object):
81::CODE;;'''Core text label.
82::CODE;;This is the abstract class used by different backends to render text.
83::CODE;;.. warning::
84::CODE;;The core text label can't be changed at runtime. You must recreate one.
85::CODE;;:Parameters:
86::CODE;;`font_size`: int, defaults to 12
87::CODE;;Font size of the text
88::CODE;;`font_context`: str, defaults to None
89::CODE;;Context for the specified font (see :class:`kivy.uix.label.Label`
90::CODE;;for details). `None` will autocreate an isolated context named
91::CODE;;after the resolved font file.
92::CODE;;`font_name`: str, defaults to DEFAULT_FONT
93::CODE;;Font name of the text
94::CODE;;`font_family`: str, defaults to None
95::CODE;;Font family name to request for drawing, this can only be used
96::CODE;;with `font_context`.
97::CODE;;`bold`: bool, defaults to False
98::CODE;;Activate "bold" text style
99::CODE;;`italic`: bool, defaults to False
100::CODE;;Activate "italic" text style
101::CODE;;`text_size`: tuple, defaults to (None, None)
102::CODE;;Add constraint to render the text (inside a bounding box).
103::CODE;;If no size is given, the label size will be set to the text size.
104::CODE;;`padding`: int|float or list|tuple, defaults to [0, 0, 0, 0].
105::CODE;;Padding of the text in the format [padding_left, padding_top,
106::CODE;;padding_right, padding_bottom].
107::CODE;;``padding`` should be int|float or a list|tuple with 1, 2 or 4
108::CODE;;elements.
109::CODE;;`padding_x`: float, defaults to 0.0
110::CODE;;Left/right padding
111::CODE;;`padding_y`: float, defaults to 0.0
112::CODE;;Top/bottom padding
113::CODE;;`halign`: str, defaults to "left"
114::CODE;;Horizontal text alignment inside the bounding box
115::CODE;;`valign`: str, defaults to "bottom"
116::CODE;;Vertical text alignment inside the bounding box
117::CODE;;`shorten`: bool, defaults to False
118::CODE;;Indicate whether the label should attempt to shorten its textual
119::CODE;;contents as much as possible if a `size` is given.
120::CODE;;Setting this to True without an appropriately set size will lead to
121::CODE;;unexpected results.
122::CODE;;`shorten_from`: str, defaults to `center`
123::CODE;;The side from which we should shorten the text from, can be left,
124::CODE;;right, or center. E.g. if left, the ellipsis will appear towards
125::CODE;;the left side and it will display as much text starting from the
126::CODE;;right as possible.
127::CODE;;`split_str`: string, defaults to `' '` (space)
128::CODE;;The string to use to split the words by when shortening. If empty,
129::CODE;;we can split after every character filling up the line as much as
130::CODE;;possible.
131::CODE;;`max_lines`: int, defaults to 0 (unlimited)
132::CODE;;If set, this indicate how maximum line are allowed to render the
133::CODE;;text. Works only if a limitation on text_size is set.
134::CODE;;`mipmap`: bool, defaults to False
135::CODE;;Create a mipmap for the texture
136::CODE;;`strip`: bool, defaults to False
137::CODE;;Whether each row of text has its leading and trailing spaces
138::CODE;;stripped. If `halign` is `justify` it is implicitly True.
139::CODE;;`strip_reflow`: bool, defaults to True
140::CODE;;Whether text that has been reflowed into a second line should
141::CODE;;be stripped, even if `strip` is False. This is only in effect when
142::CODE;;`size_hint_x` is not None, because otherwise lines are never
143::CODE;;split.
144::CODE;;`unicode_errors`: str, defaults to `'replace'`
145::CODE;;How to handle unicode decode errors. Can be `'strict'`, `'replace'`
146::CODE;;or `'ignore'`.
147::CODE;;`outline_width`: int, defaults to None
148::CODE;;Width in pixels for the outline.
149::CODE;;`outline_color`: tuple, defaults to (0, 0, 0)
150::CODE;;Color of the outline.
151::CODE;;`font_features`: str, defaults to None
152::CODE;;OpenType font features in CSS format (Pango only)
153::CODE;;`base_direction`: str, defaults to None (auto)
154::CODE;;Text direction, one of `None`, `'ltr'`, `'rtl'`, `'weak_ltr'`,
155::CODE;;or `'weak_rtl'` (Pango only)
156::CODE;;`text_language`: str, defaults to None (user locale)
157::CODE;;RFC-3066 format language tag as a string (Pango only)
158::CODE;;`limit_render_to_text_bbox`: bool, defaults to False. Available for SDL3
159::CODE;;and PIL text providers.
160::CODE;;If set to ``True``, this parameter indicates that rendering should
161::CODE;;be limited to the bounding box of the text, excluding any
162::CODE;;additional white spaces designated for ascent and descent.
163::CODE;;By limiting the rendering to the bounding box of the text, it
164::CODE;;ensures a more precise alignment with surrounding elements when
165::CODE;;utilizing properties such as `valign`, `y`, `pos`, `pos_hint`, etc.
166::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 3.0.0
167::CODE;;`limit_render_to_text_bbox` was implemented for SDL3 text provider.
168::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 2.3.0
169::CODE;;`limit_render_to_text_bbox` was added to allow to limit text rendering
170::CODE;;to the text bounding box (PIL only).
171::CODE;;.. deprecated:: 2.2.0
172::CODE;;`padding_x` and `padding_y` have been deprecated. Please use `padding`
173::CODE;;instead.
174::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 2.2.0
175::CODE;;`padding` is now a list and defaults to [0, 0, 0, 0]. `padding` accepts
176::CODE;;int|float or a list|tuple with 1, 2 or 4 elements.
177::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.10.1
178::CODE;;`font_context`, `font_family`, `font_features`, `base_direction`
179::CODE;;and `text_language` were added.
180::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.10.0
181::CODE;;`outline_width` and `outline_color` were added.
182::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.9.0
183::CODE;;`strip`, `strip_reflow`, `shorten_from`, `split_str`, and
184::CODE;;`unicode_errors` were added.
185::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.9.0
186::CODE;;`padding_x` and `padding_y` has been fixed to work as expected.
187::CODE;;In the past, the text was padded by the negative of their values.
188::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.8.0
189::CODE;;`max_lines` parameters has been added.
190::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.0.8
191::CODE;;`size` have been deprecated and replaced with `text_size`.
192::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.0.7
193::CODE;;The `valign` is now respected. This wasn't the case previously
194::CODE;;so you might have an issue in your application if you have not
195::CODE;;considered this.
196::CODE;;'''

413::CODE;;def shorten(self, text, margin=2):
414::CODE;;''' Shortens the text to fit into a single line by the width specified
415::CODE;;by :attr:`text_size` [0]. If :attr:`text_size` [0] is None, it returns
416::CODE;;text unchanged.
417::CODE;;:attr:`split_str` and :attr:`shorten_from` determines how the text is
418::CODE;;shortened.
419::CODE;;:params:
420::CODE;;`text` str, the text to be shortened.
421::CODE;;`margin` int, the amount of space to leave between the margins
422::CODE;;and the text. This is in addition to :attr:`padding_x`.
423::CODE;;:returns:
424::CODE;;the text shortened to fit into a single line.
425::CODE;;'''
426::CODE;;textwidth = self.get_cached_extents()
427::CODE;;uw = self.text_size[0]
428::CODE;;if uw is None or not text:
429::CODE;;return text
430::CODE;;opts = self.options
431::CODE;;uw = max(0, int(uw - opts['padding'][0] - opts['padding'][2] - margin))
433::CODE;;chr = type(text)
434::CODE;;text = text.replace(chr('\n'), chr(' '))
435::CODE;;if len(text) <= uw and textwidth(text)[0] <= uw:
436::CODE;;return text
437::CODE;;c = opts['split_str']
438::CODE;;offset = 0 if len(c) else 1
439::CODE;;dir = opts['shorten_from'][0]
440::CODE;;elps = textwidth('...')[0]
441::CODE;;if elps > uw:
442::CODE;;self.is_shortened = True
443::CODE;;if textwidth('..')[0] <= uw:
444::CODE;;return '..'
445::CODE;;else:
446::CODE;;return '.'
447::CODE;;uw -= elps
448::CODE;;f = partial(text.find, c)
449::CODE;;f_rev = partial(text.rfind, c)
451::CODE;;e1, s2 = f(), f_rev()
454::CODE;;if e1 != -1:
455::CODE;;l1 = textwidth(text[:e1])[0]
456::CODE;;l2 = textwidth(text[s2 + 1:])[0]
457::CODE;;if e1 == -1 or l1 + l2 > uw:
458::CODE;;self.is_shortened = True
459::CODE;;if len(c):
460::CODE;;opts['split_str'] = ''
461::CODE;;res = self.shorten(text, margin)
462::CODE;;opts['split_str'] = c
463::CODE;;return res
465::CODE;;if l1 <= uw:
466::CODE;;return chr('{0}...').format(text[:e1])
467::CODE;;return chr('...')
470::CODE;;self.is_shortened = True
471::CODE;;return chr('{0}...{1}').format(text[:e1], text[s2 + 1:])
473::CODE;;if dir == 'r':
474::CODE;;ee1 = f(e1 + 1)
475::CODE;;while l2 + textwidth(text[:ee1])[0] <= uw:
476::CODE;;e1 = ee1
477::CODE;;if e1 == s2:
478::CODE;;break
479::CODE;;ee1 = f(e1 + 1)
480::CODE;;else:
481::CODE;;while True:
482::CODE;;if l1 <= l2:
483::CODE;;ee1 = f(e1 + 1)
484::CODE;;l1 = textwidth(text[:ee1])[0]
485::CODE;;if l2 + l1 > uw:
486::CODE;;break

489::CODE;;break

504::CODE;;if s2 == -1 or l2 + l1 > uw:

509::CODE;;opts['split_str'] = c
510::CODE;;return res

514::CODE;;self.is_shortened = True
515::CODE;;return chr('{0}...{1}').format(text[:e1], text[s2 + 1:])

519::CODE;;s2 = ss2

548::CODE;;def render_lines(self, lines, options, render_text, y, size):
549::CODE;;get_extents = self.get_cached_extents()
550::CODE;;uw, uh = options['text_size']
551::CODE;;padding_left = options['padding'][0]
552::CODE;;padding_right = options['padding'][2]
553::CODE;;if uw is not None:
555::CODE;;w = size[0]

557::CODE;;halign = options['halign']
558::CODE;;split = re.split
559::CODE;;find_base_dir = self.find_base_direction
560::CODE;;cur_base_dir = options['base_direction']
562::CODE;;lw, lh = layout_line.w, layout_line.h
563::CODE;;line = ''
564::CODE;;assert len(layout_line.words) < 2
565::CODE;;if len(layout_line.words):
566::CODE;;last_word = layout_line.words[0]
567::CODE;;line = last_word.text
568::CODE;;if not cur_base_dir:
569::CODE;;cur_base_dir = find_base_dir(line)
570::CODE;;x = padding_left
571::CODE;;if halign == 'auto':
572::CODE;;if cur_base_dir and 'rtl' in cur_base_dir:
574::CODE;;x = max(0, int(w - lw - padding_right))
575::CODE;;elif halign == 'center':
576::CODE;;x = min(
577::CODE;;int(w - lw),
578::CODE;;max(

580::CODE;;int((w - lw + padding_left - padding_right) / 2.0)
581::CODE;;)

796::CODE;;@staticmethod
797::CODE;;def create(font_context):
798::CODE;;'''Create a font context, you must specify a unique name (string).
799::CODE;;Returns `True` on success and `False` on failure.
800::CODE;;If `font_context` starts with one of the reserved words `'system://'`,
801::CODE;;`'directory://'`, `'fontconfig://'` or `'systemconfig://'`, the context
802::CODE;;is setup accordingly (exact results of this depends on your platform,
803::CODE;;environment and configuration).
804::CODE;;* `'system://'` loads the default system's FontConfig configuration
805::CODE;;and all fonts (usually including user fonts).
806::CODE;;* `directory://` contexts preload a directory of font files (specified
807::CODE;;in the context name), `systemconfig://` loads the system's FontConfig
808::CODE;;configuration (but no fonts), and `fontconfig://` loads FontConfig
809::CODE;;configuration file (specified in the context name!). These are for
810::CODE;;advanced users only, check the source code and FontConfig
811::CODE;;documentation for details.
812::CODE;;* Fonts automatically loaded to an isolated context (ie when no
813::CODE;;font context was specified) start with `'isolated://'`. This has
814::CODE;;no special effect, and only serves to help you identify them in
815::CODE;;the results returned from :meth:`list`.
816::CODE;;* Any other string is a context that will only draw with the font
817::CODE;;file(s) you explicitly add to it.
818::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.11.0
819::CODE;;.. note::
820::CODE;;Font contexts are created automatically by specifying a name in the
821::CODE;;`font_context` property of :class:`kivy.uix.label.Label` or
822::CODE;;:class:`kivy.uix.textinput.TextInput`. They are also auto-created
823::CODE;;by :meth:`add_font` by default, so you normally don't need to
824::CODE;;call this directly.
825::CODE;;.. note:: This feature requires the Pango text provider.
826::CODE;;'''
827::CODE;;raise NotImplementedError("No font_context support in text provider")
