1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Text Markup
3::CODE;;===========
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.1.0
5::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.10.1
6::CODE;;Added `font_context`, `font_features` and `text_language` (Pango only)
7::CODE;;We provide a simple text-markup for inline text styling. The syntax look the
8::CODE;;same as the `BBCode <http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBCode>`_.
9::CODE;;A tag is defined as ``[tag]``, and should have a corresponding
10::CODE;;``[/tag]`` closing tag. For example::
11::CODE;;[b]Hello [color=ff0000]world[/color][/b]
12::CODE;;The following tags are available:
13::CODE;;``[b][/b]``
14::CODE;;Activate bold text
15::CODE;;``[i][/i]``
16::CODE;;Activate italic text
17::CODE;;``[u][/u]``
18::CODE;;Underlined text
19::CODE;;``[s][/s]``
20::CODE;;Strikethrough text
21::CODE;;``[font=<str>][/font]``
22::CODE;;Change the font (note: this refers to a TTF file or registered alias)
23::CODE;;``[font_context=<str>][/font_context]``
24::CODE;;Change context for the font, use string value "none" for isolated context.
25::CODE;;``[font_family=<str>][/font_family]``
26::CODE;;Font family to request for drawing. This is only valid when using a
27::CODE;;font context, and takes precedence over `[font]`. See
28::CODE;;:class:`kivy.uix.label.Label` for details.
29::CODE;;``[font_features=<str>][/font_features]``
30::CODE;;OpenType font features, in CSS format, this is passed straight
31::CODE;;through to Pango. The effects of requesting a feature depends on loaded
32::CODE;;fonts, library versions, etc. Pango only, requires v1.38 or later.
33::CODE;;``[size=<size>][/size]``
34::CODE;;Change the font size. <size> should be an integer, optionally with a
35::CODE;;unit (i.e. ``16sp``)
37::CODE;;Change the text color
38::CODE;;``[ref=<str>][/ref]``
39::CODE;;Add an interactive zone. The reference + all the word box inside the
40::CODE;;reference will be available in :attr:`MarkupLabel.refs`
41::CODE;;``[anchor=<str>]``
42::CODE;;Put an anchor in the text. You can get the position of your anchor within
43::CODE;;the text with :attr:`MarkupLabel.anchors`
44::CODE;;``[sub][/sub]``
45::CODE;;Display the text at a subscript position relative to the text before it.
46::CODE;;``[sup][/sup]``
47::CODE;;Display the text at a superscript position relative to the text before it.
48::CODE;;``[text_language=<str>][/text_language]``
49::CODE;;Language of the text, this is an RFC-3066 format language tag (as string),
50::CODE;;for example "en_US", "zh_CN", "fr" or "ja". This can impact font selection,
51::CODE;;metrics and rendering. For example, the same bytes of text can look
52::CODE;;different for `ur` and `ar` languages, though both use Arabic script.
53::CODE;;Use the string `'none'` to revert to locale detection. Pango only.
54::CODE;;If you need to escape the markup from the current text, use
55::CODE;;:func:`kivy.utils.escape_markup`.
56::CODE;;'''

476::CODE;;def shorten_post(self, lines, w, h, margin=2):
477::CODE;;''' Shortens the text to a single line according to the label options.
478::CODE;;This function operates on a text that has already been laid out because
479::CODE;;for markup, parts of text can have different size and options.
480::CODE;;If :attr:`text_size` [0] is None, the lines are returned unchanged.
481::CODE;;Otherwise, the lines are converted to a single line fitting within the
482::CODE;;constrained width, :attr:`text_size` [0].

484::CODE;;`lines`: list of `LayoutLine` instances describing the text.

486::CODE;;`h`: int, the height of the text in lines, including padding.

488::CODE;;addition to :attr:`padding_x`.
489::CODE;;:returns:
490::CODE;;3-tuple of (xw, h, lines), where w, and h is similar to the input
491::CODE;;and contains the resulting width / height of the text, including
492::CODE;;padding. lines, is a list containing a single `LayoutLine`, which
493::CODE;;contains the words for the line.
494::CODE;;'''
495::CODE;;def n(line, c):

497::CODE;;returns successive occurrences of string c in list line. line is
498::CODE;;not a string, but a list of LayoutWord instances that we walk
499::CODE;;from left to right returning the indices of c in the words as we
500::CODE;;encounter them. Note that the options can be different among the
501::CODE;;words.
502::CODE;;:returns:

504::CODE;;occurrence in word, and the extents (width) of the combined
505::CODE;;words until this occurrence, not including the occurrence char.
506::CODE;;If no more are found it returns (-1, -1, total_w) where total_w

5::CODE;;.. warning::
6::CODE;;The low-level Pango API is experimental, and subject to change without
7::CODE;;notice for as long as this warning is present.
8::CODE;;Installation
9::CODE;;------------
10::CODE;;1. Install pangoft2 (`apt install libfreetype6-dev libpango1.0-dev
11::CODE;;libpangoft2-1.0-0`) or ensure it is available in pkg-config
12::CODE;;2. Recompile kivy. Check that pangoft2 is found `use_pangoft2 = 1`
13::CODE;;3. Test it! Enforce the text core renderer to pango using environment variable:
14::CODE;;`export KIVY_TEXT=pango`
15::CODE;;This has been tested on OSX and Linux, Python 3.6.
16::CODE;;Font context types for FontConfig+FreeType2 backend
17::CODE;;---------------------------------------------------
18::CODE;;* `system://` - `FcInitLoadConfigAndFonts()`
19::CODE;;* `systemconfig://` - `FcInitLoadConfig()`
20::CODE;;* `directory://<PATH>` - `FcInitLoadConfig()` + `FcAppFontAddDir()`
21::CODE;;* `fontconfig://<PATH>` - `FcConfigCreate()` + `FcConfigParseAndLoad()`
22::CODE;;* Any other context name - `FcConfigCreate()`
23::CODE;;Low-level Pango access
24::CODE;;----------------------
25::CODE;;Since Kivy currently does its own text layout, the Label and TextInput widgets
26::CODE;;do not take full advantage of Pango. For example, line breaks do not take
27::CODE;;language/script into account, and switching alignment per paragraph (for bi-
28::CODE;;directional text) is not supported. For advanced i18n requirements, we provide
29::CODE;;a simple wrapper around PangoLayout that you can use to render text.
30::CODE;;* https://developer.gnome.org/pango/1.40/pango-Layout-Objects.html
31::CODE;;* https://developer.gnome.org/pango/1.40/PangoMarkupFormat.html
32::CODE;;* See the `kivy/core/text/_text_pango.pyx` file @ `cdef class KivyPangoLayout`
33::CODE;;for more information. Not all features of PangoLayout are implemented.
34::CODE;;.. python::
36::CODE;;from kivy.core.text._text_pango import KivyPangoLayout
37::CODE;;layout = KivyPangoLayout('system://')
38::CODE;;layout.set_markup('<span font="20">Hello <b>World!</b></span>')
39::CODE;;tex = layout.render_as_Texture()
40::CODE;;Known limitations
41::CODE;;-----------------
42::CODE;;* Pango versions older than v1.38 has not been tested. It may work on
43::CODE;;some systems with older pango and newer FontConfig/FreeType2 versions.
44::CODE;;* Kivy's text layout is used, not Pango. This means we do not use Pango's
45::CODE;;line-breaking feature (which is superior to Kivy's), and we can't use
46::CODE;;Pango's bidirectional cursor helpers in TextInput.
47::CODE;;* Font family collisions can happen. For example, if you use a `system://`
48::CODE;;context and add a custom `Arial.ttf`, using `arial` as the `font_family`
49::CODE;;may or may not draw with your custom font (depending on whether or not
50::CODE;;there is already a system-wide "arial" font installed)
51::CODE;;* Rendering is inefficient; the normal way to integrate Pango would be
52::CODE;;using a dedicated PangoLayout per widget. This is not currently practical
53::CODE;;due to missing abstractions in Kivy core (in the current implementation,
54::CODE;;we have a dedicated PangoLayout *per font context,* which is rendered
55::CODE;;once for each LayoutWord)
56::CODE;;'''

12::CODE;;def _select_font(self):
13::CODE;;if self.options['font_size'] < 1:
14::CODE;;return None
15::CODE;;fontsize = int(self.options['font_size'])
16::CODE;;fontname = self.options['font_name_r']
17::CODE;;try:
18::CODE;;id = '%s.%s' % (str(fontname), str(fontsize))
19::CODE;;except UnicodeDecodeError:
20::CODE;;id = '%s.%s' % (fontname, fontsize)
21::CODE;;if id not in self._cache:
22::CODE;;font = ImageFont.truetype(fontname, fontsize)
23::CODE;;self._cache[id] = font
24::CODE;;return self._cache[id]
25::CODE;;def get_extents(self, text):
26::CODE;;font = self._select_font()
27::CODE;;if not font:
28::CODE;;return 0, 0
29::CODE;;left, top, right, bottom = font.getbbox(text)
30::CODE;;ascent, descent = font.getmetrics()
31::CODE;;if self.options['limit_render_to_text_bbox']:
32::CODE;;h = bottom - top
33::CODE;;else:
34::CODE;;h = ascent + descent
35::CODE;;w = right - left
36::CODE;;return w, h
37::CODE;;def get_cached_extents(self):
38::CODE;;return self.get_extents
39::CODE;;def _render_begin(self):
41::CODE;;self._pil_im = Image.new('RGBA', self._size, color=(255, 255, 255, 0))
42::CODE;;self._pil_draw = ImageDraw.Draw(self._pil_im)
43::CODE;;def _render_text(self, text, x, y):
44::CODE;;font = self._select_font()
45::CODE;;if not font:
46::CODE;;return
47::CODE;;color = tuple([int(c * 255) for c in self.options['color']])
49::CODE;;if self.options['limit_render_to_text_bbox']:
50::CODE;;bbox = font.getbbox(text)
51::CODE;;x -= bbox[0]
52::CODE;;y -= bbox[1]
53::CODE;;self._pil_draw.text((int(x), int(y)), text, font=font, fill=color)
54::CODE;;def _render_end(self):
55::CODE;;data = ImageData(self._size[0], self._size[1],
56::CODE;;self._pil_im.mode.lower(), self._pil_im.tobytes())
57::CODE;;del self._pil_im
58::CODE;;del self._pil_draw
59::CODE;;return data

21::CODE;;'''VideoBase, a class used to implement a video reader.
22::CODE;;:Parameters:
23::CODE;;`filename`: str

39::CODE;;Fired when the video is loaded and the texture is available.

41::CODE;;Fired when a new frame is written to the texture.

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;FFmpeg based video abstraction
3::CODE;;==============================
4::CODE;;To use, you need to install ffpyplayer and have a compiled ffmpeg shared
5::CODE;;library.
6::CODE;;https://github.com/matham/ffpyplayer
7::CODE;;The docs there describe how to set this up. But briefly, first you need to
8::CODE;;compile ffmpeg using the shared flags while disabling the static flags (you'll
9::CODE;;probably have to set the fPIC flag, e.g. CFLAGS=-fPIC). Here are some
10::CODE;;instructions: https://trac.ffmpeg.org/wiki/CompilationGuide. For Windows, you
11::CODE;;can download compiled GPL binaries from http://ffmpeg.zeranoe.com/builds/.
12::CODE;;Similarly, you should download SDL3.
13::CODE;;Now, you should have ffmpeg and sdl directories. In each, you should have an
14::CODE;;'include', 'bin' and 'lib' directory, where e.g. for Windows, 'lib' contains
15::CODE;;the .dll.a files, while 'bin' contains the actual dlls. The 'include' directory
16::CODE;;holds the headers. The 'bin' directory is only needed if the shared libraries
17::CODE;;are not already in the path. In the environment, define FFMPEG_ROOT and
18::CODE;;SDL_ROOT, each pointing to the ffmpeg and SDL directories respectively. (If
19::CODE;;you're using SDL3, the 'include' directory will contain an 'SDL3' directory,
20::CODE;;which then holds the headers).
21::CODE;;Once defined, download the ffpyplayer git repo and run
22::CODE;;python setup.py build_ext --inplace
23::CODE;;Finally, before running you need to ensure that ffpyplayer is in python's path.
24::CODE;;..Note::
25::CODE;;When kivy exits by closing the window while the video is playing,
26::CODE;;it appears that the __del__method of VideoFFPy
27::CODE;;is not called. Because of this, the VideoFFPy object is not
28::CODE;;properly deleted when kivy exits. The consequence is that because
29::CODE;;MediaPlayer creates internal threads which do not have their daemon
30::CODE;;flag set, when the main threads exists, it'll hang and wait for the other
31::CODE;;MediaPlayer threads to exit. But since __del__ is not called to delete the
32::CODE;;MediaPlayer object, those threads will remain alive, hanging kivy. What
33::CODE;;this means is that you have to be sure to delete the MediaPlayer object
34::CODE;;before kivy exits by setting it to None.
35::CODE;;'''
36::CODE;;__all__ = ('VideoFFPy', )

152::CODE;;def string_to_keycode(self, value):
153::CODE;;'''Convert a string to a keycode number according to the
154::CODE;;:attr:`Keyboard.keycodes`. If the value is not found in the
155::CODE;;keycodes, it will return -1.
156::CODE;;'''
157::CODE;;return Keyboard.keycodes.get(value, -1)
158::CODE;;def keycode_to_string(self, value):
159::CODE;;'''Convert a keycode number to a string according to the
160::CODE;;:attr:`Keyboard.keycodes`. If the value is not found in the
161::CODE;;keycodes, it will return ''.
162::CODE;;'''
163::CODE;;keycodes = list(Keyboard.keycodes.values())

165::CODE;;return list(Keyboard.keycodes.keys())[keycodes.index(value)]

361::CODE;;def _get_unrotated_size(self):
362::CODE;;w, h = self._size
363::CODE;;w *= self._density
364::CODE;;h *= self._density
365::CODE;;return w, h
366::CODE;;unrotated_size = AliasProperty(
367::CODE;;_get_unrotated_size, None, bind=("_size", "_density")
368::CODE;;)
369::CODE;;'''The unrotated size of the window in drawable pixels. This is the actual
370::CODE;;pixel size of the drawable area of the window, and takes into account the
371::CODE;;window's pixel density.
372::CODE;;The pixel density is the ratio of the physical pixels to the size of the
373::CODE;;window in window coordinates. For example, on a Retina HiDPI display, the
374::CODE;;pixel density is typically 2.0, meaning that the window's drawable size in
375::CODE;;pixels is twice the size in window coordinates.
376::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 3.0.0
377::CODE;;:attr:`unrotated_size` is a
378::CODE;;read-only :class:`~kivy.properties.AliasProperty`.
379::CODE;;'''
380::CODE;;def _get_size(self):
381::CODE;;w, h = self._get_unrotated_size()
382::CODE;;r = self._rotation
383::CODE;;if r not in (0, 180):
384::CODE;;h, w = w, h
385::CODE;;return w, h
386::CODE;;def _set_size(self, size):
387::CODE;;r = self._rotation
388::CODE;;new_w, new_h = size
389::CODE;;if r not in (0, 180):
390::CODE;;new_h, new_w = new_w, new_h
391::CODE;;if (
392::CODE;;new_w / self._density == self._size[0]
393::CODE;;and new_h / self._density == self._size[1]
394::CODE;;):
396::CODE;;return
397::CODE;;self._size = (new_w / self._density, new_h / self._density)
398::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_pre_resize', *self._size)
399::CODE;;size = AliasProperty(_get_size, _set_size, bind=('_size', '_rotation'))
400::CODE;;'''The rotated size of the window in drawable pixels. This is the actual
401::CODE;;pixel size of the drawable area of the window, and takes into account the
402::CODE;;window's :attr:`rotation` and pixel density.
403::CODE;;The pixel density is the ratio of the physical pixels to the size of the
404::CODE;;window in window coordinates. For example, on a Retina HiDPI display, the
405::CODE;;pixel density is typically 2.0, meaning that the window's drawable size in
406::CODE;;pixels is twice the size in window coordinates.
407::CODE;;Consider using :attr:`system_size` if you want to programmatically set the
408::CODE;;window size, as is more portable, and will give a nicer UX across different
409::CODE;;OSes and displays.

474::CODE;;softinput_mode = OptionProperty(
475::CODE;;'', options=('', 'below_target', 'pan', 'scale', 'resize')
476::CODE;;)
477::CODE;;'''This specifies the behavior of window contents on display of the soft
478::CODE;;keyboard on mobile platforms. It can be one of '', 'pan', 'scale',
479::CODE;;'resize' or 'below_target'. Their effects are listed below.
480::CODE;;+----------------+-------------------------------------------------------+
481::CODE;;| Value | Effect |
482::CODE;;+================+=======================================================+
483::CODE;;| '' | The main window is left as is, allowing you to use |
484::CODE;;| | the :attr:`keyboard_height` to manage the window |
485::CODE;;| | contents manually. |
486::CODE;;+----------------+-------------------------------------------------------+
487::CODE;;| 'pan' | The main window pans, moving the bottom part of the |
488::CODE;;| | window to be always on top of the keyboard. |
489::CODE;;+----------------+-------------------------------------------------------+
490::CODE;;| 'resize' | The window is resized and the contents scaled to fit |
491::CODE;;| | the remaining space. |
492::CODE;;+----------------+-------------------------------------------------------+
493::CODE;;| 'below_target' | The window pans so that the current target TextInput |
494::CODE;;| | widget requesting the keyboard is presented just above|
495::CODE;;| | the soft keyboard. |
496::CODE;;+----------------+-------------------------------------------------------+
497::CODE;;:attr:`softinput_mode` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.OptionProperty` and
498::CODE;;defaults to ''.
499::CODE;;.. note:: The `resize` option does not currently work with SDL3 on Android.
500::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.9.0
501::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.9.1
502::CODE;;The 'below_target' option was added.
503::CODE;;'''

1324::CODE;;accepted = manager.dispatch(etype, me) or accepted

1388::CODE;;def update_viewport(self):
1389::CODE;;from kivy.graphics.opengl import glViewport
1390::CODE;;from kivy.graphics.transformation import Matrix
1391::CODE;;from math import radians
1392::CODE;;w, h = self.unrotated_size
1393::CODE;;smode = self.softinput_mode
1394::CODE;;target = self._system_keyboard.target
1395::CODE;;targettop = max(0, target.to_window(0, target.y)[1]) if target else 0
1396::CODE;;kheight = self._kheight
1397::CODE;;w2, h2 = w / 2., h / 2.
1398::CODE;;r = radians(self.rotation)
1399::CODE;;y = 0
1400::CODE;;_h = h
1401::CODE;;if smode == 'pan':
1402::CODE;;y = kheight
1403::CODE;;elif smode == 'below_target':
1404::CODE;;y = 0 if kheight < targettop else (kheight - targettop)
1405::CODE;;if smode == 'scale':
1406::CODE;;_h -= kheight
1408::CODE;;glViewport(0, 0, w, _h)
1410::CODE;;projection_mat = Matrix()
1411::CODE;;projection_mat.view_clip(0.0, w, 0.0, h, -1.0, 1.0, 0)
1412::CODE;;self.render_context['projection_mat'] = projection_mat
1414::CODE;;modelview_mat = Matrix().translate(w2, h2, 0)
1415::CODE;;modelview_mat = modelview_mat.multiply(Matrix().rotate(r, 0, 0, 1))
1416::CODE;;w, h = self.size
1417::CODE;;w2, h2 = w / 2., h / 2. - y
1418::CODE;;modelview_mat = modelview_mat.multiply(Matrix().translate(-w2, -h2, 0))
1419::CODE;;self.render_context['modelview_mat'] = modelview_mat

1450::CODE;;c_w = shw_min

1840::CODE;;self, callback, target, input_type='text', keyboard_suggestions=True
1841::CODE;;):
1842::CODE;;'''.. versionadded:: 1.0.4
1843::CODE;;Internal widget method to request the keyboard. This method is rarely
1844::CODE;;required by the end-user as it is handled automatically by the
1845::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.textinput.TextInput`. We expose it in case you want
1846::CODE;;to handle the keyboard manually for unique input scenarios.
1847::CODE;;A widget can request the keyboard, indicating a callback to call
1848::CODE;;when the keyboard is released (or taken by another widget).
1849::CODE;;:Parameters:
1850::CODE;;`callback`: func
1851::CODE;;Callback that will be called when the keyboard is
1852::CODE;;closed. This can be because somebody else requested the
1853::CODE;;keyboard or the user closed it.
1854::CODE;;`target`: Widget
1855::CODE;;Attach the keyboard to the specified `target`. This should be
1856::CODE;;the widget that requested the keyboard. Ensure you have a
1857::CODE;;different target attached to each keyboard if you're working in
1858::CODE;;a multi user mode.
1859::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.8
1860::CODE;;`input_type`: string
1861::CODE;;Choose the type of soft keyboard to request. Can be one of
1862::CODE;;'null', 'text', 'number', 'url', 'mail', 'datetime', 'tel',
1863::CODE;;'address'.
1864::CODE;;.. note::
1865::CODE;;`input_type` is currently only honored on Android.

1868::CODE;;Added `null` to soft keyboard types.
1869::CODE;;`keyboard_suggestions`: bool
1870::CODE;;If True provides auto suggestions on top of keyboard.

1872::CODE;;`mail` or `address`.
1873::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 2.1.0

1878::CODE;;*.widget* property.

1881::CODE;;`keyboard_mode`. Please see the Config's

1::CODE;;'''Kivy module for binary dependencies.

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Effects
3::CODE;;=======
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.7.0
5::CODE;;Everything starts with the :class:`~kinetic.KineticEffect`, the base class for
6::CODE;;computing velocity out of a movement.
7::CODE;;This base class is used to implement the :class:`~scroll.ScrollEffect`, a base
8::CODE;;class used for our :class:`~kivy.uix.scrollview.ScrollView` widget effect.
9::CODE;;We have multiple implementations:
10::CODE;;- :class:`~kivy.effects.scroll.ScrollEffect`: base class used for implementing
11::CODE;;an effect. It only calculates the scrolling and the overscroll.
12::CODE;;- :class:`~kivy.effects.dampedscroll.DampedScrollEffect`: uses the overscroll
13::CODE;;information to allow the user to drag more than expected. Once the user stops
14::CODE;;the drag, the position is returned to one of the bounds.
15::CODE;;- :class:`~kivy.effects.opacityscroll.OpacityScrollEffect`: uses the overscroll
16::CODE;;information to reduce the opacity of the scrollview widget. When the user
17::CODE;;stops the drag, the opacity is set back to 1.
18::CODE;;'''
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Damped scroll effect
3::CODE;;====================
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.7.0
5::CODE;;This damped scroll effect will use the
6::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.effects.scroll.ScrollEffect.overscroll` to calculate the scroll
7::CODE;;value, and slows going back to the upper or lower limit.
8::CODE;;'''
9::CODE;;__all__ = ('DampedScrollEffect',)
10::CODE;;from kivy.effects.scroll import ScrollEffect
11::CODE;;from kivy.properties import NumericProperty, BooleanProperty
12::CODE;;from kivy.metrics import sp
13::CODE;;class DampedScrollEffect(ScrollEffect):
14::CODE;;'''DampedScrollEffect class. See the module documentation for more
15::CODE;;information.
16::CODE;;'''
17::CODE;;edge_damping = NumericProperty(0.25)
18::CODE;;'''Edge damping.
19::CODE;;:attr:`edge_damping` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
20::CODE;;defaults to 0.25
21::CODE;;'''
22::CODE;;spring_constant = NumericProperty(2.0)
23::CODE;;'''Spring constant.
24::CODE;;:attr:`spring_constant` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
25::CODE;;defaults to 2.0
26::CODE;;'''
27::CODE;;min_overscroll = NumericProperty(.5)
28::CODE;;'''An overscroll less than this amount will be normalized to 0.
29::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.8.0
30::CODE;;:attr:`min_overscroll` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
31::CODE;;defaults to .5.
32::CODE;;'''
33::CODE;;round_value = BooleanProperty(True)
34::CODE;;'''If True, when the motion stops, :attr:`value` is rounded to the nearest
35::CODE;;integer.
36::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.8.0
37::CODE;;:attr:`round_value` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty` and
38::CODE;;defaults to True.
39::CODE;;'''
40::CODE;;def update_velocity(self, dt):
41::CODE;;if abs(self.velocity) <= self.min_velocity and self.overscroll == 0:
42::CODE;;self.velocity = 0
44::CODE;;if self.round_value:
45::CODE;;self.value = round(self.value)
46::CODE;;return
47::CODE;;total_force = self.velocity * self.friction * dt / self.std_dt
48::CODE;;if abs(self.overscroll) > self.min_overscroll:
49::CODE;;total_force += self.velocity * self.edge_damping
50::CODE;;total_force += self.overscroll * self.spring_constant
51::CODE;;else:
52::CODE;;self.overscroll = 0
53::CODE;;stop_overscroll = ''
54::CODE;;if not self.is_manual:
55::CODE;;if self.overscroll > 0 and self.velocity < 0:
56::CODE;;stop_overscroll = 'max'
57::CODE;;elif self.overscroll < 0 and self.velocity > 0:
58::CODE;;stop_overscroll = 'min'
59::CODE;;self.velocity = self.velocity - total_force
60::CODE;;if not self.is_manual:
61::CODE;;self.apply_distance(self.velocity * dt)
62::CODE;;if stop_overscroll == 'min' and self.value > self.min:
63::CODE;;self.value = self.min
64::CODE;;self.velocity = 0
65::CODE;;return
66::CODE;;if stop_overscroll == 'max' and self.value < self.max:
67::CODE;;self.value = self.max
68::CODE;;self.velocity = 0
69::CODE;;return
70::CODE;;self.trigger_velocity_update()
71::CODE;;def on_value(self, *args):
72::CODE;;scroll_min = self.min
73::CODE;;scroll_max = self.max
74::CODE;;if scroll_min > scroll_max:
75::CODE;;scroll_min, scroll_max = scroll_max, scroll_min
76::CODE;;if self.value < scroll_min:
77::CODE;;self.overscroll = self.value - scroll_min
78::CODE;;elif self.value > scroll_max:
79::CODE;;self.overscroll = self.value - scroll_max
80::CODE;;else:
81::CODE;;self.overscroll = 0
82::CODE;;self.scroll = self.value
83::CODE;;def on_overscroll(self, *args):
84::CODE;;self.trigger_velocity_update()
85::CODE;;def apply_distance(self, distance):
86::CODE;;os = abs(self.overscroll)
87::CODE;;if os:
88::CODE;;distance /= 1. + os / sp(200.)
89::CODE;;super(DampedScrollEffect, self).apply_distance(distance)
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Kinetic effect
3::CODE;;==============
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.7.0
5::CODE;;The :class:`KineticEffect` is the base class that is used to compute the
6::CODE;;velocity out of a movement. When the movement is finished, the effect will
7::CODE;;compute the position of the movement according to the velocity, and reduce the
8::CODE;;velocity with a friction. The movement stop until the velocity is 0.
9::CODE;;Conceptually, the usage could be::
10::CODE;;>>> effect = KineticEffect()
11::CODE;;>>> effect.start(10)
12::CODE;;>>> effect.update(15)
13::CODE;;>>> effect.update(30)
14::CODE;;>>> effect.stop(48)
15::CODE;;Over the time, you will start a movement of a value, update it, and stop the
16::CODE;;movement. At this time, you'll get the movement value into
17::CODE;;:attr:`KineticEffect.value`. On the example i've typed manually, the computed
18::CODE;;velocity will be::
19::CODE;;>>> effect.velocity
20::CODE;;3.1619100231163046
21::CODE;;After multiple clock interaction, the velocity will decrease according to
22::CODE;;:attr:`KineticEffect.friction`. The computed value will be stored in
23::CODE;;:attr:`KineticEffect.value`. The output of this `value` could be::
24::CODE;;46.30038145219605
25::CODE;;54.58302451968686
26::CODE;;61.9229016256196
28::CODE;;'''
29::CODE;;__all__ = ('KineticEffect', )
30::CODE;;from time import time
31::CODE;;from collections import deque
32::CODE;;from kivy.event import EventDispatcher
33::CODE;;from kivy.properties import NumericProperty, BooleanProperty
34::CODE;;from kivy.clock import Clock
35::CODE;;class KineticEffect(EventDispatcher):
36::CODE;;'''Kinetic effect class. See module documentation for more information.
37::CODE;;'''
38::CODE;;velocity = NumericProperty(0)
39::CODE;;'''Velocity of the movement.
40::CODE;;:attr:`velocity` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
41::CODE;;defaults to 0.
42::CODE;;'''
43::CODE;;friction = NumericProperty(0.05)
44::CODE;;'''Friction to apply on the velocity
45::CODE;;:attr:`friction` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
46::CODE;;defaults to 0.05.
47::CODE;;'''
48::CODE;;value = NumericProperty(0)
49::CODE;;'''Value (during the movement and computed) of the effect.
50::CODE;;:attr:`value` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
51::CODE;;defaults to 0.
52::CODE;;'''
53::CODE;;is_manual = BooleanProperty(False)
54::CODE;;'''Indicate if a movement is in progress (True) or not (False).
55::CODE;;:attr:`is_manual` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty` and
56::CODE;;defaults to False.
57::CODE;;'''
58::CODE;;max_history = NumericProperty(5)
59::CODE;;'''Save up to `max_history` movement value into the history. This is used
60::CODE;;for correctly calculating the velocity according to the movement.
61::CODE;;:attr:`max_history` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
62::CODE;;defaults to 5.
63::CODE;;'''
64::CODE;;min_distance = NumericProperty(.1)
65::CODE;;'''The minimal distance for a movement to have nonzero velocity.
66::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.8.0
67::CODE;;:attr:`min_distance` is :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
68::CODE;;defaults to 0.1.
69::CODE;;'''
70::CODE;;min_velocity = NumericProperty(.5)
71::CODE;;'''Velocity below this quantity is normalized to 0. In other words,
72::CODE;;any motion whose velocity falls below this number is stopped.
73::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.8.0
74::CODE;;:attr:`min_velocity` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
75::CODE;;defaults to 0.5.
76::CODE;;'''
77::CODE;;std_dt = NumericProperty(0.017)
78::CODE;;''' std_dt
79::CODE;;correction update_velocity if dt is not constant
80::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 2.0.0
81::CODE;;:attr:`std_dt` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
82::CODE;;defaults to 0.017.
83::CODE;;'''
84::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
85::CODE;;self.history = deque(maxlen=kwargs.get("max_history", self.max_history))
86::CODE;;self.trigger_velocity_update = Clock.create_trigger(
87::CODE;;self.update_velocity, 0)
88::CODE;;super(KineticEffect, self).__init__(**kwargs)
89::CODE;;self.bind(max_history=self._resize_history)
90::CODE;;def _resize_history(self, *args):
91::CODE;;self.history = deque(self.history, maxlen=self.max_history)
92::CODE;;def apply_distance(self, distance):
93::CODE;;if abs(distance) < self.min_distance:
94::CODE;;self.velocity = 0
95::CODE;;self.value += distance
96::CODE;;def start(self, val, t=None):
97::CODE;;'''Start the movement.
98::CODE;;:Parameters:
99::CODE;;`val`: float or int
100::CODE;;Value of the movement
101::CODE;;`t`: float, defaults to None
102::CODE;;Time when the movement happen. If no time is set, it will use
103::CODE;;time.time()
104::CODE;;'''
105::CODE;;self.is_manual = True
106::CODE;;t = t or time()
107::CODE;;self.velocity = 0
108::CODE;;self.history.clear()
109::CODE;;self.history.append((t, val))
110::CODE;;def update(self, val, t=None):
111::CODE;;'''Update the movement.
112::CODE;;See :meth:`start` for the arguments.
113::CODE;;'''
114::CODE;;t = t or time()
115::CODE;;distance = val - self.history[-1][1]
116::CODE;;self.apply_distance(distance)
117::CODE;;self.history.append((t, val))
118::CODE;;def stop(self, val, t=None):
119::CODE;;'''Stop the movement.
120::CODE;;See :meth:`start` for the arguments.
121::CODE;;'''
122::CODE;;self.is_manual = False
123::CODE;;t = t or time()
124::CODE;;distance = val - self.history[-1][1]
125::CODE;;self.apply_distance(distance)
126::CODE;;newest_sample = (t, val)
127::CODE;;old_sample = self.history[0]
128::CODE;;for sample in self.history:
129::CODE;;if (newest_sample[0] - sample[0]) < 10. / 60.:
130::CODE;;break
131::CODE;;old_sample = sample
132::CODE;;distance = newest_sample[1] - old_sample[1]
134::CODE;;duration = abs(newest_sample[0] - old_sample[0])
135::CODE;;self.velocity = (distance / max(duration, 0.0001))
136::CODE;;self.trigger_velocity_update()
137::CODE;;def cancel(self):
138::CODE;;'''Cancel a movement. This can be used in case :meth:`stop` cannot be
139::CODE;;called. It will reset :attr:`is_manual` to False, and compute the
140::CODE;;movement if the velocity is > 0.
141::CODE;;'''
142::CODE;;self.is_manual = False
143::CODE;;self.trigger_velocity_update()
144::CODE;;def update_velocity(self, dt):
145::CODE;;'''(internal) Update the velocity according to the frametime and
146::CODE;;friction.
147::CODE;;'''
148::CODE;;if abs(self.velocity) <= self.min_velocity:
149::CODE;;self.velocity = 0
150::CODE;;return
151::CODE;;self.velocity -= self.velocity * self.friction * dt / self.std_dt
152::CODE;;self.apply_distance(self.velocity * dt)
153::CODE;;self.trigger_velocity_update()
154::CODE;;def halt(self):
155::CODE;;'''Stop the movement immediately without momentum.
156::CODE;;This method immediately stops any ongoing kinetic scrolling effect by:
157::CODE;;- Cancelling any scheduled velocity updates to prevent further movement
158::CODE;;- Setting is_manual to False to indicate no manual interaction is in progress
159::CODE;;Unlike the stop() method which calculates final velocity for momentum
160::CODE;;scrolling, this method provides instant cessation of movement without
161::CODE;;any residual animation.
162::CODE;;This is useful when you need to programmatically stop scrolling in
163::CODE;;response to user actions or when the scroll position needs to be fixed
164::CODE;;immediately. The halt() method is called by ScrollView.scroll_to to
165::CODE;;stop scrolling animation prior to moving to the target widget.
166::CODE;;'''
167::CODE;;self.is_manual = False
168::CODE;;self.velocity = 0
169::CODE;;self.trigger_velocity_update.cancel()
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Opacity scroll effect
3::CODE;;=====================
4::CODE;;Based on the :class:`~kivy.effects.damped.DampedScrollEffect`, this one will
5::CODE;;also decrease the opacity of the target widget during the overscroll.
6::CODE;;'''
7::CODE;;__all__ = ('OpacityScrollEffect', )
8::CODE;;from kivy.effects.dampedscroll import DampedScrollEffect
9::CODE;;class OpacityScrollEffect(DampedScrollEffect):
10::CODE;;'''OpacityScrollEffect class. Uses the overscroll
11::CODE;;information to reduce the opacity of the scrollview widget. When the user
12::CODE;;stops the drag, the opacity is set back to 1.
13::CODE;;'''
14::CODE;;def on_overscroll(self, *args):
15::CODE;;if self.target_widget and self.target_widget.height != 0:
16::CODE;;alpha = (1.0 -
17::CODE;;abs(self.overscroll / float(self.target_widget.height)))
18::CODE;;self.target_widget.opacity = min(1, alpha)
19::CODE;;self.trigger_velocity_update()
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Scroll effect
3::CODE;;=============
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.7.0
5::CODE;;Based on the :class:`~kivy.effects.kinetic` effect, the :class:`ScrollEffect`
6::CODE;;will limit the movement to bounds determined by its :attr:`~ScrollEffect.min`
7::CODE;;and :attr:`~ScrollEffect.max` properties. If the movement exceeds these
8::CODE;;bounds, it will calculate the amount of :attr:`~ScrollEffect.overscroll` and
9::CODE;;try to return to the value of one of the bounds.
10::CODE;;This is very useful for implementing a scrolling list. We actually use this
11::CODE;;class as a base effect for our :class:`~kivy.uix.scrollview.ScrollView` widget.
12::CODE;;'''
13::CODE;;__all__ = ('ScrollEffect', )
14::CODE;;from time import time
15::CODE;;from kivy.effects.kinetic import KineticEffect
16::CODE;;from kivy.uix.widget import Widget
17::CODE;;from kivy.properties import NumericProperty, ObjectProperty
18::CODE;;class ScrollEffect(KineticEffect):
19::CODE;;'''ScrollEffect class. See the module documentation for more information.
20::CODE;;'''
21::CODE;;drag_threshold = NumericProperty('20sp')
22::CODE;;'''Minimum distance to travel before the movement is considered as a drag.
23::CODE;;:attr:`drag_threshold` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
24::CODE;;defaults to 20sp.
25::CODE;;'''
26::CODE;;min = NumericProperty(0)
27::CODE;;'''Minimum boundary to use for scrolling.
28::CODE;;:attr:`min` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and defaults to
29::CODE;;0.
30::CODE;;'''
31::CODE;;max = NumericProperty(0)
32::CODE;;'''Maximum boundary to use for scrolling.
33::CODE;;:attr:`max` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and defaults to
34::CODE;;0.
35::CODE;;'''
36::CODE;;scroll = NumericProperty(0)
37::CODE;;'''Computed value for scrolling. This value is different from
38::CODE;;:py:attr:`kivy.effects.kinetic.KineticEffect.value`
39::CODE;;in that it will return to one of the min/max bounds.
40::CODE;;:attr:`scroll` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and defaults
41::CODE;;to 0.
42::CODE;;'''
43::CODE;;overscroll = NumericProperty(0)
44::CODE;;'''Computed value when the user over-scrolls i.e. goes out of the bounds.
45::CODE;;:attr:`overscroll` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
46::CODE;;defaults to 0.
47::CODE;;'''
48::CODE;;target_widget = ObjectProperty(None, allownone=True, baseclass=Widget)
49::CODE;;'''Widget to attach to this effect. Even if this class doesn't make changes
50::CODE;;to the `target_widget` by default, subclasses can use it to change the
51::CODE;;graphics or apply custom transformations.
52::CODE;;:attr:`target_widget` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.ObjectProperty` and
53::CODE;;defaults to None.
54::CODE;;'''
55::CODE;;displacement = NumericProperty(0)
56::CODE;;'''Cumulative distance of the movement during the interaction. This is used
57::CODE;;to determine if the movement is a drag (more than :attr:`drag_threshold`)
58::CODE;;or not.
59::CODE;;:attr:`displacement` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
60::CODE;;defaults to 0.
61::CODE;;'''
62::CODE;;def reset(self, pos):
63::CODE;;'''(internal) Reset the value and the velocity to the `pos`.
64::CODE;;Mostly used when the bounds are checked.
65::CODE;;'''
66::CODE;;self.value = pos
67::CODE;;self.velocity = 0
68::CODE;;if (history := self.history):
69::CODE;;val = history[-1][1]
70::CODE;;history.clear()
71::CODE;;history.append((time(), val))
72::CODE;;def on_value(self, *args):
73::CODE;;scroll_min = self.min
74::CODE;;scroll_max = self.max
75::CODE;;if scroll_min > scroll_max:
76::CODE;;scroll_min, scroll_max = scroll_max, scroll_min
77::CODE;;if self.value < scroll_min:
78::CODE;;self.overscroll = self.value - scroll_min
79::CODE;;self.reset(scroll_min)
80::CODE;;elif self.value > scroll_max:
81::CODE;;self.overscroll = self.value - scroll_max
82::CODE;;self.reset(scroll_max)
83::CODE;;else:
84::CODE;;self.scroll = self.value
85::CODE;;def start(self, val, t=None):
86::CODE;;self.is_manual = True
87::CODE;;self.displacement = 0
88::CODE;;return super(ScrollEffect, self).start(val, t)
89::CODE;;def update(self, val, t=None):
90::CODE;;self.displacement += abs(val - self.history[-1][1])
91::CODE;;return super(ScrollEffect, self).update(val, t)
92::CODE;;def stop(self, val, t=None):
93::CODE;;self.is_manual = False
94::CODE;;self.displacement += abs(val - self.history[-1][1])
95::CODE;;if self.displacement <= self.drag_threshold:
96::CODE;;self.velocity = 0
97::CODE;;return
98::CODE;;return super(ScrollEffect, self).stop(val, t)
6::CODE;;__all__ = ('EventDispatcher', 'ObjectWithUid', 'Observable')
7::CODE;;import kivy._event
8::CODE;;__doc__ = kivy._event.__doc__
9::CODE;;EventDispatcher = kivy._event.EventDispatcher
10::CODE;;ObjectWithUid = kivy._event.ObjectWithUid
11::CODE;;Observable = kivy._event.Observable
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Event Manager
3::CODE;;=============
4::CODE;;The :class:`EventManagerBase` is the abstract class intended for specific
5::CODE;;implementation of dispatching motion events
6::CODE;;(instances of :class:`~kivy.input.motionevent.MotionEvent`) to widgets through
7::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.on_motion` method of the
8::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget` class.
9::CODE;;.. warning::
10::CODE;;This feature is experimental and it remains so while this warning is
11::CODE;;present.
12::CODE;;Manager is a layer between the window and its widgets.
13::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.core.window.WindowBase` will forward all the events it receives
14::CODE;;in :meth:`~kivy.core.window.WindowBase.on_motion` method to the all managers
15::CODE;;who declared to receive types of those events. Event will continue to go
16::CODE;;through the managers list even if one of them accept it (by returning `True`).
17::CODE;;When to use an event manager
18::CODE;;----------------------------
19::CODE;;Use a manager when you want to:
20::CODE;;- Dispatch touch, hover, keyboard, joystick or any other events to the widgets
21::CODE;;through :meth:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.on_motion` method.
22::CODE;;- Dispatch filtered motion events by any criteria, like by a
23::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.input.motionevent.MotionEvent.device` or a
24::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.input.motionevent.MotionEvent.profile`.
25::CODE;;- Combine several motion events (touch, hover etc.) into one new event and
26::CODE;;dispatch it to the widgets.
27::CODE;;- Dispatch one-time generic events, like app pause/resume.
28::CODE;;- Write an event simulator, like a touch simulator which draws a circle on
29::CODE;;window's canvas for every simulated touch.
30::CODE;;Defining and registering an event manager
31::CODE;;-----------------------------------------
32::CODE;;1. Inherit :class:`EventManagerBase` and set which events this manager
33::CODE;;should receive by declaring event types in
34::CODE;;:attr:`EventManagerBase.type_ids` attribute.
35::CODE;;2. Implement :meth:`EventManagerBase.dispatch` which will be called by window
36::CODE;;to pass event type (one of "begin", "update", "end") and an event.
37::CODE;;3. Implement :meth:`EventManagerBase.start` and :meth:`EventManagerBase.stop`
38::CODE;;to allocate and release additional resources if needed.
39::CODE;;4. Register a manager instance to window using method
40::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.core.window.WindowBase.register_event_manager`. This can be
41::CODE;;done by overriding methods :meth:`~kivy.app.App.build` or
42::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.app.App.on_start`.
43::CODE;;All registered managers are kept in the
44::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.core.window.WindowBase.event_managers` list. To unregister a
45::CODE;;manager call :meth:`~kivy.core.window.WindowBase.unregister_event_manager`
46::CODE;;which itself can be called in :meth:`~kivy.app.App.on_stop` method.
47::CODE;;Dispatching events to the widgets
48::CODE;;---------------------------------
49::CODE;;Once registered, window will start the manager and forward all events of types
50::CODE;;declared in :attr:`EventManagerBase.type_ids` to the manager's
51::CODE;;:meth:`EventManagerBase.dispatch` method. It's up to manager to decide how to
52::CODE;;dispatch them, either by going through :attr:`EventManagerBase.window.children`
53::CODE;;list and dispatching `on_motion` event or by using some different logic. It's
54::CODE;;also up to manager to dispatch grabbed events if grab feature is supported by
55::CODE;;the event (see :meth:`~kivy.input.motionevent.MotionEvent.grab` and
56::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.input.motionevent.MotionEvent.ungrab` methods).
57::CODE;;Manager can assign a different dispatch mode to decide how event
58::CODE;;should be dispatched throughout the widget tree by changing the value of the
59::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.input.motionevent.MotionEvent.dispatch_mode` attribute. Before
60::CODE;;changing the mode manager should store/restore the current one, either by using
61::CODE;;a local variable or by using event's
62::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.input.motionevent.MotionEvent.push` /
63::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.input.motionevent.MotionEvent.pop` methods.
64::CODE;;Currently there are three dispatch modes (behaviors) recognized by the
65::CODE;;`on_motion` method in :class:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget` class:
66::CODE;;1. Default dispatch (requires :const:`MODE_DEFAULT_DISPATCH`) - event will go
67::CODE;;through widget's `children` list, starting with the first widget in the
68::CODE;;list until event gets accepted or last widget registered for that event is
69::CODE;;reached. Mode :const:`MODE_DEFAULT_DISPATCH` is assigned by default in
70::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.input.motionevent.MotionEvent` class.
71::CODE;;2. Filtered dispatch (requires :const:`MODE_FILTERED_DISPATCH`) - event will go
72::CODE;;only through registered child widgets.
73::CODE;;3. No dispatch to children (requires :const:`MODE_DONT_DISPATCH`) - event will
74::CODE;;not be dispatched to child widgets.
75::CODE;;Note that window does not have a `motion_filter` property and therefore does
76::CODE;;not have a list of filtered widgets from its `children` list.
77::CODE;;'''
78::CODE;;MODE_DEFAULT_DISPATCH = 'default'
79::CODE;;'''Assign this mode to make event dispatch through widget's `children` list,
80::CODE;;starting with the first widget in the list until event gets accepted or last
81::CODE;;widget registered for that event is reached. Widgets after the last registered
82::CODE;;widget are ignored.
83::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 2.1.0
84::CODE;;'''
85::CODE;;MODE_FILTERED_DISPATCH = 'filtered'
86::CODE;;'''Assign this mode to make event dispatch only to child widgets which were
87::CODE;;previously registered to receive events of the same
88::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.input.motionevent.MotionEvent.type_id` and not to all
89::CODE;;child widgets.
90::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 2.1.0
91::CODE;;'''
92::CODE;;MODE_DONT_DISPATCH = 'none'
93::CODE;;'''Assign this mode to prevent event from dispatching to child widgets.
94::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 2.1.0
95::CODE;;'''
96::CODE;;class EventManagerBase(object):
97::CODE;;'''Abstract class with methods :meth:`start`, :meth:`stop` and
98::CODE;;:meth:`dispatch` for specific class to implement.
99::CODE;;Example of the manager receiving touch and hover events::
100::CODE;;class TouchHoverManager(EventManagerBase):
101::CODE;;type_ids = ('touch', 'hover')
102::CODE;;def start(self):
104::CODE;;def dispatch(self, etype, me):
105::CODE;;if me.type_id == 'touch':
107::CODE;;elif me.type_id == 'hover'
109::CODE;;def stop(self):
111::CODE;;'''
112::CODE;;type_ids = None
113::CODE;;'''Override this attribute to declare the type ids of the events which
114::CODE;;manager wants to receive. This attribute will be used by
115::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.core.window.WindowBase` to know which events to pass to the
116::CODE;;:meth:`dispatch` method.
117::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 2.1.0
118::CODE;;'''
119::CODE;;window = None
120::CODE;;'''Holds the instance of the :class:`~kivy.core.window.WindowBase`.
121::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 2.1.0
122::CODE;;'''
123::CODE;;def start(self):
124::CODE;;'''Start the manager, bind callbacks to the objects and create
125::CODE;;additional resources. Attribute :attr:`window` is assigned when this
126::CODE;;method is called.
127::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 2.1.0
128::CODE;;'''
129::CODE;;def dispatch(self, etype, me):
130::CODE;;'''Dispatch event `me` to the widgets in the :attr:`window`.
131::CODE;;:Parameters:
132::CODE;;`etype`: `str`
133::CODE;;One of "begin", "update" or "end"
134::CODE;;`me`: :class:`~kivy.input.motionevent.MotionEvent`
135::CODE;;The Motion Event currently dispatched.
136::CODE;;:Returns: `bool`
137::CODE;;`True` to stop event dispatching
138::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 2.1.0
139::CODE;;'''
140::CODE;;def stop(self):
141::CODE;;'''Stop the manager, unbind from any objects and release any allocated
142::CODE;;resources.
143::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 2.1.0
144::CODE;;'''
1::CODE;;'''Pygments lexer for kv language

6::CODE;;from pygments.token import Comment, Text, Name, Punctuation, Operator
7::CODE;;from pygments.formatters import get_formatter_by_name
8::CODE;;import sys
9::CODE;;class KivyLexer(RegexLexer):
10::CODE;;name = 'Kivy'
11::CODE;;aliases = ['kivy', 'kv']
12::CODE;;filenames = ['*.kv']
13::CODE;;tokens = {
14::CODE;;'root': [
17::CODE;;(r'\s+', Text),
18::CODE;;(r'<.+>', Name.Namespace),

20::CODE;;bygroups(Punctuation, Text, Name.Class, Text, Operator),
21::CODE;;'classList'),
22::CODE;;(r'[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$', Name.Attribute),
23::CODE;;(r'(.*?)(\s*)(:)(\s*)$',
24::CODE;;bygroups(Name.Class, Text, Punctuation, Text)),
25::CODE;;(r'(.*?)(\s*)(:)(\s*)(.*?)$',
26::CODE;;bygroups(Name.Attribute, Text, Punctuation, Text,
27::CODE;;using(PythonLexer))),
28::CODE;;(r'[^:]+?$', using(PythonLexer))],
29::CODE;;'classList': [
30::CODE;;(r'(,)(\s*)([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*)',
31::CODE;;bygroups(Punctuation, Text, Name.Class)),
32::CODE;;(r'(\+)(\s*)([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*)',
33::CODE;;bygroups(Operator, Text, Name.Class)),
34::CODE;;(r'\s+', Text),
35::CODE;;(r'[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*', Name.Class),
37::CODE;;if __name__ == '__main__':
38::CODE;;''' This lexer will highlight .kv file. The first argument is the source
39::CODE;;file, the second argument is the format of the destination and the third
40::CODE;;argument is the output filename
41::CODE;;'''
42::CODE;;if len(sys.argv) != 4:
43::CODE;;raise Exception('Three arguments expected, found %s' %

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Factory object
3::CODE;;==============
4::CODE;;The factory can be used to automatically register any class or module
5::CODE;;and instantiate classes from it anywhere in your project. It is an
6::CODE;;implementation of the
7::CODE;;`Factory Pattern <http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Factory_pattern>`_.
8::CODE;;The class list and available modules are automatically generated by setup.py.
9::CODE;;Example for registering a class/module::
10::CODE;;>>> from kivy.factory import Factory
11::CODE;;>>> Factory.register('Widget', module='kivy.uix.widget')
12::CODE;;>>> Factory.register('Vector', module='kivy.vector')
13::CODE;;Example of using the Factory::
14::CODE;;>>> from kivy.factory import Factory
15::CODE;;>>> widget = Factory.Widget(pos=(456,456))
16::CODE;;>>> vector = Factory.Vector(9, 2)
17::CODE;;Example using a class name::
18::CODE;;>>> from kivy.factory import Factory
19::CODE;;>>> Factory.register('MyWidget', cls=MyWidget)
20::CODE;;By default, the first classname you register via the factory is permanent.
21::CODE;;If you wish to change the registered class, you need to unregister the
22::CODE;;classname before you re-assign it::
23::CODE;;>>> from kivy.factory import Factory
24::CODE;;>>> Factory.register('MyWidget', cls=MyWidget)
25::CODE;;>>> widget = Factory.MyWidget()
26::CODE;;>>> Factory.unregister('MyWidget')
27::CODE;;>>> Factory.register('MyWidget', cls=CustomWidget)
28::CODE;;>>> customWidget = Factory.MyWidget()
29::CODE;;'''
30::CODE;;__all__ = ('Factory', 'FactoryBase', 'FactoryException')
31::CODE;;import copy
32::CODE;;import importlib
33::CODE;;from kivy.logger import Logger
34::CODE;;from kivy.context import register_context
35::CODE;;class FactoryException(Exception):
36::CODE;;pass
37::CODE;;class FactoryBase(object):
38::CODE;;def __init__(self):
39::CODE;;super(FactoryBase, self).__init__()
40::CODE;;self.classes = {}
41::CODE;;@classmethod
42::CODE;;def create_from(cls, factory):
48::CODE;;obj = cls()
49::CODE;;obj.classes = copy.copy(factory.classes)
50::CODE;;return obj
51::CODE;;def is_template(self, classname):
52::CODE;;'''Return True if the classname is a template from the
53::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.lang.Builder`.
54::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.5
55::CODE;;'''
56::CODE;;if classname in self.classes:
57::CODE;;return self.classes[classname]['is_template']
58::CODE;;else:
59::CODE;;return False
60::CODE;;def register(self, classname, cls=None, module=None, is_template=False,
61::CODE;;baseclasses=None, filename=None, warn=False):
62::CODE;;'''Register a new classname referring to a real class or
63::CODE;;class definition in a module. Warn, if True will emit a warning message
64::CODE;;when a class is re-declared.
65::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.9.0
66::CODE;;`warn` was added.
67::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.7.0
68::CODE;;:attr:`baseclasses` and :attr:`filename` added
69::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.0.5
70::CODE;;:attr:`is_template` has been added in 1.0.5.
71::CODE;;'''
72::CODE;;if cls is None and module is None and baseclasses is None:
73::CODE;;raise ValueError(
74::CODE;;'You must specify either cls= or module= or baseclasses =')
75::CODE;;if classname in self.classes:
76::CODE;;if warn:
77::CODE;;info = self.classes[classname]
78::CODE;;Logger.warning('Factory: Ignored class "{}" re-declaration. '
79::CODE;;'Current - module: {}, cls: {}, baseclass: {}, filename: {}. '
80::CODE;;'Ignored - module: {}, cls: {}, baseclass: {}, filename: {}.'.
81::CODE;;format(classname, info['module'], info['cls'],
82::CODE;;info['baseclasses'], info['filename'], module, cls,
83::CODE;;baseclasses, filename))
84::CODE;;return
85::CODE;;self.classes[classname] = {
86::CODE;;'module': module,
87::CODE;;'cls': cls,
88::CODE;;'is_template': is_template,
89::CODE;;'baseclasses': baseclasses,
90::CODE;;'filename': filename}
91::CODE;;def unregister(self, *classnames):
92::CODE;;'''Unregisters the classnames previously registered via the
93::CODE;;register method. This allows the same classnames to be re-used in
94::CODE;;different contexts.
95::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.7.1
96::CODE;;'''
97::CODE;;for classname in classnames:
98::CODE;;if classname in self.classes:
99::CODE;;self.classes.pop(classname)
100::CODE;;def unregister_from_filename(self, filename):
101::CODE;;'''Unregister all the factory objects related to the filename passed in
102::CODE;;the parameter.
103::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.7.0
104::CODE;;'''
105::CODE;;to_remove = [x for x in self.classes
106::CODE;;if self.classes[x]['filename'] == filename]
107::CODE;;for name in to_remove:
108::CODE;;del self.classes[name]
109::CODE;;def __getattr__(self, name):
110::CODE;;classes = self.classes
111::CODE;;if name not in classes:
112::CODE;;if name[0] == name[0].lower():
115::CODE;;raise AttributeError(
116::CODE;;'First letter of class name <%s> is in lowercase' % name)
117::CODE;;raise FactoryException('Unknown class <%s>' % name)
118::CODE;;item = classes[name]
119::CODE;;cls = item['cls']
121::CODE;;if cls is None:
122::CODE;;if item['module']:
123::CODE;;module = importlib.__import__(
124::CODE;;name=item['module'],
125::CODE;;fromlist='*',
127::CODE;;)
128::CODE;;if not hasattr(module, name):
129::CODE;;raise FactoryException(
130::CODE;;'No class named <%s> in module <%s>' % (
131::CODE;;name, item['module']))
132::CODE;;cls = item['cls'] = getattr(module, name)
133::CODE;;elif item['baseclasses']:
134::CODE;;rootwidgets = []
135::CODE;;for basecls in item['baseclasses'].split('+'):
136::CODE;;rootwidgets.append(Factory.get(basecls))
137::CODE;;cls = item['cls'] = type(str(name), tuple(rootwidgets), {})
138::CODE;;else:
139::CODE;;raise FactoryException('No information to create the class')
140::CODE;;return cls
141::CODE;;get = __getattr__
143::CODE;;Factory: FactoryBase = register_context('Factory', FactoryBase)
147::CODE;;Logger.info('Factory: %d symbols loaded' % len(Factory.classes))

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Garden
3::CODE;;======
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.7.0
5::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.11.1
6::CODE;;Garden is a project to centralize addons for Kivy maintained by users. You can
7::CODE;;find more information at `Kivy Garden <http://kivy-garden.github.io/>`_. All
8::CODE;;the garden packages are centralized on the `kivy-garden Github
9::CODE;;<https://github.com/kivy-garden>`_ repository.
10::CODE;;.. warning::
11::CODE;;The garden flower widgets are contributed by regular users such as
12::CODE;;yourself. The kivy developers do not take any responsibility for the code
13::CODE;;hosted in the garden organization repositories - we do not actively monitor
14::CODE;;the flower repos. Please use at your own risk.
15::CODE;;Update to garden structure
16::CODE;;--------------------------
17::CODE;;Starting with the kivy 1.11.0 release, kivy has
18::CODE;;`shifted <https://github.com/kivy/kivy/wiki/Moving-kivy.garden.xxx-to-kivy_\
19::CODE;;garden.xxx-and-kivy.deps.xxx-to-kivy_deps.xxx>`_ from using the garden legacy
20::CODE;;tool that installs flowers with `garden install flower` where the flower
21::CODE;;does not have a proper python package structure to flowers that can be
22::CODE;;installed with pip and uploaded to pypi. Kivy supports the legacy garden
23::CODE;;flowers side by side with the newer packages so the garden tool and legacy
24::CODE;;flowers will be able to be used indefinitely. But we will only provide support
25::CODE;;for the newer packages format in the future.
26::CODE;;For garden package maintainers - for a guide how to migrate your garden package
27::CODE;;from the legacy structure `garden.flower` to the newer `flower` structure used
28::CODE;;with the pip, see `this guide
30::CODE;;We hope most garden packages will be converted to the newer format to help
31::CODE;;with installation.
32::CODE;;General Usage Guidelines
33::CODE;;------------------------
34::CODE;;To use a kivy garden flower, first check if the flower is in the legacy format.
35::CODE;;If the flower name is in the format of `garden.flower`, such as
36::CODE;;`garden.graph <https://github.com/kivy-garden/garden.graph>`_ it is a legacy
37::CODE;;flower. If it is just `flower` such as
38::CODE;;`graph <https://github.com/kivy-garden/graph>`_ it is in the present format.
39::CODE;;If it is in the legacy format see `Legacy garden tool instructions`_ for how to
40::CODE;;install and use it. Otherwise, continue with the guide below.
41::CODE;;Garden flowers can now be installed with the `pip` tool like a normal python
42::CODE;;package. Given a flower that you want to install, lets use
43::CODE;;`graph <https://github.com/kivy-garden/graph>`_ as an example. You can install
44::CODE;;master directly from github with::
45::CODE;;python -m pip install \
46::CODE;;https://github.com/kivy-garden/graph/archive/master.zip
47::CODE;;Look under the repository's releases tab if you'd like to install a specific
48::CODE;;release or a pre-compiled wheel, if the flower has any. Then use the url with
49::CODE;;`pip`.
50::CODE;;Or you can automatically install it using garden's pypi server with::
51::CODE;;python -m pip install kivy_garden.graph \
52::CODE;;--extra-index-url https://kivy-garden.github.io/simple/
53::CODE;;To permanently add our garden server to your pip configuration so that you
54::CODE;;don't have to specify it with `--extra-index-url`, add::
55::CODE;;[global]
56::CODE;;timeout = 60
57::CODE;;index-url = https://kivy-garden.github.io/simple/
59::CODE;;If the flower maintainer has uploaded the flower to
60::CODE;;`pypi <https://pypi.org/>`_, you can just install it with
61::CODE;;`pip install kivy_garden.flower`.
62::CODE;;Legacy garden tool instructions
63::CODE;;-------------------------------
64::CODE;;Garden is now distributed as a separate Python module, kivy-garden. You can
65::CODE;;install it with pip::
66::CODE;;pip install kivy-garden
67::CODE;;The garden module does not initially include any packages. You can download
68::CODE;;them with the garden tool installed by the pip package::
70::CODE;;garden install graph
72::CODE;;garden install --upgrade graph
74::CODE;;garden uninstall graph
76::CODE;;garden list
78::CODE;;garden search
80::CODE;;garden search graph
82::CODE;;garden --help
83::CODE;;All the garden packages are installed by default in `~/.kivy/garden`.
84::CODE;;.. Note:: In previous versions of Kivy, garden was a tool at
85::CODE;;kivy/tools/garden. This no longer exists, but the
86::CODE;;kivy-garden module provides exactly the same functionality.
87::CODE;;Packaging
88::CODE;;~~~~~~~~~
89::CODE;;If you want to include garden packages in your application, you can add `--app`
90::CODE;;to the `install` command. This will create a `libs/garden` directory in your
91::CODE;;current directory which will be used by `kivy.garden`.
92::CODE;;For example::
93::CODE;;cd myapp
94::CODE;;garden install --app graph
95::CODE;;'''
96::CODE;;__path__ = 'kivy.garden'
