1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Geometry utilities
3::CODE;;==================
4::CODE;;This module contains some helper functions for geometric calculations.
5::CODE;;'''
6::CODE;;__all__ = ('circumcircle', 'minimum_bounding_circle')
7::CODE;;from kivy.vector import Vector
8::CODE;;def circumcircle(a, b, c):
9::CODE;;'''
10::CODE;;Computes the circumcircle of a triangle defined by a, b, c.
11::CODE;;See: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circumscribed_circle
12::CODE;;:Parameters:
13::CODE;;`a`: iterable containing at least 2 values (for x and y)
14::CODE;;The 1st point of the triangle.
15::CODE;;`b`: iterable containing at least 2 values (for x and y)
16::CODE;;The 2nd point of the triangle.
17::CODE;;`c`: iterable containing at least 2 values (for x and y)
18::CODE;;The 3rd point of the triangle.
19::CODE;;:Return:
20::CODE;;A tuple that defines the circle :
21::CODE;;* The first element in the returned tuple is the center as (x, y)
22::CODE;;* The second is the radius (float)
23::CODE;;'''
24::CODE;;P = Vector(a[0], a[1])
25::CODE;;Q = Vector(b[0], b[1])
26::CODE;;R = Vector(c[0], c[1])
27::CODE;;mPQ = (P + Q) * .5
28::CODE;;mQR = (Q + R) * .5
29::CODE;;numer = -(- mPQ.y * R.y + mPQ.y * Q.y + mQR.y * R.y - mQR.y * Q.y -
30::CODE;;mPQ.x * R.x + mPQ.x * Q.x + mQR.x * R.x - mQR.x * Q.x)
31::CODE;;denom = (-Q.x * R.y + P.x * R.y - P.x * Q.y +
32::CODE;;Q.y * R.x - P.y * R.x + P.y * Q.x)
33::CODE;;t = numer / denom
34::CODE;;cx = -t * (Q.y - P.y) + mPQ.x
35::CODE;;cy = t * (Q.x - P.x) + mPQ.y
36::CODE;;return ((cx, cy), (P - (cx, cy)).length())
37::CODE;;def minimum_bounding_circle(points):
38::CODE;;'''
39::CODE;;Returns the minimum bounding circle for a set of points.
40::CODE;;For a description of the problem being solved, see the `Smallest Circle
41::CODE;;Problem <http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smallest_circle_problem>`_.
42::CODE;;The function uses Applet's Algorithm, the runtime is ``O(h^3, *n)``,
43::CODE;;where h is the number of points in the convex hull of the set of points.
44::CODE;;**But** it runs in linear time in almost all real world cases.
45::CODE;;See: http://tinyurl.com/6e4n5yb
46::CODE;;:Parameters:
47::CODE;;`points`: iterable
48::CODE;;A list of points (2 tuple with x,y coordinates)
49::CODE;;:Return:
50::CODE;;A tuple that defines the circle:
51::CODE;;* The first element in the returned tuple is the center (x, y)
52::CODE;;* The second the radius (float)
53::CODE;;'''
54::CODE;;points = [Vector(p[0], p[1]) for p in points]
55::CODE;;if len(points) == 1:
56::CODE;;return (points[0].x, points[0].y), 0.0
57::CODE;;if len(points) == 2:
58::CODE;;p1, p2 = points
59::CODE;;return (p1 + p2) * .5, ((p1 - p2) * .5).length()
61::CODE;;P = min(points, key=lambda p: p.y)
64::CODE;;def x_axis_angle(q):
65::CODE;;if q == P:
67::CODE;;return abs((q - P).angle((1, 0)))
68::CODE;;Q = min(points, key=x_axis_angle)
69::CODE;;for p in points:
71::CODE;;def angle_pq(r):
72::CODE;;if r in (P, Q):
74::CODE;;return abs((r - P).angle(r - Q))
75::CODE;;R = min(points, key=angle_pq)
78::CODE;;if angle_pq(R) > 90.0:
79::CODE;;return (P + Q) * .5, ((P - Q) * .5).length()
81::CODE;;if abs((R - P).angle(Q - P)) > 90:
82::CODE;;P = R
83::CODE;;continue
85::CODE;;if abs((P - Q).angle(R - Q)) > 90:
86::CODE;;Q = R
87::CODE;;continue
90::CODE;;break
92::CODE;;return circumcircle(P, Q, R)
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Gesture recognition
3::CODE;;===================
4::CODE;;This class allows you to easily create new
5::CODE;;gestures and compare them::
6::CODE;;from kivy.gesture import Gesture, GestureDatabase
8::CODE;;g = Gesture()
9::CODE;;g.add_stroke(point_list=[(1,1), (3,4), (2,1)])
10::CODE;;g.normalize()
12::CODE;;gdb = GestureDatabase()
13::CODE;;gdb.add_gesture(g)
15::CODE;;g2 = Gesture()
17::CODE;;gdb.find(g2)
18::CODE;;.. warning::
19::CODE;;You don't really want to do this: it's more of an example of how
20::CODE;;to construct gestures dynamically. Typically, you would
21::CODE;;need a lot more points, so it's better to record gestures in a file and
22::CODE;;reload them to compare later. Look in the examples/gestures directory for
23::CODE;;an example of how to do that.
24::CODE;;'''
25::CODE;;__all__ = ('Gesture', 'GestureDatabase', 'GesturePoint', 'GestureStroke')
26::CODE;;import pickle
27::CODE;;import base64
28::CODE;;import zlib
29::CODE;;import math
30::CODE;;from kivy.vector import Vector
31::CODE;;from io import BytesIO
32::CODE;;class GestureDatabase(object):
33::CODE;;'''Class to handle a gesture database.'''
34::CODE;;def __init__(self):
35::CODE;;self.db = []
36::CODE;;def add_gesture(self, gesture):
37::CODE;;'''Add a new gesture to the database.'''
38::CODE;;self.db.append(gesture)
39::CODE;;def find(self, gesture, minscore=0.9, rotation_invariant=True):
40::CODE;;'''Find a matching gesture in the database.'''
41::CODE;;if not gesture:
42::CODE;;return
43::CODE;;best = None
44::CODE;;bestscore = minscore
45::CODE;;for g in self.db:
46::CODE;;score = g.get_score(gesture, rotation_invariant)
47::CODE;;if score < bestscore:
48::CODE;;continue
49::CODE;;bestscore = score
50::CODE;;best = g
51::CODE;;if not best:
52::CODE;;return
53::CODE;;return (bestscore, best)
54::CODE;;def gesture_to_str(self, gesture):
55::CODE;;'''Convert a gesture into a unique string.'''
56::CODE;;io = BytesIO()
57::CODE;;p = pickle.Pickler(io)
58::CODE;;p.dump(gesture)
59::CODE;;data = base64.b64encode(zlib.compress(io.getvalue(), 9))
60::CODE;;return data
61::CODE;;def str_to_gesture(self, data):
62::CODE;;'''Convert a unique string to a gesture.'''
63::CODE;;io = BytesIO(zlib.decompress(base64.b64decode(data)))
64::CODE;;p = pickle.Unpickler(io)
65::CODE;;gesture = p.load()
66::CODE;;return gesture
67::CODE;;class GesturePoint:
68::CODE;;def __init__(self, x, y):
69::CODE;;'''Stores the x,y coordinates of a point in the gesture.'''
70::CODE;;self.x = float(x)
71::CODE;;self.y = float(y)
72::CODE;;def scale(self, factor):
73::CODE;;''' Scales the point by the given factor.'''
74::CODE;;self.x *= factor
75::CODE;;self.y *= factor
76::CODE;;return self
77::CODE;;def __repr__(self):
78::CODE;;return 'Mouse_point: %f,%f' % (self.x, self.y)
79::CODE;;class GestureStroke:
80::CODE;;''' Gestures can be made up of multiple strokes.'''
81::CODE;;def __init__(self):
82::CODE;;''' A stroke in the gesture.'''
83::CODE;;self.points = list()
84::CODE;;self.screenpoints = list()
86::CODE;;@property
87::CODE;;def max_x(self):
88::CODE;;if len(self.points) == 0:
89::CODE;;return 0
90::CODE;;return max(self.points, key=lambda pt: pt.x).x
91::CODE;;@property
92::CODE;;def min_x(self):
93::CODE;;if len(self.points) == 0:
94::CODE;;return 0
95::CODE;;return min(self.points, key=lambda pt: pt.x).x
96::CODE;;@property
97::CODE;;def max_y(self):
98::CODE;;if len(self.points) == 0:
99::CODE;;return 0
100::CODE;;return max(self.points, key=lambda pt: pt.y).y
101::CODE;;@property
102::CODE;;def min_y(self):
103::CODE;;if len(self.points) == 0:
104::CODE;;return 0
105::CODE;;return min(self.points, key=lambda pt: pt.y).y
106::CODE;;def add_point(self, x, y):
107::CODE;;'''
108::CODE;;add_point(x=x_pos, y=y_pos)
109::CODE;;Adds a point to the stroke.
110::CODE;;'''
111::CODE;;self.points.append(GesturePoint(x, y))
112::CODE;;self.screenpoints.append((x, y))
113::CODE;;def scale_stroke(self, scale_factor):
114::CODE;;'''
115::CODE;;scale_stroke(scale_factor=float)
116::CODE;;Scales the stroke down by scale_factor.
117::CODE;;'''
118::CODE;;self.points = [pt.scale(scale_factor) for pt in self.points]
119::CODE;;def points_distance(self, point1, point2):
120::CODE;;'''
121::CODE;;points_distance(point1=GesturePoint, point2=GesturePoint)
122::CODE;;Returns the distance between two GesturePoints.
123::CODE;;'''
124::CODE;;x = point1.x - point2.x
125::CODE;;y = point1.y - point2.y
126::CODE;;return math.sqrt(x * x + y * y)
127::CODE;;def stroke_length(self, point_list=None):
128::CODE;;'''Finds the length of the stroke. If a point list is given,
129::CODE;;finds the length of that list.
130::CODE;;'''
131::CODE;;if point_list is None:
132::CODE;;point_list = self.points
133::CODE;;gesture_length = 0.0
135::CODE;;return gesture_length
136::CODE;;for i in range(len(point_list) - 1):
137::CODE;;gesture_length += self.points_distance(
138::CODE;;point_list[i], point_list[i + 1])
139::CODE;;return gesture_length
140::CODE;;def normalize_stroke(self, sample_points=32):
141::CODE;;'''Normalizes strokes so that every stroke has a standard number of
142::CODE;;points. Returns True if stroke is normalized, False if it can't be
143::CODE;;normalized. sample_points controls the resolution of the stroke.
144::CODE;;'''
146::CODE;;if len(self.points) <= 1 or self.stroke_length(self.points) == 0.0:
147::CODE;;return False
149::CODE;;target_stroke_size = \
150::CODE;;self.stroke_length(self.points) / float(sample_points)
151::CODE;;new_points = list()
152::CODE;;new_points.append(self.points[0])
154::CODE;;prev = self.points[0]
155::CODE;;src_distance = 0.0
156::CODE;;dst_distance = target_stroke_size
157::CODE;;for curr in self.points[1:]:
158::CODE;;d = self.points_distance(prev, curr)
159::CODE;;if d > 0:
160::CODE;;prev = curr
161::CODE;;src_distance = src_distance + d
164::CODE;;while dst_distance < src_distance:
165::CODE;;x_dir = curr.x - prev.x
166::CODE;;y_dir = curr.y - prev.y
167::CODE;;ratio = (src_distance - dst_distance) / d
168::CODE;;to_x = x_dir * ratio + prev.x
169::CODE;;to_y = y_dir * ratio + prev.y
170::CODE;;new_points.append(GesturePoint(to_x, to_y))
171::CODE;;dst_distance = self.stroke_length(self.points) / \
172::CODE;;float(sample_points) * len(new_points)
174::CODE;;if not len(new_points) == sample_points:
175::CODE;;raise ValueError('Invalid number of strokes points; got '
176::CODE;;'%d while it should be %d' %
177::CODE;;(len(new_points), sample_points))
178::CODE;;self.points = new_points
179::CODE;;return True
180::CODE;;def center_stroke(self, offset_x, offset_y):
181::CODE;;'''Centers the stroke by offsetting the points.'''
182::CODE;;for point in self.points:
183::CODE;;point.x -= offset_x
184::CODE;;point.y -= offset_y
185::CODE;;class Gesture:
186::CODE;;'''A python implementation of a gesture recognition algorithm by
187::CODE;;Oleg Dopertchouk: http://www.gamedev.net/reference/articles/article2039.asp
188::CODE;;Implemented by Jeiel Aranal (chemikhazi@gmail.com),
189::CODE;;released into the public domain.
190::CODE;;'''
192::CODE;;DEFAULT_TOLERANCE = 0.1
193::CODE;;def __init__(self, tolerance=None):
194::CODE;;'''
195::CODE;;Gesture([tolerance=float])
196::CODE;;Creates a new gesture with an optional matching tolerance value.
197::CODE;;'''
198::CODE;;self.width = 0.
199::CODE;;self.height = 0.
200::CODE;;self.gesture_product = 0.
201::CODE;;self.strokes = list()
202::CODE;;if tolerance is None:
203::CODE;;self.tolerance = Gesture.DEFAULT_TOLERANCE
204::CODE;;else:
205::CODE;;self.tolerance = tolerance
206::CODE;;def _scale_gesture(self):
207::CODE;;''' Scales down the gesture to a unit of 1.'''
210::CODE;;min_x = min([stroke.min_x for stroke in self.strokes])
211::CODE;;max_x = max([stroke.max_x for stroke in self.strokes])
212::CODE;;min_y = min([stroke.min_y for stroke in self.strokes])
213::CODE;;max_y = max([stroke.max_y for stroke in self.strokes])
214::CODE;;x_len = max_x - min_x
215::CODE;;self.width = x_len
216::CODE;;y_len = max_y - min_y
217::CODE;;self.height = y_len
218::CODE;;scale_factor = max(x_len, y_len)
219::CODE;;if scale_factor <= 0.0:
220::CODE;;return False
221::CODE;;scale_factor = 1.0 / scale_factor
222::CODE;;for stroke in self.strokes:
223::CODE;;stroke.scale_stroke(scale_factor)
224::CODE;;return True
225::CODE;;def _center_gesture(self):
226::CODE;;''' Centers the Gesture.points of the gesture.'''
227::CODE;;total_x = 0.0
228::CODE;;total_y = 0.0
229::CODE;;total_points = 0
230::CODE;;for stroke in self.strokes:
232::CODE;;stroke_y = sum([pt.y for pt in stroke.points])
233::CODE;;stroke_x = sum([pt.x for pt in stroke.points])
234::CODE;;total_y += stroke_y
235::CODE;;total_x += stroke_x
236::CODE;;total_points += len(stroke.points)
237::CODE;;if total_points == 0:
238::CODE;;return False
240::CODE;;total_x /= total_points
241::CODE;;total_y /= total_points
243::CODE;;for stroke in self.strokes:
244::CODE;;stroke.center_stroke(total_x, total_y)
245::CODE;;return True
246::CODE;;def add_stroke(self, point_list=None):
247::CODE;;'''Adds a stroke to the gesture and returns the Stroke instance.
248::CODE;;Optional point_list argument is a list of the mouse points for
249::CODE;;the stroke.
250::CODE;;'''
251::CODE;;self.strokes.append(GestureStroke())
252::CODE;;if isinstance(point_list, list) or isinstance(point_list, tuple):
253::CODE;;for point in point_list:
254::CODE;;if isinstance(point, GesturePoint):
255::CODE;;self.strokes[-1].points.append(point)
256::CODE;;elif isinstance(point, list) or isinstance(point, tuple):
257::CODE;;if len(point) != 2:
258::CODE;;raise ValueError("Stroke entry must have 2 values max")
259::CODE;;self.strokes[-1].add_point(point[0], point[1])
260::CODE;;else:
261::CODE;;raise TypeError("The point list should either be "
262::CODE;;"tuples of x and y or a list of "
263::CODE;;"GesturePoint objects")
264::CODE;;elif point_list is not None:
265::CODE;;raise ValueError("point_list should be a tuple/list")
266::CODE;;return self.strokes[-1]
267::CODE;;def normalize(self, stroke_samples=32):
268::CODE;;'''Runs the gesture normalization algorithm and calculates the dot
269::CODE;;product with self.
270::CODE;;'''
271::CODE;;if not self._scale_gesture() or not self._center_gesture():
272::CODE;;self.gesture_product = False
273::CODE;;return False
274::CODE;;for stroke in self.strokes:
275::CODE;;stroke.normalize_stroke(stroke_samples)
276::CODE;;self.gesture_product = self.dot_product(self)
277::CODE;;def get_rigid_rotation(self, dstpts):
278::CODE;;'''
279::CODE;;Extract the rotation to apply to a group of points to minimize the
280::CODE;;distance to a second group of points. The two groups of points are
281::CODE;;assumed to be centered. This is a simple version that just picks
282::CODE;;an angle based on the first point of the gesture.
283::CODE;;'''
284::CODE;;if len(self.strokes) < 1 or len(self.strokes[0].points) < 1:
285::CODE;;return 0
286::CODE;;if len(dstpts.strokes) < 1 or len(dstpts.strokes[0].points) < 1:
287::CODE;;return 0
288::CODE;;p = dstpts.strokes[0].points[0]
289::CODE;;target = Vector([p.x, p.y])
290::CODE;;source = Vector([p.x, p.y])
291::CODE;;return source.angle(target)
292::CODE;;def dot_product(self, comparison_gesture):
293::CODE;;''' Calculates the dot product of the gesture with another gesture.'''
294::CODE;;if len(comparison_gesture.strokes) != len(self.strokes):
295::CODE;;return -1
296::CODE;;if getattr(comparison_gesture, 'gesture_product', True) is False or \
297::CODE;;getattr(self, 'gesture_product', True) is False:
298::CODE;;return -1
299::CODE;;dot_product = 0.0
300::CODE;;for stroke_index, (my_stroke, cmp_stroke) in enumerate(
301::CODE;;list(zip(self.strokes, comparison_gesture.strokes))):
302::CODE;;for pt_index, (my_point, cmp_point) in enumerate(
303::CODE;;list(zip(my_stroke.points, cmp_stroke.points))):
304::CODE;;dot_product += (my_point.x * cmp_point.x +
305::CODE;;my_point.y * cmp_point.y)
306::CODE;;return dot_product
307::CODE;;def rotate(self, angle):
308::CODE;;g = Gesture()
309::CODE;;for stroke in self.strokes:
310::CODE;;tmp = []
311::CODE;;for j in stroke.points:
312::CODE;;v = Vector([j.x, j.y]).rotate(angle)
313::CODE;;tmp.append(v)
314::CODE;;g.add_stroke(tmp)
315::CODE;;g.gesture_product = g.dot_product(g)
316::CODE;;return g
317::CODE;;def get_score(self, comparison_gesture, rotation_invariant=True):
318::CODE;;''' Returns the matching score of the gesture against another gesture.
319::CODE;;'''
320::CODE;;if isinstance(comparison_gesture, Gesture):
321::CODE;;if rotation_invariant:
323::CODE;;angle = self.get_rigid_rotation(comparison_gesture)
325::CODE;;comparison_gesture = comparison_gesture.rotate(angle)
327::CODE;;score = self.dot_product(comparison_gesture)
328::CODE;;if score <= 0:
329::CODE;;return score
330::CODE;;score /= math.sqrt(
331::CODE;;self.gesture_product * comparison_gesture.gesture_product)
332::CODE;;return score
333::CODE;;def __eq__(self, comparison_gesture):
334::CODE;;''' Allows easy comparisons between gesture instances.'''
335::CODE;;if isinstance(comparison_gesture, Gesture):
338::CODE;;score = self.get_score(comparison_gesture)
339::CODE;;if (score > (1.0 - self.tolerance) and
340::CODE;;score < (1.0 + self.tolerance)):
341::CODE;;return True
342::CODE;;else:
343::CODE;;return False
344::CODE;;else:
345::CODE;;return NotImplemented
346::CODE;;def __ne__(self, comparison_gesture):
347::CODE;;result = self.__eq__(comparison_gesture)
348::CODE;;if result is NotImplemented:
349::CODE;;return result
350::CODE;;else:
351::CODE;;return not result
352::CODE;;def __lt__(self, comparison_gesture):
353::CODE;;raise TypeError("Gesture cannot be evaluated with <")
354::CODE;;def __gt__(self, comparison_gesture):
355::CODE;;raise TypeError("Gesture cannot be evaluated with >")
356::CODE;;def __le__(self, comparison_gesture):
357::CODE;;raise TypeError("Gesture cannot be evaluated with <=")
358::CODE;;def __ge__(self, comparison_gesture):
359::CODE;;raise TypeError("Gesture cannot be evaluated with >=")
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Graphics
3::CODE;;========
4::CODE;;This package assembles many low level functions used for drawing. The whole
5::CODE;;graphics package is compatible with OpenGL ES 2.0 and has many rendering
6::CODE;;optimizations.
7::CODE;;The basics
8::CODE;;----------
9::CODE;;For drawing on a screen, you will need :
10::CODE;;1. a :class:`~kivy.graphics.instructions.Canvas` object.
11::CODE;;2. :class:`~kivy.graphics.instructions.Instruction` objects.
12::CODE;;Each :class:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget`
13::CODE;;in Kivy already has a :class:`Canvas` by default. When you create
14::CODE;;a widget, you can create all the instructions needed for drawing. If
15::CODE;;`self` is your current widget, you can do::
16::CODE;;from kivy.graphics import *
17::CODE;;with self.canvas:
19::CODE;;Color(1., 0, 0)
21::CODE;;Rectangle(pos=(10, 10), size=(500, 500))
22::CODE;;The instructions :class:`Color` and :class:`Rectangle` are automatically added
23::CODE;;to the canvas object and will be used when the window is drawn.
24::CODE;;.. note::
25::CODE;;Kivy drawing instructions are not automatically relative to the position
26::CODE;;or size of the widget. You, therefore, need to consider these factors when
27::CODE;;drawing. In order to make your drawing instructions relative to the widget,
28::CODE;;the instructions need either to be
29::CODE;;declared in the :mod:`KvLang <kivy.lang>` or bound to pos and size changes.
30::CODE;;Please see :ref:`adding_widget_background` for more detail.
31::CODE;;GL Reloading mechanism
32::CODE;;----------------------
33::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.2.0
34::CODE;;During the lifetime of the application, the OpenGL context might be lost. This
35::CODE;;happens:
36::CODE;;- when Android releases the app resources: when your application goes to the
37::CODE;;background, Android might reclaim your opengl context to give the
38::CODE;;resource to another app. When the user switches back to your application, a
39::CODE;;newly created gl context is given to your app.
40::CODE;;Starting from 1.2.0, we have introduced a mechanism for reloading all the
41::CODE;;graphics resources using the GPU: Canvas, FBO, Shader, Texture, VBO,
42::CODE;;and VertexBatch:
43::CODE;;- VBO and VertexBatch are constructed by our graphics instructions. We have all
44::CODE;;the data needed to reconstruct when reloading.
45::CODE;;- Shader: same as VBO, we store the source and values used in the
46::CODE;;shader so we are able to recreate the vertex/fragment/program.
47::CODE;;- Texture: if the texture has a source (an image file or atlas), the image
48::CODE;;is reloaded from the source and reuploaded to the GPU.
49::CODE;;You should cover these cases yourself:
50::CODE;;- Textures without a source: if you manually created a texture and manually
51::CODE;;blit data / a buffer to it, you must handle the reloading yourself. Check the
52::CODE;;:doc:`api-kivy.graphics.texture` to learn how to manage that case. (The text
53::CODE;;rendering already generates the texture and handles the reloading. You
54::CODE;;don't need to reload text yourself.)
55::CODE;;- FBO: if you added / removed / drew things multiple times on the FBO, we
56::CODE;;can't reload it. We don't keep a history of the instructions put on it.
57::CODE;;As for textures without a source, check the :doc:`api-kivy.graphics.fbo` to
58::CODE;;learn how to manage that case.
59::CODE;;'''
60::CODE;;from kivy.graphics.instructions import Callback, Canvas, CanvasBase, \
61::CODE;;ContextInstruction, Instruction, InstructionGroup, RenderContext, \
62::CODE;;VertexInstruction
63::CODE;;from kivy.graphics.context_instructions import BindTexture, Color, \

2::CODE;;'''
3::CODE;;Input management
4::CODE;;================
5::CODE;;Our input system is wide and simple at the same time. We are currently able to
6::CODE;;natively support :
7::CODE;;* Windows multitouch events (pencil and finger)
8::CODE;;* OS X touchpads
9::CODE;;* Linux multitouch events (kernel and mtdev)
10::CODE;;* Linux wacom drivers (pencil and finger)
11::CODE;;* TUIO
12::CODE;;All the input management is configurable in the Kivy :mod:`~kivy.config`. You
13::CODE;;can easily use many multitouch devices in one Kivy application.
14::CODE;;When the events have been read from the devices, they are dispatched through
15::CODE;;a post processing module before being sent to your application. We also have
16::CODE;;several default modules for :
17::CODE;;* Double tap detection
18::CODE;;* Decreasing jittering
19::CODE;;* Decreasing the inaccuracy of touch on "bad" DIY hardware
20::CODE;;* Ignoring regions
21::CODE;;'''

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;.. _motionevent:
3::CODE;;Motion Event
4::CODE;;============
5::CODE;;The :class:`MotionEvent` is the base class used for events provided by
6::CODE;;pointing devices (touch and non-touch). This class defines all the properties
7::CODE;;and methods needed to handle 2D and 3D movements but has many more
8::CODE;;capabilities.
9::CODE;;Usually you would never need to create the :class:`MotionEvent` yourself as
10::CODE;;this is the role of the :mod:`~kivy.input.providers`.
11::CODE;;Flow of the motion events
12::CODE;;-------------------------
13::CODE;;1. The :class:`MotionEvent` 's are gathered from input providers by
14::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.base.EventLoopBase`.
15::CODE;;2. Post processing is performed by registered processors
16::CODE;;:mod:`~kivy.input.postproc`.
17::CODE;;3. :class:`~kivy.base.EventLoopBase` dispatches all motion events using
18::CODE;;`on_motion` event to all registered listeners including the
19::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.core.window.WindowBase`.
20::CODE;;4. Once received in :meth:`~kivy.core.window.WindowBase.on_motion` events
21::CODE;;(touch or non-touch) are all registered managers. If a touch event is not
22::CODE;;handled by at least one manager, then it is dispatched through
23::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.core.window.WindowBase.on_touch_down`,
24::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.core.window.WindowBase.on_touch_move` and
25::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.core.window.WindowBase.on_touch_up`.
26::CODE;;5. Widgets receive events in :meth:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.on_motion` method
27::CODE;;(if passed by a manager) or on `on_touch_xxx` methods.
28::CODE;;Motion events and event managers
29::CODE;;--------------------------------
30::CODE;;A motion event is a touch event if its :attr:`MotionEvent.is_touch` is set to
31::CODE;;`True`. Beside `is_touch` attribute, :attr:`MotionEvent.type_id` can be used to
32::CODE;;check for event's general type. Currently two types are dispatched by
33::CODE;;input providers: "touch" and "hover".
34::CODE;;Event managers can be used to dispatch any motion event throughout the widget
35::CODE;;tree and a manager uses `type_id` to specify which event types it want to
36::CODE;;receive. See :mod:`~kivy.eventmanager` to learn how to define and register
37::CODE;;an event manager.
38::CODE;;A manager can also assign a new `type_id` to
39::CODE;;:attr:`MotionEvent.type_id` before dispatching it to the widgets. This useful
40::CODE;;when dispatching a specific event::
41::CODE;;class MouseTouchManager(EventManagerBase):
42::CODE;;type_ids = ('touch',)
43::CODE;;def dispatch(self, etype, me):
44::CODE;;accepted = False
45::CODE;;if me.device == 'mouse':
47::CODE;;me.type_id = 'mouse_touch'
48::CODE;;self.window.transform_motion_event_2d(me)
51::CODE;;for widget in self.window.children[:]:
52::CODE;;if widget.dispatch('on_motion', etype, me):
53::CODE;;accepted = True
54::CODE;;break
56::CODE;;return accepted
57::CODE;;Listening to a motion event
58::CODE;;---------------------------
59::CODE;;If you want to receive all motion events, touch or not, you can bind the
60::CODE;;MotionEvent from the :class:`~kivy.core.window.Window` to your own callback::
61::CODE;;def on_motion(self, etype, me):
63::CODE;;pass
64::CODE;;Window.bind(on_motion=on_motion)
65::CODE;;You can also listen to changes of the mouse position by watching
66::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.core.window.WindowBase.mouse_pos`.
67::CODE;;Profiles
68::CODE;;--------
69::CODE;;The :class:`MotionEvent` stores device specific information in various
70::CODE;;properties listed in the :attr:`~MotionEvent.profile`.
71::CODE;;For example, you can receive a MotionEvent that has an angle, a fiducial
72::CODE;;ID, or even a shape. You can check the :attr:`~MotionEvent.profile`
73::CODE;;attribute to see what is currently supported by the MotionEvent provider.
74::CODE;;This is a short list of the profile values supported by default. Please check
75::CODE;;the :attr:`MotionEvent.profile` property to see what profile values are
76::CODE;;available.
77::CODE;;============== ================================================================
78::CODE;;Profile value Description
79::CODE;;-------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------
80::CODE;;angle 2D angle. Accessed via the `a` property.
81::CODE;;button Mouse button ('left', 'right', 'middle', 'scrollup' or
82::CODE;;'scrolldown'). Accessed via the `button` property.
83::CODE;;markerid Marker or Fiducial ID. Accessed via the `fid` property.
84::CODE;;pos 2D position. Accessed via the `x`, `y` or `pos` properties.
85::CODE;;pos3d 3D position. Accessed via the `x`, `y` or `z` properties.
86::CODE;;pressure Pressure of the contact. Accessed via the `pressure` property.
87::CODE;;shape Contact shape. Accessed via the `shape` property .
88::CODE;;============== ================================================================
89::CODE;;If you want to know whether the current :class:`MotionEvent` has an angle::
90::CODE;;def on_touch_move(self, touch):
91::CODE;;if 'angle' in touch.profile:
92::CODE;;print('The touch angle is', touch.a)
93::CODE;;If you want to select only the fiducials::
94::CODE;;def on_touch_move(self, touch):
95::CODE;;if 'markerid' not in touch.profile:
96::CODE;;return
97::CODE;;'''

110::CODE;;return super(EnhancedDictionary, self).__getattr__(attr)

112::CODE;;self.__setitem__(attr, value)

117::CODE;;if hasattr(base, '__attrs__'):
118::CODE;;__attrs__.extend(base.__attrs__)
119::CODE;;if '__attrs__' in attrs:

121::CODE;;attrs['__attrs__'] = tuple(__attrs__)

309::CODE;;If this event is a touch you can grab it if you want to receive
310::CODE;;subsequent :meth:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.on_touch_move` and

312::CODE;;is not dispatched by the parent:
313::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
314::CODE;;def on_touch_down(self, touch):

333::CODE;;class_instance = weakref.ref(class_instance.__self__)
334::CODE;;if exclusive:

342::CODE;;self.grab_exclusive_class = None
343::CODE;;if class_instance in self.grab_list:
344::CODE;;self.grab_list.remove(class_instance)

359::CODE;;else:
360::CODE;;self.psx, self.psy, self.psz = self.sx, self.sy, self.sz
361::CODE;;self.time_update = time()
362::CODE;;self.depack(args)
363::CODE;;def scale_for_screen(self, w, h, p=None, rotation=0,
364::CODE;;smode='None', kheight=0):
365::CODE;;'''Scale position for the screen.
366::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 2.1.0
367::CODE;;Max value for `x`, `y` and `z` is changed respectively to `w` - 1,
368::CODE;;`h` - 1 and `p` - 1.
369::CODE;;'''
370::CODE;;x_max, y_max = max(0, w - 1), max(0, h - 1)
371::CODE;;absolute = self.to_absolute_pos
372::CODE;;self.x, self.y = absolute(self.sx, self.sy, x_max, y_max, rotation)
373::CODE;;self.ox, self.oy = absolute(self.osx, self.osy, x_max, y_max, rotation)
374::CODE;;self.px, self.py = absolute(self.psx, self.psy, x_max, y_max, rotation)
375::CODE;;z_max = 0 if p is None else max(0, p - 1)
376::CODE;;self.z = self.sz * z_max
377::CODE;;self.oz = self.osz * z_max
378::CODE;;self.pz = self.psz * z_max
379::CODE;;if smode:
381::CODE;;if smode == 'pan' or smode == 'below_target':
382::CODE;;self.y -= kheight
383::CODE;;self.oy -= kheight
384::CODE;;self.py -= kheight
385::CODE;;elif smode == 'scale':
386::CODE;;offset = kheight * (self.y - h) / (h - kheight)
387::CODE;;self.y += offset
388::CODE;;self.oy += offset
389::CODE;;self.py += offset
391::CODE;;self.dx = self.x - self.px
392::CODE;;self.dy = self.y - self.py
393::CODE;;self.dz = self.z - self.pz
395::CODE;;self.pos = self.x, self.y
396::CODE;;def to_absolute_pos(self, nx, ny, x_max, y_max, rotation):
397::CODE;;'''Transforms normalized (0-1) coordinates `nx` and `ny` to absolute
398::CODE;;coordinates using `x_max`, `y_max` and `rotation`.
399::CODE;;:raises:
400::CODE;;`ValueError`: If `rotation` is not one of: 0, 90, 180 or 270
401::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 2.1.0
402::CODE;;'''
403::CODE;;if rotation == 0:
404::CODE;;return nx * x_max, ny * y_max
405::CODE;;elif rotation == 90:
406::CODE;;return ny * y_max, (1 - nx) * x_max
407::CODE;;elif rotation == 180:
408::CODE;;return (1 - nx) * x_max, (1 - ny) * y_max
409::CODE;;elif rotation == 270:
410::CODE;;return (1 - ny) * y_max, nx * x_max
411::CODE;;raise ValueError('Invalid rotation %s, '
412::CODE;;'valid values are 0, 90, 180 or 270' % rotation)
413::CODE;;def push(self, attrs=None):
414::CODE;;'''Push attribute values in `attrs` onto the stack.
415::CODE;;'''
416::CODE;;if attrs is None:
417::CODE;;attrs = self.push_attrs
418::CODE;;values = [getattr(self, x) for x in attrs]
419::CODE;;self.push_attrs_stack.append((attrs, values))
420::CODE;;def pop(self):
421::CODE;;'''Pop attributes values from the stack.
422::CODE;;'''
423::CODE;;attrs, values = self.push_attrs_stack.pop()
424::CODE;;for i in range(len(attrs)):
425::CODE;;setattr(self, attrs[i], values[i])
426::CODE;;def apply_transform_2d(self, transform):
427::CODE;;'''Apply a transformation on x, y, z, px, py, pz,
428::CODE;;ox, oy, oz, dx, dy, dz.
429::CODE;;'''
430::CODE;;self.x, self.y = self.pos = transform(self.x, self.y)
431::CODE;;self.px, self.py = transform(self.px, self.py)
432::CODE;;self.ox, self.oy = transform(self.ox, self.oy)
433::CODE;;self.dx = self.x - self.px
434::CODE;;self.dy = self.y - self.py
435::CODE;;def copy_to(self, to):
436::CODE;;'''Copy some attribute to another motion event object.'''
437::CODE;;for attr in self.__attrs__:
438::CODE;;to.__setattr__(attr, copy(self.__getattribute__(attr)))
439::CODE;;def distance(self, other_touch):
440::CODE;;'''Return the distance between the two events.
441::CODE;;'''
442::CODE;;return Vector(self.pos).distance(other_touch.pos)
443::CODE;;def update_time_end(self):
444::CODE;;self.time_end = time()
446::CODE;;@property
447::CODE;;def dpos(self):
448::CODE;;'''Return delta between last position and current position, in the
449::CODE;;screen coordinate system (self.dx, self.dy).'''
450::CODE;;return self.dx, self.dy
451::CODE;;@property
452::CODE;;def opos(self):
453::CODE;;'''Return the initial position of the motion event in the screen
454::CODE;;coordinate system (self.ox, self.oy).'''
455::CODE;;return self.ox, self.oy
456::CODE;;@property
457::CODE;;def ppos(self):
458::CODE;;'''Return the previous position of the motion event in the screen
459::CODE;;coordinate system (self.px, self.py).'''
460::CODE;;return self.px, self.py
461::CODE;;@property
462::CODE;;def spos(self):
463::CODE;;'''Return the position in the 0-1 coordinate system (self.sx, self.sy).
464::CODE;;'''
465::CODE;;return self.sx, self.sy
466::CODE;;def __str__(self):
467::CODE;;basename = str(self.__class__)
468::CODE;;classname = basename.split('.')[-1].replace('>', '').replace('\'', '')
469::CODE;;return '<%s spos=%s pos=%s>' % (classname, self.spos, self.pos)
470::CODE;;def __repr__(self):
471::CODE;;out = []
472::CODE;;for x in dir(self):
473::CODE;;v = getattr(self, x)
474::CODE;;if x[0] == '_':
475::CODE;;continue
476::CODE;;if isroutine(v):
477::CODE;;continue
478::CODE;;out.append('%s="%s"' % (x, v))
479::CODE;;return '<%s %s>' % (
480::CODE;;self.__class__.__name__,
481::CODE;;' '.join(out))

18::CODE;;kivy_postproc_modules['retaintouch'] = InputPostprocRetainTouch()

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Calibration
3::CODE;;===========
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.9.0
5::CODE;;Recalibrate input device to a specific range / offset.
6::CODE;;Let's say you have 3 1080p displays, the 2 firsts are multitouch. By default,
7::CODE;;both will have mixed touch, the range will conflict with each others: the 0-1
8::CODE;;range will goes to 0-5760 px (remember, 3 * 1920 = 5760.)
9::CODE;;To fix it, you need to manually reference them. For example::
10::CODE;;[input]
11::CODE;;left = mtdev,/dev/input/event17
12::CODE;;middle = mtdev,/dev/input/event15
14::CODE;;Then, you can use the calibration postproc module::
15::CODE;;[postproc:calibration]
16::CODE;;left = xratio=0.3333
17::CODE;;middle = xratio=0.3333,xoffset=0.3333
18::CODE;;Now, the touches from the left screen will be within 0-0.3333 range, and the
19::CODE;;touches from the middle screen will be within 0.3333-0.6666 range.
20::CODE;;You can also match calibration rules to devices based on their provider type.
21::CODE;;This is useful when probesysfs is used to match devices. For example::
22::CODE;;[input]
23::CODE;;mtdev_%(name)s = probesysfs,provider=mtdev
24::CODE;;Then to apply calibration to any mtdev device, you can assign rules to the
25::CODE;;provider name enclosed by parentheses::
26::CODE;;[postproc:calibration]
27::CODE;;(mtdev) = xratio=0.3333,xoffset=0.3333
28::CODE;;Calibrating devices like this means the device's path doesn't need to be
29::CODE;;configured ahead of time. Note that with this method, all mtdev inputs will
30::CODE;;have the same calibration applied to them. For this reason, matching by
31::CODE;;provider will typically be useful when expecting only one input device.
32::CODE;;'''
33::CODE;;__all__ = ('InputPostprocCalibration', )
34::CODE;;from kivy.config import Config
35::CODE;;from kivy.logger import Logger
36::CODE;;from kivy.input import providers
37::CODE;;from kivy.input.factory import MotionEventFactory
38::CODE;;from kivy.input.motionevent import MotionEvent
39::CODE;;class InputPostprocCalibration(object):
40::CODE;;'''Recalibrate the inputs.
41::CODE;;The configuration must go within a section named `postproc:calibration`.
42::CODE;;Within the section, you must have a line like::
43::CODE;;devicename = param=value,param=value
44::CODE;;If you wish to match by provider, you must have a line like::
45::CODE;;(provider) = param=value,param=value
46::CODE;;:Parameters:
47::CODE;;`xratio`: float
48::CODE;;Value to multiply X
49::CODE;;`yratio`: float
50::CODE;;Value to multiply Y
51::CODE;;`xoffset`: float
52::CODE;;Value to add to X
53::CODE;;`yoffset`: float
54::CODE;;Value to add to Y
55::CODE;;`auto`: str
56::CODE;;If set, then the touch is transformed from screen-relative
57::CODE;;to window-relative The value is used as an indication of
58::CODE;;screen size, e.g for fullHD:
59::CODE;;auto=1920x1080
60::CODE;;If present, this setting overrides all the others.
61::CODE;;This assumes the input device exactly covers the display
62::CODE;;area, if they are different, the computations will be wrong.
63::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.11.0
64::CODE;;Added `auto` parameter
65::CODE;;'''
66::CODE;;def __init__(self):
67::CODE;;super(InputPostprocCalibration, self).__init__()
68::CODE;;self.devices = {}
69::CODE;;self.frame = 0
70::CODE;;self.provider_map = self._get_provider_map()
71::CODE;;if not Config.has_section('postproc:calibration'):
72::CODE;;return
73::CODE;;default_params = {'xoffset': 0, 'yoffset': 0, 'xratio': 1, 'yratio': 1}
74::CODE;;for device_key, params_str in Config.items('postproc:calibration'):
75::CODE;;params = default_params.copy()
76::CODE;;for param in params_str.split(','):
77::CODE;;param = param.strip()
78::CODE;;if not param:
79::CODE;;continue
80::CODE;;key, value = param.split('=', 1)
81::CODE;;if key == 'auto':
82::CODE;;width, height = [float(x) for x in value.split('x')]
83::CODE;;params['auto'] = width, height
84::CODE;;break
85::CODE;;if key not in ('xoffset', 'yoffset', 'xratio', 'yratio'):
86::CODE;;Logger.error(
87::CODE;;'Calibration: invalid key provided: {}'.format(key))
88::CODE;;params[key] = float(value)
89::CODE;;self.devices[device_key] = params
90::CODE;;def _get_provider_map(self):
95::CODE;;provider_map = {}
96::CODE;;for input_provider in MotionEventFactory.list():
97::CODE;;if not hasattr(providers, input_provider):
98::CODE;;continue
99::CODE;;p = getattr(providers, input_provider)
100::CODE;;for m in p.__all__:
101::CODE;;event = getattr(p, m)
102::CODE;;if issubclass(event, MotionEvent):
103::CODE;;provider_map[event] = input_provider
104::CODE;;return provider_map
105::CODE;;def _get_provider_key(self, event):
109::CODE;;input_type = self.provider_map.get(event.__class__)
110::CODE;;key = '({})'.format(input_type)
111::CODE;;if input_type and key in self.devices:
112::CODE;;return key
113::CODE;;def process(self, events):
115::CODE;;if not self.devices:
116::CODE;;return events
117::CODE;;self.frame += 1
118::CODE;;frame = self.frame
119::CODE;;to_remove = []
120::CODE;;for etype, event in events:
123::CODE;;if etype == 'end':
124::CODE;;continue
125::CODE;;if event.device in self.devices:
126::CODE;;dev = event.device
127::CODE;;else:
128::CODE;;dev = self._get_provider_key(event)
129::CODE;;if not dev:
130::CODE;;continue
132::CODE;;if 'calibration:frame' not in event.ud:
133::CODE;;event.ud['calibration:frame'] = frame
134::CODE;;elif event.ud['calibration:frame'] == frame:
135::CODE;;continue
136::CODE;;event.ud['calibration:frame'] = frame
137::CODE;;params = self.devices[dev]
138::CODE;;if 'auto' in params:
139::CODE;;event.sx, event.sy = self.auto_calibrate(
140::CODE;;event.sx, event.sy, params['auto'])
141::CODE;;if not (0 <= event.sx <= 1 and 0 <= event.sy <= 1):
142::CODE;;to_remove.append((etype, event))
143::CODE;;else:
144::CODE;;event.sx = event.sx * params['xratio'] + params['xoffset']
145::CODE;;event.sy = event.sy * params['yratio'] + params['yoffset']
146::CODE;;for event in to_remove:
147::CODE;;events.remove(event)
148::CODE;;return events
149::CODE;;def auto_calibrate(self, sx, sy, size):
150::CODE;;from kivy.core.window import Window as W
151::CODE;;WIDTH, HEIGHT = size
152::CODE;;xratio = WIDTH / W.width
153::CODE;;yratio = HEIGHT / W.height
154::CODE;;xoffset = - W.left / W.width
155::CODE;;yoffset = - (HEIGHT - W.top - W.height) / W.height
156::CODE;;sx = sx * xratio + xoffset
157::CODE;;sy = sy * yratio + yoffset
158::CODE;;return sx, sy
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Dejitter
3::CODE;;========
4::CODE;;Prevent blob jittering.
5::CODE;;A problem that is often faced (esp. in optical MT setups) is that of
6::CODE;;jitterish BLOBs caused by bad camera characteristics. With this module
7::CODE;;you can get rid of that jitter. You just define a threshold
8::CODE;;`jitter_distance` in your config, and all touch movements that move
9::CODE;;the touch by less than the jitter distance are considered 'bad'
10::CODE;;movements caused by jitter and will be discarded.
11::CODE;;'''
12::CODE;;__all__ = ('InputPostprocDejitter', )
13::CODE;;from kivy.config import Config
14::CODE;;class InputPostprocDejitter(object):
15::CODE;;'''
16::CODE;;Get rid of jitterish BLOBs.
17::CODE;;Example::
18::CODE;;[postproc]
19::CODE;;jitter_distance = 0.004
20::CODE;;jitter_ignore_devices = mouse,mactouch
21::CODE;;:Configuration:
22::CODE;;`jitter_distance`: float
23::CODE;;A float in range 0-1.
24::CODE;;`jitter_ignore_devices`: string
25::CODE;;A comma-separated list of device identifiers that
26::CODE;;should not be processed by dejitter (because they're
27::CODE;;very precise already).
28::CODE;;'''
29::CODE;;def __init__(self):
30::CODE;;self.jitterdist = Config.getfloat('postproc', 'jitter_distance')
31::CODE;;ignore_devices = Config.get('postproc', 'jitter_ignore_devices')
32::CODE;;self.ignore_devices = ignore_devices.split(',')
33::CODE;;self.last_touches = {}
34::CODE;;def taxicab_distance(self, p, q):
36::CODE;;return abs(p[0] - q[0]) + abs(p[1] - q[1])
37::CODE;;def process(self, events):
38::CODE;;if not self.jitterdist:
39::CODE;;return events
40::CODE;;processed = []
41::CODE;;for etype, touch in events:
42::CODE;;if not touch.is_touch:
43::CODE;;continue
44::CODE;;if touch.device in self.ignore_devices:
45::CODE;;processed.append((etype, touch))
46::CODE;;continue
47::CODE;;if etype == 'begin':
48::CODE;;self.last_touches[touch.id] = touch.spos
49::CODE;;if etype == 'end':
50::CODE;;if touch.id in self.last_touches:
51::CODE;;del self.last_touches[touch.id]
52::CODE;;if etype != 'update':
53::CODE;;processed.append((etype, touch))
54::CODE;;continue
56::CODE;;last_spos = self.last_touches[touch.id]
57::CODE;;dist = self.taxicab_distance(last_spos, touch.spos)
58::CODE;;if dist > self.jitterdist:
61::CODE;;self.last_touches[touch.id] = touch.spos
62::CODE;;processed.append((etype, touch))
63::CODE;;return processed
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Double Tap
3::CODE;;==========
4::CODE;;Search touch for a double tap
5::CODE;;'''
6::CODE;;__all__ = ('InputPostprocDoubleTap', )
7::CODE;;from time import time
8::CODE;;from kivy.config import Config
9::CODE;;from kivy.vector import Vector
10::CODE;;class InputPostprocDoubleTap(object):
11::CODE;;'''
12::CODE;;InputPostProcDoubleTap is a post-processor to check if
13::CODE;;a touch is a double tap or not.
14::CODE;;Double tap can be configured in the Kivy config file::
15::CODE;;[postproc]
16::CODE;;double_tap_time = 250
17::CODE;;double_tap_distance = 20
18::CODE;;Distance parameter is in the range 0-1000 and time is in milliseconds.
19::CODE;;'''
20::CODE;;def __init__(self):
21::CODE;;dist = Config.getint('postproc', 'double_tap_distance')
22::CODE;;self.double_tap_distance = dist / 1000.0
23::CODE;;tap_time = Config.getint('postproc', 'double_tap_time')
24::CODE;;self.double_tap_time = tap_time / 1000.0
25::CODE;;self.touches = {}
26::CODE;;def find_double_tap(self, ref):
27::CODE;;'''Find a double tap touch within self.touches.
28::CODE;;The touch must be not a previous double tap and the distance must be
29::CODE;;within the specified threshold. Additionally, the touch profiles
30::CODE;;must be the same kind of touch.
31::CODE;;'''
32::CODE;;ref_button = None
33::CODE;;if 'button' in ref.profile:
34::CODE;;ref_button = ref.button
35::CODE;;for touchid in self.touches:
36::CODE;;if ref.uid == touchid:
37::CODE;;continue
38::CODE;;etype, touch = self.touches[touchid]
39::CODE;;if etype != 'end':
40::CODE;;continue
41::CODE;;if touch.is_double_tap:
42::CODE;;continue
43::CODE;;distance = Vector.distance(
44::CODE;;Vector(ref.sx, ref.sy),
45::CODE;;Vector(touch.osx, touch.osy))
46::CODE;;if distance > self.double_tap_distance:
47::CODE;;continue
48::CODE;;if touch.is_mouse_scrolling or ref.is_mouse_scrolling:
49::CODE;;continue
50::CODE;;touch_button = None
51::CODE;;if 'button' in touch.profile:
52::CODE;;touch_button = touch.button
53::CODE;;if touch_button != ref_button:
54::CODE;;continue
55::CODE;;touch.double_tap_distance = distance
56::CODE;;return touch
57::CODE;;def process(self, events):
58::CODE;;if self.double_tap_distance == 0 or self.double_tap_time == 0:
59::CODE;;return events
61::CODE;;for etype, touch in events:
62::CODE;;if not touch.is_touch:
63::CODE;;continue
64::CODE;;if etype == 'begin':
65::CODE;;double_tap = self.find_double_tap(touch)
66::CODE;;if double_tap:
67::CODE;;touch.is_double_tap = True
68::CODE;;tap_time = touch.time_start - double_tap.time_start
69::CODE;;touch.double_tap_time = tap_time
70::CODE;;distance = double_tap.double_tap_distance
71::CODE;;touch.double_tap_distance = distance
73::CODE;;self.touches[touch.uid] = (etype, touch)
75::CODE;;time_current = time()
76::CODE;;to_delete = []
77::CODE;;for touchid in self.touches.keys():
78::CODE;;etype, touch = self.touches[touchid]
79::CODE;;if etype != 'end':
80::CODE;;continue
81::CODE;;if time_current - touch.time_start < self.double_tap_time:
82::CODE;;continue
83::CODE;;to_delete.append(touchid)
84::CODE;;for touchid in to_delete:
85::CODE;;del self.touches[touchid]
86::CODE;;return events
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Ignore list
3::CODE;;===========
4::CODE;;Ignore touch on some areas of the screen
5::CODE;;'''
6::CODE;;__all__ = ('InputPostprocIgnoreList', )
7::CODE;;from kivy.config import Config
8::CODE;;from kivy.utils import strtotuple
9::CODE;;class InputPostprocIgnoreList(object):
10::CODE;;'''
11::CODE;;InputPostprocIgnoreList is a post-processor which removes touches in the
12::CODE;;Ignore list. The Ignore list can be configured in the Kivy config file::
13::CODE;;[postproc]
15::CODE;;ignore = [(0.1, 0.1, 0.15, 0.15)]
16::CODE;;The Ignore list coordinates are in the range 0-1, not in screen pixels.
17::CODE;;'''
18::CODE;;def __init__(self):
19::CODE;;self.ignore_list = strtotuple(Config.get('postproc', 'ignore'))
20::CODE;;def collide_ignore(self, touch):
21::CODE;;x, y = touch.sx, touch.sy
22::CODE;;for l in self.ignore_list:
23::CODE;;xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax = l
24::CODE;;if x > xmin and x < xmax and y > ymin and y < ymax:
25::CODE;;return True
26::CODE;;def process(self, events):
27::CODE;;if not len(self.ignore_list):
28::CODE;;return events
29::CODE;;for etype, touch in events:
30::CODE;;if not touch.is_touch:
31::CODE;;continue
32::CODE;;if etype != 'begin':
33::CODE;;continue
34::CODE;;if self.collide_ignore(touch):
35::CODE;;touch.ud.__pp_ignore__ = True
36::CODE;;return [(etype, touch) for etype, touch in events
37::CODE;;if '__pp_ignore__' not in touch.ud]
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Retain Touch
3::CODE;;============
4::CODE;;Reuse touch to counter lost finger behavior
5::CODE;;'''
6::CODE;;__all__ = ('InputPostprocRetainTouch', )
7::CODE;;from kivy.config import Config
8::CODE;;from kivy.vector import Vector
9::CODE;;import time
10::CODE;;class InputPostprocRetainTouch(object):
11::CODE;;'''
12::CODE;;InputPostprocRetainTouch is a post-processor to delay the 'up' event of a
13::CODE;;touch, to reuse it under certains conditions. This module is designed to
14::CODE;;prevent lost finger touches on some hardware/setups.
15::CODE;;Retain touch can be configured in the Kivy config file::
16::CODE;;[postproc]
17::CODE;;retain_time = 100
18::CODE;;retain_distance = 50
19::CODE;;The distance parameter is in the range 0-1000 and time is in milliseconds.
20::CODE;;'''
21::CODE;;def __init__(self):
22::CODE;;self.timeout = Config.getint('postproc', 'retain_time') / 1000.0
23::CODE;;self.distance = Config.getint('postproc', 'retain_distance') / 1000.0
24::CODE;;self._available = []
25::CODE;;self._links = {}
26::CODE;;def process(self, events):
28::CODE;;if self.timeout == 0:
29::CODE;;return events
30::CODE;;d = time.time()
31::CODE;;for etype, touch in events[:]:
32::CODE;;if not touch.is_touch:
33::CODE;;continue
34::CODE;;if etype == 'end':
35::CODE;;events.remove((etype, touch))
36::CODE;;if touch.uid in self._links:
37::CODE;;selection = self._links[touch.uid]
38::CODE;;selection.ud.__pp_retain_time__ = d
39::CODE;;self._available.append(selection)
40::CODE;;del self._links[touch.uid]
41::CODE;;else:
42::CODE;;touch.ud.__pp_retain_time__ = d
43::CODE;;self._available.append(touch)
44::CODE;;elif etype == 'update':
45::CODE;;if touch.uid in self._links:
46::CODE;;selection = self._links[touch.uid]
47::CODE;;selection.x = touch.x
48::CODE;;selection.y = touch.y
49::CODE;;selection.sx = touch.sx
50::CODE;;selection.sy = touch.sy
51::CODE;;events.remove((etype, touch))
52::CODE;;events.append((etype, selection))
53::CODE;;else:
54::CODE;;pass
55::CODE;;elif etype == 'begin':
57::CODE;;selection = None
58::CODE;;selection_distance = 99999
59::CODE;;for touch2 in self._available:
60::CODE;;touch_distance = Vector(touch2.spos).distance(touch.spos)
61::CODE;;if touch_distance > self.distance:
62::CODE;;continue
63::CODE;;if touch2.__class__ != touch.__class__:
64::CODE;;continue
65::CODE;;if touch_distance < selection_distance:
67::CODE;;selection_distance = touch_distance
68::CODE;;selection = touch2
69::CODE;;if selection is None:
70::CODE;;continue
71::CODE;;self._links[touch.uid] = selection
72::CODE;;self._available.remove(selection)
73::CODE;;events.remove((etype, touch))
74::CODE;;for touch in self._available[:]:
75::CODE;;t = touch.ud.__pp_retain_time__
76::CODE;;if d - t > self.timeout:
77::CODE;;self._available.remove(touch)
78::CODE;;events.append(('end', touch))
79::CODE;;return events
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Triple Tap
3::CODE;;==========
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.7.0
5::CODE;;Search touch for a triple tap
6::CODE;;'''
7::CODE;;__all__ = ('InputPostprocTripleTap', )
8::CODE;;from time import time
9::CODE;;from kivy.config import Config
10::CODE;;from kivy.vector import Vector
11::CODE;;class InputPostprocTripleTap(object):
12::CODE;;'''
13::CODE;;InputPostProcTripleTap is a post-processor to check if
14::CODE;;a touch is a triple tap or not.
15::CODE;;Triple tap can be configured in the Kivy config file::
16::CODE;;[postproc]
17::CODE;;triple_tap_time = 250
18::CODE;;triple_tap_distance = 20
19::CODE;;The distance parameter is in the range 0-1000 and time is in milliseconds.
20::CODE;;'''
21::CODE;;def __init__(self):
22::CODE;;dist = Config.getint('postproc', 'triple_tap_distance')
23::CODE;;self.triple_tap_distance = dist / 1000.0
24::CODE;;time = Config.getint('postproc', 'triple_tap_time')
25::CODE;;self.triple_tap_time = time / 1000.0
26::CODE;;self.touches = {}
27::CODE;;def find_triple_tap(self, ref):
28::CODE;;'''Find a triple tap touch within *self.touches*.
29::CODE;;The touch must be not be a previous triple tap and the distance
30::CODE;;must be within the bounds specified. Additionally, the touch profile
31::CODE;;must be the same kind of touch.
32::CODE;;'''
33::CODE;;ref_button = None
34::CODE;;if 'button' in ref.profile:
35::CODE;;ref_button = ref.button
36::CODE;;for touchid in self.touches:
37::CODE;;if ref.uid == touchid:
38::CODE;;continue
39::CODE;;etype, touch = self.touches[touchid]
40::CODE;;if not touch.is_double_tap:
41::CODE;;continue
42::CODE;;if etype != 'end':
43::CODE;;continue
44::CODE;;if touch.is_triple_tap:
45::CODE;;continue
46::CODE;;distance = Vector.distance(
47::CODE;;Vector(ref.sx, ref.sy),
48::CODE;;Vector(touch.osx, touch.osy))
49::CODE;;if distance > self.triple_tap_distance:
50::CODE;;continue
51::CODE;;if touch.is_mouse_scrolling or ref.is_mouse_scrolling:
52::CODE;;continue
53::CODE;;touch_button = None
54::CODE;;if 'button' in touch.profile:
55::CODE;;touch_button = touch.button
56::CODE;;if touch_button != ref_button:
57::CODE;;continue
58::CODE;;touch.triple_tap_distance = distance
59::CODE;;return touch
60::CODE;;def process(self, events):
61::CODE;;if self.triple_tap_distance == 0 or self.triple_tap_time == 0:
62::CODE;;return events
64::CODE;;for etype, touch in events:
65::CODE;;if not touch.is_touch:
66::CODE;;continue
67::CODE;;if etype == 'begin':
68::CODE;;triple_tap = self.find_triple_tap(touch)
69::CODE;;if triple_tap:
70::CODE;;touch.is_double_tap = False
71::CODE;;touch.is_triple_tap = True
72::CODE;;tap_time = touch.time_start - triple_tap.time_start
73::CODE;;touch.triple_tap_time = tap_time
74::CODE;;distance = triple_tap.triple_tap_distance
75::CODE;;touch.triple_tap_distance = distance
77::CODE;;self.touches[touch.uid] = (etype, touch)
79::CODE;;time_current = time()
80::CODE;;to_delete = []
81::CODE;;for touchid in self.touches.keys():
82::CODE;;etype, touch = self.touches[touchid]
83::CODE;;if etype != 'end':
84::CODE;;continue
85::CODE;;if time_current - touch.time_start < self.triple_tap_time:
86::CODE;;continue
87::CODE;;to_delete.append(touchid)
88::CODE;;for touchid in to_delete:
89::CODE;;del self.touches[touchid]
90::CODE;;return events
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Motion Event Provider
3::CODE;;=====================

7::CODE;;:meth:`~MotionEventProvider.start`, :meth:`~MotionEventProvider.stop` and
8::CODE;;:meth:`~MotionEventProvider.update` methods.
9::CODE;;'''
10::CODE;;__all__ = ('MotionEventProvider', )

12::CODE;;'''Base class for a provider.
13::CODE;;'''

17::CODE;;raise NotImplementedError('class MotionEventProvider is abstract')
18::CODE;;def start(self):
19::CODE;;'''Start the provider. This method is automatically called when the
20::CODE;;application is started and if the configuration uses the current
21::CODE;;provider.
22::CODE;;'''
23::CODE;;pass
24::CODE;;def stop(self):
25::CODE;;'''Stop the provider.
26::CODE;;'''
27::CODE;;pass
28::CODE;;def update(self, dispatch_fn):
29::CODE;;'''Update the provider and dispatch all the new touch events though the
30::CODE;;`dispatch_fn` argument.
31::CODE;;'''
32::CODE;;pass

22::CODE;;import pygame.joystick
23::CODE;;class AndroidMotionEvent(MotionEvent):
24::CODE;;def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
25::CODE;;kwargs.setdefault('is_touch', True)
26::CODE;;kwargs.setdefault('type_id', 'touch')
27::CODE;;super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
28::CODE;;self.profile = ['pos', 'pressure', 'shape']
29::CODE;;def depack(self, args):
30::CODE;;self.sx, self.sy, self.pressure, radius = args
31::CODE;;self.shape = ShapeRect()
32::CODE;;self.shape.width = radius
33::CODE;;self.shape.height = radius
34::CODE;;super().depack(args)

36::CODE;;def __init__(self, device, args):
37::CODE;;super(AndroidMotionEventProvider, self).__init__(device, args)
38::CODE;;self.joysticks = []
39::CODE;;self.touches = {}
40::CODE;;self.uid = 0
41::CODE;;self.window = None
42::CODE;;def create_joystick(self, index):
43::CODE;;Logger.info('Android: create joystick <%d>' % index)
44::CODE;;js = pygame.joystick.Joystick(index)
45::CODE;;js.init()
46::CODE;;if js.get_numbuttons() == 0:
47::CODE;;Logger.info('Android: discard joystick <%d> cause no button' %
48::CODE;;index)

54::CODE;;for i in range(pygame.joystick.get_count()):
55::CODE;;self.create_joystick(i)
56::CODE;;def stop(self):
57::CODE;;self.joysticks = []
58::CODE;;def update(self, dispatch_fn):
59::CODE;;if not self.window:
60::CODE;;from kivy.core.window import Window
61::CODE;;self.window = Window
62::CODE;;w, h = self.window.system_size
63::CODE;;touches = self.touches
64::CODE;;for joy in self.joysticks:
65::CODE;;jid = joy.get_id()
66::CODE;;pressed = joy.get_button(0)
67::CODE;;if pressed or jid in touches:
68::CODE;;x = joy.get_axis(0) * 32768. / w
69::CODE;;y = 1. - (joy.get_axis(1) * 32768. / h)
71::CODE;;pressure = joy.get_axis(2) / 1000.
72::CODE;;radius = joy.get_axis(3) / 1000.
74::CODE;;if pressed and jid not in touches:
75::CODE;;self.uid += 1
76::CODE;;touch = AndroidMotionEvent(self.device, self.uid,
77::CODE;;[x, y, pressure, radius])
78::CODE;;touches[jid] = touch
79::CODE;;dispatch_fn('begin', touch)
81::CODE;;elif pressed:
82::CODE;;touch = touches[jid]
84::CODE;;if (touch.sx == x and touch.sy == y and
85::CODE;;touch.pressure == pressure):
86::CODE;;continue
87::CODE;;touch.move([x, y, pressure, radius])
88::CODE;;dispatch_fn('update', touch)
90::CODE;;elif not pressed and jid in touches:
91::CODE;;touch = touches[jid]
92::CODE;;touch.move([x, y, pressure, radius])
93::CODE;;touch.update_time_end()
94::CODE;;dispatch_fn('end', touch)
95::CODE;;touches.pop(jid)
96::CODE;;MotionEventFactory.register('android', AndroidMotionEventProvider)
2::CODE;;'''
3::CODE;;Native support for HID input from the linux kernel
4::CODE;;==================================================
5::CODE;;Support starts from 2.6.32-ubuntu, or 2.6.34.
6::CODE;;To configure HIDInput, add this to your configuration::
7::CODE;;[input]
10::CODE;;stantum = hidinput,/dev/input/event2
11::CODE;;.. note::
12::CODE;;You must have read access to the input event.
13::CODE;;You can use a custom range for the X, Y and pressure values.
14::CODE;;For some drivers, the range reported is invalid.
15::CODE;;To fix that, you can add these options to the argument line:
16::CODE;;* invert_x : 1 to invert X axis
17::CODE;;* invert_y : 1 to invert Y axis
18::CODE;;* min_position_x : X relative minimum
19::CODE;;* max_position_x : X relative maximum
20::CODE;;* min_position_y : Y relative minimum
21::CODE;;* max_position_y : Y relative maximum
22::CODE;;* min_abs_x : X absolute minimum
23::CODE;;* min_abs_y : Y absolute minimum
24::CODE;;* max_abs_x : X absolute maximum
25::CODE;;* max_abs_y : Y absolute maximum
26::CODE;;* min_pressure : pressure minimum
27::CODE;;* max_pressure : pressure maximum
28::CODE;;* rotation : rotate the input coordinate (0, 90, 180, 270)
29::CODE;;For example, on the Asus T101M, the touchscreen reports a range from 0-4095 for
30::CODE;;the X and Y values, but the real values are in a range from 0-32768. To correct
31::CODE;;this, you can add the following to the configuration::
32::CODE;;[input]
33::CODE;;t101m = hidinput,/dev/input/event7,max_position_x=32768,\
34::CODE;;max_position_y=32768
35::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.9.1
36::CODE;;`rotation` configuration token added.
37::CODE;;'''

323::CODE;;continue
325::CODE;;key, value = arg

327::CODE;;Logger.error('HIDInput: unknown %s option' % key)
328::CODE;;continue

332::CODE;;except ValueError:

334::CODE;;key, value)
335::CODE;;Logger.error(err)
336::CODE;;continue

339::CODE;;key, int(value)))
340::CODE;;if 'rotation' not in self.default_ranges:
341::CODE;;self.default_ranges['rotation'] = 0
342::CODE;;elif self.default_ranges['rotation'] not in (0, 90, 180, 270):

344::CODE;;self.default_ranges['rotation']))
345::CODE;;self.default_ranges['rotation'] = 0

348::CODE;;return

361::CODE;;self.thread.start()

363::CODE;;input_fn = kwargs.get('input_fn')
364::CODE;;queue = self.queue
365::CODE;;dispatch_queue = self.dispatch_queue
366::CODE;;device = kwargs.get('device')

376::CODE;;range_max_position_y = 2048

378::CODE;;range_max_pressure = 255

384::CODE;;range_max_abs_pressure = 255

388::CODE;;def assign_coord(point, value, invert, coords):
389::CODE;;cx, cy = coords
390::CODE;;if invert:
391::CODE;;value = 1. - value
392::CODE;;if rotation == 0:
393::CODE;;point[cx] = value
394::CODE;;elif rotation == 90:
395::CODE;;point[cy] = value
396::CODE;;elif rotation == 180:
397::CODE;;point[cx] = 1. - value
398::CODE;;elif rotation == 270:
399::CODE;;point[cy] = 1. - value
400::CODE;;def assign_rel_coord(point, value, invert, coords):
401::CODE;;cx, cy = coords
402::CODE;;if invert:
403::CODE;;value = -1 * value
404::CODE;;if rotation == 0:
405::CODE;;point[cx] += value
406::CODE;;elif rotation == 90:
407::CODE;;point[cy] += value
408::CODE;;elif rotation == 180:
409::CODE;;point[cx] += -value
410::CODE;;elif rotation == 270:
411::CODE;;point[cy] += -value
413::CODE;;point['x'] = min(1., max(0., point['x']))
414::CODE;;point['y'] = min(1., max(0., point['y']))
415::CODE;;def process_as_multitouch(tv_sec, tv_usec, ev_type,

194::CODE;;actives = list(points.keys())
195::CODE;;for args in points.values():

197::CODE;;try:

199::CODE;;except KeyError:
200::CODE;;touch = LinuxWacomMotionEvent(device, tid, args)
201::CODE;;touches[touch.id] = touch
202::CODE;;if touch.sx == args['x'] \
203::CODE;;and touch.sy == args['y'] \

219::CODE;;def normalize(value, vmin, vmax):
220::CODE;;return (value - vmin) / float(vmax - vmin)
222::CODE;;try:
223::CODE;;fd = open(input_fn, 'rb')
224::CODE;;except IOError:
225::CODE;;Logger.exception('Unable to open %s' % input_fn)
226::CODE;;return

229::CODE;;" " * 256).split('\x00')[0]

232::CODE;;bit = fcntl.ioctl(fd, EVIOCGBIT + (EV_MAX << 16), ' ' * sz_l)
233::CODE;;bit, = struct.unpack('Q', bit)
234::CODE;;for x in range(EV_MAX):

237::CODE;;continue

240::CODE;;continue

243::CODE;;' ' * sz_l)

261::CODE;;range_max_position_y = drs('max_position_y', abs_max)
262::CODE;;Logger.info('LinuxWacom: ' +
263::CODE;;'<%s> range position Y is %d - %d' % (
264::CODE;;device_name, abs_min, abs_max))

266::CODE;;range_min_pressure = drs('min_pressure', abs_min)
267::CODE;;range_max_pressure = drs('max_pressure', abs_max)
268::CODE;;Logger.info('LinuxWacom: ' +
269::CODE;;'<%s> range pressure is %d - %d' % (
270::CODE;;device_name, abs_min, abs_max))
272::CODE;;changed = False
273::CODE;;touch_id = 0
274::CODE;;touch_x = 0
275::CODE;;touch_y = 0
276::CODE;;touch_pressure = 0
277::CODE;;while fd:

279::CODE;;if len(data) < struct_input_event_sz:
280::CODE;;break

286::CODE;;struct.unpack('LLHHi', ev[:struct_input_event_sz])
287::CODE;;if ev_type == EV_SYN and ev_code == SYN_REPORT:
288::CODE;;if touch_id in l_points:
289::CODE;;p = l_points[touch_id]
290::CODE;;else:

292::CODE;;l_points[touch_id] = p
293::CODE;;p['id'] = touch_id
294::CODE;;if not reset_touch:
295::CODE;;p['x'] = touch_x

299::CODE;;and touch_pressure == 0 \
300::CODE;;and not reset_touch:

302::CODE;;if changed:
303::CODE;;if 'x' not in p:
304::CODE;;reset_touch = False
305::CODE;;continue
306::CODE;;process(l_points)
307::CODE;;changed = False

309::CODE;;l_points.clear()
310::CODE;;reset_touch = False
311::CODE;;process(l_points)
312::CODE;;elif ev_type == EV_MSC and ev_code == MSC_SERIAL:

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Mouse provider implementation
3::CODE;;=============================
4::CODE;;On linux systems, the mouse provider can be annoying when used with another
5::CODE;;multitouch provider (hidinput or mtdev). The Mouse can conflict with them: a
6::CODE;;single touch can generate one event from the mouse provider and another
7::CODE;;from the multitouch provider.
8::CODE;;To avoid this behavior, you can activate the "disable_on_activity" token in
9::CODE;;the mouse configuration. Then, if any touches are created by another
10::CODE;;provider, the mouse event will be discarded. Add this to your configuration::
11::CODE;;[input]
12::CODE;;mouse = mouse,disable_on_activity
13::CODE;;Using multitouch interaction with the mouse
14::CODE;;-------------------------------------------
15::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.3.0
16::CODE;;By default, the middle and right mouse buttons, as well as a combination of
17::CODE;;ctrl + left mouse button are used for multitouch emulation.
18::CODE;;If you want to use them for other purposes, you can disable this behavior by
19::CODE;;activating the "disable_multitouch" token::
20::CODE;;[input]
21::CODE;;mouse = mouse,disable_multitouch
22::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.9.0
23::CODE;;You can now selectively control whether a click initiated as described above
24::CODE;;will emulate multi-touch. If the touch has been initiated in the above manner
25::CODE;;(e.g. right mouse button), a `multitouch_sim` value will be added to the
26::CODE;;touch's profile, and a `multitouch_sim` property will be added to the touch.
27::CODE;;By default, `multitouch_sim` is True and multitouch will be emulated for that
28::CODE;;touch. If, however, `multitouch_on_demand` is added to the config::
29::CODE;;[input]
30::CODE;;mouse = mouse,multitouch_on_demand
31::CODE;;then `multitouch_sim` defaults to `False`. In that case, if `multitouch_sim`
32::CODE;;is set to True before the mouse is released (e.g. in on_touch_down/move), the
33::CODE;;touch will simulate a multi-touch event. For example::
34::CODE;;if 'multitouch_sim' in touch.profile:
35::CODE;;touch.multitouch_sim = True
36::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 2.1.0
37::CODE;;Provider dispatches hover events by listening to properties/events in
38::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.core.window.Window`. Dispatching can be disabled by setting
39::CODE;;:attr:`MouseMotionEventProvider.disable_hover` to ``True`` or by adding
40::CODE;;`disable_hover` in the config::
41::CODE;;[input]
42::CODE;;mouse = mouse,disable_hover
43::CODE;;It's also possible to enable/disable hover events at runtime with
44::CODE;;:attr:`MouseMotionEventProvider.disable_hover` property.
45::CODE;;Following is a list of the supported values for the
46::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.input.motionevent.MotionEvent.profile` property list.
47::CODE;;================ ==========================================================
48::CODE;;Profile value Description
49::CODE;;---------------- ----------------------------------------------------------
50::CODE;;button Mouse button (one of `left`, `right`, `middle`, `scrollup`
51::CODE;;or `scrolldown`). Accessed via the 'button' property.
52::CODE;;pos 2D position. Also reflected in the
53::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.input.motionevent.MotionEvent.x`,
54::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.input.motionevent.MotionEvent.y`
55::CODE;;and :attr:`~kivy.input.motionevent.MotionEvent.pos`
56::CODE;;properties.
57::CODE;;multitouch_sim Specifies whether multitouch is simulated or not. Accessed
58::CODE;;via the 'multitouch_sim' property.
59::CODE;;modifiers Active keyboard modifiers (list of strings: 'ctrl', 'alt',
60::CODE;;'shift', etc.). Accessed via the 'modifiers' property.
61::CODE;;================ ==========================================================
62::CODE;;'''

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Native support for Multitouch devices on Linux, using libmtdev.
3::CODE;;===============================================================
4::CODE;;The Mtdev project is a part of the Ubuntu Maverick multitouch architecture.
5::CODE;;You can read more on http://wiki.ubuntu.com/Multitouch
6::CODE;;To configure MTDev, it's preferable to use probesysfs providers.
7::CODE;;Check :py:class:`~kivy.input.providers.probesysfs` for more information.
8::CODE;;Otherwise, add this to your configuration::
9::CODE;;[input]
11::CODE;;acert230h = mtdev,/dev/input/event2
12::CODE;;.. note::
13::CODE;;You must have read access to the input event.
14::CODE;;You can use a custom range for the X, Y and pressure values.
15::CODE;;On some drivers, the range reported is invalid.
16::CODE;;To fix that, you can add these options to the argument line:
17::CODE;;* invert_x : 1 to invert X axis
18::CODE;;* invert_y : 1 to invert Y axis
19::CODE;;* min_position_x : X minimum
20::CODE;;* max_position_x : X maximum
21::CODE;;* min_position_y : Y minimum
22::CODE;;* max_position_y : Y maximum
23::CODE;;* min_pressure : pressure minimum
24::CODE;;* max_pressure : pressure maximum
25::CODE;;* min_touch_major : width shape minimum
26::CODE;;* max_touch_major : width shape maximum
27::CODE;;* min_touch_minor : width shape minimum
28::CODE;;* max_touch_minor : height shape maximum
29::CODE;;* rotation : 0,90,180 or 270 to rotate
30::CODE;;An inverted display configuration will look like this::
31::CODE;;[input]
33::CODE;;display = mtdev,/dev/input/event0,invert_x=1,invert_y=1
34::CODE;;'''

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Auto Create Input Provider Config Entry for Available MT Hardware (linux only).
3::CODE;;===============================================================================
4::CODE;;Thanks to Marc Tardif for the probing code, taken from scan-for-mt-device.
5::CODE;;The device discovery is done by this provider. However, the reading of
6::CODE;;input can be performed by other providers like: hidinput, mtdev and
7::CODE;;linuxwacom. mtdev is used prior to other providers. For more
8::CODE;;information about mtdev, check :py:class:`~kivy.input.providers.mtdev`.
9::CODE;;Here is an example of auto creation::

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;TUIO Input Provider
3::CODE;;===================
4::CODE;;TUIO is the de facto standard network protocol for the transmission of
5::CODE;;touch and fiducial information between a server and a client. To learn
6::CODE;;more about TUIO (which is itself based on the OSC protocol), please
7::CODE;;refer to http://tuio.org -- The specification should be of special
8::CODE;;interest.
9::CODE;;Configure a TUIO provider in the config.ini
10::CODE;;-------------------------------------------
11::CODE;;The TUIO provider can be configured in the configuration file in the
12::CODE;;``[input]`` section::
13::CODE;;[input]
15::CODE;;multitouchtable = tuio,192.168.0.1:3333
16::CODE;;Configure a TUIO provider in the App
17::CODE;;------------------------------------
18::CODE;;You must add the provider before your application is run, like this::
19::CODE;;from kivy.app import App
20::CODE;;from kivy.config import Config
21::CODE;;class TestApp(App):
22::CODE;;def build(self):
23::CODE;;Config.set('input', 'multitouchscreen1', 'tuio,0.0.0.0:3333')
28::CODE;;return
29::CODE;;'''
30::CODE;;__all__ = ('TuioMotionEventProvider', 'Tuio2dCurMotionEvent',
31::CODE;;'Tuio2dObjMotionEvent')
32::CODE;;from kivy.logger import Logger
33::CODE;;from functools import partial
34::CODE;;from collections import deque
35::CODE;;from kivy.input.provider import MotionEventProvider
36::CODE;;from kivy.input.factory import MotionEventFactory
37::CODE;;from kivy.input.motionevent import MotionEvent
38::CODE;;from kivy.input.shape import ShapeRect
39::CODE;;class TuioMotionEventProvider(MotionEventProvider):
40::CODE;;'''The TUIO provider listens to a socket and handles some of the incoming
41::CODE;;OSC messages:
42::CODE;;* /tuio/2Dcur
43::CODE;;* /tuio/2Dobj
44::CODE;;You can easily extend the provider to handle new TUIO paths like so::
47::CODE;;class TuioNEWPATHMotionEvent(MotionEvent):
48::CODE;;def depack(self, args):
53::CODE;;if len(args) == 2:
54::CODE;;self.sx, self.sy = args
55::CODE;;self.profile = ('pos', )
56::CODE;;self.sy = 1 - self.sy
57::CODE;;super().depack(args)
60::CODE;;TuioMotionEventProvider.register('/tuio/PATH', TuioNEWPATHMotionEvent)
61::CODE;;.. note::
62::CODE;;The class name is of no technical importance. Your class will be
63::CODE;;associated with the path that you pass to the ``register()``
64::CODE;;function. To keep things simple, you should name your class after the
65::CODE;;path that it handles, though.
66::CODE;;'''
67::CODE;;__handlers__ = {}
68::CODE;;def __init__(self, device, args):
69::CODE;;super().__init__(device, args)
70::CODE;;args = args.split(',')
71::CODE;;if len(args) == 0:
72::CODE;;Logger.error('Tuio: Invalid configuration for TUIO provider')
73::CODE;;Logger.error('Tuio: Format must be ip:port (eg. 127.0.0.1:3333)')
74::CODE;;err = 'Tuio: Current configuration is <%s>' % (str(','.join(args)))
75::CODE;;Logger.error(err)
76::CODE;;return
77::CODE;;ipport = args[0].split(':')
78::CODE;;if len(ipport) != 2:
79::CODE;;Logger.error('Tuio: Invalid configuration for TUIO provider')
80::CODE;;Logger.error('Tuio: Format must be ip:port (eg. 127.0.0.1:3333)')
81::CODE;;err = 'Tuio: Current configuration is <%s>' % (str(','.join(args)))
82::CODE;;Logger.error(err)
83::CODE;;return
84::CODE;;self.ip, self.port = args[0].split(':')
85::CODE;;self.port = int(self.port)
86::CODE;;self.handlers = {}
87::CODE;;self.oscid = None
88::CODE;;self.tuio_event_q = deque()
89::CODE;;self.touches = {}
90::CODE;;@staticmethod
91::CODE;;def register(oscpath, classname):
92::CODE;;'''Register a new path to handle in TUIO provider'''
93::CODE;;TuioMotionEventProvider.__handlers__[oscpath] = classname
94::CODE;;@staticmethod
95::CODE;;def unregister(oscpath, classname):
96::CODE;;'''Unregister a path to stop handling it in the TUIO provider'''
97::CODE;;if oscpath in TuioMotionEventProvider.__handlers__:
98::CODE;;del TuioMotionEventProvider.__handlers__[oscpath]
99::CODE;;@staticmethod
100::CODE;;def create(oscpath, **kwargs):
101::CODE;;'''Create a touch event from a TUIO path'''
102::CODE;;if oscpath not in TuioMotionEventProvider.__handlers__:
103::CODE;;raise Exception('Unknown %s touch path' % oscpath)
104::CODE;;return TuioMotionEventProvider.__handlers__[oscpath](**kwargs)
105::CODE;;def start(self):
106::CODE;;'''Start the TUIO provider'''
107::CODE;;try:
108::CODE;;from oscpy.server import OSCThreadServer
109::CODE;;except ImportError:
110::CODE;;Logger.info(
111::CODE;;'Please install the oscpy python module to use the TUIO '
112::CODE;;'provider.'
113::CODE;;)
114::CODE;;raise
115::CODE;;self.oscid = osc = OSCThreadServer()
116::CODE;;osc.listen(self.ip, self.port, default=True)
117::CODE;;for oscpath in TuioMotionEventProvider.__handlers__:
118::CODE;;self.touches[oscpath] = {}
119::CODE;;osc.bind(oscpath, partial(self._osc_tuio_cb, oscpath))
120::CODE;;def stop(self):
121::CODE;;'''Stop the TUIO provider'''
122::CODE;;self.oscid.stop_all()
123::CODE;;def update(self, dispatch_fn):
124::CODE;;'''Update the TUIO provider (pop events from the queue)'''
126::CODE;;while True:
127::CODE;;try:
128::CODE;;value = self.tuio_event_q.pop()
129::CODE;;except IndexError:
131::CODE;;return
132::CODE;;self._update(dispatch_fn, value)
133::CODE;;def _osc_tuio_cb(self, oscpath, address, *args):
134::CODE;;self.tuio_event_q.appendleft([oscpath, address, args])
135::CODE;;def _update(self, dispatch_fn, value):
136::CODE;;oscpath, command, args = value
138::CODE;;if command not in [b'alive', b'set']:
139::CODE;;return
141::CODE;;if command == b'set':
142::CODE;;id = args[0]
143::CODE;;if id not in self.touches[oscpath]:
145::CODE;;touch = TuioMotionEventProvider.__handlers__[oscpath](
146::CODE;;self.device, id, args[1:])
147::CODE;;self.touches[oscpath][id] = touch
148::CODE;;dispatch_fn('begin', touch)
149::CODE;;else:
151::CODE;;touch = self.touches[oscpath][id]
152::CODE;;touch.move(args[1:])
153::CODE;;dispatch_fn('update', touch)
155::CODE;;if command == b'alive':
156::CODE;;alives = args
157::CODE;;to_delete = []
158::CODE;;for id in self.touches[oscpath]:
159::CODE;;if id not in alives:
161::CODE;;touch = self.touches[oscpath][id]
162::CODE;;if touch not in to_delete:
163::CODE;;to_delete.append(touch)
164::CODE;;for touch in to_delete:
165::CODE;;dispatch_fn('end', touch)
166::CODE;;del self.touches[oscpath][touch.id]
167::CODE;;class TuioMotionEvent(MotionEvent):
168::CODE;;'''Abstraction for TUIO touches/fiducials.
169::CODE;;Depending on the tracking software you use (e.g. Movid, CCV, etc.) and its
170::CODE;;TUIO implementation, the TuioMotionEvent object can support multiple
171::CODE;;profiles such as:
172::CODE;;* Fiducial ID: profile name 'markerid', attribute ``.fid``
173::CODE;;* Position: profile name 'pos', attributes ``.x``, ``.y``
174::CODE;;* Angle: profile name 'angle', attribute ``.a``
175::CODE;;* Velocity vector: profile name 'mov', attributes ``.X``, ``.Y``
176::CODE;;* Rotation velocity: profile name 'rot', attribute ``.A``
177::CODE;;* Motion acceleration: profile name 'motacc', attribute ``.m``
178::CODE;;* Rotation acceleration: profile name 'rotacc', attribute ``.r``
179::CODE;;'''
180::CODE;;__attrs__ = ('a', 'b', 'c', 'X', 'Y', 'Z', 'A', 'B', 'C', 'm', 'r')
181::CODE;;def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
182::CODE;;kwargs.setdefault('is_touch', True)
183::CODE;;kwargs.setdefault('type_id', 'touch')
184::CODE;;super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
186::CODE;;self.a = 0.0
187::CODE;;self.b = 0.0
188::CODE;;self.c = 0.0
189::CODE;;self.X = 0.0
190::CODE;;self.Y = 0.0
191::CODE;;self.Z = 0.0
192::CODE;;self.A = 0.0
193::CODE;;self.B = 0.0
194::CODE;;self.C = 0.0
195::CODE;;self.m = 0.0
196::CODE;;self.r = 0.0
197::CODE;;angle = property(lambda self: self.a)
198::CODE;;mot_accel = property(lambda self: self.m)
199::CODE;;rot_accel = property(lambda self: self.r)
200::CODE;;xmot = property(lambda self: self.X)
201::CODE;;ymot = property(lambda self: self.Y)
202::CODE;;zmot = property(lambda self: self.Z)
