1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Input recorder
3::CODE;;==============
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.1.0
5::CODE;;.. warning::
6::CODE;;This part of Kivy is still experimental and this API is subject to
7::CODE;;change in a future version.
8::CODE;;This is a class that can record and replay some input events. This can
9::CODE;;be used for test cases, screen savers etc.
10::CODE;;Once activated, the recorder will listen for any input event and save its
11::CODE;;properties in a file with the delta time. Later, you can play the input
12::CODE;;file: it will generate fake touch events with the saved properties and
13::CODE;;dispatch it to the event loop.
14::CODE;;By default, only the position is saved ('pos' profile and 'sx', 'sy',
15::CODE;;attributes). Change it only if you understand how input handling works.
16::CODE;;Recording events
17::CODE;;----------------
18::CODE;;The best way is to use the "recorder" module. Check the :doc:`api-kivy.modules`
19::CODE;;documentation to see how to activate a module.
20::CODE;;Once activated, you can press F8 to start the recording. By default,
21::CODE;;events will be written to `<currentpath>/recorder.kvi`. When you want to
22::CODE;;stop recording, press F8 again.
23::CODE;;You can replay the file by pressing F7.
24::CODE;;Check the :doc:`api-kivy.modules.recorder` module for more information.
25::CODE;;Manual play
26::CODE;;-----------
27::CODE;;You can manually open a recorder file, and play it by doing::
28::CODE;;from kivy.input.recorder import Recorder
29::CODE;;rec = Recorder(filename='myrecorder.kvi')
30::CODE;;rec.play = True
31::CODE;;If you want to loop over that file, you can do::
32::CODE;;from kivy.input.recorder import Recorder
33::CODE;;def recorder_loop(instance, value):
34::CODE;;if value is False:
35::CODE;;instance.play = True
36::CODE;;rec = Recorder(filename='myrecorder.kvi')
37::CODE;;rec.bind(play=recorder_loop)
38::CODE;;rec.play = True
39::CODE;;Recording more attributes
40::CODE;;-------------------------
41::CODE;;You can extend the attributes to save on one condition: attributes values must
42::CODE;;be simple values, not instances of complex classes.
43::CODE;;Let's say you want to save the angle and pressure of the touch, if available::
44::CODE;;from kivy.input.recorder import Recorder
45::CODE;;rec = Recorder(filename='myrecorder.kvi',
46::CODE;;record_attrs=['is_touch', 'sx', 'sy', 'angle', 'pressure'],
47::CODE;;record_profile_mask=['pos', 'angle', 'pressure'])
48::CODE;;rec.record = True
49::CODE;;Or with modules variables::
50::CODE;;$ python main.py -m recorder,attrs=is_touch:sx:sy:angle:pressure, \
51::CODE;;profile_mask=pos:angle:pressure
52::CODE;;Known limitations
53::CODE;;-----------------
54::CODE;;- Unable to save attributes with instances of complex classes.
55::CODE;;- Values that represent time will not be adjusted.
56::CODE;;- Can replay only complete records. If a begin/update/end event is missing,
57::CODE;;this could lead to ghost touches.
58::CODE;;- Stopping the replay before the end can lead to ghost touches.
59::CODE;;'''
60::CODE;;__all__ = ('Recorder', )
61::CODE;;from os.path import exists
62::CODE;;from time import time
63::CODE;;from kivy.event import EventDispatcher
64::CODE;;from kivy.properties import ObjectProperty, BooleanProperty, StringProperty, \
65::CODE;;NumericProperty, ListProperty
66::CODE;;from kivy.input.motionevent import MotionEvent

72::CODE;;def depack(self, args):
73::CODE;;for key, value in list(args.items()):
74::CODE;;setattr(self, key, value)
75::CODE;;super(RecorderMotionEvent, self).depack(args)

169::CODE;;else:

177::CODE;;pass
178::CODE;;def on_play(self, instance, value):
179::CODE;;if not value:

181::CODE;;EventLoop.remove_input_provider(self)
182::CODE;;return
183::CODE;;if not exists(self.filename):

187::CODE;;with open(self.filename, 'r') as fd:

189::CODE;;if len(data) < 2:

199::CODE;;self.play_time = time()
200::CODE;;self.play_me = {}

202::CODE;;(len(self.play_data), self.filename))

207::CODE;;if not self.play_data:
208::CODE;;Logger.info('Recorder: Playing finished.')
209::CODE;;self.play = False
210::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_stop')
211::CODE;;dt = time() - self.play_time
212::CODE;;while self.play_data:
213::CODE;;event = self.play_data[0]
214::CODE;;assert len(event) == 4
215::CODE;;if event[0] > dt:
216::CODE;;return
217::CODE;;me = None
218::CODE;;etype, uid, args = event[1:]
219::CODE;;if etype == 'begin':
220::CODE;;me = RecorderMotionEvent('recorder', uid, args)
221::CODE;;self.play_me[uid] = me
222::CODE;;elif etype == 'update':
223::CODE;;me = self.play_me[uid]
224::CODE;;me.depack(args)
225::CODE;;elif etype == 'end':
226::CODE;;me = self.play_me.pop(uid)
227::CODE;;me.depack(args)
228::CODE;;elif etype == 'keydown':
229::CODE;;self.window.dispatch(
230::CODE;;'on_key_down',
231::CODE;;args['key'],
232::CODE;;args['scancode'],
233::CODE;;args['codepoint'],
234::CODE;;args['modifier'])
235::CODE;;elif etype == 'keyup':
236::CODE;;self.window.dispatch(
237::CODE;;'on_key_up',
238::CODE;;args['key'],
239::CODE;;args['scancode'],
240::CODE;;args['codepoint'],
241::CODE;;args['modifier'])
242::CODE;;elif etype == 'keyboard':
243::CODE;;self.window.dispatch(
244::CODE;;'on_keyboard',
245::CODE;;args['key'],
246::CODE;;args['scancode'],
247::CODE;;args['codepoint'],
248::CODE;;args['modifier'])
249::CODE;;if me:
250::CODE;;dispatch_fn(etype, me)
251::CODE;;self.play_data.pop(0)
252::CODE;;def start(win, ctx):
253::CODE;;ctx.recorder = Recorder(window=win)
254::CODE;;def stop(win, ctx):
255::CODE;;if hasattr(ctx, 'recorder'):
256::CODE;;ctx.recorder.release()

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Interactive launcher
3::CODE;;====================
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.3.0
5::CODE;;.. deprecated:: 1.10.0
6::CODE;;The interactive launcher has been deprecated.
7::CODE;;The :class:`InteractiveLauncher` provides a user-friendly python shell
8::CODE;;interface to an :class:`App` so that it can be prototyped and debugged
9::CODE;;interactively.
10::CODE;;.. note::
11::CODE;;The Kivy API intends for some functions to only be run once or before the
12::CODE;;main EventLoop has started. Methods that can normally be called during the
13::CODE;;course of an application will work as intended, but specifically overriding
14::CODE;;methods such as :meth:`on_touch` dynamically leads to trouble.
15::CODE;;Creating an InteractiveLauncher
16::CODE;;-------------------------------
17::CODE;;Take your existing subclass of :class:`App` (this can be production code) and
18::CODE;;pass an instance to the :class:`InteractiveLauncher` constructor. ::
19::CODE;;from kivy.interactive import InteractiveLauncher
20::CODE;;from kivy.app import App
21::CODE;;from kivy.uix.button import Button
22::CODE;;class MyApp(App):
23::CODE;;def build(self):
24::CODE;;return Button(text='Hello Shell')
25::CODE;;launcher = InteractiveLauncher(MyApp())
26::CODE;;launcher.run()
27::CODE;;After pressing *enter*, the script will return. This allows the interpreter to
28::CODE;;continue running. Inspection or modification of the :class:`App` can be done
29::CODE;;safely through the InteractiveLauncher instance or the provided
30::CODE;;:class:`SafeMembrane` class instances.
31::CODE;;.. note::
32::CODE;;If you want to test this example, start Python without any file to have
33::CODE;;already an interpreter, and copy/paste all the lines. You'll still have the
34::CODE;;interpreter at the end + the kivy application running.
35::CODE;;Interactive Development
36::CODE;;-----------------------
37::CODE;;IPython provides a fast way to learn the Kivy API. The :class:`App` instance
38::CODE;;and all of its attributes, including methods and the entire widget tree,
39::CODE;;can be quickly listed by using the '.' operator and pressing 'tab'. Try this
40::CODE;;code in an Ipython shell. ::
41::CODE;;from kivy.interactive import InteractiveLauncher
42::CODE;;from kivy.app import App
43::CODE;;from kivy.uix.widget import Widget
44::CODE;;from kivy.graphics import Color, Ellipse
45::CODE;;class MyPaintWidget(Widget):
46::CODE;;def on_touch_down(self, touch):
47::CODE;;with self.canvas:
48::CODE;;Color(1, 1, 0)
49::CODE;;d = 30.
50::CODE;;Ellipse(pos=(touch.x - d/2, touch.y - d/2), size=(d, d))
51::CODE;;class TestApp(App):
52::CODE;;def build(self):
53::CODE;;return Widget()
54::CODE;;i = InteractiveLauncher(TestApp())
55::CODE;;i.run()
59::CODE;;i.root.add_widget(MyPaintWidget())
60::CODE;;i.safeIn()
63::CODE;;i.safeOut()
66::CODE;;i.root.canvas.clear()
67::CODE;;.. note::
68::CODE;;All of the proxies used in the module store their referent in the
69::CODE;;:attr:`_ref` attribute, which can be accessed directly if needed, such as
70::CODE;;for getting doc strings. :func:`help` and :func:`type` will access the
71::CODE;;proxy, not its referent.
72::CODE;;Directly Pausing the Application
73::CODE;;--------------------------------
74::CODE;;Both the :class:`InteractiveLauncher` and :class:`SafeMembrane` hold internal
75::CODE;;references to the :class:`EventLoop`'s 'safe' and 'confirmed'
76::CODE;;:class:`threading.Event` objects. You can use their safing methods to control
77::CODE;;the application manually.
78::CODE;;:meth:`SafeMembrane.safeIn` will cause the application to pause and
79::CODE;;:meth:`SafeMembrane.safeOut` will allow a paused application
80::CODE;;to continue running. This is potentially useful for scripting actions into
81::CODE;;functions that need the screen to update etc.
82::CODE;;.. note::
83::CODE;;The pausing is implemented via the
84::CODE;;:class:`Clocks' <kivy.clock.Clock>`
85::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.clock.ClockBase.schedule_once` method
86::CODE;;and occurs before the start of each frame.
87::CODE;;Adding Attributes Dynamically
88::CODE;;-----------------------------
89::CODE;;.. note::
90::CODE;;This module uses threading and object proxies to encapsulate the running
91::CODE;;:class:`App`. Deadlocks and memory corruption can occur if making direct
92::CODE;;references inside the thread without going through the provided proxy(s).
93::CODE;;The :class:`InteractiveLauncher` can have attributes added to it exactly like a
94::CODE;;normal object and if these were created from outside the membrane, they will
95::CODE;;not be threadsafe because the external references to them in the python
96::CODE;;interpreter do not go through InteractiveLauncher's membrane behavior,
97::CODE;;inherited from :class:`SafeMembrane`.
98::CODE;;To threadsafe these external references, simply assign them to
99::CODE;;:class:`SafeMembrane` instances of themselves like so::
100::CODE;;from kivy.interactive import SafeMembrane
101::CODE;;interactiveLauncher.attribute = myNewObject
103::CODE;;myNewObject = SafeMembrane(myNewObject)
105::CODE;;myNewObject.method()
106::CODE;;TODO
107::CODE;;====
108::CODE;;Unit tests, examples, and a better explanation of which methods are safe in a
109::CODE;;running application would be nice. All three would be excellent.
110::CODE;;Could be re-written with a context-manager style i.e. ::
111::CODE;;with safe:
112::CODE;;foo()
113::CODE;;Any use cases besides compacting code?
114::CODE;;'''
115::CODE;;__all__ = ('SafeMembrane', 'InteractiveLauncher')
116::CODE;;import inspect
117::CODE;;from threading import Thread, Event
118::CODE;;from kivy.app import App
119::CODE;;from kivy.base import EventLoop
120::CODE;;from kivy.clock import Clock
121::CODE;;from kivy.utils import deprecated
122::CODE;;def safeWait(dt):
123::CODE;;EventLoop.confirmed.set()
124::CODE;;EventLoop.safe.wait()
125::CODE;;EventLoop.confirmed.clear()
126::CODE;;def unwrap(ob):
127::CODE;;while isinstance(ob, SafeMembrane):
128::CODE;;ob = ob._ref
129::CODE;;return ob
130::CODE;;class SafeMembrane(object):
131::CODE;;'''
132::CODE;;This help is for a proxy object. Did you want help on the proxy's referent
133::CODE;;instead? Try using help(<instance>._ref)
134::CODE;;The SafeMembrane is a threadsafe proxy that also returns attributes as new
135::CODE;;thread-safe objects
136::CODE;;and makes thread-safe method calls, preventing thread-unsafe objects
137::CODE;;from leaking into the user's environment.
138::CODE;;'''
139::CODE;;__slots__ = ('_ref', 'safe', 'confirmed')
140::CODE;;def __init__(self, ob, *args, **kwargs):
141::CODE;;self.confirmed = EventLoop.confirmed
142::CODE;;self.safe = EventLoop.safe
143::CODE;;self._ref = ob
144::CODE;;def safeIn(self):
151::CODE;;self.safe.set()
152::CODE;;def isMethod(self, fn):
153::CODE;;return inspect.ismethod(fn)
159::CODE;;def __repr__(self):
160::CODE;;return self._ref.__repr__()
161::CODE;;def __call__(self, *args, **kw):
162::CODE;;self.safeIn()
163::CODE;;args = list(map(unwrap, args))
164::CODE;;for k in list(kw.keys()):
165::CODE;;kw[k] = unwrap(kw[k])
166::CODE;;r = self._ref(*args, **kw)
167::CODE;;self.safeOut()
168::CODE;;if r is not None:
169::CODE;;return SafeMembrane(r)
170::CODE;;def __getattribute__(self, attr, oga=object.__getattribute__):
171::CODE;;if attr.startswith('__') or attr == '_ref':
172::CODE;;subject = oga(self, '_ref')
173::CODE;;if attr == '_ref':
174::CODE;;return subject
175::CODE;;return getattr(subject, attr)
176::CODE;;return oga(self, attr)
177::CODE;;def __getattr__(self, attr, oga=object.__getattribute__):
178::CODE;;r = getattr(oga(self, '_ref'), attr)
179::CODE;;return SafeMembrane(r)
180::CODE;;def __setattr__(self, attr, val, osa=object.__setattr__):
181::CODE;;if (attr == '_ref' or
182::CODE;;hasattr(type(self), attr) and not attr.startswith('__')):
183::CODE;;osa(self, attr, val)
184::CODE;;else:
185::CODE;;self.safeIn()
186::CODE;;val = unwrap(val)
187::CODE;;setattr(self._ref, attr, val)
188::CODE;;self.safeOut()
189::CODE;;def __delattr__(self, attr, oda=object.__delattr__):
190::CODE;;self.safeIn()
191::CODE;;delattr(self._ref, attr)
192::CODE;;self.safeOut()
193::CODE;;def __bool__(self):
194::CODE;;return bool(self._ref)
195::CODE;;def __getitem__(self, arg):
196::CODE;;return SafeMembrane(self._ref[arg])
197::CODE;;def __setitem__(self, arg, val):
198::CODE;;self.safeIn()
199::CODE;;val = unwrap(val)
200::CODE;;self._ref[arg] = val
201::CODE;;self.safeOut()
202::CODE;;def __delitem__(self, arg):
203::CODE;;self.safeIn()
204::CODE;;del self._ref[arg]
205::CODE;;self.safeOut()
206::CODE;;def __getslice__(self, i, j):
207::CODE;;return SafeMembrane(self._ref[i:j])
208::CODE;;def __setslice__(self, i, j, val):
209::CODE;;self.safeIn()
210::CODE;;val = unwrap(val)
211::CODE;;self._ref[i:j] = val
212::CODE;;self.safeOut()
213::CODE;;def __delslice__(self, i, j):
214::CODE;;self.safeIn()
215::CODE;;del self._ref[i:j]
216::CODE;;self.safeOut()
217::CODE;;def __enter__(self, *args, **kwargs):
218::CODE;;self.safeIn()
219::CODE;;self._ref.__enter__(*args, **kwargs)
220::CODE;;def __exit__(self, *args, **kwargs):
221::CODE;;self._ref.__exit__(*args, **kwargs)
222::CODE;;self.safeOut()
223::CODE;;class InteractiveLauncher(SafeMembrane):
224::CODE;;'''
225::CODE;;Proxy to an application instance that launches it in a thread and
226::CODE;;then returns and acts as a proxy to the application in the thread.
227::CODE;;'''
228::CODE;;__slots__ = ('_ref', 'safe', 'confirmed', 'thread', 'app')
229::CODE;;@deprecated
230::CODE;;def __init__(self, app=None, *args, **kwargs):
231::CODE;;if app is None:
232::CODE;;app = App()
233::CODE;;EventLoop.safe = Event()
234::CODE;;self.safe = EventLoop.safe
235::CODE;;self.safe.set()
236::CODE;;EventLoop.confirmed = Event()
237::CODE;;self.confirmed = EventLoop.confirmed
238::CODE;;self.app = app
239::CODE;;def startApp(app=app, *args, **kwargs):
240::CODE;;app.run(*args, **kwargs)
241::CODE;;self.thread = Thread(target=startApp, *args, **kwargs)
242::CODE;;def run(self):
243::CODE;;self.thread.start()
246::CODE;;self._ref = self.app
247::CODE;;def stop(self):
248::CODE;;EventLoop.quit = True
249::CODE;;self.thread.join()
251::CODE;;def __repr__(self):
252::CODE;;return self.app.__repr__()
1::CODE;;'''Kivy Language
2::CODE;;=============
3::CODE;;The Kivy language is a language dedicated to describing user interface and
4::CODE;;interactions. You could compare this language to Qt's QML
5::CODE;;(http://qt.nokia.com), but we included new concepts such as rule definitions
6::CODE;;(which are somewhat akin to what you may know from CSS), templating and so on.
7::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.7.0
8::CODE;;The Builder doesn't execute canvas expressions in realtime anymore. It will
9::CODE;;pack all the expressions that need to be executed first and execute them
10::CODE;;after dispatching input, just before drawing the frame. If you want to
11::CODE;;force the execution of canvas drawing, just call
12::CODE;;:meth:`Builder.sync <BuilderBase.sync>`.
13::CODE;;An experimental profiling tool for the kv lang is also included. You can
14::CODE;;activate it by setting the environment variable `KIVY_PROFILE_LANG=1`.
15::CODE;;It will then generate an html file named `builder_stats.html`.
16::CODE;;Overview
17::CODE;;--------
18::CODE;;The language consists of several constructs that you can use:
19::CODE;;Rules
20::CODE;;A rule is similar to a CSS rule. A rule applies to specific widgets (or
21::CODE;;classes thereof) in your widget tree and modifies them in a
22::CODE;;certain way.
23::CODE;;You can use rules to specify interactive behavior or use them to add
24::CODE;;graphical representations of the widgets they apply to.
25::CODE;;You can target a specific class of widgets (similar to the CSS
26::CODE;;concept of a *class*) by using the ``cls`` attribute (e.g.
27::CODE;;``cls=MyTestWidget``).
28::CODE;;A Root Widget
29::CODE;;You can use the language to create your entire user interface.
30::CODE;;A kv file must contain only one root widget at most.
31::CODE;;Dynamic Classes
32::CODE;;*(introduced in version 1.7.0)*
33::CODE;;Dynamic classes let you create new widgets and rules on-the-fly,
34::CODE;;without any Python declaration.
35::CODE;;Templates (deprecated)
36::CODE;;*(introduced in version 1.0.5, deprecated from version 1.7.0)*
37::CODE;;Templates were used to populate parts of an application, such as
38::CODE;;styling the content of a list (e.g. icon on the left, text on the
39::CODE;;right). They are now deprecated by dynamic classes.
40::CODE;;Syntax of a kv File
41::CODE;;-------------------
42::CODE;;.. highlight:: kv
43::CODE;;A Kivy language file must have ``.kv`` as filename extension.
44::CODE;;The content of the file should always start with the Kivy header, where
45::CODE;;`version` must be replaced with the Kivy language version you're using.
46::CODE;;For now, use 1.0::
49::CODE;;The `content` can contain rule definitions, a root widget, dynamic class
50::CODE;;definitions and templates::
53::CODE;;<Rule1,Rule2>:
55::CODE;;<Rule3>:
58::CODE;;RootClassName:
61::CODE;;<NewWidget@BaseClass>:
64::CODE;;[TemplateName@BaseClass1,BaseClass2]:
66::CODE;;Regardless of whether it's a rule, root widget, dynamic class or
67::CODE;;template you're defining, the definition should look like this::
69::CODE;;<ClassName>:
70::CODE;;prop1: value1
71::CODE;;prop2: value2
72::CODE;;canvas:
73::CODE;;CanvasInstruction1:
74::CODE;;canvasprop1: value1
75::CODE;;CanvasInstruction2:
76::CODE;;canvasprop2: value2
77::CODE;;AnotherClass:
78::CODE;;prop3: value1
79::CODE;;Here `prop1` and `prop2` are the properties of `ClassName` and `prop3` is the
80::CODE;;property of `AnotherClass`. If the widget doesn't have a property with
81::CODE;;the given name, an :class:`~kivy.properties.ObjectProperty` will be
82::CODE;;automatically created and added to the widget.
83::CODE;;`AnotherClass` will be created and added as a child of the `ClassName`
84::CODE;;instance.
85::CODE;;- The indentation is important and must be consistent. The spacing must be a
86::CODE;;multiple of the number of spaces used on the first indented line. Spaces
87::CODE;;are encouraged: mixing tabs and spaces is not recommended.
88::CODE;;- The value of a property must be given on a single line (for now at least).
89::CODE;;- Keep class names capitalized to avoid syntax errors.
90::CODE;;- The `canvas` property is special: you can put graphics instructions in it
91::CODE;;to create a graphical representation of the current class.
92::CODE;;Here is a simple example of a kv file that contains a root widget::
94::CODE;;Button:
95::CODE;;text: 'Hello world'
96::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.7.0
97::CODE;;The indentation is not limited to 4 spaces anymore. The spacing must be a
98::CODE;;multiple of the number of spaces used on the first indented line.
99::CODE;;Both the :meth:`~BuilderBase.load_file` and the
100::CODE;;:meth:`~BuilderBase.load_string` methods
101::CODE;;return the root widget defined in your kv file/string. They will also add any
102::CODE;;class and template definitions to the :class:`~kivy.factory.Factory` for later
103::CODE;;usage.
104::CODE;;Value Expressions, on_property Expressions, ids, and Reserved Keywords
105::CODE;;---------------------------------------------------------------------
106::CODE;;When you specify a property's value, the value is evaluated as a Python
107::CODE;;expression. This expression can be static or dynamic, which means that
108::CODE;;the value can use the values of other properties using reserved keywords.
109::CODE;;self
110::CODE;;The keyword self references the "current widget instance"::
111::CODE;;Button:
112::CODE;;text: 'My state is %s' % self.state
113::CODE;;root
114::CODE;;This keyword is available only in rule definitions and represents the
115::CODE;;root widget of the rule (the first instance of the rule)::
116::CODE;;<MyWidget>:
117::CODE;;custom: 'Hello world'
118::CODE;;Button:
119::CODE;;text: root.custom
120::CODE;;app
121::CODE;;This keyword always refers to your app instance. It's equivalent
122::CODE;;to a call to :meth:`kivy.app.App.get_running_app` in Python. ::
123::CODE;;Label:
124::CODE;;text: app.name
125::CODE;;args
126::CODE;;This keyword is available in on_<action> callbacks. It refers to the
127::CODE;;arguments passed to the callback. ::
128::CODE;;TextInput:
129::CODE;;on_focus: self.insert_text("Focus" if args[1] else "No focus")
130::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 2.1.0
131::CODE;;f-strings are now parsed in value expressions, allowing to bind to the
132::CODE;;properties that they contain.
133::CODE;;.. kv-lang-ids:
134::CODE;;ids
135::CODE;;~~~
136::CODE;;Class definitions may contain ids which can be used as a keywords:::
137::CODE;;<MyWidget>:
138::CODE;;Button:
139::CODE;;id: btn1
140::CODE;;Button:
141::CODE;;text: 'The state of the other button is %s' % btn1.state
142::CODE;;Please note that the `id` will not be available in the widget instance:
143::CODE;;it is used exclusively for external references. `id` is a weakref to the
144::CODE;;widget, and not the widget itself. The widget itself can be accessed
145::CODE;;with `<id>.__self__` (`btn1.__self__` in this case).
146::CODE;;When the kv file is processed, weakrefs to all the widgets tagged with ids are
147::CODE;;added to the root widget's `ids` dictionary. In other words, following on from
148::CODE;;the example above, the buttons state could also be accessed as follows:
149::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
150::CODE;;widget = MyWidget()
151::CODE;;state = widget.ids["btn1"].state
153::CODE;;state = widget.ids.btn1.state
154::CODE;;Note that the outermost widget applies the kv rules to all its inner widgets
155::CODE;;before any other rules are applied. This means if an inner widget contains ids,
156::CODE;;these ids may not be available during the inner widget's `__init__` function.
157::CODE;;Valid expressions
158::CODE;;~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
159::CODE;;There are two places that accept python statements in a kv file:
160::CODE;;after a property, which assigns to the property the result of the expression
161::CODE;;(such as the text of a button as shown above) and after a on_property, which
162::CODE;;executes the statement when the property is updated (such as on_state).
163::CODE;;In the former case, the
164::CODE;;`expression <http://docs.python.org/2/reference/expressions.html>`_ can only
165::CODE;;span a single line, cannot be extended to multiple lines using newline
166::CODE;;escaping, and must return a value. An example of a valid expression is
167::CODE;;``text: self.state and ('up' if self.pressed else 'down')``.
168::CODE;;In the latter case, multiple single line statements are valid, including
169::CODE;;those that escape their newline, as long as they don't add an indentation
170::CODE;;level.
171::CODE;;Examples of valid statements are:
172::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
173::CODE;;on_press: if self.state == 'normal': print('normal')
174::CODE;;on_state:
175::CODE;;if self.state == 'normal': print('normal')
176::CODE;;else: print('down')
177::CODE;;if self.state == 'normal': \\
178::CODE;;print('multiline normal')
179::CODE;;for i in range(10): print(i)
180::CODE;;print([1,2,3,4,
181::CODE;;5,6,7])
182::CODE;;An example of a invalid statement:
183::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
184::CODE;;on_state:
185::CODE;;if self.state == 'normal':
186::CODE;;print('normal')
187::CODE;;Relation Between Values and Properties
188::CODE;;--------------------------------------
189::CODE;;When you use the Kivy language, you might notice that we do some work
190::CODE;;behind the scenes to automatically make things work properly. You should
191::CODE;;know that :doc:`api-kivy.properties` implement the
192::CODE;;`Observer Design Pattern <http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Observer_pattern>`_.
193::CODE;;That means that you can bind your own function to be
194::CODE;;called when the value of a property changes (i.e. you passively
195::CODE;;`observe` the property for potential changes).
196::CODE;;The Kivy language detects properties in your `value` expression and will create
197::CODE;;callbacks to automatically update the property via your expression when changes
198::CODE;;occur.
199::CODE;;Here's a simple example that demonstrates this behavior::
200::CODE;;Button:
201::CODE;;text: str(self.state)
202::CODE;;In this example, the parser detects that `self.state` is a dynamic value (a
203::CODE;;property). The :attr:`~kivy.uix.button.Button.state` property of the button
204::CODE;;can change at any moment (when the user touches it).
205::CODE;;We now want this button to display its own state as text, even as the state
206::CODE;;changes. To do this, we use the state property of the Button and use it in the
207::CODE;;value expression for the button's `text` property, which controls what text is
208::CODE;;displayed on the button (We also convert the state to a string representation).
209::CODE;;Now, whenever the button state changes, the text property will be updated
210::CODE;;automatically.
211::CODE;;Remember: The value is a python expression! That means that you can do
212::CODE;;something more interesting like::
213::CODE;;Button:
214::CODE;;text: 'Plop world' if self.pressed else 'Release me!'
215::CODE;;The Button text changes with the state of the button. By default, the button
216::CODE;;text will be 'Plop world', but when the button is being pressed, the text will
217::CODE;;change to 'Release me!'.
218::CODE;;More precisely, the kivy language parser detects all substrings of the form
219::CODE;;`X.a.b` where `X` is `self` or `root` or `app` or a known id, and `a` and `b`
220::CODE;;are properties: it then adds the appropriate dependencies to cause the
221::CODE;;constraint to be reevaluated whenever something changes. For example,
222::CODE;;this works exactly as expected::
223::CODE;;<IndexedExample>:
224::CODE;;beta: self.a.b[self.c.d]
225::CODE;;However, due to limitations in the parser which hopefully may be lifted in the
226::CODE;;future, the following doesn't work::
227::CODE;;<BadExample>:
228::CODE;;beta: self.a.b[self.c.d].e.f
229::CODE;;indeed the `.e.f` part is not recognized because it doesn't follow the expected
230::CODE;;pattern, and so, does not result in an appropriate dependency being setup.
231::CODE;;Instead, an intermediate property should be introduced to allow the following
232::CODE;;constraint::
233::CODE;;<GoodExample>:
234::CODE;;alpha: self.a.b[self.c.d]
235::CODE;;beta: self.alpha.e.f
236::CODE;;In addition, properties in python f-strings are also not yet supported::
237::CODE;;<FStringExample>:
238::CODE;;text: f"I want to use {self.a} in property"
239::CODE;;Instead, the ``format()`` method should be used::
240::CODE;;<FormatStringExample>:
241::CODE;;text: "I want to use {} in property".format(self.a)
242::CODE;;Graphical Instructions
243::CODE;;----------------------
244::CODE;;The graphical instructions are a special part of the Kivy language. They are
245::CODE;;handled by the 'canvas' property definition::
246::CODE;;Widget:
247::CODE;;canvas:
248::CODE;;Color:
249::CODE;;rgb: (1, 1, 1)
250::CODE;;Rectangle:
251::CODE;;size: self.size
252::CODE;;pos: self.pos
253::CODE;;All the classes added inside the canvas property must be derived from the
254::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.graphics.Instruction` class. You cannot put any Widget class
255::CODE;;inside the canvas property (as that would not make sense because a
256::CODE;;widget is not a graphics instruction).
257::CODE;;If you want to do theming, you'll have the same question as in CSS: which rules
258::CODE;;have been executed first? In our case, the rules are executed
259::CODE;;in processing order (i.e. top-down).
260::CODE;;If you want to change how Buttons are rendered, you can create your own kv file
261::CODE;;and add something like this::
262::CODE;;<Button>:
263::CODE;;canvas:
264::CODE;;Color:
265::CODE;;rgb: (1, 0, 0)
266::CODE;;Rectangle:
267::CODE;;pos: self.pos
268::CODE;;size: self.size
269::CODE;;Rectangle:
270::CODE;;pos: self.pos
271::CODE;;size: self.texture_size
272::CODE;;texture: self.texture
273::CODE;;This will result in buttons having a red background with the label in the
274::CODE;;bottom left, in addition to all the preceding rules.
275::CODE;;You can clear all the previous instructions by using the `Clear` command::
276::CODE;;<Button>:
277::CODE;;canvas:
278::CODE;;Clear
279::CODE;;Color:
280::CODE;;rgb: (1, 0, 0)
281::CODE;;Rectangle:
282::CODE;;pos: self.pos
283::CODE;;size: self.size
284::CODE;;Rectangle:
285::CODE;;pos: self.pos
286::CODE;;size: self.texture_size
287::CODE;;texture: self.texture
288::CODE;;Then, only your rules that follow the `Clear` command will be taken into
289::CODE;;consideration.
290::CODE;;.. _dynamic_classes:
291::CODE;;Dynamic classes
292::CODE;;---------------
293::CODE;;Dynamic classes allow you to create new widgets on-the-fly, without any python
294::CODE;;declaration in the first place. The syntax of the dynamic classes is similar to
295::CODE;;the Rules, but you need to specify the base classes you want to
296::CODE;;subclass.
297::CODE;;The syntax looks like:
298::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
300::CODE;;<NewWidget@Button>:
303::CODE;;<NewWidget@ButtonBehavior+Label>:
305::CODE;;The `@` character is used to separate your class name from the classes you want
306::CODE;;to subclass. The Python equivalent would have been:
307::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
309::CODE;;class NewWidget(Button):
310::CODE;;pass
312::CODE;;class NewWidget(ButtonBehavior, Label):
313::CODE;;pass
314::CODE;;Any new properties, usually added in python code, should be declared
315::CODE;;first. If the property doesn't exist in the dynamic class, it will be
316::CODE;;automatically created as an :class:`~kivy.properties.ObjectProperty`
317::CODE;;(pre 1.8.0) or as an appropriate typed property (from version
318::CODE;;1.8.0).
319::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.8.0
320::CODE;;If the property value is an expression that can be evaluated right away (no
321::CODE;;external binding), then the value will be used as default value of the
322::CODE;;property, and the type of the value will be used for the specialization of
323::CODE;;the Property class. In other terms: if you declare `hello: "world"`, a new
324::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.properties.StringProperty` will be instantiated, with the
325::CODE;;default value `"world"`. Lists, tuples, dictionaries and strings are
326::CODE;;supported.
327::CODE;;Let's illustrate the usage of these dynamic classes with an
328::CODE;;implementation of a basic Image button. We could derive our classes from
329::CODE;;the Button and just add a property for the image filename:
330::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
331::CODE;;<ImageButton@Button>:
332::CODE;;source: None
333::CODE;;Image:
334::CODE;;source: root.source
335::CODE;;pos: root.pos
336::CODE;;size: root.size
338::CODE;;<MainUI>:
339::CODE;;BoxLayout:
340::CODE;;ImageButton:
341::CODE;;source: 'hello.png'
342::CODE;;on_press: root.do_something()
343::CODE;;ImageButton:
344::CODE;;source: 'world.png'
345::CODE;;on_press: root.do_something_else()
346::CODE;;In Python, you can create an instance of the dynamic class as follows:
347::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
348::CODE;;from kivy.factory import Factory
349::CODE;;button_inst = Factory.ImageButton()
350::CODE;;.. note::
351::CODE;;Using dynamic classes, a child class can be declared before its parent.
352::CODE;;This however, leads to the unintuitive situation where the parent
353::CODE;;properties/methods override those of the child. Be careful if you choose
354::CODE;;to do this.
355::CODE;;.. _template_usage:
356::CODE;;Templates
357::CODE;;---------
358::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.7.0
359::CODE;;Template usage is now deprecated. Please use Dynamic classes instead.
360::CODE;;Syntax of templates
361::CODE;;~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
362::CODE;;Using a template in Kivy requires 2 things :
365::CODE;;Syntax of a template:
366::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
368::CODE;;[ClassName@BaseClass]:
371::CODE;;[ClassName@BaseClass1,BaseClass2]:
373::CODE;;For example, for a list, you'll need to create a entry with a image on
374::CODE;;the left, and a label on the right. You can create a template for making
375::CODE;;that definition easier to use.
376::CODE;;So, we'll create a template that uses 2 entries in the context: an image
377::CODE;;filename and a title:
378::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
379::CODE;;[IconItem@BoxLayout]:
380::CODE;;Image:
381::CODE;;source: ctx.image
382::CODE;;Label:
383::CODE;;text: ctx.title
384::CODE;;Then in Python, you can instantiate the template using:
385::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
386::CODE;;from kivy.lang import Builder
390::CODE;;icon1 = Builder.template('IconItem', title='Hello world',
391::CODE;;image='myimage.png')
393::CODE;;ctx = {'title': 'Another hello world',
394::CODE;;'image': 'myimage2.png'}
395::CODE;;icon2 = Builder.template('IconItem', **ctx)
397::CODE;;Template example
398::CODE;;~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
399::CODE;;Most of time, when you are creating a screen in the kv lang, you use a lot of
400::CODE;;redefinitions. In our example, we'll create a Toolbar, based on a
401::CODE;;BoxLayout, and put in a few :class:`~kivy.uix.image.Image` widgets that
402::CODE;;will react to the *on_touch_down* event.
403::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
404::CODE;;<MyToolbar>:
405::CODE;;BoxLayout:
406::CODE;;Image:
407::CODE;;source: 'data/text.png'
408::CODE;;size: self.texture_size
409::CODE;;size_hint: None, None
410::CODE;;on_touch_down: self.collide_point(*args[1].pos) and\
411::CODE;;root.create_text()
412::CODE;;Image:
413::CODE;;source: 'data/image.png'
414::CODE;;size: self.texture_size
415::CODE;;size_hint: None, None
416::CODE;;on_touch_down: self.collide_point(*args[1].pos) and\
417::CODE;;root.create_image()
418::CODE;;Image:
419::CODE;;source: 'data/video.png'
420::CODE;;size: self.texture_size
421::CODE;;size_hint: None, None
422::CODE;;on_touch_down: self.collide_point(*args[1].pos) and\
423::CODE;;root.create_video()
424::CODE;;We can see that the size and size_hint attribute are exactly the same.
425::CODE;;More than that, the callback in on_touch_down and the image are changing.
426::CODE;;These can be the variable part of the template that we can put into a context.
427::CODE;;Let's try to create a template for the Image:
428::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
429::CODE;;[ToolbarButton@Image]:
431::CODE;;size: self.texture_size
432::CODE;;size_hint: None, None
434::CODE;;source: 'data/%s.png' % ctx.image
435::CODE;;on_touch_down: self.collide_point(*args[1].pos) and ctx.callback()
436::CODE;;The template can be used directly in the MyToolbar rule:
437::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
438::CODE;;<MyToolbar>:
439::CODE;;BoxLayout:
440::CODE;;ToolbarButton:
441::CODE;;image: 'text'
442::CODE;;callback: root.create_text
443::CODE;;ToolbarButton:
444::CODE;;image: 'image'
445::CODE;;callback: root.create_image
446::CODE;;ToolbarButton:
447::CODE;;image: 'video'
448::CODE;;callback: root.create_video
449::CODE;;That's all :)
450::CODE;;Template limitations
451::CODE;;~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
452::CODE;;When you are creating a context:
454::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
455::CODE;;<MyRule>:
456::CODE;;Widget:
457::CODE;;id: mywidget
458::CODE;;value: 'bleh'
459::CODE;;Template:
463::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
464::CODE;;<MyRule>:
465::CODE;;Template:
469::CODE;;Template definitions also replace any similarly named definitions in their
470::CODE;;entirety and thus do not support inheritance.
471::CODE;;.. _redefining-style:
472::CODE;;Redefining a widget's style
473::CODE;;---------------------------
474::CODE;;Sometimes we would like to inherit from a widget in order to use its Python
475::CODE;;properties without also using its .kv defined style. For example, we would
476::CODE;;like to inherit from a Label, but we would also like to define our own
477::CODE;;canvas instructions instead of automatically using the canvas instructions
478::CODE;;inherited from the Label. We can achieve this by prepending a dash (-) before
479::CODE;;the class name in the .kv style definition.
480::CODE;;In myapp.py:
481::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
482::CODE;;class MyWidget(Label):
483::CODE;;pass
484::CODE;;and in my.kv:
485::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
486::CODE;;<-MyWidget>:
487::CODE;;canvas:
488::CODE;;Color:
489::CODE;;rgb: 1, 1, 1
490::CODE;;Rectangle:
491::CODE;;size: (32, 32)
492::CODE;;MyWidget will now have a Color and Rectangle instruction in its canvas
493::CODE;;without any of the instructions inherited from the Label.
494::CODE;;Redefining a widget's property style
495::CODE;;------------------------------------
496::CODE;;Similar to :ref:`redefining style <redefining-style>`, sometimes we
497::CODE;;would like to inherit from a widget, keep all its KV defined styles, except for
498::CODE;;the style applied to a specific property. For example, we would
499::CODE;;like to inherit from a :class:`~kivy.uix.button.Button`, but we would also
500::CODE;;like to set our own `state_image`, rather then relying on the
501::CODE;;`background_normal` and `background_down` values. We can achieve this by
502::CODE;;prepending a dash (-) before the `state_image` property name in the .kv style
503::CODE;;definition.
504::CODE;;In myapp.py:
505::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
506::CODE;;class MyWidget(Button):
507::CODE;;new_background = StringProperty('my_background.png')
508::CODE;;and in my.kv:
509::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
510::CODE;;<MyWidget>:
511::CODE;;-state_image: self.new_background
512::CODE;;MyWidget will now have a `state_image` background set only by `new_background`,
513::CODE;;and not by any previous styles that may have set `state_image`.
514::CODE;;.. note::
515::CODE;;Although the previous rules are cleared, they are still applied during
516::CODE;;widget construction and are only removed when the new rule with the dash
517::CODE;;is reached. This means that initially, previous rules could be used to set
518::CODE;;the property.
519::CODE;;Order of kwargs and KV rule application
520::CODE;;---------------------------------------
521::CODE;;Properties can be initialized in KV as well as in python. For example, in KV:
522::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
523::CODE;;<MyRule@Widget>:
524::CODE;;text: 'Hello'
525::CODE;;ramp: 45.
526::CODE;;order: self.x + 10
527::CODE;;Then `MyRule()` would initialize all three kivy properties to
528::CODE;;the given KV values. Separately in python, if the properties already exist as
529::CODE;;kivy properties one can do for example `MyRule(line='Bye', side=55)`.
530::CODE;;However, what will be the final values of the properties when
531::CODE;;`MyRule(text='Bye', order=55)` is executed? The quick rule is that python
532::CODE;;initialization is stronger than KV initialization only for constant rules.
533::CODE;;Specifically, the `kwargs` provided to the python initializer are always
534::CODE;;applied first. So in the above example, `text` is set to
535::CODE;;`'Bye'` and `order` is set to `55`. Then, all the KV rules are applied, except
536::CODE;;those constant rules that overwrite a python initializer provided value.
537::CODE;;That is, the KV rules that do not creates bindings such as `text: 'Hello'`
538::CODE;;and `ramp: 45.`, if a value for that property has been provided in python, then
539::CODE;;that rule will not be applied.
540::CODE;;So in the `MyRule(text='Bye', order=55)` example, `text` will be `'Bye'`,
541::CODE;;`ramp` will be `45.`, and `order`, which creates a binding, will first be set
542::CODE;;to `55`, but then when KV rules are applied will end up being whatever
543::CODE;;`self.x + 10` is.
544::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.9.1
545::CODE;;Before, KV rules always overwrote the python values, now, python values
546::CODE;;are not overwritten by constant rules.
547::CODE;;Lang Directives
548::CODE;;---------------
549::CODE;;You can use directives to add declarative commands, such as imports or constant
550::CODE;;definitions, to the lang files. Directives are added as comments in the
551::CODE;;following format:
552::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
554::CODE;;import <package>
555::CODE;;~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
556::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.5
557::CODE;;Syntax:
558::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
560::CODE;;You can import a package by writing:
561::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
563::CODE;;<Rule>:
564::CODE;;Button:
565::CODE;;text: os.getcwd()
566::CODE;;Or more complex:
567::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
569::CODE;;<Rule>:
570::CODE;;canvas:
571::CODE;;Color:
572::CODE;;rgba: ut.get_random_color()
573::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.7
574::CODE;;You can directly import classes from a module:
575::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
577::CODE;;<Rule>:
578::CODE;;on_prop: Animation(x=.5).start(self)
579::CODE;;set <key> <expr>
580::CODE;;~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
581::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.6
582::CODE;;Syntax:
583::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
585::CODE;;Set a key that will be available anywhere in the kv. For example:
586::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
589::CODE;;<Rule>:
590::CODE;;state: 'normal'
591::CODE;;canvas:
592::CODE;;Color:
593::CODE;;rgb: my_color if self.pressed else my_color_hl
594::CODE;;include <file>
595::CODE;;~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
596::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.9.0
597::CODE;;Syntax:
598::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
600::CODE;;Includes an external kivy file. This allows you to split complex
601::CODE;;widgets into their own files. If the include is forced, the file
602::CODE;;will first be unloaded and then reloaded again. For example:
603::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
607::CODE;;<Rule>:
608::CODE;;state: 'normal'
609::CODE;;MyButton:
610::CODE;;MyComponent:
611::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
614::CODE;;<MyComponent>:
615::CODE;;MyButton:
616::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
618::CODE;;<MyButton>:
619::CODE;;canvas:
620::CODE;;Color:
621::CODE;;rgb: (1.0, 0.0, 0.0)
622::CODE;;Rectangle:
623::CODE;;pos: self.pos
624::CODE;;size: (self.size[0]/4, self.size[1]/4)
625::CODE;;'''
626::CODE;;from kivy.lang.builder import (Observable, Builder, BuilderBase,
627::CODE;;BuilderException)
628::CODE;;from kivy.lang.parser import Parser, ParserException, global_idmap
629::CODE;;__all__ = ('Observable', 'Builder', 'BuilderBase', 'BuilderException',
630::CODE;;'Parser', 'ParserException', 'global_idmap')
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Builder
3::CODE;;======
4::CODE;;Class used for the registering and application of rules for specific widgets.
5::CODE;;'''
6::CODE;;import sys
7::CODE;;from os import environ
8::CODE;;from os.path import join
9::CODE;;from copy import copy
10::CODE;;from types import CodeType
11::CODE;;from functools import partial
12::CODE;;from kivy.factory import Factory
13::CODE;;from kivy.lang.parser import (
14::CODE;;Parser,
15::CODE;;ParserException,
16::CODE;;_handlers,
17::CODE;;global_idmap,
18::CODE;;ParserRuleProperty,
19::CODE;;)
20::CODE;;from kivy.logger import Logger
21::CODE;;from kivy.utils import QueryDict
22::CODE;;from kivy.cache import Cache
23::CODE;;from kivy import kivy_data_dir
24::CODE;;from kivy.context import register_context
25::CODE;;from kivy.resources import resource_find
26::CODE;;from kivy._event import Observable, EventDispatcher
27::CODE;;__all__ = ('Observable', 'Builder', 'BuilderBase', 'BuilderException')
28::CODE;;trace = Logger.trace
30::CODE;;Instruction = None
35::CODE;;_delayed_start = None
36::CODE;;class BuilderException(ParserException):
37::CODE;;'''Exception raised when the Builder fails to apply a rule on a widget.
38::CODE;;'''
39::CODE;;pass
40::CODE;;def get_proxy(widget):
41::CODE;;try:
42::CODE;;return widget.proxy_ref
43::CODE;;except AttributeError:
44::CODE;;return widget
45::CODE;;def custom_callback(__kvlang__, idmap, *largs, **kwargs):
46::CODE;;idmap['args'] = largs
47::CODE;;exec(__kvlang__.co_value, idmap)
48::CODE;;def call_fn(args, instance, v):
49::CODE;;element, key, value, rule, idmap = args
50::CODE;;if __debug__:
51::CODE;;trace('Lang: call_fn %s, key=%s, value=%r, %r' % (
52::CODE;;element, key, value, rule.value))
53::CODE;;rule.count += 1
54::CODE;;e_value = eval(value, idmap)
55::CODE;;if __debug__:
56::CODE;;trace('Lang: call_fn => value=%r' % (e_value, ))
57::CODE;;setattr(element, key, e_value)
58::CODE;;def delayed_call_fn(args, instance, v):
60::CODE;;if args[-1] is not None:
61::CODE;;return
62::CODE;;global _delayed_start
63::CODE;;if _delayed_start is None:
64::CODE;;_delayed_start = args
65::CODE;;args[-1] = StopIteration
66::CODE;;else:
67::CODE;;args[-1] = _delayed_start
68::CODE;;_delayed_start = args
69::CODE;;def update_intermediates(base, keys, bound, s, fn, args, instance, value):
70::CODE;;''' Function that is called when an intermediate property is updated
71::CODE;;and `rebind` of that property is True. In that case, we unbind
72::CODE;;all bound funcs that were bound to attrs of the old value of the
73::CODE;;property and rebind them to the new value of the property.
74::CODE;;For example, if the rule is `self.a.b.c.d`, then when b is changed, we
75::CODE;;unbind from `b`, `c` and `d`, if they were bound before (they were not
76::CODE;;None and `rebind` of the respective properties was True) and we rebind
77::CODE;;to the new values of the attrs `b`, `c``, `d` that are not None and
78::CODE;;`rebind` is True.
79::CODE;;:Parameters:
80::CODE;;`base`
81::CODE;;A (proxied) ref to the base widget, `self` in the example
82::CODE;;above.
83::CODE;;`keys`
84::CODE;;A list of the name off the attrs of `base` being watched. In
85::CODE;;the example above it'd be `['a', 'b', 'c', 'd']`.
86::CODE;;`bound`
87::CODE;;A list 4-tuples, each tuple being (widget, attr, callback, uid)
88::CODE;;representing callback functions bound to the attributed `attr`
89::CODE;;of `widget`. `uid` is returned by `fbind` when binding.
90::CODE;;The callback may be None, in which case the attr
91::CODE;;was not bound, but is there to be able to walk the attr tree.
92::CODE;;E.g. in the example above, if `b` was not an eventdispatcher,
93::CODE;;`(_b_ref_, `c`, None)` would be added to the list so we can get
94::CODE;;to `c` and `d`, which may be eventdispatchers and their attrs.
95::CODE;;`s`
96::CODE;;The index in `keys` of the of the attr that needs to be
97::CODE;;updated. That is all the keys from `s` and further will be
98::CODE;;rebound, since the `s` key was changed. In bound, the
99::CODE;;corresponding index is `s - 1`. If `s` is None, we start from
100::CODE;;1 (first attr).
101::CODE;;`fn`
102::CODE;;The function to be called args, `args` on bound callback.
103::CODE;;'''
105::CODE;;for f, k, fun, uid in bound[s:]:
106::CODE;;if fun is None:
107::CODE;;continue
108::CODE;;try:
109::CODE;;f.unbind_uid(k, uid)
110::CODE;;except ReferenceError:
111::CODE;;pass
112::CODE;;del bound[s:]
114::CODE;;f = getattr(*bound[-1][:2])
115::CODE;;if f is None:
116::CODE;;fn(args, None, None)
117::CODE;;return
118::CODE;;s += 1
119::CODE;;append = bound.append
121::CODE;;for val in keys[s:-1]:
124::CODE;;if isinstance(f, (EventDispatcher, Observable)):
125::CODE;;prop = f.property(val, True)
126::CODE;;if prop is not None and getattr(prop, 'rebind', False):
130::CODE;;uid = f.fbind(
131::CODE;;val, update_intermediates, base, keys, bound, s, fn, args)
132::CODE;;append([f.proxy_ref, val, update_intermediates, uid])
133::CODE;;else:
134::CODE;;append([f.proxy_ref, val, None, None])
135::CODE;;else:
136::CODE;;append([getattr(f, 'proxy_ref', f), val, None, None])
137::CODE;;f = getattr(f, val, None)
138::CODE;;if f is None:
139::CODE;;break
140::CODE;;s += 1
143::CODE;;if isinstance(f, (EventDispatcher, Observable)):
144::CODE;;uid = f.fbind(keys[-1], fn, args)
145::CODE;;if uid:
146::CODE;;append([f.proxy_ref, keys[-1], fn, uid])
151::CODE;;fn(args, None, None)
152::CODE;;def create_handler(iself, element, key, value, rule, idmap, delayed=False):
153::CODE;;idmap = copy(idmap)
154::CODE;;idmap.update(global_idmap)
155::CODE;;idmap['self'] = iself.proxy_ref
156::CODE;;bound_list = _handlers[iself.uid][key]
157::CODE;;handler_append = bound_list.append
160::CODE;;if delayed:
161::CODE;;fn = delayed_call_fn
163::CODE;;else:
164::CODE;;fn = call_fn
165::CODE;;args = (element, key, value, rule, idmap)
167::CODE;;if rule.watched_keys is not None:
168::CODE;;for keys in rule.watched_keys:
169::CODE;;base = idmap.get(keys[0])
170::CODE;;if base is None:
171::CODE;;continue
172::CODE;;f = base = getattr(base, 'proxy_ref', base)
173::CODE;;bound = []
174::CODE;;was_bound = False
175::CODE;;append = bound.append
177::CODE;;k = 1
178::CODE;;for val in keys[1:-1]:
181::CODE;;if isinstance(f, (EventDispatcher, Observable)):
182::CODE;;prop = f.property(val, True)
183::CODE;;if prop is not None and getattr(prop, 'rebind', False):
187::CODE;;uid = f.fbind(
188::CODE;;val, update_intermediates, base, keys, bound, k,
189::CODE;;fn, args)
190::CODE;;append([f.proxy_ref, val, update_intermediates, uid])
191::CODE;;was_bound = True
192::CODE;;else:
193::CODE;;append([f.proxy_ref, val, None, None])
194::CODE;;elif not isinstance(f, type):
195::CODE;;append([getattr(f, 'proxy_ref', f), val, None, None])
196::CODE;;else:
197::CODE;;append([f, val, None, None])
198::CODE;;f = getattr(f, val, None)
199::CODE;;if f is None:
200::CODE;;break
201::CODE;;k += 1
204::CODE;;if isinstance(f, (EventDispatcher, Observable)):
206::CODE;;if uid:
207::CODE;;append([f.proxy_ref, keys[-1], fn, uid])
208::CODE;;was_bound = True
209::CODE;;if was_bound:
210::CODE;;handler_append(bound)
211::CODE;;try:
212::CODE;;return eval(value, idmap), bound_list
213::CODE;;except Exception as e:
214::CODE;;tb = sys.exc_info()[2]
215::CODE;;raise BuilderException(rule.ctx, rule.line,
216::CODE;;'{}: {}'.format(e.__class__.__name__, e),
217::CODE;;cause=tb)
218::CODE;;class BuilderBase(object):
219::CODE;;'''The Builder is responsible for creating a :class:`Parser` for parsing a
220::CODE;;kv file, merging the results into its internal rules, templates, etc.
221::CODE;;By default, :class:`Builder` is a global Kivy instance used in widgets
222::CODE;;that you can use to load other kv files in addition to the default ones.
223::CODE;;See :mod:`kivy.lang` for details about the rules built here.
224::CODE;;:attributes:
225::CODE;;`files`: list
226::CODE;;Filenames of Kivy-language code that have already been loaded.
227::CODE;;Not necessarily real files on disk; see :meth:`load_string`.
228::CODE;;`dynamic_classes`: dict
229::CODE;;Classes crated in Kivy-language code.
230::CODE;;They were created with the ``<Class@Superclass>:`` syntax,
231::CODE;;rather than in Python.
232::CODE;;`templates`: dict
233::CODE;;Superseded by :attr:`dynamic_classes` in version 1.0.5.
234::CODE;;Modern Kivy apps should not use templates.
235::CODE;;`rules`: list
236::CODE;;Rules loaded from Kivy-language code.
237::CODE;;`rulectx`: dict
238::CODE;;Context used by each rule.
239::CODE;;Mostly, the IDs of widgets.
240::CODE;;'''
241::CODE;;def __init__(self):
242::CODE;;super(BuilderBase, self).__init__()
243::CODE;;self._match_cache = {}
244::CODE;;self._match_name_cache = {}
245::CODE;;self.files = []
246::CODE;;self.dynamic_classes = {}
247::CODE;;self.templates = {}
248::CODE;;self.rules = []
249::CODE;;self.rulectx = {}
250::CODE;;@classmethod
251::CODE;;def create_from(cls, builder):
257::CODE;;obj = cls()
258::CODE;;obj._match_cache = copy(builder._match_cache)
259::CODE;;obj._match_name_cache = copy(builder._match_name_cache)
260::CODE;;obj.files = copy(builder.files)
261::CODE;;obj.dynamic_classes = copy(builder.dynamic_classes)
262::CODE;;obj.templates = copy(builder.templates)
263::CODE;;obj.rules = list(builder.rules)
264::CODE;;assert not builder.rulectx
265::CODE;;obj.rulectx = dict(builder.rulectx)
266::CODE;;return obj
267::CODE;;def load_file(self, filename, encoding='utf8', **kwargs):
268::CODE;;'''Insert a file into the language builder and return the root widget
269::CODE;;(if defined) of the kv file.
270::CODE;;:parameters:
271::CODE;;`rulesonly`: bool, defaults to False
272::CODE;;If True, the Builder will raise an exception if you have a root
273::CODE;;widget inside the definition.
274::CODE;;`encoding`: File character encoding. Defaults to utf-8,
275::CODE;;'''
276::CODE;;filename = resource_find(filename) or filename
277::CODE;;if __debug__:
278::CODE;;trace('Lang: load file %s, using %s encoding', filename, encoding)
279::CODE;;kwargs['filename'] = filename
280::CODE;;with open(filename, 'r', encoding=encoding) as fd:
281::CODE;;data = fd.read()
282::CODE;;return self.load_string(data, **kwargs)
283::CODE;;def unload_file(self, filename):
284::CODE;;'''Unload all rules associated with a previously imported file.
285::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.8
286::CODE;;.. warning::
287::CODE;;This will not remove rules or templates already applied/used on
288::CODE;;current widgets. It will only effect the next widgets creation or
289::CODE;;template invocation.
290::CODE;;'''
292::CODE;;filename = resource_find(filename) or filename
293::CODE;;self.rules = [x for x in self.rules if x[1].ctx.filename != filename]
294::CODE;;self._clear_matchcache()
295::CODE;;templates = {}
296::CODE;;for x, y in self.templates.items():
297::CODE;;if y[2] != filename:
298::CODE;;templates[x] = y
299::CODE;;self.templates = templates
300::CODE;;if filename in self.files:
301::CODE;;self.files.remove(filename)
303::CODE;;Factory.unregister_from_filename(filename)
304::CODE;;def load_string(self, string, **kwargs):
305::CODE;;'''Insert a string into the Language Builder and return the root widget
306::CODE;;(if defined) of the kv string.
307::CODE;;:Parameters:
308::CODE;;`rulesonly`: bool, defaults to False
309::CODE;;If True, the Builder will raise an exception if you have a root
310::CODE;;widget inside the definition.
311::CODE;;`filename`: str, defaults to None
312::CODE;;If specified, the filename used to index the kv rules.
313::CODE;;The filename parameter can be used to unload kv strings in the same way
314::CODE;;as you unload kv files. This can be achieved using pseudo file names
315::CODE;;e.g.::
321::CODE;;can be unloaded via::
322::CODE;;Build.unload_file("myrule.kv")
323::CODE;;'''
324::CODE;;kwargs.setdefault('rulesonly', False)
325::CODE;;self._current_filename = fn = kwargs.get('filename', None)
327::CODE;;if fn in self.files:
328::CODE;;Logger.warning(
329::CODE;;'Lang: The file {} is loaded multiples times, '
330::CODE;;'you might have unwanted behaviors.'.format(fn))
331::CODE;;try:
333::CODE;;parser = Parser(content=string, filename=fn)
335::CODE;;self.rules.extend(parser.rules)
336::CODE;;self._clear_matchcache()
338::CODE;;for name, cls, template in parser.templates:
339::CODE;;self.templates[name] = (cls, template, fn)
340::CODE;;Factory.register(name,
341::CODE;;cls=partial(self.template, name),
342::CODE;;is_template=True, warn=True)
344::CODE;;for name, baseclasses in parser.dynamic_classes.items():
345::CODE;;Factory.register(name, baseclasses=baseclasses, filename=fn,
346::CODE;;warn=True)
348::CODE;;if kwargs['rulesonly'] and parser.root:
349::CODE;;filename = kwargs.get('rulesonly', '<string>')
350::CODE;;raise Exception('The file <%s> contain also non-rules '
351::CODE;;'directives' % filename)
354::CODE;;if fn and (parser.templates or
355::CODE;;parser.dynamic_classes or parser.rules):
356::CODE;;self.files.append(fn)
357::CODE;;if parser.root:
358::CODE;;widget = Factory.get(parser.root.name)(__no_builder=True)
359::CODE;;rule_children = []
360::CODE;;widget.apply_class_lang_rules(
361::CODE;;root=widget, rule_children=rule_children)
362::CODE;;self._apply_rule(
363::CODE;;widget, parser.root, parser.root,
364::CODE;;rule_children=rule_children)
365::CODE;;for child in rule_children:
366::CODE;;child.dispatch('on_kv_post', widget)
367::CODE;;widget.dispatch('on_kv_post', widget)
368::CODE;;return widget
369::CODE;;finally:
370::CODE;;self._current_filename = None
371::CODE;;def template(self, *args, **ctx):
372::CODE;;'''Create a specialized template using a specific context.
373::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.5
374::CODE;;With templates, you can construct custom widgets from a kv lang
375::CODE;;definition by giving them a context. Check :ref:`Template usage
376::CODE;;<template_usage>`.
377::CODE;;'''
380::CODE;;name = args[0]
381::CODE;;if name not in self.templates:
382::CODE;;raise Exception('Unknown <%s> template name' % name)
383::CODE;;baseclasses, rule, fn = self.templates[name]
384::CODE;;key = '%s|%s' % (name, baseclasses)
385::CODE;;cls = Cache.get('kv.lang', key)
386::CODE;;if cls is None:
387::CODE;;rootwidgets = []
388::CODE;;for basecls in baseclasses.split('+'):
389::CODE;;rootwidgets.append(Factory.get(basecls))
390::CODE;;cls = type(name, tuple(rootwidgets), {})
391::CODE;;Cache.append('kv.lang', key, cls)
392::CODE;;widget = cls()
396::CODE;;proxy_ctx = {k: get_proxy(v) for k, v in ctx.items()}
397::CODE;;self._apply_rule(widget, rule, rule, template_ctx=proxy_ctx)
398::CODE;;return widget
399::CODE;;def apply_rules(
400::CODE;;self, widget, rule_name, ignored_consts=set(), rule_children=None,
401::CODE;;dispatch_kv_post=False):
402::CODE;;'''Search all the rules that match the name `rule_name`
403::CODE;;and apply them to `widget`.
404::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.10.0
405::CODE;;:Parameters:
406::CODE;;`widget`: :class:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget`
407::CODE;;The widget to whom the matching rules should be applied to.
408::CODE;;`ignored_consts`: set
409::CODE;;A set or list type whose elements are property names for which
410::CODE;;constant KV rules (i.e. those that don't create bindings) of
411::CODE;;that widget will not be applied. This allows e.g. skipping
412::CODE;;constant rules that overwrite a value initialized in python.
413::CODE;;`rule_children`: list
414::CODE;;If not ``None``, it should be a list that will be populated
415::CODE;;with all the widgets created by the kv rules being applied.
416::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.11.0
417::CODE;;`dispatch_kv_post`: bool
418::CODE;;Normally the class `Widget` dispatches the `on_kv_post` event
419::CODE;;to widgets created during kv rule application.
420::CODE;;But if the rules are manually applied by calling :meth:`apply`,
421::CODE;;that may not happen, so if this is `True`, we will dispatch the
422::CODE;;`on_kv_post` event where needed after applying the rules to
423::CODE;;`widget` (we won't dispatch it for `widget` itself).
424::CODE;;Defaults to False.
425::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.11.0
426::CODE;;'''
427::CODE;;rules = self.match_rule_name(rule_name)
428::CODE;;if __debug__:
429::CODE;;trace('Lang: Found %d rules for %s' % (len(rules), rule_name))
430::CODE;;if not rules:
431::CODE;;return
432::CODE;;if dispatch_kv_post:
433::CODE;;rule_children = rule_children if rule_children is not None else []
434::CODE;;for rule in rules:
435::CODE;;self._apply_rule(
436::CODE;;widget, rule, rule, ignored_consts=ignored_consts,
437::CODE;;rule_children=rule_children)
438::CODE;;if dispatch_kv_post:
439::CODE;;for w in rule_children:
440::CODE;;w.dispatch('on_kv_post', widget)
441::CODE;;def apply(self, widget, ignored_consts=set(), rule_children=None,
442::CODE;;dispatch_kv_post=False):
443::CODE;;'''Search all the rules that match the widget and apply them.
444::CODE;;:Parameters:
445::CODE;;`widget`: :class:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget`
446::CODE;;The widget whose class rules should be applied to this widget.
447::CODE;;`ignored_consts`: set
448::CODE;;A set or list type whose elements are property names for which
449::CODE;;constant KV rules (i.e. those that don't create bindings) of
450::CODE;;that widget will not be applied. This allows e.g. skipping
451::CODE;;constant rules that overwrite a value initialized in python.
452::CODE;;`rule_children`: list
453::CODE;;If not ``None``, it should be a list that will be populated
454::CODE;;with all the widgets created by the kv rules being applied.
455::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.11.0
456::CODE;;`dispatch_kv_post`: bool
457::CODE;;Normally the class `Widget` dispatches the `on_kv_post` event
458::CODE;;to widgets created during kv rule application.
459::CODE;;But if the rules are manually applied by calling :meth:`apply`,
460::CODE;;that may not happen, so if this is `True`, we will dispatch the
461::CODE;;`on_kv_post` event where needed after applying the rules to
462::CODE;;`widget` (we won't dispatch it for `widget` itself).
463::CODE;;Defaults to False.
464::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.11.0
465::CODE;;'''
466::CODE;;rules = self.match(widget)
467::CODE;;if __debug__:
468::CODE;;trace('Lang: Found %d rules for %s' % (len(rules), widget))
469::CODE;;if not rules:
470::CODE;;return
471::CODE;;if dispatch_kv_post:
472::CODE;;rule_children = rule_children if rule_children is not None else []
473::CODE;;for rule in rules:
474::CODE;;self._apply_rule(
475::CODE;;widget, rule, rule, ignored_consts=ignored_consts,
476::CODE;;rule_children=rule_children)
477::CODE;;if dispatch_kv_post:
478::CODE;;for w in rule_children:
479::CODE;;w.dispatch('on_kv_post', widget)
480::CODE;;def _clear_matchcache(self):
481::CODE;;self._match_cache.clear()
482::CODE;;self._match_name_cache.clear()
483::CODE;;def _apply_rule(self, widget, rule, rootrule, template_ctx=None,
484::CODE;;ignored_consts=set(), rule_children=None):
489::CODE;;assert rule not in self.rulectx
490::CODE;;self.rulectx[rule] = rctx = {
491::CODE;;'ids': {'root': widget.proxy_ref},
492::CODE;;'set': [], 'hdl': []}
494::CODE;;assert rootrule in self.rulectx
495::CODE;;rctx = self.rulectx[rootrule]
497::CODE;;if template_ctx is not None:
498::CODE;;rctx['ids']['ctx'] = QueryDict(template_ctx)
500::CODE;;if rule.id:
503::CODE;;rctx['ids'][rule.id] = widget.proxy_ref
506::CODE;;_ids = dict(rctx['ids'])
507::CODE;;_root = _ids.pop('root')
508::CODE;;_new_ids = _root.ids
509::CODE;;for _key, _value in _ids.items():
510::CODE;;if _value == _root:
512::CODE;;continue
513::CODE;;_new_ids[_key] = _value
514::CODE;;_root.ids = _new_ids
517::CODE;;rule.create_missing(widget)
519::CODE;;if rule.canvas_before:
520::CODE;;with widget.canvas.before:
521::CODE;;self._build_canvas(widget.canvas.before, widget,
522::CODE;;rule.canvas_before, rootrule)
523::CODE;;if rule.canvas_root:
524::CODE;;with widget.canvas:
525::CODE;;self._build_canvas(widget.canvas, widget,
526::CODE;;rule.canvas_root, rootrule)
527::CODE;;if rule.canvas_after:
528::CODE;;with widget.canvas.after:
529::CODE;;self._build_canvas(widget.canvas.after, widget,
530::CODE;;rule.canvas_after, rootrule)
532::CODE;;Factory_get = Factory.get
533::CODE;;Factory_is_template = Factory.is_template
534::CODE;;for crule in rule.children:
535::CODE;;cname = crule.name
536::CODE;;if cname in ('canvas', 'canvas.before', 'canvas.after'):
537::CODE;;raise ParserException(
538::CODE;;crule.ctx, crule.line,
539::CODE;;'Canvas instructions added in kv must '
540::CODE;;'be declared before child widgets.')
543::CODE;;cls = Factory_get(cname)
544::CODE;;if Factory_is_template(cname):
547::CODE;;ctx = {}
548::CODE;;idmap = copy(global_idmap)
549::CODE;;idmap.update({'root': rctx['ids']['root']})
550::CODE;;if 'ctx' in rctx['ids']:
551::CODE;;idmap.update({'ctx': rctx['ids']['ctx']})
552::CODE;;try:
553::CODE;;for prule in crule.properties.values():
554::CODE;;value = prule.co_value
555::CODE;;if type(value) is CodeType:
556::CODE;;value = eval(value, idmap)
557::CODE;;ctx[prule.name] = value
558::CODE;;for prule in crule.handlers:
559::CODE;;value = eval(prule.value, idmap)
560::CODE;;ctx[prule.name] = value
561::CODE;;except Exception as e:
562::CODE;;tb = sys.exc_info()[2]
563::CODE;;raise BuilderException(
564::CODE;;prule.ctx, prule.line,
565::CODE;;'{}: {}'.format(e.__class__.__name__, e), cause=tb)
567::CODE;;child = cls(**ctx)
568::CODE;;widget.add_widget(child)
570::CODE;;if crule.id:
571::CODE;;rctx['ids'][crule.id] = child
572::CODE;;else:
577::CODE;;child = cls(__no_builder=True)
578::CODE;;widget.add_widget(child)
579::CODE;;child.apply_class_lang_rules(
580::CODE;;root=rctx['ids']['root'], rule_children=rule_children)
581::CODE;;self._apply_rule(
582::CODE;;child, crule, rootrule, rule_children=rule_children)
583::CODE;;if rule_children is not None:
584::CODE;;rule_children.append(child)
586::CODE;;if rule.properties:
587::CODE;;rctx['set'].append((widget.proxy_ref,
588::CODE;;list(rule.properties.values())))
589::CODE;;for key, crule in rule.properties.items():
591::CODE;;if crule.ignore_prev:
592::CODE;;Builder.unbind_property(widget, key)
593::CODE;;if rule.handlers:
594::CODE;;rctx['hdl'].append((widget.proxy_ref, rule.handlers))
597::CODE;;if rootrule is not rule:
598::CODE;;del self.rulectx[rule]
599::CODE;;return
601::CODE;;try:
602::CODE;;rule = None
603::CODE;;for widget_set, rules in reversed(rctx['set']):
604::CODE;;for rule in rules:
605::CODE;;assert isinstance(rule, ParserRuleProperty)
606::CODE;;key = rule.name
607::CODE;;value = rule.co_value
608::CODE;;if type(value) is CodeType:
609::CODE;;value, bound = create_handler(
610::CODE;;widget_set, widget_set, key, value, rule,
611::CODE;;rctx['ids'])
613::CODE;;if (widget_set != widget or bound or
614::CODE;;key not in ignored_consts):
615::CODE;;setattr(widget_set, key, value)
616::CODE;;else:
617::CODE;;if (widget_set != widget or
618::CODE;;key not in ignored_consts):
619::CODE;;setattr(widget_set, key, value)
620::CODE;;except Exception as e:
621::CODE;;if rule is not None:
622::CODE;;tb = sys.exc_info()[2]
623::CODE;;raise BuilderException(rule.ctx, rule.line,
624::CODE;;'{}: {}'.format(e.__class__.__name__,
625::CODE;;e), cause=tb)
626::CODE;;raise e
628::CODE;;try:
629::CODE;;crule = None
630::CODE;;for widget_set, rules in rctx['hdl']:
631::CODE;;for crule in rules:
632::CODE;;assert isinstance(crule, ParserRuleProperty)
633::CODE;;assert crule.name.startswith('on_')
634::CODE;;key = crule.name
635::CODE;;if not widget_set.is_event_type(key):
636::CODE;;key = key[3:]
637::CODE;;idmap = copy(global_idmap)
638::CODE;;idmap.update(rctx['ids'])
639::CODE;;idmap['self'] = widget_set.proxy_ref
640::CODE;;if not widget_set.fbind(key, custom_callback, crule,
641::CODE;;idmap):
642::CODE;;raise AttributeError(key)
644::CODE;;if crule.name == 'on_parent':
645::CODE;;Factory.Widget.parent.dispatch(widget_set.__self__)
646::CODE;;except Exception as e:
647::CODE;;if crule is not None:
648::CODE;;tb = sys.exc_info()[2]
649::CODE;;raise BuilderException(
650::CODE;;crule.ctx, crule.line,
651::CODE;;'{}: {}'.format(e.__class__.__name__, e), cause=tb)
652::CODE;;raise e
654::CODE;;del self.rulectx[rootrule]
655::CODE;;def match(self, widget):
656::CODE;;'''Return a list of :class:`ParserRule` objects matching the widget.
657::CODE;;'''
658::CODE;;cache = self._match_cache
659::CODE;;k = (widget.__class__, tuple(widget.cls))
660::CODE;;if k in cache:
661::CODE;;return cache[k]
662::CODE;;rules = []
663::CODE;;for selector, rule in self.rules:
664::CODE;;if selector.match(widget):
665::CODE;;if rule.avoid_previous_rules:
666::CODE;;del rules[:]
667::CODE;;rules.append(rule)
668::CODE;;cache[k] = rules
669::CODE;;return rules
670::CODE;;def match_rule_name(self, rule_name):
671::CODE;;'''Return a list of :class:`ParserRule` objects matching the widget.
672::CODE;;'''
673::CODE;;cache = self._match_name_cache
674::CODE;;rule_name = str(rule_name)
675::CODE;;k = rule_name.lower()
676::CODE;;if k in cache:
677::CODE;;return cache[k]
678::CODE;;rules = []
679::CODE;;for selector, rule in self.rules:
680::CODE;;if selector.match_rule_name(rule_name):
681::CODE;;if rule.avoid_previous_rules:
682::CODE;;del rules[:]
683::CODE;;rules.append(rule)
684::CODE;;cache[k] = rules
685::CODE;;return rules
686::CODE;;def sync(self):
687::CODE;;'''Execute all the waiting operations, such as the execution of all the
688::CODE;;expressions related to the canvas.
689::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.7.0
690::CODE;;'''
691::CODE;;global _delayed_start
692::CODE;;next_args = _delayed_start
693::CODE;;if next_args is None:
694::CODE;;return
695::CODE;;while next_args is not StopIteration:
698::CODE;;try:
699::CODE;;call_fn(next_args[:-1], None, None)
700::CODE;;except ReferenceError:
701::CODE;;pass
702::CODE;;args = next_args

704::CODE;;args[-1] = None
705::CODE;;_delayed_start = None
706::CODE;;def unbind_widget(self, uid):
707::CODE;;'''Unbind all the handlers created by the KV rules of the
708::CODE;;widget. The :attr:`kivy.uix.widget.Widget.uid` is passed here
709::CODE;;instead of the widget itself, because Builder is using it in the
710::CODE;;widget destructor.
711::CODE;;This effectively clears all the KV rules associated with this widget.
712::CODE;;For example:
713::CODE;;.. code-block:: python-console
714::CODE;;>>> w = Builder.load_string(\'''
715::CODE;;... Widget:
716::CODE;;... height: self.width / 2. if self.disabled else self.width
717::CODE;;... x: self.y + 50
718::CODE;;... \''')
719::CODE;;>>> w.size
720::CODE;;[100, 100]
721::CODE;;>>> w.pos
722::CODE;;[50, 0]
723::CODE;;>>> w.width = 500
724::CODE;;>>> w.size
725::CODE;;[500, 500]
726::CODE;;>>> Builder.unbind_widget(w.uid)
727::CODE;;>>> w.width = 222
728::CODE;;>>> w.y = 500
729::CODE;;>>> w.size
730::CODE;;[222, 500]
731::CODE;;>>> w.pos
732::CODE;;[50, 500]
733::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.7.2
734::CODE;;'''
735::CODE;;if uid not in _handlers:
736::CODE;;return
737::CODE;;for prop_callbacks in _handlers[uid].values():
738::CODE;;for callbacks in prop_callbacks:
739::CODE;;for f, k, fn, bound_uid in callbacks:
741::CODE;;continue
742::CODE;;try:
743::CODE;;f.unbind_uid(k, bound_uid)
744::CODE;;except ReferenceError:
746::CODE;;pass
747::CODE;;del _handlers[uid]
748::CODE;;def unbind_property(self, widget, name):
749::CODE;;'''Unbind the handlers created by all the rules of the widget that set
750::CODE;;the name.
751::CODE;;This effectively clears all the rules of widget that take the form::
752::CODE;;name: rule
753::CODE;;For example:
754::CODE;;.. code-block:: python-console
755::CODE;;>>> w = Builder.load_string(\'''
756::CODE;;... Widget:
757::CODE;;... height: self.width / 2. if self.disabled else self.width
758::CODE;;... x: self.y + 50
759::CODE;;... \''')
760::CODE;;>>> w.size
761::CODE;;[100, 100]
762::CODE;;>>> w.pos
763::CODE;;[50, 0]
764::CODE;;>>> w.width = 500
765::CODE;;>>> w.size
766::CODE;;[500, 500]
767::CODE;;>>> Builder.unbind_property(w, 'height')
768::CODE;;>>> w.width = 222
769::CODE;;>>> w.size
770::CODE;;[222, 500]
771::CODE;;>>> w.y = 500
772::CODE;;>>> w.pos
773::CODE;;[550, 500]
774::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.9.1
775::CODE;;'''
776::CODE;;uid = widget.uid
777::CODE;;if uid not in _handlers:
778::CODE;;return
779::CODE;;prop_handlers = _handlers[uid]
780::CODE;;if name not in prop_handlers:
781::CODE;;return
782::CODE;;for callbacks in prop_handlers[name]:
783::CODE;;for f, k, fn, bound_uid in callbacks:
785::CODE;;continue
786::CODE;;try:
787::CODE;;f.unbind_uid(k, bound_uid)
788::CODE;;except ReferenceError:
790::CODE;;pass
791::CODE;;del prop_handlers[name]
792::CODE;;if not prop_handlers:
793::CODE;;del _handlers[uid]

383::CODE;;class Parser(object):
384::CODE;;'''Create a Parser object to parse a Kivy language file or Kivy content.
385::CODE;;'''

389::CODE;;list(range(ord('A'), ord('Z') + 1)) +

407::CODE;;def execute_directives(self):

414::CODE;;version = cmd[5:].strip()

416::CODE;;version += '.0'
417::CODE;;require(version)

419::CODE;;try:

426::CODE;;except:

429::CODE;;global_idmap[name] = value

431::CODE;;ref = cmd[8:].strip()

434::CODE;;ref = ref[6:].strip()
435::CODE;;force_load = True
437::CODE;;if ref[0] == ref[-1] and ref[0] in ('"', "'"):
438::CODE;;c = ref[:3].count(ref[0])
439::CODE;;ref = ref[c:-c] if c != 2 else ref
440::CODE;;if ref[-3:] != '.kv':

442::CODE;;'Language extension (.kv)'.format(ref))
443::CODE;;break
444::CODE;;if ref in __KV_INCLUDES__:
445::CODE;;if not os.path.isfile(resource_find(ref) or ref):
446::CODE;;raise ParserException(self, ln,

448::CODE;;.format(ref))

451::CODE;;.format(ref))

455::CODE;;'because include was forced.'

458::CODE;;kivy.lang.builder.Builder.load_file(ref)
459::CODE;;continue

461::CODE;;__KV_INCLUDES__.append(ref)
462::CODE;;kivy.lang.builder.Builder.load_file(ref)
463::CODE;;elif cmd[:7] == 'import ':

516::CODE;;def strip_comments(self, lines):
517::CODE;;'''Remove all comments from all lines in-place.
518::CODE;;Comments need to be on a single line and not at the end of a line.
520::CODE;;'''
522::CODE;;for ln, line in lines[:]:
