525::CODE;;self.directives.append((ln, stripped[2:]))
527::CODE;;lines.remove((ln, line))
528::CODE;;if not stripped:
529::CODE;;lines.remove((ln, line))
530::CODE;;def parse_level(self, level, lines, spaces=0):
531::CODE;;'''Parse the current level (level * spaces) indentation.
532::CODE;;'''
533::CODE;;indent = spaces * level if spaces > 0 else 0
534::CODE;;objects = []
535::CODE;;current_object = None
536::CODE;;current_property = None
537::CODE;;current_propobject = None
538::CODE;;i = 0
539::CODE;;while i < len(lines):
540::CODE;;line = lines[i]
541::CODE;;ln, content = line
543::CODE;;tmp = content.lstrip(' \t')
545::CODE;;tmp = content[:len(content) - len(tmp)]
546::CODE;;tmp = tmp.replace('\t', ' ')
548::CODE;;if spaces == 0:
549::CODE;;spaces = len(tmp)
550::CODE;;count = len(tmp)
551::CODE;;if spaces > 0 and count % spaces != 0:
552::CODE;;raise ParserException(self, ln,
553::CODE;;'Invalid indentation, '
554::CODE;;'must be a multiple of '
555::CODE;;'%s spaces' % spaces)
556::CODE;;content = content.strip()
557::CODE;;rlevel = count // spaces if spaces > 0 else 0
559::CODE;;if count < indent:
560::CODE;;return objects, lines[i - 1:]
562::CODE;;elif count == indent:
563::CODE;;x = content.split(':', 1)
564::CODE;;if not x[0]:
565::CODE;;raise ParserException(self, ln, 'Identifier missing')
566::CODE;;if (len(x) == 2 and len(x[1]) and
568::CODE;;raise ParserException(self, ln,
569::CODE;;'Invalid data after declaration')
570::CODE;;name = x[0].rstrip()
573::CODE;;if count != 0:
574::CODE;;if False in [ord(z) in Parser.PROP_RANGE for z in name]:
575::CODE;;raise ParserException(self, ln, 'Invalid class name')
576::CODE;;current_object = ParserRule(self, ln, name, rlevel)
577::CODE;;current_property = None
578::CODE;;objects.append(current_object)
580::CODE;;elif count == indent + spaces:
581::CODE;;x = content.split(':', 1)
582::CODE;;if not x[0]:
583::CODE;;raise ParserException(self, ln, 'Identifier missing')
585::CODE;;current_property = None
586::CODE;;name = x[0].rstrip()
587::CODE;;ignore_prev = name[0] == '-'
588::CODE;;if ignore_prev:
589::CODE;;name = name[1:]
590::CODE;;if ord(name[0]) in Parser.CLASS_RANGE:
591::CODE;;if ignore_prev:
592::CODE;;raise ParserException(
593::CODE;;self, ln, 'clear previous, `-`, not allowed here')
594::CODE;;_objects, _lines = self.parse_level(
595::CODE;;level + 1, lines[i:], spaces)
596::CODE;;if current_object is None:
597::CODE;;raise ParserException(self, ln, 'Invalid indentation')
598::CODE;;current_object.children = _objects
599::CODE;;lines = _lines
600::CODE;;i = 0
602::CODE;;else:
603::CODE;;if name not in Parser.PROP_ALLOWED:
604::CODE;;if not all(ord(z) in Parser.PROP_RANGE for z in name):
605::CODE;;raise ParserException(self, ln,
606::CODE;;'Invalid property name')
607::CODE;;if len(x) == 1:
608::CODE;;raise ParserException(self, ln, 'Syntax error')
609::CODE;;value = x[1].strip()
610::CODE;;if name == 'id':
611::CODE;;if len(value) <= 0:
612::CODE;;raise ParserException(self, ln, 'Empty id')
613::CODE;;if value in ('self', 'root'):
614::CODE;;raise ParserException(
615::CODE;;self, ln,
616::CODE;;'Invalid id, cannot be "self" or "root"')
617::CODE;;current_object.id = value
618::CODE;;elif len(value):
619::CODE;;rule = ParserRuleProperty(
620::CODE;;self, ln, name, value, ignore_prev)
621::CODE;;if name[:3] == 'on_':
622::CODE;;current_object.handlers.append(rule)
623::CODE;;else:
624::CODE;;ignore_prev = False
625::CODE;;current_object.properties[name] = rule
626::CODE;;else:
627::CODE;;current_property = name
628::CODE;;current_propobject = None
630::CODE;;raise ParserException(
631::CODE;;self, ln, 'clear previous, `-`, not allowed here')
633::CODE;;elif count == indent + 2 * spaces:
634::CODE;;if current_property in (
635::CODE;;'canvas', 'canvas.after', 'canvas.before'):
636::CODE;;_objects, _lines = self.parse_level(
637::CODE;;level + 2, lines[i:], spaces)
638::CODE;;rl = ParserRule(self, ln, current_property, rlevel)
639::CODE;;rl.children = _objects
640::CODE;;if current_property == 'canvas':
641::CODE;;current_object.canvas_root = rl
642::CODE;;elif current_property == 'canvas.before':
643::CODE;;current_object.canvas_before = rl
644::CODE;;else:
645::CODE;;current_object.canvas_after = rl
646::CODE;;current_property = None
647::CODE;;lines = _lines
648::CODE;;i = 0
649::CODE;;else:
650::CODE;;if current_propobject is None:
651::CODE;;current_propobject = ParserRuleProperty(
652::CODE;;self, ln, current_property, content)
653::CODE;;if not current_property:
654::CODE;;raise ParserException(self, ln,
655::CODE;;"Invalid indentation")
656::CODE;;if current_property[:3] == 'on_':
657::CODE;;current_object.handlers.append(current_propobject)
658::CODE;;else:
659::CODE;;current_object.properties[current_property] = \
660::CODE;;current_propobject
661::CODE;;else:
662::CODE;;current_propobject.value += '\n' + content
664::CODE;;else:
665::CODE;;raise ParserException(self, ln,
666::CODE;;'Invalid indentation (too many levels)')
668::CODE;;i += 1
669::CODE;;return objects, []
670::CODE;;class ParserSelector(object):
671::CODE;;def __init__(self, key):
672::CODE;;self.key = key.lower()
673::CODE;;def match(self, widget):
674::CODE;;raise NotImplementedError
675::CODE;;def __repr__(self):
676::CODE;;return '<%s key=%s>' % (self.__class__.__name__, self.key)
677::CODE;;class ParserSelectorClass(ParserSelector):
678::CODE;;def match(self, widget):
679::CODE;;return self.key in widget.cls
680::CODE;;class ParserSelectorName(ParserSelector):
681::CODE;;parents = {}
682::CODE;;def get_bases(self, cls):
683::CODE;;for base in cls.__bases__:
684::CODE;;if base.__name__ == 'object':
685::CODE;;break
686::CODE;;yield base
687::CODE;;if base.__name__ == 'Widget':
688::CODE;;break
689::CODE;;for cbase in self.get_bases(base):
690::CODE;;yield cbase
691::CODE;;def match(self, widget):
692::CODE;;parents = ParserSelectorName.parents
693::CODE;;cls = widget.__class__
694::CODE;;if cls not in parents:
695::CODE;;classes = [x.__name__.lower() for x in
696::CODE;;[cls] + list(self.get_bases(cls))]
697::CODE;;parents[cls] = classes
698::CODE;;return self.key in parents[cls]
699::CODE;;def match_rule_name(self, rule_name):
700::CODE;;return self.key == rule_name.lower()
1::CODE;;'''

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;DDS File library
3::CODE;;================
4::CODE;;This library can be used to parse and save DDS
5::CODE;;(`DirectDraw Surface <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DirectDraw_Surface>`)
6::CODE;;files.
7::CODE;;The initial version was written by::
8::CODE;;Alexey Borzenkov (snaury@gmail.com)
9::CODE;;All the initial work credits go to him! Thank you :)
10::CODE;;This version uses structs instead of ctypes.
11::CODE;;DDS Format
12::CODE;;----------
13::CODE;;::
14::CODE;;[DDS ][SurfaceDesc][Data]
15::CODE;;[SurfaceDesc]:: (everything is uint32)
16::CODE;;Size
17::CODE;;Flags
18::CODE;;Height
19::CODE;;Width
20::CODE;;PitchOrLinearSize
21::CODE;;Depth
22::CODE;;MipmapCount
23::CODE;;Reserved1 * 11
24::CODE;;[PixelFormat]::
25::CODE;;Size
26::CODE;;Flags
27::CODE;;FourCC
28::CODE;;RGBBitCount
29::CODE;;RBitMask
30::CODE;;GBitMask
31::CODE;;BBitMask
32::CODE;;ABitMask
33::CODE;;[Caps]::
34::CODE;;Caps1
35::CODE;;Caps2
36::CODE;;Reserved1 * 2
37::CODE;;Reserverd2
38::CODE;;.. warning::
39::CODE;;This is an external library and Kivy does not provide any support for it.
40::CODE;;It might change in the future and we advise you don't rely on it in your
41::CODE;;code.
42::CODE;;'''
44::CODE;;from struct import pack, unpack, calcsize
46::CODE;;DDSD_CAPS = 0x00000001
47::CODE;;DDSD_HEIGHT = 0x00000002
48::CODE;;DDSD_WIDTH = 0x00000004
49::CODE;;DDSD_PITCH = 0x00000008
50::CODE;;DDSD_PIXELFORMAT = 0x00001000
51::CODE;;DDSD_MIPMAPCOUNT = 0x00020000
52::CODE;;DDSD_LINEARSIZE = 0x00080000
53::CODE;;DDSD_DEPTH = 0x00800000
55::CODE;;DDPF_ALPHAPIXELS = 0x00000001
56::CODE;;DDPF_FOURCC = 0x00000004
57::CODE;;DDPF_RGB = 0x00000040
58::CODE;;DDPF_LUMINANCE = 0x00020000
60::CODE;;DDSCAPS_COMPLEX = 0x00000008
61::CODE;;DDSCAPS_TEXTURE = 0x00001000
62::CODE;;DDSCAPS_MIPMAP = 0x00400000
64::CODE;;DDSCAPS2_CUBEMAP = 0x00000200
65::CODE;;DDSCAPS2_CUBEMAP_POSITIVEX = 0x00000400
66::CODE;;DDSCAPS2_CUBEMAP_NEGATIVEX = 0x00000800
67::CODE;;DDSCAPS2_CUBEMAP_POSITIVEY = 0x00001000
68::CODE;;DDSCAPS2_CUBEMAP_NEGATIVEY = 0x00002000
69::CODE;;DDSCAPS2_CUBEMAP_POSITIVEZ = 0x00004000
70::CODE;;DDSCAPS2_CUBEMAP_NEGATIVEZ = 0x00008000
71::CODE;;DDSCAPS2_VOLUME = 0x00200000
73::CODE;;DDS_DXTN = 0x00545844
74::CODE;;DDS_DXT1 = 0x31545844
75::CODE;;DDS_DXT2 = 0x32545844
76::CODE;;DDS_DXT3 = 0x33545844
77::CODE;;DDS_DXT4 = 0x34545844
78::CODE;;DDS_DXT5 = 0x35545844
79::CODE;;def dxt_to_str(dxt):
80::CODE;;if dxt == DDS_DXT1:
81::CODE;;return 's3tc_dxt1'
82::CODE;;elif dxt == DDS_DXT2:
83::CODE;;return 's3tc_dxt2'
84::CODE;;elif dxt == DDS_DXT3:
85::CODE;;return 's3tc_dxt3'
86::CODE;;elif dxt == DDS_DXT4:
87::CODE;;return 's3tc_dxt4'
88::CODE;;elif dxt == DDS_DXT5:
89::CODE;;return 's3tc_dxt5'
90::CODE;;elif dxt == 0:
91::CODE;;return 'rgba'
92::CODE;;elif dxt == 1:
93::CODE;;return 'alpha'
94::CODE;;elif dxt == 2:
95::CODE;;return 'luminance'
96::CODE;;elif dxt == 3:
97::CODE;;return 'luminance_alpha'
98::CODE;;def str_to_dxt(dxt):
99::CODE;;if dxt == 's3tc_dxt1':
100::CODE;;return DDS_DXT1
101::CODE;;if dxt == 's3tc_dxt2':
102::CODE;;return DDS_DXT2
103::CODE;;if dxt == 's3tc_dxt3':
104::CODE;;return DDS_DXT3
105::CODE;;if dxt == 's3tc_dxt4':
106::CODE;;return DDS_DXT4
107::CODE;;if dxt == 's3tc_dxt5':
108::CODE;;return DDS_DXT5
109::CODE;;if dxt == 'rgba':
110::CODE;;return 0
111::CODE;;if dxt == 'alpha':
112::CODE;;return 1
113::CODE;;if dxt == 'luminance':
114::CODE;;return 2
115::CODE;;if dxt == 'luminance_alpha':
116::CODE;;return 3
117::CODE;;def align_value(val, b):
118::CODE;;return val + (-val % b)
119::CODE;;def check_flags(val, fl):
120::CODE;;return (val & fl) == fl
121::CODE;;def dxt_size(w, h, dxt):
122::CODE;;w = max(1, w // 4)
123::CODE;;h = max(1, h // 4)
124::CODE;;if dxt == DDS_DXT1:
125::CODE;;return w * h * 8
126::CODE;;elif dxt in (DDS_DXT2, DDS_DXT3, DDS_DXT4, DDS_DXT5):
127::CODE;;return w * h * 16
128::CODE;;return -1
129::CODE;;class QueryDict(dict):
130::CODE;;def __getattr__(self, attr):
131::CODE;;try:
132::CODE;;return self.__getitem__(attr)
133::CODE;;except KeyError:
134::CODE;;try:
135::CODE;;return super(QueryDict, self).__getattr__(attr)
136::CODE;;except AttributeError:
137::CODE;;raise KeyError(attr)
138::CODE;;def __setattr__(self, attr, value):
139::CODE;;self.__setitem__(attr, value)
140::CODE;;class DDSException(Exception):
141::CODE;;pass
142::CODE;;class DDSFile(object):
143::CODE;;fields = (
144::CODE;;('size', 0), ('flags', 1), ('height', 2),
145::CODE;;('width', 3), ('pitchOrLinearSize', 4), ('depth', 5),
146::CODE;;('mipmapCount', 6), ('pf_size', 18), ('pf_flags', 19),
147::CODE;;('pf_fourcc', 20), ('pf_rgbBitCount', 21), ('pf_rBitMask', 22),
148::CODE;;('pf_gBitMask', 23), ('pf_bBitMask', 24), ('pf_aBitMask', 25),
149::CODE;;('caps1', 26), ('caps2', 27))
150::CODE;;def __init__(self, filename=None):
151::CODE;;super(DDSFile, self).__init__()
152::CODE;;self._dxt = 0
153::CODE;;self._fmt = None
154::CODE;;self.meta = meta = QueryDict()
155::CODE;;self.count = 0
156::CODE;;self.images = []
157::CODE;;self.images_size = []
158::CODE;;for field, index in DDSFile.fields:
159::CODE;;meta[field] = 0
160::CODE;;if filename:
161::CODE;;self.load(filename)
162::CODE;;def load(self, filename):
163::CODE;;self.filename = filename
164::CODE;;with open(filename, 'rb') as fd:
165::CODE;;data = fd.read()
166::CODE;;if data[:4] != b'DDS ':
167::CODE;;raise DDSException('Invalid magic header {}'.format(data[:4]))
169::CODE;;fmt = 'I' * 31
170::CODE;;fmt_size = calcsize(fmt)
171::CODE;;pf_size = calcsize('I' * 8)
172::CODE;;header, data = data[4:4+fmt_size], data[4+fmt_size:]
173::CODE;;if len(header) != fmt_size:
174::CODE;;raise DDSException('Truncated header in')
176::CODE;;header = unpack(fmt, header)
177::CODE;;meta = self.meta
178::CODE;;for name, index in DDSFile.fields:
179::CODE;;meta[name] = header[index]
181::CODE;;if meta.size != fmt_size:
182::CODE;;raise DDSException('Invalid header size (%d instead of %d)' %
183::CODE;;(meta.size, fmt_size))
184::CODE;;if meta.pf_size != pf_size:
185::CODE;;raise DDSException('Invalid pixelformat size (%d instead of %d)' %
186::CODE;;(meta.pf_size, pf_size))
187::CODE;;if not check_flags(meta.flags,
188::CODE;;DDSD_CAPS | DDSD_PIXELFORMAT | DDSD_WIDTH | DDSD_HEIGHT):
189::CODE;;raise DDSException('Not enough flags')
190::CODE;;if not check_flags(meta.caps1, DDSCAPS_TEXTURE):
191::CODE;;raise DDSException('Not a DDS texture')
192::CODE;;self.count = 1
193::CODE;;if check_flags(meta.flags, DDSD_MIPMAPCOUNT):
194::CODE;;if not check_flags(meta.caps1, DDSCAPS_COMPLEX | DDSCAPS_MIPMAP):
195::CODE;;raise DDSException('Invalid mipmap without flags')
196::CODE;;self.count = meta.mipmapCount
197::CODE;;hasrgb = check_flags(meta.pf_flags, DDPF_RGB)
198::CODE;;hasalpha = check_flags(meta.pf_flags, DDPF_ALPHAPIXELS)
199::CODE;;hasluminance = check_flags(meta.pf_flags, DDPF_LUMINANCE)
200::CODE;;bpp = None
201::CODE;;dxt = block = pitch = 0
202::CODE;;if hasrgb or hasalpha or hasluminance:
203::CODE;;bpp = meta.pf_rgbBitCount
204::CODE;;if hasrgb and hasluminance:
205::CODE;;raise DDSException('File have RGB and Luminance')
206::CODE;;if hasrgb:
207::CODE;;dxt = 0
208::CODE;;elif hasalpha and not hasluminance:
209::CODE;;dxt = 1
210::CODE;;elif hasluminance and not hasalpha:
211::CODE;;dxt = 2
212::CODE;;elif hasalpha and hasluminance:
213::CODE;;dxt = 3
214::CODE;;elif check_flags(meta.pf_flags, DDPF_FOURCC):
215::CODE;;dxt = meta.pf_fourcc
216::CODE;;if dxt not in (DDS_DXT1, DDS_DXT2, DDS_DXT3, DDS_DXT4, DDS_DXT5):
217::CODE;;raise DDSException('Unsupported FOURCC')
218::CODE;;else:
219::CODE;;raise DDSException('Unsupported format specified')
220::CODE;;if bpp:
221::CODE;;block = align_value(bpp, 8) // 8
222::CODE;;pitch = align_value(block * meta.width, 4)
223::CODE;;if check_flags(meta.flags, DDSD_LINEARSIZE):
224::CODE;;if dxt in (0, 1, 2, 3):
225::CODE;;size = pitch * meta.height
226::CODE;;else:
227::CODE;;size = dxt_size(meta.width, meta.height, dxt)
228::CODE;;w = meta.width
229::CODE;;h = meta.height
230::CODE;;images = self.images
231::CODE;;images_size = self.images_size
232::CODE;;for i in range(self.count):
233::CODE;;if dxt in (0, 1, 2, 3):
234::CODE;;size = align_value(block * w, 4) * h
235::CODE;;else:
236::CODE;;size = dxt_size(w, h, dxt)
237::CODE;;image, data = data[:size], data[size:]
238::CODE;;if len(image) < size:
239::CODE;;raise DDSException('Truncated image for mipmap %d' % i)
240::CODE;;images_size.append((w, h))
241::CODE;;images.append(image)
242::CODE;;if w == 1 and h == 1:
243::CODE;;break
244::CODE;;w = max(1, w // 2)
245::CODE;;h = max(1, h // 2)
246::CODE;;if len(images) == 0:
247::CODE;;raise DDSException('No images available')
248::CODE;;if len(images) < self.count:
249::CODE;;raise DDSException('Not enough images')
250::CODE;;self._dxt = dxt
251::CODE;;def save(self, filename):
252::CODE;;if len(self.images) == 0:
253::CODE;;raise DDSException('No images to save')
254::CODE;;fields = dict(DDSFile.fields)
255::CODE;;fields_keys = list(fields.keys())
256::CODE;;fields_index = list(fields.values())
257::CODE;;mget = self.meta.get
258::CODE;;header = []
259::CODE;;for idx in range(31):
260::CODE;;if idx in fields_index:
261::CODE;;value = mget(fields_keys[fields_index.index(idx)], 0)
262::CODE;;else:
263::CODE;;value = 0
264::CODE;;header.append(value)
265::CODE;;with open(filename, 'wb') as fd:
266::CODE;;fd.write('DDS ')
267::CODE;;fd.write(pack('I' * 31, *header))
268::CODE;;for image in self.images:
269::CODE;;fd.write(image)
270::CODE;;def add_image(self, level, bpp, fmt, width, height, data):
271::CODE;;assert bpp == 32
272::CODE;;assert fmt in ('rgb', 'rgba', 'dxt1', 'dxt2', 'dxt3', 'dxt4', 'dxt5')
273::CODE;;assert width > 0
274::CODE;;assert height > 0
275::CODE;;assert level >= 0
276::CODE;;meta = self.meta
277::CODE;;images = self.images
278::CODE;;if len(images) == 0:
279::CODE;;assert level == 0
281::CODE;;for k in meta.keys():
282::CODE;;meta[k] = 0
283::CODE;;self._fmt = fmt
284::CODE;;meta.size = calcsize('I' * 31)
285::CODE;;meta.pf_size = calcsize('I' * 8)
286::CODE;;meta.pf_flags = 0
287::CODE;;meta.flags = DDSD_CAPS | DDSD_PIXELFORMAT | DDSD_WIDTH | DDSD_HEIGHT
288::CODE;;meta.width = width
289::CODE;;meta.height = height
290::CODE;;meta.caps1 = DDSCAPS_TEXTURE
291::CODE;;meta.flags |= DDSD_LINEARSIZE
292::CODE;;meta.pitchOrLinearSize = len(data)
293::CODE;;meta.pf_rgbBitCount = 32
294::CODE;;meta.pf_rBitMask = 0x00ff0000
295::CODE;;meta.pf_gBitMask = 0x0000ff00
296::CODE;;meta.pf_bBitMask = 0x000000ff
297::CODE;;meta.pf_aBitMask = 0xff000000
298::CODE;;if fmt in ('rgb', 'rgba'):
299::CODE;;assert True
300::CODE;;assert bpp == 32
301::CODE;;meta.pf_flags |= DDPF_RGB
302::CODE;;meta.pf_rgbBitCount = 32
303::CODE;;meta.pf_rBitMask = 0x00ff0000
304::CODE;;meta.pf_gBitMask = 0x0000ff00
305::CODE;;meta.pf_bBitMask = 0x000000ff
306::CODE;;meta.pf_aBitMask = 0x00000000
307::CODE;;if fmt == 'rgba':
308::CODE;;meta.pf_flags |= DDPF_ALPHAPIXELS
309::CODE;;meta.pf_aBitMask = 0xff000000
310::CODE;;else:
311::CODE;;meta.pf_flags |= DDPF_FOURCC
312::CODE;;if fmt == 'dxt1':
313::CODE;;meta.pf_fourcc = DDS_DXT1
314::CODE;;elif fmt == 'dxt2':
315::CODE;;meta.pf_fourcc = DDS_DXT2
316::CODE;;elif fmt == 'dxt3':
317::CODE;;meta.pf_fourcc = DDS_DXT3
318::CODE;;elif fmt == 'dxt4':
319::CODE;;meta.pf_fourcc = DDS_DXT4
320::CODE;;elif fmt == 'dxt5':
321::CODE;;meta.pf_fourcc = DDS_DXT5
322::CODE;;images.append(data)
323::CODE;;else:
324::CODE;;assert level == len(images)
325::CODE;;assert fmt == self._fmt
326::CODE;;images.append(data)
327::CODE;;meta.flags |= DDSD_MIPMAPCOUNT
328::CODE;;meta.caps1 |= DDSCAPS_COMPLEX | DDSCAPS_MIPMAP
329::CODE;;meta.mipmapCount = len(images)
330::CODE;;def __repr__(self):
331::CODE;;return '<DDSFile filename=%r size=%r dxt=%r len(images)=%r>' % (
332::CODE;;self.filename, self.size, self.dxt, len(self.images))
333::CODE;;def _get_size(self):
334::CODE;;meta = self.meta
335::CODE;;return meta.width, meta.height
336::CODE;;def _set_size(self, size):
337::CODE;;self.meta.update({'width': size[0], 'height': size[1]})
338::CODE;;size = property(_get_size, _set_size)
339::CODE;;def _get_dxt(self):
340::CODE;;return dxt_to_str(self._dxt)
341::CODE;;def _set_dxt(self, dxt):
342::CODE;;self._dxt = str_to_dxt(dxt)
343::CODE;;dxt = property(_get_dxt, _set_dxt)
344::CODE;;if __name__ == '__main__':
345::CODE;;import sys
346::CODE;;if len(sys.argv) == 1:
347::CODE;;print('Usage: python ddsfile.py <file1> <file2> ...')
348::CODE;;sys.exit(0)

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Python mtdev
3::CODE;;============
4::CODE;;The mtdev module provides Python bindings to the `Kernel multi-touch
5::CODE;;transformation library <https://launchpad.net/mtdev>`_, also known as mtdev
6::CODE;;(MIT license).
7::CODE;;The mtdev library transforms all variants of kernel MT events to the
8::CODE;;slotted type B protocol. The events put into mtdev may be from any MT
9::CODE;;device, specifically type A without contact tracking, type A with
10::CODE;;contact tracking, or type B with contact tracking. See the kernel
11::CODE;;documentation for further details.
12::CODE;;.. warning::
13::CODE;;This is an external library and Kivy does not provide any support for it.
14::CODE;;It might change in the future and we advise you don't rely on it in your
15::CODE;;code.
16::CODE;;'''
18::CODE;;import os
19::CODE;;import time
20::CODE;;from ctypes import cdll, Structure, c_ulong, c_int, c_ushort, \
21::CODE;;c_void_p, pointer, POINTER, byref
23::CODE;;if 'KIVY_DOC' not in os.environ:
24::CODE;;libmtdev = cdll.LoadLibrary('libmtdev.so.1')
38::CODE;;MTDEV_CODE_ABS_X = 0x00
39::CODE;;MTDEV_CODE_ABS_Y = 0x01
40::CODE;;MTDEV_CODE_ABS_Z = 0x02
41::CODE;;MTDEV_CODE_BTN_DIGI = 0x140
42::CODE;;MTDEV_CODE_BTN_TOOL_PEN = 0x140
43::CODE;;MTDEV_CODE_BTN_TOOL_RUBBER = 0x141

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Asynchronous data loader
3::CODE;;========================
4::CODE;;This is the Asynchronous Loader. You can use it to load an image
5::CODE;;and use it, even if data are not yet available. You must specify a default
6::CODE;;loading image when using the loader::
7::CODE;;from kivy.loader import Loader
8::CODE;;image = Loader.image('mysprite.png')
9::CODE;;You can also load an image from a url::
10::CODE;;image = Loader.image('http://mysite.com/test.png')
11::CODE;;If you want to change the default loading image, you can do::
12::CODE;;Loader.loading_image = Image('another_loading.png')
13::CODE;;Tweaking the asynchronous loader
14::CODE;;--------------------------------
15::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.6.0
16::CODE;;You can tweak the loader to provide a better user experience or more
17::CODE;;performance, depending of the images you are going to load. Take a look at the
18::CODE;;parameters:
19::CODE;;- :attr:`Loader.num_workers` - define the number of threads to start for
20::CODE;;loading images.
21::CODE;;- :attr:`Loader.max_upload_per_frame` - define the maximum image uploads in
22::CODE;;GPU to do per frame.
23::CODE;;'''

102::CODE;;'''Number of workers to use while loading (used only if the loader
103::CODE;;implementation supports it). This setting impacts the loader only on
104::CODE;;initialization. Once the loader is started, the setting has no impact::
105::CODE;;from kivy.loader import Loader

122::CODE;;'''The number of images to upload per frame. By default, we'll
123::CODE;;upload only 2 images to the GPU per frame. If you are uploading many
124::CODE;;small images, you can easily increase this parameter to 10 or more.
125::CODE;;If you are loading multiple full HD images, the upload time may have
126::CODE;;consequences and block the application. If you want a
127::CODE;;smooth experience, use the default.

129::CODE;;so it may take time. If you have activated mipmap=True too, then the
130::CODE;;GPU must calculate the mipmap of these big images too, in real time.

132::CODE;;or 2. If you want to get rid of that (or reduce it a lot), take a
133::CODE;;look at the DDS format.

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Metrics
3::CODE;;=======
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.5.0
5::CODE;;A screen is defined by its physical size, density and resolution. These
6::CODE;;factors are essential for creating UI's with correct size everywhere.
7::CODE;;In Kivy, all the graphics pipelines work with pixels. But using pixels as a
8::CODE;;measurement unit is problematic because sizes change according to the
9::CODE;;screen.
10::CODE;;Dimensions
11::CODE;;----------
12::CODE;;If you want to design your UI for different screen sizes, you will want better
13::CODE;;measurement units to work with. Kivy provides some more scalable alternatives.
14::CODE;;:Units:
15::CODE;;`pt`
16::CODE;;Points - 1/72 of an inch based on the physical size of the screen.
17::CODE;;Prefer to use sp instead of pt.
18::CODE;;`mm`
19::CODE;;Millimeters - Based on the physical size of the screen.
20::CODE;;`cm`
21::CODE;;Centimeters - Based on the physical size of the screen.
22::CODE;;`in`
23::CODE;;Inches - Based on the physical size of the screen.
24::CODE;;`dp`
25::CODE;;Density-independent Pixels - An abstract unit that is based on the
26::CODE;;physical density of the screen. With a :attr:`~MetricsBase.density` of
27::CODE;;1, 1dp is equal to 1px. When running on a higher density screen, the
28::CODE;;number of pixels used to draw 1dp is scaled up a factor appropriate to
29::CODE;;the screen's dpi, and the inverse for a lower dpi.
30::CODE;;The ratio of dp-to-pixels will change with the screen density, but not
31::CODE;;necessarily in direct proportion. Using the dp unit is a simple
32::CODE;;solution to making the view dimensions in your layout resize
33::CODE;;properly for different screen densities. In others words, it
34::CODE;;provides consistency for the real-world size of your UI across
35::CODE;;different devices.
36::CODE;;`sp`
37::CODE;;Scale-independent Pixels - This is like the dp unit, but it is also
38::CODE;;scaled by the user's font size preference. We recommend you use this
39::CODE;;unit when specifying font sizes, so the font size will be adjusted to
40::CODE;;both the screen density and the user's preference.
41::CODE;;Examples
42::CODE;;--------
43::CODE;;Here is an example of creating a label with a sp font_size and setting the
44::CODE;;height manually with a 10dp margin::
46::CODE;;<MyWidget>:
47::CODE;;Label:
48::CODE;;text: 'Hello world'
49::CODE;;font_size: '15sp'
50::CODE;;size_hint_y: None
51::CODE;;height: self.texture_size[1] + dp(10)
52::CODE;;Manual control of metrics
53::CODE;;-------------------------
54::CODE;;The metrics cannot be changed at runtime. Once a value has been converted to
55::CODE;;pixels, you can't retrieve the original value anymore. This stems from the fact
56::CODE;;that the DPI and density of a device cannot be changed at runtime.
57::CODE;;We provide some environment variables to control metrics:
58::CODE;;- `KIVY_METRICS_DENSITY`: if set, this value will be used for
59::CODE;;:attr:`~MetricsBase.density` instead of the systems one. On android,
60::CODE;;the value varies between 0.75, 1, 1.5 and 2.
61::CODE;;- `KIVY_METRICS_FONTSCALE`: if set, this value will be used for
62::CODE;;:attr:`~MetricsBase.fontscale` instead of the systems one. On android, the
63::CODE;;value varies between 0.8 and 1.2.
64::CODE;;- `KIVY_DPI`: if set, this value will be used for :attr:`~MetricsBase.dpi`.
65::CODE;;Please
66::CODE;;note that setting the DPI will not impact the dp/sp notation because these
67::CODE;;are based on the screen density.
68::CODE;;For example, if you want to simulate a high-density screen (like the HTC One
69::CODE;;X)::
70::CODE;;KIVY_DPI=320 KIVY_METRICS_DENSITY=2 python main.py --size 1280x720
71::CODE;;Or a medium-density (like Motorola Droid 2)::
72::CODE;;KIVY_DPI=240 KIVY_METRICS_DENSITY=1.5 python main.py --size 854x480
73::CODE;;You can also simulate an alternative user preference for fontscale as follows::
74::CODE;;KIVY_METRICS_FONTSCALE=1.2 python main.py
75::CODE;;'''

172::CODE;;set to change the value. But, the :attr:`density` is reloaded and reset if
173::CODE;;we got it from the Window and the Window ``dpi`` changed.

317::CODE;;Metrics: MetricsBase = register_context('Metrics', MetricsBase)
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Modules
3::CODE;;=======
4::CODE;;Modules are classes that can be loaded when a Kivy application is starting. The
5::CODE;;loading of modules is managed by the config file. Currently, we include:
6::CODE;;* :class:`~kivy.modules.touchring`: Draw a circle around each touch.
7::CODE;;* :class:`~kivy.modules.monitor`: Add a red topbar that indicates the FPS
8::CODE;;and a small graph indicating input activity.
9::CODE;;* :class:`~kivy.modules.keybinding`: Bind some keys to actions, such as a
10::CODE;;screenshot.
11::CODE;;* :class:`~kivy.modules.recorder`: Record and playback a sequence of
12::CODE;;events.
13::CODE;;* :class:`~kivy.modules.screen`: Emulate the characteristics (dpi/density/
14::CODE;;resolution) of different screens.
15::CODE;;* :class:`~kivy.modules.inspector`: Examines your widget hierarchy and
16::CODE;;widget properties.
17::CODE;;* :class:`~kivy.modules.webdebugger`: Realtime examination of your app
18::CODE;;internals via a web browser.
19::CODE;;* :class:`~kivy.modules.joycursor`: Navigate in your app with a joystick.
20::CODE;;* :class:`~kivy.modules.showborder`: Show widget's border.
21::CODE;;Modules are automatically loaded from the Kivy path and User path:
22::CODE;;* `PATH_TO_KIVY/kivy/modules`
23::CODE;;* `HOME/.kivy/mods`
24::CODE;;Activating a module
25::CODE;;-------------------
26::CODE;;There are various ways in which you can activate a kivy module.
27::CODE;;Activate a module in the config
28::CODE;;^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
29::CODE;;To activate a module this way, you can edit your configuration file (in your
30::CODE;;`HOME/.kivy/config.ini`)::
31::CODE;;[modules]
33::CODE;;touchring =
36::CODE;;Only the name of the module followed by "=" is sufficient to activate the
37::CODE;;module.
38::CODE;;Activate a module in Python
39::CODE;;^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
40::CODE;;Before starting your application, preferably at the start of your import, you
41::CODE;;can do something like this::
42::CODE;;import kivy
43::CODE;;kivy.require('1.0.8')
45::CODE;;from kivy.config import Config
46::CODE;;Config.set('modules', 'touchring', '')
47::CODE;;Activate a module via the commandline
48::CODE;;^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
49::CODE;;When starting your application from the commandline, you can add a
50::CODE;;*-m <modulename>* to the arguments. For example::
51::CODE;;python main.py -m webdebugger
52::CODE;;.. note::
53::CODE;;Some modules, such as the screen, may require additional parameters. They
54::CODE;;will, however, print these parameters to the console when launched without
55::CODE;;them.
56::CODE;;Create your own module
57::CODE;;----------------------
58::CODE;;Create a file in your `HOME/.kivy/mods`, and create 2 functions::
59::CODE;;def start(win, ctx):
60::CODE;;pass
61::CODE;;def stop(win, ctx):
62::CODE;;pass
63::CODE;;Start/stop are functions that will be called for every window opened in
64::CODE;;Kivy. When you are starting a module, you can use these to store and
65::CODE;;manage the module state. Use the `ctx` variable as a dictionary. This
66::CODE;;context is unique for each instance/start() call of the module, and will
67::CODE;;be passed to stop() too.
68::CODE;;'''

109::CODE;;def import_module(self, name):

172::CODE;;'''Update the status of the module for each window'''

2::CODE;;Cursor
3::CODE;;======
4::CODE;;Shows a cursor following mouse motion events, useful on systems with no
5::CODE;;visible native mouse cursor.
6::CODE;;Configuration
7::CODE;;-------------
8::CODE;;:Parameters:
9::CODE;;`texture`: str, defaults to
10::CODE;;'data/images/cursor.png' Image used to represent the cursor if
11::CODE;;displayed
12::CODE;;`size`: tuple, defaults to (40, 40)
13::CODE;;Apparent size of the mouse cursor, if displayed, (None,None) value
14::CODE;;will keep its real size.
15::CODE;;`offset`: tuple, defaults to (None, None)
16::CODE;;Offset of the texture image. The default value will align the
17::CODE;;top-left corner of the image to the mouse pos.
18::CODE;;Example
19::CODE;;-------
20::CODE;;In your configuration (`~/.kivy/config.ini`), you can add something like
21::CODE;;this::
22::CODE;;[modules]
23::CODE;;cursor = texture=mypointer.png,size=20x20,offset=20x20
24::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.10.0
25::CODE;;'''
26::CODE;;__all__ = ('start', 'stop')
27::CODE;;from kivy.core.image import Image
28::CODE;;from kivy.graphics import Color, Rectangle
29::CODE;;from kivy import kivy_data_dir
30::CODE;;from os.path import join
31::CODE;;from functools import partial
32::CODE;;def _mouse_move(texture, size, offset, win, pos, *args):
33::CODE;;if hasattr(win, '_cursor'):
34::CODE;;c = win._cursor
35::CODE;;else:
36::CODE;;with win.canvas.after:
37::CODE;;Color(1, 1, 1, 1, mode='rgba')
38::CODE;;win._cursor = c = Rectangle(texture=texture, size=size)
39::CODE;;c.pos = pos[0] + offset[0], pos[1] - size[1] + offset[1]
40::CODE;;def start(win, ctx):
41::CODE;;cursor_texture = Image(
42::CODE;;ctx.config.get('texture', join(kivy_data_dir, 'images', 'cursor.png'))
43::CODE;;).texture
44::CODE;;cursor_size = ctx.config.get('size')
45::CODE;;if isinstance(cursor_size, str):
46::CODE;;cursor_size = [int(x) for x in cursor_size.split('x')]
47::CODE;;elif not cursor_size:
48::CODE;;cursor_size = cursor_texture.size
49::CODE;;cursor_offset = ctx.config.get('offset', (0, 0))
50::CODE;;if isinstance(cursor_offset, str):
51::CODE;;cursor_offset = [int(x) for x in cursor_offset.split('x')]
52::CODE;;win.bind(
53::CODE;;mouse_pos=partial(
54::CODE;;_mouse_move, cursor_texture, cursor_size, cursor_offset))
55::CODE;;def stop(win, ctx):
56::CODE;;win.unbind(mouse_pos=_mouse_move)
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Inspector
3::CODE;;=========
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.9
5::CODE;;.. warning::
6::CODE;;This module is highly experimental, use it with care.
7::CODE;;The Inspector is a tool for finding a widget in the widget tree by clicking or
8::CODE;;tapping on it.
9::CODE;;Some keyboard shortcuts are activated:
10::CODE;;* "Ctrl + e": activate / deactivate the inspector view
11::CODE;;* "Escape": cancel widget lookup first, then hide the inspector view
12::CODE;;Available inspector interactions:
13::CODE;;* tap once on a widget to select it without leaving inspect mode
14::CODE;;* double tap on a widget to select and leave inspect mode (then you can
15::CODE;;manipulate the widget again)
16::CODE;;Some properties can be edited live. However, due to the delayed usage of
17::CODE;;some properties, it might crash if you don't handle all the cases.
18::CODE;;Usage
19::CODE;;-----
20::CODE;;For normal module usage, please see the :mod:`~kivy.modules` documentation.
21::CODE;;The Inspector, however, can also be imported and used just like a normal
22::CODE;;python module. This has the added advantage of being able to activate and
23::CODE;;deactivate the module programmatically::
24::CODE;;from kivy.core.window import Window
25::CODE;;from kivy.app import App
26::CODE;;from kivy.uix.button import Button
27::CODE;;from kivy.modules import inspector
28::CODE;;class Demo(App):
29::CODE;;def build(self):
30::CODE;;button = Button(text="Test")
31::CODE;;inspector.create_inspector(Window, button)
32::CODE;;return button
33::CODE;;Demo().run()
34::CODE;;To remove the Inspector, you can do the following::
35::CODE;;inspector.stop(Window, button)
36::CODE;;'''

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;JoyCursor
3::CODE;;=========
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.10.0
5::CODE;;The JoyCursor is a tool for navigating with a joystick as if using a mouse
6::CODE;;or touch. Most of the actions that are possible for a mouse user are available
7::CODE;;in this module.
8::CODE;;For example:
9::CODE;;* left click
10::CODE;;* right click
11::CODE;;* double click (two clicks)
12::CODE;;* moving the cursor
13::CODE;;* holding the button (+ moving at the same time)
14::CODE;;* selecting
15::CODE;;* scrolling
16::CODE;;There are some properties that can be edited live, such as intensity of the
17::CODE;;JoyCursor movement and toggling mouse button holding.
18::CODE;;Usage
19::CODE;;-----
20::CODE;;For normal module usage, please see the :mod:`~kivy.modules` documentation
21::CODE;;and these bindings:
22::CODE;;+------------------+--------------------+
23::CODE;;| Event | Joystick |
24::CODE;;+==================+====================+
25::CODE;;| cursor move | Axis 3, Axis 4 |
26::CODE;;+------------------+--------------------+
27::CODE;;| cursor intensity | Button 0, Button 1 |
28::CODE;;+------------------+--------------------+
29::CODE;;| left click | Button 2 |
30::CODE;;+------------------+--------------------+
31::CODE;;| right click | Button 3 |
32::CODE;;+------------------+--------------------+
33::CODE;;| scroll up | Button 4 |
34::CODE;;+------------------+--------------------+
35::CODE;;| scroll down | Button 5 |
36::CODE;;+------------------+--------------------+
37::CODE;;| hold button | Button 6 |
38::CODE;;+------------------+--------------------+
39::CODE;;| joycursor on/off | Button 7 |
40::CODE;;+------------------+--------------------+
41::CODE;;The JoyCursor, like Inspector, can also be imported and used as a normal
42::CODE;;python module. This has the added advantage of being able to activate and
43::CODE;;deactivate the module programmatically::
44::CODE;;from kivy.lang import Builder
45::CODE;;from kivy.base import runTouchApp
56::CODE;;'''
57::CODE;;__all__ = ('start', 'stop', 'create_joycursor')
58::CODE;;from kivy.clock import Clock
59::CODE;;from kivy.logger import Logger
60::CODE;;from kivy.uix.widget import Widget
61::CODE;;from kivy.graphics import Color, Line

63::CODE;;ObjectProperty,
64::CODE;;NumericProperty,
65::CODE;;BooleanProperty
66::CODE;;)
67::CODE;;class JoyCursor(Widget):
68::CODE;;win = ObjectProperty()

78::CODE;;self.avoid_bring_to_top = False
79::CODE;;self.size_hint = (None, None)
80::CODE;;self.size = (21, 21)
81::CODE;;self.set_cursor()

84::CODE;;Color(rgba=(0.19, 0.64, 0.81, 0.5))
85::CODE;;self.cursor_ox = Line(
86::CODE;;points=self.cursor_pts[:4],
87::CODE;;width=self.cursor_width + 0.1
88::CODE;;)
89::CODE;;self.cursor_oy = Line(
90::CODE;;points=self.cursor_pts[4:],
91::CODE;;width=self.cursor_width + 0.1
92::CODE;;)
93::CODE;;Color(rgba=(1, 1, 1, 0.5))

95::CODE;;points=self.cursor_pts[:4],
96::CODE;;width=self.cursor_width
97::CODE;;)
98::CODE;;self.cursor_y = Line(
99::CODE;;points=self.cursor_pts[4:],
100::CODE;;width=self.cursor_width
101::CODE;;)
102::CODE;;self.pos = [-i for i in self.size]
103::CODE;;def on_window_children(self, win, *args):
106::CODE;;if self.avoid_bring_to_top or not self.activated:
107::CODE;;return
108::CODE;;self.avoid_bring_to_top = True

110::CODE;;win.add_widget(self)
111::CODE;;self.avoid_bring_to_top = False
112::CODE;;def on_activated(self, instance, activated):
114::CODE;;if activated:
115::CODE;;self.win.add_widget(self)
116::CODE;;self.move = Clock.schedule_interval(self.move_cursor, 0)
117::CODE;;self.win.fbind('on_joy_axis', self.check_cursor)
118::CODE;;self.win.fbind('on_joy_button_down', self.set_intensity)
119::CODE;;self.win.fbind('on_joy_button_down', self.check_dispatch)
120::CODE;;self.win.fbind('mouse_pos', self.stop_cursor)
121::CODE;;mouse_pos = self.win.mouse_pos
122::CODE;;self.pos = (
123::CODE;;mouse_pos[0] - self.size[0] / 2.0,
124::CODE;;mouse_pos[1] - self.size[1] / 2.0
125::CODE;;)
126::CODE;;Logger.info('JoyCursor: joycursor activated')
127::CODE;;else:
128::CODE;;self.pos = [-i for i in self.size]
129::CODE;;Clock.unschedule(self.move)
130::CODE;;self.win.funbind('on_joy_axis', self.check_cursor)
131::CODE;;self.win.funbind('on_joy_button_down', self.set_intensity)
132::CODE;;self.win.funbind('on_joy_button_down', self.check_dispatch)
133::CODE;;self.win.funbind('mouse_pos', self.stop_cursor)
134::CODE;;self.win.remove_widget(self)
135::CODE;;Logger.info('JoyCursor: joycursor deactivated')
136::CODE;;def set_cursor(self, *args):
138::CODE;;px, py = self.pos
139::CODE;;sx, sy = self.size
140::CODE;;self.cursor_pts = [
141::CODE;;px, py + round(sy / 2.0), px + sx, py + round(sy / 2.0),
142::CODE;;px + round(sx / 2.0), py, px + round(sx / 2.0), py + sy
143::CODE;;]
144::CODE;;def check_cursor(self, win, stickid, axisid, value):
146::CODE;;intensity = self.intensity
147::CODE;;dead = self.dead_zone
148::CODE;;if axisid == 3:
149::CODE;;if value < -dead:
150::CODE;;self.offset_x = -intensity
151::CODE;;elif value > dead:
152::CODE;;self.offset_x = intensity
153::CODE;;else:
154::CODE;;self.offset_x = 0
155::CODE;;elif axisid == 4:
157::CODE;;if value < -dead:
158::CODE;;self.offset_y = intensity
159::CODE;;elif value > dead:
160::CODE;;self.offset_y = -intensity
161::CODE;;else:
162::CODE;;self.offset_y = 0
163::CODE;;else:
164::CODE;;self.offset_x = 0
165::CODE;;self.offset_y = 0
166::CODE;;def set_intensity(self, win, stickid, buttonid):
168::CODE;;intensity = self.intensity
169::CODE;;if buttonid == 0 and intensity > 2:
170::CODE;;intensity -= 1
171::CODE;;elif buttonid == 1:
172::CODE;;intensity += 1
173::CODE;;self.intensity = intensity
174::CODE;;def check_dispatch(self, win, stickid, buttonid):
175::CODE;;if buttonid == 6:
176::CODE;;self.cursor_hold = not self.cursor_hold
177::CODE;;if buttonid not in (2, 3, 4, 5, 6):
178::CODE;;return
179::CODE;;x, y = self.center
181::CODE;;y = self.win.system_size[1] - y
182::CODE;;modifiers = []
183::CODE;;actions = {
184::CODE;;2: 'left',
185::CODE;;3: 'right',
186::CODE;;4: 'scrollup',
187::CODE;;5: 'scrolldown',
188::CODE;;6: 'left'
189::CODE;;}
190::CODE;;button = actions[buttonid]
191::CODE;;self.win.dispatch('on_mouse_down', x, y, button, modifiers)
192::CODE;;if not self.cursor_hold:
193::CODE;;self.win.dispatch('on_mouse_up', x, y, button, modifiers)
194::CODE;;def move_cursor(self, *args):
196::CODE;;self.pos[0] += self.offset_x
197::CODE;;self.pos[1] += self.offset_y
198::CODE;;modifiers = []
199::CODE;;if self.cursor_hold:
200::CODE;;self.win.dispatch(
201::CODE;;'on_mouse_move',
202::CODE;;self.center[0],
203::CODE;;self.win.system_size[1] - self.center[1],
204::CODE;;modifiers
205::CODE;;)
206::CODE;;def stop_cursor(self, instance, mouse_pos):
208::CODE;;self.offset_x = 0
209::CODE;;self.offset_y = 0
210::CODE;;self.pos = (
211::CODE;;mouse_pos[0] - self.size[0] / 2.0,
212::CODE;;mouse_pos[1] - self.size[1] / 2.0
213::CODE;;)
214::CODE;;def on_pos(self, instance, new_pos):
215::CODE;;self.set_cursor()
216::CODE;;self.cursor_x.points = self.cursor_pts[:4]
217::CODE;;self.cursor_y.points = self.cursor_pts[4:]
218::CODE;;self.cursor_ox.points = self.cursor_pts[:4]
219::CODE;;self.cursor_oy.points = self.cursor_pts[4:]
220::CODE;;def keyboard_shortcuts(self, win, scancode, *args):
221::CODE;;modifiers = args[-1]
222::CODE;;if scancode == 101 and modifiers == ['ctrl']:
223::CODE;;self.activated = not self.activated

225::CODE;;elif scancode == 27:
226::CODE;;if self.activated:
227::CODE;;self.activated = False
228::CODE;;return True

230::CODE;;if buttonid == 7:
231::CODE;;self.activated = not self.activated
232::CODE;;if self.activated:
233::CODE;;self.pos = [round(i / 2.0) for i in win.size]

1::CODE;;'''Keybinding
2::CODE;;==========
3::CODE;;This module forces the mapping of some keys to functions:
4::CODE;;* F11: Rotate the Window through 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees
5::CODE;;* Shift + F11: Switches between portrait and landscape on desktops
6::CODE;;* F12: Take a screenshot

8::CODE;;Usage
9::CODE;;-----
10::CODE;;For normal module usage, please see the :mod:`~kivy.modules` documentation.
11::CODE;;The Keybinding module, however, can also be imported and used just
12::CODE;;like a normal python module. This has the added advantage of being
13::CODE;;able to activate and deactivate the module programmatically::
14::CODE;;from kivy.app import App
15::CODE;;from kivy.uix.button import Button

21::CODE;;keybinding.start(Window, button)
22::CODE;;return button
23::CODE;;Demo().run()
24::CODE;;To remove the Keybinding, you can do the following::
25::CODE;;Keybinding.stop(Window, button)
26::CODE;;'''

29::CODE;;def _on_keyboard_handler(instance, key, scancode, codepoint, modifiers):

33::CODE;;instance.rotation += 90
35::CODE;;if platform in ('win', 'linux', 'macosx'):
36::CODE;;instance.rotation = 0
37::CODE;;w, h = instance.size
38::CODE;;w, h = h, w
39::CODE;;instance.size = (w, h)
40::CODE;;def start(win, ctx):
41::CODE;;win.bind(on_keyboard=_on_keyboard_handler)
42::CODE;;def stop(win, ctx):
43::CODE;;win.unbind(on_keyboard=_on_keyboard_handler)

31::CODE;;ctx.statsr[i].pos = (

42::CODE;;if _statsinput > _maxinput:

2::CODE;;Recorder module
3::CODE;;===============
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.1.0
5::CODE;;Create an instance of :class:`~kivy.input.recorder.Recorder`, attach to the
6::CODE;;class, and bind some keys to record / play sequences:
7::CODE;;- F6: play the last record in a loop
8::CODE;;- F7: read the latest recording
9::CODE;;- F8: record input events
10::CODE;;Configuration
11::CODE;;-------------
12::CODE;;.. |attrs| replace:: :attr:`~kivy.input.recorder.Recorder.record_attrs`
13::CODE;;.. |profile_mask| replace::
14::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.input.recorder.Recorder.record_profile_mask`
15::CODE;;:Parameters:
16::CODE;;`attrs`: str, defaults to |attrs| value.
17::CODE;;Attributes to record from the motion event
18::CODE;;`profile_mask`: str, defaults to |profile_mask| value.
19::CODE;;Mask for motion event profile. Used to filter which profile will appear
20::CODE;;in the fake motion event when replayed.
21::CODE;;`filename`: str, defaults to 'recorder.kvi'
22::CODE;;Name of the file to record / play with
23::CODE;;Usage
24::CODE;;-----
25::CODE;;For normal module usage, please see the :mod:`~kivy.modules` documentation.
26::CODE;;'''
27::CODE;;__all__ = ('start', 'stop')
28::CODE;;from kivy.logger import Logger
29::CODE;;from functools import partial
30::CODE;;def replay(recorder, *args):
31::CODE;;if recorder.play:
32::CODE;;return
33::CODE;;else:
34::CODE;;recorder.play = True
35::CODE;;def on_recorder_key(recorder, window, key, *largs):
37::CODE;;if recorder.play:
38::CODE;;Logger.error('Recorder: Cannot start recording while playing.')
39::CODE;;return
40::CODE;;recorder.record = not recorder.record
42::CODE;;if recorder.record:
43::CODE;;Logger.error('Recorder: Cannot start playing while recording.')
44::CODE;;return
45::CODE;;recorder.play = not recorder.play
47::CODE;;if recorder.play:
48::CODE;;recorder.unbind(play=replay)
49::CODE;;else:
50::CODE;;recorder.bind(play=replay)
51::CODE;;recorder.play = True
52::CODE;;def start(win, ctx):
53::CODE;;keys = {}
55::CODE;;value = ctx.config.get('attrs', None)
56::CODE;;if value is not None:
57::CODE;;keys['record_attrs'] = value.split(':')
59::CODE;;value = ctx.config.get('profile_mask', None)
60::CODE;;if value is not None:
61::CODE;;keys['record_profile_mask'] = value.split(':')
63::CODE;;value = ctx.config.get('filename', None)
64::CODE;;if value is not None:
65::CODE;;keys['filename'] = value
66::CODE;;from kivy.input.recorder import Recorder
67::CODE;;ctx.recorder = Recorder(window=win, **keys)
68::CODE;;win.bind(on_key_down=partial(on_recorder_key, ctx.recorder))
69::CODE;;def stop(win, ctx):
70::CODE;;if hasattr(ctx, 'recorder'):
71::CODE;;ctx.recorder.release()

2::CODE;;Touchring
3::CODE;;=========
4::CODE;;Shows rings around every touch on the surface / screen. You can use this module
5::CODE;;to check that you don't have any calibration issues with touches.
6::CODE;;Configuration
7::CODE;;-------------
8::CODE;;:Parameters:
9::CODE;;`image`: str, defaults to '<kivy>/data/images/ring.png'
10::CODE;;Filename of the image to use.
11::CODE;;`scale`: float, defaults to 1.
12::CODE;;Scale of the image.
13::CODE;;`alpha`: float, defaults to 1.
14::CODE;;Opacity of the image.
15::CODE;;Example
16::CODE;;-------
17::CODE;;In your configuration (`~/.kivy/config.ini`), you can add something like
18::CODE;;this::
19::CODE;;[modules]
20::CODE;;touchring = image=mypointer.png,scale=.3,alpha=.7
21::CODE;;'''
22::CODE;;__all__ = ('start', 'stop')
23::CODE;;from kivy.core.image import Image
24::CODE;;from kivy.graphics import Color, Rectangle
25::CODE;;pointer_image = None
26::CODE;;pointer_scale = 1.0
27::CODE;;pointer_alpha = 0.7
28::CODE;;def _touch_down(win, touch):
29::CODE;;ud = touch.ud
30::CODE;;with win.canvas.after:
31::CODE;;ud['tr.color'] = Color(1, 1, 1, pointer_alpha)
32::CODE;;iw, ih = pointer_image.size
33::CODE;;ud['tr.rect'] = Rectangle(
34::CODE;;pos=(
35::CODE;;touch.x - (pointer_image.width / 2. * pointer_scale),
36::CODE;;touch.y - (pointer_image.height / 2. * pointer_scale)),
37::CODE;;size=(iw * pointer_scale, ih * pointer_scale),
38::CODE;;texture=pointer_image.texture)
39::CODE;;def _touch_move(win, touch):
40::CODE;;ud = touch.ud
41::CODE;;if 'tr.rect' not in ud:
42::CODE;;_touch_down(win, touch)
43::CODE;;ud['tr.rect'].pos = (
44::CODE;;touch.x - (pointer_image.width / 2. * pointer_scale),
45::CODE;;touch.y - (pointer_image.height / 2. * pointer_scale))
46::CODE;;def _touch_up(win, touch):
47::CODE;;ud = touch.ud
48::CODE;;if 'tr.rect' in ud:
49::CODE;;remove = win.canvas.after.remove
50::CODE;;remove(ud['tr.color'])
51::CODE;;remove(ud['tr.rect'])
52::CODE;;def start(win, ctx):
54::CODE;;global pointer_image, pointer_scale, pointer_alpha
55::CODE;;pointer_fn = ctx.config.get('image',
56::CODE;;'atlas://data/images/defaulttheme/ring')
57::CODE;;pointer_scale = float(ctx.config.get('scale', 1.0))
58::CODE;;pointer_alpha = float(ctx.config.get('alpha', 1.0))
59::CODE;;pointer_image = Image(pointer_fn)
60::CODE;;win.bind(on_touch_down=_touch_down,
61::CODE;;on_touch_move=_touch_move,
62::CODE;;on_touch_up=_touch_up)
63::CODE;;def stop(win, ctx):
64::CODE;;win.unbind(on_touch_down=_touch_down,
65::CODE;;on_touch_move=_touch_move,
66::CODE;;on_touch_up=_touch_up)

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Multistroke gesture recognizer
3::CODE;;==============================
4::CODE;;.. versionadded::
5::CODE;;1.9.0
6::CODE;;.. warning::
7::CODE;;This is experimental and subject to change as long as this warning notice
8::CODE;;is present.
9::CODE;;See :file:`kivy/examples/demo/multistroke/main.py` for a complete application
10::CODE;;example.
11::CODE;;Conceptual Overview
12::CODE;;-------------------
13::CODE;;This module implements the Protractor gesture recognition algorithm.
14::CODE;;:class:`Recognizer` is the search/database API similar to
15::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.gesture.GestureDatabase`. It maintains a list of
16::CODE;;:class:`MultistrokeGesture` objects and allows you to search for a
17::CODE;;user-input gestures among them.
18::CODE;;:class:`ProgressTracker` tracks the progress of a :meth:`Recognizer.recognize`
19::CODE;;call. It can be used to interact with the running recognizer task, for example
20::CODE;;forcing it to stop half-way, or analyzing results as they arrive.
21::CODE;;:class:`MultistrokeGesture` represents a gesture in the gesture database
22::CODE;;(:attr:`Recognizer.db`). It is a container for :class:`UnistrokeTemplate`
23::CODE;;objects, and implements the heap permute algorithm to automatically generate
24::CODE;;all possible stroke orders (if desired).
25::CODE;;:class:`UnistrokeTemplate` represents a single stroke path. It's typically
26::CODE;;instantiated automatically by :class:`MultistrokeGesture`, but sometimes you
27::CODE;;may need to create them manually.
28::CODE;;:class:`Candidate` represents a user-input gesture that is used to search
29::CODE;;the gesture database for matches. It is normally instantiated automatically
30::CODE;;by calling :meth:`Recognizer.recognize`.
31::CODE;;Usage examples
32::CODE;;--------------
33::CODE;;See :file:`kivy/examples/demo/multistroke/main.py` for a complete application
34::CODE;;example.
35::CODE;;You can bind to events on :class:`Recognizer` to track the state of all
36::CODE;;calls to :meth:`Recognizer.recognize`. The callback function will receive an
37::CODE;;instance of :class:`ProgressTracker` that can be used to analyze and control
38::CODE;;various aspects of the recognition process ::
39::CODE;;from kivy.vector import Vector
40::CODE;;from kivy.multistroke import Recognizer
41::CODE;;gdb = Recognizer()
42::CODE;;def search_start(gdb, pt):
43::CODE;;print("A search is starting with %d tasks" % (pt.tasks))
44::CODE;;def search_stop(gdb, pt):
47::CODE;;best = pt.best
48::CODE;;print("Search ended (%s). Best is %s (score %f, distance %f)" % (
49::CODE;;pt.status, best['name'], best['score'], best['dist'] ))
51::CODE;;gdb.bind(on_search_start=search_start)
52::CODE;;gdb.bind(on_search_complete=search_stop)
56::CODE;;gdb.add_gesture('T', [
57::CODE;;[Vector(30, 7), Vector(103, 7)],
58::CODE;;[Vector(66, 7), Vector(66, 87)]])
61::CODE;;gdb.recognize([
62::CODE;;[Vector(45, 8), Vector(110, 12)],
63::CODE;;[Vector(88, 9), Vector(85, 95)]])
64::CODE;;On the next :class:`~kivy.clock.Clock` tick, the matching process starts
65::CODE;;(and, in this case, completes).
66::CODE;;To track individual calls to :meth:`Recognizer.recognize`, use the return
67::CODE;;value (also a :class:`ProgressTracker` instance) ::
69::CODE;;progress = gdb.recognize([
70::CODE;;[Vector(45, 8), Vector(110, 12)],
71::CODE;;[Vector(88, 9), Vector(85, 95)]])
72::CODE;;progress.bind(on_progress=my_other_callback)
76::CODE;;Algorithm details
77::CODE;;-----------------
78::CODE;;For more information about the matching algorithm, see:
79::CODE;;"Protractor: A fast and accurate gesture recognizer" by Yang Li
80::CODE;;http://yangl.org/pdf/protractor-chi2010.pdf
81::CODE;;"$N-Protractor" by Lisa Anthony and Jacob O. Wobbrock
82::CODE;;http://depts.washington.edu/aimgroup/proj/dollar/ndollar-protractor.pdf
83::CODE;;Some of the code is derived from the JavaScript implementation here:
84::CODE;;http://depts.washington.edu/aimgroup/proj/dollar/ndollar.html
85::CODE;;'''
86::CODE;;__all__ = ('Recognizer', 'ProgressTracker', 'MultistrokeGesture',
87::CODE;;'UnistrokeTemplate', 'Candidate')
88::CODE;;import pickle
89::CODE;;import base64
90::CODE;;import zlib
91::CODE;;from re import match as re_match
92::CODE;;from collections import deque
93::CODE;;from math import sqrt, pi, radians, acos, atan, atan2, pow, floor
94::CODE;;from math import sin as math_sin, cos as math_cos
95::CODE;;from kivy.vector import Vector
96::CODE;;from kivy.clock import Clock
97::CODE;;from kivy.event import EventDispatcher
98::CODE;;from kivy.properties import ListProperty
99::CODE;;from io import BytesIO
102::CODE;;DEFAULT_GPF = 10

105::CODE;;ONEDTHRESHOLD = 0.25
106::CODE;;ORIGIN = Vector(0, 0)

112::CODE;;class Recognizer(EventDispatcher):
113::CODE;;''':class:`Recognizer` provides a gesture database with matching
114::CODE;;facilities.
115::CODE;;:Events:
116::CODE;;`on_search_start`
117::CODE;;Fired when a new search is started using this Recognizer.
118::CODE;;`on_search_complete`
119::CODE;;Fired when a running search ends, for whatever reason.
120::CODE;;(use :data:`ProgressTracker.status` to find out)
121::CODE;;:Properties:
122::CODE;;`db`
123::CODE;;A :class:`ListProperty` that contains the available
124::CODE;;:class:`MultistrokeGesture` objects.
125::CODE;;:attr:`db` is a
126::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.properties.ListProperty` and defaults to []
127::CODE;;'''
128::CODE;;db = ListProperty([])
129::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
130::CODE;;super(Recognizer, self).__init__(**kwargs)
131::CODE;;self.register_event_type('on_search_start')
132::CODE;;self.register_event_type('on_search_complete')
133::CODE;;def filter(self, **kwargs):
134::CODE;;''':meth:`filter` returns a subset of objects in :attr:`self.db`,
135::CODE;;according to given criteria. This is used by many other methods of
136::CODE;;the :class:`Recognizer`; the arguments below can for example be
137::CODE;;used when calling :meth:`Recognizer.recognize` or
138::CODE;;:meth:`Recognizer.export_gesture`. You normally don't need to call
139::CODE;;this directly.
140::CODE;;:Arguments:
141::CODE;;`name`
142::CODE;;Limits the returned list to gestures where
143::CODE;;:attr:`MultistrokeGesture.name` matches given regular
144::CODE;;expression(s). If re.match(name, MultistrokeGesture.name)
145::CODE;;tests true, the gesture is included in the returned list.
146::CODE;;Can be a string or an array of strings ::
147::CODE;;gdb = Recognizer()
150::CODE;;gdb.filter(name='N')
152::CODE;;gdb.filter(name='N$')
154::CODE;;gdb.filter(name=['[Nn]', '(?i)T', '(?i)F'])
155::CODE;;`priority`
156::CODE;;Limits the returned list to gestures with certain
157::CODE;;:attr:`MultistrokeGesture.priority` values. If specified as an
158::CODE;;integer, only gestures with a lower priority are returned. If
159::CODE;;specified as a list (min/max) ::
161::CODE;;gdb.filter(priority=50)
163::CODE;;gdb.filter(priority=[0, 50])
165::CODE;;gdb.filter(priority=[50, 100])
166::CODE;;When this option is used, :attr:`Recognizer.db` is
167::CODE;;automatically sorted according to priority, incurring extra
168::CODE;;cost. You can use `force_priority_sort` to override this
169::CODE;;behavior if your gestures are already sorted according to
170::CODE;;priority.
171::CODE;;`orientation_sensitive`
172::CODE;;Limits the returned list to gestures that are
173::CODE;;orientation sensitive (True), gestures that are not orientation
174::CODE;;sensitive (False) or None (ignore template sensitivity, this is
175::CODE;;the default).
176::CODE;;`numstrokes`
177::CODE;;Limits the returned list to gestures that have the specified
178::CODE;;number of strokes (in :attr:`MultistrokeGesture.strokes`).
179::CODE;;Can be a single integer or a list of integers.
180::CODE;;`numpoints`
181::CODE;;Limits the returned list to gestures that have specific
182::CODE;;:attr:`MultistrokeGesture.numpoints` values. This is provided
183::CODE;;for flexibility, do not use it unless you understand what it
184::CODE;;does. Can be a single integer or a list of integers.
185::CODE;;`force_priority_sort`
186::CODE;;Can be used to override the default sort behavior. Normally
187::CODE;;:class:`MultistrokeGesture` objects are returned in priority
188::CODE;;order if the `priority` option is used. Setting this to True
189::CODE;;will return gestures sorted in priority order, False will
190::CODE;;return in the order gestures were added. None means decide
191::CODE;;automatically (the default).
192::CODE;;.. Note ::
193::CODE;;For improved performance, you can load your gesture
194::CODE;;database in priority order and set this to False when
195::CODE;;calling :meth:`Recognizer.recognize`
196::CODE;;`db`
197::CODE;;Can be set if you want to filter a different list of objects
198::CODE;;than :attr:`Recognizer.db`. You probably don't want to do this;
199::CODE;;it is used internally by :meth:`import_gesture`.
200::CODE;;'''
201::CODE;;have_filters = False
202::CODE;;kwargs_get = kwargs.get
203::CODE;;name = kwargs_get('name', None)
204::CODE;;if name is not None:
205::CODE;;have_filters = True
206::CODE;;if not isinstance(name, list):
207::CODE;;name = [name]
208::CODE;;priority = kwargs_get('priority', None)
209::CODE;;min_p, max_p = None, None
210::CODE;;if priority is not None:
211::CODE;;have_filters = True
212::CODE;;if isinstance(priority, list):
213::CODE;;min_p, max_p = priority
214::CODE;;elif isinstance(priority, int):
215::CODE;;min_p, max_p = None, priority
216::CODE;;numstrokes = kwargs_get('numstrokes', None)
217::CODE;;if numstrokes is not None:
218::CODE;;have_filters = True
219::CODE;;if not isinstance(numstrokes, list):
220::CODE;;numstrokes = [numstrokes]
221::CODE;;numpoints = kwargs_get('numpoints', None)
222::CODE;;if numpoints is not None:
223::CODE;;have_filters = True
224::CODE;;if not isinstance(numpoints, list):
225::CODE;;numpoints = [numpoints]
226::CODE;;orientation_sens = kwargs_get('orientation_sensitive', None)
227::CODE;;if orientation_sens is not None:
228::CODE;;have_filters = True
230::CODE;;force_priority_sort = kwargs.get('force_priority_sort', None)
231::CODE;;force_sort_on = force_priority_sort and True
232::CODE;;force_sort_off = (force_priority_sort is False) and True
233::CODE;;db = kwargs.get('db', None) or self.db
234::CODE;;if (force_sort_on or priority) and not force_sort_off:
235::CODE;;tasklist = sorted(db, key=lambda n: n.priority)
236::CODE;;else:
237::CODE;;tasklist = db
239::CODE;;out = deque()
240::CODE;;if not have_filters:
241::CODE;;out.extend(tasklist)
242::CODE;;return out
243::CODE;;out_append = out.append
244::CODE;;for gesture in tasklist:
245::CODE;;if (orientation_sens is not None and
246::CODE;;orientation_sens != gesture.orientation_sens):
247::CODE;;continue
248::CODE;;if numpoints and gesture.numpoints not in numpoints:
249::CODE;;continue
250::CODE;;if numstrokes and len(gesture.strokes) not in numstrokes:
251::CODE;;continue
252::CODE;;if min_p is not None and gesture.priority < min_p:
253::CODE;;continue
254::CODE;;if max_p is not None and gesture.priority > max_p:
255::CODE;;return out
256::CODE;;if name:
257::CODE;;for f in name:
258::CODE;;if re_match(f, gesture.name):
259::CODE;;out_append(gesture)
260::CODE;;break
261::CODE;;else:
262::CODE;;out_append(gesture)
263::CODE;;return out
264::CODE;;def add_gesture(self, name, strokes, **kwargs):
265::CODE;;'''Add a new gesture to the database. This will instantiate a new
266::CODE;;:class:`MultistrokeGesture` with `strokes` and append it to self.db.
267::CODE;;.. Note ::
268::CODE;;If you already have instantiated a :class:`MultistrokeGesture`
269::CODE;;object and wish to add it, append it to :attr:`Recognizer.db`
270::CODE;;manually.
271::CODE;;'''
272::CODE;;if not strokes:
273::CODE;;return False
274::CODE;;self.db.append(
275::CODE;;MultistrokeGesture(name=name, strokes=strokes, **kwargs)
276::CODE;;)
277::CODE;;return True
278::CODE;;def parse_gesture(self, data):
279::CODE;;'''Parse data formatted by export_gesture(). Returns a list of
280::CODE;;:class:`MultistrokeGesture` objects. This is used internally by
281::CODE;;:meth:`import_gesture`, you normally don't need to call this
282::CODE;;directly.'''
283::CODE;;io = BytesIO(zlib.decompress(base64.b64decode(data)))
284::CODE;;p = pickle.Unpickler(io)
285::CODE;;multistrokes = []
286::CODE;;ms_append = multistrokes.append
287::CODE;;for multistroke in p.load():
288::CODE;;strokes = multistroke['strokes']
289::CODE;;multistroke['strokes'] = [[Vector(
290::CODE;;x, y) for x, y in line] for line in strokes]
291::CODE;;ms_append(MultistrokeGesture(**multistroke))
292::CODE;;return multistrokes
294::CODE;;def export_gesture(self, filename=None, **kwargs):
295::CODE;;'''Export a list of :class:`MultistrokeGesture` objects. Outputs a
296::CODE;;base64-encoded string that can be decoded to a Python list with
297::CODE;;the :meth:`parse_gesture` function or imported directly to
298::CODE;;:attr:`self.db` using :meth:`Recognizer.import_gesture`. If
299::CODE;;`filename` is specified, the output is written to disk, otherwise
300::CODE;;returned.
301::CODE;;This method accepts optional :meth:`Recognizer.filter` arguments.
302::CODE;;'''
303::CODE;;io = BytesIO()
304::CODE;;p = pickle.Pickler(io, protocol=0)
305::CODE;;multistrokes = []

368::CODE;;def recognize(self, strokes, goodscore=None, timeout=0, delay=0, **kwargs):
369::CODE;;'''Search for gestures matching `strokes`. Returns a
370::CODE;;:class:`ProgressTracker` instance.
371::CODE;;This method accepts optional :meth:`Recognizer.filter` arguments.
372::CODE;;:Arguments:
373::CODE;;`strokes`
374::CODE;;A list of stroke paths (list of lists of
375::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.vector.Vector` objects) that will be matched
376::CODE;;against gestures in the database. Can also be a
377::CODE;;:class:`Candidate` instance.
378::CODE;;.. Warning ::
379::CODE;;If you manually supply a :class:`Candidate` that has a
380::CODE;;skip-flag, make sure that the correct filter arguments
381::CODE;;are set. Otherwise the system will attempt to load vectors
382::CODE;;that have not been computed. For example, if you set
383::CODE;;`skip_bounded` and do not set `orientation_sensitive` to
384::CODE;;False, it will raise an exception if an
385::CODE;;orientation_sensitive :class:`UnistrokeTemplate`
386::CODE;;is encountered.
387::CODE;;`goodscore`
388::CODE;;If this is set (between 0.0 - 1.0) and a gesture score is
389::CODE;;equal to or higher than the specified value, the search is
390::CODE;;immediately halted and the on_search_complete event is
391::CODE;;fired (+ the on_complete event of the associated
392::CODE;;:class:`ProgressTracker` instance). Default is None (disabled).
393::CODE;;`timeout`
394::CODE;;Specifies a timeout (in seconds) for when the search is
395::CODE;;aborted and the results returned. This option applies only
396::CODE;;when `max_gpf` is not 0. Default value is 0, meaning all
397::CODE;;gestures in the database will be tested, no matter how long
398::CODE;;it takes.
399::CODE;;`max_gpf`
400::CODE;;Specifies the maximum number of :class:`MultistrokeGesture`
401::CODE;;objects that can be processed per frame. When exceeded, will
402::CODE;;cause the search to halt and resume work in the next frame.
403::CODE;;Setting to 0 will complete the search immediately (and block
404::CODE;;the UI).
405::CODE;;.. Warning ::
406::CODE;;This does not limit the number of
407::CODE;;:class:`UnistrokeTemplate` objects matched! If a single
408::CODE;;gesture has a million templates, they will all be
409::CODE;;processed in a single frame with max_gpf=1!
410::CODE;;`delay`
411::CODE;;Sets an optional delay between each run of the recognizer
412::CODE;;loop. Normally, a run is scheduled for the next frame until
413::CODE;;the tasklist is exhausted. If you set this, there will be an
414::CODE;;additional delay between each run (specified in seconds).
415::CODE;;Default is 0, resume in the next frame.
416::CODE;;`force_numpoints`
417::CODE;;forces all templates (and candidate) to be prepared to a
418::CODE;;certain number of points. This can be useful for example if
419::CODE;;you are evaluating templates for optimal n (do not use this
420::CODE;;unless you understand what it does).
421::CODE;;'''
422::CODE;;GPF = kwargs.get('max_gpf', DEFAULT_GPF)
424::CODE;;tasklist = self.filter(**kwargs)
426::CODE;;cand = self._candidate(strokes)
427::CODE;;result = ProgressTracker(cand, len(tasklist))
430::CODE;;if not tasklist:
431::CODE;;result.status = 'complete'
432::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_search_complete', result)
433::CODE;;def result_hack(dt):
434::CODE;;result.dispatch('on_complete')
435::CODE;;Clock.schedule_once(result_hack)
436::CODE;;return result
438::CODE;;def _recognize_tick(dt):
439::CODE;;start_gc = result._completed
440::CODE;;stop_now = False
441::CODE;;while not stop_now and (tasklist and not result._break_flag) and \
442::CODE;;(not GPF or (result._completed - start_gc < GPF)):
443::CODE;;if (timeout and
444::CODE;;Clock.get_time() - result._start_time >= timeout):
445::CODE;;result.status = 'timeout'
446::CODE;;stop_now = True
447::CODE;;break
449::CODE;;gesture = tasklist.popleft()
450::CODE;;tpl, d, res, mos = gesture.match_candidate(
451::CODE;;cand, **kwargs)
452::CODE;;if tpl is not None:
453::CODE;;score = result._add_result(gesture, d, tpl, res)
454::CODE;;if goodscore is not None and score >= goodscore:
455::CODE;;result.status = 'goodscore'
456::CODE;;stop_now = True
457::CODE;;result._match_ops += mos
458::CODE;;result._completed += 1
459::CODE;;result.dispatch('on_progress')
461::CODE;;def _dispatch():
462::CODE;;result.dispatch('on_complete')
463::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_search_complete', result)
464::CODE;;return False
466::CODE;;if not tasklist:
467::CODE;;result.status = 'complete'
468::CODE;;return _dispatch()
469::CODE;;elif result._break_flag:
470::CODE;;result.status = 'stop'
471::CODE;;return _dispatch()
472::CODE;;elif stop_now:
473::CODE;;return _dispatch()
474::CODE;;else:
475::CODE;;Clock.schedule_once(_recognize_tick, delay)
476::CODE;;return True
478::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_search_start', result)
479::CODE;;if not GPF:
480::CODE;;_recognize_tick(0)
481::CODE;;else:
482::CODE;;Clock.schedule_once(_recognize_tick, 0)
483::CODE;;return result

510::CODE;;class ProgressTracker(EventDispatcher):
511::CODE;;'''Represents an ongoing (or completed) search operation. Instantiated and
512::CODE;;returned by the :meth:`Recognizer.recognize` method when it is called. The
513::CODE;;`results` attribute is a dictionary that is updated as the recognition
514::CODE;;operation progresses.
515::CODE;;.. Note ::
516::CODE;;You do not need to instantiate this class.
517::CODE;;:Arguments:
518::CODE;;`candidate`
519::CODE;;:class:`Candidate` object to be evaluated
520::CODE;;`tasks`
521::CODE;;Total number of gestures in tasklist (to test against)
522::CODE;;:Events:
523::CODE;;`on_progress`
524::CODE;;Fired for every gesture that is processed
525::CODE;;`on_result`
526::CODE;;Fired when a new result is added, and it is the first match
527::CODE;;for the `name` so far, or a consecutive match with better score.
528::CODE;;`on_complete`
529::CODE;;Fired when the search is completed, for whatever reason.
530::CODE;;(use `ProgressTracker.status` to find out)
531::CODE;;:Attributes:
532::CODE;;`results`
533::CODE;;A dictionary of all results (so far). The key is the name of the
534::CODE;;gesture (ie :attr:`UnistrokeTemplate.name` usually inherited from
535::CODE;;:class:`MultistrokeGesture`). Each item in the dictionary is a
536::CODE;;dict with the following entries:
537::CODE;;`name`
538::CODE;;Name of the matched template (redundant)
539::CODE;;`score`
540::CODE;;Computed score from 1.0 (perfect match) to 0.0
541::CODE;;`dist`
542::CODE;;Cosine distance from candidate to template (low=closer)
543::CODE;;`gesture`
544::CODE;;The :class:`MultistrokeGesture` object that was matched
545::CODE;;`best_template`
546::CODE;;Index of the best matching template (in
547::CODE;;:attr:`MultistrokeGesture.templates`)
548::CODE;;`template_results`
549::CODE;;List of distances for all templates. The list index
550::CODE;;corresponds to a :class:`UnistrokeTemplate` index in
551::CODE;;gesture.templates.
552::CODE;;`status`
553::CODE;;`search`
554::CODE;;Currently working
555::CODE;;`stop`
556::CODE;;Was stopped by the user (:meth:`stop` called)
557::CODE;;`timeout`
558::CODE;;A timeout occurred (specified as `timeout=` to recognize())
559::CODE;;`goodscore`
560::CODE;;The search was stopped early because a gesture with a high
561::CODE;;enough score was found (specified as `goodscore=` to
562::CODE;;recognize())
563::CODE;;`complete`
564::CODE;;The search is complete (all gestures matching filters were
565::CODE;;tested)
566::CODE;;'''

575::CODE;;self._break_flag = False
577::CODE;;self.register_event_type('on_complete')
578::CODE;;self.register_event_type('on_progress')
580::CODE;;self.register_event_type('on_result')
581::CODE;;super(ProgressTracker, self).__init__(**kwargs)
582::CODE;;@property

585::CODE;;is a Python property.'''
586::CODE;;if not self.tasks:
587::CODE;;return 1
