639::CODE;;class MultistrokeGesture(object):
640::CODE;;''':class:`MultistrokeGesture` represents a gesture. It maintains a set of
641::CODE;;`strokes` and generates unistroke (ie :class:`UnistrokeTemplate`)
642::CODE;;permutations that are used for evaluating candidates against this gesture
643::CODE;;later.
644::CODE;;:Arguments:
645::CODE;;`name`
646::CODE;;Identifies the name of the gesture - it is returned to you in the
647::CODE;;results of a :meth:`Recognizer.recognize` search. You can have any
648::CODE;;number of MultistrokeGesture objects with the same name; many
649::CODE;;definitions of one gesture. The same name is given to all the
650::CODE;;generated unistroke permutations. Required, no default.
651::CODE;;`strokes`
652::CODE;;A list of paths that represents the gesture. A path is a list of
653::CODE;;Vector objects::
654::CODE;;gesture = MultistrokeGesture('my_gesture', strokes=[
658::CODE;;])
659::CODE;;For template matching purposes, all the strokes are combined to a
660::CODE;;single list (unistroke). You should still specify the strokes
661::CODE;;individually, and set `stroke_sensitive` True (whenever possible).
662::CODE;;Once you do this, unistroke permutations are immediately generated
663::CODE;;and stored in `self.templates` for later, unless you set the
664::CODE;;`permute` flag to False.
665::CODE;;`priority`
666::CODE;;Determines when :func:`Recognizer.recognize` will attempt to match
667::CODE;;this template, lower priorities are evaluated first (only if
668::CODE;;a priority `filter` is used). You should use lower priority on
669::CODE;;gestures that are more likely to match. For example, set user
670::CODE;;templates at lower number than generic templates. Default is 100.
671::CODE;;`numpoints`
672::CODE;;Determines the number of points this gesture should be resampled to
673::CODE;;(for matching purposes). The default is 16.
674::CODE;;`stroke_sensitive`
675::CODE;;Determines if the number of strokes (paths) in this gesture is
676::CODE;;required to be the same in the candidate (user input) gesture
677::CODE;;during matching. If this is False, candidates will always be
678::CODE;;evaluated, disregarding the number of strokes. Default is True.
679::CODE;;`orientation_sensitive`
680::CODE;;Determines if this gesture is orientation sensitive. If True,
681::CODE;;aligns the indicative orientation with the one of eight base
682::CODE;;orientations that requires least rotation. Default is True.
683::CODE;;`angle_similarity`
684::CODE;;This is used by the :func:`Recognizer.recognize` function when a
685::CODE;;candidate is evaluated against this gesture. If the angles between
686::CODE;;them are too far off, the template is considered a non-match.
687::CODE;;Default is 30.0 (degrees)
688::CODE;;`permute`
689::CODE;;If False, do not use Heap Permute algorithm to generate different
690::CODE;;stroke orders when instantiated. If you set this to False, a
691::CODE;;single UnistrokeTemplate built from `strokes` is used.
692::CODE;;'''
693::CODE;;def __init__(self, name, strokes=None, **kwargs):
694::CODE;;self.name = name
695::CODE;;self.priority = kwargs.get('priority', 100)
696::CODE;;self.numpoints = kwargs.get('numpoints', 16)
697::CODE;;self.stroke_sens = kwargs.get('stroke_sensitive', True)
698::CODE;;self.orientation_sens = kwargs.get('orientation_sensitive', True)
699::CODE;;self.angle_similarity = kwargs.get('angle_similarity', 30.0)
700::CODE;;self.strokes = []
701::CODE;;if strokes is not None:
702::CODE;;self.strokes = strokes
703::CODE;;if kwargs.get('permute', True):
704::CODE;;self.permute()
705::CODE;;else:
706::CODE;;self.templates = [UnistrokeTemplate(name,
707::CODE;;points=[i for sub in strokes for i in sub],
708::CODE;;numpoints=self.numpoints,
709::CODE;;orientation_sensitive=self.orientation_sens)]
710::CODE;;def angle_similarity_threshold(self):
711::CODE;;return radians(self.angle_similarity)
712::CODE;;def add_stroke(self, stroke, permute=False):
713::CODE;;'''Add a stroke to the self.strokes list. If `permute` is True, the
714::CODE;;:meth:`permute` method is called to generate new unistroke templates'''
715::CODE;;self.strokes.append(stroke)
716::CODE;;if permute:
717::CODE;;self.permute()
718::CODE;;def get_distance(self, cand, tpl, numpoints=None):
719::CODE;;'''Compute the distance from this Candidate to a UnistrokeTemplate.
720::CODE;;Returns the Cosine distance between the stroke paths.
721::CODE;;`numpoints` will prepare both the UnistrokeTemplate and Candidate path
722::CODE;;to n points (when necessary), you probably don't want to do this.
723::CODE;;'''
724::CODE;;n = numpoints
725::CODE;;if n is None or n < 2:
726::CODE;;n = self.numpoints
728::CODE;;v1 = tpl.get_vector(n)
729::CODE;;v2 = cand.get_protractor_vector(n, tpl.orientation_sens)
730::CODE;;a = 0.0
731::CODE;;b = 0.0
732::CODE;;for i in range(0, len(v1), 2):
733::CODE;;a += (v1[i] * v2[i]) + (v1[i + 1] * v2[i + 1])
734::CODE;;b += (v1[i] * v2[i + 1]) - (v1[i + 1] * v2[i])
735::CODE;;angle = atan(b / a)
742::CODE;;result = a * math_cos(angle) + b * math_sin(angle)
744::CODE;;if result >= 1:
745::CODE;;result = 1
747::CODE;;result = -1
748::CODE;;return acos(result)
749::CODE;;def match_candidate(self, cand, **kwargs):
750::CODE;;'''Match a given candidate against this MultistrokeGesture object. Will
751::CODE;;test against all templates and report results as a list of four
752::CODE;;items:
753::CODE;;`index 0`
754::CODE;;Best matching template's index (in self.templates)
755::CODE;;`index 1`
756::CODE;;Computed distance from the template to the candidate path
757::CODE;;`index 2`
758::CODE;;List of distances for all templates. The list index
759::CODE;;corresponds to a :class:`UnistrokeTemplate` index in
760::CODE;;self.templates.
761::CODE;;`index 3`
762::CODE;;Counter for the number of performed matching operations, ie
763::CODE;;templates matched against the candidate
764::CODE;;'''
765::CODE;;best_d = float('infinity')
766::CODE;;best_tpl = None
767::CODE;;mos = 0
768::CODE;;out = []
769::CODE;;if (self.stroke_sens and len(self.strokes) != len(cand.strokes)):
770::CODE;;return (best_tpl, best_d, out, mos)
771::CODE;;skip_bounded = cand.skip_bounded
772::CODE;;skip_invariant = cand.skip_invariant
773::CODE;;get_distance = self.get_distance
774::CODE;;ang_sim_threshold = self.angle_similarity_threshold()
775::CODE;;for idx, tpl in enumerate(self.templates):
780::CODE;;if tpl.orientation_sens:
781::CODE;;if skip_bounded:
782::CODE;;continue
783::CODE;;elif skip_invariant:
784::CODE;;continue
788::CODE;;mos += 1
793::CODE;;n = kwargs.get('force_numpoints', tpl.numpoints)
795::CODE;;ang_sim = cand.get_angle_similarity(tpl, numpoints=n)
796::CODE;;if ang_sim > ang_sim_threshold:
797::CODE;;continue
799::CODE;;d = get_distance(cand, tpl, numpoints=n)
800::CODE;;out.append(d)
801::CODE;;if d < best_d:
802::CODE;;best_d = d
803::CODE;;best_tpl = idx
804::CODE;;return (best_tpl, best_d, out, mos)
805::CODE;;def permute(self):
806::CODE;;'''Generate all possible unistroke permutations from self.strokes and
807::CODE;;save the resulting list of UnistrokeTemplate objects in self.templates.
808::CODE;;Quote from http://faculty.washington.edu/wobbrock/pubs/gi-10.2.pdf ::
809::CODE;;We use Heap Permute [16] (p. 179) to generate all stroke orders
810::CODE;;in a multistroke gesture. Then, to generate stroke directions for
811::CODE;;each order, we treat each component stroke as a dichotomous
812::CODE;;[0,1] variable. There are 2^N combinations for N strokes, so we
813::CODE;;convert the decimal values 0 to 2^N-1, inclusive, to binary
814::CODE;;representations and regard each bit as indicating forward (0) or
815::CODE;;reverse (1). This algorithm is often used to generate truth tables
816::CODE;;in propositional logic.
817::CODE;;See section 4.1: "$N Algorithm" of the linked paper for details.
818::CODE;;.. Warning ::
819::CODE;;Using heap permute for gestures with more than 3 strokes
820::CODE;;can result in very large number of templates (a 9-stroke
821::CODE;;gesture = 38 million templates). If you are dealing with
822::CODE;;these types of gestures, you should manually compose
823::CODE;;all the desired stroke orders.
824::CODE;;'''
826::CODE;;self._order = [i for i in range(0, len(self.strokes))]
828::CODE;;self._orders = []
829::CODE;;self._heap_permute(len(self.strokes))
830::CODE;;del self._order
832::CODE;;self.templates = [UnistrokeTemplate(
833::CODE;;self.name,
834::CODE;;points=permutation,
835::CODE;;numpoints=self.numpoints,
836::CODE;;orientation_sensitive=self.orientation_sens
837::CODE;;) for permutation in self._make_unistrokes()]
838::CODE;;del self._orders
839::CODE;;def _heap_permute(self, n):
841::CODE;;self_order = self._order
842::CODE;;if n == 1:
843::CODE;;self._orders.append(self_order[:])
844::CODE;;else:
845::CODE;;i = 0
846::CODE;;for i in range(0, n):
847::CODE;;self._heap_permute(n - 1)
848::CODE;;if n % 2 == 1:
849::CODE;;tmp = self_order[0]
850::CODE;;self_order[0] = self_order[n - 1]
851::CODE;;self_order[n - 1] = tmp
852::CODE;;else:
853::CODE;;tmp = self_order[i]
854::CODE;;self_order[i] = self_order[n - 1]
855::CODE;;self_order[n - 1] = tmp
856::CODE;;def _make_unistrokes(self):
858::CODE;;unistrokes = []
859::CODE;;unistrokes_append = unistrokes.append
860::CODE;;self_strokes = self.strokes
861::CODE;;for r in self._orders:
862::CODE;;b = 0
864::CODE;;unistroke = []
865::CODE;;unistroke_append = unistroke.append
866::CODE;;for i in range(0, len(r)):
867::CODE;;pts = self_strokes[r[i]][:]
869::CODE;;pts.reverse()
870::CODE;;unistroke_append(None)
871::CODE;;unistroke[-1:] = pts
872::CODE;;unistrokes_append(unistroke)
873::CODE;;b += 1
874::CODE;;return unistrokes
878::CODE;;class UnistrokeTemplate(object):
879::CODE;;'''Represents a (uni)stroke path as a list of Vectors. Normally, this class
880::CODE;;is instantiated by MultistrokeGesture and not by the programmer directly.
881::CODE;;However, it is possible to manually compose UnistrokeTemplate objects.
882::CODE;;:Arguments:
883::CODE;;`name`
884::CODE;;Identifies the name of the gesture. This is normally inherited from
885::CODE;;the parent MultistrokeGesture object when a template is generated.
886::CODE;;`points`
887::CODE;;A list of points that represents a unistroke path. This is normally
888::CODE;;one of the possible stroke order permutations from a
889::CODE;;MultistrokeGesture.
890::CODE;;`numpoints`
891::CODE;;The number of points this template should (ideally) be resampled to
892::CODE;;before the matching process. The default is 16, but you can use a
893::CODE;;template-specific settings if that improves results.
894::CODE;;`orientation_sensitive`
895::CODE;;Determines if this template is orientation sensitive (True) or
896::CODE;;fully rotation invariant (False). The default is True.
897::CODE;;.. Note::
898::CODE;;You will get an exception if you set a skip-flag and then attempt to
899::CODE;;retrieve those vectors.
900::CODE;;'''
901::CODE;;def __init__(self, name, points=None, **kwargs):
902::CODE;;self.name = name
903::CODE;;self.numpoints = kwargs.get('numpoints', 16)
904::CODE;;self.orientation_sens = kwargs.get('orientation_sensitive', True)
905::CODE;;self.db = {}
906::CODE;;self.points = []
907::CODE;;if points is not None:
908::CODE;;self.points = points
909::CODE;;def add_point(self, p):
910::CODE;;'''Add a point to the unistroke/path. This invalidates all previously
911::CODE;;computed vectors.'''
912::CODE;;self.points.append(p)
914::CODE;;self.db = {}
916::CODE;;def _get_db_key(self, key, numpoints=None):
917::CODE;;n = numpoints and numpoints or self.numpoints
918::CODE;;if n not in self.db:
919::CODE;;self.prepare(n)
920::CODE;;return self.db[n][key]
921::CODE;;def get_start_unit_vector(self, numpoints=None):
922::CODE;;return self._get_db_key('startvector', numpoints)
923::CODE;;def get_vector(self, numpoints=None):
924::CODE;;return self._get_db_key('vector', numpoints)
925::CODE;;def get_points(self, numpoints=None):
926::CODE;;return self._get_db_key('points', numpoints)
927::CODE;;def prepare(self, numpoints=None):
928::CODE;;'''This function prepares the UnistrokeTemplate for matching given a
929::CODE;;target number of points (for resample). 16 is optimal.'''
930::CODE;;if not self.points:
931::CODE;;raise MultistrokeError('prepare() called without self.points')
933::CODE;;n = numpoints or self.numpoints
934::CODE;;if not n or n < 2:
935::CODE;;raise MultistrokeError('prepare() called with invalid numpoints')
936::CODE;;p = resample(self.points, n)
937::CODE;;radians = indicative_angle(p)
938::CODE;;p = rotate_by(p, -radians)
939::CODE;;p = scale_dim(p, SQUARESIZE, ONEDTHRESHOLD)
940::CODE;;if self.orientation_sens:
942::CODE;;p = translate_to(p, ORIGIN)
947::CODE;;self.db[n] = {
949::CODE;;'startvector': start_unit_vector(p, (n / 8)),
950::CODE;;'vector': vectorize(p, self.orientation_sens)
951::CODE;;}
955::CODE;;class Candidate(object):
956::CODE;;'''Represents a set of unistroke paths of user input, ie data to be matched
957::CODE;;against a :class:`UnistrokeTemplate` object using the Protractor algorithm.
958::CODE;;By default, data is precomputed to match both rotation bounded and fully
959::CODE;;invariant :class:`UnistrokeTemplate` objects.
960::CODE;;:Arguments:
961::CODE;;`strokes`
962::CODE;;See :data:`MultistrokeGesture.strokes` for format example. The
963::CODE;;Candidate strokes are simply combined to a unistroke in the order
964::CODE;;given. The idea is that this will match one of the unistroke
965::CODE;;permutations in `MultistrokeGesture.templates`.
966::CODE;;`numpoints`
967::CODE;;The Candidate's default N; this is only for a fallback, it is not
968::CODE;;normally used since n is driven by the UnistrokeTemplate we are
969::CODE;;being compared to.
970::CODE;;`skip_bounded`
971::CODE;;If True, do not generate/store rotation bounded vectors
972::CODE;;`skip_invariant`
973::CODE;;If True, do not generate/store rotation invariant vectors
974::CODE;;Note that you WILL get errors if you set a skip-flag and then attempt to
975::CODE;;retrieve the data.'''
976::CODE;;def __init__(self, strokes=None, numpoints=16, **kwargs):
977::CODE;;self.skip_invariant = kwargs.get('skip_invariant', False)
978::CODE;;self.skip_bounded = kwargs.get('skip_bounded', False)
979::CODE;;self.numpoints = numpoints
980::CODE;;self.db = {}
981::CODE;;self.strokes = []
982::CODE;;if strokes is not None:
983::CODE;;self.strokes = strokes
984::CODE;;def add_stroke(self, stroke):
985::CODE;;'''Add a stroke to the candidate; this will invalidate all
986::CODE;;previously computed vectors'''
987::CODE;;self.points.append(stroke)
988::CODE;;self.db = {}
990::CODE;;def _get_db_key(self, key, numpoints, orientation_sens):
991::CODE;;n = numpoints and numpoints or self.numpoints
992::CODE;;if n not in self.db:
993::CODE;;self.prepare(n)
994::CODE;;prefix = orientation_sens and 'bound_' or 'inv_'
995::CODE;;return self.db[n][prefix + key]
996::CODE;;def get_start_unit_vector(self, numpoints, orientation_sens):
997::CODE;;'''(Internal use only) Get the start vector for this Candidate,
998::CODE;;with the path resampled to `numpoints` points. This is the first
999::CODE;;step in the matching process. It is compared to a
1000::CODE;;UnistrokeTemplate object's start vector to determine angle
1001::CODE;;similarity.'''
1002::CODE;;return self._get_db_key('startvector', numpoints, orientation_sens)
1003::CODE;;def get_protractor_vector(self, numpoints, orientation_sens):
1004::CODE;;'''(Internal use only) Return vector for comparing to a
1005::CODE;;UnistrokeTemplate with Protractor'''
1006::CODE;;return self._get_db_key('vector', numpoints, orientation_sens)
1007::CODE;;def get_angle_similarity(self, tpl, **kwargs):
1008::CODE;;'''(Internal use only) Compute the angle similarity between this
1009::CODE;;Candidate and a UnistrokeTemplate object. Returns a number that
1010::CODE;;represents the angle similarity (lower is more similar).'''
1011::CODE;;n = kwargs.get('numpoints', self.numpoints)
1013::CODE;;v1x, v1y = self.get_start_unit_vector(n, tpl.orientation_sens)
1014::CODE;;v2x, v2y = tpl.get_start_unit_vector(n)
1015::CODE;;n = (v1x * v2x + v1y * v2y)
1018::CODE;;if n >= 1:
1019::CODE;;return 0.0
1020::CODE;;if n <= -1:
1021::CODE;;return pi
1022::CODE;;return acos(n)
1023::CODE;;def prepare(self, numpoints=None):
1024::CODE;;'''Prepare the Candidate vectors. self.strokes is combined to a single
1025::CODE;;unistroke (connected end-to-end), resampled to :attr:`numpoints`
1026::CODE;;points, and then the vectors are calculated and stored in self.db (for
1027::CODE;;use by `get_distance` and `get_angle_similarity`)'''
1028::CODE;;n = numpoints and numpoints or self.numpoints
1030::CODE;;points = [i for sub in self.strokes for i in sub]
1031::CODE;;points = resample(points, n)
1032::CODE;;radians = indicative_angle(points)
1033::CODE;;points = rotate_by(points, -radians)
1034::CODE;;points = scale_dim(points, SQUARESIZE, ONEDTHRESHOLD)
1036::CODE;;angidx = n / 8
1037::CODE;;cand = {}
1039::CODE;;if not self.skip_invariant:
1040::CODE;;inv_points = translate_to(points, ORIGIN)
1041::CODE;;cand['inv_startvector'] = start_unit_vector(inv_points, angidx)
1042::CODE;;cand['inv_vector'] = vectorize(inv_points, False)
1044::CODE;;if not self.skip_bounded:
1046::CODE;;bound_points = translate_to(bound_points, ORIGIN)
1047::CODE;;cand['bound_startvector'] = start_unit_vector(bound_points, angidx)
1048::CODE;;cand['bound_vector'] = vectorize(bound_points, True)
1049::CODE;;self.db[n] = cand
1054::CODE;;def resample(points, n):
1056::CODE;;if not len(points) or not n or n < 2:
1057::CODE;;raise MultistrokeError('resample() called with invalid arguments')
1058::CODE;;interval = path_length(points) / (n - 1)
1059::CODE;;D = 0.0
1060::CODE;;i = 1
1061::CODE;;newpoints = [points[0]]
1062::CODE;;workpoints = points[:]
1063::CODE;;newpoints_len = 1
1064::CODE;;workpoints_len = len(points)
1065::CODE;;new_append = newpoints.append
1066::CODE;;work_insert = workpoints.insert
1067::CODE;;while i < len(workpoints):
1068::CODE;;p1 = workpoints[i - 1]
1069::CODE;;p2 = workpoints[i]
1070::CODE;;d = distance(p1, p2)
1071::CODE;;if D + d >= interval:
1072::CODE;;qx = p1[0] + ((interval - D) / d) * (p2[0] - p1[0])
1073::CODE;;qy = p1[1] + ((interval - D) / d) * (p2[1] - p1[1])
1074::CODE;;q = Vector(qx, qy)
1075::CODE;;new_append(q)
1077::CODE;;newpoints_len += 1
1078::CODE;;workpoints_len += 1
1079::CODE;;D = 0.0
1080::CODE;;else:
1081::CODE;;D += d
1082::CODE;;i += 1
1084::CODE;;if newpoints_len < n:
1085::CODE;;new_append(points[-1])
1086::CODE;;return newpoints
1087::CODE;;def indicative_angle(points):
1088::CODE;;cx, cy = centroid(points)
1089::CODE;;return atan2(cy - points[0][1], cx - points[0][0])
1090::CODE;;def rotate_by(points, radians):
1092::CODE;;cx, cy = centroid(points)
1093::CODE;;cos = math_cos(radians)
1094::CODE;;sin = math_sin(radians)
1095::CODE;;newpoints = []
1096::CODE;;newpoints_append = newpoints.append
1097::CODE;;for i in range(0, len(points)):
1098::CODE;;qx = (points[i][0] - cx) * cos - (points[i][1] - cy) * sin + cx
1099::CODE;;qy = (points[i][0] - cx) * sin + (points[i][1] - cy) * cos + cy
1100::CODE;;newpoints_append(Vector(qx, qy))
1101::CODE;;return newpoints
1102::CODE;;def scale_dim(points, size, oneDratio):
1103::CODE;;bbox_x, bbox_y, bbox_w, bbox_h = bounding_box(points)
1104::CODE;;if bbox_h == 0 or bbox_w == 0:
1105::CODE;;raise MultistrokeError(
1106::CODE;;'scale_dim() called with invalid points: h:{}, w:{}'
1107::CODE;;.format(bbox_h, bbox_w))
1109::CODE;;uniformly = min(bbox_w / bbox_h, bbox_h / bbox_w) <= oneDratio
1110::CODE;;if uniformly:
1111::CODE;;qx_size = size / max(bbox_w, bbox_h)
1112::CODE;;qy_size = size / max(bbox_w, bbox_h)
1113::CODE;;else:
1114::CODE;;qx_size = size / bbox_w
1115::CODE;;qy_size = size / bbox_h
1116::CODE;;newpoints = []
1117::CODE;;newpoints_append = newpoints.append
1118::CODE;;for p in points:
1119::CODE;;qx = p[0] * qx_size
1120::CODE;;qy = p[1] * qy_size
1121::CODE;;newpoints_append(Vector(qx, qy))
1122::CODE;;return newpoints
1123::CODE;;def translate_to(points, pt):
1125::CODE;;cx, cy = centroid(points)
1126::CODE;;ptx, pty = pt
1127::CODE;;newpoints = []
1128::CODE;;for p in points:
1129::CODE;;qx = p[0] + ptx - cx
1130::CODE;;qy = p[1] + pty - cy
1131::CODE;;newpoints.append(Vector(qx, qy))
1132::CODE;;return newpoints
1133::CODE;;def vectorize(points, use_bounded_rotation_invariance):
1135::CODE;;cos = 1.0
1136::CODE;;sin = 0.0
1137::CODE;;if use_bounded_rotation_invariance:
1138::CODE;;ang = atan2(points[0][1], points[0][0])
1139::CODE;;bo = (pi / 4.) * floor((ang + pi / 8.) / (pi / 4.))
1140::CODE;;cos = math_cos(bo - ang)
1141::CODE;;sin = math_sin(bo - ang)
1142::CODE;;sum = 0.0
1143::CODE;;vector = []
1144::CODE;;vector_len = 0
1145::CODE;;vector_append = vector.append
1146::CODE;;for px, py in points:
1147::CODE;;newx = px * cos - py * sin
1148::CODE;;newy = py * cos + px * sin
1149::CODE;;vector_append(newx)
1150::CODE;;vector_append(newy)
1151::CODE;;vector_len += 2
1152::CODE;;sum += newx ** 2 + newy ** 2
1153::CODE;;magnitude = sqrt(sum)
1154::CODE;;for i in range(0, vector_len):
1155::CODE;;vector[i] /= magnitude
1156::CODE;;return vector
1157::CODE;;def centroid(points):
1158::CODE;;x = 0.0
1159::CODE;;y = 0.0
1160::CODE;;points_len = len(points)
1161::CODE;;for i in range(0, points_len):
1162::CODE;;x += points[i][0]
1163::CODE;;y += points[i][1]
1164::CODE;;x /= points_len
1165::CODE;;y /= points_len
1166::CODE;;return Vector(x, y)
1167::CODE;;def bounding_box(points):
1168::CODE;;minx = float('infinity')
1169::CODE;;miny = float('infinity')
1170::CODE;;maxx = float('-infinity')
1171::CODE;;maxy = float('-infinity')
1172::CODE;;for px, py in points:
1173::CODE;;if px < minx:
1174::CODE;;minx = px
1175::CODE;;if px > maxx:
1176::CODE;;maxx = px
1177::CODE;;if py < miny:
1178::CODE;;miny = py
1179::CODE;;if py > maxy:
1180::CODE;;maxy = py
1181::CODE;;return (minx, miny, maxx - minx + 1, maxy - miny + 1)
1182::CODE;;def path_length(points):
1183::CODE;;d = 0.0
1184::CODE;;for i in range(1, len(points)):
1185::CODE;;d += distance(points[i - 1], points[i])
1186::CODE;;return d
1187::CODE;;def distance(p1, p2):
1188::CODE;;dx = p2[0] - p1[0]
1189::CODE;;dy = p2[1] - p1[1]
1190::CODE;;return sqrt(dx ** 2 + dy ** 2)
1191::CODE;;def start_unit_vector(points, index):
1192::CODE;;i = int(index)
1193::CODE;;vx, vy = points[i][0] - points[0][0], points[i][1] - points[0][1]
1194::CODE;;length = sqrt(vx ** 2 + vy ** 2)
1195::CODE;;return Vector(vx / length, vy / length)
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Network support
3::CODE;;===============
4::CODE;;Kivy currently supports basic, asynchronous network requests.
5::CODE;;Please refer to :class:`kivy.network.urlrequest.UrlRequest`.
6::CODE;;'''
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;UrlRequest
3::CODE;;==========
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.8
5::CODE;;You can use the :class:`UrlRequest` to make asynchronous requests on the
6::CODE;;web and get the result when the request is completed. The spirit is the
7::CODE;;same as the XHR object in Javascript.
8::CODE;;The content is also decoded if the Content-Type is
9::CODE;;application/json and the result automatically passed through json.loads.
10::CODE;;The syntax to create a request::
11::CODE;;from kivy.network.urlrequest import UrlRequest
12::CODE;;req = UrlRequest(url, on_success, on_redirect, on_failure, on_error,
13::CODE;;on_progress, req_body, req_headers, chunk_size,
14::CODE;;timeout, method, decode, debug, file_path, ca_file,
15::CODE;;verify)
16::CODE;;Only the first argument is mandatory: the rest are optional.
17::CODE;;By default, a "GET" request will be sent. If the :attr:`UrlRequest.req_body` is
18::CODE;;not None, a "POST" request will be sent. It's up to you to adjust
19::CODE;;:attr:`UrlRequest.req_headers` to suit your requirements and the response
20::CODE;;to the request will be accessible as the parameter called "result" on
21::CODE;;the callback function of the on_success event.
22::CODE;;Example of fetching JSON::
23::CODE;;def got_json(req, result):
24::CODE;;for key, value in req.resp_headers.items():
25::CODE;;print('{}: {}'.format(key, value))
26::CODE;;req = UrlRequest('https://httpbin.org/headers', got_json)
27::CODE;;Example of Posting data (adapted from httplib example)::
28::CODE;;import urllib
29::CODE;;def bug_posted(req, result):
30::CODE;;print('Our bug is posted!')
31::CODE;;print(result)
32::CODE;;params = urllib.urlencode({'@number': 12524, '@type': 'issue',
33::CODE;;'@action': 'show'})
34::CODE;;headers = {'Content-type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded',
35::CODE;;'Accept': 'text/plain'}
36::CODE;;req = UrlRequest('bugs.python.org', on_success=bug_posted, req_body=params,
37::CODE;;req_headers=headers)
38::CODE;;If you want a synchronous request, you can call the wait() method.
39::CODE;;'''
40::CODE;;import os
41::CODE;;from base64 import b64encode
42::CODE;;from collections import deque
43::CODE;;from http.client import HTTPConnection
44::CODE;;from json import loads
45::CODE;;from threading import Event, Thread
46::CODE;;from time import sleep
47::CODE;;from urllib.parse import urlparse, urlunparse
48::CODE;;import requests

57::CODE;;except ImportError:
60::CODE;;HTTPSConnection = None

63::CODE;;class UrlRequestBase(Thread):
64::CODE;;'''A UrlRequest. See module documentation for usage.
65::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.5.1
66::CODE;;Add `debug` parameter
67::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.0.10
68::CODE;;Add `method` parameter
69::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.8.0
70::CODE;;Parameter `decode` added.
71::CODE;;Parameter `file_path` added.
72::CODE;;Parameter `on_redirect` added.
73::CODE;;Parameter `on_failure` added.
74::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.9.1
75::CODE;;Parameter `ca_file` added.
76::CODE;;Parameter `verify` added.
77::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.10.0
78::CODE;;Parameters `proxy_host`, `proxy_port` and `proxy_headers` added.
79::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.11.0
80::CODE;;Parameters `on_cancel` added.
81::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 2.2.0
82::CODE;;Parameters `on_finish` added.
83::CODE;;Parameters `auth` added.
84::CODE;;:Parameters:
85::CODE;;`url`: str
86::CODE;;Complete url string to call.
87::CODE;;`on_success`: callback(request, result)
88::CODE;;Callback function to call when the result has been fetched.
89::CODE;;`on_redirect`: callback(request, result)
90::CODE;;Callback function to call if the server returns a Redirect.
91::CODE;;`on_failure`: callback(request, result)
92::CODE;;Callback function to call if the server returns a Client or
93::CODE;;Server Error.
94::CODE;;`on_error`: callback(request, error)
95::CODE;;Callback function to call if an error occurs.
96::CODE;;`on_progress`: callback(request, current_size, total_size)
97::CODE;;Callback function that will be called to report progression of the
98::CODE;;download. `total_size` might be -1 if no Content-Length has been
99::CODE;;reported in the http response.
100::CODE;;This callback will be called after each `chunk_size` is read.
101::CODE;;`on_cancel`: callback(request)
102::CODE;;Callback function to call if user requested to cancel the download
103::CODE;;operation via the .cancel() method.
104::CODE;;`on_finish`: callback(request)
105::CODE;;Additional callback function to call if request is done.
106::CODE;;`req_body`: str, defaults to None
107::CODE;;Data to sent in the request. If it's not None, a POST will be done
108::CODE;;instead of a GET.
109::CODE;;`req_headers`: dict, defaults to None
110::CODE;;Custom headers to add to the request.
111::CODE;;`chunk_size`: int, defaults to 8192
112::CODE;;Size of each chunk to read, used only when `on_progress` callback
113::CODE;;has been set. If you decrease it too much, a lot of on_progress
114::CODE;;callbacks will be fired and will slow down your download. If you
115::CODE;;want to have the maximum download speed, increase the chunk_size
116::CODE;;or don't use ``on_progress``.
117::CODE;;`timeout`: int, defaults to None
118::CODE;;If set, blocking operations will timeout after this many seconds.
119::CODE;;`method`: str, defaults to 'GET' (or 'POST' if ``body`` is specified)
120::CODE;;The HTTP method to use.
121::CODE;;`decode`: bool, defaults to True
122::CODE;;If False, skip decoding of the response.
123::CODE;;`debug`: bool, defaults to False
124::CODE;;If True, it will use the Logger.debug to print information
125::CODE;;about url access/progression/errors.
126::CODE;;`file_path`: str, defaults to None
127::CODE;;If set, the result of the UrlRequest will be written to this path
128::CODE;;instead of in memory.
129::CODE;;`ca_file`: str, defaults to None
130::CODE;;Indicates a SSL CA certificate file path to validate HTTPS
131::CODE;;certificates against
132::CODE;;`verify`: bool, defaults to True
133::CODE;;If False, disables SSL CA certificate verification
134::CODE;;`proxy_host`: str, defaults to None
135::CODE;;If set, the proxy host to use for this connection.
136::CODE;;`proxy_port`: int, defaults to None
137::CODE;;If set, and `proxy_host` is also set, the port to use for
138::CODE;;connecting to the proxy server.
139::CODE;;`proxy_headers`: dict, defaults to None
140::CODE;;If set, and `proxy_host` is also set, the headers to send to the
141::CODE;;proxy server in the ``CONNECT`` request.
142::CODE;;`auth`: HTTPBasicAuth, defaults to None
143::CODE;;If set, request will use basicauth to authenticate.
144::CODE;;Only used in "Requests" implementation
145::CODE;;'''
146::CODE;;def __init__(
147::CODE;;self, url, on_success=None, on_redirect=None,

201::CODE;;def run(self):
202::CODE;;q = self._queue.appendleft
203::CODE;;url = self.url
204::CODE;;req_body = self.req_body
205::CODE;;req_headers = self.req_headers or {}
206::CODE;;user_agent = self._user_agent

210::CODE;;elif (

212::CODE;;and 'useragent' in Config.items('network')

27::CODE;;def parse_color(text):
28::CODE;;'''Parse a string to a kivy color. Supported formats:
29::CODE;;* rgb(r, g, b)
30::CODE;;* rgba(r, g, b, a)
31::CODE;;* rgb
32::CODE;;* rgba
33::CODE;;* rrggbb
34::CODE;;* rrggbbaa
35::CODE;;For hexadecimal values, you case also use:
40::CODE;;'''
41::CODE;;value = [1, 1, 1, 1]
42::CODE;;if text.startswith('rgb'):
43::CODE;;res = re.match(r'rgba?\((.*)\)', text)
44::CODE;;if res:
45::CODE;;try:
47::CODE;;value = [1 if int(x) > 255. else (int(x) / 255.)
48::CODE;;for x in re.split(', ?', res.groups()[0])]
49::CODE;;if len(value) < 3:
51::CODE;;raise ValueError
52::CODE;;except ValueError:
53::CODE;;return color_error('ColorParser: Invalid color for %r' % text)
54::CODE;;except AttributeError:
55::CODE;;return color_error('ColorParser: Invalid color for %r' % text)
56::CODE;;else:
57::CODE;;return color_error('ColorParser: Invalid color for %r' % text)
58::CODE;;if len(value) == 3:
59::CODE;;value.append(1.)
60::CODE;;elif len(text):
61::CODE;;res = text
63::CODE;;res = text[1:]
64::CODE;;lres = len(res)
65::CODE;;if lres == 3 or lres == 4:
66::CODE;;res = ''.join([x + x for x in res])
67::CODE;;elif lres != 6 and lres != 8:
69::CODE;;return color_error(
70::CODE;;'ColorParser: Invalid color format for %r' % text)
71::CODE;;try:
72::CODE;;value = [int(res[i:i + 2], 16) / 255.
73::CODE;;for i in range(0, len(res), 2)]
74::CODE;;except ValueError:
75::CODE;;return color_error('ColorParser: Invalid color for %r' % text)
76::CODE;;if lres == 6 or lres == 3:
77::CODE;;value.append(1.)
78::CODE;;return value
79::CODE;;def parse_bool(text):
80::CODE;;'''Parse a string to a boolean, ignoring case. "true"/"1" is True,
81::CODE;;"false"/"0" is False. Anything else throws an exception.'''
82::CODE;;if text.lower() in ('true', '1'):
83::CODE;;return True
84::CODE;;elif text.lower() in ('false', '0'):
85::CODE;;return False
86::CODE;;raise Exception('Invalid boolean: %s' % text)
87::CODE;;def parse_string(text):
88::CODE;;'''Parse a string to a string (removing single and double quotes).'''
89::CODE;;if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] in ('"', "'") and text[-1] in ('"', "'"):
90::CODE;;text = text[1:-1]
91::CODE;;return text.strip()
92::CODE;;def parse_int2(text):
93::CODE;;'''Parse a string to a list of exactly 2 integers.
94::CODE;;>>> print(parse_int2("12 54"))
95::CODE;;12, 54
96::CODE;;'''
97::CODE;;texts = [x for x in text.split(' ') if x.strip() != '']
98::CODE;;value = list(map(parse_int, texts))
99::CODE;;if len(value) < 1:
100::CODE;;raise Exception('Invalid int2 format: %s' % text)
101::CODE;;elif len(value) == 1:
102::CODE;;return [value[0], value[0]]
103::CODE;;elif len(value) > 2:
104::CODE;;raise Exception('Too many values in %s: %s' % (text, str(value)))
105::CODE;;return value
106::CODE;;def parse_float4(text):
107::CODE;;'''Parse a string to a list of exactly 4 floats.
108::CODE;;>>> parse_float4('54 87. 35 0')
109::CODE;;54, 87., 35, 0
110::CODE;;'''
111::CODE;;texts = [x for x in text.split(' ') if x.strip() != '']
112::CODE;;value = list(map(parse_float, texts))
113::CODE;;if len(value) < 1:
114::CODE;;raise Exception('Invalid float4 format: %s' % text)
115::CODE;;elif len(value) == 1:
116::CODE;;return [value[0] for x in range(4)]
117::CODE;;elif len(value) == 2:
118::CODE;;return [value[0], value[1], value[0], value[1]]
119::CODE;;elif len(value) == 3:
121::CODE;;return [value[0], value[1], value[0], value[2]]
122::CODE;;elif len(value) > 4:
123::CODE;;raise Exception('Too many values in %s' % text)
124::CODE;;return value

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Resources management
3::CODE;;====================
4::CODE;;Resource management can be a pain if you have multiple paths and projects.
5::CODE;;Kivy offers 2 functions for searching for specific resources across a list
6::CODE;;of paths.
7::CODE;;Resource lookup
8::CODE;;---------------
9::CODE;;When Kivy looks for a resource e.g. an image or a kv file, it searches through
10::CODE;;a predetermined set of folders. You can modify this folder list using the
11::CODE;;:meth:`resource_add_path` and :meth:`resource_remove_path` functions.
12::CODE;;Customizing Kivy
13::CODE;;----------------
14::CODE;;These functions can also be helpful if you want to replace standard Kivy
15::CODE;;resources with your own. For example, if you wish to customize or re-style
16::CODE;;Kivy, you can force your *style.kv* or *data/defaulttheme-0.png* files to be
17::CODE;;used in preference to the defaults simply by adding the path to your preferred
18::CODE;;alternatives via the :meth:`resource_add_path` method.
19::CODE;;As almost all Kivy resources are looked up using the :meth:`resource_find`, so
20::CODE;;you can use this approach to add fonts and keyboard layouts and to replace
21::CODE;;images and icons.
22::CODE;;'''
23::CODE;;__all__ = ('resource_find', 'resource_add_path', 'resource_remove_path')
24::CODE;;from os.path import join, dirname, exists, abspath
25::CODE;;from kivy import kivy_data_dir
26::CODE;;from kivy.cache import Cache
27::CODE;;from kivy.utils import platform
28::CODE;;from kivy.logger import Logger
29::CODE;;import sys
30::CODE;;import os
31::CODE;;import kivy
32::CODE;;resource_paths = ['.', dirname(sys.argv[0])]
33::CODE;;if platform == 'ios':
34::CODE;;resource_paths += [join(dirname(sys.argv[0]), 'YourApp')]
35::CODE;;resource_paths += [dirname(kivy.__file__), join(kivy_data_dir, '..')]
36::CODE;;Cache.register('kv.resourcefind', timeout=60)
37::CODE;;def resource_find(filename, use_cache=("KIVY_DOC_INCLUDE" not in os.environ)):
38::CODE;;'''Search for a resource in the list of paths.
39::CODE;;Use resource_add_path to add a custom path to the search.
40::CODE;;By default, results are cached for 60 seconds.
41::CODE;;This can be disabled using use_cache=False.
42::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 2.1.0
43::CODE;;`use_cache` parameter added and made True by default.
44::CODE;;'''
45::CODE;;if not filename:
46::CODE;;return
47::CODE;;found_filename = None
48::CODE;;if use_cache:
49::CODE;;found_filename = Cache.get('kv.resourcefind', filename)
50::CODE;;if found_filename:
51::CODE;;return found_filename
52::CODE;;if filename[:8] == 'atlas://':
53::CODE;;found_filename = filename
54::CODE;;else:
55::CODE;;abspath_filename = abspath(filename)
56::CODE;;if exists(abspath_filename):
57::CODE;;found_filename = abspath(filename)
58::CODE;;else:
59::CODE;;for path in reversed(resource_paths):
60::CODE;;abspath_filename = abspath(join(path, filename))
61::CODE;;if exists(abspath_filename):
62::CODE;;found_filename = abspath_filename
63::CODE;;break
64::CODE;;if not found_filename and filename.startswith("data:"):
65::CODE;;found_filename = filename
66::CODE;;if use_cache and found_filename:
67::CODE;;Cache.append('kv.resourcefind', filename, found_filename)
68::CODE;;return found_filename
69::CODE;;def resource_add_path(path):
70::CODE;;'''Add a custom path to search in.
71::CODE;;'''
72::CODE;;if path in resource_paths:
73::CODE;;return
74::CODE;;Logger.debug('Resource: add <%s> in path list' % path)
75::CODE;;resource_paths.append(path)
76::CODE;;def resource_remove_path(path):
77::CODE;;'''Remove a search path.
78::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.8
79::CODE;;'''
80::CODE;;if path not in resource_paths:
81::CODE;;return
82::CODE;;Logger.debug('Resource: remove <%s> from path list' % path)
83::CODE;;resource_paths.remove(path)
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Storage
3::CODE;;=======
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.7.0
5::CODE;;.. warning::
6::CODE;;This module is still experimental, and the API is subject to change in a
7::CODE;;future version.
8::CODE;;Usage
9::CODE;;-----
10::CODE;;The idea behind the Storage module is to be able to load/store any number of
11::CODE;;key-value pairs via an indexed key. The default model is abstract so you
12::CODE;;cannot use it directly. We provide some implementations such as:
13::CODE;;- :class:`kivy.storage.dictstore.DictStore`: use a python dict as a store
14::CODE;;- :class:`kivy.storage.jsonstore.JsonStore`: use a
15::CODE;;`JSON <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JSON>`_ file as a store
16::CODE;;- :class:`kivy.storage.redisstore.RedisStore`: use a `Redis <http://redis.io>`_
17::CODE;;database with `redis-py <https://github.com/andymccurdy/redis-py>`_
18::CODE;;Examples
19::CODE;;--------
20::CODE;;For example, let's use a JsonStore::
21::CODE;;from kivy.storage.jsonstore import JsonStore
22::CODE;;store = JsonStore('hello.json')
24::CODE;;store.put('tito', name='Mathieu', org='kivy')
25::CODE;;store.put('tshirtman', name='Gabriel', age=27)
27::CODE;;store.put('tito', name='Mathieu', age=30)
29::CODE;;print('tito is', store.get('tito')['age'])
31::CODE;;for item in store.find(name='Gabriel'):
32::CODE;;print('tshirtmans index key is', item[0])
33::CODE;;print('his key value pairs are', str(item[1]))
34::CODE;;Because the data is persistent, you can check later to see if the key exists::
35::CODE;;from kivy.storage.jsonstore import JsonStore
36::CODE;;store = JsonStore('hello.json')
37::CODE;;if store.exists('tito'):
38::CODE;;print('tite exists:', store.get('tito'))
39::CODE;;store.delete('tito')
40::CODE;;Synchronous / Asynchronous API
41::CODE;;------------------------------
42::CODE;;All the standard methods (:meth:`~AbstractStore.get`,
43::CODE;;:meth:`~AbstractStore.put` , :meth:`~AbstractStore.exists`,
44::CODE;;:meth:`~AbstractStore.delete`, :meth:`~AbstractStore.find`) have an
45::CODE;;asynchronous version.
46::CODE;;For example, the *get* method has a `callback` parameter. If set, the
47::CODE;;`callback` will be used to return the result to the user when available:
48::CODE;;the request will be asynchronous. If the `callback` is None, then the
49::CODE;;request will be synchronous and the result will be returned directly.
50::CODE;;Without callback (Synchronous API)::
51::CODE;;entry = mystore.get('tito')
52::CODE;;print('tito =', entry)
53::CODE;;With callback (Asynchronous API)::
54::CODE;;def my_callback(store, key, result):
55::CODE;;print('the key', key, 'has a value of', result)
56::CODE;;mystore.get('plop', callback=my_callback)
57::CODE;;The callback signature (for almost all methods) is::
58::CODE;;def callback(store, key, result):
64::CODE;;Synchronous container type
65::CODE;;--------------------------
66::CODE;;The storage API emulates the container type for the synchronous API::
67::CODE;;store = JsonStore('hello.json')
69::CODE;;store['tito']
71::CODE;;store['tito'] = {'name': 'Mathieu'}
73::CODE;;del store['tito']
75::CODE;;len(store)
77::CODE;;'tito' in store
79::CODE;;for key in store:
80::CODE;;pass
81::CODE;;'''
82::CODE;;from kivy.clock import Clock
83::CODE;;from kivy.event import EventDispatcher
84::CODE;;class AbstractStore(EventDispatcher):
85::CODE;;'''Abstract class used to implement a Store
86::CODE;;'''
87::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
88::CODE;;super(AbstractStore, self).__init__(**kwargs)
89::CODE;;self.store_load()
90::CODE;;def exists(self, key):
91::CODE;;'''Check if a key exists in the store.
92::CODE;;'''
93::CODE;;return self.store_exists(key)
94::CODE;;def async_exists(self, callback, key):
95::CODE;;'''Asynchronous version of :meth:`exists`.
96::CODE;;:Callback arguments:
97::CODE;;`store`: :class:`AbstractStore` instance
98::CODE;;Store instance
99::CODE;;`key`: string
100::CODE;;Name of the key to search for
101::CODE;;`result`: boo
102::CODE;;Result of the query, None if any error
103::CODE;;'''
104::CODE;;self._schedule(self.store_exists_async,
105::CODE;;key=key, callback=callback)
106::CODE;;def get(self, key):
107::CODE;;'''Get the key-value pairs stored at `key`. If the key is not found, a
108::CODE;;`KeyError` exception will be thrown.
109::CODE;;'''
110::CODE;;return self.store_get(key)
111::CODE;;def async_get(self, callback, key):
112::CODE;;'''Asynchronous version of :meth:`get`.
113::CODE;;:Callback arguments:
114::CODE;;`store`: :class:`AbstractStore` instance
115::CODE;;Store instance
116::CODE;;`key`: string
117::CODE;;Name of the key to search for
118::CODE;;`result`: dict
119::CODE;;Result of the query, None if any error
120::CODE;;'''
121::CODE;;self._schedule(self.store_get_async, key=key, callback=callback)
122::CODE;;def put(self, key, **values):
123::CODE;;'''Put new key-value pairs (given in *values*) into the storage. Any
124::CODE;;existing key-value pairs will be removed.
125::CODE;;'''
126::CODE;;need_sync = self.store_put(key, values)
127::CODE;;if need_sync:
128::CODE;;self.store_sync()
129::CODE;;return need_sync
130::CODE;;def async_put(self, callback, key, **values):
131::CODE;;'''Asynchronous version of :meth:`put`.
132::CODE;;:Callback arguments:
133::CODE;;`store`: :class:`AbstractStore` instance
134::CODE;;Store instance
135::CODE;;`key`: string
136::CODE;;Name of the key to search for
137::CODE;;`result`: bool
138::CODE;;Indicate True if the storage has been updated, or False if
139::CODE;;nothing has been done (no changes). None if any error.
140::CODE;;'''
141::CODE;;self._schedule(self.store_put_async,
142::CODE;;key=key, value=values, callback=callback)
143::CODE;;def delete(self, key):
144::CODE;;'''Delete a key from the storage. If the key is not found, a `KeyError`
145::CODE;;exception will be thrown.'''
146::CODE;;need_sync = self.store_delete(key)
147::CODE;;if need_sync:
148::CODE;;self.store_sync()
149::CODE;;return need_sync
150::CODE;;def async_delete(self, callback, key):
151::CODE;;'''Asynchronous version of :meth:`delete`.
152::CODE;;:Callback arguments:
153::CODE;;`store`: :class:`AbstractStore` instance
154::CODE;;Store instance
155::CODE;;`key`: string
156::CODE;;Name of the key to search for
157::CODE;;`result`: bool
158::CODE;;Indicate True if the storage has been updated, or False if
159::CODE;;nothing has been done (no changes). None if any error.
160::CODE;;'''
161::CODE;;self._schedule(self.store_delete_async, key=key,
162::CODE;;callback=callback)
163::CODE;;def find(self, **filters):
164::CODE;;'''Return all the entries matching the filters. The entries are
165::CODE;;returned through a generator as a list of (key, entry) pairs
166::CODE;;where *entry* is a dict of key-value pairs ::
167::CODE;;for key, entry in store.find(name='Mathieu'):
168::CODE;;print('key:', key, ', entry:', entry)
169::CODE;;Because it's a generator, you cannot directly use it as a list. You can
170::CODE;;do::
172::CODE;;entries = list(store.find(name='Mathieu'))
174::CODE;;entries = list((x[1] for x in store.find(name='Mathieu')))
175::CODE;;'''
176::CODE;;return self.store_find(filters)
177::CODE;;def async_find(self, callback, **filters):
178::CODE;;'''Asynchronous version of :meth:`find`.
179::CODE;;The callback will be called for each entry in the result.
180::CODE;;:Callback arguments:
181::CODE;;`store`: :class:`AbstractStore` instance
182::CODE;;Store instance
183::CODE;;`key`: string
184::CODE;;Name of the key to search for, or None if we reach the end of
185::CODE;;the results
186::CODE;;`result`: bool
187::CODE;;Indicate True if the storage has been updated, or False if
188::CODE;;nothing has been done (no changes). None if any error.
189::CODE;;'''
190::CODE;;self._schedule(self.store_find_async,
191::CODE;;callback=callback, filters=filters)
192::CODE;;def keys(self):
193::CODE;;'''Return a list of all the keys in the storage.
194::CODE;;'''
195::CODE;;return self.store_keys()
196::CODE;;def async_keys(self, callback):
197::CODE;;'''Asynchronously return all the keys in the storage.
198::CODE;;'''
199::CODE;;self._schedule(self.store_keys_async, callback=callback)
200::CODE;;def count(self):
201::CODE;;'''Return the number of entries in the storage.
202::CODE;;'''
203::CODE;;return self.store_count()
204::CODE;;def async_count(self, callback):
205::CODE;;'''Asynchronously return the number of entries in the storage.
206::CODE;;'''
207::CODE;;self._schedule(self.store_count_async, callback=callback)
208::CODE;;def clear(self):
209::CODE;;'''Wipe the whole storage.
210::CODE;;'''
211::CODE;;return self.store_clear()
212::CODE;;def async_clear(self, callback):
213::CODE;;'''Asynchronous version of :meth:`clear`.
214::CODE;;'''
215::CODE;;self._schedule(self.store_clear_async, callback=callback)
219::CODE;;def __setitem__(self, key, values):
220::CODE;;if not isinstance(values, dict):
221::CODE;;raise Exception('Only dict are accepted for the store[key] = dict')
222::CODE;;self.put(key, **values)
223::CODE;;def __getitem__(self, key):
224::CODE;;return self.get(key)
225::CODE;;def __delitem__(self, key):
226::CODE;;return self.keys()
227::CODE;;def __contains__(self, key):
228::CODE;;return self.exists(key)
229::CODE;;def __len__(self):
230::CODE;;return self.count()
231::CODE;;def __iter__(self):
232::CODE;;for key in self.keys():
233::CODE;;yield key
237::CODE;;def store_load(self):
238::CODE;;pass
239::CODE;;def store_sync(self):
240::CODE;;pass
241::CODE;;def store_get(self, key):
242::CODE;;raise NotImplementedError
243::CODE;;def store_put(self, key, value):
244::CODE;;raise NotImplementedError
245::CODE;;def store_exists(self, key):
246::CODE;;raise NotImplementedError
247::CODE;;def store_delete(self, key):
248::CODE;;raise NotImplementedError
249::CODE;;def store_find(self, filters):
250::CODE;;return []
251::CODE;;def store_keys(self):
252::CODE;;return []
253::CODE;;def store_count(self):
254::CODE;;return len(self.store_keys())
255::CODE;;def store_clear(self):
256::CODE;;for key in self.store_keys():
257::CODE;;self.store_delete(key)
258::CODE;;self.store_sync()
259::CODE;;def store_get_async(self, key, callback):
260::CODE;;try:
261::CODE;;value = self.store_get(key)
262::CODE;;callback(self, key, value)
263::CODE;;except KeyError:
264::CODE;;callback(self, key, None)
265::CODE;;def store_put_async(self, key, value, callback):
266::CODE;;try:
267::CODE;;value = self.put(key, **value)
268::CODE;;callback(self, key, value)
269::CODE;;except:
270::CODE;;callback(self, key, None)
271::CODE;;def store_exists_async(self, key, callback):
272::CODE;;try:
273::CODE;;value = self.store_exists(key)
274::CODE;;callback(self, key, value)
275::CODE;;except:
276::CODE;;callback(self, key, None)
277::CODE;;def store_delete_async(self, key, callback):
278::CODE;;try:
279::CODE;;value = self.delete(key)
280::CODE;;callback(self, key, value)
281::CODE;;except:
282::CODE;;callback(self, key, None)
283::CODE;;def store_find_async(self, filters, callback):
284::CODE;;for key, entry in self.store_find(filters):
285::CODE;;callback(self, filters, key, entry)
286::CODE;;callback(self, filters, None, None)
287::CODE;;def store_count_async(self, callback):
288::CODE;;try:
289::CODE;;value = self.store_count()
290::CODE;;callback(self, value)
291::CODE;;except:
292::CODE;;callback(self, 0)
293::CODE;;def store_keys_async(self, callback):
294::CODE;;try:
295::CODE;;keys = self.store_keys()
296::CODE;;callback(self, keys)
297::CODE;;except:
298::CODE;;callback(self, [])
299::CODE;;def store_clear_async(self, callback):
300::CODE;;self.store_clear()
301::CODE;;callback(self)
305::CODE;;def _schedule(self, cb, **kwargs):
307::CODE;;Clock.schedule_once(lambda dt: cb(**kwargs), 0)
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Dictionary store
3::CODE;;=================
4::CODE;;Use a Python dictionary as a store.
5::CODE;;'''
6::CODE;;__all__ = ('DictStore', )
7::CODE;;try:
8::CODE;;import cPickle as pickle
9::CODE;;except ImportError:
10::CODE;;import pickle
11::CODE;;import errno
12::CODE;;from os.path import exists, abspath, dirname
13::CODE;;from kivy.storage import AbstractStore
14::CODE;;class DictStore(AbstractStore):
15::CODE;;'''Store implementation using a pickled `dict`.
16::CODE;;See the :mod:`kivy.storage` module documentation for more information.
17::CODE;;'''
18::CODE;;def __init__(self, filename, data=None, **kwargs):
19::CODE;;if isinstance(filename, dict):
21::CODE;;self.filename = None
22::CODE;;self._data = filename
23::CODE;;else:
24::CODE;;self.filename = filename
25::CODE;;self._data = data or {}
26::CODE;;self._is_changed = True
27::CODE;;super(DictStore, self).__init__(**kwargs)
28::CODE;;def store_load(self):
29::CODE;;if self.filename is None:
30::CODE;;return
31::CODE;;if not exists(self.filename):
32::CODE;;folder = abspath(dirname(self.filename))
33::CODE;;if not exists(folder):
34::CODE;;not_found = IOError(
35::CODE;;"The folder '{}' doesn't exist!"
36::CODE;;"".format(folder)
37::CODE;;)
38::CODE;;not_found.errno = errno.ENOENT
39::CODE;;raise not_found
40::CODE;;return
41::CODE;;with open(self.filename, 'rb') as fd:
42::CODE;;data = fd.read()
43::CODE;;if data:
44::CODE;;self._data = pickle.loads(data)
45::CODE;;def store_sync(self):
46::CODE;;if self.filename is None:
47::CODE;;return
48::CODE;;if not self._is_changed:
49::CODE;;return
50::CODE;;with open(self.filename, 'wb') as fd:
51::CODE;;pickle.dump(self._data, fd)
52::CODE;;self._is_changed = False
53::CODE;;def store_exists(self, key):
54::CODE;;return key in self._data
55::CODE;;def store_get(self, key):
56::CODE;;return self._data[key]
57::CODE;;def store_put(self, key, value):
58::CODE;;self._data[key] = value
59::CODE;;self._is_changed = True
60::CODE;;return True
61::CODE;;def store_delete(self, key):
62::CODE;;del self._data[key]
63::CODE;;self._is_changed = True
64::CODE;;return True
65::CODE;;def store_find(self, filters):
66::CODE;;for key, values in self._data.items():
67::CODE;;found = True
68::CODE;;for fkey, fvalue in filters.items():
69::CODE;;if fkey not in values:
70::CODE;;found = False
71::CODE;;break
72::CODE;;if values[fkey] != fvalue:
73::CODE;;found = False
74::CODE;;break
75::CODE;;if found:
76::CODE;;yield key, values
77::CODE;;def store_count(self):
78::CODE;;return len(self._data)
79::CODE;;def store_keys(self):
80::CODE;;return list(self._data.keys())
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;JSON store
3::CODE;;==========
4::CODE;;A :mod:`Storage <kivy.storage>` module used to save/load key-value pairs from
5::CODE;;a json file.
6::CODE;;'''
7::CODE;;__all__ = ('JsonStore', )
8::CODE;;import errno
9::CODE;;from os.path import exists, abspath, dirname
10::CODE;;from kivy.storage import AbstractStore
11::CODE;;from json import loads, dump
12::CODE;;class JsonStore(AbstractStore):
13::CODE;;'''Store implementation using a json file for storing the key-value pairs.
14::CODE;;See the :mod:`kivy.storage` module documentation for more information.
15::CODE;;'''
16::CODE;;def __init__(self, filename, indent=None, sort_keys=False, **kwargs):
17::CODE;;self.filename = filename
18::CODE;;self.indent = indent
19::CODE;;self.sort_keys = sort_keys
20::CODE;;self._data = {}
21::CODE;;self._is_changed = True
22::CODE;;super(JsonStore, self).__init__(**kwargs)
23::CODE;;def store_load(self):
24::CODE;;if not exists(self.filename):
25::CODE;;folder = abspath(dirname(self.filename))
26::CODE;;if not exists(folder):
27::CODE;;not_found = IOError(
28::CODE;;"The folder '{}' doesn't exist!"
29::CODE;;"".format(folder)
30::CODE;;)
31::CODE;;not_found.errno = errno.ENOENT
32::CODE;;raise not_found
33::CODE;;return
34::CODE;;with open(self.filename) as fd:
35::CODE;;data = fd.read()
36::CODE;;if len(data) == 0:
37::CODE;;return
38::CODE;;self._data = loads(data)
39::CODE;;def store_sync(self):
40::CODE;;if not self._is_changed:
41::CODE;;return
42::CODE;;with open(self.filename, 'w') as fd:
43::CODE;;dump(
44::CODE;;self._data, fd,
45::CODE;;indent=self.indent,
46::CODE;;sort_keys=self.sort_keys
47::CODE;;)
48::CODE;;self._is_changed = False
49::CODE;;def store_exists(self, key):
50::CODE;;return key in self._data
51::CODE;;def store_get(self, key):
52::CODE;;return self._data[key]
53::CODE;;def store_put(self, key, value):
54::CODE;;self._data[key] = value
55::CODE;;self._is_changed = True
56::CODE;;return True
57::CODE;;def store_delete(self, key):
58::CODE;;del self._data[key]
59::CODE;;self._is_changed = True
60::CODE;;return True
61::CODE;;def store_find(self, filters):
62::CODE;;for key, values in self._data.items():
63::CODE;;found = True
64::CODE;;for fkey, fvalue in filters.items():
65::CODE;;if fkey not in values:
66::CODE;;found = False
67::CODE;;break
68::CODE;;if values[fkey] != fvalue:
69::CODE;;found = False
70::CODE;;break
71::CODE;;if found:
72::CODE;;yield key, values
73::CODE;;def store_count(self):
74::CODE;;return len(self._data)
75::CODE;;def store_keys(self):
76::CODE;;return list(self._data.keys())
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Redis Store
3::CODE;;===========
4::CODE;;Store implementation using Redis. You must have redis-py installed.
5::CODE;;Usage example::
6::CODE;;from kivy.storage.redisstore import RedisStore
7::CODE;;params = dict(host='localhost', port=6379, db=14)
8::CODE;;store = RedisStore(params)
9::CODE;;All the key-value pairs will be stored with a prefix 'store' by default.
10::CODE;;You can instantiate the storage with another prefix like this::
11::CODE;;from kivy.storage.redisstore import RedisStore
12::CODE;;params = dict(host='localhost', port=6379, db=14)
13::CODE;;store = RedisStore(params, prefix='mystore2')
14::CODE;;The params dictionary will be passed to the redis.StrictRedis class.
15::CODE;;See `redis-py <https://github.com/andymccurdy/redis-py>`_.
16::CODE;;'''
17::CODE;;__all__ = ('RedisStore', )
18::CODE;;import os
19::CODE;;from json import loads, dumps
20::CODE;;from kivy.properties import StringProperty
21::CODE;;from kivy.storage import AbstractStore
23::CODE;;if 'KIVY_DOC' not in os.environ:
24::CODE;;import redis
25::CODE;;class RedisStore(AbstractStore):
26::CODE;;'''Store implementation using a Redis database.
27::CODE;;See the :mod:`kivy.storage` module documentation for more information.
28::CODE;;'''
29::CODE;;prefix = StringProperty('store')
30::CODE;;def __init__(self, redis_params, **kwargs):
31::CODE;;self.redis_params = redis_params
32::CODE;;self.r = None
33::CODE;;super(RedisStore, self).__init__(**kwargs)
34::CODE;;def store_load(self):
35::CODE;;self.r = redis.StrictRedis(**self.redis_params)
36::CODE;;def store_sync(self):
37::CODE;;pass
38::CODE;;def store_exists(self, key):
39::CODE;;key = self.prefix + '.d.' + key
40::CODE;;value = self.r.exists(key)
41::CODE;;return value
42::CODE;;def store_get(self, key):
43::CODE;;key = self.prefix + '.d.' + key
44::CODE;;if not self.r.exists(key):
45::CODE;;raise KeyError(key)
46::CODE;;result = self.r.hgetall(key)
47::CODE;;for k in result.keys():
48::CODE;;result[k] = loads(result[k])
49::CODE;;return result
50::CODE;;def store_put(self, key, values):
51::CODE;;key = self.prefix + '.d.' + key
52::CODE;;pipe = self.r.pipeline()
53::CODE;;pipe.delete(key)
54::CODE;;for k, v in values.items():
55::CODE;;pipe.hset(key, k, dumps(v))
56::CODE;;pipe.execute()
57::CODE;;return True
58::CODE;;def store_delete(self, key):
59::CODE;;key = self.prefix + '.d.' + key
60::CODE;;if not self.r.exists(key):
61::CODE;;raise KeyError(key)
62::CODE;;return self.r.delete(key)
63::CODE;;def store_keys(self):
64::CODE;;z = len(self.prefix + '.d.')
65::CODE;;return [x[z:] for x in self.r.keys(self.prefix + '.d.*')]
66::CODE;;def store_find(self, filters):
67::CODE;;fkeys = filters.keys()
68::CODE;;fvalues = filters.values()
69::CODE;;for key in self.store_keys():
70::CODE;;skey = self.prefix + '.d.' + key
71::CODE;;svalues = self.r.hmget(skey, fkeys)
72::CODE;;if None in svalues:
73::CODE;;continue
74::CODE;;svalues = [loads(x) for x in svalues]
75::CODE;;if fvalues != svalues:
76::CODE;;continue
77::CODE;;yield key, self.r.hgetall(skey)
1::CODE;;'''

8::CODE;;def install_gobject_iteration():
9::CODE;;'''Import and install gobject context iteration inside our event loop.
10::CODE;;This is used as soon as gobject is used (like gstreamer).
11::CODE;;'''
12::CODE;;from kivy.clock import Clock
13::CODE;;try:
14::CODE;;from gi.repository import GObject as gobject
15::CODE;;except ImportError:
16::CODE;;import gobject
17::CODE;;if hasattr(gobject, '_gobject_already_installed'):
19::CODE;;return
20::CODE;;gobject._gobject_already_installed = True
22::CODE;;loop = gobject.MainLoop()
23::CODE;;gobject.threads_init()
24::CODE;;context = loop.get_context()
26::CODE;;def _gobject_iteration(*largs):
28::CODE;;loop = 0
29::CODE;;while context.pending() and loop < 10:
30::CODE;;context.iteration(False)
31::CODE;;loop += 1
32::CODE;;Clock.schedule_interval(_gobject_iteration, 0)
36::CODE;;g_android_redraw_count = 0

44::CODE;;g_android_redraw_count -= 1
45::CODE;;if g_android_redraw_count < 0:

114::CODE;;def install_twisted_reactor(**kwargs):
115::CODE;;'''Installs a threaded twisted reactor, which will schedule one
116::CODE;;reactor iteration before the next frame only when twisted needs
117::CODE;;to do some work.
118::CODE;;Any arguments or keyword arguments passed to this function will be
119::CODE;;passed on the threadedselect reactors interleave function. These
120::CODE;;are the arguments one would usually pass to twisted's reactor.startRunning.
121::CODE;;Unlike the default twisted reactor, the installed reactor will not handle
122::CODE;;any signals unless you set the 'installSignalHandlers' keyword argument
123::CODE;;to 1 explicitly. This is done to allow kivy to handle the signals as
124::CODE;;usual unless you specifically want the twisted reactor to handle the
125::CODE;;signals (e.g. SIGINT).
126::CODE;;.. note::
127::CODE;;Twisted is not included in iOS build by default. To use it on iOS,
128::CODE;;put the twisted distribution (and zope.interface dependency) in your
129::CODE;;application directory.

31::CODE;;class WidgetResolver(object):
34::CODE;;base_widget = None
35::CODE;;matched_widget = None
36::CODE;;_kwargs_filter = {}
37::CODE;;_funcs_filter = []

39::CODE;;self.base_widget = base_widget
40::CODE;;self._kwargs_filter = {}
41::CODE;;self._funcs_filter = []
42::CODE;;super(WidgetResolver, self).__init__(**kwargs)
43::CODE;;def __call__(self):
44::CODE;;if self.matched_widget is not None:
45::CODE;;return self.matched_widget
46::CODE;;if not self._kwargs_filter and not self._funcs_filter:
47::CODE;;return self.base_widget
48::CODE;;return None
49::CODE;;def match(self, **kwargs_filter):
50::CODE;;self._kwargs_filter.update(kwargs_filter)
51::CODE;;def match_funcs(self, funcs_filter=()):
52::CODE;;self._funcs_filter.extend(funcs_filter)
53::CODE;;def check_widget(self, widget):
54::CODE;;if not all(func(widget) for func in self._funcs_filter):
55::CODE;;return False
56::CODE;;for attr, val in self._kwargs_filter.items():
57::CODE;;if getattr(widget, attr, _unique_value) != val:
58::CODE;;return False
59::CODE;;return True
60::CODE;;def not_found(self, op):
61::CODE;;raise ValueError(
62::CODE;;'Cannot find widget matching <{}, {}> starting from base '
63::CODE;;'widget "{}" doing "{}" traversal'.format(
64::CODE;;self._kwargs_filter, self._funcs_filter, self.base_widget, op))
65::CODE;;def down(self, **kwargs_filter):
66::CODE;;self.match(**kwargs_filter)
67::CODE;;check = self.check_widget
68::CODE;;fifo = deque([self.base_widget])
69::CODE;;while fifo:
70::CODE;;widget = fifo.popleft()
71::CODE;;if check(widget):
72::CODE;;return WidgetResolver(base_widget=widget)
73::CODE;;fifo.extend(widget.children)

75::CODE;;def up(self, **kwargs_filter):
76::CODE;;self.match(**kwargs_filter)
77::CODE;;check = self.check_widget
78::CODE;;parent = self.base_widget
79::CODE;;while parent is not None:
80::CODE;;if check(parent):
81::CODE;;return WidgetResolver(base_widget=parent)
82::CODE;;new_parent = parent.parent
84::CODE;;if new_parent is parent:
85::CODE;;break
86::CODE;;parent = new_parent
87::CODE;;self.not_found('up')

89::CODE;;self.match(**kwargs_filter)
90::CODE;;check = self.check_widget
91::CODE;;base_widget = self.base_widget
92::CODE;;already_checked_base = None
93::CODE;;while base_widget is not None:
94::CODE;;fifo = deque([base_widget])
95::CODE;;while fifo:
96::CODE;;widget = fifo.popleft()
98::CODE;;if widget is already_checked_base:

102::CODE;;fifo.extend(widget.children)

106::CODE;;if new_base_widget is base_widget:
107::CODE;;break

1::CODE;;'''

3::CODE;;graphics with an OpenGL context.
4::CODE;;The idea is to render a Widget tree, and after 1, 2 or more frames, a
5::CODE;;screenshot will be made and be compared to the original one.
6::CODE;;If no screenshot exists for the current test, the very first one will be used.
7::CODE;;The screenshots live in the 'kivy/tests/results' folder and are in PNG format,
8::CODE;;320x240 pixels.

419::CODE;;def _convert_points(self, points):
420::CODE;;if points and isinstance(points[0], (list, tuple)):
421::CODE;;return list(itertools.chain(*points))
422::CODE;;else:
423::CODE;;return list(points)
426::CODE;;def _filtered_points(self, points):
427::CODE;;index = 0
428::CODE;;p = self._convert_points(points)
431::CODE;;if len(p) < 6:
432::CODE;;return []
433::CODE;;while index < len(p) - 2:
434::CODE;;x1, y1 = p[index], p[index + 1]
435::CODE;;x2, y2 = p[index + 2], p[index + 3]
436::CODE;;if abs(x2 - x1) < 1.0 and abs(y2 - y1) < 1.0:
437::CODE;;del p[index + 2: index + 4]
438::CODE;;else:
439::CODE;;index += 2
440::CODE;;if abs(p[0] - p[-2]) < 1.0 and abs(p[1] - p[-1]) < 1.0:
441::CODE;;del p[:2]
442::CODE;;return p

30::CODE;;def has_alpha(fmt):
31::CODE;;return fmt in ('rgba', 'bgra', 'argb', 'abgr')
32::CODE;;def bytes_per_pixel(fmt):
33::CODE;;if fmt in ('rgb', 'bgr'):
34::CODE;;return 3
35::CODE;;if fmt in ('rgba', 'bgra', 'argb', 'abgr'):
36::CODE;;return 4
37::CODE;;raise Exception('bytes_per_pixel: unknown format {}'.format(fmt))
38::CODE;;def get_pixel_alpha(pix, fmt):
39::CODE;;if fmt in ('rgba', 'bgra'):

41::CODE;;elif fmt in ('abgr', 'argb'):
42::CODE;;return pix[0]

45::CODE;;def rgba_to(pix_in, target_fmt, w, h, pitch=None):
46::CODE;;if not isinstance(pix_in, (bytes, bytearray)):
47::CODE;;pix_in = bytearray(pix_in)
48::CODE;;assert w > 0 and h > 0, "Must specify w and h"
49::CODE;;assert len(pix_in) == w * h * 4, "Invalid rgba data {}".format(pix_in)
50::CODE;;assert target_fmt in ('rgba', 'bgra', 'argb', 'abgr', 'rgb', 'bgr')
51::CODE;;if target_fmt == 'rgba':
52::CODE;;return pix_in
53::CODE;;pixels = [pix_in[i:i + 4] for i in range(0, len(pix_in), 4)]
54::CODE;;if target_fmt == 'bgra':
55::CODE;;return b''.join([bytes(p[:3][::-1] + p[3:]) for p in pixels])
56::CODE;;elif target_fmt == 'abgr':
57::CODE;;return b''.join([bytes(p[3:] + p[:3][::-1]) for p in pixels])
58::CODE;;elif target_fmt == 'argb':
59::CODE;;return b''.join([bytes(p[3:] + p[:3]) for p in pixels])
61::CODE;;if pitch is None:
62::CODE;;pitch = ((3 * w) + 3) & ~3
64::CODE;;elif pitch == 0:
65::CODE;;pitch = 3 * w
66::CODE;;out = b''
67::CODE;;padding = b'\x00' * (pitch - w * 3)
68::CODE;;for row in [pix_in[i:i + w * 4] for i in range(0, len(pix_in), w * 4)]:
69::CODE;;pixelrow = [row[i:i + 4] for i in range(0, len(row), 4)]
70::CODE;;if target_fmt == 'rgb':
71::CODE;;out += b''.join([bytes(p[:3]) for p in pixelrow])
72::CODE;;elif target_fmt == 'bgr':
73::CODE;;out += b''.join([bytes(p[:3][::-1]) for p in pixelrow])
74::CODE;;out += padding
75::CODE;;return out
76::CODE;;def match_prediction(pixels, fmt, fd, pitch):
77::CODE;;assert len(fd['alpha']) == 2
78::CODE;;assert len(fd['pattern']) > 0
79::CODE;;bpp = bytes_per_pixel(fmt)
80::CODE;;rowlen = fd['w'] * bpp
81::CODE;;if pitch is None:
82::CODE;;pitch = (rowlen + 3) & ~3
83::CODE;;elif pitch == 0:
84::CODE;;pitch = fd['w'] * bpp
85::CODE;;pitchalign = pitch - rowlen
86::CODE;;errors = []
87::CODE;;fail = errors.append
88::CODE;;if len(pixels) != pitch * fd['h']:
89::CODE;;fail("Pitch error: pitch {} * {} height != {} pixelbytes"
90::CODE;;.format(pitch, fd['h'], len(pixels)))
91::CODE;;ptr = 0
92::CODE;;pixnum = 0
93::CODE;;for char in fd['pattern']:
94::CODE;;pix = list(bytearray(pixels[ptr:ptr + bpp]))
96::CODE;;if len(pix) != bpp:
97::CODE;;fail("Want {} bytes per pixel, got {}: {}"
98::CODE;;.format(bpp, len(pix), pix))
99::CODE;;break
100::CODE;;if char == 't':
101::CODE;;if get_pixel_alpha(pix, fmt) != 0:
102::CODE;;fail("pixel {} nonzero 't' pixel alpha {:02X}: {}".format(
103::CODE;;pixnum, get_pixel_alpha(pix, fmt), pix))
104::CODE;;else:
105::CODE;;srcpix = v0_PIXELS[char] + list(bytearray.fromhex(fd['alpha']))
106::CODE;;predict = rgba_to(srcpix, fmt, 1, 1, pitch=0)
107::CODE;;predict = list(bytearray(predict))
108::CODE;;if not predict or not pix or predict != pix:
109::CODE;;fail("pixel {} {} format mismatch: want {} ({}) -- got {}"
110::CODE;;.format(pixnum, fmt, predict, char, pix))
111::CODE;;if pitchalign and (pixnum + 1) % fd['w'] == 0:
112::CODE;;check = list(bytearray(pixels[ptr + bpp:ptr + bpp + pitchalign]))
113::CODE;;if check != [0] * pitchalign:
114::CODE;;fail("Want {} 0x00 pitch align pixnum={}, pos={} got: {}"
115::CODE;;.format(pitchalign, pixnum, ptr + bpp, check))
116::CODE;;ptr += pitchalign
117::CODE;;ptr += bpp
118::CODE;;pixnum += 1
119::CODE;;if ptr != len(pixels):
120::CODE;;fail("Excess data: pixnum={} ptr={} bytes={}, bpp={} pitchalign={}"
121::CODE;;.format(pixnum, ptr, len(pixels), bpp, pitchalign))
122::CODE;;return (len(errors) == 0, errors)

5::CODE;;import unittest
6::CODE;;import os
7::CODE;;from weakref import proxy
8::CODE;;from functools import partial
9::CODE;;from textwrap import dedent
10::CODE;;class BaseClass(object):
11::CODE;;uid = 0
13::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
14::CODE;;super(BaseClass, self).__init__()
15::CODE;;self.proxy_ref = proxy(self)
16::CODE;;self.children = []
17::CODE;;self.parent = None
18::CODE;;self.binded_func = {}
19::CODE;;self.id = None
20::CODE;;self.ids = {}
21::CODE;;self.cls = []
22::CODE;;self.ids = {}
23::CODE;;self.uid = BaseClass.uid
24::CODE;;BaseClass.uid += 1
25::CODE;;def add_widget(self, widget):
26::CODE;;self.children.append(widget)
27::CODE;;widget.parent = self
28::CODE;;def dispatch(self, event_type, *largs, **kwargs):
29::CODE;;pass
30::CODE;;def create_property(self, name, value=None, default_value=True):
31::CODE;;pass
32::CODE;;def is_event_type(self, key):
33::CODE;;return key.startswith('on_')
34::CODE;;def fbind(self, name, func, *largs):
35::CODE;;self.binded_func[name] = partial(func, *largs)
36::CODE;;return True

3::CODE;;from collections import defaultdict
4::CODE;;class TrackCallbacks(object):
5::CODE;;kv_pre_events = []
6::CODE;;'''Stores values added during the pre event dispatched callbacks.
7::CODE;;'''
8::CODE;;kv_applied_events = []
9::CODE;;'''Stores values added during the applied event dispatched callbacks.
10::CODE;;'''
11::CODE;;kv_post_events = []
12::CODE;;'''Stores values added during the post event dispatched callbacks.
13::CODE;;'''
14::CODE;;events_in_pre = []
15::CODE;;'''List of expected events that should be in kv_pre_events after all the
16::CODE;;callbacks has been executed.
17::CODE;;'''
18::CODE;;events_in_applied = []
19::CODE;;'''List of expected events that should be in kv_applied_events after all
20::CODE;;the callbacks has been executed.
21::CODE;;'''
22::CODE;;events_in_post = []
23::CODE;;'''List of expected events that should be in kv_post_events after all the
24::CODE;;callbacks has been executed.
25::CODE;;'''
26::CODE;;instantiated_widgets = []
27::CODE;;'''Whenever a widget of this class is instantiated, it is added to this
28::CODE;;list, which is class specific.
29::CODE;;It lets us iterate through all the instance of this class and assert for
30::CODE;;all of them as needed.
31::CODE;;'''
32::CODE;;root_widget = None
33::CODE;;'''The expected root widget in the kv rule as dispatched in on_kv_applied.
34::CODE;;'''
35::CODE;;base_widget = None
36::CODE;;'''The expected base widget as dispatched in on_kv_post.
37::CODE;;'''
38::CODE;;actual_root_widget = None
39::CODE;;'''The actual root widget in the kv rule as dispatched in on_kv_applied.
40::CODE;;'''
41::CODE;;actual_base_widget = None
42::CODE;;'''The actual base widget as dispatched in on_kv_post.
43::CODE;;'''
44::CODE;;name = 'none'
45::CODE;;'''Optional name given to the widget to help it identify during a test
46::CODE;;failure.
47::CODE;;'''
48::CODE;;my_roots_expected_ids = {}
49::CODE;;'''Dictionary containing the expected ids as stored in the root
50::CODE;;widget's `ids`. The root being this widget's root widget from kv.
51::CODE;;'''
52::CODE;;actual_ids = {}
53::CODE;;'''Dictionary containing the actual ids as stored in the root
54::CODE;;widget's `ids`. The root being this widget's root widget from kv.
55::CODE;;The ids is saved here during the `on_kv_post` callback.
56::CODE;;'''
57::CODE;;expected_prop_values = {}
58::CODE;;'''A dict of property names and the values they are expected to have
59::CODE;;during the on_kv_post dispatch.
60::CODE;;'''
61::CODE;;actual_prop_values = {}
62::CODE;;'''A dict of property names and the values they actually had
63::CODE;;during the on_kv_post dispatch.
64::CODE;;'''
65::CODE;;def __init__(self, name='none', **kwargs):
66::CODE;;self.kv_pre_events = self.kv_pre_events[:]
67::CODE;;self.kv_applied_events = self.kv_applied_events[:]
68::CODE;;self.kv_post_events = self.kv_post_events[:]
69::CODE;;self.events_in_pre = self.events_in_pre[:]
70::CODE;;self.events_in_applied = self.events_in_applied[:]
71::CODE;;self.events_in_post = self.events_in_post[:]
72::CODE;;self.name = name
73::CODE;;super(TrackCallbacks, self).__init__(**kwargs)
74::CODE;;self.instantiated_widgets.append(self)
75::CODE;;def add(self, name, event):
76::CODE;;'''Add name to the list of the names added in the callbacks for this
77::CODE;;event.
78::CODE;;'''
79::CODE;;events = getattr(self, 'kv_{}_events'.format(event))
80::CODE;;events.append(name)
81::CODE;;@classmethod
82::CODE;;def check(cls, testcase):
83::CODE;;'''Checks that all the widgets of this class pass all the assertions.
84::CODE;;'''
85::CODE;;for widget in cls.instantiated_widgets:
87::CODE;;for event in ('pre', 'applied', 'post'):
88::CODE;;cls.check_event(widget, event, testcase)
90::CODE;;expected = {
91::CODE;;k: v.__self__ for k, v in widget.my_roots_expected_ids.items()}
92::CODE;;actual = {k: v.__self__ for k, v in widget.actual_ids.items()}
93::CODE;;testcase.assertEqual(expected, actual)
95::CODE;;testcase.assertIs(
96::CODE;;widget.root_widget and widget.root_widget.__self__,
97::CODE;;widget.actual_root_widget and
98::CODE;;widget.actual_root_widget.__self__,
99::CODE;;'expected "{}", got "{}" instead for root_widget'.format(
100::CODE;;widget.root_widget and widget.root_widget.name,
101::CODE;;widget.actual_root_widget and
102::CODE;;widget.actual_root_widget.name))
104::CODE;;testcase.assertIs(
105::CODE;;widget.base_widget and widget.base_widget.__self__,
106::CODE;;widget.actual_base_widget and
107::CODE;;widget.actual_base_widget.__self__,
108::CODE;;'expected "{}", got "{}" instead for base_widget'.format(
109::CODE;;widget.base_widget and widget.base_widget.name,
110::CODE;;widget.actual_base_widget and
111::CODE;;widget.actual_base_widget.name))
113::CODE;;testcase.assertEqual(
114::CODE;;widget.expected_prop_values, widget.actual_prop_values)
115::CODE;;@staticmethod
116::CODE;;def check_event(widget, event_name, testcase):
117::CODE;;'''Check that the names are added as expected for this event.
118::CODE;;'''
119::CODE;;events = getattr(widget, 'kv_{}_events'.format(event_name))
120::CODE;;should_be_in = getattr(widget, 'events_in_{}'.format(event_name))
121::CODE;;counter = defaultdict(int)
122::CODE;;for name in events:
123::CODE;;counter[name] += 1
124::CODE;;for name, value in counter.items():
125::CODE;;testcase.assertEqual(
126::CODE;;value, 1,
127::CODE;;'"{}" was present "{}" times for event "{}" for widget "{} '
128::CODE;;'({})"'.format(name, value, event_name, widget.name, widget))
129::CODE;;testcase.assertEqual(
130::CODE;;set(should_be_in), set(events),
131::CODE;;'Expected and actual event callbacks do not match for event "{}" '
132::CODE;;'for widget "{} ({})"'.format(
133::CODE;;event_name, widget.name, widget))
134::CODE;;@staticmethod
135::CODE;;def get_base_class():
136::CODE;;'''The base class to use for widgets during testing so we can use
137::CODE;;this class variables to ease testing.
138::CODE;;'''
139::CODE;;from kivy.uix.widget import Widget
140::CODE;;class TestEventsBase(TrackCallbacks, Widget):
141::CODE;;__events__ = ('on_kv_pre', 'on_kv_applied')
142::CODE;;instantiated_widgets = []

144::CODE;;events_in_applied = [1, ]
145::CODE;;events_in_post = [1, ]
146::CODE;;def on_kv_pre(self):
147::CODE;;self.add(1, 'pre')
148::CODE;;def on_kv_applied(self, root_widget):
149::CODE;;self.add(1, 'applied')

393::CODE;;self.button.button is not None else 'Unset')

6::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
7::CODE;;super(_TestSliderHandle, self).__init__(**kwargs)
8::CODE;;self.sensitivity = 'handle'
9::CODE;;class _TestSliderAll(Slider):
10::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
11::CODE;;super(_TestSliderAll, self).__init__(**kwargs)

13::CODE;;class SliderMoveTestCase(GraphicUnitTest):
14::CODE;;framecount = 0
15::CODE;;def setUp(self):
17::CODE;;import kivy.lang.builder as builder
18::CODE;;if not hasattr(self, '_trace'):
19::CODE;;self._trace = builder.trace
20::CODE;;self.builder = builder
21::CODE;;builder.trace = lambda *_, **__: None
22::CODE;;super(SliderMoveTestCase, self).setUp()
23::CODE;;def tearDown(self, *args, **kwargs):
25::CODE;;import kivy.lang.builder as builder
26::CODE;;builder.trace = self._trace
27::CODE;;super(SliderMoveTestCase, self).tearDown(*args, **kwargs)
28::CODE;;def test_slider_move(self):
29::CODE;;EventLoop.ensure_window()
30::CODE;;win = EventLoop.window
31::CODE;;layout = BoxLayout(orientation='vertical')
32::CODE;;s_handle = _TestSliderHandle()
33::CODE;;s_all = _TestSliderAll()
34::CODE;;layout.add_widget(s_handle)
35::CODE;;layout.add_widget(s_all)
36::CODE;;win.add_widget(layout)
38::CODE;;EventLoop.idle()
39::CODE;;cur1 = s_handle.children[0]
40::CODE;;cur2 = s_all.children[0]
41::CODE;;h1 = cur1.to_window(*cur1.center)[1]
42::CODE;;h2 = h1 - s_handle.cursor_height
43::CODE;;h3 = cur2.to_window(*cur2.center)[1]
44::CODE;;h4 = h3 - s_all.cursor_height
45::CODE;;w1 = cur1.to_window(*cur1.center)[0]
46::CODE;;w2 = cur2.to_window(*cur2.center)[0]
47::CODE;;wh = win.width / 2.0
48::CODE;;dt = 2
50::CODE;;points = [
51::CODE;;[w1, h1, wh, h1, 'handle'],
52::CODE;;[w1, h2, wh, h2, 'handle'],
53::CODE;;[w2, h3, wh, h3, 'all'],
54::CODE;;[w2, h4, wh, h4, 'all'],
55::CODE;;]
56::CODE;;for point in points:
57::CODE;;x, y, nx, ny, id = point
59::CODE;;touch = UTMotionEvent("unittest", 1, {
60::CODE;;"x": x / float(win.width),
61::CODE;;"y": y / float(win.height),
62::CODE;;})
64::CODE;;EventLoop.post_dispatch_input("begin", touch)
65::CODE;;if id == 'handle':
67::CODE;;if x == w1 and y == h1:
68::CODE;;self.assertAlmostEqual(
69::CODE;;s_handle.value, 0.0,
70::CODE;;delta=dt
71::CODE;;)
73::CODE;;elif x == w1 and y == h2:
74::CODE;;self.assertAlmostEqual(
75::CODE;;s_handle.value, 50.0,
76::CODE;;delta=dt
77::CODE;;)
78::CODE;;elif id == 'all':
80::CODE;;if x == w1 and y == h3:
81::CODE;;self.assertAlmostEqual(
82::CODE;;s_all.value, 0.0,
83::CODE;;delta=dt
84::CODE;;)
86::CODE;;elif x == w1 and y == h4:
87::CODE;;self.assertAlmostEqual(
88::CODE;;s_all.value, 0.0,
89::CODE;;delta=dt
90::CODE;;)
92::CODE;;touch.move({
93::CODE;;"x": nx / float(win.width),
94::CODE;;"y": ny / float(win.height)
95::CODE;;})
96::CODE;;EventLoop.post_dispatch_input("update", touch)
97::CODE;;if id == 'handle':
99::CODE;;if nx == wh and ny == h1:
100::CODE;;self.assertAlmostEqual(
101::CODE;;s_handle.value, 50.0,
102::CODE;;delta=dt
103::CODE;;)
105::CODE;;elif nx == wh and ny == h2:
106::CODE;;self.assertAlmostEqual(
107::CODE;;s_handle.value, 50.0,
108::CODE;;delta=dt
109::CODE;;)
110::CODE;;elif id == 'all':
112::CODE;;if nx == wh and ny == h3:
113::CODE;;self.assertAlmostEqual(
114::CODE;;s_all.value, 50.0,
115::CODE;;delta=dt
116::CODE;;)
118::CODE;;elif nx == wh and ny == h4:
119::CODE;;self.assertAlmostEqual(
120::CODE;;s_all.value, 50.0,
121::CODE;;delta=dt
122::CODE;;)
124::CODE;;EventLoop.post_dispatch_input("end", touch)
125::CODE;;self.render(layout)
126::CODE;;if __name__ == '__main__':
127::CODE;;import unittest
128::CODE;;unittest.main()
