12::CODE;;def wait_request_is_finished(kivy_clock, request, timeout=10):
13::CODE;;start_time = datetime.now()
14::CODE;;timed_out = False
15::CODE;;while not request.is_finished and not timed_out:
16::CODE;;kivy_clock.tick()
17::CODE;;sleep(.1)
18::CODE;;timed_out = (datetime.now() - start_time).total_seconds() > timeout
19::CODE;;assert request.is_finished
20::CODE;;def ensure_called_from_thread(queue):
29::CODE;;assert len(queue) >= 3
30::CODE;;assert queue[0][1] == 'progress'
31::CODE;;assert queue[-2][1] == 'progress'
32::CODE;;assert queue[-1][1] in ('success', 'redirect')
33::CODE;;assert queue[0][2][0] == 0
34::CODE;;assert queue[-2][2][0] == queue[-2][2][1]
35::CODE;;class UrlRequestQueue:
36::CODE;;def __init__(self, queue):
37::CODE;;self.queue = queue
38::CODE;;def _on_success(self, req, *args):
39::CODE;;self.queue.append((threading.get_ident(), 'success', args))
40::CODE;;def _on_redirect(self, req, *args):
41::CODE;;self.queue.append((threading.get_ident(), 'redirect', args))
42::CODE;;def _on_error(self, req, *args):
43::CODE;;self.queue.append((threading.get_ident(), 'error', args))
44::CODE;;def _on_progress(self, req, *args):
45::CODE;;self.queue.append((threading.get_ident(), 'progress', args))

29::CODE;;def iter_filename_info(dir_name):
39::CODE;;pattern = re.compile(r'^((.+)__(.+)__([^-]+))\.png')
40::CODE;;for t in os.walk(dir_name):
41::CODE;;for filename in t[2]:
42::CODE;;if filename.endswith('.png'):

44::CODE;;if m is None:
45::CODE;;yield {'error': 'png filename not following screenshot'
46::CODE;;' pattern: {}'.format(filename)}
47::CODE;;else:

49::CODE;;yield {'dunder': m.group(1),
50::CODE;;'dir': d,
51::CODE;;'file': m.group(3),

55::CODE;;def parse_docstring_info(text):
56::CODE;;''' parse docstring from text (normal string with '\n's) and return an info
57::CODE;;dict. A docstring should the first triple quoted string, have a title
58::CODE;;followed by a line of equal signs, and then a description at
59::CODE;;least one sentence long.
60::CODE;;fields are 'docstring', 'title', and 'first_sentence' if not 'error'
61::CODE;;'first_sentence' is a single line without newlines.
62::CODE;;'''
63::CODE;;q = '\"\"\"|\'\'\''
64::CODE;;p = r'({})\s+([^\n]+)\s+\=+\s+(.*?)(\1)'.format(q)
65::CODE;;m = re.search(p, text, re.S)
66::CODE;;if m:
67::CODE;;comment = m.group(3).replace('\n', ' ')
68::CODE;;first_sentence = comment[:comment.find('.') + 1]
69::CODE;;return {'docstring': m.group(0), 'title': m.group(2),
70::CODE;;'description': m.group(3), 'first_sentence': first_sentence}
71::CODE;;else:
72::CODE;;return {'error': 'Did not find docstring with title at top of file.'}
73::CODE;;def iter_docstring_info(dir_name):
74::CODE;;''' Iterate over screenshots in directory, yield info from the file
75::CODE;;name and initial parse of the docstring. Errors are logged, but
76::CODE;;files with errors are skipped.
77::CODE;;'''
78::CODE;;for file_info in iter_filename_info(dir_name):
79::CODE;;if 'error' in file_info:
80::CODE;;Logger.error(file_info['error'])
81::CODE;;continue
82::CODE;;source = slash(examples_dir, file_info['dir'],
83::CODE;;file_info['file'] + '.' + file_info['ext'])
84::CODE;;if not os.path.exists(source):
85::CODE;;Logger.error('Screen shot references source code that does '
86::CODE;;'not exist: %s', source)
87::CODE;;continue
88::CODE;;with open(source) as f:
89::CODE;;text = f.read()
90::CODE;;docstring_info = parse_docstring_info(text)
91::CODE;;if 'error' in docstring_info:
92::CODE;;Logger.error(docstring_info['error'] + ' File: ' + source)
94::CODE;;else:
95::CODE;;file_info.update(docstring_info)
96::CODE;;yield file_info
97::CODE;;def enhance_info_description(info, line_length=79):
98::CODE;;''' Using the info['description'], add fields to info.
99::CODE;;info['files'] is the source filename and any filenames referenced by the
100::CODE;;magic words in the description, e.g. 'the file xxx.py' or
101::CODE;;'The image this.png'. These are as written in the description, do
102::CODE;;not allow ../dir notation, and are relative to the source directory.
103::CODE;;info['enhanced_description'] is the description, as an array of
104::CODE;;paragraphs where each paragraph is an array of lines wrapped to width
105::CODE;;line_length. This enhanced description include the rst links to
106::CODE;;the files of info['files'].
107::CODE;;'''
109::CODE;;paragraphs = info['description'].split('\n\n')
110::CODE;;lines = [
111::CODE;;paragraph.replace('\n', '$newline$')
112::CODE;;for paragraph in paragraphs
113::CODE;;]
114::CODE;;text = '\n'.join(lines)
115::CODE;;info['files'] = [info['file'] + '.' + info['ext']]
116::CODE;;regex = r'[tT]he (?:file|image) ([\w\/]+\.\w+)'
117::CODE;;for name in re.findall(regex, text):
118::CODE;;if name not in info['files']:
119::CODE;;info['files'].append(name)
121::CODE;;folder = '_'.join(info['source'].split(sep)[:-1]) + '_'
122::CODE;;text = re.sub(r'([tT]he (?:file|image) )([\w\/]+\.\w+)',
123::CODE;;r'\1:ref:`\2 <$folder$\2>`', text)
124::CODE;;text = text.replace('$folder$', folder)
126::CODE;;lines = [line.replace('$newline$', '\n') for line in text.split('\n')]
127::CODE;;paragraphs = [
128::CODE;;textwrap.wrap(line, line_length)
130::CODE;;if not line.startswith(' ') else [line]
131::CODE;;for line in lines
132::CODE;;]
133::CODE;;info['enhanced_description'] = paragraphs

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Common GLES Subset Extraction Script
3::CODE;;====================================
4::CODE;;In Kivy, our goal is to use OpenGL ES 2.0 (GLES2) for all drawing on all
5::CODE;;platforms. The problem is that GLES2 is not a proper subset of any OpenGL
6::CODE;;Desktop (GL) version prior to version 4.1.
7::CODE;;However, to keep all our drawing cross-platform compatible, we're
8::CODE;;restricting the Kivy drawing core to a real subset of GLES2 that is
9::CODE;;available on all platforms.
10::CODE;;This script therefore parses the GL and GL Extension (GLEXT) headers and
11::CODE;;compares them with the GLES2 header. It then generates a header that only
12::CODE;;contains symbols that are common to GLES2 and at least either GL or GLEXT.
13::CODE;;However, since GLES2 doesn't support double values, we also need to do some
14::CODE;;renaming, because functions in GL that took doubles as arguments now take
15::CODE;;floats in GLES2, with their function name being suffixed with 'f'.
16::CODE;;Furthermore, sometimes the pure symbol name doesn't match because there
17::CODE;;might be an _EXT or _ARB or something akin to that at the end of a symbol
18::CODE;;name. In that case, we take the symbol from the original header and add
20::CODE;;extension.
21::CODE;;'''
22::CODE;;from __future__ import print_function
23::CODE;;gl = open("/Developer/SDKs/MacOSX10.6.sdk/System/Library/Frameworks/" +
24::CODE;;"OpenGL.framework/Versions/A/Headers/gl.h", 'r')
25::CODE;;glext = open("/Developer/SDKs/MacOSX10.6.sdk/System/Library/Frameworks/" +
26::CODE;;"OpenGL.framework/Versions/A/Headers/glext.h", 'r')
27::CODE;;gles = open("gl2.h", 'r')
28::CODE;;def add_defines_to_set(header):
29::CODE;;symbols = []
30::CODE;;lineno = 0
31::CODE;;for line in header:
32::CODE;;symbol = None
33::CODE;;hexcode = None
34::CODE;;lineno += 1
35::CODE;;line = line.strip()
36::CODE;;try:
37::CODE;;elements = line.split()
39::CODE;;symbol = elements[1]
40::CODE;;for element in elements:
41::CODE;;if element.startswith("0x"):
42::CODE;;hexcode = element
43::CODE;;elif line.startswith("typedef"):
44::CODE;;symbol = elements[-1]
45::CODE;;else:
46::CODE;;for element in elements:
47::CODE;;if element.startswith("gl"):
48::CODE;;symbol = element
49::CODE;;if symbol:
50::CODE;;symbols.append((symbol, lineno, line, hexcode))
51::CODE;;except Exception as e:
52::CODE;;print('error:', lineno, ':', line)
53::CODE;;print(e)
54::CODE;;return symbols
55::CODE;;def extract_common_symbols(symbols1, symbols2, already_extracted):
56::CODE;;for symbol1, lineno1, line1, hexcode1 in symbols1:
57::CODE;;for symbol2, lineno2, line2, hexcode2 in symbols2:
58::CODE;;if symbol1 in already_extracted or symbol2 in already_extracted:
59::CODE;;continue
60::CODE;;if symbol1 == symbol2 + 'f':
63::CODE;;print("// Different Name; Redefine")
64::CODE;;print(line2)
66::CODE;;elif symbol1 == symbol2:
67::CODE;;already_extracted.append(symbol1)
68::CODE;;print(line1)
69::CODE;;if symbol1 == 'GLclampf;':
71::CODE;;print('typedef GLclampf GLclampd;')
72::CODE;;elif hexcode1 and hexcode2 and hexcode1 == hexcode2:
73::CODE;;already_extracted.append(symbol1)
74::CODE;;already_extracted.append(symbol2)
75::CODE;;print("// Different Name; Redefine")
76::CODE;;print(line2)
80::CODE;;gl_symbols = add_defines_to_set(gl)
81::CODE;;glext_symbols = add_defines_to_set(glext)
82::CODE;;gles_symbols = add_defines_to_set(gles)
83::CODE;;print('// GLES 2.0 Header file, generated for Kivy')
84::CODE;;print('// Check kivy/kivy/tools/gles_compat/subset_gles.py')
88::CODE;;print('extern "C" {')
91::CODE;;already_extracted = []
92::CODE;;print('\n// Subset common to GLES and GL: ===================================')
93::CODE;;extract_common_symbols(gles_symbols, gl_symbols, already_extracted)
94::CODE;;print('\n// Subset common to GLES and GLEXT: ================================')
95::CODE;;extract_common_symbols(gles_symbols, glext_symbols, already_extracted)
96::CODE;;print()
97::CODE;;print('// What follows was manually extracted from the GLES2 headers because')
98::CODE;;print('// it was not present in any other header.', end=' ')
99::CODE;;print('''
102::CODE;;''')
104::CODE;;print('}')
106::CODE;;print('\n')

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Pyinstaller hooks
3::CODE;;=================
4::CODE;;Module that exports pyinstaller related methods and parameters.
5::CODE;;Hooks
6::CODE;;-----
7::CODE;;PyInstaller comes with a default hook for kivy that lists the indirectly
8::CODE;;imported modules that pyinstaller would not find on its own using
9::CODE;;:func:`get_deps_all`. :func:`hookspath` returns the path to an alternate kivy
10::CODE;;hook, ``kivy/tools/packaging/pyinstaller_hooks/kivy-hook.py`` that does not
11::CODE;;add these dependencies to its list of hidden imports and they have to be
12::CODE;;explicitly included instead.
13::CODE;;One can overwrite the default hook by providing on the command line the
14::CODE;;``--additional-hooks-dir=HOOKSPATH`` option. Because although the default
15::CODE;;hook will still run, the `important global variables
17::CODE;;``excludedimports`` and ``hiddenimports`` will be overwritten by the
18::CODE;;new hook, if set there.
19::CODE;;Additionally, one can add a hook to be run after the default hook by
20::CODE;;passing e.g. ``hookspath=[HOOKSPATH]`` to the ``Analysis`` class. In both
21::CODE;;cases, ``HOOKSPATH`` is the path to a directory containing a file named
22::CODE;;``hook-kivy.py`` that is the pyinstaller hook for kivy to be processed
23::CODE;;after the default hook.
24::CODE;;hiddenimports
25::CODE;;-------------
26::CODE;;When a module is imported indirectly, e.g. with ``__import__``, pyinstaller
27::CODE;;won't know about it and the module has to be added through ``hiddenimports``.
28::CODE;;``hiddenimports`` and other hook variables can be specified within a hook as
29::CODE;;described above. Also, these variable can be passed to ``Analysis`` and their
30::CODE;;values are then appended to the hook's values for these variables.
31::CODE;;Most of kivy's core modules, e.g. video are imported indirectly and therefore
32::CODE;;need to be added in hiddenimports. The default PyInstaller hook adds all the
33::CODE;;providers. To overwrite, a modified kivy-hook similar to the default hook, such
34::CODE;;as :func:`hookspath` that only imports the desired modules can be added. One
35::CODE;;then uses :func:`get_deps_minimal` or :func:`get_deps_all` to get the list of
36::CODE;;modules and adds them manually in a modified hook or passes them to
37::CODE;;``Analysis`` in the spec file.
38::CODE;;Hook generator
39::CODE;;--------------
40::CODE;;:mod:`pyinstaller_hooks` includes a tool to generate a hook which lists
41::CODE;;all the provider modules in a list so that one can manually comment out
42::CODE;;the providers not to be included. To use, do::
43::CODE;;python -m kivy.tools.packaging.pyinstaller_hooks hook filename
44::CODE;;``filename`` is the name and path of the hook file to create. If ``filename``
45::CODE;;is not provided the hook is printed to the terminal.
46::CODE;;'''
47::CODE;;import os
48::CODE;;import sys
49::CODE;;import pkgutil
50::CODE;;import logging
51::CODE;;from os.path import dirname, join
52::CODE;;import importlib
53::CODE;;import subprocess

55::CODE;;import glob

69::CODE;;except ImportError:

121::CODE;;def get_deps_minimal(exclude_ignored=True, **kwargs):
122::CODE;;'''Returns Kivy hidden modules as well as excluded modules to be used
123::CODE;;with ``Analysis``.
124::CODE;;The function takes core modules as keyword arguments and their value
125::CODE;;indicates which of the providers to include/exclude from the compiled app.
126::CODE;;The possible keyword names are ``audio, camera, clipboard, image, spelling,
127::CODE;;text, video, and window``. Their values can be:
128::CODE;;``True``: Include current provider
129::CODE;;The providers imported when the core module is
130::CODE;;loaded on this system are added to hidden imports. This is the
131::CODE;;default if the keyword name is not specified.
132::CODE;;``None``: Exclude
133::CODE;;Don't return this core module at all.
134::CODE;;``A string or list of strings``: Providers to include
135::CODE;;Each string is the name of a provider for this module to be
136::CODE;;included.
137::CODE;;For example, ``get_deps_minimal(video=None, window=True,
138::CODE;;audio=['gstplayer', 'ffpyplayer'], spelling='enchant')`` will exclude all
139::CODE;;the video providers, will include the gstreamer and ffpyplayer providers
140::CODE;;for audio, will include the enchant provider for spelling, and will use the
141::CODE;;current default provider for ``window``.
142::CODE;;``exclude_ignored``, if ``True`` (the default), if the value for a core
143::CODE;;library is ``None``, then if ``exclude_ignored`` is True, not only will the
144::CODE;;library not be included in the hiddenimports but it'll also added to the
145::CODE;;excluded imports to prevent it being included accidentally by pyinstaller.
146::CODE;;:returns:
147::CODE;;A dict with three keys, ``hiddenimports``, ``excludes``, and
148::CODE;;``binaries``. Their values are a list of the corresponding modules to
149::CODE;;include/exclude. This can be passed directly to `Analysis`` with
150::CODE;;e.g. ::
151::CODE;;a = Analysis(['..\\kivy\\examples\\demo\\touchtracer\\main.py'],
152::CODE;;...
153::CODE;;hookspath=hookspath(),
154::CODE;;runtime_hooks=[],
155::CODE;;win_no_prefer_redirects=False,
156::CODE;;win_private_assemblies=False,
157::CODE;;cipher=block_cipher,
158::CODE;;**get_deps_minimal(video=None, audio=None))
159::CODE;;'''
160::CODE;;core_mods = ['audio', 'camera', 'clipboard', 'image', 'spelling', 'text',
161::CODE;;'video', 'window']
162::CODE;;mods = kivy_modules[:]
163::CODE;;excludes = excludedimports[:]
164::CODE;;for mod_name, val in kwargs.items():
165::CODE;;if mod_name not in core_mods:
166::CODE;;raise KeyError('{} not found in {}'.format(mod_name, core_mods))
167::CODE;;full_name = 'kivy.core.{}'.format(mod_name)
168::CODE;;if not val:
169::CODE;;core_mods.remove(mod_name)
170::CODE;;if exclude_ignored:
171::CODE;;excludes.extend(collect_submodules(full_name))
172::CODE;;continue
173::CODE;;if val is True:
174::CODE;;continue
175::CODE;;core_mods.remove(mod_name)
176::CODE;;mods.append(full_name)
177::CODE;;single_mod = False
178::CODE;;if isinstance(val, (str, bytes)):
179::CODE;;single_mod = True
180::CODE;;mods.append('kivy.core.{0}.{0}_{1}'.format(mod_name, val))
181::CODE;;if not single_mod:
182::CODE;;for v in val:
183::CODE;;mods.append('kivy.core.{0}.{0}_{1}'.format(mod_name, v))
185::CODE;;full_name = 'kivy.core.{}'.format(mod_name)
186::CODE;;mods.append(full_name)
187::CODE;;m = importlib.import_module(full_name)
188::CODE;;if mod_name == 'clipboard' and m.CutBuffer:
189::CODE;;mods.append(m.CutBuffer.__module__)
191::CODE;;val = getattr(m, mod_name.capitalize())
192::CODE;;if val:
193::CODE;;mods.append(getattr(val, '__module__'))
194::CODE;;if hasattr(m, 'libs_loaded') and m.libs_loaded:
195::CODE;;for name in m.libs_loaded:
196::CODE;;mods.append('kivy.core.{}.{}'.format(mod_name, name))
197::CODE;;mods = sorted(set(mods))
198::CODE;;binaries = []
199::CODE;;if any('gstplayer' in m for m in mods):
200::CODE;;binaries = _find_gst_binaries()
201::CODE;;elif exclude_ignored:
202::CODE;;excludes.append('kivy.lib.gstplayer')
203::CODE;;return {
204::CODE;;'hiddenimports': mods,
205::CODE;;'excludes': excludes,
206::CODE;;'binaries': binaries,
207::CODE;;}
208::CODE;;def get_deps_all():
209::CODE;;'''Similar to :func:`get_deps_minimal`, but this returns all the
210::CODE;;kivy modules that can indirectly imported. Which includes all
211::CODE;;the possible kivy providers.
212::CODE;;This can be used to get a list of all the possible providers
213::CODE;;which can then manually be included/excluded by commenting out elements
214::CODE;;in the list instead of passing on all the items. See module description.
215::CODE;;:returns:
216::CODE;;A dict with three keys, ``hiddenimports``, ``excludes``, and
217::CODE;;``binaries``. Their values are a list of the corresponding modules to
218::CODE;;include/exclude. This can be passed directly to `Analysis`` with
219::CODE;;e.g. ::
220::CODE;;a = Analysis(['..\\kivy\\examples\\demo\\touchtracer\\main.py'],
221::CODE;;...
222::CODE;;**get_deps_all())
223::CODE;;'''

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Texture compression tool
3::CODE;;========================
4::CODE;;This tool is designed to compress images into:
5::CODE;;- PVRTC (PowerVR Texture Compression), mostly iOS devices
6::CODE;;- ETC1 (Ericson compression), working on all GLES2/Android devices
7::CODE;;Usage
8::CODE;;-----
9::CODE;;In order to compress a texture::
10::CODE;;texturecompress.py [--dir <directory>] <format> <image.png>
11::CODE;;This will create a `image.tex` file with a json header that contains all the
12::CODE;;image information and the compressed data.
13::CODE;;TODO
14::CODE;;----
15::CODE;;Support more format, such as:
16::CODE;;- S3TC (already supported in Kivy)
17::CODE;;- DXT1 (already supported in Kivy)
18::CODE;;'''
19::CODE;;import json
20::CODE;;from struct import pack
21::CODE;;from pprint import pprint
22::CODE;;from subprocess import Popen
23::CODE;;from PIL import Image
24::CODE;;from argparse import ArgumentParser
25::CODE;;from sys import exit
26::CODE;;from os.path import join, exists, dirname, basename
27::CODE;;from os import environ, unlink
28::CODE;;class Tool(object):
29::CODE;;def __init__(self, options):
30::CODE;;super(Tool, self).__init__()
31::CODE;;self.options = options
32::CODE;;self.source_fn = options.image
33::CODE;;self.dest_dir = options.dir or dirname(options.image)
34::CODE;;@property
35::CODE;;def tex_fn(self):
36::CODE;;fn = basename(self.source_fn).rsplit('.', 1)[0] + '.tex'
37::CODE;;return join(self.dest_dir, fn)
38::CODE;;def compress(self):
39::CODE;;pass
40::CODE;;def nearest_pow2(self, v):
42::CODE;;v -= 1
43::CODE;;v |= v >> 1
44::CODE;;v |= v >> 2
45::CODE;;v |= v >> 4
46::CODE;;v |= v >> 8
47::CODE;;v |= v >> 16
48::CODE;;return v + 1
49::CODE;;def runcmd(self, cmd):
50::CODE;;print('Run: {}'.format(' '.join(cmd)))
51::CODE;;Popen(cmd).communicate()
52::CODE;;def write_tex(self, data, fmt, image_size, texture_size, mipmap=False,
53::CODE;;formatinfo=None):
54::CODE;;infos = {
55::CODE;;'datalen': len(data),
56::CODE;;'image_size': image_size,
57::CODE;;'texture_size': texture_size,
58::CODE;;'mipmap': mipmap,
59::CODE;;'format': fmt}
60::CODE;;if formatinfo:
61::CODE;;infos['formatinfo'] = formatinfo
62::CODE;;header = json.dumps(infos, indent=0, separators=(',', ':'))
63::CODE;;header = header.replace('\n', '')
64::CODE;;with open(self.tex_fn, 'wb') as fd:
65::CODE;;fd.write('KTEX')
66::CODE;;fd.write(pack('I', len(header)))
67::CODE;;fd.write(header)
68::CODE;;fd.write(data)
69::CODE;;print('Done! Compressed texture written at {}'.format(self.tex_fn))
70::CODE;;pprint(infos)
71::CODE;;@staticmethod
72::CODE;;def run():
73::CODE;;parser = ArgumentParser(
74::CODE;;description='Convert images to compressed texture')
75::CODE;;parser.add_argument('--mipmap', type=bool, default=False,
76::CODE;;help='Auto generate mipmaps')
77::CODE;;parser.add_argument('--dir', type=str, default=None,
78::CODE;;help='Output directory to generate the compressed texture')
79::CODE;;parser.add_argument('format', type=str, choices=['pvrtc', 'etc1'],
80::CODE;;help='Format of the final texture')
81::CODE;;parser.add_argument('image', type=str,
82::CODE;;help='Image filename')
83::CODE;;args = parser.parse_args()
84::CODE;;if args.format == 'pvrtc':
85::CODE;;PvrtcTool(args).compress()
86::CODE;;elif args.format == 'etc1':
87::CODE;;Etc1Tool(args).compress()
88::CODE;;else:
89::CODE;;print('Unknown compression format')
90::CODE;;exit(1)
91::CODE;;class Etc1Tool(Tool):
92::CODE;;def __init__(self, options):
93::CODE;;super(Etc1Tool, self).__init__(options)
94::CODE;;self.etc1tool = None
95::CODE;;self.locate_etc1tool()
96::CODE;;def locate_etc1tool(self):
97::CODE;;search_directories = [environ.get('ANDROIDSDK', '/')]
98::CODE;;search_directories += environ.get('PATH', '').split(':')
99::CODE;;for directory in search_directories:
100::CODE;;fn = join(directory, 'etc1tool')
101::CODE;;if not exists(fn):
102::CODE;;fn = join(directory, 'tools', 'etc1tool')
103::CODE;;if not exists(fn):
104::CODE;;continue
105::CODE;;print('Found texturetool at {}'.format(directory))
106::CODE;;self.etc1tool = fn
107::CODE;;return
108::CODE;;if self.etc1tool is None:
109::CODE;;print('Error: Unable to locate "etc1tool".\n'
110::CODE;;'Make sure that "etc1tool" is available in your PATH.\n'
111::CODE;;'Or export the path of your Android SDK to ANDROIDSDK')
112::CODE;;exit(1)
113::CODE;;def compress(self):
115::CODE;;image = Image.open(self.source_fn)
116::CODE;;w, h = image.size
117::CODE;;print('Image size is {}x{}'.format(*image.size))
119::CODE;;w2 = self.nearest_pow2(w)
120::CODE;;h2 = self.nearest_pow2(h)
121::CODE;;print('Nearest power-of-2 size is {}x{}'.format(w2, h2))
123::CODE;;raw_tex_fn = self.tex_fn + '.raw'
124::CODE;;cmd = [self.etc1tool, self.source_fn, '--encodeNoHeader', '-o',
125::CODE;;raw_tex_fn]
126::CODE;;try:
127::CODE;;self.runcmd(cmd)
128::CODE;;with open(raw_tex_fn, 'rb') as fd:
129::CODE;;data = fd.read()
130::CODE;;finally:
131::CODE;;if exists(raw_tex_fn):
132::CODE;;unlink(raw_tex_fn)
134::CODE;;self.write_tex(data, 'etc1_rgb8', (w, h), (w2, h2),
135::CODE;;self.options.mipmap)
136::CODE;;class PvrtcTool(Tool):
137::CODE;;def __init__(self, options):
138::CODE;;super(PvrtcTool, self).__init__(options)
139::CODE;;self.texturetool = None
140::CODE;;self.locate_texturetool()
141::CODE;;def locate_texturetool(self):
142::CODE;;search_directories = [
143::CODE;;('/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Platforms/'
144::CODE;;'iPhoneOS.platform/Developer/usr/bin/'),
145::CODE;;'/Developer/Platforms/iPhoneOS.platform/Developer/usr/bin/']
146::CODE;;search_directories += environ.get('PATH', '').split(':')
147::CODE;;for directory in search_directories:
148::CODE;;fn = join(directory, 'texturetool')
149::CODE;;if not exists(fn):
150::CODE;;continue
151::CODE;;print('Found texturetool at {}'.format(directory))
152::CODE;;self.texturetool = fn
153::CODE;;return
154::CODE;;print('Error: Unable to locate "texturetool".\n'
155::CODE;;'Please install the iPhone SDK, or the PowerVR SDK.\n'
156::CODE;;'Then make sure that "texturetool" is available in your PATH.')
157::CODE;;exit(1)
158::CODE;;def compress(self):
160::CODE;;image = Image.open(self.source_fn)
161::CODE;;w, h = image.size
162::CODE;;print('Image size is {}x{}'.format(*image.size))
164::CODE;;w2 = self.nearest_pow2(w)
165::CODE;;h2 = self.nearest_pow2(h)
166::CODE;;print('Nearest power-of-2 size is {}x{}'.format(w2, h2))
168::CODE;;s2 = max(w2, h2)
169::CODE;;print('PVR need a square image, the texture will be {0}x{0}'
170::CODE;;.format(s2))
171::CODE;;ext = self.source_fn.rsplit('.', 1)[-1]
172::CODE;;tmpfile = '/tmp/ktexturecompress.{}'.format(ext)
173::CODE;;image = image.resize((s2, s2))
174::CODE;;image.save(tmpfile)
176::CODE;;raw_tex_fn = self.tex_fn + '.raw'
177::CODE;;cmd = [self.texturetool]
178::CODE;;if self.options.mipmap:
179::CODE;;cmd += ['-m']
180::CODE;;cmd += ['-e', 'PVRTC', '-o', raw_tex_fn, '-f', 'RAW', tmpfile]
181::CODE;;try:
182::CODE;;self.runcmd(cmd)
183::CODE;;with open(raw_tex_fn, 'rb') as fd:
184::CODE;;data = fd.read()
185::CODE;;finally:
186::CODE;;if exists(raw_tex_fn):
187::CODE;;unlink(raw_tex_fn)
189::CODE;;self.write_tex(data, 'pvrtc_rgba4', (w, h), (s2, s2),
190::CODE;;self.options.mipmap)
191::CODE;;if __name__ == '__main__':
192::CODE;;Tool.run()
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Widgets
3::CODE;;=======
4::CODE;;Widgets are elements of a graphical user interface that form part of the
5::CODE;;`User Experience <http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_experience>`_.
6::CODE;;The `kivy.uix` module contains classes for creating and managing Widgets.
7::CODE;;Please refer to the :doc:`api-kivy.uix.widget` documentation for further
8::CODE;;information.
9::CODE;;Kivy widgets can be categorized as follows:
10::CODE;;- **UX widgets**: Classical user interface widgets, ready to be assembled to
11::CODE;;create more complex widgets.
12::CODE;;:doc:`api-kivy.uix.label`, :doc:`api-kivy.uix.button`,
13::CODE;;:doc:`api-kivy.uix.checkbox`,
14::CODE;;:doc:`api-kivy.uix.image`, :doc:`api-kivy.uix.slider`,
15::CODE;;:doc:`api-kivy.uix.progressbar`, :doc:`api-kivy.uix.textinput`,
16::CODE;;:doc:`api-kivy.uix.togglebutton`, :doc:`api-kivy.uix.switch`,
17::CODE;;:doc:`api-kivy.uix.video`
18::CODE;;- **Layouts**: A layout widget does no rendering but just acts as a trigger
19::CODE;;that arranges its children in a specific way. Read more on
20::CODE;;:doc:`Layouts here <api-kivy.uix.layout>`.
21::CODE;;:doc:`api-kivy.uix.anchorlayout`, :doc:`api-kivy.uix.boxlayout`,
22::CODE;;:doc:`api-kivy.uix.floatlayout`,
23::CODE;;:doc:`api-kivy.uix.gridlayout`, :doc:`api-kivy.uix.pagelayout`,
24::CODE;;:doc:`api-kivy.uix.relativelayout`, :doc:`api-kivy.uix.scatterlayout`,
25::CODE;;:doc:`api-kivy.uix.stacklayout`
26::CODE;;- **Complex UX widgets**: Non-atomic widgets that are the result of
27::CODE;;combining multiple classic widgets.
28::CODE;;We call them complex because their assembly and usage are not as
29::CODE;;generic as the classical widgets.
30::CODE;;:doc:`api-kivy.uix.bubble`, :doc:`api-kivy.uix.dropdown`,
31::CODE;;:doc:`api-kivy.uix.filechooser`, :doc:`api-kivy.uix.popup`,
32::CODE;;:doc:`api-kivy.uix.spinner`,
33::CODE;;:doc:`api-kivy.uix.recycleview`,
34::CODE;;:doc:`api-kivy.uix.tabbedpanel`, :doc:`api-kivy.uix.videoplayer`,
35::CODE;;:doc:`api-kivy.uix.vkeyboard`,
36::CODE;;- **Behaviors widgets**: These widgets do no rendering but act on the
37::CODE;;graphics instructions or interaction (touch) behavior of their children.
38::CODE;;:doc:`api-kivy.uix.scatter`, :doc:`api-kivy.uix.stencilview`
39::CODE;;- **Screen manager**: Manages screens and transitions when switching
40::CODE;;from one to another.
41::CODE;;:doc:`api-kivy.uix.screenmanager`
42::CODE;;----
43::CODE;;'''
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Accordion
3::CODE;;=========
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.8
5::CODE;;.. image:: images/accordion.jpg
6::CODE;;:align: right
7::CODE;;The Accordion widget is a form of menu where the options are stacked either
8::CODE;;vertically or horizontally and the item in focus (when touched) opens up to
9::CODE;;display its content.
10::CODE;;The :class:`Accordion` should contain one or many :class:`AccordionItem`
11::CODE;;instances, each of which should contain one root content widget. You'll end up
12::CODE;;with a Tree something like this:
13::CODE;;- Accordion
14::CODE;;- AccordionItem
15::CODE;;- YourContent
16::CODE;;- AccordionItem
17::CODE;;- BoxLayout
18::CODE;;- Another user content 1
19::CODE;;- Another user content 2
20::CODE;;- AccordionItem
21::CODE;;- Another user content
22::CODE;;The current implementation divides the :class:`AccordionItem` into two parts:
25::CODE;;The title bar is made from a Kv template. We'll see how to create a new
26::CODE;;template to customize the design of the title bar.
27::CODE;;.. warning::
28::CODE;;If you see message like::
29::CODE;;[WARNING] [Accordion] not have enough space for displaying all children
30::CODE;;[WARNING] [Accordion] need 440px, got 100px
31::CODE;;[WARNING] [Accordion] layout aborted.
32::CODE;;That means you have too many children and there is no more space to
33::CODE;;display the content. This is "normal" and nothing will be done. Try to
34::CODE;;increase the space for the accordion or reduce the number of children. You
35::CODE;;can also reduce the :attr:`Accordion.min_space`.
36::CODE;;Simple example
37::CODE;;--------------
38::CODE;;.. include:: ../../examples/widgets/accordion_1.py
39::CODE;;:literal:
40::CODE;;Customize the accordion
41::CODE;;-----------------------
42::CODE;;You can increase the default size of the title bar::
43::CODE;;root = Accordion(min_space=60)
44::CODE;;Or change the orientation to vertical::
45::CODE;;root = Accordion(orientation='vertical')
46::CODE;;The AccordionItem is more configurable and you can set your own title
47::CODE;;background when the item is collapsed or opened::
48::CODE;;item = AccordionItem(background_normal='image_when_collapsed.png',
49::CODE;;background_selected='image_when_selected.png')
50::CODE;;'''
51::CODE;;__all__ = ('Accordion', 'AccordionItem', 'AccordionException')
52::CODE;;from kivy.animation import Animation
53::CODE;;from kivy.uix.floatlayout import FloatLayout
54::CODE;;from kivy.clock import Clock
55::CODE;;from kivy.lang import Builder
56::CODE;;from kivy.properties import (ObjectProperty, StringProperty,
57::CODE;;BooleanProperty, NumericProperty,
58::CODE;;ListProperty, OptionProperty, DictProperty)
59::CODE;;from kivy.uix.widget import Widget
60::CODE;;from kivy.logger import Logger
61::CODE;;class AccordionException(Exception):
62::CODE;;'''AccordionException class.
63::CODE;;'''
64::CODE;;pass
65::CODE;;class AccordionItem(FloatLayout):
66::CODE;;'''AccordionItem class that must be used in conjunction with the
67::CODE;;:class:`Accordion` class. See the module documentation for more
68::CODE;;information.
69::CODE;;'''
70::CODE;;title = StringProperty('')
71::CODE;;'''Title string of the item. The title might be used in conjunction with the
72::CODE;;`AccordionItemTitle` template. If you are using a custom template, you can
73::CODE;;use that property as a text entry, or not. By default, it's used for the
74::CODE;;title text. See title_template and the example below.
75::CODE;;:attr:`title` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.StringProperty` and defaults
76::CODE;;to ''.
77::CODE;;'''
78::CODE;;title_template = StringProperty('AccordionItemTitle')
79::CODE;;'''Template to use for creating the title part of the accordion item. The
80::CODE;;default template is a simple Label, not customizable (except the text) that
81::CODE;;supports vertical and horizontal orientation and different backgrounds for
82::CODE;;collapse and selected mode.
83::CODE;;It's better to create and use your own template if the default template
84::CODE;;does not suffice.
85::CODE;;:attr:`title` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.StringProperty` and defaults to
86::CODE;;'AccordionItemTitle'. The current default template lives in the
87::CODE;;`kivy/data/style.kv` file.
88::CODE;;Here is the code if you want to build your own template::
89::CODE;;[AccordionItemTitle@Label]:
90::CODE;;text: ctx.title
91::CODE;;canvas.before:
92::CODE;;Color:
93::CODE;;rgb: 1, 1, 1
94::CODE;;BorderImage:
95::CODE;;source:
96::CODE;;ctx.item.background_normal \
97::CODE;;if ctx.item.collapse \
98::CODE;;else ctx.item.background_selected
99::CODE;;pos: self.pos
100::CODE;;size: self.size
101::CODE;;PushMatrix
102::CODE;;Translate:
103::CODE;;xy: self.center_x, self.center_y
104::CODE;;Rotate:
105::CODE;;angle: 90 if ctx.item.orientation == 'horizontal' else 0
106::CODE;;axis: 0, 0, 1
107::CODE;;Translate:
108::CODE;;xy: -self.center_x, -self.center_y
109::CODE;;canvas.after:
110::CODE;;PopMatrix
111::CODE;;'''
112::CODE;;title_args = DictProperty({})
113::CODE;;'''Default arguments that will be passed to the
114::CODE;;:meth:`kivy.lang.Builder.template` method.
115::CODE;;:attr:`title_args` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.DictProperty` and defaults
116::CODE;;to {}.
117::CODE;;'''
118::CODE;;collapse = BooleanProperty(True)
119::CODE;;'''Boolean to indicate if the current item is collapsed or not.
120::CODE;;:attr:`collapse` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty` and
121::CODE;;defaults to True.
122::CODE;;'''
123::CODE;;collapse_alpha = NumericProperty(1.)
124::CODE;;'''Value between 0 and 1 to indicate how much the item is collapsed (1) or
125::CODE;;whether it is selected (0). It's mostly used for animation.
126::CODE;;:attr:`collapse_alpha` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
127::CODE;;defaults to 1.
128::CODE;;'''
129::CODE;;accordion = ObjectProperty(None)
130::CODE;;'''Instance of the :class:`Accordion` that the item belongs to.
131::CODE;;:attr:`accordion` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.ObjectProperty` and
132::CODE;;defaults to None.
133::CODE;;'''
134::CODE;;background_normal = StringProperty(
135::CODE;;'atlas://data/images/defaulttheme/button')
136::CODE;;'''Background image of the accordion item used for the default graphical
137::CODE;;representation when the item is collapsed.
138::CODE;;:attr:`background_normal` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.StringProperty` and
139::CODE;;defaults to 'atlas://data/images/defaulttheme/button'.
140::CODE;;'''
141::CODE;;background_disabled_normal = StringProperty(
142::CODE;;'atlas://data/images/defaulttheme/button_disabled')
143::CODE;;'''Background image of the accordion item used for the default graphical
144::CODE;;representation when the item is collapsed and disabled.
145::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.8.0
146::CODE;;:attr:`background__disabled_normal` is a
147::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.properties.StringProperty` and defaults to
148::CODE;;'atlas://data/images/defaulttheme/button_disabled'.
149::CODE;;'''
150::CODE;;background_selected = StringProperty(
151::CODE;;'atlas://data/images/defaulttheme/button_pressed')
152::CODE;;'''Background image of the accordion item used for the default graphical
153::CODE;;representation when the item is selected (not collapsed).
154::CODE;;:attr:`background_normal` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.StringProperty` and
155::CODE;;defaults to 'atlas://data/images/defaulttheme/button_pressed'.
156::CODE;;'''
157::CODE;;background_disabled_selected = StringProperty(
158::CODE;;'atlas://data/images/defaulttheme/button_disabled_pressed')
159::CODE;;'''Background image of the accordion item used for the default graphical
160::CODE;;representation when the item is selected (not collapsed) and disabled.
161::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.8.0
162::CODE;;:attr:`background_disabled_selected` is a
163::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.properties.StringProperty` and defaults to
164::CODE;;'atlas://data/images/defaulttheme/button_disabled_pressed'.
165::CODE;;'''
166::CODE;;orientation = OptionProperty('vertical', options=(
167::CODE;;'horizontal', 'vertical'))
168::CODE;;'''Link to the :attr:`Accordion.orientation` property.
169::CODE;;'''
170::CODE;;min_space = NumericProperty('44dp')
171::CODE;;'''Link to the :attr:`Accordion.min_space` property.
172::CODE;;'''
173::CODE;;content_size = ListProperty([100, 100])
174::CODE;;'''(internal) Set by the :class:`Accordion` to the size allocated for the
175::CODE;;content.
176::CODE;;'''
177::CODE;;container = ObjectProperty(None)
178::CODE;;'''(internal) Property that will be set to the container of children inside
179::CODE;;the AccordionItem representation.
180::CODE;;'''
181::CODE;;container_title = ObjectProperty(None)
182::CODE;;'''(internal) Property that will be set to the container of title inside
183::CODE;;the AccordionItem representation.
184::CODE;;'''
185::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
186::CODE;;self._trigger_title = Clock.create_trigger(self._update_title, -1)
187::CODE;;self._anim_collapse = None
188::CODE;;super(AccordionItem, self).__init__(**kwargs)
189::CODE;;trigger_title = self._trigger_title
190::CODE;;fbind = self.fbind
191::CODE;;fbind('title', trigger_title)
192::CODE;;fbind('title_template', trigger_title)
193::CODE;;fbind('title_args', trigger_title)
194::CODE;;trigger_title()
195::CODE;;def add_widget(self, *args, **kwargs):
196::CODE;;if self.container is None:
197::CODE;;super(AccordionItem, self).add_widget(*args, **kwargs)
198::CODE;;return
199::CODE;;self.container.add_widget(*args, **kwargs)
200::CODE;;def remove_widget(self, *args, **kwargs):
201::CODE;;if self.container:
202::CODE;;self.container.remove_widget(*args, **kwargs)
203::CODE;;return
204::CODE;;super(AccordionItem, self).remove_widget(*args, **kwargs)
205::CODE;;def on_collapse(self, instance, value):
206::CODE;;accordion = self.accordion
207::CODE;;if accordion is None:
208::CODE;;return
209::CODE;;if not value:
210::CODE;;self.accordion.select(self)
211::CODE;;collapse_alpha = float(value)
212::CODE;;if self._anim_collapse:
213::CODE;;self._anim_collapse.stop(self)
214::CODE;;self._anim_collapse = None
215::CODE;;if self.collapse_alpha != collapse_alpha:
216::CODE;;self._anim_collapse = Animation(
217::CODE;;collapse_alpha=collapse_alpha,
218::CODE;;t=accordion.anim_func,
219::CODE;;d=accordion.anim_duration)
220::CODE;;self._anim_collapse.start(self)
221::CODE;;def on_collapse_alpha(self, instance, value):
222::CODE;;self.accordion._trigger_layout()
223::CODE;;def on_touch_down(self, touch):
224::CODE;;if not self.collide_point(*touch.pos):
225::CODE;;return
226::CODE;;if self.disabled:
227::CODE;;return True
228::CODE;;if self.collapse:
229::CODE;;self.collapse = False
230::CODE;;return True
231::CODE;;else:
232::CODE;;return super(AccordionItem, self).on_touch_down(touch)
233::CODE;;def _update_title(self, dt):
234::CODE;;if not self.container_title:
235::CODE;;self._trigger_title()
236::CODE;;return
237::CODE;;c = self.container_title
238::CODE;;c.clear_widgets()
239::CODE;;instance = Builder.template(self.title_template,
240::CODE;;title=self.title,
241::CODE;;item=self,
242::CODE;;**self.title_args)
243::CODE;;c.add_widget(instance)
244::CODE;;class Accordion(Widget):
245::CODE;;'''Accordion class. See module documentation for more information.
246::CODE;;'''
247::CODE;;orientation = OptionProperty('horizontal', options=(
248::CODE;;'horizontal', 'vertical'))
249::CODE;;'''Orientation of the layout.
250::CODE;;:attr:`orientation` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.OptionProperty`
251::CODE;;and defaults to 'horizontal'. Can take a value of 'vertical' or
252::CODE;;'horizontal'.
253::CODE;;'''
254::CODE;;anim_duration = NumericProperty(.25)
255::CODE;;'''Duration of the animation in seconds when a new accordion item is
256::CODE;;selected.
257::CODE;;:attr:`anim_duration` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
258::CODE;;defaults to .25 (250ms).
259::CODE;;'''
260::CODE;;anim_func = ObjectProperty('out_expo')
261::CODE;;'''Easing function to use for the animation. Check
262::CODE;;:class:`kivy.animation.AnimationTransition` for more information about
263::CODE;;available animation functions.
264::CODE;;:attr:`anim_func` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.ObjectProperty` and
265::CODE;;defaults to 'out_expo'. You can set a string or a function to use as an
266::CODE;;easing function.
267::CODE;;'''
268::CODE;;min_space = NumericProperty('44dp')
269::CODE;;'''Minimum space to use for the title of each item. This value is
270::CODE;;automatically set for each child every time the layout event occurs.
271::CODE;;:attr:`min_space` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
272::CODE;;defaults to 44 (px).
273::CODE;;'''
274::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
275::CODE;;super(Accordion, self).__init__(**kwargs)
276::CODE;;update = self._trigger_layout = \
277::CODE;;Clock.create_trigger(self._do_layout, -1)
278::CODE;;fbind = self.fbind
279::CODE;;fbind('orientation', update)
280::CODE;;fbind('children', update)
281::CODE;;fbind('size', update)
282::CODE;;fbind('pos', update)
283::CODE;;fbind('min_space', update)
284::CODE;;def add_widget(self, widget, *args, **kwargs):
285::CODE;;if not isinstance(widget, AccordionItem):
286::CODE;;raise AccordionException('Accordion accept only AccordionItem')
287::CODE;;widget.accordion = self
288::CODE;;super(Accordion, self).add_widget(widget, *args, **kwargs)
289::CODE;;def select(self, instance):
290::CODE;;if instance not in self.children:
291::CODE;;raise AccordionException(
292::CODE;;'Accordion: instance not found in children')
293::CODE;;for widget in self.children:
294::CODE;;widget.collapse = widget is not instance
295::CODE;;self._trigger_layout()
296::CODE;;def _do_layout(self, dt):
297::CODE;;children = self.children
298::CODE;;if children:
299::CODE;;all_collapsed = all(x.collapse for x in children)
300::CODE;;else:
301::CODE;;all_collapsed = False
302::CODE;;if all_collapsed:
303::CODE;;children[0].collapse = False
304::CODE;;orientation = self.orientation
305::CODE;;min_space = self.min_space
306::CODE;;min_space_total = len(children) * self.min_space
307::CODE;;w, h = self.size
308::CODE;;x, y = self.pos
309::CODE;;if orientation == 'horizontal':
310::CODE;;display_space = self.width - min_space_total
311::CODE;;else:
312::CODE;;display_space = self.height - min_space_total
313::CODE;;if display_space <= 0:
314::CODE;;Logger.warning('Accordion: not enough space '
315::CODE;;'for displaying all children')
316::CODE;;Logger.warning('Accordion: need %dpx, got %dpx' % (
317::CODE;;min_space_total, min_space_total + display_space))
318::CODE;;Logger.warning('Accordion: layout aborted.')
319::CODE;;return
320::CODE;;if orientation == 'horizontal':
321::CODE;;children = reversed(children)
322::CODE;;for child in children:
323::CODE;;child_space = min_space
324::CODE;;child_space += display_space * (1 - child.collapse_alpha)
325::CODE;;child._min_space = min_space
326::CODE;;child.x = x
327::CODE;;child.y = y
328::CODE;;child.orientation = self.orientation
329::CODE;;if orientation == 'horizontal':
330::CODE;;child.content_size = display_space, h
331::CODE;;child.width = child_space
332::CODE;;child.height = h
333::CODE;;x += child_space
334::CODE;;else:
335::CODE;;child.content_size = w, display_space
336::CODE;;child.width = w
337::CODE;;child.height = child_space
338::CODE;;y += child_space
339::CODE;;if __name__ == '__main__':
340::CODE;;from kivy.base import runTouchApp
341::CODE;;from kivy.uix.button import Button
342::CODE;;from kivy.uix.boxlayout import BoxLayout
343::CODE;;from kivy.uix.label import Label
344::CODE;;acc = Accordion()
345::CODE;;for x in range(10):
346::CODE;;item = AccordionItem(title='Title %d' % x)
347::CODE;;if x == 0:
348::CODE;;item.add_widget(Button(text='Content %d' % x))
349::CODE;;elif x == 1:
350::CODE;;z = BoxLayout(orientation='vertical')
351::CODE;;z.add_widget(Button(text=str(x), size_hint_y=None, height=35))
352::CODE;;z.add_widget(Label(text='Content %d' % x))
353::CODE;;item.add_widget(z)
354::CODE;;else:
355::CODE;;item.add_widget(Label(text='This is a big content\n' * 20))
356::CODE;;acc.add_widget(item)
357::CODE;;def toggle_layout(*l):
358::CODE;;o = acc.orientation
359::CODE;;acc.orientation = 'vertical' if o == 'horizontal' else 'horizontal'
360::CODE;;btn = Button(text='Toggle layout')
361::CODE;;btn.bind(on_release=toggle_layout)
362::CODE;;def select_2nd_item(*l):
363::CODE;;acc.select(acc.children[-2])
364::CODE;;btn2 = Button(text='Select 2nd item')
365::CODE;;btn2.bind(on_release=select_2nd_item)
366::CODE;;from kivy.uix.slider import Slider
367::CODE;;slider = Slider()
368::CODE;;def update_min_space(instance, value):
369::CODE;;acc.min_space = value
370::CODE;;slider.bind(value=update_min_space)
371::CODE;;root = BoxLayout(spacing=20, padding=20)
372::CODE;;controls = BoxLayout(orientation='vertical', size_hint_x=.3)
373::CODE;;controls.add_widget(btn)
374::CODE;;controls.add_widget(btn2)
375::CODE;;controls.add_widget(slider)
376::CODE;;root.add_widget(controls)
377::CODE;;root.add_widget(acc)
378::CODE;;runTouchApp(root)
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Action Bar
3::CODE;;==========
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.8.0
5::CODE;;.. image:: images/actionbar.png
6::CODE;;:align: right
7::CODE;;The ActionBar widget is like Android's `ActionBar
8::CODE;;<http://developer.android.com/guide/topics/ui/actionbar.html>`_, where items
9::CODE;;are stacked horizontally. When the area becomes to small, widgets are moved
10::CODE;;into the :class:`ActionOverflow` area.
11::CODE;;An :class:`ActionBar` must contain an :class:`ActionView` with various
12::CODE;;:class:`ContextualActionViews <kivy.uix.actionbar.ContextualActionView>`.
13::CODE;;An :class:`ActionView` must contain a child :class:`ActionPrevious` which may
14::CODE;;have title, app_icon and previous_icon properties. :class:`ActionView` children
15::CODE;;must be
16::CODE;;subclasses of :class:`ActionItems <ActionItem>`. Some predefined ones include
17::CODE;;an :class:`ActionButton`, an :class:`ActionToggleButton`, an
18::CODE;;:class:`ActionCheck`, an :class:`ActionSeparator` and an :class:`ActionGroup`.
19::CODE;;An :class:`ActionGroup` is used to display :class:`ActionItems <ActionItem>`
20::CODE;;in a group. An :class:`ActionView` will always display an :class:`ActionGroup`
21::CODE;;after other :class:`ActionItems <ActionItem>`. An :class:`ActionView` contains
22::CODE;;an :class:`ActionOverflow`, but this is only made visible when required i.e.
23::CODE;;the available area is too small to fit all the widgets. A
24::CODE;;:class:`ContextualActionView` is a subclass of an:class:`ActionView`.
25::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.10.1
26::CODE;;:class:`ActionGroup` core rewritten from :class:`Spinner` to pure
27::CODE;;:class:`DropDown`
28::CODE;;'''
29::CODE;;__all__ = ('ActionBarException', 'ActionItem', 'ActionButton',
30::CODE;;'ActionToggleButton', 'ActionCheck', 'ActionSeparator',
31::CODE;;'ActionDropDown', 'ActionGroup', 'ActionOverflow',
32::CODE;;'ActionView', 'ContextualActionView', 'ActionPrevious',
33::CODE;;'ActionBar')
34::CODE;;from kivy.uix.boxlayout import BoxLayout
35::CODE;;from kivy.uix.dropdown import DropDown
36::CODE;;from kivy.uix.widget import Widget
37::CODE;;from kivy.uix.button import Button
38::CODE;;from kivy.uix.togglebutton import ToggleButton
39::CODE;;from kivy.uix.checkbox import CheckBox
40::CODE;;from kivy.uix.spinner import Spinner
41::CODE;;from kivy.uix.label import Label
42::CODE;;from kivy.config import Config
43::CODE;;from kivy.properties import ObjectProperty, NumericProperty, BooleanProperty, \
44::CODE;;StringProperty, ListProperty, OptionProperty, AliasProperty, ColorProperty
45::CODE;;from kivy.metrics import sp
46::CODE;;from kivy.lang import Builder
47::CODE;;from functools import partial
48::CODE;;window_icon = ''
49::CODE;;if Config:
50::CODE;;window_icon = Config.get('kivy', 'window_icon')
51::CODE;;class ActionBarException(Exception):
52::CODE;;'''
53::CODE;;ActionBarException class
54::CODE;;'''
55::CODE;;pass
56::CODE;;class ActionItem(object):
57::CODE;;'''
58::CODE;;ActionItem class, an abstract class for all ActionBar widgets. To create a
59::CODE;;custom widget for an ActionBar, inherit from this class. See module
60::CODE;;documentation for more information.
61::CODE;;'''
62::CODE;;minimum_width = NumericProperty('90sp')
63::CODE;;'''
64::CODE;;Minimum Width required by an ActionItem.
65::CODE;;:attr:`minimum_width` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
66::CODE;;defaults to '90sp'.
67::CODE;;'''
68::CODE;;def get_pack_width(self):
69::CODE;;return max(self.minimum_width, self.width)
70::CODE;;pack_width = AliasProperty(get_pack_width,
71::CODE;;bind=('minimum_width', 'width'),
72::CODE;;cache=True)
73::CODE;;'''
74::CODE;;(read-only) The actual width to use when packing the items. Equal to the
75::CODE;;greater of minimum_width and width.
76::CODE;;:attr:`pack_width` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.AliasProperty`.
77::CODE;;'''
78::CODE;;important = BooleanProperty(False)
79::CODE;;'''
80::CODE;;Determines if an ActionItem is important or not. If an item is important
81::CODE;;and space is limited, this item will be displayed in preference to others.
82::CODE;;:attr:`important` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty` and
83::CODE;;defaults to False.
84::CODE;;'''
85::CODE;;inside_group = BooleanProperty(False)
86::CODE;;'''
87::CODE;;(internal) Determines if an ActionItem is displayed inside an

2::CODE;;Anchor Layout
3::CODE;;=============
4::CODE;;.. only:: html

6::CODE;;:align: right
7::CODE;;.. only:: latex
8::CODE;;.. image:: images/anchorlayout.png
9::CODE;;:align: right
10::CODE;;The :class:`AnchorLayout` aligns its children to a border (top, bottom,
11::CODE;;left, right) or center.
12::CODE;;To draw a button in the lower-right corner::
13::CODE;;layout = AnchorLayout(
14::CODE;;anchor_x='right', anchor_y='bottom')
15::CODE;;btn = Button(text='Hello World')

17::CODE;;'''
18::CODE;;__all__ = ('AnchorLayout', )
19::CODE;;from kivy.uix.layout import Layout
20::CODE;;from kivy.properties import OptionProperty, VariableListProperty
21::CODE;;class AnchorLayout(Layout):
22::CODE;;'''Anchor layout class. See the module documentation for more information.
23::CODE;;'''
24::CODE;;padding = VariableListProperty([0, 0, 0, 0])
25::CODE;;'''Padding between the widget box and its children, in pixels:
26::CODE;;[padding_left, padding_top, padding_right, padding_bottom].
27::CODE;;padding also accepts a two argument form [padding_horizontal,
28::CODE;;padding_vertical] and a one argument form [padding].
29::CODE;;:attr:`padding` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.VariableListProperty` and
30::CODE;;defaults to [0, 0, 0, 0].
31::CODE;;'''
32::CODE;;anchor_x = OptionProperty('center', options=(
33::CODE;;'left', 'center', 'right'))
34::CODE;;'''Horizontal anchor.
35::CODE;;:attr:`anchor_x` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.OptionProperty` and
36::CODE;;defaults to 'center'. It accepts values of 'left', 'center' or
37::CODE;;'right'.
38::CODE;;'''
39::CODE;;anchor_y = OptionProperty('center', options=(
40::CODE;;'top', 'center', 'bottom'))
41::CODE;;'''Vertical anchor.
42::CODE;;:attr:`anchor_y` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.OptionProperty` and
43::CODE;;defaults to 'center'. It accepts values of 'top', 'center' or
44::CODE;;'bottom'.
45::CODE;;'''
46::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
47::CODE;;super(AnchorLayout, self).__init__(**kwargs)
48::CODE;;fbind = self.fbind
49::CODE;;update = self._trigger_layout
50::CODE;;fbind('children', update)
51::CODE;;fbind('parent', update)
52::CODE;;fbind('padding', update)
53::CODE;;fbind('anchor_x', update)
54::CODE;;fbind('anchor_y', update)
55::CODE;;fbind('size', update)
56::CODE;;fbind('pos', update)
57::CODE;;def do_layout(self, *largs):
58::CODE;;_x, _y = self.pos
59::CODE;;width = self.width
60::CODE;;height = self.height
61::CODE;;anchor_x = self.anchor_x
62::CODE;;anchor_y = self.anchor_y
63::CODE;;pad_left, pad_top, pad_right, pad_bottom = self.padding
64::CODE;;for c in self.children:
65::CODE;;x, y = _x, _y
66::CODE;;cw, ch = c.size
67::CODE;;shw, shh = c.size_hint
68::CODE;;shw_min, shh_min = c.size_hint_min
69::CODE;;shw_max, shh_max = c.size_hint_max
70::CODE;;if shw is not None:
71::CODE;;cw = shw * (width - pad_left - pad_right)
72::CODE;;if shw_min is not None and cw < shw_min:
73::CODE;;cw = shw_min
74::CODE;;elif shw_max is not None and cw > shw_max:
75::CODE;;cw = shw_max
76::CODE;;if shh is not None:
77::CODE;;ch = shh * (height - pad_top - pad_bottom)
78::CODE;;if shh_min is not None and ch < shh_min:
79::CODE;;ch = shh_min
80::CODE;;elif shh_max is not None and ch > shh_max:
81::CODE;;ch = shh_max
82::CODE;;if anchor_x == 'left':
83::CODE;;x = x + pad_left
84::CODE;;elif anchor_x == 'right':
85::CODE;;x = x + width - (cw + pad_right)
86::CODE;;else:
87::CODE;;x = x + (width - pad_right + pad_left - cw) / 2
88::CODE;;if anchor_y == 'bottom':
89::CODE;;y = y + pad_bottom
90::CODE;;elif anchor_y == 'top':
91::CODE;;y = y + height - (ch + pad_top)
92::CODE;;else:
93::CODE;;y = y + (height - pad_top + pad_bottom - ch) / 2
94::CODE;;c.pos = x, y
95::CODE;;c.size = cw, ch

2::CODE;;Code Navigation Behavior
3::CODE;;========================
4::CODE;;The :class:`~kivy.uix.bahviors.CodeNavigationBehavior` modifies navigation
5::CODE;;behavior in the :class:`~kivy.uix.textinput.TextInput`, making it work like an
6::CODE;;IDE instead of a word processor.
7::CODE;;Using this mixin gives the TextInput the ability to recognize whitespace,
8::CODE;;punctuation and case variations (e.g. CamelCase) when moving over text. It
9::CODE;;is currently used by the :class:`~kivy.uix.codeinput.CodeInput` widget.
10::CODE;;'''
11::CODE;;__all__ = ('CodeNavigationBehavior', )
12::CODE;;from kivy.event import EventDispatcher
13::CODE;;import string
14::CODE;;class CodeNavigationBehavior(EventDispatcher):
15::CODE;;'''Code navigation behavior. Modifies the navigation behavior in TextInput
16::CODE;;to work like an IDE instead of a word processor. Please see the
17::CODE;;:mod:`code navigation behaviors module <kivy.uix.behaviors.codenavigation>`
18::CODE;;documentation for more information.
19::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.9.1
20::CODE;;'''
21::CODE;;def _move_cursor_word_left(self, index=None):
22::CODE;;pos = index or self.cursor_index()
23::CODE;;pos -= 1
24::CODE;;if pos == 0:
25::CODE;;return 0, 0
26::CODE;;col, row = self.get_cursor_from_index(pos)
27::CODE;;lines = self._lines
28::CODE;;ucase = string.ascii_uppercase
29::CODE;;lcase = string.ascii_lowercase
30::CODE;;ws = string.whitespace
31::CODE;;punct = string.punctuation
32::CODE;;mode = 'normal'
33::CODE;;rline = lines[row]
34::CODE;;c = rline[col] if len(rline) > col else '\n'
35::CODE;;if c in ws:
36::CODE;;mode = 'ws'
37::CODE;;elif c == '_':
38::CODE;;mode = 'us'
39::CODE;;elif c in punct:
40::CODE;;mode = 'punct'
41::CODE;;elif c not in ucase:
42::CODE;;mode = 'camel'
43::CODE;;while True:
44::CODE;;if col == -1:
45::CODE;;if row == 0:
46::CODE;;return 0, 0
47::CODE;;row -= 1
48::CODE;;rline = lines[row]
49::CODE;;col = len(rline)
50::CODE;;lc = c
51::CODE;;c = rline[col] if len(rline) > col else '\n'
52::CODE;;if c == '\n':
53::CODE;;if lc not in ws:
54::CODE;;col += 1
55::CODE;;break
56::CODE;;if mode in ('normal', 'camel') and c in ws:
57::CODE;;col += 1
58::CODE;;break
59::CODE;;if mode in ('normal', 'camel') and c in punct:
60::CODE;;col += 1
61::CODE;;break
62::CODE;;if mode == 'camel' and c in ucase:
63::CODE;;break
64::CODE;;if mode == 'punct' and (c == '_' or c not in punct):
65::CODE;;col += 1
66::CODE;;break
67::CODE;;if mode == 'us' and c != '_' and (c in punct or c in ws):
68::CODE;;col += 1
69::CODE;;break
70::CODE;;if mode == 'us' and c != '_':
71::CODE;;mode = ('normal' if c in ucase
72::CODE;;else 'ws' if c in ws
73::CODE;;else 'camel')
74::CODE;;elif mode == 'ws' and c not in ws:
75::CODE;;mode = ('normal' if c in ucase
76::CODE;;else 'us' if c == '_'
77::CODE;;else 'punct' if c in punct
78::CODE;;else 'camel')
79::CODE;;col -= 1
80::CODE;;if col > len(rline):
81::CODE;;if row == len(lines) - 1:
82::CODE;;return row, len(lines[row])
83::CODE;;row += 1
84::CODE;;col = 0
85::CODE;;return col, row
86::CODE;;def _move_cursor_word_right(self, index=None):
87::CODE;;pos = index or self.cursor_index()
88::CODE;;col, row = self.get_cursor_from_index(pos)
89::CODE;;lines = self._lines
90::CODE;;mrow = len(lines) - 1
91::CODE;;if row == mrow and col == len(lines[row]):
92::CODE;;return col, row
93::CODE;;ucase = string.ascii_uppercase
94::CODE;;lcase = string.ascii_lowercase
95::CODE;;ws = string.whitespace
96::CODE;;punct = string.punctuation
97::CODE;;mode = 'normal'
98::CODE;;rline = lines[row]
99::CODE;;c = rline[col] if len(rline) > col else '\n'
100::CODE;;if c in ws:
101::CODE;;mode = 'ws'
102::CODE;;elif c == '_':
103::CODE;;mode = 'us'
104::CODE;;elif c in punct:
105::CODE;;mode = 'punct'
106::CODE;;elif c in lcase:
107::CODE;;mode = 'camel'
108::CODE;;while True:
109::CODE;;if mode in ('normal', 'camel', 'punct') and c in ws:
110::CODE;;mode = 'ws'
111::CODE;;elif mode in ('normal', 'camel') and c == '_':
112::CODE;;mode = 'us'
113::CODE;;elif mode == 'normal' and c not in ucase:
114::CODE;;mode = 'camel'
115::CODE;;if mode == 'us':
116::CODE;;if c in ws:
117::CODE;;mode = 'ws'
118::CODE;;elif c != '_':
119::CODE;;break
120::CODE;;if mode == 'ws' and c not in ws:
121::CODE;;break
122::CODE;;if mode == 'camel' and c in ucase:
123::CODE;;break
124::CODE;;if mode == 'punct' and (c == '_' or c not in punct):
125::CODE;;break
126::CODE;;if mode != 'punct' and c != '_' and c in punct:
127::CODE;;break
128::CODE;;col += 1
129::CODE;;if col > len(rline):
130::CODE;;if row == mrow:
131::CODE;;return len(rline), mrow
132::CODE;;row += 1
133::CODE;;rline = lines[row]

136::CODE;;if c == '\n':

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Compound Selection Behavior
3::CODE;;===========================
4::CODE;;The :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.compoundselection.CompoundSelectionBehavior`
5::CODE;;`mixin <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixin>`_ class implements the logic
6::CODE;;behind keyboard and touch selection of selectable widgets managed by the
7::CODE;;derived widget. For example, it can be combined with a
8::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.gridlayout.GridLayout` to add selection to the layout.
9::CODE;;Compound selection concepts
10::CODE;;---------------------------
11::CODE;;At its core, it keeps a dynamic list of widgets that can be selected.
12::CODE;;Then, as the touches and keyboard input are passed in, it selects one or
13::CODE;;more of the widgets based on these inputs. For example, it uses the mouse
14::CODE;;scroll and keyboard up/down buttons to scroll through the list of widgets.
15::CODE;;Multiselection can also be achieved using the keyboard shift and ctrl keys.
16::CODE;;Finally, in addition to the up/down type keyboard inputs, compound selection
17::CODE;;can also accept letters from the keyboard to be used to select nodes with
18::CODE;;associated strings that start with those letters, similar to how files
19::CODE;;are selected by a file browser.
20::CODE;;Selection mechanics
21::CODE;;-------------------
22::CODE;;When the controller needs to select a node, it calls :meth:`select_node` and
23::CODE;;:meth:`deselect_node`. Therefore, they must be overwritten in order alter
24::CODE;;node selection. By default, the class doesn't listen for keyboard or
25::CODE;;touch events, so the derived widget must call
26::CODE;;:meth:`select_with_touch`, :meth:`select_with_key_down`, and
27::CODE;;:meth:`select_with_key_up` on events that it wants to pass on for selection
28::CODE;;purposes.
29::CODE;;Example
30::CODE;;-------
31::CODE;;To add selection to a grid layout which will contain
32::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.Button` widgets. For each button added to the layout, you
33::CODE;;need to bind the :attr:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.on_touch_down` of the button
34::CODE;;to :meth:`select_with_touch` to pass on the touch events::
35::CODE;;from kivy.uix.behaviors.compoundselection import CompoundSelectionBehavior
36::CODE;;from kivy.uix.button import Button
37::CODE;;from kivy.uix.gridlayout import GridLayout
38::CODE;;from kivy.uix.behaviors import FocusBehavior
39::CODE;;from kivy.core.window import Window
40::CODE;;from kivy.app import App
41::CODE;;class SelectableGrid(FocusBehavior, CompoundSelectionBehavior, GridLayout):
42::CODE;;def keyboard_on_key_down(self, window, keycode, text, modifiers):
46::CODE;;if super(SelectableGrid, self).keyboard_on_key_down(
47::CODE;;window, keycode, text, modifiers):
48::CODE;;return True
49::CODE;;if self.select_with_key_down(window, keycode, text, modifiers):
50::CODE;;return True
51::CODE;;return False
52::CODE;;def keyboard_on_key_up(self, window, keycode):
56::CODE;;if super(SelectableGrid, self).keyboard_on_key_up(window, keycode):
57::CODE;;return True
58::CODE;;if self.select_with_key_up(window, keycode):
59::CODE;;return True
60::CODE;;return False
61::CODE;;def add_widget(self, widget, *args, **kwargs):
64::CODE;;widget.bind(on_touch_down=self.button_touch_down,
65::CODE;;on_touch_up=self.button_touch_up)
66::CODE;;return super(SelectableGrid, self)\
67::CODE;;.add_widget(widget, *args, **kwargs)
68::CODE;;def button_touch_down(self, button, touch):
71::CODE;;if button.collide_point(*touch.pos):
72::CODE;;self.select_with_touch(button, touch)
73::CODE;;def button_touch_up(self, button, touch):
76::CODE;;if not (button.collide_point(*touch.pos) or
77::CODE;;self.touch_multiselect):
78::CODE;;self.deselect_node(button)
79::CODE;;def select_node(self, node):
80::CODE;;node.background_color = (1, 0, 0, 1)
81::CODE;;return super(SelectableGrid, self).select_node(node)
82::CODE;;def deselect_node(self, node):
83::CODE;;node.background_color = (1, 1, 1, 1)
84::CODE;;super(SelectableGrid, self).deselect_node(node)
85::CODE;;def on_selected_nodes(self, grid, nodes):
86::CODE;;print("Selected nodes = {0}".format(nodes))
87::CODE;;class TestApp(App):
88::CODE;;def build(self):
89::CODE;;grid = SelectableGrid(cols=3, rows=2, touch_multiselect=True,
90::CODE;;multiselect=True)
91::CODE;;for i in range(0, 6):
92::CODE;;grid.add_widget(Button(text="Button {0}".format(i)))
93::CODE;;return grid
94::CODE;;TestApp().run()
95::CODE;;.. warning::
96::CODE;;This code is still experimental, and its API is subject to change in a
97::CODE;;future version.
98::CODE;;'''
99::CODE;;__all__ = ('CompoundSelectionBehavior', )
100::CODE;;from time import time

103::CODE;;if 'KIVY_DOC' not in environ:

108::CODE;;class CompoundSelectionBehavior(object):
109::CODE;;'''The Selection behavior `mixin <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixin>`_
110::CODE;;implements the logic behind keyboard and touch
111::CODE;;selection of selectable widgets managed by the derived widget. Please see
112::CODE;;the :mod:`compound selection behaviors module
113::CODE;;<kivy.uix.behaviors.compoundselection>` documentation
114::CODE;;for more information.
115::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.9.0
116::CODE;;'''
117::CODE;;selected_nodes = ListProperty([])
118::CODE;;'''The list of selected nodes.
119::CODE;;.. note::
120::CODE;;Multiple nodes can be selected right after one another e.g. using the
121::CODE;;keyboard. When listening to :attr:`selected_nodes`, one should be
122::CODE;;aware of this.
123::CODE;;:attr:`selected_nodes` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.ListProperty` and
124::CODE;;defaults to the empty list, []. It is read-only and should not be modified.
125::CODE;;'''
126::CODE;;touch_multiselect = BooleanProperty(False)
127::CODE;;'''A special touch mode which determines whether touch events, as
128::CODE;;processed by :meth:`select_with_touch`, will add the currently touched
129::CODE;;node to the selection, or if it will clear the selection before adding the
130::CODE;;node. This allows the selection of multiple nodes by simply touching them.

278::CODE;;def select_with_key_down(self, keyboard, scancode, codepoint, modifiers,
279::CODE;;**kwargs):
280::CODE;;'''Processes a key press. This is called when a key press is to be used
281::CODE;;for selection. Depending on the keyboard keys pressed and the
282::CODE;;configuration, it could select or deselect nodes or node ranges
283::CODE;;from the selectable nodes list, :meth:`get_selectable_nodes`.
284::CODE;;The parameters are such that it could be bound directly to the
285::CODE;;on_key_down event of a keyboard. Therefore, it is safe to be called
286::CODE;;repeatedly when the key is held down as is done by the keyboard.
287::CODE;;:Returns:
288::CODE;;bool, True if the keypress was used, False otherwise.
289::CODE;;'''
290::CODE;;if not self.keyboard_select:
291::CODE;;return False
292::CODE;;keys = self._key_list
293::CODE;;multi = self.multiselect
294::CODE;;node_src, idx_src = self._resolve_last_node()
295::CODE;;text = scancode[1]
296::CODE;;if text == 'shift':
297::CODE;;self._shift_down = True
298::CODE;;elif text in ('ctrl', 'lctrl', 'rctrl'):
299::CODE;;self._ctrl_down = True
300::CODE;;elif (multi and 'ctrl' in modifiers and text in ('a', 'A') and
301::CODE;;text not in keys):
302::CODE;;sister_nodes = self.get_selectable_nodes()
303::CODE;;select = self.select_node
304::CODE;;for node in sister_nodes:
305::CODE;;select(node)
306::CODE;;keys.append(text)
307::CODE;;else:
308::CODE;;s = text
309::CODE;;if len(text) > 1:
310::CODE;;d = {'divide': '/', 'mul': '*', 'substract': '-', 'add': '+',
311::CODE;;'decimal': '.'}
312::CODE;;if text.startswith('numpad'):
313::CODE;;s = text[6:]
314::CODE;;if len(s) > 1:
315::CODE;;if s in d:
316::CODE;;s = d[s]
317::CODE;;else:
318::CODE;;s = None
319::CODE;;else:
320::CODE;;s = None
321::CODE;;if s is not None:
323::CODE;;if time() - self._last_key_time <= self.text_entry_timeout:
324::CODE;;self._word_filter += s
325::CODE;;else:
326::CODE;;self._word_filter = s
327::CODE;;keys.append(s)
328::CODE;;self._last_key_time = time()
329::CODE;;node, idx = self.goto_node(self._word_filter, node_src,
330::CODE;;idx_src)
331::CODE;;else:
332::CODE;;self._word_filter = ''
333::CODE;;node, idx = self.goto_node(text, node_src, idx_src)
334::CODE;;if node == node_src:
335::CODE;;return False
336::CODE;;multiselect = multi and 'ctrl' in modifiers
337::CODE;;if multi and 'shift' in modifiers:
338::CODE;;self._select_range(multiselect, True, node, idx)
339::CODE;;else:
340::CODE;;if not multiselect:
341::CODE;;self.clear_selection()

366::CODE;;def _update_counts(self, *largs):
368::CODE;;pc = self.page_count
369::CODE;;uc = self.up_count
370::CODE;;rc = self.right_count
371::CODE;;sc = self.scroll_count
372::CODE;;self._offset_counts = {'pageup': -pc, 'pagedown': pc, 'up': -uc,
373::CODE;;'down': uc, 'right': rc, 'left': -rc, 'scrollup': sc,
374::CODE;;'scrolldown': -sc, 'scrollright': -sc, 'scrollleft': sc}
375::CODE;;def _resolve_last_node(self):
378::CODE;;sister_nodes = self.get_selectable_nodes()
379::CODE;;if not len(sister_nodes):
380::CODE;;return None, 0

382::CODE;;last_idx = self._last_node_idx
383::CODE;;end = len(sister_nodes) - 1
384::CODE;;if last_node is None:
385::CODE;;last_node = self._anchor
386::CODE;;last_idx = self._anchor_idx
387::CODE;;if last_node is None:
388::CODE;;return sister_nodes[end], end
389::CODE;;if last_idx > end or sister_nodes[last_idx] != last_node:
390::CODE;;try:

392::CODE;;sister_nodes)

396::CODE;;def _select_range(self, multiselect, keep_anchor, node, idx):
397::CODE;;'''Selects a range between self._anchor and node or idx.
398::CODE;;If multiselect is True, it will be added to the selection, otherwise
399::CODE;;it will unselect everything before selecting the range. This is only
400::CODE;;called if self.multiselect is True.
401::CODE;;If keep anchor is False, the anchor is moved to node. This should
402::CODE;;always be True for keyboard selection.
403::CODE;;'''
404::CODE;;select = self.select_node
405::CODE;;sister_nodes = self.get_selectable_nodes()
406::CODE;;end = len(sister_nodes) - 1
407::CODE;;last_node = self._anchor
408::CODE;;last_idx = self._anchor_idx
409::CODE;;if last_node is None:
410::CODE;;last_idx = end
411::CODE;;last_node = sister_nodes[end]
412::CODE;;else:
413::CODE;;if last_idx > end or sister_nodes[last_idx] != last_node:
414::CODE;;try:
415::CODE;;last_idx = self.get_index_of_node(last_node, sister_nodes)
416::CODE;;except ValueError:
418::CODE;;return

421::CODE;;idx = self.get_index_of_node(node, sister_nodes)
422::CODE;;except ValueError:
423::CODE;;return

427::CODE;;self.clear_selection()
428::CODE;;for item in sister_nodes[last_idx:idx + 1]:
429::CODE;;select(item)
430::CODE;;if keep_anchor:
431::CODE;;self._anchor = last_node
432::CODE;;self._anchor_idx = last_idx
433::CODE;;else:
435::CODE;;self._anchor_idx = idx

437::CODE;;self._last_node_idx = idx
438::CODE;;def clear_selection(self):
439::CODE;;''' Deselects all the currently selected nodes.
440::CODE;;'''

447::CODE;;def get_selectable_nodes(self):
448::CODE;;'''(internal) Returns a list of the nodes that can be selected. It can
449::CODE;;be overwritten by the derived widget to return the correct list.
450::CODE;;This list is used to determine which nodes to select with group
451::CODE;;selection. E.g. the last element in the list will be selected when
452::CODE;;home is pressed, pagedown will move (or add to, if shift is held) the
453::CODE;;selection from the current position by negative :attr:`page_count`
454::CODE;;nodes starting from the position of the currently selected node in
455::CODE;;this list and so on. Still, nodes can be selected even if they are not
456::CODE;;in this list.
457::CODE;;.. note::
458::CODE;;It is safe to dynamically change this list including removing,
459::CODE;;adding, or re-arranging its elements. Nodes can be selected even
460::CODE;;if they are not on this list. And selected nodes removed from the
461::CODE;;list will remain selected until :meth:`deselect_node` is called.
462::CODE;;.. warning::
463::CODE;;Layouts display their children in the reverse order. That is, the
464::CODE;;contents of :attr:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.children` is displayed
465::CODE;;form right to left, bottom to top. Therefore, internally, the
466::CODE;;indices of the elements returned by this function are reversed to
467::CODE;;make it work by default for most layouts so that the final result
468::CODE;;is consistent e.g. home, although it will select the last element
469::CODE;;in this list visually, will select the first element when
470::CODE;;counting from top to bottom and left to right. If this behavior is
471::CODE;;not desired, a reversed list should be returned instead.
472::CODE;;Defaults to returning :attr:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.children`.
473::CODE;;'''
474::CODE;;return self.children
475::CODE;;def get_index_of_node(self, node, selectable_nodes):
476::CODE;;'''(internal) Returns the index of the `node` within the
477::CODE;;`selectable_nodes` returned by :meth:`get_selectable_nodes`.
478::CODE;;'''
479::CODE;;return selectable_nodes.index(node)
480::CODE;;def goto_node(self, key, last_node, last_node_idx):
481::CODE;;'''(internal) Used by the controller to get the node at the position
482::CODE;;indicated by key. The key can be keyboard inputs, e.g. pageup,
483::CODE;;or scroll inputs from the mouse scroll wheel, e.g. scrollup.
484::CODE;;'last_node' is the last node selected and is used to find the resulting
485::CODE;;node. For example, if the key is up, the returned node is one node
486::CODE;;up from the last node.
487::CODE;;It can be overwritten by the derived widget.
488::CODE;;:Parameters:
489::CODE;;`key`
490::CODE;;str, the string used to find the desired node. It can be any
491::CODE;;of the keyboard keys, as well as the mouse scrollup,
492::CODE;;scrolldown, scrollright, and scrollleft strings. If letters
493::CODE;;are typed in quick succession, the letters will be combined
494::CODE;;before it's passed in as key and can be used to find nodes that
495::CODE;;have an associated string that starts with those letters.
496::CODE;;`last_node`
497::CODE;;The last node that was selected.
498::CODE;;`last_node_idx`
499::CODE;;The cached index of the last node selected in the
500::CODE;;:meth:`get_selectable_nodes` list. If the list hasn't changed
501::CODE;;it saves having to look up the index of `last_node` in that
502::CODE;;list.
503::CODE;;:Returns:
504::CODE;;tuple, the node targeted by key and its index in the
505::CODE;;:meth:`get_selectable_nodes` list. Returning
506::CODE;;`(last_node, last_node_idx)` indicates a node wasn't found.
507::CODE;;'''
508::CODE;;sister_nodes = self.get_selectable_nodes()
509::CODE;;end = len(sister_nodes) - 1
510::CODE;;counts = self._offset_counts
511::CODE;;if end == -1:
512::CODE;;return last_node, last_node_idx
513::CODE;;if last_node_idx > end or sister_nodes[last_node_idx] != last_node:
515::CODE;;last_node_idx = self.get_index_of_node(last_node, sister_nodes)
516::CODE;;except ValueError:
517::CODE;;return last_node, last_node_idx
518::CODE;;is_reversed = self.nodes_order_reversed
519::CODE;;if key in counts:
520::CODE;;count = -counts[key] if is_reversed else counts[key]
521::CODE;;idx = max(min(count + last_node_idx, end), 0)
522::CODE;;return sister_nodes[idx], idx
523::CODE;;elif key == 'home':
524::CODE;;if is_reversed:
525::CODE;;return sister_nodes[end], end
526::CODE;;return sister_nodes[0], 0
527::CODE;;elif key == 'end':
528::CODE;;if is_reversed:
529::CODE;;return sister_nodes[0], 0
530::CODE;;return sister_nodes[end], end
531::CODE;;else:
532::CODE;;return last_node, last_node_idx

547::CODE;;'''
548::CODE;;nodes = self.selected_nodes
549::CODE;;if node in nodes:
550::CODE;;return False
551::CODE;;if (not self.multiselect) and len(nodes):
552::CODE;;self.clear_selection()
553::CODE;;if node not in nodes:

555::CODE;;self._anchor = node

574::CODE;;return False
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Cover Behavior
3::CODE;;==============
4::CODE;;The :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.cover.CoverBehavior`
5::CODE;;`mixin <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixin>`_ is intended for rendering
6::CODE;;textures to full widget size keeping the aspect ratio of the original texture.
7::CODE;;Use cases are i.e. rendering full size background images or video content in
8::CODE;;a dynamic layout.
9::CODE;;For an overview of behaviors, please refer to the :mod:`~kivy.uix.behaviors`
10::CODE;;documentation.
11::CODE;;Example
12::CODE;;-------
13::CODE;;The following examples add cover behavior to an image:
14::CODE;;In python:
15::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
16::CODE;;from kivy.app import App
17::CODE;;from kivy.uix.behaviors import CoverBehavior
18::CODE;;from kivy.uix.image import Image
19::CODE;;class CoverImage(CoverBehavior, Image):
20::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
21::CODE;;super(CoverImage, self).__init__(**kwargs)
22::CODE;;texture = self._coreimage.texture
23::CODE;;self.reference_size = texture.size
24::CODE;;self.texture = texture
25::CODE;;class MainApp(App):
26::CODE;;def build(self):
27::CODE;;return CoverImage(source='image.jpg')
28::CODE;;MainApp().run()
29::CODE;;In Kivy Language:
30::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
31::CODE;;CoverImage:
32::CODE;;source: 'image.png'
33::CODE;;<CoverImage@CoverBehavior+Image>:
34::CODE;;reference_size: self.texture_size
35::CODE;;See :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.cover.CoverBehavior` for details.
36::CODE;;'''
37::CODE;;__all__ = ('CoverBehavior', )
38::CODE;;from decimal import Decimal
39::CODE;;from kivy.lang import Builder
40::CODE;;from kivy.properties import ListProperty
61::CODE;;class CoverBehavior(object):
62::CODE;;'''The CoverBehavior `mixin <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixin>`_
63::CODE;;provides rendering a texture covering full widget size keeping aspect ratio
64::CODE;;of the original texture.
65::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.10.0
66::CODE;;'''
67::CODE;;reference_size = ListProperty([])
68::CODE;;'''Reference size used for aspect ratio approximation calculation.
69::CODE;;:attr:`reference_size` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.ListProperty` and
70::CODE;;defaults to `[]`.
71::CODE;;'''
72::CODE;;cover_size = ListProperty([0, 0])
73::CODE;;'''Size of the aspect ratio aware texture. Gets calculated in
74::CODE;;``CoverBehavior.calculate_cover``.
75::CODE;;:attr:`cover_size` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.ListProperty` and
76::CODE;;defaults to `[0, 0]`.
77::CODE;;'''
78::CODE;;cover_pos = ListProperty([0, 0])
79::CODE;;'''Position of the aspect ratio aware texture. Gets calculated in
80::CODE;;``CoverBehavior.calculate_cover``.
81::CODE;;:attr:`cover_pos` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.ListProperty` and
82::CODE;;defaults to `[0, 0]`.
83::CODE;;'''
84::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
85::CODE;;super(CoverBehavior, self).__init__(**kwargs)
87::CODE;;self.bind(
88::CODE;;size=self.calculate_cover,
89::CODE;;pos=self.calculate_cover
90::CODE;;)
91::CODE;;def _aspect_ratio_approximate(self, size):
93::CODE;;return Decimal('%.2f' % (float(size[0]) / size[1]))
94::CODE;;def _scale_size(self, size, sizer):
97::CODE;;size_new = list(sizer)
98::CODE;;i = size_new.index(None)
99::CODE;;j = i * -1 + 1
100::CODE;;size_new[i] = (size_new[j] * size[i]) / size[j]
101::CODE;;return tuple(size_new)
102::CODE;;def calculate_cover(self, *args):
104::CODE;;if not self.reference_size:
105::CODE;;return
106::CODE;;size = self.size
107::CODE;;origin_appr = self._aspect_ratio_approximate(self.reference_size)
108::CODE;;crop_appr = self._aspect_ratio_approximate(size)
110::CODE;;if origin_appr == crop_appr:
111::CODE;;crop_size = self.size
112::CODE;;offset = (0, 0)
114::CODE;;elif origin_appr < crop_appr:
115::CODE;;crop_size = self._scale_size(self.reference_size, (size[0], None))
116::CODE;;offset = (0, ((crop_size[1] - size[1]) / 2) * -1)
118::CODE;;else:
119::CODE;;crop_size = self._scale_size(self.reference_size, (None, size[1]))
120::CODE;;offset = (((crop_size[0] - size[0]) / 2) * -1, 0)
122::CODE;;self.cover_size = crop_size
123::CODE;;self.cover_pos = offset

112::CODE;;x, y = touch.pos
113::CODE;;if not self.collide_point(x, y):
114::CODE;;touch.ud[self._get_uid('svavoid')] = True

116::CODE;;if self._drag_touch or ('button' in touch.profile and
117::CODE;;touch.button.startswith('scroll')) or\
118::CODE;;not ((xx < x <= xx + w) and (yy < y <= yy + h)):
119::CODE;;return super(DragBehavior, self).on_touch_down(touch)

131::CODE;;def on_touch_move(self, touch):
132::CODE;;if self._get_uid('svavoid') in touch.ud or\
133::CODE;;self._drag_touch is not touch:
134::CODE;;return super(DragBehavior, self).on_touch_move(touch) or\
135::CODE;;self._get_uid() in touch.ud
136::CODE;;if touch.grab_current is not self:
137::CODE;;return True
