140::CODE;;mode = ud['mode']
141::CODE;;if mode == 'unknown':
142::CODE;;ud['dx'] += abs(touch.dx)
143::CODE;;ud['dy'] += abs(touch.dy)
144::CODE;;if ud['dx'] > sp(self.drag_distance):
145::CODE;;mode = 'drag'
146::CODE;;if ud['dy'] > sp(self.drag_distance):
147::CODE;;mode = 'drag'
148::CODE;;ud['mode'] = mode
149::CODE;;if mode == 'drag':
150::CODE;;self.x += touch.dx
151::CODE;;self.y += touch.dy

155::CODE;;return super(DragBehavior, self).on_touch_up(touch)
156::CODE;;if self._drag_touch and self in [x() for x in touch.grab_list]:

161::CODE;;super(DragBehavior, self).on_touch_down(touch)
162::CODE;;Clock.schedule_once(partial(self._do_touch_up, touch), .1)
163::CODE;;else:

165::CODE;;super(DragBehavior, self).on_touch_up(touch)
166::CODE;;return self._get_uid() in touch.ud
167::CODE;;def _do_touch_up(self, touch, *largs):
168::CODE;;super(DragBehavior, self).on_touch_up(touch)
170::CODE;;for x in touch.grab_list[:]:
171::CODE;;touch.grab_list.remove(x)
172::CODE;;x = x()
173::CODE;;if not x:
174::CODE;;continue
175::CODE;;touch.grab_current = x
176::CODE;;super(DragBehavior, self).on_touch_up(touch)
177::CODE;;touch.grab_current = None
178::CODE;;def _change_touch_mode(self, *largs):
179::CODE;;if not self._drag_touch:
180::CODE;;return
181::CODE;;uid = self._get_uid()
182::CODE;;touch = self._drag_touch
183::CODE;;ud = touch.ud[uid]
184::CODE;;if ud['mode'] != 'unknown':
185::CODE;;return
186::CODE;;touch.ungrab(self)
187::CODE;;self._drag_touch = None
188::CODE;;touch.push()
189::CODE;;touch.apply_transform_2d(self.parent.to_widget)
190::CODE;;super(DragBehavior, self).on_touch_down(touch)
191::CODE;;touch.pop()
192::CODE;;return

3::CODE;;Emacs Behavior

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Focus Behavior
3::CODE;;==============
4::CODE;;The :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.FocusBehavior`
5::CODE;;`mixin <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixin>`_ class provides
6::CODE;;keyboard focus behavior. When combined with other
7::CODE;;FocusBehavior widgets it allows one to cycle focus among them by pressing
8::CODE;;tab. In addition, upon gaining focus, the instance will automatically
9::CODE;;receive keyboard input.
10::CODE;;Focus, very different from selection, is intimately tied with the keyboard;
11::CODE;;each keyboard can focus on zero or one widgets, and each widget can only
12::CODE;;have the focus of one keyboard. However, multiple keyboards can focus
13::CODE;;simultaneously on different widgets. When escape is hit, the widget having
14::CODE;;the focus of that keyboard will de-focus.
15::CODE;;Managing focus
16::CODE;;--------------
17::CODE;;In essence, focus is implemented as a doubly linked list, where each
18::CODE;;node holds a (weak) reference to the instance before it and after it,
19::CODE;;as visualized when cycling through the nodes using tab (forward) or
20::CODE;;shift+tab (backward). If a previous or next widget is not specified,
21::CODE;;:attr:`focus_next` and :attr:`focus_previous` defaults to `None`. This
22::CODE;;means that the :attr:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.children` list and
23::CODE;;:attr:`parents <kivy.uix.widget.Widget.parent>` are
24::CODE;;walked to find the next focusable widget, unless :attr:`focus_next` or
25::CODE;;:attr:`focus_previous` is set to the `StopIteration` class, in which case
26::CODE;;focus stops there.
27::CODE;;For example, to cycle focus between :class:`~kivy.uix.button.Button`
28::CODE;;elements of a :class:`~kivy.uix.gridlayout.GridLayout`::
29::CODE;;class FocusButton(FocusBehavior, Button):
30::CODE;;pass
31::CODE;;grid = GridLayout(cols=4)
32::CODE;;for i in range(40):
33::CODE;;grid.add_widget(FocusButton(text=str(i)))
36::CODE;;When using a software keyboard, typical on mobile and touch devices, the
37::CODE;;keyboard display behavior is determined by the
38::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.core.window.WindowBase.softinput_mode` property. You can use
39::CODE;;this property to ensure the focused widget is not covered or obscured by the
40::CODE;;keyboard.
41::CODE;;Initializing focus
42::CODE;;------------------
43::CODE;;Widgets needs to be visible before they can receive the focus. This means that
44::CODE;;setting their *focus* property to True before they are visible will have no
45::CODE;;effect. To initialize focus, you can use the 'on_parent' event::
46::CODE;;from kivy.app import App
47::CODE;;from kivy.uix.textinput import TextInput
48::CODE;;class MyTextInput(TextInput):
49::CODE;;def on_parent(self, widget, parent):
50::CODE;;self.focus = True
51::CODE;;class SampleApp(App):
52::CODE;;def build(self):
53::CODE;;return MyTextInput()
54::CODE;;SampleApp().run()
55::CODE;;If you are using a :class:`~kivy.uix.popup`, you can use the 'on_open' event.
56::CODE;;For an overview of behaviors, please refer to the :mod:`~kivy.uix.behaviors`
57::CODE;;documentation.
58::CODE;;.. warning::
59::CODE;;This code is still experimental, and its API is subject to change in a
60::CODE;;future version.
61::CODE;;'''
62::CODE;;__all__ = ('FocusBehavior', )
63::CODE;;from kivy.properties import OptionProperty, ObjectProperty, BooleanProperty, \
64::CODE;;AliasProperty
65::CODE;;from kivy.config import Config
66::CODE;;from kivy.base import EventLoop
68::CODE;;_is_desktop = False
69::CODE;;_keyboard_mode = 'system'
70::CODE;;if Config:
71::CODE;;_is_desktop = Config.getboolean('kivy', 'desktop')
72::CODE;;_keyboard_mode = Config.get('kivy', 'keyboard_mode')
73::CODE;;class FocusBehavior(object):
74::CODE;;'''Provides keyboard focus behavior. When combined with other
75::CODE;;FocusBehavior widgets it allows one to cycle focus among them by pressing
76::CODE;;tab. Please see the
77::CODE;;:mod:`focus behavior module documentation <kivy.uix.behaviors.focus>`
78::CODE;;for more information.
79::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.9.0
80::CODE;;'''
81::CODE;;_requested_keyboard = False
82::CODE;;_keyboard = ObjectProperty(None, allownone=True)
83::CODE;;_keyboards = {}
84::CODE;;ignored_touch = []
85::CODE;;'''A list of touches that should not be used to defocus. After on_touch_up,
86::CODE;;every touch that is not in :attr:`ignored_touch` will defocus all the
87::CODE;;focused widgets if the config keyboard mode is not multi. Touches on
88::CODE;;focusable widgets that were used to focus are automatically added here.
89::CODE;;Example usage::
90::CODE;;class Unfocusable(Widget):
91::CODE;;def on_touch_down(self, touch):
92::CODE;;if self.collide_point(*touch.pos):
93::CODE;;FocusBehavior.ignored_touch.append(touch)
94::CODE;;Notice that you need to access this as a class, not an instance variable.
95::CODE;;'''
96::CODE;;def _set_keyboard(self, value):
97::CODE;;focus = self.focus
98::CODE;;keyboard = self._keyboard
99::CODE;;keyboards = FocusBehavior._keyboards
100::CODE;;if keyboard:
103::CODE;;del keyboards[keyboard]
104::CODE;;if value and value not in keyboards:
105::CODE;;keyboards[value] = None
106::CODE;;self._keyboard = value
107::CODE;;self.focus = focus
108::CODE;;def _get_keyboard(self):
109::CODE;;return self._keyboard
110::CODE;;keyboard = AliasProperty(_get_keyboard, _set_keyboard,
111::CODE;;bind=('_keyboard', ))
112::CODE;;'''The keyboard to bind to (or bound to the widget) when focused.
113::CODE;;When None, a keyboard is requested and released whenever the widget comes
114::CODE;;into and out of focus. If not None, it must be a keyboard, which gets
115::CODE;;bound and unbound from the widget whenever it's in or out of focus. It is
116::CODE;;useful only when more than one keyboard is available, so it is recommended
117::CODE;;to be set to None when only one keyboard is available.
118::CODE;;If more than one keyboard is available, whenever an instance gets focused
119::CODE;;a new keyboard will be requested if None. Unless the other instances lose
120::CODE;;focus (e.g. if tab was used), a new keyboard will appear. When this is
121::CODE;;undesired, the keyboard property can be used. For example, if there are
122::CODE;;two users with two keyboards, then each keyboard can be assigned to
123::CODE;;different groups of instances of FocusBehavior, ensuring that within
124::CODE;;each group, only one FocusBehavior will have focus, and will receive input
125::CODE;;from the correct keyboard. See `keyboard_mode` in :mod:`~kivy.config` for
126::CODE;;more information on the keyboard modes.
127::CODE;;**Keyboard and focus behavior**
128::CODE;;When using the keyboard, there are some important default behaviors you
129::CODE;;should keep in mind.
130::CODE;;* When Config's `keyboard_mode` is multi, each new touch is considered
131::CODE;;a touch by a different user and will set the focus (if clicked on a
132::CODE;;focusable) with a new keyboard. Already focused elements will not lose
133::CODE;;their focus (even if an unfocusable widget is touched).
134::CODE;;* If the keyboard property is set, that keyboard will be used when the
135::CODE;;instance gets focused. If widgets with different keyboards are linked
136::CODE;;through :attr:`focus_next` and :attr:`focus_previous`, then as they are
137::CODE;;tabbed through, different keyboards will become active. Therefore,
138::CODE;;typically it's undesirable to link instances which are assigned
139::CODE;;different keyboards.
140::CODE;;* When a widget has focus, setting its keyboard to None will remove its
141::CODE;;keyboard, but the widget will then immediately try to get
142::CODE;;another keyboard. In order to remove its keyboard, rather set its
143::CODE;;:attr:`focus` to False.
144::CODE;;* When using a software keyboard, typical on mobile and touch devices, the
145::CODE;;keyboard display behavior is determined by the
146::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.core.window.WindowBase.softinput_mode` property. You can use
147::CODE;;this property to ensure the focused widget is not covered or obscured.
148::CODE;;:attr:`keyboard` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.AliasProperty` and defaults
149::CODE;;to None.
150::CODE;;.. warning:
151::CODE;;When assigning a keyboard, the keyboard must not be released while
152::CODE;;it is still assigned to an instance. Similarly, the keyboard created
153::CODE;;by the instance on focus and assigned to :attr:`keyboard` if None,
154::CODE;;will be released by the instance when the instance loses focus.
155::CODE;;Therefore, it is not safe to assign this keyboard to another instance's
156::CODE;;:attr:`keyboard`.
157::CODE;;'''
158::CODE;;is_focusable = BooleanProperty(_is_desktop)
159::CODE;;'''Whether the instance can become focused. If focused, it'll lose focus
160::CODE;;when set to False.
161::CODE;;:attr:`is_focusable` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty` and
162::CODE;;defaults to True on a desktop (i.e. `desktop` is True in
163::CODE;;:mod:`~kivy.config`), False otherwise.
164::CODE;;'''
165::CODE;;focus = BooleanProperty(False)
166::CODE;;'''Whether the instance currently has focus.
167::CODE;;Setting it to True will bind to and/or request the keyboard, and input
168::CODE;;will be forwarded to the instance. Setting it to False will unbind
169::CODE;;and/or release the keyboard. For a given keyboard, only one widget can
170::CODE;;have its focus, so focusing one will automatically unfocus the other
171::CODE;;instance holding its focus.
172::CODE;;When using a software keyboard, please refer to the
173::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.core.window.WindowBase.softinput_mode` property to determine
174::CODE;;how the keyboard display is handled.
175::CODE;;:attr:`focus` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty` and defaults
176::CODE;;to False.
177::CODE;;'''
178::CODE;;focused = focus
179::CODE;;'''An alias of :attr:`focus`.
180::CODE;;:attr:`focused` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty` and defaults
181::CODE;;to False.
182::CODE;;.. warning::
183::CODE;;:attr:`focused` is an alias of :attr:`focus` and will be removed in
184::CODE;;2.0.0.
185::CODE;;'''
186::CODE;;keyboard_suggestions = BooleanProperty(True)
187::CODE;;'''If True provides auto suggestions on top of keyboard.
188::CODE;;This will only work if :attr:`input_type` is set to `text`, `url`, `mail` or
189::CODE;;`address`.
190::CODE;;.. warning::
191::CODE;;On Android, `keyboard_suggestions` relies on
192::CODE;;`InputType.TYPE_TEXT_FLAG_NO_SUGGESTIONS` to work, but some keyboards
193::CODE;;just ignore this flag. If you want to disable suggestions at all on
194::CODE;;Android, you can set `input_type` to `null`, which will request the
195::CODE;;input method to run in a limited "generate key events" mode.
196::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 2.1.0
197::CODE;;:attr:`keyboard_suggestions` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty`
198::CODE;;and defaults to True
199::CODE;;'''
200::CODE;;def _set_on_focus_next(self, instance, value):
201::CODE;;'''If changing focus, ensure your code does not create an infinite loop.
202::CODE;;eg:
203::CODE;;```python
204::CODE;;widget.focus_next = widget
205::CODE;;widget.focus_previous = widget
206::CODE;;```
207::CODE;;'''
208::CODE;;next_ = self._old_focus_next
210::CODE;;return
211::CODE;;if isinstance(next_, FocusBehavior):
212::CODE;;next_.focus_previous = None
213::CODE;;self._old_focus_next = value
214::CODE;;if value is None or value is StopIteration:
215::CODE;;return
216::CODE;;if not isinstance(value, FocusBehavior):
217::CODE;;raise ValueError('focus_next accepts only objects based on'
218::CODE;;' FocusBehavior, or the `StopIteration` class.')
219::CODE;;value.focus_previous = self

221::CODE;;'''The :class:`FocusBehavior` instance to acquire focus when

2::CODE;;Kivy Namespaces
3::CODE;;===============
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.9.1
5::CODE;;.. warning::
6::CODE;;This code is still experimental, and its API is subject to change in a
7::CODE;;future version.
8::CODE;;The :class:`KNSpaceBehavior` `mixin <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixin>`_
9::CODE;;class provides namespace functionality for Kivy objects. It allows kivy objects
10::CODE;;to be named and then accessed using namespaces.
11::CODE;;:class:`KNSpace` instances are the namespaces that store the named objects
12::CODE;;in Kivy :class:`~kivy.properties.ObjectProperty` instances.
13::CODE;;In addition, when inheriting from :class:`KNSpaceBehavior`, if the derived
14::CODE;;object is named, the name will automatically be added to the associated
15::CODE;;namespace and will point to a :attr:`~kivy.uix.widget.proxy_ref` of the
16::CODE;;derived object.
17::CODE;;Basic examples
18::CODE;;--------------
19::CODE;;By default, there's only a single namespace: the :attr:`knspace` namespace. The
20::CODE;;simplest example is adding a widget to the namespace:
21::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
22::CODE;;from kivy.uix.behaviors.knspace import knspace
23::CODE;;widget = Widget()
24::CODE;;knspace.my_widget = widget
25::CODE;;This adds a kivy :class:`~kivy.properties.ObjectProperty` with `rebind=True`
26::CODE;;and `allownone=True` to the :attr:`knspace` namespace with a property name
27::CODE;;`my_widget`. And the property now also points to this widget.
28::CODE;;This can be done automatically with:
29::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
30::CODE;;class MyWidget(KNSpaceBehavior, Widget):
31::CODE;;pass
32::CODE;;widget = MyWidget(knsname='my_widget')
33::CODE;;Or in kv:
34::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
35::CODE;;<MyWidget@KNSpaceBehavior+Widget>
36::CODE;;MyWidget:
37::CODE;;knsname: 'my_widget'
38::CODE;;Now, `knspace.my_widget` will point to that widget.
39::CODE;;When one creates a second widget with the same name, the namespace will
40::CODE;;also change to point to the new widget. E.g.:
41::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
42::CODE;;widget = MyWidget(knsname='my_widget')
44::CODE;;widget2 = MyWidget(knsname='my_widget')
46::CODE;;Setting the namespace
47::CODE;;---------------------
48::CODE;;One can also create ones own namespace rather than using the default
49::CODE;;:attr:`knspace` by directly setting :attr:`KNSpaceBehavior.knspace`:
50::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
51::CODE;;class MyWidget(KNSpaceBehavior, Widget):
52::CODE;;pass
53::CODE;;widget = MyWidget(knsname='my_widget')
54::CODE;;my_new_namespace = KNSpace()
55::CODE;;widget.knspace = my_new_namespace
56::CODE;;Initially, `my_widget` is added to the default namespace, but when the widget's
57::CODE;;namespace is changed to `my_new_namespace`, the reference to `my_widget` is
58::CODE;;moved to that namespace. We could have also of course first set the namespace
59::CODE;;to `my_new_namespace` and then have named the widget `my_widget`, thereby
60::CODE;;avoiding the initial assignment to the default namespace.
61::CODE;;Similarly, in kv:
62::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
63::CODE;;<MyWidget@KNSpaceBehavior+Widget>
64::CODE;;MyWidget:
65::CODE;;knspace: KNSpace()
66::CODE;;knsname: 'my_widget'
67::CODE;;Inheriting the namespace
68::CODE;;------------------------
69::CODE;;In the previous example, we directly set the namespace we wished to use.
70::CODE;;In the following example, we inherit it from the parent, so we only have to set
71::CODE;;it once:
72::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
73::CODE;;<MyWidget@KNSpaceBehavior+Widget>
74::CODE;;<MyLabel@KNSpaceBehavior+Label>
75::CODE;;<MyComplexWidget@MyWidget>:
76::CODE;;knsname: 'my_complex'
77::CODE;;MyLabel:
78::CODE;;knsname: 'label1'
79::CODE;;MyLabel:
80::CODE;;knsname: 'label2'
81::CODE;;Then, we do:
82::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
83::CODE;;widget = MyComplexWidget()
84::CODE;;new_knspace = KNSpace()
85::CODE;;widget.knspace = new_knspace
86::CODE;;The rule is that if no knspace has been assigned to a widget, it looks for a
87::CODE;;namespace in its parent and parent's parent and so on until it find one to
88::CODE;;use. If none are found, it uses the default :attr:`knspace`.
89::CODE;;When `MyComplexWidget` is created, it still used the default namespace.
90::CODE;;However, when we assigned the root widget its new namespace, all its
91::CODE;;children switched to using that new namespace as well. So `new_knspace` now
92::CODE;;contains `label1` and `label2` as well as `my_complex`.
93::CODE;;If we had first done:
94::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
95::CODE;;widget = MyComplexWidget()
96::CODE;;new_knspace = KNSpace()
97::CODE;;knspace.label1.knspace = knspace
98::CODE;;widget.knspace = new_knspace
99::CODE;;Then `label1` would remain stored in the default :attr:`knspace` since it was
100::CODE;;directly set, but `label2` and `my_complex` would still be added to the new
101::CODE;;namespace.
102::CODE;;One can customize the attribute used to search the parent tree by changing
103::CODE;;:attr:`KNSpaceBehavior.knspace_key`. If the desired knspace is not reachable
104::CODE;;through a widgets parent tree, e.g. in a popup that is not a widget's child,
105::CODE;;:attr:`KNSpaceBehavior.knspace_key` can be used to establish a different
106::CODE;;search order.
107::CODE;;Accessing the namespace
108::CODE;;-----------------------
109::CODE;;As seen in the previous example, if not directly assigned, the namespace is
110::CODE;;found by searching the parent tree. Consequently, if a namespace was assigned
111::CODE;;further up the parent tree, all its children and below could access that
112::CODE;;namespace through their :attr:`KNSpaceBehavior.knspace` property.
113::CODE;;This allows the creation of multiple widgets with identically given names
114::CODE;;if each root widget instance is assigned a new namespace. For example:
115::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
116::CODE;;<MyComplexWidget@KNSpaceBehavior+Widget>:
117::CODE;;Label:
118::CODE;;text: root.knspace.pretty.text if root.knspace.pretty else ''
119::CODE;;<MyPrettyWidget@KNSpaceBehavior+TextInput>:
120::CODE;;knsname: 'pretty'
121::CODE;;text: 'Hello'
122::CODE;;<MyCompositeWidget@KNSpaceBehavior+BoxLayout>:
123::CODE;;MyComplexWidget
124::CODE;;MyPrettyWidget
125::CODE;;Now, when we do:
126::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
127::CODE;;knspace1, knspace2 = KNSpace(), KNSpace()
128::CODE;;composite1 = MyCompositeWidget()
129::CODE;;composite1.knspace = knspace1
130::CODE;;composite2 = MyCompositeWidget()
131::CODE;;composite2.knspace = knspace2
132::CODE;;knspace1.pretty = "Here's the ladder, now fix the roof!"
133::CODE;;knspace2.pretty = "Get that raccoon off me!"
134::CODE;;Because each of the `MyCompositeWidget` instances have a different namespace
135::CODE;;their children also use different namespaces. Consequently, the
136::CODE;;pretty and complex widgets of each instance will have different text.
137::CODE;;Further, because both the namespace :class:`~kivy.properties.ObjectProperty`
138::CODE;;references, and :attr:`KNSpaceBehavior.knspace` have `rebind=True`, the
139::CODE;;text of the `MyComplexWidget` label is rebound to match the text of
140::CODE;;`MyPrettyWidget` when either the root's namespace changes or when the
141::CODE;;`root.knspace.pretty` property changes, as expected.
142::CODE;;Forking a namespace
143::CODE;;-------------------
144::CODE;;Forking a namespace provides the opportunity to create a new namespace
145::CODE;;from a parent namespace so that the forked namespace will contain everything
146::CODE;;in the origin namespace, but the origin namespace will not have access to
147::CODE;;anything added to the forked namespace.
148::CODE;;For example:
149::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
150::CODE;;child = knspace.fork()
151::CODE;;grandchild = child.fork()
152::CODE;;child.label = Label()
153::CODE;;grandchild.button = Button()
154::CODE;;Now label is accessible by both child and grandchild, but not by knspace. And
155::CODE;;button is only accessible by the grandchild but not by the child or by knspace.
156::CODE;;Finally, doing `grandchild.label = Label()` will leave `grandchild.label`
157::CODE;;and `child.label` pointing to different labels.
158::CODE;;A motivating example is the example from above:
159::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
160::CODE;;<MyComplexWidget@KNSpaceBehavior+Widget>:
161::CODE;;Label:
162::CODE;;text: root.knspace.pretty.text if root.knspace.pretty else ''
163::CODE;;<MyPrettyWidget@KNSpaceBehavior+TextInput>:
164::CODE;;knsname: 'pretty'
165::CODE;;text: 'Hello'
166::CODE;;<MyCompositeWidget@KNSpaceBehavior+BoxLayout>:
167::CODE;;knspace: 'fork'
168::CODE;;MyComplexWidget
169::CODE;;MyPrettyWidget
170::CODE;;Notice the addition of `knspace: 'fork'`. This is identical to doing
171::CODE;;`knspace: self.knspace.fork()`. However, doing that would lead to infinite
172::CODE;;recursion as that kv rule would be executed recursively because `self.knspace`
173::CODE;;will keep on changing. However, allowing `knspace: 'fork'` cirumvents that.
174::CODE;;See :attr:`KNSpaceBehavior.knspace`.
175::CODE;;Now, having forked, we just need to do:
176::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
177::CODE;;composite1 = MyCompositeWidget()
178::CODE;;composite2 = MyCompositeWidget()
179::CODE;;composite1.knspace.pretty = "Here's the ladder, now fix the roof!"
180::CODE;;composite2.knspace.pretty = "Get that raccoon off me!"
181::CODE;;Since by forking we automatically created a unique namespace for each
182::CODE;;`MyCompositeWidget` instance.
183::CODE;;'''
184::CODE;;__all__ = ('KNSpace', 'KNSpaceBehavior', 'knspace')
185::CODE;;from kivy.event import EventDispatcher
186::CODE;;from kivy.properties import StringProperty, ObjectProperty, AliasProperty
187::CODE;;from kivy.context import register_context
188::CODE;;class KNSpace(EventDispatcher):
189::CODE;;'''Each :class:`KNSpace` instance is a namespace that stores the named Kivy
190::CODE;;objects associated with this namespace. Each named object is
191::CODE;;stored as the value of a Kivy :class:`~kivy.properties.ObjectProperty` of
192::CODE;;this instance whose property name is the object's given name. Both `rebind`
193::CODE;;and `allownone` are set to `True` for the property.
194::CODE;;See :attr:`KNSpaceBehavior.knspace` for details on how a namespace is
195::CODE;;associated with a named object.
196::CODE;;When storing an object in the namespace, the object's `proxy_ref` is
197::CODE;;stored if the object has such an attribute.
198::CODE;;:Parameters:
199::CODE;;`parent`: (internal) A :class:`KNSpace` instance or None.
200::CODE;;If specified, it's a parent namespace, in which case, the current
201::CODE;;namespace will have in its namespace all its named objects
202::CODE;;as well as the named objects of its parent and parent's parent
203::CODE;;etc. See :meth:`fork` for more details.
204::CODE;;'''
205::CODE;;parent = None
206::CODE;;'''(internal) The parent namespace instance, :class:`KNSpace`, or None. See
207::CODE;;:meth:`fork`.
208::CODE;;'''
209::CODE;;__has_applied = None
210::CODE;;keep_ref = False
211::CODE;;'''Whether a direct reference should be kept to the stored objects.
212::CODE;;If ``True``, we use the direct object, otherwise we use
213::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.uix.widget.proxy_ref` when present.
214::CODE;;Defaults to False.
215::CODE;;'''
216::CODE;;def __init__(self, parent=None, keep_ref=False, **kwargs):
217::CODE;;self.keep_ref = keep_ref
218::CODE;;super(KNSpace, self).__init__(**kwargs)
219::CODE;;self.parent = parent
220::CODE;;self.__has_applied = set(self.properties().keys())
221::CODE;;def __setattr__(self, name, value):
222::CODE;;prop = super(KNSpace, self).property(name, quiet=True)
223::CODE;;has_applied = self.__has_applied
224::CODE;;if prop is None:
225::CODE;;if hasattr(self, name):
226::CODE;;super(KNSpace, self).__setattr__(name, value)
227::CODE;;else:
228::CODE;;self.apply_property(
229::CODE;;**{name:
230::CODE;;ObjectProperty(None, rebind=True, allownone=True)}
231::CODE;;)
232::CODE;;if not self.keep_ref:
233::CODE;;value = getattr(value, 'proxy_ref', value)
234::CODE;;has_applied.add(name)
235::CODE;;super(KNSpace, self).__setattr__(name, value)
236::CODE;;elif name not in has_applied:
237::CODE;;self.apply_property(**{name: prop})
238::CODE;;has_applied.add(name)
239::CODE;;if not self.keep_ref:
240::CODE;;value = getattr(value, 'proxy_ref', value)
241::CODE;;super(KNSpace, self).__setattr__(name, value)
242::CODE;;else:
243::CODE;;if not self.keep_ref:
244::CODE;;value = getattr(value, 'proxy_ref', value)
245::CODE;;super(KNSpace, self).__setattr__(name, value)
246::CODE;;def __getattribute__(self, name):
247::CODE;;if name in super(KNSpace, self).__getattribute__('__dict__'):
248::CODE;;return super(KNSpace, self).__getattribute__(name)
249::CODE;;try:
250::CODE;;value = super(KNSpace, self).__getattribute__(name)
251::CODE;;except AttributeError:
252::CODE;;parent = super(KNSpace, self).__getattribute__('parent')
253::CODE;;if parent is None:
254::CODE;;raise AttributeError(name)
255::CODE;;return getattr(parent, name)
256::CODE;;if value is not None:
257::CODE;;return value
258::CODE;;parent = super(KNSpace, self).__getattribute__('parent')
259::CODE;;if parent is None:
260::CODE;;return None
261::CODE;;try:
263::CODE;;except AttributeError:
264::CODE;;return None
265::CODE;;def property(self, name, quiet=False):
267::CODE;;prop = super(KNSpace, self).property(name, quiet=True)
268::CODE;;if prop is not None:
269::CODE;;return prop
270::CODE;;prop = ObjectProperty(None, rebind=True, allownone=True)
271::CODE;;self.apply_property(**{name: prop})
272::CODE;;self.__has_applied.add(name)
273::CODE;;return prop
274::CODE;;def fork(self):
275::CODE;;'''Returns a new :class:`KNSpace` instance which will have access to
276::CODE;;all the named objects in the current namespace but will also have a
277::CODE;;namespace of its own that is unique to it.
278::CODE;;For example:
279::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
280::CODE;;forked_knspace1 = knspace.fork()
281::CODE;;forked_knspace2 = knspace.fork()
282::CODE;;Now, any names added to `knspace` will be accessible by the
283::CODE;;`forked_knspace1` and `forked_knspace2` namespaces by the normal means.
284::CODE;;However, any names added to `forked_knspace1` will not be accessible
285::CODE;;from `knspace` or `forked_knspace2`. Similar for `forked_knspace2`.
286::CODE;;'''
287::CODE;;return KNSpace(parent=self)
288::CODE;;class KNSpaceBehavior(object):
289::CODE;;'''Inheriting from this class allows naming of the inherited objects, which
290::CODE;;are then added to the associated namespace :attr:`knspace` and accessible
291::CODE;;through it.
292::CODE;;Please see the :mod:`knspace behaviors module <kivy.uix.behaviors.knspace>`
293::CODE;;documentation for more information.
294::CODE;;'''
295::CODE;;_knspace = ObjectProperty(None, allownone=True)
296::CODE;;_knsname = StringProperty('')
297::CODE;;__last_knspace = None
298::CODE;;__callbacks = None
299::CODE;;def __init__(self, knspace=None, **kwargs):
300::CODE;;self.knspace = knspace
301::CODE;;super(KNSpaceBehavior, self).__init__(**kwargs)
302::CODE;;def __knspace_clear_callbacks(self, *largs):
303::CODE;;for obj, name, uid in self.__callbacks:
304::CODE;;obj.unbind_uid(name, uid)
305::CODE;;last = self.__last_knspace
306::CODE;;self.__last_knspace = self.__callbacks = None
307::CODE;;assert self._knspace is None
308::CODE;;assert last
309::CODE;;new = self.__set_parent_knspace()
310::CODE;;if new is last:
311::CODE;;return
312::CODE;;self.property('_knspace').dispatch(self)
313::CODE;;name = self.knsname
314::CODE;;if not name:
315::CODE;;return
316::CODE;;if getattr(last, name) == self:
317::CODE;;setattr(last, name, None)
318::CODE;;if new:
319::CODE;;setattr(new, name, self)
320::CODE;;else:
321::CODE;;raise ValueError('Object has name "{}", but no namespace'.
322::CODE;;format(name))
323::CODE;;def __set_parent_knspace(self):
324::CODE;;callbacks = self.__callbacks = []
325::CODE;;fbind = self.fbind
326::CODE;;append = callbacks.append
327::CODE;;parent_key = self.knspace_key
328::CODE;;clear = self.__knspace_clear_callbacks
329::CODE;;append((self, 'knspace_key', fbind('knspace_key', clear)))
330::CODE;;if not parent_key:
331::CODE;;self.__last_knspace = knspace
332::CODE;;return knspace
333::CODE;;append((self, parent_key, fbind(parent_key, clear)))
334::CODE;;parent = getattr(self, parent_key, None)
335::CODE;;while parent is not None:
336::CODE;;fbind = parent.fbind
337::CODE;;parent_knspace = getattr(parent, 'knspace', 0)
338::CODE;;if parent_knspace != 0:
339::CODE;;append((parent, 'knspace', fbind('knspace', clear)))
340::CODE;;self.__last_knspace = parent_knspace
341::CODE;;return parent_knspace
342::CODE;;append((parent, parent_key, fbind(parent_key, clear)))
343::CODE;;new_parent = getattr(parent, parent_key, None)
344::CODE;;if new_parent is parent:
345::CODE;;break
346::CODE;;parent = new_parent
347::CODE;;self.__last_knspace = knspace
348::CODE;;return knspace
349::CODE;;def _get_knspace(self):
350::CODE;;_knspace = self._knspace
351::CODE;;if _knspace is not None:
352::CODE;;return _knspace
353::CODE;;if self.__callbacks is not None:
354::CODE;;return self.__last_knspace
356::CODE;;return self.__set_parent_knspace()
357::CODE;;def _set_knspace(self, value):
358::CODE;;if value is self._knspace:
359::CODE;;return
360::CODE;;knspace = self._knspace or self.__last_knspace
361::CODE;;name = self.knsname
362::CODE;;if name and knspace and getattr(knspace, name) == self:
364::CODE;;if value == 'fork':
365::CODE;;if not knspace:
367::CODE;;if knspace:
368::CODE;;value = knspace.fork()
369::CODE;;else:
370::CODE;;raise ValueError('Cannot fork with no namespace')
371::CODE;;for obj, prop_name, uid in self.__callbacks or []:
372::CODE;;obj.unbind_uid(prop_name, uid)
373::CODE;;self.__last_knspace = self.__callbacks = None
374::CODE;;if name:
376::CODE;;knspace = self.__set_parent_knspace()
377::CODE;;if knspace:
378::CODE;;setattr(knspace, name, self)
380::CODE;;else:
381::CODE;;setattr(value, name, self)
382::CODE;;knspace = self._knspace = value
383::CODE;;if not knspace:
384::CODE;;raise ValueError('Object has name "{}", but no namespace'.
385::CODE;;format(name))
386::CODE;;else:
387::CODE;;if value is None:
389::CODE;;self._knspace = value
390::CODE;;knspace = AliasProperty(
391::CODE;;_get_knspace, _set_knspace, bind=('_knspace', ), cache=False,
392::CODE;;rebind=True, allownone=True)
393::CODE;;'''The namespace instance, :class:`KNSpace`, associated with this widget.
394::CODE;;The :attr:`knspace` namespace stores this widget when naming this widget
395::CODE;;with :attr:`knsname`.
396::CODE;;If the namespace has been set with a :class:`KNSpace` instance, e.g. with
397::CODE;;`self.knspace = KNSpace()`, then that instance is returned (setting with
398::CODE;;`None` doesn't count). Otherwise, if :attr:`knspace_key` is not None, we
399::CODE;;look for a namespace to use in the object that is stored in the property
400::CODE;;named :attr:`knspace_key`, of this instance. I.e.
401::CODE;;`object = getattr(self, self.knspace_key)`.
402::CODE;;If that object has a knspace property, then we return its value. Otherwise,
403::CODE;;we go further up, e.g. with `getattr(object, self.knspace_key)` and look
404::CODE;;for its `knspace` property.
405::CODE;;Finally, if we reach a value of `None`, or :attr:`knspace_key` was `None`,
406::CODE;;the default :attr:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.knspace.knspace` namespace is
407::CODE;;returned.
408::CODE;;If :attr:`knspace` is set to the string `'fork'`, the current namespace
409::CODE;;in :attr:`knspace` will be forked with :meth:`KNSpace.fork` and the
410::CODE;;resulting namespace will be assigned to this instance's :attr:`knspace`.
411::CODE;;See the module examples for a motivating example.
412::CODE;;Both `rebind` and `allownone` are `True`.
413::CODE;;'''
414::CODE;;knspace_key = StringProperty('parent', allownone=True)
415::CODE;;'''The name of the property of this instance, to use to search upwards for
416::CODE;;a namespace to use by this instance. Defaults to `'parent'` so that we'll
417::CODE;;search the parent tree. See :attr:`knspace`.
418::CODE;;When `None`, we won't search the parent tree for the namespace.
419::CODE;;`allownone` is `True`.
420::CODE;;'''
421::CODE;;def _get_knsname(self):
422::CODE;;return self._knsname
423::CODE;;def _set_knsname(self, value):
424::CODE;;old_name = self._knsname
425::CODE;;knspace = self.knspace
426::CODE;;if old_name and knspace and getattr(knspace, old_name) == self:
427::CODE;;setattr(knspace, old_name, None)
428::CODE;;self._knsname = value
429::CODE;;if value:
430::CODE;;if knspace:
431::CODE;;setattr(knspace, value, self)
432::CODE;;else:
433::CODE;;raise ValueError('Object has name "{}", but no namespace'.
434::CODE;;format(value))
435::CODE;;knsname = AliasProperty(
436::CODE;;_get_knsname, _set_knsname, bind=('_knsname', ), cache=False)
437::CODE;;'''The name given to this instance. If named, the name will be added to the
438::CODE;;associated :attr:`knspace` namespace, which will then point to the
439::CODE;;`proxy_ref` of this instance.
440::CODE;;When named, one can access this object by e.g. self.knspace.name, where
441::CODE;;`name` is the given name of this instance. See :attr:`knspace` and the
442::CODE;;module description for more details.
443::CODE;;'''
444::CODE;;knspace = register_context('knspace', KNSpace)
445::CODE;;'''The default :class:`KNSpace` namespace. See :attr:`KNSpaceBehavior.knspace`
446::CODE;;for more details.
447::CODE;;'''

118::CODE;;class _GroupAccessor:
127::CODE;;def __get__(self, instance, owner):
128::CODE;;if instance is None:
130::CODE;;return lambda group: self._get_by_identifier(owner, group)
131::CODE;;else:
133::CODE;;return lambda: self._get_by_instance(instance)

142::CODE;;def _get_widgets_from_group(self, cls, owner, name):
149::CODE;;This mixin extends :class:`ButtonBehavior` to provide persistent on/off
150::CODE;;state that survives beyond the press/release interaction. It supports
151::CODE;;grouping multiple toggles together for radio button behavior.
152::CODE;;State Management
153::CODE;;----------------
154::CODE;;Unlike the transient :attr:`pressed` property from ButtonBehavior (which
155::CODE;;is True only during active touch), the :attr:`active` property maintains
156::CODE;;persistent state:
157::CODE;;- **active=True**: Button is in "on" state (persists after release)
158::CODE;;- **active=False**: Button is in "off" state (default)
159::CODE;;The :attr:`active` property can be set programmatically or toggled by
160::CODE;;user interaction. When :attr:`allow_no_selection` is False, attempts to
161::CODE;;deactivate the last active button in a group will be silently rejected.
162::CODE;;Group Behavior
163::CODE;;--------------
164::CODE;;When buttons share a :attr:`group`, they act like radio buttons:
165::CODE;;- Activating one button automatically deactivates others in the group
166::CODE;;- Only one button per group can be active at a time
167::CODE;;- :attr:`allow_no_selection` controls whether all buttons can be deactivated
168::CODE;;**Without group**: Buttons toggle independently
169::CODE;;**With group**: Buttons behave as mutually exclusive options
170::CODE;;Group Scoping
171::CODE;;~~~~~~~~~~~~~
172::CODE;;Groups can be either global or scoped to a specific widget owner:
173::CODE;;**Global groups** (string)::
174::CODE;;ToggleButton:
176::CODE;;**Scoped groups** (tuple)::
177::CODE;;ToggleButton:
179::CODE;;Scoped groups allow multiple widget hierarchies to use the same group
180::CODE;;name without interference. This is useful when creating reusable
181::CODE;;components with internal toggle groups.
182::CODE;;Example::
183::CODE;;<MyComponent>:
185::CODE;;ToggleButton:
186::CODE;;group: (root, "options")
187::CODE;;ToggleButton:
188::CODE;;group: (root, "options")
189::CODE;;Events
190::CODE;;------
191::CODE;;Inherits all events from ButtonBehavior:
192::CODE;;- :meth:`on_press`: First touch down
193::CODE;;- :meth:`on_release`: All touches released
194::CODE;;- :meth:`on_cancel`: Touch moved outside bounds
195::CODE;;Additional property events:
196::CODE;;- :meth:`on_active`: When active state changes
197::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.8.0
198::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 3.0.0
199::CODE;;- Replaced ``state`` OptionProperty with ``active`` AliasProperty
200::CODE;;- Added backward-compatible ``state`` alias
201::CODE;;- Improved group management with automatic cleanup
202::CODE;;- Added scoped group support via tuple syntax
203::CODE;;- Replaced ``get_widgets(groupname)`` static method with unified
204::CODE;;``get_group()`` descriptor that works as both instance and class method
209::CODE;;independently).
210::CODE;;Accepts two formats:
211::CODE;;- **Hashable value** (string, int, etc.): Global group shared across entire
212::CODE;;application
213::CODE;;- **Tuple (owner, name)**: Scoped group limited to owner's context
214::CODE;;Global groups (any hashable)::
215::CODE;;group: "mygroup"
216::CODE;;group: 42
217::CODE;;group: MyEnum.OPTION_A
218::CODE;;Scoped groups (tuple of any object + hashable name)::
219::CODE;;group: (root, "mygroup")
220::CODE;;group: (self.parent, "options")
221::CODE;;group: (app.current_screen, "filters")
222::CODE;;**Tuple format**: ``(owner, name)``
223::CODE;;- **owner**: Any object to scope the group to (typically a widget).
224::CODE;;Uses object identity, not equality. Can be weakly referenced.
225::CODE;;- **name**: Hashable identifier for the group (string, int, enum, etc.)
226::CODE;;Only one button per group can be active at a time. When a button in a
227::CODE;;group is activated, all other buttons in that group are automatically
228::CODE;;deactivated.
229::CODE;;Scoped groups allow multiple widget instances to use the same group name
230::CODE;;without interference, making it easier to create reusable components.
231::CODE;;Example of reusable component::
233::CODE;;<FilterPanel>:
234::CODE;;ToggleButton:
235::CODE;;group: (root, "size")
236::CODE;;text: "Small"
237::CODE;;ToggleButton:
238::CODE;;group: (root, "size")
239::CODE;;text: "Large"
241::CODE;;FilterPanel:
242::CODE;;id: panel1
243::CODE;;FilterPanel:
244::CODE;;id: panel2
245::CODE;;:attr:`group` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.ObjectProperty` and defaults
246::CODE;;to None.
247::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 3.0.0
248::CODE;;Added support for tuple format to enable scoped groups.
252::CODE;;- **True (default)**: Clicking active button deactivates it (all buttons off)
253::CODE;;- **False**: At least one button must remain active (radio button behavior)
254::CODE;;When False, attempts to deactivate the last active button (via touch or
255::CODE;;programmatic ``active = False``) are silently rejected.
256::CODE;;Only applies when :attr:`group` is set.
257::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.9.0
258::CODE;;:attr:`allow_no_selection` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty`
259::CODE;;and defaults to True.
263::CODE;;return self._active
264::CODE;;def _set_active(self, value):
272::CODE;;self._change_active_state(value)
273::CODE;;active = AliasProperty(
274::CODE;;_get_active, _set_active, bind=["_active"], cache=True
275::CODE;;)
290::CODE;;toggle_on = OptionProperty("release", options=["press", "release"])
302::CODE;;get_group = _GroupAccessor()
342::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
346::CODE;;self._current_group_key = (None, None)
348::CODE;;self.fbind("group", self._handle_group)
350::CODE;;super().__init__(**kwargs)
352::CODE;;def _do_press(self):
353::CODE;;if self.toggle_on == "press":
354::CODE;;self._handle_toggle_on()
356::CODE;;def _do_release(self):
357::CODE;;if self.toggle_on == "release":
358::CODE;;self._handle_toggle_on()
359::CODE;;def _change_active_state(self, new_value):
375::CODE;;owner, name = self._current_group_key
377::CODE;;if not new_value and not self.allow_no_selection and name:
378::CODE;;for w in self._toggle_groups[owner][name]:
379::CODE;;if w is not self and w.active:
380::CODE;;break
381::CODE;;else:
384::CODE;;self._active = new_value
387::CODE;;if new_value and name is not None:
388::CODE;;self._deactivate_group_siblings()
389::CODE;;def _handle_toggle_on(self, *args):
399::CODE;;owner, name = self._current_group_key
400::CODE;;if not self.allow_no_selection and name and self.active:
401::CODE;;return
402::CODE;;self._change_active_state(not self.active)
403::CODE;;def _parse_group(self, group):
412::CODE;;return self._parse_group_static(group)
413::CODE;;@staticmethod
414::CODE;;def _parse_group_static(group):
421::CODE;;if group is None:
422::CODE;;return None, None
423::CODE;;if isinstance(group, tuple):
424::CODE;;if len(group) != 2:
425::CODE;;raise ValueError(
426::CODE;;f"Group tuple must have exactly 2 elements (owner, name), "
427::CODE;;f"got {len(group)}"
428::CODE;;)
429::CODE;;owner, name = group
430::CODE;;if name is None:
431::CODE;;raise ValueError(
432::CODE;;"Group name (second tuple element) cannot be None"
433::CODE;;)
434::CODE;;return owner, name
435::CODE;;return None, group
436::CODE;;def _validate_group_name(self, name):
441::CODE;;if name is not None:
442::CODE;;try:
443::CODE;;hash(name)
444::CODE;;except TypeError:
445::CODE;;raise ValueError(
446::CODE;;f"Group name must be hashable, got {type(name).__name__}"
447::CODE;;)
448::CODE;;def _handle_group(self, instance, new_group):
459::CODE;;owner, name = self._parse_group(new_group)
460::CODE;;self._validate_group_name(name)
462::CODE;;old_owner, old_name = self._current_group_key
463::CODE;;if old_name is not None:
464::CODE;;self._toggle_groups[old_owner][old_name].discard(self)
466::CODE;;if not self._toggle_groups[old_owner][old_name]:
467::CODE;;del self._toggle_groups[old_owner][old_name]
469::CODE;;if not self._toggle_groups[old_owner]:
470::CODE;;del self._toggle_groups[old_owner]
472::CODE;;if name is not None:
473::CODE;;self._toggle_groups[owner][name].add(self)
474::CODE;;self._current_group_key = (owner, name)
476::CODE;;if self.active and name is not None:
477::CODE;;self._deactivate_group_siblings()
478::CODE;;def _deactivate_group_siblings(self):
482::CODE;;owner, name = self._current_group_key
483::CODE;;if name is None:
484::CODE;;return
485::CODE;;for widget in self._toggle_groups[owner][name]:
486::CODE;;if widget is not self and widget.active:
487::CODE;;widget.active = False
488::CODE;;def on_active(self, instance, value):
494::CODE;;pass
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Touch Ripple
3::CODE;;============
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.10.1
5::CODE;;.. warning::
6::CODE;;This code is still experimental, and its API is subject to change in a
7::CODE;;future version.
8::CODE;;This module contains `mixin <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixin>`_ classes
9::CODE;;to add a touch ripple visual effect known from `Google Material Design
10::CODE;;<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Material_Design>_` to widgets.
11::CODE;;For an overview of behaviors, please refer to the :mod:`~kivy.uix.behaviors`
12::CODE;;documentation.
13::CODE;;The class :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.touchripple.TouchRippleBehavior` provides
14::CODE;;rendering the ripple animation.
15::CODE;;The class :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.touchripple.TouchRippleButtonBehavior`
16::CODE;;basically provides the same functionality as
17::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.button.ButtonBehavior` but rendering the ripple
18::CODE;;animation instead of default press/release visualization.
19::CODE;;'''
20::CODE;;from kivy.animation import Animation
21::CODE;;from kivy.clock import Clock
22::CODE;;from kivy.graphics import CanvasBase, Color, Ellipse, ScissorPush, ScissorPop
23::CODE;;from kivy.properties import BooleanProperty, ListProperty, NumericProperty, \
24::CODE;;ObjectProperty, StringProperty
25::CODE;;from kivy.uix.relativelayout import RelativeLayout
26::CODE;;__all__ = (
27::CODE;;'TouchRippleBehavior',
28::CODE;;'TouchRippleButtonBehavior'
29::CODE;;)
30::CODE;;class TouchRippleBehavior(object):
31::CODE;;'''Touch ripple behavior.
32::CODE;;Supposed to be used as mixin on widget classes.
33::CODE;;Ripple behavior does not trigger automatically, concrete implementation
34::CODE;;needs to call :func:`ripple_show` respective :func:`ripple_fade` manually.
35::CODE;;Example
36::CODE;;-------
37::CODE;;Here we create a Label which renders the touch ripple animation on
38::CODE;;interaction::
39::CODE;;class RippleLabel(TouchRippleBehavior, Label):
40::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
41::CODE;;super(RippleLabel, self).__init__(**kwargs)
42::CODE;;def on_touch_down(self, touch):
43::CODE;;collide_point = self.collide_point(touch.x, touch.y)
44::CODE;;if collide_point:
45::CODE;;touch.grab(self)
46::CODE;;self.ripple_show(touch)
47::CODE;;return True
48::CODE;;return False
49::CODE;;def on_touch_up(self, touch):
50::CODE;;if touch.grab_current is self:
51::CODE;;touch.ungrab(self)
52::CODE;;self.ripple_fade()
53::CODE;;return True
54::CODE;;return False
55::CODE;;'''
56::CODE;;ripple_rad_default = NumericProperty(10)
57::CODE;;'''Default radius the animation starts from.
58::CODE;;:attr:`ripple_rad_default` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty`
59::CODE;;and defaults to `10`.
60::CODE;;'''
61::CODE;;ripple_duration_in = NumericProperty(.5)
62::CODE;;'''Animation duration taken to show the overlay.
63::CODE;;:attr:`ripple_duration_in` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty`
64::CODE;;and defaults to `0.5`.
65::CODE;;'''
66::CODE;;ripple_duration_out = NumericProperty(.2)
67::CODE;;'''Animation duration taken to fade the overlay.
68::CODE;;:attr:`ripple_duration_out` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty`
69::CODE;;and defaults to `0.2`.
70::CODE;;'''
71::CODE;;ripple_fade_from_alpha = NumericProperty(.5)
72::CODE;;'''Alpha channel for ripple color the animation starts with.
73::CODE;;:attr:`ripple_fade_from_alpha` is a
74::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and defaults to `0.5`.
75::CODE;;'''
76::CODE;;ripple_fade_to_alpha = NumericProperty(.8)
77::CODE;;'''Alpha channel for ripple color the animation targets to.
78::CODE;;:attr:`ripple_fade_to_alpha` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty`
79::CODE;;and defaults to `0.8`.
80::CODE;;'''
81::CODE;;ripple_scale = NumericProperty(2.)
82::CODE;;'''Max scale of the animation overlay calculated from max(width/height) of
83::CODE;;the decorated widget.
84::CODE;;:attr:`ripple_scale` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty`
85::CODE;;and defaults to `2.0`.
86::CODE;;'''
87::CODE;;ripple_func_in = StringProperty('in_cubic')
88::CODE;;'''Animation callback for showing the overlay.
89::CODE;;:attr:`ripple_func_in` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.StringProperty`
90::CODE;;and defaults to `in_cubic`.
91::CODE;;'''
92::CODE;;ripple_func_out = StringProperty('out_quad')
93::CODE;;'''Animation callback for hiding the overlay.
94::CODE;;:attr:`ripple_func_out` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.StringProperty`
95::CODE;;and defaults to `out_quad`.
96::CODE;;'''
97::CODE;;ripple_rad = NumericProperty(10)
98::CODE;;ripple_pos = ListProperty([0, 0])
99::CODE;;ripple_color = ListProperty((1., 1., 1., .5))
100::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
101::CODE;;super(TouchRippleBehavior, self).__init__(**kwargs)
102::CODE;;self.ripple_pane = CanvasBase()
103::CODE;;self.bind(
104::CODE;;disabled=self._ripple_fade,
105::CODE;;ripple_color=self._ripple_set_color,
106::CODE;;ripple_pos=self._ripple_set_ellipse,
107::CODE;;ripple_rad=self._ripple_set_ellipse
108::CODE;;)
109::CODE;;self.ripple_ellipse = None
110::CODE;;self.ripple_col_instruction = None
111::CODE;;def ripple_show(self, touch):
112::CODE;;'''Begin ripple animation on current widget.
113::CODE;;Expects touch event as argument.
114::CODE;;'''
115::CODE;;Animation.cancel_all(self, 'ripple_rad', 'ripple_color')
116::CODE;;self._ripple_reset_pane()
117::CODE;;self.canvas.add(self.ripple_pane)
118::CODE;;x, y = self.to_window(*self.pos)
119::CODE;;width, height = self.size
120::CODE;;if isinstance(self, RelativeLayout):
121::CODE;;self.ripple_pos = ripple_pos = (touch.x - x, touch.y - y)
122::CODE;;else:
123::CODE;;self.ripple_pos = ripple_pos = (touch.x, touch.y)
124::CODE;;rc = self.ripple_color
125::CODE;;ripple_rad = self.ripple_rad
126::CODE;;self.ripple_color = [rc[0], rc[1], rc[2], self.ripple_fade_from_alpha]
127::CODE;;with self.ripple_pane:
128::CODE;;ScissorPush(
129::CODE;;x=int(round(x)),
130::CODE;;y=int(round(y)),
131::CODE;;width=int(round(width)),
132::CODE;;height=int(round(height))
133::CODE;;)
134::CODE;;self.ripple_col_instruction = Color(rgba=self.ripple_color)
135::CODE;;self.ripple_ellipse = Ellipse(
136::CODE;;size=(ripple_rad, ripple_rad),
137::CODE;;pos=(
138::CODE;;ripple_pos[0] - ripple_rad / 2.,
139::CODE;;ripple_pos[1] - ripple_rad / 2.
140::CODE;;)
141::CODE;;)
142::CODE;;ScissorPop()
143::CODE;;anim = Animation(
144::CODE;;ripple_rad=max(width, height) * self.ripple_scale,
145::CODE;;t=self.ripple_func_in,
146::CODE;;ripple_color=[rc[0], rc[1], rc[2], self.ripple_fade_to_alpha],
147::CODE;;duration=self.ripple_duration_in
148::CODE;;)
149::CODE;;anim.start(self)
150::CODE;;def ripple_fade(self):
151::CODE;;'''Finish ripple animation on current widget.
152::CODE;;'''
153::CODE;;Animation.cancel_all(self, 'ripple_rad', 'ripple_color')
154::CODE;;width, height = self.size
155::CODE;;rc = self.ripple_color
156::CODE;;duration = self.ripple_duration_out
157::CODE;;anim = Animation(
158::CODE;;ripple_rad=max(width, height) * self.ripple_scale,
159::CODE;;ripple_color=[rc[0], rc[1], rc[2], 0.],
160::CODE;;t=self.ripple_func_out,
161::CODE;;duration=duration
162::CODE;;)
163::CODE;;anim.bind(on_complete=self._ripple_anim_complete)
164::CODE;;anim.start(self)
165::CODE;;def _ripple_fade(self, *args):
166::CODE;;self.ripple_fade()
167::CODE;;def _ripple_set_ellipse(self, instance, value):
168::CODE;;ellipse = self.ripple_ellipse
169::CODE;;if not ellipse:
170::CODE;;return
171::CODE;;ripple_pos = self.ripple_pos
172::CODE;;ripple_rad = self.ripple_rad
173::CODE;;ellipse.size = (ripple_rad, ripple_rad)
174::CODE;;ellipse.pos = (
175::CODE;;ripple_pos[0] - ripple_rad / 2.,
176::CODE;;ripple_pos[1] - ripple_rad / 2.
177::CODE;;)
178::CODE;;def _ripple_set_color(self, instance, value):
179::CODE;;if not self.ripple_col_instruction:
180::CODE;;return
181::CODE;;self.ripple_col_instruction.rgba = value
182::CODE;;def _ripple_anim_complete(self, anim, instance):
183::CODE;;self._ripple_reset_pane()
184::CODE;;def _ripple_reset_pane(self):
185::CODE;;self.ripple_rad = self.ripple_rad_default
186::CODE;;self.ripple_pane.clear()
187::CODE;;self.canvas.remove(self.ripple_pane)
188::CODE;;class TouchRippleButtonBehavior(TouchRippleBehavior):
189::CODE;;'''
190::CODE;;This `mixin <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixin>`_ class provides
191::CODE;;a similar behavior to :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.button.ButtonBehavior`
192::CODE;;but provides touch ripple animation instead of button pressed/released as
193::CODE;;visual effect.
194::CODE;;:Events:
195::CODE;;`on_press`
196::CODE;;Fired when the button is pressed.
197::CODE;;`on_release`
198::CODE;;Fired when the button is released (i.e. the touch/click that
199::CODE;;pressed the button goes away).
200::CODE;;'''
201::CODE;;last_touch = ObjectProperty(None)
202::CODE;;'''Contains the last relevant touch received by the Button. This can
203::CODE;;be used in `on_press` or `on_release` in order to know which touch
204::CODE;;dispatched the event.
205::CODE;;:attr:`last_touch` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.ObjectProperty` and
206::CODE;;defaults to `None`.
207::CODE;;'''
208::CODE;;always_release = BooleanProperty(False)
209::CODE;;'''This determines whether or not the widget fires an `on_release` event if
210::CODE;;the touch_up is outside the widget.
211::CODE;;:attr:`always_release` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty` and
212::CODE;;defaults to `False`.
213::CODE;;'''
214::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
215::CODE;;self.register_event_type('on_press')
216::CODE;;self.register_event_type('on_release')
217::CODE;;super(TouchRippleButtonBehavior, self).__init__(**kwargs)
218::CODE;;def on_touch_down(self, touch):
219::CODE;;if super(TouchRippleButtonBehavior, self).on_touch_down(touch):
220::CODE;;return True
221::CODE;;if touch.is_mouse_scrolling:
222::CODE;;return False
223::CODE;;if not self.collide_point(touch.x, touch.y):
224::CODE;;return False
225::CODE;;if self in touch.ud:
226::CODE;;return False
227::CODE;;touch.grab(self)
228::CODE;;touch.ud[self] = True
229::CODE;;self.last_touch = touch
230::CODE;;self.ripple_show(touch)
231::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_press')
232::CODE;;return True
233::CODE;;def on_touch_move(self, touch):
234::CODE;;if touch.grab_current is self:
235::CODE;;return True
236::CODE;;if super(TouchRippleButtonBehavior, self).on_touch_move(touch):
237::CODE;;return True
238::CODE;;return self in touch.ud
239::CODE;;def on_touch_up(self, touch):
240::CODE;;if touch.grab_current is not self:
241::CODE;;return super(TouchRippleButtonBehavior, self).on_touch_up(touch)
242::CODE;;assert self in touch.ud
243::CODE;;touch.ungrab(self)
244::CODE;;self.last_touch = touch
245::CODE;;if self.disabled:
246::CODE;;return
247::CODE;;self.ripple_fade()
248::CODE;;if not self.always_release and not self.collide_point(*touch.pos):
249::CODE;;return
251::CODE;;def defer_release(dt):
252::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_release')
253::CODE;;Clock.schedule_once(defer_release, self.ripple_duration_out)
254::CODE;;return True
255::CODE;;def on_press(self):
256::CODE;;pass
257::CODE;;def on_release(self):
258::CODE;;pass
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Box Layout
3::CODE;;==========
4::CODE;;.. only:: html
5::CODE;;.. image:: images/boxlayout.gif
6::CODE;;:align: right
7::CODE;;.. only:: latex
8::CODE;;.. image:: images/boxlayout.png
9::CODE;;:align: right
10::CODE;;:class:`BoxLayout` arranges children in a vertical or horizontal box.
11::CODE;;To position widgets above/below each other, use a vertical BoxLayout::
12::CODE;;layout = BoxLayout(orientation='vertical')
13::CODE;;btn1 = Button(text='Hello')
14::CODE;;btn2 = Button(text='World')
15::CODE;;layout.add_widget(btn1)
16::CODE;;layout.add_widget(btn2)
17::CODE;;To position widgets next to each other, use a horizontal BoxLayout. In this
18::CODE;;example, we use 10 pixel spacing between children; the first button covers
19::CODE;;70% of the horizontal space, the second covers 30%::
20::CODE;;layout = BoxLayout(spacing=10)
21::CODE;;btn1 = Button(text='Hello', size_hint=(.7, 1))
22::CODE;;btn2 = Button(text='World', size_hint=(.3, 1))
23::CODE;;layout.add_widget(btn1)
24::CODE;;layout.add_widget(btn2)
25::CODE;;Position hints are partially working, depending on the orientation:
26::CODE;;* If the orientation is `vertical`: `x`, `right` and `center_x` will be used.
27::CODE;;* If the orientation is `horizontal`: `y`, `top` and `center_y` will be used.
28::CODE;;Kv Example::
29::CODE;;BoxLayout:
30::CODE;;orientation: 'vertical'
31::CODE;;Label:
32::CODE;;text: 'this on top'
33::CODE;;Label:
34::CODE;;text: 'this right aligned'
35::CODE;;size_hint_x: None
36::CODE;;size: self.texture_size
37::CODE;;pos_hint: {'right': 1}
38::CODE;;Label:
39::CODE;;text: 'this on bottom'
40::CODE;;You can check the `examples/widgets/boxlayout_poshint.py` for a live example.
41::CODE;;.. note::
42::CODE;;The `size_hint` uses the available space after subtracting all the
43::CODE;;fixed-size widgets. For example, if you have a layout that is 800px
44::CODE;;wide, and add three buttons like this::
45::CODE;;btn1 = Button(text='Hello', size=(200, 100), size_hint=(None, None))
46::CODE;;btn2 = Button(text='Kivy', size_hint=(.5, 1))
47::CODE;;btn3 = Button(text='World', size_hint=(.5, 1))
48::CODE;;The first button will be 200px wide as specified, the second and third
49::CODE;;will be 300px each, e.g. (800-200) * 0.5
50::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.4.1
51::CODE;;Added support for `pos_hint`.
52::CODE;;'''
53::CODE;;__all__ = ('BoxLayout', )
54::CODE;;from kivy.uix.layout import Layout
55::CODE;;from kivy.properties import (NumericProperty, OptionProperty,
56::CODE;;VariableListProperty, ReferenceListProperty)
57::CODE;;class BoxLayout(Layout):
58::CODE;;'''Box layout class. See module documentation for more information.
59::CODE;;'''
60::CODE;;spacing = NumericProperty(0)
61::CODE;;'''Spacing between children, in pixels.
62::CODE;;:attr:`spacing` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and defaults
63::CODE;;to 0.
64::CODE;;'''
65::CODE;;padding = VariableListProperty([0, 0, 0, 0])
66::CODE;;'''Padding between layout box and children: [padding_left, padding_top,
67::CODE;;padding_right, padding_bottom].
68::CODE;;padding also accepts a two argument form [padding_horizontal,
69::CODE;;padding_vertical] and a one argument form [padding].
70::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.7.0
71::CODE;;Replaced NumericProperty with VariableListProperty.
72::CODE;;:attr:`padding` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.VariableListProperty` and
73::CODE;;defaults to [0, 0, 0, 0].
74::CODE;;'''
75::CODE;;orientation = OptionProperty('horizontal', options=(
76::CODE;;'horizontal', 'vertical'))
77::CODE;;'''Orientation of the layout.
78::CODE;;:attr:`orientation` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.OptionProperty` and
79::CODE;;defaults to 'horizontal'. Can be 'vertical' or 'horizontal'.
80::CODE;;'''
81::CODE;;minimum_width = NumericProperty(0)
82::CODE;;'''Automatically computed minimum width needed to contain all children.
83::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.10.0
84::CODE;;:attr:`minimum_width` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
85::CODE;;defaults to 0. It is read only.
86::CODE;;'''
87::CODE;;minimum_height = NumericProperty(0)
88::CODE;;'''Automatically computed minimum height needed to contain all children.
89::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.10.0
90::CODE;;:attr:`minimum_height` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
91::CODE;;defaults to 0. It is read only.
92::CODE;;'''
93::CODE;;minimum_size = ReferenceListProperty(minimum_width, minimum_height)
94::CODE;;'''Automatically computed minimum size needed to contain all children.
95::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.10.0
96::CODE;;:attr:`minimum_size` is a
97::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.properties.ReferenceListProperty` of
98::CODE;;(:attr:`minimum_width`, :attr:`minimum_height`) properties. It is read
99::CODE;;only.
100::CODE;;'''
101::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
102::CODE;;super(BoxLayout, self).__init__(**kwargs)
103::CODE;;update = self._trigger_layout
104::CODE;;fbind = self.fbind
105::CODE;;fbind('spacing', update)
106::CODE;;fbind('padding', update)
107::CODE;;fbind('children', update)
108::CODE;;fbind('orientation', update)
109::CODE;;fbind('parent', update)
110::CODE;;fbind('size', update)
111::CODE;;fbind('pos', update)
112::CODE;;def _iterate_layout(self, sizes):
114::CODE;;len_children = len(sizes)
115::CODE;;padding_left, padding_top, padding_right, padding_bottom = self.padding
116::CODE;;spacing = self.spacing
117::CODE;;orientation = self.orientation
118::CODE;;padding_x = padding_left + padding_right
119::CODE;;padding_y = padding_top + padding_bottom
121::CODE;;stretch_sum = 0.
122::CODE;;has_bound = False
123::CODE;;hint = [None] * len_children
125::CODE;;minimum_size_bounded = 0
126::CODE;;if orientation == 'horizontal':
127::CODE;;minimum_size_y = 0
128::CODE;;minimum_size_none = padding_x + spacing * (len_children - 1)
129::CODE;;for i, ((w, h), (shw, shh), _, (shw_min, shh_min),
130::CODE;;(shw_max, _)) in enumerate(sizes):
131::CODE;;if shw is None:
132::CODE;;minimum_size_none += w
133::CODE;;else:
134::CODE;;hint[i] = shw
135::CODE;;if shw_min:
136::CODE;;has_bound = True
137::CODE;;minimum_size_bounded += shw_min
138::CODE;;elif shw_max is not None:
139::CODE;;has_bound = True
140::CODE;;stretch_sum += shw
141::CODE;;if shh is None:
142::CODE;;minimum_size_y = max(minimum_size_y, h)
143::CODE;;elif shh_min:
144::CODE;;minimum_size_y = max(minimum_size_y, shh_min)
145::CODE;;minimum_size_x = minimum_size_bounded + minimum_size_none
146::CODE;;minimum_size_y += padding_y
147::CODE;;else:
148::CODE;;minimum_size_x = 0
149::CODE;;minimum_size_none = padding_y + spacing * (len_children - 1)
150::CODE;;for i, ((w, h), (shw, shh), _, (shw_min, shh_min),
151::CODE;;(_, shh_max)) in enumerate(sizes):
152::CODE;;if shh is None:
153::CODE;;minimum_size_none += h
154::CODE;;else:
155::CODE;;hint[i] = shh
156::CODE;;if shh_min:
157::CODE;;has_bound = True
158::CODE;;minimum_size_bounded += shh_min
159::CODE;;elif shh_max is not None:
160::CODE;;has_bound = True
161::CODE;;stretch_sum += shh
162::CODE;;if shw is None:
163::CODE;;minimum_size_x = max(minimum_size_x, w)
164::CODE;;elif shw_min:
165::CODE;;minimum_size_x = max(minimum_size_x, shw_min)
166::CODE;;minimum_size_y = minimum_size_bounded + minimum_size_none
167::CODE;;minimum_size_x += padding_x
168::CODE;;self.minimum_size = minimum_size_x, minimum_size_y
170::CODE;;selfx = self.x
171::CODE;;selfy = self.y
172::CODE;;if orientation == 'horizontal':
173::CODE;;stretch_space = max(0.0, self.width - minimum_size_none)
174::CODE;;dim = 0
175::CODE;;else:
176::CODE;;stretch_space = max(0.0, self.height - minimum_size_none)
177::CODE;;dim = 1
178::CODE;;if has_bound:
180::CODE;;if stretch_space < 1e-9:
182::CODE;;stretch_sum = stretch_space = 1.
183::CODE;;for i, val in enumerate(sizes):
184::CODE;;sh = val[1][dim]
185::CODE;;if sh is None:
186::CODE;;continue
187::CODE;;sh_min = val[3][dim]
188::CODE;;if sh_min is not None:
189::CODE;;hint[i] = sh_min
190::CODE;;else:
192::CODE;;else:
194::CODE;;self.layout_hint_with_bounds(
195::CODE;;stretch_sum, stretch_space, minimum_size_bounded,
196::CODE;;(val[3][dim] for val in sizes),
197::CODE;;(elem[4][dim] for elem in sizes), hint)
198::CODE;;if orientation == 'horizontal':
199::CODE;;x = padding_left + selfx
200::CODE;;size_y = self.height - padding_y
201::CODE;;for i, (sh, ((w, h), (_, shh), pos_hint, _, _)) in enumerate(
202::CODE;;zip(reversed(hint), reversed(sizes))):
203::CODE;;cy = selfy + padding_bottom
204::CODE;;if sh:
205::CODE;;w = max(0., stretch_space * sh / stretch_sum)
206::CODE;;if shh:
207::CODE;;h = max(0, shh * size_y)
208::CODE;;for key, value in pos_hint.items():
209::CODE;;posy = value * size_y
210::CODE;;if key == 'y':
211::CODE;;cy += posy
212::CODE;;elif key == 'top':
213::CODE;;cy += posy - h
214::CODE;;elif key == 'center_y':
215::CODE;;cy += posy - (h / 2.)
216::CODE;;yield len_children - i - 1, x, cy, w, h
217::CODE;;x += w + spacing
218::CODE;;else:
219::CODE;;y = padding_bottom + selfy
220::CODE;;size_x = self.width - padding_x
221::CODE;;for i, (sh, ((w, h), (shw, _), pos_hint, _, _)) in enumerate(
222::CODE;;zip(hint, sizes)):
223::CODE;;cx = selfx + padding_left
224::CODE;;if sh:
225::CODE;;h = max(0., stretch_space * sh / stretch_sum)
226::CODE;;if shw:
227::CODE;;w = max(0, shw * size_x)
228::CODE;;for key, value in pos_hint.items():
229::CODE;;posx = value * size_x
230::CODE;;if key == 'x':
231::CODE;;cx += posx
232::CODE;;elif key == 'right':
233::CODE;;cx += posx - w
234::CODE;;elif key == 'center_x':
235::CODE;;cx += posx - (w / 2.)
236::CODE;;yield i, cx, y, w, h
237::CODE;;y += h + spacing
238::CODE;;def do_layout(self, *largs):
239::CODE;;children = self.children
240::CODE;;if not children:
241::CODE;;l, t, r, b = self.padding
242::CODE;;self.minimum_size = l + r, t + b
243::CODE;;return
244::CODE;;for i, x, y, w, h in self._iterate_layout(
245::CODE;;[(c.size, c.size_hint, c.pos_hint, c.size_hint_min,
246::CODE;;c.size_hint_max) for c in children]):
247::CODE;;c = children[i]
248::CODE;;c.pos = x, y
249::CODE;;shw, shh = c.size_hint
250::CODE;;if shw is None:
251::CODE;;if shh is not None:
252::CODE;;c.height = h
253::CODE;;else:

260::CODE;;return super(BoxLayout, self).add_widget(widget, *args, **kwargs)
261::CODE;;def remove_widget(self, widget, *args, **kwargs):

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Bubble
3::CODE;;======
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.1.0
5::CODE;;.. image:: images/bubble.jpg
6::CODE;;:align: right
7::CODE;;The :class:`Bubble` widget is a form of menu or a small popup with an arrow
8::CODE;;arranged on one side of it's content.
9::CODE;;The :class:`Bubble` contains an arrow attached to the content
10::CODE;;(e.g., :class:`BubbleContent`) pointing in the direction you choose. It can
11::CODE;;be placed either at a predefined location or flexibly by specifying a relative
12::CODE;;position on the border of the widget.
13::CODE;;The :class:`BubbleContent` is a styled BoxLayout and is thought to be added to
14::CODE;;the :class:`Bubble` as a child widget. The :class:`Bubble` will then arrange
15::CODE;;an arrow around the content as desired. Instead of the class:`BubbleContent`,
16::CODE;;you can theoretically use any other :class:`Widget` as well as long as it
17::CODE;;supports the 'bind' and 'unbind' function of the :class:`EventDispatcher` and
18::CODE;;is compatible with Kivy to be placed inside a :class:`BoxLayout`.
19::CODE;;The :class:`BubbleButton`is a styled Button. It suits to the style of
20::CODE;;:class:`Bubble` and :class:`BubbleContent`. Feel free to place other Widgets
21::CODE;;inside the 'content' of the :class:`Bubble`.
22::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 2.2.0
23::CODE;;The properties :attr:`background_image`, :attr:`background_color`,
24::CODE;;:attr:`border` and :attr:`border_auto_scale` were removed from :class:`Bubble`.
25::CODE;;These properties had only been used by the content widget that now uses it's
26::CODE;;own properties instead. The color of the arrow is now changed with
27::CODE;;:attr:`arrow_color` instead of :attr:`background_color`.
28::CODE;;These changes makes the :class:`Bubble` transparent to use with other layouts
29::CODE;;as content without any side-effects due to property inheritance.
30::CODE;;The property :attr:`flex_arrow_pos` has been added to allow further
31::CODE;;customization of the arrow positioning.
32::CODE;;The properties :attr:`arrow_margin`, :attr:`arrow_margin_x`,
33::CODE;;:attr:`arrow_margin_y`, :attr:`content_size`, :attr:`content_width` and
34::CODE;;:attr:`content_height` have been added to ease proper sizing of a
35::CODE;;:class:`Bubble` e.g., based on it's content size.
36::CODE;;BubbleContent
37::CODE;;=============
38::CODE;;The :class:`BubbleContent` is a styled BoxLayout that can be used to
39::CODE;;add e.g., :class:`BubbleButtons` as menu items.
40::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 2.2.0
41::CODE;;The properties :attr:`background_image`, :attr:`background_color`,
42::CODE;;:attr:`border` and :attr:`border_auto_scale` were added to the
43::CODE;;:class:`BubbleContent`. The :class:`BubbleContent` does no longer rely on these
44::CODE;;properties being present in the parent class.
45::CODE;;BubbleButton
46::CODE;;============
47::CODE;;The :class:`BubbleButton` is a styled :class:`Button` that can be used to be
48::CODE;;added to the :class:`BubbleContent`.
49::CODE;;Simple example
50::CODE;;--------------
51::CODE;;.. include:: ../../examples/widgets/bubble_test.py
52::CODE;;:literal:
53::CODE;;Customize the Bubble
54::CODE;;--------------------
55::CODE;;You can choose the direction in which the arrow points::
56::CODE;;Bubble(arrow_pos='top_mid')
57::CODE;;or
58::CODE;;Bubble(size=(200, 40), flex_arrow_pos=(175, 40))
59::CODE;;Similarly, the corresponding properties in the '.kv' language can be used
60::CODE;;as well.
61::CODE;;You can change the appearance of the bubble::
62::CODE;;Bubble(
63::CODE;;arrow_image='/path/to/arrow/image',
64::CODE;;arrow_color=(1, 0, 0, .5)),
65::CODE;;)
66::CODE;;BubbleContent(
67::CODE;;background_image='/path/to/background/image',
69::CODE;;border=(0,0,0,0),
70::CODE;;)
71::CODE;;Similarly, the corresponding properties in the '.kv' language can be used
72::CODE;;as well.
73::CODE;;-----------------------------
74::CODE;;'''

368::CODE;;arrow_width = self._arrow_image.width
372::CODE;;def calc_x0(x, length):
373::CODE;;return x * (length - arrow_width) / (length * length)
374::CODE;;if base_layout_key == "bottom_mid":

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Button
3::CODE;;======
4::CODE;;.. image:: images/button.jpg
5::CODE;;:align: right
6::CODE;;The :class:`Button` is a :class:`~kivy.uix.label.Label` with associated actions
7::CODE;;that are triggered when the button is pressed (or released after a
8::CODE;;click/touch). To configure the button, the same properties (padding,
9::CODE;;font_size, etc) and
10::CODE;;:ref:`sizing system <kivy-uix-label-sizing-and-text-content>`
11::CODE;;are used as for the :class:`~kivy.uix.label.Label` class::
12::CODE;;button = Button(text='Hello world', font_size=14)
13::CODE;;To attach a callback when the button is pressed (clicked/touched), use
14::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.bind`::
15::CODE;;def callback(instance):
16::CODE;;print('The button <%s> is being pressed' % instance.text)
17::CODE;;btn1 = Button(text='Hello world 1')
18::CODE;;btn1.bind(on_press=callback)
19::CODE;;btn2 = Button(text='Hello world 2')
20::CODE;;btn2.bind(on_press=callback)
21::CODE;;If you want to be notified every time the button state changes, you can bind
22::CODE;;to the :attr:`Button.state` property::
23::CODE;;def callback(instance, value):
24::CODE;;print('My button <%s> state is <%s>' % (instance, value))
25::CODE;;btn1 = Button(text='Hello world 1')
26::CODE;;btn1.bind(state=callback)
27::CODE;;Kv Example::
28::CODE;;Button:
29::CODE;;text: 'press me'
30::CODE;;on_press: print("ouch! More gently please")
31::CODE;;on_release: print("ahhh")
32::CODE;;on_state:
33::CODE;;print("my current state is {}".format(self.state))
34::CODE;;'''

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Camera
3::CODE;;======
4::CODE;;The :class:`Camera` widget is used to capture and display video from a camera.
5::CODE;;Once the widget is created, the texture inside the widget will be automatically
6::CODE;;updated. Our :class:`~kivy.core.camera.CameraBase` implementation is used under
7::CODE;;the hood::
8::CODE;;cam = Camera()
9::CODE;;By default, the first camera found on your system is used. To use a different
10::CODE;;camera, set the index property::
11::CODE;;cam = Camera(index=1)
12::CODE;;You can also select the camera resolution::
13::CODE;;cam = Camera(resolution=(320, 240))
14::CODE;;.. warning::
15::CODE;;The camera texture is not updated as soon as you have created the object.
16::CODE;;The camera initialization is asynchronous, so there may be a delay before
17::CODE;;the requested texture is created.
18::CODE;;'''
19::CODE;;__all__ = ('Camera', )
20::CODE;;from kivy.uix.image import Image
21::CODE;;from kivy.core.camera import Camera as CoreCamera
22::CODE;;from kivy.properties import NumericProperty, ListProperty, \
23::CODE;;BooleanProperty
24::CODE;;class Camera(Image):
25::CODE;;'''Camera class. See module documentation for more information.
26::CODE;;'''
27::CODE;;play = BooleanProperty(False)
28::CODE;;'''Boolean indicating whether the camera is playing or not.
29::CODE;;You can start/stop the camera by setting this property::
31::CODE;;cam = Camera(play=True)
33::CODE;;cam = Camera(play=False)
35::CODE;;cam.play = True
36::CODE;;:attr:`play` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty` and defaults to
37::CODE;;False.
38::CODE;;'''
39::CODE;;index = NumericProperty(-1)
40::CODE;;'''Index of the used camera, starting from 0.
41::CODE;;:attr:`index` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and defaults
42::CODE;;to -1 to allow auto selection.
43::CODE;;'''
44::CODE;;resolution = ListProperty([-1, -1])
45::CODE;;'''Preferred resolution to use when invoking the camera. If you are using
46::CODE;;[-1, -1], the resolution will be the default one::
48::CODE;;cam = Camera()
50::CODE;;cam = Camera(resolution=(320, 240))
51::CODE;;.. warning::
52::CODE;;Depending on the implementation, the camera may not respect this
53::CODE;;property.
54::CODE;;:attr:`resolution` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.ListProperty` and defaults
55::CODE;;to [-1, -1].
56::CODE;;'''
57::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
58::CODE;;self._camera = None
59::CODE;;super(Camera, self).__init__(**kwargs)
60::CODE;;if self.index == -1:
61::CODE;;self.index = 0
62::CODE;;on_index = self._on_index
63::CODE;;fbind = self.fbind
64::CODE;;fbind('index', on_index)
65::CODE;;fbind('resolution', on_index)
66::CODE;;on_index()
67::CODE;;def on_tex(self, camera):
68::CODE;;self.texture = texture = camera.texture
69::CODE;;self.texture_size = list(texture.size)
70::CODE;;self.canvas.ask_update()
71::CODE;;def _on_index(self, *largs):
72::CODE;;self._camera = None
73::CODE;;if self.index < 0:
74::CODE;;return
75::CODE;;if self.resolution[0] < 0 or self.resolution[1] < 0:
76::CODE;;self._camera = CoreCamera(index=self.index, stopped=True)
77::CODE;;else:
78::CODE;;self._camera = CoreCamera(index=self.index,
79::CODE;;resolution=self.resolution, stopped=True)
80::CODE;;if self.play:
81::CODE;;self._camera.start()
82::CODE;;self._camera.bind(on_texture=self.on_tex)
83::CODE;;def on_play(self, instance, value):
84::CODE;;if not self._camera:
85::CODE;;return

87::CODE;;self._camera.start()
88::CODE;;else:
89::CODE;;self._camera.stop()

2::CODE;;Carousel
3::CODE;;========
4::CODE;;.. image:: images/carousel.gif
5::CODE;;:align: right
6::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.4.0
7::CODE;;The :class:`Carousel` widget provides the classic mobile-friendly carousel view
8::CODE;;where you can swipe between slides.
9::CODE;;You can add any content to the carousel and have it move horizontally or
10::CODE;;vertically. The carousel can display pages in a sequence or a loop.
11::CODE;;Example::
12::CODE;;from kivy.app import App
13::CODE;;from kivy.uix.carousel import Carousel
14::CODE;;from kivy.uix.image import AsyncImage
15::CODE;;class CarouselApp(App):
16::CODE;;def build(self):

18::CODE;;for i in range(10):
19::CODE;;src = "http://placehold.it/480x270.png&text=slide-%d&.png" % i
20::CODE;;image = AsyncImage(source=src, fit_mode="contain")
21::CODE;;carousel.add_widget(image)
22::CODE;;return carousel
23::CODE;;CarouselApp().run()
24::CODE;;Kv Example::
25::CODE;;Carousel:
26::CODE;;direction: 'right'
27::CODE;;AsyncImage:
28::CODE;;source: 'http://placehold.it/480x270.png&text=slide-1.png'
29::CODE;;AsyncImage:
30::CODE;;source: 'http://placehold.it/480x270.png&text=slide-2.png'
31::CODE;;AsyncImage:
32::CODE;;source: 'http://placehold.it/480x270.png&text=slide-3.png'
33::CODE;;AsyncImage:
34::CODE;;source: 'http://placehold.it/480x270.png&text=slide-4.png'
35::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.5.0
36::CODE;;The carousel now supports active children, like the
37::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.scrollview.ScrollView`. It will detect a swipe gesture
38::CODE;;according to the :attr:`Carousel.scroll_timeout` and
39::CODE;;:attr:`Carousel.scroll_distance` properties.
40::CODE;;In addition, the slide container is no longer exposed by the API.
41::CODE;;The impacted properties are
42::CODE;;:attr:`Carousel.slides`, :attr:`Carousel.current_slide`,
43::CODE;;:attr:`Carousel.previous_slide` and :attr:`Carousel.next_slide`.
44::CODE;;'''

53::CODE;;NumericProperty, ListProperty, ObjectProperty, StringProperty

67::CODE;;options=('right', 'left', 'top', 'bottom'))

69::CODE;;corresponds to the direction from which the user swipes to go from one

82::CODE;;If the movement doesn't reach this minimum value, the movement is
83::CODE;;cancelled and the content is restored to its original position.
84::CODE;;:attr:`min_move` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and

94::CODE;;accepted. This is generally when the user does not make a large enough

7::CODE;;This widget requires ``pygments`` package to run. Install it with ``pip``.
8::CODE;;The :class:`CodeInput` provides a box of editable highlighted text like the one
9::CODE;;shown in the image.
10::CODE;;It supports all the features provided by the :class:`~kivy.uix.textinput` as
11::CODE;;well as code highlighting for `languages supported by pygments
12::CODE;;<http://pygments.org/docs/lexers/>`_ along with `KivyLexer` for
13::CODE;;:mod:`kivy.lang` highlighting.
14::CODE;;Usage example
15::CODE;;-------------
16::CODE;;To create a CodeInput with highlighting for `KV language`::
17::CODE;;from kivy.uix.codeinput import CodeInput
18::CODE;;from kivy.extras.highlight import KivyLexer

21::CODE;;from kivy.uix.codeinput import CodeInput

24::CODE;;'''

2::CODE;;Color Picker

25::CODE;;from math import cos, sin, pi, sqrt, atan

28::CODE;;from kivy.graphics import Mesh, InstructionGroup, Color
