112::CODE;;[1, 1, 1, 1].
113::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 2.0.0
114::CODE;;Changed from :class:`~kivy.properties.ListProperty` to
115::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.properties.ColorProperty`.
116::CODE;;'''
117::CODE;;allow_stretch = BooleanProperty(False, deprecated=True)
118::CODE;;'''If True, the normalized image size will be maximized to fit in the image
119::CODE;;box. Otherwise, if the box is too tall, the image will not be
120::CODE;;stretched more than 1:1 pixels.
121::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.7
122::CODE;;.. deprecated:: 2.2.0
123::CODE;;:attr:`allow_stretch` have been deprecated. Please use `fit_mode`
124::CODE;;instead.
125::CODE;;:attr:`allow_stretch` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty` and
126::CODE;;defaults to False.
127::CODE;;'''
128::CODE;;keep_ratio = BooleanProperty(True, deprecated=True)
129::CODE;;'''If False along with allow_stretch being True, the normalized image
130::CODE;;size will be maximized to fit in the image box and ignores the aspect
131::CODE;;ratio of the image.
132::CODE;;Otherwise, if the box is too tall, the image will not be stretched more
133::CODE;;than 1:1 pixels.
134::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.8
135::CODE;;.. deprecated:: 2.2.0
136::CODE;;:attr:`keep_ratio` have been deprecated. Please use `fit_mode`
137::CODE;;instead.
138::CODE;;:attr:`keep_ratio` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty` and
139::CODE;;defaults to True.
140::CODE;;'''
141::CODE;;fit_mode = OptionProperty(
142::CODE;;"scale-down", options=["scale-down", "fill", "contain", "cover"]
143::CODE;;)
144::CODE;;'''If the size of the image is different than the size of the widget,
145::CODE;;determine how the image should be resized to fit inside the widget box.
146::CODE;;Available options:
147::CODE;;- ``"scale-down"``: the image will be scaled down to fit inside the widget
148::CODE;;box, **maintaining its aspect ratio and without stretching**. If the size
149::CODE;;of the image is smaller than the widget, it will be displayed at its
150::CODE;;original size. If the image has a different aspect ratio than the widget,
151::CODE;;there will be blank areas on the widget box.
152::CODE;;- ``"fill"``: the image is stretched to fill the widget, **regardless of
153::CODE;;its aspect ratio or dimensions**. If the image has a different aspect ratio
154::CODE;;than the widget, this option can lead to distortion of the image.
155::CODE;;- ``"contain"``: the image is resized to fit inside the widget box,
156::CODE;;**maintaining its aspect ratio**. If the image size is larger than the
157::CODE;;widget size, the behavior will be similar to ``"scale-down"``. However, if
158::CODE;;the size of the image is smaller than the widget size, unlike
159::CODE;;``"scale-down``, the image will be resized to fit inside the widget.
160::CODE;;If the image has a different aspect ratio than the widget, there will be
161::CODE;;blank areas on the widget box.
162::CODE;;- ``"cover"``: the image will be stretched horizontally or vertically to
163::CODE;;fill the widget box, **maintaining its aspect ratio**. If the image has a
164::CODE;;different aspect ratio than the widget, then the image will be clipped to
165::CODE;;fit.
166::CODE;;:attr:`fit_mode` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.OptionProperty` and
167::CODE;;defaults to ``"scale-down"``.
168::CODE;;'''
169::CODE;;keep_data = BooleanProperty(False)
170::CODE;;'''If True, the underlying _coreimage will store the raw image data.
171::CODE;;This is useful when performing pixel based collision detection.
172::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.3.0
173::CODE;;:attr:`keep_data` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty` and
174::CODE;;defaults to False.
175::CODE;;'''
176::CODE;;anim_delay = NumericProperty(0.25)
177::CODE;;'''Delay the animation if the image is sequenced (like an animated gif).
178::CODE;;If anim_delay is set to -1, the animation will be stopped.
179::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.8
180::CODE;;:attr:`anim_delay` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
181::CODE;;defaults to 0.25 (4 FPS).
182::CODE;;'''
183::CODE;;anim_loop = NumericProperty(0)
184::CODE;;'''Number of loops to play then stop animating. 0 means keep animating.
185::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.9.0
186::CODE;;:attr:`anim_loop` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
187::CODE;;defaults to 0.
188::CODE;;'''
189::CODE;;nocache = BooleanProperty(False)
190::CODE;;'''If this property is set True, the image will not be added to the
191::CODE;;internal cache. The cache will simply ignore any calls trying to
192::CODE;;append the core image.
193::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.6.0
194::CODE;;:attr:`nocache` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty` and defaults
195::CODE;;to False.
196::CODE;;'''
197::CODE;;def get_norm_image_size(self):
198::CODE;;if not self.texture:
199::CODE;;return list(self.size)
200::CODE;;ratio = self.image_ratio
201::CODE;;w, h = self.size
202::CODE;;tw, th = self.texture.size
203::CODE;;if self.fit_mode == "cover":
204::CODE;;widget_ratio = w / max(1, h)
205::CODE;;if widget_ratio > ratio:
206::CODE;;return [w, (w * th) / tw]
207::CODE;;else:
208::CODE;;return [(h * tw) / th, h]
209::CODE;;elif self.fit_mode == "fill":
210::CODE;;return [w, h]
211::CODE;;elif self.fit_mode == "contain":
212::CODE;;iw = w
213::CODE;;else:
214::CODE;;iw = min(w, tw)
216::CODE;;ih = iw / ratio
219::CODE;;if ih > h:
220::CODE;;if self.fit_mode == "contain":
221::CODE;;ih = h
222::CODE;;else:
223::CODE;;ih = min(h, th)
224::CODE;;iw = ih * ratio
225::CODE;;return [iw, ih]

341::CODE;;class AsyncImage(Image):
342::CODE;;'''Asynchronous Image class. See the module documentation for more
343::CODE;;information.
344::CODE;;.. note::
345::CODE;;The AsyncImage is a specialized form of the Image class. You may
346::CODE;;want to refer to the :mod:`~kivy.loader` documentation and in
347::CODE;;particular, the :class:`~kivy.loader.ProxyImage` for more detail
348::CODE;;on how to handle events around asynchronous image loading.
349::CODE;;.. note::
350::CODE;;AsyncImage currently does not support properties
351::CODE;;:attr:`anim_loop` and :attr:`mipmap` and setting those properties will
352::CODE;;have no effect.
353::CODE;;'''
354::CODE;;__events__ = ('on_error', 'on_load')
355::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
356::CODE;;self._found_source = None
357::CODE;;self._coreimage = None

361::CODE;;self.fbind('source', self._load_source)
362::CODE;;super().__init__(**kwargs)
363::CODE;;def _load_source(self, *args):
364::CODE;;source = self.source
365::CODE;;if not source:
366::CODE;;self._clear_core_image()
367::CODE;;return
368::CODE;;if not self.is_uri(source):
369::CODE;;source = resource_find(source)
370::CODE;;if not source:
371::CODE;;Logger.error('AsyncImage: Not found <%s>' % self.source)

1::CODE;;'''Label
2::CODE;;=====
3::CODE;;.. image:: images/label.png
4::CODE;;:align: right
5::CODE;;The :class:`Label` widget is for rendering text::
7::CODE;;l = Label(text='Hello world')
9::CODE;;l = Label(text='Hello world ' + chr(2764))
11::CODE;;l = Label(text='Multi\\nLine')
13::CODE;;l = Label(text='Hello world', font_size='20sp')
14::CODE;;.. _kivy-uix-label-sizing-and-text-content:
15::CODE;;Sizing and text content
16::CODE;;---------------------------
17::CODE;;By default, the size of :class:`Label` is not affected by :attr:`~Label.text`
18::CODE;;content and the text is not affected by the size. In order to control
19::CODE;;sizing, you must specify :attr:`~Label.text_size` to constrain the text
20::CODE;;and/or bind :attr:`~Label.size` to :attr:`~Label.texture_size` to grow with
21::CODE;;the text.
22::CODE;;For example, this label's size will be set to the text content
23::CODE;;(plus :attr:`~Label.padding`):
24::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
25::CODE;;Label:
26::CODE;;size: self.texture_size
27::CODE;;This label's text will wrap at the specified width and be clipped to the
28::CODE;;height:
29::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
30::CODE;;Label:
31::CODE;;text_size: cm(6), cm(4)
32::CODE;;.. note:: The :attr:`~Label.shorten` and :attr:`~Label.max_lines` attributes
33::CODE;;control how overflowing text behaves.
34::CODE;;Combine these concepts to create a Label that can grow vertically but wraps the
35::CODE;;text at a certain width:
36::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
37::CODE;;Label:
38::CODE;;text_size: root.width, None
39::CODE;;size: self.texture_size
40::CODE;;How to have a custom background color in the label:
41::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
43::CODE;;<BackgroundColor@Widget>
44::CODE;;background_color: 1, 1, 1, 1
45::CODE;;canvas.before:
46::CODE;;Color:
47::CODE;;rgba: root.background_color
48::CODE;;Rectangle:
49::CODE;;size: self.size
50::CODE;;pos: self.pos
53::CODE;;<BackgroundLabel@Label+BackgroundColor>
54::CODE;;background_color: 0, 0, 0, 0
58::CODE;;BackgroundLabel
59::CODE;;text: 'Hello'
60::CODE;;background_color: 1, 0, 0, 1
61::CODE;;Text alignment and wrapping
62::CODE;;---------------------------
63::CODE;;The :class:`Label` has :attr:`~Label.halign` and :attr:`~Label.valign`
64::CODE;;properties to control the alignment of its text. However, by default the text
65::CODE;;image (:attr:`~Label.texture`) is only just large enough to contain the
66::CODE;;characters and is positioned in the center of the Label. The valign property
67::CODE;;will have no effect and halign will only have an effect if your text has
68::CODE;;newlines; a single line of text will appear to be centered even though halign
69::CODE;;is set to left (by default).
70::CODE;;In order for the alignment properties to take effect, set the
71::CODE;;:attr:`~Label.text_size`, which specifies the size of the bounding box within
72::CODE;;which text is aligned. For instance, the following code binds this size to the
73::CODE;;size of the Label, so text will be aligned within the widget bounds. This
74::CODE;;will also automatically wrap the text of the Label to remain within this area.
75::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
76::CODE;;Label:
77::CODE;;text_size: self.size
78::CODE;;halign: 'right'
79::CODE;;valign: 'middle'
80::CODE;;Markup text
81::CODE;;-----------
82::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.1.0
83::CODE;;You can change the style of the text using :doc:`api-kivy.core.text.markup`.
84::CODE;;The syntax is similar to the bbcode syntax but only the inline styling is
85::CODE;;allowed::
87::CODE;;l = Label(text='Hello [b]World[/b]', markup=True)
89::CODE;;l = Label(text='[color=ff3333]Hello[/color][color=3333ff]World[/color]',
90::CODE;;markup = True)
91::CODE;;If you need to escape the markup from the current text, use
92::CODE;;:func:`kivy.utils.escape_markup`::
93::CODE;;text = 'This is an important message [1]'
94::CODE;;l = Label(text='[b]' + escape_markup(text) + '[/b]', markup=True)
95::CODE;;The following tags are available:
96::CODE;;``[b][/b]``
97::CODE;;Activate bold text
98::CODE;;``[i][/i]``
99::CODE;;Activate italic text
100::CODE;;``[u][/u]``
101::CODE;;Underlined text
102::CODE;;``[s][/s]``
103::CODE;;Strikethrough text
104::CODE;;``[font=<str>][/font]``
105::CODE;;Change the font (note: this refers to a TTF file or registered alias)
106::CODE;;``[font_context=<str>][/font_context]``
107::CODE;;Change context for the font, use string value "none" for isolated context
108::CODE;;(this is equivalent to `None`; if you created a font context named
109::CODE;;`'none'`, it cannot be referred to using markup)
110::CODE;;``[font_family=<str>][/font_family]``
111::CODE;;Font family to request for drawing. This is only valid when using a
112::CODE;;font context, see :class:`kivy.uix.label.Label` for details.
113::CODE;;``[font_features=<str>][/font_features]``
114::CODE;;OpenType font features, in CSS format, this is passed straight
115::CODE;;through to Pango. The effects of requesting a feature depends on loaded
116::CODE;;fonts, library versions, etc. Pango only, requires v1.38 or later.
117::CODE;;``[size=<integer>][/size]``
118::CODE;;Change the font size
120::CODE;;Change the text color
121::CODE;;``[ref=<str>][/ref]``
122::CODE;;Add an interactive zone. The reference + bounding box inside the
123::CODE;;reference will be available in :attr:`Label.refs`
124::CODE;;``[anchor=<str>]``
125::CODE;;Put an anchor in the text. You can get the position of your anchor within
126::CODE;;the text with :attr:`Label.anchors`
127::CODE;;``[sub][/sub]``
128::CODE;;Display the text at a subscript position relative to the text before it.
129::CODE;;``[sup][/sup]``
130::CODE;;Display the text at a superscript position relative to the text before it.
131::CODE;;``[text_language=<str>][/text_language]``
132::CODE;;Language of the text, this is an RFC-3066 format language tag (as string),
133::CODE;;for example "en_US", "zh_CN", "fr" or "ja". This can impact font selection
134::CODE;;and metrics. Use the string "None" to revert to locale detection.
135::CODE;;Pango only.
136::CODE;;If you want to render the markup text with a [ or ] or & character, you need to
137::CODE;;escape them. We created a simple syntax::
138::CODE;;[ -> &bl;
139::CODE;;] -> &br;
140::CODE;;& -> &amp;
141::CODE;;Then you can write::
142::CODE;;"[size=24]Hello &bl;World&br;[/size]"
143::CODE;;Interactive zone in text
144::CODE;;------------------------
145::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.1.0
146::CODE;;You can now have definable "links" using text markup. The idea is to be able
147::CODE;;to detect when the user clicks on part of the text and to react.
148::CODE;;The tag ``[ref=xxx]`` is used for that.
149::CODE;;In this example, we are creating a reference on the word "World". When
150::CODE;;this word is clicked, the function ``print_it`` will be called with the
151::CODE;;name of the reference::
152::CODE;;def print_it(instance, value):
153::CODE;;print('User clicked on', value)
154::CODE;;widget = Label(text='Hello [ref=world]World[/ref]', markup=True)
155::CODE;;widget.bind(on_ref_press=print_it)
156::CODE;;For prettier rendering, you could add a color for the reference. Replace the
157::CODE;;``text=`` in the previous example with::
158::CODE;;'Hello [ref=world][color=0000ff]World[/color][/ref]'
159::CODE;;Catering for Unicode languages
160::CODE;;------------------------------
161::CODE;;The font kivy uses does not contain all the characters required for displaying
162::CODE;;all languages. When you use the built-in widgets, this results in a block being
163::CODE;;drawn where you expect a character.
164::CODE;;If you want to display such characters, you can chose a font that supports them
165::CODE;;and deploy it universally via kv:
166::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
167::CODE;;<Label>:
168::CODE;;font_name: '/<path>/<to>/<font>'
169::CODE;;Note that this needs to be done before your widgets are loaded as kv rules are
170::CODE;;only applied at load time.
171::CODE;;Usage example
172::CODE;;-------------
173::CODE;;The following example marks the anchors and references contained in a label::
174::CODE;;from kivy.app import App
175::CODE;;from kivy.uix.label import Label
176::CODE;;from kivy.clock import Clock
177::CODE;;from kivy.graphics import Color, Rectangle
178::CODE;;class TestApp(App):
179::CODE;;@staticmethod
180::CODE;;def get_x(label, ref_x):
188::CODE;;return label.center_y + label.texture_size[1] * 0.5 - ref_y
189::CODE;;def show_marks(self, label):
191::CODE;;for name, anc in label.anchors.items():
192::CODE;;with label.canvas:
193::CODE;;Color(1, 0, 0)
194::CODE;;Rectangle(pos=(self.get_x(label, anc[0]),
195::CODE;;self.get_y(label, anc[1])),
196::CODE;;size=(3, 3))
198::CODE;;for name, boxes in label.refs.items():
199::CODE;;for box in boxes:
200::CODE;;with label.canvas:
201::CODE;;Color(0, 1, 0, 0.25)
202::CODE;;Rectangle(pos=(self.get_x(label, box[0]),
203::CODE;;self.get_y(label, box[1])),
204::CODE;;size=(box[2] - box[0],
205::CODE;;box[1] - box[3]))
206::CODE;;def build(self):
207::CODE;;label = Label(
208::CODE;;text='[anchor=a]a\\nChars [anchor=b]b\\n[ref=myref]ref[/ref]',
209::CODE;;markup=True)
210::CODE;;Clock.schedule_once(lambda dt: self.show_marks(label), 1)
211::CODE;;return label
212::CODE;;TestApp().run()
213::CODE;;'''

314::CODE;;'''Force texture recreation with the current Label properties.
315::CODE;;After this function call, the :attr:`texture` and :attr:`texture_size`

338::CODE;;self.disabled_color if

346::CODE;;self.anchors = self._label.anchors
347::CODE;;else:

354::CODE;;def on_touch_down(self, touch):
355::CODE;;if super(Label, self).on_touch_down(touch):
356::CODE;;return True
357::CODE;;if not len(self.refs):
358::CODE;;return False
359::CODE;;tx, ty = touch.pos
360::CODE;;tx -= self.center_x - self.texture_size[0] / 2.
361::CODE;;ty -= self.center_y - self.texture_size[1] / 2.
362::CODE;;ty = self.texture_size[1] - ty
363::CODE;;for uid, zones in self.refs.items():
364::CODE;;for zone in zones:
365::CODE;;x, y, w, h = zone
366::CODE;;if x <= tx <= w and y <= ty <= h:
367::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_ref_press', uid)
368::CODE;;return True
369::CODE;;return False

387::CODE;;Creation of a simple hello world::
388::CODE;;widget = Label(text='Hello world')
389::CODE;;:attr:`text` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.StringProperty` and defaults to
390::CODE;;''.
391::CODE;;'''
392::CODE;;text_size = ListProperty([None, None])
393::CODE;;'''By default, the label is not constrained to any bounding box.
394::CODE;;You can set the size constraint of the label with this property.
395::CODE;;The text will autoflow into the constraints. So although the font size
396::CODE;;will not be reduced, the text will be arranged to fit into the box as best
397::CODE;;as possible, with any text still outside the box clipped.
398::CODE;;This sets and clips :attr:`texture_size` to text_size if not None.
399::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.4
400::CODE;;For example, whatever your current widget size is, if you want the label to
401::CODE;;be created in a box with width=200 and unlimited height::
402::CODE;;Label(text='Very big big line', text_size=(200, None))
403::CODE;;.. note::
404::CODE;;This text_size property is the same as the
405::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.core.text.Label.usersize` property in the
406::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.core.text.Label` class. (It is named size= in the
407::CODE;;constructor.)
408::CODE;;:attr:`text_size` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.ListProperty` and
409::CODE;;defaults to (None, None), meaning no size restriction by default.
410::CODE;;'''
411::CODE;;base_direction = OptionProperty(None,
412::CODE;;options=['ltr', 'rtl', 'weak_rtl', 'weak_ltr', None],
413::CODE;;allownone=True)
414::CODE;;'''Base direction of text, this impacts horizontal alignment when
415::CODE;;:attr:`halign` is `auto` (the default). Available options are: None,
416::CODE;;"ltr" (left to right), "rtl" (right to left) plus "weak_ltr" and
417::CODE;;"weak_rtl".
418::CODE;;.. note::
419::CODE;;This feature requires the Pango text provider.
420::CODE;;.. note::
421::CODE;;Weak modes are currently not implemented in Kivy text layout, and
422::CODE;;have the same effect as setting strong mode.
423::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.11.0
424::CODE;;:attr:`base_direction` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.OptionProperty` and
425::CODE;;defaults to None (autodetect RTL if possible, otherwise LTR).
426::CODE;;'''
427::CODE;;text_language = StringProperty(None, allownone=True)
428::CODE;;'''Language of the text, if None Pango will determine it from locale.
429::CODE;;This is an RFC-3066 format language tag (as a string), for example
430::CODE;;"en_US", "zh_CN", "fr" or "ja". This can impact font selection, metrics
431::CODE;;and rendering. For example, the same bytes of text can look different
432::CODE;;for `ur` and `ar` languages, though both use Arabic script.
433::CODE;;.. note::
434::CODE;;This feature requires the Pango text provider.
435::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.11.0
436::CODE;;:attr:`text_language` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.StringProperty` and
437::CODE;;defaults to None.
438::CODE;;'''
439::CODE;;font_context = StringProperty(None, allownone=True)
440::CODE;;'''Font context. `None` means the font is used in isolation, so you are
441::CODE;;guaranteed to be drawing with the TTF file resolved by :attr:`font_name`.
442::CODE;;Specifying a value here will load the font file into a named context,
443::CODE;;enabling fallback between all fonts in the same context. If a font
444::CODE;;context is set, you are not guaranteed that rendering will actually use
445::CODE;;the specified TTF file for all glyphs (Pango will pick the one it
446::CODE;;thinks is best).
447::CODE;;If Kivy is linked against a system-wide installation of FontConfig,
448::CODE;;you can load the system fonts by specifying a font context starting
449::CODE;;with the special string `system://`. This will load the system
450::CODE;;fontconfig configuration, and add your application-specific fonts on
451::CODE;;top of it (this imposes a significant risk of family name collision,
452::CODE;;Pango may not use your custom font file, but pick one from the system)
453::CODE;;.. note::
454::CODE;;This feature requires the Pango text provider.
455::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.11.0
456::CODE;;:attr:`font_context` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.StringProperty` and
457::CODE;;defaults to None.
458::CODE;;'''
459::CODE;;font_family = StringProperty(None, allownone=True)
460::CODE;;'''Font family, this is only applicable when using :attr:`font_context`
461::CODE;;option. The specified font family will be requested, but note that it may
462::CODE;;not be available, or there could be multiple fonts registered with the
463::CODE;;same family. The value can be a family name (string) available in the
464::CODE;;font context (for example a system font in a `system://` context, or a
465::CODE;;custom font file added using :class:`kivy.core.text.FontContextManager`).
466::CODE;;If set to `None`, font selection is controlled by the :attr:`font_name`
467::CODE;;setting.
468::CODE;;.. note::
469::CODE;;If using :attr:`font_name` to reference a custom font file, you
470::CODE;;should leave this as `None`. The family name is managed automatically
471::CODE;;in this case.
472::CODE;;.. note::
473::CODE;;This feature requires the Pango text provider.
474::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.11.0
475::CODE;;:attr:`font_family` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.StringProperty` and
476::CODE;;defaults to None.
477::CODE;;'''
478::CODE;;font_name = StringProperty(DEFAULT_FONT)
479::CODE;;'''Filename of the font to use. The path can be absolute or relative.
480::CODE;;Relative paths are resolved by the :func:`~kivy.resources.resource_find`
481::CODE;;function.
482::CODE;;.. warning::
483::CODE;;Depending of your text provider, the font file can be ignored. However,
484::CODE;;you can mostly use this without problems.
485::CODE;;If the font used lacks the glyphs for the particular language/symbols
486::CODE;;you are using, you will see '[]' blank box characters instead of the
487::CODE;;actual glyphs. The solution is to use a font that has the glyphs you
488::CODE;;need to display. For example, to display |unicodechar|, use a font such

819::CODE;;to this list.

821::CODE;;your markup text, automatically doing the collision with the touch and
822::CODE;;dispatching an `on_ref_press` event.

824::CODE;;def print_it(instance, value):
825::CODE;;print('User click on', value)

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Layout
3::CODE;;======
4::CODE;;Layouts are used to calculate and assign widget positions.
5::CODE;;The :class:`Layout` class itself cannot be used directly.
6::CODE;;You should use one of the following layout classes:
7::CODE;;- Anchor layout: :class:`kivy.uix.anchorlayout.AnchorLayout`
8::CODE;;- Box layout: :class:`kivy.uix.boxlayout.BoxLayout`
9::CODE;;- Float layout: :class:`kivy.uix.floatlayout.FloatLayout`
10::CODE;;- Grid layout: :class:`kivy.uix.gridlayout.GridLayout`
11::CODE;;- Page Layout: :class:`kivy.uix.pagelayout.PageLayout`
12::CODE;;- Relative layout: :class:`kivy.uix.relativelayout.RelativeLayout`
13::CODE;;- Scatter layout: :class:`kivy.uix.scatterlayout.ScatterLayout`
14::CODE;;- Stack layout: :class:`kivy.uix.stacklayout.StackLayout`
15::CODE;;Understanding the `size_hint` Property in `Widget`
16::CODE;;--------------------------------------------------
17::CODE;;The :attr:`~kivy.uix.Widget.size_hint` is a tuple of values used by
18::CODE;;layouts to manage the sizes of their children. It indicates the size
19::CODE;;relative to the layout's size instead of an absolute size (in
20::CODE;;pixels/points/cm/etc). The format is::
21::CODE;;widget.size_hint = (width_proportion, height_proportion)
22::CODE;;The proportions are specified as floating point numbers in the range 0-1. For
23::CODE;;example, 0.5 represents 50%, 1 represents 100%.
24::CODE;;If you want a widget's width to be half of the parent's width and the
25::CODE;;height to be identical to the parent's height, you would do::
26::CODE;;widget.size_hint = (0.5, 1.0)
27::CODE;;If you don't want to use a size_hint for either the width or height, set the
28::CODE;;value to None. For example, to make a widget that is 250px wide and 30%
29::CODE;;of the parent's height, do::
30::CODE;;widget.size_hint = (None, 0.3)
31::CODE;;widget.width = 250
32::CODE;;Being :class:`Kivy properties <kivy.properties>`, these can also be set via
33::CODE;;constructor arguments::
34::CODE;;widget = Widget(size_hint=(None, 0.3), width=250)
35::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.4.1
36::CODE;;The `reposition_child` internal method (made public by mistake) has
37::CODE;;been removed.
38::CODE;;'''

79::CODE;;def layout_hint_with_bounds(
80::CODE;;self, sh_sum, available_space, min_bounded_size, sh_min_vals,
81::CODE;;sh_max_vals, hint):
82::CODE;;'''(internal) Computes the appropriate (size) hint for all the
83::CODE;;widgets given (potential) min or max bounds on the widgets' size.
84::CODE;;The ``hint`` list is updated with appropriate sizes.
85::CODE;;It walks through the hints and for any widgets whose hint will result
86::CODE;;in violating min or max constraints, it fixes the hint. Any remaining
87::CODE;;or missing space after all the widgets are fixed get distributed
88::CODE;;to the widgets making them smaller or larger according to their
89::CODE;;size hint.
90::CODE;;This algorithms knows nothing about the widgets other than what is
91::CODE;;passed through the input params, so it's fairly generic for laying
92::CODE;;things out according to constraints using size hints.
93::CODE;;:Parameters:
94::CODE;;`sh_sum`: float
95::CODE;;The sum of the size hints (basically ``sum(size_hint)``).
96::CODE;;`available_space`: float
97::CODE;;The amount of pixels available for all the widgets
98::CODE;;whose size hint is not None. Cannot be zero.
99::CODE;;`min_bounded_size`: float
100::CODE;;The minimum amount of space required according to the
101::CODE;;`size_hint_min` of the widgets (basically
102::CODE;;``sum(size_hint_min)``).
103::CODE;;`sh_min_vals`: list or iterable
104::CODE;;Items in the iterable are the size_hint_min for each widget.
105::CODE;;Can be None. The length should be the same as ``hint``
106::CODE;;`sh_max_vals`: list or iterable
107::CODE;;Items in the iterable are the size_hint_max for each widget.
108::CODE;;Can be None. The length should be the same as ``hint``
109::CODE;;`hint`: list
110::CODE;;A list whose size is the same as the length of ``sh_min_vals``
111::CODE;;and ``sh_min_vals`` whose each element is the corresponding
112::CODE;;size hint value of that element. This list is updated in place
113::CODE;;with correct size hints that ensure the constraints are not
114::CODE;;violated.
115::CODE;;:returns:
116::CODE;;Nothing. ``hint`` is updated in place.
117::CODE;;'''
118::CODE;;if not sh_sum:
119::CODE;;return
122::CODE;;stretch_ratio = sh_sum / float(available_space)
123::CODE;;if available_space <= min_bounded_size or \
124::CODE;;isclose(available_space, min_bounded_size):
126::CODE;;for i, (sh, sh_min) in enumerate(zip(hint, sh_min_vals)):
127::CODE;;if sh is None:
128::CODE;;continue
129::CODE;;if sh_min is not None:
131::CODE;;else:
133::CODE;;return
139::CODE;;oversize_amt = undersize_amt = 0
140::CODE;;hint_orig = hint[:]
144::CODE;;for i, (sh, sh_min, sh_max) in enumerate(
145::CODE;;zip(hint, sh_min_vals, sh_max_vals)):
146::CODE;;if sh is None:
147::CODE;;continue
148::CODE;;diff = 0
149::CODE;;if sh_min is not None:
150::CODE;;sh_min *= stretch_ratio
152::CODE;;if diff > 0:
153::CODE;;hint[i] = sh_min
154::CODE;;undersize_amt += diff
155::CODE;;else:
156::CODE;;not_mined_contrib[i] = None
157::CODE;;sh_mins_avail[i] = hint[i] - sh_min
158::CODE;;else:
159::CODE;;not_mined_contrib[i] = None
160::CODE;;sh_mins_avail[i] = hint[i]
161::CODE;;if sh_max is not None:
162::CODE;;sh_max *= stretch_ratio
163::CODE;;diff = sh - sh_max
164::CODE;;if diff > 0:
166::CODE;;oversize_amt += diff
167::CODE;;else:
168::CODE;;not_maxed_contrib[i] = None
169::CODE;;sh_maxs_avail[i] = sh_max - hint[i]
170::CODE;;else:
171::CODE;;not_maxed_contrib[i] = None
172::CODE;;sh_maxs_avail[i] = sh_sum - hint[i]
173::CODE;;if i in not_mined_contrib:
175::CODE;;if i in not_maxed_contrib:
180::CODE;;margin = oversize_amt - undersize_amt
181::CODE;;if isclose(oversize_amt, undersize_amt, abs_tol=1e-15):
182::CODE;;return
189::CODE;;if margin > 1e-15:
190::CODE;;contrib_amt = not_maxed_contrib
191::CODE;;sh_available = sh_maxs_avail
192::CODE;;mult = 1.
193::CODE;;contrib_proportion = hint_orig
194::CODE;;elif margin < -1e-15:
195::CODE;;margin *= -1.
196::CODE;;contrib_amt = not_mined_contrib
197::CODE;;sh_available = sh_mins_avail
198::CODE;;mult = -1.
201::CODE;;mn = min((h for h in hint_orig if h))
202::CODE;;mx = max((h for h in hint_orig if h is not None))
203::CODE;;hint_top = (2. * mn if mn else 1.) if mn == mx else mn + mx
204::CODE;;contrib_proportion = [None if h is None else hint_top - h for
205::CODE;;h in hint_orig]
209::CODE;;contrib_prop_sum = float(
210::CODE;;sum((contrib_proportion[i] for i in contrib_amt)))
211::CODE;;if contrib_prop_sum < 1e-9:
213::CODE;;return
214::CODE;;contrib_height = {
215::CODE;;i: val / (contrib_proportion[i] / contrib_prop_sum) for
216::CODE;;i, val in contrib_amt.items()}
217::CODE;;items = sorted(
218::CODE;;(i for i in contrib_amt),
219::CODE;;key=lambda x: contrib_height[x])
220::CODE;;j = items[0]
221::CODE;;sum_i_contributed = contrib_amt[j]
222::CODE;;last_height = contrib_height[j]
223::CODE;;sh_available_i = {j: sh_available[j]}
224::CODE;;contrib_prop_sum_i = contrib_proportion[j]
226::CODE;;i = 1
227::CODE;;if 1 < n:
228::CODE;;j = items[1]
229::CODE;;curr_height = contrib_height[j]
230::CODE;;done = False
231::CODE;;while not done and i < n:
232::CODE;;while i < n and last_height == curr_height:
233::CODE;;j = items[i]
234::CODE;;sum_i_contributed += contrib_amt[j]
235::CODE;;contrib_prop_sum_i += contrib_proportion[j]
236::CODE;;sh_available_i[j] = sh_available[j]
237::CODE;;curr_height = contrib_height[j]
238::CODE;;i += 1
239::CODE;;last_height = curr_height
240::CODE;;while not done:
241::CODE;;margin_height = ((margin + sum_i_contributed) /
242::CODE;;(contrib_prop_sum_i / contrib_prop_sum))
243::CODE;;if margin_height - curr_height > 1e-9 and i < n:
244::CODE;;break
245::CODE;;done = True
246::CODE;;for k, available_sh in list(sh_available_i.items()):
247::CODE;;if margin_height - available_sh / (
248::CODE;;contrib_proportion[k] / contrib_prop_sum) > 1e-9:
249::CODE;;del sh_available_i[k]
250::CODE;;sum_i_contributed -= contrib_amt[k]
251::CODE;;contrib_prop_sum_i -= contrib_proportion[k]
252::CODE;;margin -= available_sh
253::CODE;;hint[k] += mult * available_sh
254::CODE;;done = False
256::CODE;;break
257::CODE;;if sh_available_i:
258::CODE;;assert contrib_prop_sum_i and margin
259::CODE;;margin_height = ((margin + sum_i_contributed) /
260::CODE;;(contrib_prop_sum_i / contrib_prop_sum))
261::CODE;;for i in sh_available_i:
262::CODE;;hint[i] += mult * (
263::CODE;;margin_height * contrib_proportion[i] / contrib_prop_sum -
264::CODE;;contrib_amt[i])

2::CODE;;Popup
3::CODE;;=====
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.7
5::CODE;;.. image:: images/popup.jpg
6::CODE;;:align: right
7::CODE;;The :class:`Popup` widget is used to create modal popups. By default, the popup
8::CODE;;will cover the whole "parent" window. When you are creating a popup, you
9::CODE;;must at least set a :attr:`Popup.title` and :attr:`Popup.content`.
10::CODE;;Remember that the default size of a Widget is size_hint=(1, 1). If you don't
11::CODE;;want your popup to be fullscreen, either use size hints with values less than 1
12::CODE;;(for instance size_hint=(.8, .8)) or deactivate the size_hint and use
13::CODE;;fixed size attributes.
14::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.4.0
15::CODE;;The :class:`Popup` class now inherits from
16::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.modalview.ModalView`. The :class:`Popup` offers a default
17::CODE;;layout with a title and a separation bar.
18::CODE;;Examples
19::CODE;;--------
20::CODE;;Example of a simple 400x400 Hello world popup::
21::CODE;;popup = Popup(title='Test popup',
22::CODE;;content=Label(text='Hello world'),
23::CODE;;size_hint=(None, None), size=(400, 400))
24::CODE;;By default, any click outside the popup will dismiss/close it. If you don't
25::CODE;;want that, you can set
26::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.uix.modalview.ModalView.auto_dismiss` to False::
27::CODE;;popup = Popup(title='Test popup', content=Label(text='Hello world'),
28::CODE;;auto_dismiss=False)
29::CODE;;popup.open()
30::CODE;;To manually dismiss/close the popup, use
31::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.uix.modalview.ModalView.dismiss`::
32::CODE;;popup.dismiss()
33::CODE;;Both :meth:`~kivy.uix.modalview.ModalView.open` and
34::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.uix.modalview.ModalView.dismiss` are bindable. That means you
35::CODE;;can directly bind the function to an action, e.g. to a button's on_press::
37::CODE;;content = Button(text='Close me!')
38::CODE;;popup = Popup(content=content, auto_dismiss=False)
40::CODE;;content.bind(on_press=popup.dismiss)
42::CODE;;popup.open()
43::CODE;;Same thing in KV language only with :class:`Factory`:
44::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
46::CODE;;<MyPopup@Popup>:
47::CODE;;auto_dismiss: False
48::CODE;;Button:
49::CODE;;text: 'Close me!'
50::CODE;;on_release: root.dismiss()
51::CODE;;Button:
52::CODE;;text: 'Open popup'
53::CODE;;on_release: Factory.MyPopup().open()
54::CODE;;.. note::
55::CODE;;Popup is a special widget. Don't try to add it as a child to any other
56::CODE;;widget. If you do, Popup will be handled like an ordinary widget and
57::CODE;;won't be created hidden in the background.
58::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
59::CODE;;BoxLayout:
61::CODE;;Popup Events
62::CODE;;------------
63::CODE;;There are two events available: `on_open` which is raised when the popup is
64::CODE;;opening, and `on_dismiss` which is raised when the popup is closed.
65::CODE;;For `on_dismiss`, you can prevent the
66::CODE;;popup from closing by explicitly returning True from your callback::
67::CODE;;def my_callback(instance):
68::CODE;;print('Popup', instance, 'is being dismissed but is prevented!')
69::CODE;;return True
70::CODE;;popup = Popup(content=Label(text='Hello world'))
71::CODE;;popup.bind(on_dismiss=my_callback)
72::CODE;;popup.open()
73::CODE;;'''
74::CODE;;__all__ = ('Popup', 'PopupException')

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Progress Bar
3::CODE;;============
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.8
5::CODE;;.. image:: images/progressbar.jpg
6::CODE;;:align: right
7::CODE;;The :class:`ProgressBar` widget is used to visualize the progress of some task.
8::CODE;;Only the horizontal mode is currently supported: the vertical mode is not
9::CODE;;yet available.
10::CODE;;The progress bar has no interactive elements and is a display-only widget.
11::CODE;;To use it, simply assign a value to indicate the current progress::
12::CODE;;from kivy.uix.progressbar import ProgressBar
13::CODE;;pb = ProgressBar(max=1000)
15::CODE;;pb.value = 750
16::CODE;;'''
17::CODE;;__all__ = ('ProgressBar', )
18::CODE;;from kivy.uix.widget import Widget
19::CODE;;from kivy.properties import NumericProperty, AliasProperty
20::CODE;;class ProgressBar(Widget):
21::CODE;;'''Class for creating a progress bar widget.
22::CODE;;See module documentation for more details.
23::CODE;;'''
24::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
25::CODE;;self._value = 0.
26::CODE;;super(ProgressBar, self).__init__(**kwargs)
27::CODE;;def _get_value(self):
28::CODE;;return self._value
29::CODE;;def _set_value(self, value):
30::CODE;;value = max(0, min(self.max, value))
31::CODE;;if value != self._value:
32::CODE;;self._value = value
33::CODE;;return True
34::CODE;;value = AliasProperty(_get_value, _set_value)
35::CODE;;'''Current value used for the slider.
36::CODE;;:attr:`value` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.AliasProperty` that
37::CODE;;returns the value of the progress bar. If the value is < 0 or >
38::CODE;;:attr:`max`, it will be normalized to those boundaries.
39::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.6.0
40::CODE;;The value is now limited to between 0 and :attr:`max`.
41::CODE;;'''
42::CODE;;def get_norm_value(self):
43::CODE;;d = self.max
44::CODE;;if d == 0:
45::CODE;;return 0
46::CODE;;return self.value / float(d)
47::CODE;;def set_norm_value(self, value):
48::CODE;;self.value = value * self.max
49::CODE;;value_normalized = AliasProperty(get_norm_value, set_norm_value,
50::CODE;;bind=('value', 'max'), cache=True)
51::CODE;;'''Normalized value inside the range 0-1::
52::CODE;;>>> pb = ProgressBar(value=50, max=100)
53::CODE;;>>> pb.value
54::CODE;;50
55::CODE;;>>> pb.value_normalized
56::CODE;;0.5
57::CODE;;:attr:`value_normalized` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.AliasProperty`.
58::CODE;;'''
59::CODE;;max = NumericProperty(100.)
60::CODE;;'''Maximum value allowed for :attr:`value`.
61::CODE;;:attr:`max` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and defaults to
62::CODE;;100.
63::CODE;;'''
64::CODE;;if __name__ == '__main__':
65::CODE;;from kivy.base import runTouchApp
66::CODE;;runTouchApp(ProgressBar(value=50))
13::CODE;;from kivy.uix.recyclelayout import RecycleLayout
14::CODE;;from kivy.uix.boxlayout import BoxLayout
15::CODE;;__all__ = ('RecycleBoxLayout', )
16::CODE;;class RecycleBoxLayout(RecycleLayout, BoxLayout):
17::CODE;;_rv_positions = None
18::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
19::CODE;;super(RecycleBoxLayout, self).__init__(**kwargs)
20::CODE;;self.funbind('children', self._trigger_layout)
21::CODE;;def _update_sizes(self, changed):
22::CODE;;horizontal = self.orientation == 'horizontal'
23::CODE;;padding_left, padding_top, padding_right, padding_bottom = self.padding
24::CODE;;padding_x = padding_left + padding_right
25::CODE;;padding_y = padding_top + padding_bottom
26::CODE;;selfw = self.width
27::CODE;;selfh = self.height
28::CODE;;layout_w = max(0, selfw - padding_x)
29::CODE;;layout_h = max(0, selfh - padding_y)
30::CODE;;cx = self.x + padding_left
31::CODE;;cy = self.y + padding_bottom
32::CODE;;view_opts = self.view_opts
33::CODE;;remove_view = self.remove_view
34::CODE;;for (index, widget, (w, h), (wn, hn), (shw, shh), (shnw, shnh),
35::CODE;;(shw_min, shh_min), (shwn_min, shhn_min), (shw_max, shh_max),
36::CODE;;(shwn_max, shhn_max), ph, phn) in changed:
37::CODE;;if (horizontal and
38::CODE;;(shw != shnw or w != wn or shw_min != shwn_min or
39::CODE;;shw_max != shwn_max) or
40::CODE;;not horizontal and
41::CODE;;(shh != shnh or h != hn or shh_min != shhn_min or
42::CODE;;shh_max != shhn_max)):
43::CODE;;return True
44::CODE;;remove_view(widget, index)
45::CODE;;opt = view_opts[index]
46::CODE;;if horizontal:
47::CODE;;wo, ho = opt['size']
48::CODE;;if shnh is not None:
49::CODE;;_, h = opt['size'] = [wo, shnh * layout_h]
50::CODE;;else:
51::CODE;;h = ho
52::CODE;;xo, yo = opt['pos']
53::CODE;;for key, value in phn.items():
54::CODE;;posy = value * layout_h
55::CODE;;if key == 'y':
56::CODE;;yo = posy + cy
57::CODE;;elif key == 'top':
58::CODE;;yo = posy - h
59::CODE;;elif key == 'center_y':
60::CODE;;yo = posy - (h / 2.)
61::CODE;;opt['pos'] = [xo, yo]
62::CODE;;else:
63::CODE;;wo, ho = opt['size']
64::CODE;;if shnw is not None:
65::CODE;;w, _ = opt['size'] = [shnw * layout_w, ho]
66::CODE;;else:
67::CODE;;w = wo
68::CODE;;xo, yo = opt['pos']
69::CODE;;for key, value in phn.items():
70::CODE;;posx = value * layout_w
71::CODE;;if key == 'x':
72::CODE;;xo = posx + cx
73::CODE;;elif key == 'right':
74::CODE;;xo = posx - w
75::CODE;;elif key == 'center_x':
76::CODE;;xo = posx - (w / 2.)
77::CODE;;opt['pos'] = [xo, yo]
78::CODE;;return False
79::CODE;;def compute_layout(self, data, flags):
80::CODE;;super(RecycleBoxLayout, self).compute_layout(data, flags)
81::CODE;;changed = self._changed_views
82::CODE;;if (changed is None or
83::CODE;;changed and not self._update_sizes(changed)):
84::CODE;;return
85::CODE;;self.clear_layout()
86::CODE;;self._rv_positions = None
87::CODE;;if not data:
88::CODE;;l, t, r, b = self.padding
89::CODE;;self.minimum_size = l + r, t + b
90::CODE;;return
91::CODE;;view_opts = self.view_opts
92::CODE;;n = len(view_opts)
93::CODE;;for i, x, y, w, h in self._iterate_layout(
94::CODE;;[(opt['size'], opt['size_hint'], opt['pos_hint'],
95::CODE;;opt['size_hint_min'], opt['size_hint_max']) for
96::CODE;;opt in reversed(view_opts)]):
97::CODE;;opt = view_opts[n - i - 1]
98::CODE;;shw, shh = opt['size_hint']
99::CODE;;opt['pos'] = x, y
100::CODE;;wo, ho = opt['size']
103::CODE;;opt['size'] = [(wo if shw is None else w),
104::CODE;;(ho if shh is None else h)]
105::CODE;;spacing = self.spacing
106::CODE;;pos = self._rv_positions = [None, ] * len(data)
107::CODE;;if self.orientation == 'horizontal':
108::CODE;;pos[0] = self.x
109::CODE;;last = pos[0] + self.padding[0] + view_opts[0]['size'][0] + \
110::CODE;;spacing / 2.
111::CODE;;for i, val in enumerate(view_opts[1:], 1):
112::CODE;;pos[i] = last
113::CODE;;last += val['size'][0] + spacing
114::CODE;;else:
115::CODE;;last = pos[-1] = \
116::CODE;;self.y + self.height - self.padding[1] - \
117::CODE;;view_opts[0]['size'][1] - spacing / 2.
118::CODE;;n = len(view_opts)
119::CODE;;for i, val in enumerate(view_opts[1:], 1):
120::CODE;;last -= spacing + val['size'][1]
121::CODE;;pos[n - 1 - i] = last
122::CODE;;def get_view_index_at(self, pos):
123::CODE;;calc_pos = self._rv_positions
124::CODE;;if not calc_pos:
125::CODE;;return 0
126::CODE;;x, y = pos
127::CODE;;if self.orientation == 'horizontal':
128::CODE;;if x >= calc_pos[-1] or len(calc_pos) == 1:
129::CODE;;return len(calc_pos) - 1
130::CODE;;ix = 0
131::CODE;;for val in calc_pos[1:]:
132::CODE;;if x < val:
133::CODE;;return ix
134::CODE;;ix += 1
135::CODE;;else:
136::CODE;;if y >= calc_pos[-1] or len(calc_pos) == 1:
137::CODE;;return 0
138::CODE;;iy = 0
139::CODE;;for val in calc_pos[1:]:
140::CODE;;if y < val:
141::CODE;;return len(calc_pos) - iy - 1
142::CODE;;iy += 1
143::CODE;;assert False
144::CODE;;def compute_visible_views(self, data, viewport):
145::CODE;;if self._rv_positions is None or not data:
146::CODE;;return []
147::CODE;;x, y, w, h = viewport
148::CODE;;at_idx = self.get_view_index_at
149::CODE;;if self.orientation == 'horizontal':
150::CODE;;a, b = at_idx((x, y)), at_idx((x + w, y))
151::CODE;;else:
152::CODE;;a, b = at_idx((x, y + h)), at_idx((x, y))
153::CODE;;return list(range(a, b + 1))
154::CODE;;def goto_view(self, index):
159::CODE;;if not self.view_opts or not self.parent:
160::CODE;;return
162::CODE;;num_items = len(self.view_opts)
164::CODE;;index = max(-num_items, min(index, num_items - 1))
165::CODE;;if index < 0:
166::CODE;;index = num_items + index
168::CODE;;padding_left, padding_top, padding_right, padding_bottom = self.padding
169::CODE;;spacing = self.spacing
171::CODE;;if self.orientation == "horizontal":
173::CODE;;total_width = (
174::CODE;;sum(w["size"][0] for w in self.view_opts)
175::CODE;;+ (num_items - 1) * spacing
176::CODE;;+ padding_left
177::CODE;;+ padding_right
178::CODE;;)
180::CODE;;target_pos = padding_left + sum(
181::CODE;;self.view_opts[i]["size"][0] + spacing for i in range(index)
182::CODE;;)
184::CODE;;viewport_width = self.parent.width
188::CODE;;item_width = self.view_opts[index]["size"][0]
189::CODE;;if item_width > viewport_width:
191::CODE;;target_scroll = max(
192::CODE;;0,
193::CODE;;min(
194::CODE;;1,
195::CODE;;(target_pos - (viewport_width - item_width) / 2)
196::CODE;;/ (total_width - viewport_width),
197::CODE;;),
198::CODE;;)
199::CODE;;else:
201::CODE;;target_scroll = max(
202::CODE;;0, min(1, target_pos / (total_width - viewport_width))
203::CODE;;)
205::CODE;;self.parent.scroll_x = target_scroll
208::CODE;;total_height = (
209::CODE;;sum(w["size"][1] for w in self.view_opts)
210::CODE;;+ (num_items - 1) * spacing
211::CODE;;+ padding_top
212::CODE;;+ padding_bottom
213::CODE;;)
215::CODE;;target_pos = padding_top
216::CODE;;for i in range(index):
217::CODE;;target_pos += self.view_opts[i]["size"][1] + spacing
219::CODE;;viewport_height = self.parent.height
223::CODE;;item_height = self.view_opts[index]["size"][1]
224::CODE;;if item_height > viewport_height:
226::CODE;;target_scroll = max(
227::CODE;;0,
228::CODE;;min(
229::CODE;;1,
230::CODE;;1
231::CODE;;- (target_pos - (viewport_height - item_height) / 2)
232::CODE;;/ (total_height - viewport_height),
233::CODE;;),
234::CODE;;)
235::CODE;;else:
237::CODE;;target_scroll = max(
238::CODE;;0, min(1, 1 - target_pos / (total_height - viewport_height))
239::CODE;;)
241::CODE;;self.parent.scroll_y = target_scroll
13::CODE;;import itertools

21::CODE;;_cols_pos = None
22::CODE;;_rows_pos = None
23::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):

28::CODE;;def _fill_rows_cols_sizes(self):
29::CODE;;cols, rows = self._cols, self._rows
30::CODE;;cols_sh, rows_sh = self._cols_sh, self._rows_sh
31::CODE;;cols_sh_min, rows_sh_min = self._cols_sh_min, self._rows_sh_min
32::CODE;;cols_sh_max, rows_sh_max = self._cols_sh_max, self._rows_sh_max
33::CODE;;self._cols_count = cols_count = [defaultdict(int) for _ in cols]
34::CODE;;self._rows_count = rows_count = [defaultdict(int) for _ in rows]
36::CODE;;idx_iter = self._create_idx_iter(len(cols), len(rows))
37::CODE;;has_bound_y = has_bound_x = False
38::CODE;;for opt, (col, row) in zip(self.view_opts, idx_iter):
39::CODE;;(shw, shh), (w, h) = opt['size_hint'], opt['size']
40::CODE;;shw_min, shh_min = opt['size_hint_min']
41::CODE;;shw_max, shh_max = opt['size_hint_max']
42::CODE;;if shw is None:
43::CODE;;cols_count[col][w] += 1
44::CODE;;if shh is None:
45::CODE;;rows_count[row][h] += 1
47::CODE;;if shw is None:
48::CODE;;cols[col] = nmax(cols[col], w)
49::CODE;;else:
50::CODE;;cols_sh[col] = nmax(cols_sh[col], shw)
51::CODE;;if shw_min is not None:
52::CODE;;has_bound_x = True
53::CODE;;cols_sh_min[col] = nmax(cols_sh_min[col], shw_min)
54::CODE;;if shw_max is not None:
55::CODE;;has_bound_x = True
56::CODE;;cols_sh_max[col] = nmin(cols_sh_max[col], shw_max)
57::CODE;;if shh is None:
58::CODE;;rows[row] = nmax(rows[row], h)
59::CODE;;else:
60::CODE;;rows_sh[row] = nmax(rows_sh[row], shh)
61::CODE;;if shh_min is not None:
62::CODE;;has_bound_y = True
63::CODE;;rows_sh_min[row] = nmax(rows_sh_min[row], shh_min)
64::CODE;;if shh_max is not None:
65::CODE;;has_bound_y = True
66::CODE;;rows_sh_max[row] = nmin(rows_sh_max[row], shh_max)
67::CODE;;self._has_hint_bound_x = has_bound_x
68::CODE;;self._has_hint_bound_y = has_bound_y
69::CODE;;def _update_rows_cols_sizes(self, changed):
70::CODE;;cols_count, rows_count = self._cols_count, self._rows_count
71::CODE;;cols, rows = self._cols, self._rows
72::CODE;;remove_view = self.remove_view
73::CODE;;n_cols = len(cols)
74::CODE;;n_rows = len(rows)
75::CODE;;orientation = self.orientation
77::CODE;;for index, widget, (w, h), (wn, hn), sh, shn, sh_min, shn_min, \
78::CODE;;sh_max, shn_max, _, _ in changed:
79::CODE;;if sh != shn or sh_min != shn_min or sh_max != shn_max:

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;RecycleView Data Model
3::CODE;;======================
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.10.0
5::CODE;;The data model part of the RecycleView model-view-controller pattern.
6::CODE;;It defines the models (classes) that store the data associated with a
7::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.recycleview.RecycleViewBehavior`. Each model (class)
8::CODE;;determines how the data is stored and emits requests to the controller
9::CODE;;(:class:`~kivy.uix.recycleview.RecycleViewBehavior`) when the data is
10::CODE;;modified.
11::CODE;;'''
12::CODE;;from kivy.properties import ListProperty, ObservableDict, ObjectProperty
13::CODE;;from kivy.event import EventDispatcher
14::CODE;;from functools import partial
15::CODE;;__all__ = ('RecycleDataModelBehavior', 'RecycleDataModel')
16::CODE;;def recondition_slice_assign(val, last_len, new_len):
17::CODE;;if not isinstance(val, slice):
18::CODE;;return slice(val, val + 1)
19::CODE;;diff = new_len - last_len
20::CODE;;start, stop, step = val.start, val.stop, val.step
21::CODE;;if stop <= start:
22::CODE;;return slice(0, 0)
23::CODE;;if step is not None and step != 1:
24::CODE;;assert last_len == new_len
25::CODE;;if stop < 0:
26::CODE;;stop = max(0, last_len + stop)
27::CODE;;stop = min(last_len, stop)
28::CODE;;if start < 0:
29::CODE;;start = max(0, last_len + start)
30::CODE;;start = min(last_len, start)
31::CODE;;return slice(start, stop, step)
32::CODE;;if start < 0:
33::CODE;;start = last_len + start
34::CODE;;if stop < 0:
35::CODE;;stop = last_len + stop
37::CODE;;if (start < 0 or stop < 0 or start > last_len or stop > last_len or
38::CODE;;new_len != last_len):
39::CODE;;return None
40::CODE;;return slice(start, stop)

79::CODE;;class RecycleDataModel(RecycleDataModelBehavior, EventDispatcher):
80::CODE;;'''An implementation of :class:`RecycleDataModelBehavior` that keeps the
81::CODE;;data in a indexable list. See :attr:`data`.
82::CODE;;When data changes this class currently dispatches `on_data_changed` with
83::CODE;;one of the following additional keyword arguments.
84::CODE;;`none`: no keyword argument
85::CODE;;With no additional argument it means a generic data change.
86::CODE;;`removed`: a slice or integer
87::CODE;;The value is a slice or integer indicating the indices removed.
88::CODE;;`appended`: a slice
89::CODE;;The slice in :attr:`data` indicating the first and last new items
90::CODE;;(i.e. the slice pointing to the new items added at the end).
91::CODE;;`inserted`: a integer
92::CODE;;The index in :attr:`data` where a new data item was inserted.
93::CODE;;`modified`: a slice
94::CODE;;The slice with the indices where the data has been modified.
95::CODE;;This currently does not allow changing of size etc.
96::CODE;;'''
97::CODE;;data = ListProperty([])
98::CODE;;'''Stores the model's data using a list.
99::CODE;;The data for a item at index `i` can also be accessed with
100::CODE;;:class:`RecycleDataModel` `[i]`.
101::CODE;;'''
102::CODE;;_last_len = 0
103::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
104::CODE;;self.fbind('data', self._on_data_callback)
105::CODE;;super(RecycleDataModel, self).__init__(**kwargs)
106::CODE;;def __getitem__(self, index):

113::CODE;;return partial(ObservableDict, self.__class__.data, self)

123::CODE;;def _on_data_callback(self, instance, value):
124::CODE;;last_len = self._last_len
125::CODE;;new_len = self._last_len = len(self.data)
126::CODE;;op, val = value.last_op
127::CODE;;if op == '__setitem__':
128::CODE;;val = recondition_slice_assign(val, last_len, new_len)
129::CODE;;if val is not None:
130::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_data_changed', modified=val)
131::CODE;;else:
132::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_data_changed')
133::CODE;;elif op == '__delitem__':
134::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_data_changed', removed=val)
135::CODE;;elif op == '__setslice__':
136::CODE;;val = recondition_slice_assign(slice(*val), last_len, new_len)
137::CODE;;if val is not None:
138::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_data_changed', modified=val)
139::CODE;;else:
140::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_data_changed')
141::CODE;;elif op == '__delslice__':
142::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_data_changed', removed=slice(*val))
143::CODE;;elif op == '__iadd__' or op == '__imul__':
144::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_data_changed', appended=slice(last_len, new_len))
145::CODE;;elif op == 'append':
146::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_data_changed', appended=slice(last_len, new_len))
147::CODE;;elif op == 'insert':
148::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_data_changed', inserted=val)
149::CODE;;elif op == 'pop':
150::CODE;;if val:
151::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_data_changed', removed=val[0])
152::CODE;;else:
153::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_data_changed', removed=last_len - 1)
154::CODE;;elif op == 'extend':
155::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_data_changed', appended=slice(last_len, new_len))
156::CODE;;else:
157::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_data_changed')

18::CODE;;class LayoutSelectionBehavior(CompoundSelectionBehavior):
19::CODE;;'''The :class:`LayoutSelectionBehavior` can be combined with
20::CODE;;:class:`RecycleLayoutManagerBehavior` to allow its derived classes
21::CODE;;selection behaviors similarly to how
22::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.compoundselection.CompoundSelectionBehavior`
23::CODE;;can be used to add selection behaviors to normal layout.
24::CODE;;:class:`RecycleLayoutManagerBehavior` manages its children
25::CODE;;differently than normal layouts or widgets so this class adapts
26::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.compoundselection.CompoundSelectionBehavior`
27::CODE;;based selection to work with :class:`RecycleLayoutManagerBehavior` as well.
28::CODE;;Similarly to
29::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.compoundselection.CompoundSelectionBehavior`,
30::CODE;;one can select using the keyboard or touch, which calls :meth:`select_node`
31::CODE;;or :meth:`deselect_node`, or one can call these methods directly. When a
32::CODE;;item is selected or deselected :meth:`apply_selection` is called. See
33::CODE;;:meth:`apply_selection`.
34::CODE;;'''
35::CODE;;key_selection = StringProperty(None, allownone=True)
36::CODE;;'''The key used to check whether a view of a data item can be selected
37::CODE;;with touch or the keyboard.
38::CODE;;:attr:`key_selection` is the key in data, which if present and ``True``
39::CODE;;will enable selection for this item from the keyboard or with a touch.
40::CODE;;When None, the default, not item will be selectable.
41::CODE;;:attr:`key_selection` is a :class:`StringProperty` and defaults to None.
42::CODE;;.. note::
43::CODE;;All data items can be selected directly using :meth:`select_node` or
44::CODE;;:meth:`deselect_node`, even if :attr:`key_selection` is False.
45::CODE;;'''

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;RecycleView Views
3::CODE;;=================
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.10.0
5::CODE;;The adapter part of the RecycleView which together with the layout is the
6::CODE;;view part of the model-view-controller pattern.
7::CODE;;The view module handles converting the data to a view using the adapter class
8::CODE;;which is then displayed by the layout. A view can be any Widget based class.
9::CODE;;However, inheriting from RecycleDataViewBehavior adds methods for converting
10::CODE;;the data to a view.
11::CODE;;TODO:
12::CODE;;* Make view caches specific to each view class type.
13::CODE;;'''

33::CODE;;'''Trims _cached_views cache to half the size of `_max_cache_size`.
34::CODE;;'''

37::CODE;;global _cache_count
38::CODE;;for cls, instances in _cached_views.items():
39::CODE;;_cache_count -= max(0, len(instances) - max_size)
40::CODE;;del instances[max_size:]

119::CODE;;class RecycleDataAdapter(EventDispatcher):
120::CODE;;'''The class that converts data to a view.
121::CODE;;--- Internal details ---
122::CODE;;A view can have 3 states.
123::CODE;;* It can be completely in sync with the data, which
124::CODE;;occurs when the view is displayed. These are stored in :attr:`views`.
125::CODE;;* It can be dirty, which occurs when the view is in sync with the data,
126::CODE;;except for the size/pos parameters which is controlled by the layout.
127::CODE;;This occurs when the view is not currently displayed but the data has
128::CODE;;not changed. These views are stored in :attr:`dirty_views`.
129::CODE;;* Finally the view can be dead which occurs when the data changes and
130::CODE;;the view was not updated or when a view is just created. Such views
131::CODE;;are typically added to the internal cache.
132::CODE;;Typically what happens is that the layout manager lays out the data
133::CODE;;and then asks for views, using :meth:`set_visible_views`, for some specific
134::CODE;;data items that it displays.
135::CODE;;These views are gotten from the current views, dirty or global cache. Then
136::CODE;;depending on the view state :meth:`refresh_view_attrs` is called to bring
137::CODE;;the view up to date with the data (except for sizing parameters). Finally,
138::CODE;;the layout manager gets these views, updates their size and displays them.
139::CODE;;'''
140::CODE;;recycleview = ObjectProperty(None, allownone=True)
141::CODE;;'''The :class:`~kivy.uix.recycleview.RecycleViewBehavior` associated
142::CODE;;with this instance.
143::CODE;;'''

148::CODE;;_sizing_attrs = {
149::CODE;;'size', 'width', 'height', 'size_hint', 'size_hint_x', 'size_hint_y',
150::CODE;;'pos', 'x', 'y', 'center', 'center_x', 'center_y', 'pos_hint',
151::CODE;;'size_hint_min', 'size_hint_min_x', 'size_hint_min_y', 'size_hint_max',
152::CODE;;'size_hint_max_x', 'size_hint_max_y'}

269::CODE;;def make_views_dirty(self):
270::CODE;;'''Makes all the current views dirty.
271::CODE;;Dirty views are still in sync with the corresponding data. However, the
272::CODE;;size information may go out of sync. Therefore a dirty view can be
273::CODE;;reused by the same index by just updating the sizing information.
274::CODE;;Once the underlying data of this index changes, the view should be
275::CODE;;removed from the dirty views and moved to the global cache with
276::CODE;;:meth:`invalidate`.
277::CODE;;This is typically called when the layout manager needs to re-layout all
278::CODE;;the data.
279::CODE;;'''
280::CODE;;views = self.views
281::CODE;;if not views:
282::CODE;;return
283::CODE;;dirty_views = self.dirty_views
284::CODE;;for index, view in views.items():
285::CODE;;dirty_views[view.__class__][index] = view
286::CODE;;self.views = {}
287::CODE;;def invalidate(self):
288::CODE;;'''Moves all the current views into the global cache.
289::CODE;;As opposed to making a view dirty where the view is in sync with the
290::CODE;;data except for sizing information, this will completely disconnect the
291::CODE;;view from the data, as it is assumed the data has gone out of sync with
292::CODE;;the view.
293::CODE;;This is typically called when the data changes.
294::CODE;;'''
295::CODE;;global _cache_count
296::CODE;;for view in self.views.values():
297::CODE;;_cached_views[view.__class__].append(view)
298::CODE;;_cache_count += 1
299::CODE;;for cls, views in self.dirty_views.items():
300::CODE;;_cached_views[cls].extend(views.values())
301::CODE;;_cache_count += len(views)
302::CODE;;if _cache_count >= _max_cache_size:
303::CODE;;_clean_cache()
304::CODE;;self.views = {}
305::CODE;;self.dirty_views.clear()
306::CODE;;def set_visible_views(self, indices, data, viewclasses):
307::CODE;;'''Gets a 3-tuple of the new, remaining, and old views for the current
308::CODE;;viewport.
309::CODE;;The new views are synced to the data except for the size/pos
310::CODE;;properties.
311::CODE;;The old views need to be removed from the layout, and the new views
312::CODE;;added.
313::CODE;;The new views are not necessarily *new*, but are all the currently
314::CODE;;visible views.
315::CODE;;'''
316::CODE;;visible_views = {}
317::CODE;;previous_views = self.views
318::CODE;;ret_new = []
319::CODE;;ret_remain = []
320::CODE;;get_view = self.get_view
323::CODE;;for index in indices:
324::CODE;;view = previous_views.pop(index, None)
326::CODE;;visible_views[index] = view
327::CODE;;ret_remain.append((index, view))
328::CODE;;else:
329::CODE;;view = get_view(index, data[index],
330::CODE;;viewclasses[index]['viewclass'])
331::CODE;;if view is None:
332::CODE;;continue
333::CODE;;visible_views[index] = view
334::CODE;;ret_new.append((index, view))
335::CODE;;old_views = previous_views.items()
336::CODE;;self.make_views_dirty()
337::CODE;;self.views = visible_views
338::CODE;;return ret_new, ret_remain, old_views
339::CODE;;def get_visible_view(self, index):

341::CODE;;If no view is currently displayed for ``index`` it returns ``None``.
342::CODE;;'''
343::CODE;;return self.views.get(index)
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Relative Layout
3::CODE;;===============
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.4.0
5::CODE;;This layout allows you to set relative coordinates for children. If you want
6::CODE;;absolute positioning, use the :class:`~kivy.uix.floatlayout.FloatLayout`.
7::CODE;;The :class:`RelativeLayout` class behaves just like the regular
8::CODE;;:class:`FloatLayout` except that its child widgets are positioned relative to
9::CODE;;the layout.
10::CODE;;When a widget with position = (0,0) is added to a RelativeLayout,
11::CODE;;the child widget will also move when the position of the RelativeLayout
12::CODE;;is changed. The child widgets coordinates remain (0,0) as they are
13::CODE;;always relative to the parent layout.
14::CODE;;Coordinate Systems
15::CODE;;------------------
16::CODE;;Window coordinates
17::CODE;;~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
18::CODE;;By default, there's only one coordinate system that defines the position of
19::CODE;;widgets and touch events dispatched to them: the window coordinate system,
20::CODE;;which places (0, 0) at the bottom left corner of the window.
21::CODE;;Although there are other coordinate systems defined, e.g. local
22::CODE;;and parent coordinates, these coordinate systems are identical to the window
23::CODE;;coordinate system as long as a relative layout type widget is not in the
24::CODE;;widget's parent stack. When widget.pos is read or a touch is received,
25::CODE;;the coordinate values are in parent coordinates. But as mentioned, these are
26::CODE;;identical to window coordinates, even in complex widget stacks as long as
27::CODE;;there's no relative layout type widget in the widget's parent stack.
28::CODE;;For example:
29::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
30::CODE;;BoxLayout:
31::CODE;;Label:
32::CODE;;text: 'Left'
33::CODE;;Button:
34::CODE;;text: 'Middle'
35::CODE;;on_touch_down: print('Middle: {}'.format(args[1].pos))
36::CODE;;BoxLayout:
37::CODE;;on_touch_down: print('Box: {}'.format(args[1].pos))
38::CODE;;Button:
39::CODE;;text: 'Right'
40::CODE;;on_touch_down: print('Right: {}'.format(args[1].pos))
41::CODE;;When the middle button is clicked and the touch propagates through the
42::CODE;;different parent coordinate systems, it prints the following::
43::CODE;;>>> Box: (430.0, 282.0)
44::CODE;;>>> Right: (430.0, 282.0)
45::CODE;;>>> Middle: (430.0, 282.0)
46::CODE;;As claimed, the touch has identical coordinates to the window coordinates
47::CODE;;in every coordinate system. :meth:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.collide_point`
48::CODE;;for example, takes the point in window coordinates.
49::CODE;;Parent coordinates
50::CODE;;~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
51::CODE;;Other :class:`RelativeLayout` type widgets are
52::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.scatter.Scatter`,
53::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.scatterlayout.ScatterLayout`,
54::CODE;;and :class:`~kivy.uix.scrollview.ScrollView`. If such a special widget is in
55::CODE;;the parent stack, only then does the parent and local coordinate system
56::CODE;;diverge from the window coordinate system. For each such widget in the stack,
57::CODE;;a coordinate system with (0, 0) of that coordinate system being at the bottom
58::CODE;;left corner of that widget is created. **Position and touch coordinates
59::CODE;;received and read by a widget are in the coordinate system of the most
60::CODE;;recent special widget in its parent stack (not including itself) or in window
61::CODE;;coordinates if there are none** (as in the first example). We call these
62::CODE;;coordinates parent coordinates.
63::CODE;;For example:
64::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
65::CODE;;BoxLayout:
66::CODE;;Label:
67::CODE;;text: 'Left'
68::CODE;;Button:
69::CODE;;text: 'Middle'
70::CODE;;on_touch_down: print('Middle: {}'.format(args[1].pos))
71::CODE;;RelativeLayout:
72::CODE;;on_touch_down: print('Relative: {}'.format(args[1].pos))
73::CODE;;Button:
74::CODE;;text: 'Right'
75::CODE;;on_touch_down: print('Right: {}'.format(args[1].pos))
76::CODE;;Clicking on the middle button prints::
77::CODE;;>>> Relative: (396.0, 298.0)
78::CODE;;>>> Right: (-137.33, 298.0)
79::CODE;;>>> Middle: (396.0, 298.0)
80::CODE;;As the touch propagates through the widgets, for each widget, the
81::CODE;;touch is received in parent coordinates. Because both the relative and middle
82::CODE;;widgets don't have these special widgets in their parent stack, the touch is
83::CODE;;the same as window coordinates. Only the right widget, which has a
84::CODE;;RelativeLayout in its parent stack, receives the touch in coordinates relative
85::CODE;;to that RelativeLayout which is different than window coordinates.
86::CODE;;Local and Widget coordinates
87::CODE;;~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
88::CODE;;When expressed in parent coordinates, the position is expressed in the
89::CODE;;coordinates of the most recent special widget in its parent stack, not
90::CODE;;including itself. When expressed in local or widget coordinates, the widgets
91::CODE;;themselves are also included.
92::CODE;;Changing the above example to transform the parent coordinates into local
93::CODE;;coordinates:
94::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
95::CODE;;BoxLayout:
96::CODE;;Label:
97::CODE;;text: 'Left'
98::CODE;;Button:
99::CODE;;text: 'Middle'
100::CODE;;on_touch_down: print('Middle: {}'.format(\
101::CODE;;self.to_local(*args[1].pos)))
102::CODE;;RelativeLayout:
103::CODE;;on_touch_down: print('Relative: {}'.format(\
104::CODE;;self.to_local(*args[1].pos)))
105::CODE;;Button:
106::CODE;;text: 'Right'
107::CODE;;on_touch_down: print('Right: {}'.format(\
108::CODE;;self.to_local(*args[1].pos)))
109::CODE;;Now, clicking on the middle button prints::
110::CODE;;>>> Relative: (-135.33, 301.0)
111::CODE;;>>> Right: (-135.33, 301.0)
112::CODE;;>>> Middle: (398.0, 301.0)
113::CODE;;This is because now the relative widget also expresses the coordinates
114::CODE;;relative to itself.
115::CODE;;.. note::
116::CODE;;Although all widgets including :class:`RelativeLayout` receive their touch
117::CODE;;events in ``on_touch_xxx`` in parent coordinates, these special widgets
118::CODE;;will transform the touch position to be in local coordinates before it
119::CODE;;calls ``super``. This may only be noticeable in a complex inheritance
120::CODE;;class.
121::CODE;;Coordinate transformations
122::CODE;;~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
123::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget` provides 4 functions to transform coordinates
124::CODE;;between the various coordinate systems. For now, we assume that the `relative`
125::CODE;;keyword of these functions is `False`.
126::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.to_widget` takes the coordinates expressed in
127::CODE;;window coordinates and returns them in local (widget) coordinates.
128::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.to_window` takes the coordinates expressed in
129::CODE;;local coordinates and returns them in window coordinates.
130::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.to_parent` takes the coordinates expressed in
131::CODE;;local coordinates and returns them in parent coordinates.
132::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.to_local` takes the coordinates expressed in
133::CODE;;parent coordinates and returns them in local coordinates.
134::CODE;;Each of the 4 transformation functions take a `relative` parameter. When the
135::CODE;;relative parameter is True, the coordinates are returned or originate in
136::CODE;;true relative coordinates - relative to a coordinate system with its (0, 0) at
137::CODE;;the bottom left corner of the widget in question.
138::CODE;;.. _kivy-uix-relativelayout-common-pitfalls:
139::CODE;;Common Pitfalls
140::CODE;;---------------
141::CODE;;As all positions within a :class:`RelativeLayout` are relative to the position
142::CODE;;of the layout itself, the position of the layout should never be used in
143::CODE;;determining the position of sub-widgets or the layout's :attr:`canvas`.
144::CODE;;Take the following kv code for example:
145::CODE;;.. container:: align-right
146::CODE;;.. figure:: images/relativelayout-fixedposition.png
147::CODE;;:scale: 50%
148::CODE;;expected result
149::CODE;;.. figure:: images/relativelayout-doubleposition.png
150::CODE;;:scale: 50%
151::CODE;;actual result
152::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
153::CODE;;FloatLayout:
154::CODE;;Widget:
155::CODE;;size_hint: None, None
156::CODE;;size: 200, 200
157::CODE;;pos: 200, 200
158::CODE;;canvas:
159::CODE;;Color:
160::CODE;;rgba: 1, 1, 1, 1
161::CODE;;Rectangle:
162::CODE;;pos: self.pos
163::CODE;;size: self.size
164::CODE;;RelativeLayout:
165::CODE;;size_hint: None, None
166::CODE;;size: 200, 200
167::CODE;;pos: 200, 200
168::CODE;;canvas:
169::CODE;;Color:
170::CODE;;rgba: 1, 0, 0, 0.5
171::CODE;;Rectangle:
173::CODE;;size: self.size
174::CODE;;You might expect this to render a single pink rectangle; however, the content
175::CODE;;of the :class:`RelativeLayout` is already transformed, so the use of
176::CODE;;`pos: self.pos` will double that transformation. In this case, using
177::CODE;;`pos: 0, 0` or omitting `pos` completely will provide the expected result.
178::CODE;;This also applies to the position of sub-widgets. Instead of positioning a
179::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget` based on the layout's own position:
180::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
181::CODE;;RelativeLayout:
182::CODE;;Widget:
183::CODE;;pos: self.parent.pos
184::CODE;;Widget:
185::CODE;;center: self.parent.center
186::CODE;;use the :attr:`pos_hint` property:
187::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
188::CODE;;RelativeLayout:
189::CODE;;Widget:
190::CODE;;pos_hint: {'x': 0, 'y': 0}
191::CODE;;Widget:
192::CODE;;pos_hint: {'center_x': 0.5, 'center_y': 0.5}
193::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.7.0
194::CODE;;Prior to version 1.7.0, the :class:`RelativeLayout` was implemented as a
195::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.floatlayout.FloatLayout` inside a
196::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.scatter.Scatter`. This behavior/widget has
197::CODE;;been renamed to `ScatterLayout`. The :class:`RelativeLayout` now only
198::CODE;;supports relative positions (and can't be rotated, scaled or translated on
199::CODE;;a multitouch system using two or more fingers). This was done so that the
200::CODE;;implementation could be optimized and avoid the heavier calculations of
201::CODE;;:class:`Scatter` (e.g. inverse matrix, recalculating multiple properties
202::CODE;;etc.)
203::CODE;;'''
204::CODE;;__all__ = ('RelativeLayout', )
205::CODE;;from kivy.uix.floatlayout import FloatLayout
206::CODE;;class RelativeLayout(FloatLayout):
207::CODE;;'''RelativeLayout class, see module documentation for more information.
208::CODE;;'''
209::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kw):
210::CODE;;super(RelativeLayout, self).__init__(**kw)
211::CODE;;funbind = self.funbind
212::CODE;;trigger = self._trigger_layout
213::CODE;;funbind('pos', trigger)
214::CODE;;funbind('pos_hint', trigger)
215::CODE;;def do_layout(self, *args):
216::CODE;;super(RelativeLayout, self).do_layout(pos=(0, 0))
217::CODE;;def to_parent(self, x, y, **k):
218::CODE;;return (x + self.x, y + self.y)
219::CODE;;def to_local(self, x, y, **k):
220::CODE;;return (x - self.x, y - self.y)
221::CODE;;def _apply_transform(self, m, pos=None):
222::CODE;;m.translate(self.x, self.y, 0)
223::CODE;;return super(RelativeLayout, self)._apply_transform(m, (0, 0))
224::CODE;;def on_motion(self, etype, me):
225::CODE;;if me.type_id in self.motion_filter and 'pos' in me.profile:
226::CODE;;me.push()
227::CODE;;me.apply_transform_2d(self.to_local)
228::CODE;;ret = super().on_motion(etype, me)
229::CODE;;me.pop()
230::CODE;;return ret
231::CODE;;return super().on_motion(etype, me)
232::CODE;;def on_touch_down(self, touch):
233::CODE;;x, y = touch.x, touch.y
234::CODE;;touch.push()
235::CODE;;touch.apply_transform_2d(self.to_local)
236::CODE;;ret = super(RelativeLayout, self).on_touch_down(touch)
237::CODE;;touch.pop()
238::CODE;;return ret
239::CODE;;def on_touch_move(self, touch):
240::CODE;;x, y = touch.x, touch.y
241::CODE;;touch.push()
242::CODE;;touch.apply_transform_2d(self.to_local)
243::CODE;;ret = super(RelativeLayout, self).on_touch_move(touch)
244::CODE;;touch.pop()
245::CODE;;return ret
246::CODE;;def on_touch_up(self, touch):
247::CODE;;x, y = touch.x, touch.y
248::CODE;;touch.push()
249::CODE;;touch.apply_transform_2d(self.to_local)
250::CODE;;ret = super(RelativeLayout, self).on_touch_up(touch)
251::CODE;;touch.pop()
252::CODE;;return ret
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;reStructuredText renderer
3::CODE;;=========================
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.1.0
5::CODE;;`reStructuredText <http://docutils.sourceforge.net/rst.html>`_ is an
6::CODE;;easy-to-read, what-you-see-is-what-you-get plaintext markup syntax and parser
7::CODE;;system.
8::CODE;;.. note::
9::CODE;;This widget requires the ``docutils`` package to run. Install it with
10::CODE;;``pip`` or include it as one of your deployment requirements.
11::CODE;;.. warning::
12::CODE;;This widget is highly experimental. The styling and implementation should
13::CODE;;not be considered stable until this warning has been removed.
14::CODE;;Usage with Text
15::CODE;;---------------
16::CODE;;::
25::CODE;;document = RstDocument(text=text)
26::CODE;;The rendering will output:
27::CODE;;.. image:: images/rstdocument.png
28::CODE;;Usage with Source
29::CODE;;-----------------
30::CODE;;You can also render a rst file using the :attr:`~RstDocument.source` property::
31::CODE;;document = RstDocument(source='index.rst')
32::CODE;;You can reference other documents using the role ``:doc:``. For example, in the
33::CODE;;document ``index.rst`` you can write::
34::CODE;;Go to my next document: :doc:`moreinfo.rst`
35::CODE;;It will generate a link that, when clicked, opens the ``moreinfo.rst``
36::CODE;;document.
37::CODE;;'''

463::CODE;;def preload(self, filename, encoding='utf-8', errors='strict'):
464::CODE;;'''Preload a rst file to get its toctree and its title.
465::CODE;;The result will be stored in :attr:`toctrees` with the ``filename`` as
466::CODE;;key.
467::CODE;;'''
468::CODE;;with open(filename, 'rb') as fd:
469::CODE;;text = fd.read().decode(encoding, errors)

475::CODE;;document.walkabout(visitor)
476::CODE;;self.toctrees[filename] = visitor.toctree
477::CODE;;return text

498::CODE;;def on_ref_press(self, node, ref):

500::CODE;;def goto(self, ref, *largs):
501::CODE;;'''Scroll to the reference. If it's not found, nothing will be done.
502::CODE;;For this text::
503::CODE;;.. _myref:
504::CODE;;This is something I always wanted.
505::CODE;;You can do::
506::CODE;;from kivy.clock import Clock
507::CODE;;from functools import partial
508::CODE;;doc = RstDocument(...)
509::CODE;;Clock.schedule_once(partial(doc.goto, 'myref'), 0.1)
510::CODE;;.. note::
511::CODE;;It is preferable to delay the call of the goto if you just loaded
512::CODE;;the document because the layout might not be finished or the
513::CODE;;size of the RstDocument has not yet been determined. In
514::CODE;;either case, the calculation of the scrolling would be
515::CODE;;wrong.
516::CODE;;You can, however, do a direct call if the document is already
517::CODE;;loaded.
518::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.3.0
519::CODE;;'''
521::CODE;;if ref.endswith('.rst'):
523::CODE;;self.source = ref
524::CODE;;return
526::CODE;;ref = self.refs_assoc.get(ref, ref)
528::CODE;;ax = ay = None
529::CODE;;for node in self.anchors_widgets:
530::CODE;;if ref in node.anchors:
531::CODE;;ax, ay = node.anchors[ref]
532::CODE;;break
534::CODE;;if ax is None:
535::CODE;;return
538::CODE;;ax += node.x
539::CODE;;ay = node.top - ay
542::CODE;;sx, sy = self.scatter.x, self.scatter.top
544::CODE;;ay -= self.height
545::CODE;;dx, dy = self.convert_distance_to_scroll(0, ay)
546::CODE;;dy = max(0, min(1, dy))
547::CODE;;Animation(scroll_y=dy, d=.25, t='in_out_expo').start(self)

681::CODE;;def brute_refs(self, node):
685::CODE;;def get_refs(condition, backref=False):
687::CODE;;autonum = autosym = 0
688::CODE;;_nodes = node.traverse(condition=condition, ascend=False)
689::CODE;;for f in _nodes:

693::CODE;;auto = f['auto']

696::CODE;;autonum += 1
697::CODE;;key = 'backref' + str(autonum) if backref else str(autonum)
698::CODE;;self.root.refs_assoc[key] = id
699::CODE;;elif auto == '*':
700::CODE;;sym = self.footlist[
701::CODE;;autosym % 10
702::CODE;;] * (int(autosym / 10) + 1)
703::CODE;;key = 'backref' + sym if backref else sym
704::CODE;;self.root.refs_assoc[key] = id
705::CODE;;autosym += 1
706::CODE;;else:
707::CODE;;if not backref:

710::CODE;;self.root.refs_assoc[key] = id

713::CODE;;if key in self.root.refs_assoc:
714::CODE;;self.root.refs_assoc[key].append(id)
715::CODE;;else:
716::CODE;;self.root.refs_assoc[key] = [id, ]

720::CODE;;get_refs(nodes.footnote_reference, backref=True)
