1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Sandbox
3::CODE;;=======
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.8.0
5::CODE;;.. warning::
6::CODE;;This is experimental and subject to change as long as this warning notice
7::CODE;;is present.
8::CODE;;This is a widget that runs itself and all of its children in a Sandbox. That
9::CODE;;means if a child raises an Exception, it will be caught. The Sandbox
10::CODE;;itself runs its own Clock, Cache, etc.
11::CODE;;The SandBox widget is still experimental and required for the Kivy designer.
12::CODE;;When the user designs their own widget, if they do something wrong (wrong size
13::CODE;;value, invalid python code), it will be caught correctly without breaking
14::CODE;;the whole application. Because it has been designed that way, we are still
15::CODE;;enhancing this widget and the :mod:`kivy.context` module.
16::CODE;;Don't use it unless you know what you are doing.
17::CODE;;'''
18::CODE;;__all__ = ('Sandbox', )
19::CODE;;from functools import wraps
20::CODE;;from kivy.context import Context
21::CODE;;from kivy.base import ExceptionManagerBase
22::CODE;;from kivy.clock import Clock
23::CODE;;from kivy.uix.widget import Widget
24::CODE;;from kivy.uix.floatlayout import FloatLayout
25::CODE;;from kivy.uix.relativelayout import RelativeLayout
26::CODE;;from kivy.lang import Builder
27::CODE;;def sandbox(f):
28::CODE;;@wraps(f)
29::CODE;;def _f2(self, *args, **kwargs):
30::CODE;;ret = None
31::CODE;;with self:
32::CODE;;ret = f(self, *args, **kwargs)
33::CODE;;return ret
34::CODE;;return _f2
35::CODE;;class SandboxExceptionManager(ExceptionManagerBase):
36::CODE;;def __init__(self, sandbox):
37::CODE;;ExceptionManagerBase.__init__(self)
38::CODE;;self.sandbox = sandbox
39::CODE;;def handle_exception(self, e):
40::CODE;;if not self.sandbox.on_exception(e):
41::CODE;;return ExceptionManagerBase.RAISE
42::CODE;;return ExceptionManagerBase.PASS
43::CODE;;class SandboxContent(RelativeLayout):
44::CODE;;pass
45::CODE;;class Sandbox(FloatLayout):
46::CODE;;'''Sandbox widget, used to trap all the exceptions raised by child
47::CODE;;widgets.
48::CODE;;'''
49::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
50::CODE;;self._context = Context(init=True)
51::CODE;;self._context['ExceptionManager'] = SandboxExceptionManager(self)
52::CODE;;self._context.sandbox = self
53::CODE;;self._context.push()
54::CODE;;self.on_context_created()
55::CODE;;self._container = None
56::CODE;;super(Sandbox, self).__init__(**kwargs)
57::CODE;;self._container = SandboxContent(size=self.size, pos=self.pos)
58::CODE;;super(Sandbox, self).add_widget(self._container)
59::CODE;;self._context.pop()
61::CODE;;Clock.schedule_interval(self._clock_sandbox, 0)
62::CODE;;Clock.schedule_once(self._clock_sandbox_draw, -1)
63::CODE;;self.main_clock = object.__getattribute__(Clock, '_obj')
64::CODE;;def __enter__(self):
65::CODE;;self._context.push()
66::CODE;;def __exit__(self, _type, value, traceback):
67::CODE;;self._context.pop()
68::CODE;;if _type is not None:
69::CODE;;return self.on_exception(value, _traceback=traceback)
70::CODE;;def on_context_created(self):
71::CODE;;'''Override this method in order to load your kv file or do anything
72::CODE;;else with the newly created context.
73::CODE;;'''
74::CODE;;pass
75::CODE;;def on_exception(self, exception, _traceback=None):
76::CODE;;'''Override this method in order to catch all the exceptions from
77::CODE;;children.
78::CODE;;If you return True, it will not reraise the exception.
79::CODE;;If you return False, the exception will be raised to the parent.
80::CODE;;'''
81::CODE;;import traceback
82::CODE;;traceback.print_tb(_traceback)
83::CODE;;return True
84::CODE;;on_motion = sandbox(Widget.on_motion)
85::CODE;;on_touch_down = sandbox(Widget.on_touch_down)
86::CODE;;on_touch_move = sandbox(Widget.on_touch_move)
87::CODE;;on_touch_up = sandbox(Widget.on_touch_up)
88::CODE;;@sandbox
89::CODE;;def add_widget(self, *args, **kwargs):
90::CODE;;self._container.add_widget(*args, **kwargs)
91::CODE;;@sandbox
92::CODE;;def remove_widget(self, *args, **kwargs):
93::CODE;;self._container.remove_widget(*args, **kwargs)
94::CODE;;@sandbox
95::CODE;;def clear_widgets(self, *args, **kwargs):
96::CODE;;self._container.clear_widgets(*args, **kwargs)
97::CODE;;@sandbox
98::CODE;;def on_size(self, *args):
99::CODE;;if self._container:
100::CODE;;self._container.size = self.size
101::CODE;;@sandbox
102::CODE;;def on_pos(self, *args):
103::CODE;;if self._container:
104::CODE;;self._container.pos = self.pos
105::CODE;;@sandbox
106::CODE;;def _clock_sandbox(self, dt):
108::CODE;;Clock.tick()
109::CODE;;Builder.sync()
110::CODE;;@sandbox
111::CODE;;def _clock_sandbox_draw(self, dt):
112::CODE;;Clock.tick_draw()
113::CODE;;Builder.sync()
114::CODE;;self.main_clock.schedule_once(self._call_draw, 0)
115::CODE;;def _call_draw(self, dt):
116::CODE;;self.main_clock.schedule_once(self._clock_sandbox_draw, -1)
117::CODE;;if __name__ == '__main__':
118::CODE;;from kivy.base import runTouchApp

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Scatter
3::CODE;;=======
4::CODE;;.. image:: images/scatter.gif
5::CODE;;:align: right
6::CODE;;:class:`Scatter` is used to build interactive widgets that can be translated,
7::CODE;;rotated and scaled with two or more fingers on a multitouch system.
8::CODE;;Scatter has its own matrix transformation: the modelview matrix is changed
9::CODE;;before the children are drawn and the previous matrix is restored when the
10::CODE;;drawing is finished. That makes it possible to perform rotation, scaling and
11::CODE;;translation over the entire children tree without changing any widget
12::CODE;;properties. That specific behavior makes the scatter unique, but there are some
13::CODE;;advantages / constraints that you should consider:
15::CODE;;:mod:`~kivy.uix.relativelayout.RelativeLayout`. So when dragging the
16::CODE;;scatter, the position of the children don't change, only the position of
17::CODE;;the scatter does.
20::CODE;;transforms both the scatter and its children, but does not change size.
22::CODE;;yourself.
23::CODE;;For touch events, the scatter converts from the parent matrix to the scatter
24::CODE;;matrix automatically in on_touch_down/move/up events. If you are doing things
25::CODE;;manually, you will need to use :meth:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.to_parent` and
26::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.to_local`.
27::CODE;;Usage
28::CODE;;-----
29::CODE;;By default, the Scatter does not have a graphical representation: it is a
30::CODE;;container only. The idea is to combine the Scatter with another widget, for
31::CODE;;example an :class:`~kivy.uix.image.Image`::
32::CODE;;scatter = Scatter()
33::CODE;;image = Image(source='sun.jpg')
34::CODE;;scatter.add_widget(image)
35::CODE;;Control Interactions
36::CODE;;--------------------
37::CODE;;By default, all interactions are enabled. You can selectively disable
38::CODE;;them using the do_rotation, do_translation and do_scale properties.
39::CODE;;Disable rotation::
40::CODE;;scatter = Scatter(do_rotation=False)
41::CODE;;Allow only translation::
42::CODE;;scatter = Scatter(do_rotation=False, do_scale=False)
43::CODE;;Allow only translation on x axis::
44::CODE;;scatter = Scatter(do_rotation=False, do_scale=False,
45::CODE;;do_translation_y=False)
46::CODE;;Automatic Bring to Front
47::CODE;;------------------------
48::CODE;;If the :attr:`Scatter.auto_bring_to_front` property is True, the scatter
49::CODE;;widget will be removed and re-added to the parent when it is touched
50::CODE;;(brought to front, above all other widgets in the parent). This is useful
51::CODE;;when you are manipulating several scatter widgets and don't want the active
52::CODE;;one to be partially hidden.
53::CODE;;Scale Limitation
54::CODE;;----------------
55::CODE;;We are using a 32-bit matrix in double representation. That means we have
56::CODE;;a limit for scaling. You cannot do infinite scaling down/up with our
57::CODE;;implementation. Generally, you don't hit the minimum scale (because you don't
58::CODE;;see it on the screen), but the maximum scale is 9.99506983235e+19 (2^66).
59::CODE;;You can also limit the minimum and maximum scale allowed::
60::CODE;;scatter = Scatter(scale_min=.5, scale_max=3.)
61::CODE;;Behavior
62::CODE;;--------
63::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.1.0
64::CODE;;If no control interactions are enabled, then the touch handler will never
65::CODE;;return True.
66::CODE;;'''
67::CODE;;__all__ = ('Scatter', 'ScatterPlane')
68::CODE;;from math import radians
69::CODE;;from kivy.properties import BooleanProperty, AliasProperty, \
70::CODE;;NumericProperty, ObjectProperty, BoundedNumericProperty
71::CODE;;from kivy.vector import Vector
72::CODE;;from kivy.uix.widget import Widget
73::CODE;;from kivy.graphics.transformation import Matrix
74::CODE;;class Scatter(Widget):
75::CODE;;'''Scatter class. See module documentation for more information.
76::CODE;;:Events:
77::CODE;;`on_transform_with_touch`:
78::CODE;;Fired when the scatter has been transformed by user touch
79::CODE;;or multitouch, such as panning or zooming.
80::CODE;;`on_bring_to_front`:
81::CODE;;Fired when the scatter is brought to the front.
82::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.9.0
83::CODE;;Event `on_bring_to_front` added.

88::CODE;;auto_bring_to_front = BooleanProperty(True)
89::CODE;;'''If True, the widget will be automatically pushed on the top of parent
90::CODE;;widget list for drawing.
91::CODE;;:attr:`auto_bring_to_front` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty`
92::CODE;;and defaults to True.
93::CODE;;'''
94::CODE;;do_translation_x = BooleanProperty(True)
95::CODE;;'''Allow translation on the X axis.
96::CODE;;:attr:`do_translation_x` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty` and
97::CODE;;defaults to True.
98::CODE;;'''
99::CODE;;do_translation_y = BooleanProperty(True)
100::CODE;;'''Allow translation on Y axis.
101::CODE;;:attr:`do_translation_y` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty` and
102::CODE;;defaults to True.

104::CODE;;def _get_do_translation(self):
105::CODE;;return (self.do_translation_x, self.do_translation_y)
106::CODE;;def _set_do_translation(self, value):
107::CODE;;if type(value) in (list, tuple):
108::CODE;;self.do_translation_x, self.do_translation_y = value
109::CODE;;else:
110::CODE;;self.do_translation_x = self.do_translation_y = bool(value)
111::CODE;;do_translation = AliasProperty(_get_do_translation, _set_do_translation,
112::CODE;;bind=('do_translation_x',
113::CODE;;'do_translation_y'),
114::CODE;;cache=True)

117::CODE;;(:attr:`do_translation_x` + :attr:`do_translation_y`)
118::CODE;;'''
119::CODE;;translation_touches = BoundedNumericProperty(1, min=1)

121::CODE;;touches. This only has effect when :attr:`do_translation` = True.
122::CODE;;:attr:`translation_touches` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty`
123::CODE;;and defaults to 1.

125::CODE;;'''
126::CODE;;do_rotation = BooleanProperty(True)
127::CODE;;'''Allow rotation.
128::CODE;;:attr:`do_rotation` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty` and
129::CODE;;defaults to True.
130::CODE;;'''
131::CODE;;do_scale = BooleanProperty(True)
132::CODE;;'''Allow scaling.
133::CODE;;:attr:`do_scale` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty` and
134::CODE;;defaults to True.
135::CODE;;'''
136::CODE;;do_collide_after_children = BooleanProperty(False)
137::CODE;;'''If True, the collision detection for limiting the touch inside the
138::CODE;;scatter will be done after dispaching the touch to the children.
139::CODE;;You can put children outside the bounding box of the scatter and still be
140::CODE;;able to touch them.
141::CODE;;:attr:`do_collide_after_children` is a
142::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty` and defaults to False.
143::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.3.0
144::CODE;;'''
145::CODE;;scale_min = NumericProperty(0.01)
146::CODE;;'''Minimum scaling factor allowed.
147::CODE;;:attr:`scale_min` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
148::CODE;;defaults to 0.01.
149::CODE;;'''
150::CODE;;scale_max = NumericProperty(1e20)
151::CODE;;'''Maximum scaling factor allowed.
152::CODE;;:attr:`scale_max` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
153::CODE;;defaults to 1e20.
154::CODE;;'''
155::CODE;;transform = ObjectProperty(Matrix())
156::CODE;;'''Transformation matrix.
157::CODE;;:attr:`transform` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.ObjectProperty` and
158::CODE;;defaults to the identity matrix.
159::CODE;;.. note::
160::CODE;;This matrix reflects the current state of the transformation matrix
161::CODE;;but setting it directly will erase previously applied
162::CODE;;transformations. To apply a transformation considering context,
163::CODE;;please use the :attr:`~Scatter.apply_transform` method.
164::CODE;;'''
165::CODE;;transform_inv = ObjectProperty(Matrix())
166::CODE;;'''Inverse of the transformation matrix.
167::CODE;;:attr:`transform_inv` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.ObjectProperty` and
168::CODE;;defaults to the identity matrix.
169::CODE;;'''
170::CODE;;def _get_bbox(self):
171::CODE;;xmin, ymin = xmax, ymax = self.to_parent(0, 0)
172::CODE;;for point in [(self.width, 0), (0, self.height), self.size]:
173::CODE;;x, y = self.to_parent(*point)
174::CODE;;if x < xmin:
175::CODE;;xmin = x
176::CODE;;if y < ymin:
177::CODE;;ymin = y
178::CODE;;if x > xmax:
179::CODE;;xmax = x
180::CODE;;if y > ymax:
181::CODE;;ymax = y
182::CODE;;return (xmin, ymin), (xmax - xmin, ymax - ymin)
183::CODE;;bbox = AliasProperty(_get_bbox, bind=('transform', 'width', 'height'))
184::CODE;;'''Bounding box of the widget in parent space::
185::CODE;;((x, y), (w, h))
187::CODE;;:attr:`bbox` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.AliasProperty`.
188::CODE;;'''
189::CODE;;def _get_rotation(self):
190::CODE;;v1 = Vector(0, 10)
191::CODE;;tp = self.to_parent
192::CODE;;v2 = Vector(*tp(*self.pos)) - tp(self.x, self.y + 10)
193::CODE;;return -1.0 * (v1.angle(v2) + 180) % 360
194::CODE;;def _set_rotation(self, rotation):
195::CODE;;angle_change = self.rotation - rotation
196::CODE;;r = Matrix().rotate(-radians(angle_change), 0, 0, 1)
197::CODE;;self.apply_transform(r, post_multiply=True,
198::CODE;;anchor=self.to_local(*self.center))
199::CODE;;rotation = AliasProperty(_get_rotation, _set_rotation,
200::CODE;;bind=('x', 'y', 'transform'))
201::CODE;;'''Rotation value of the scatter in degrees moving in a counterclockwise
202::CODE;;direction.
203::CODE;;:attr:`rotation` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.AliasProperty` and defaults
204::CODE;;to 0.0.
205::CODE;;'''
206::CODE;;def _get_scale(self):
207::CODE;;p1 = Vector(*self.to_parent(0, 0))
208::CODE;;p2 = Vector(*self.to_parent(1, 0))
209::CODE;;scale = p1.distance(p2)
215::CODE;;if hasattr(self, '_scale_p'):
216::CODE;;if str(scale) == str(self._scale_p):
217::CODE;;return self._scale_p
218::CODE;;self._scale_p = scale
219::CODE;;return scale
220::CODE;;def _set_scale(self, scale):
221::CODE;;rescale = scale * 1.0 / self.scale
222::CODE;;self.apply_transform(Matrix().scale(rescale, rescale, rescale),
223::CODE;;post_multiply=True,
224::CODE;;anchor=self.to_local(*self.center))
225::CODE;;scale = AliasProperty(_get_scale, _set_scale, bind=('x', 'y', 'transform'))
226::CODE;;'''Scale value of the scatter.
227::CODE;;:attr:`scale` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.AliasProperty` and defaults to
228::CODE;;1.0.
229::CODE;;'''
230::CODE;;def _get_center(self):
231::CODE;;return (self.bbox[0][0] + self.bbox[1][0] / 2.0,
232::CODE;;self.bbox[0][1] + self.bbox[1][1] / 2.0)
233::CODE;;def _set_center(self, center):
234::CODE;;if center == self.center:
235::CODE;;return False
236::CODE;;t = Vector(*center) - self.center
237::CODE;;trans = Matrix().translate(t.x, t.y, 0)
238::CODE;;self.apply_transform(trans)
239::CODE;;center = AliasProperty(_get_center, _set_center, bind=('bbox',))
240::CODE;;def _get_pos(self):
241::CODE;;return self.bbox[0]
242::CODE;;def _set_pos(self, pos):
243::CODE;;_pos = self.bbox[0]
244::CODE;;if pos == _pos:
245::CODE;;return
246::CODE;;t = Vector(*pos) - _pos
247::CODE;;trans = Matrix().translate(t.x, t.y, 0)
248::CODE;;self.apply_transform(trans)
249::CODE;;pos = AliasProperty(_get_pos, _set_pos, bind=('bbox',))
250::CODE;;def _get_x(self):
251::CODE;;return self.bbox[0][0]
252::CODE;;def _set_x(self, x):
253::CODE;;if x == self.bbox[0][0]:
254::CODE;;return False
255::CODE;;self.pos = (x, self.y)
256::CODE;;return True
257::CODE;;x = AliasProperty(_get_x, _set_x, bind=('bbox',))
258::CODE;;def _get_y(self):
259::CODE;;return self.bbox[0][1]
260::CODE;;def _set_y(self, y):
261::CODE;;if y == self.bbox[0][1]:
262::CODE;;return False
263::CODE;;self.pos = (self.x, y)
264::CODE;;return True

304::CODE;;def apply_transform(self, trans, post_multiply=False, anchor=(0, 0)):
305::CODE;;'''
306::CODE;;Transforms the scatter by applying the "trans" transformation
307::CODE;;matrix (on top of its current transformation state). The resultant
308::CODE;;matrix can be found in the :attr:`~Scatter.transform` property.
309::CODE;;:Parameters:
310::CODE;;`trans`: :class:`~kivy.graphics.transformation.Matrix`.
311::CODE;;Transformation matrix to be applied to the scatter widget.
312::CODE;;`anchor`: tuple, defaults to (0, 0).
313::CODE;;The point to use as the origin of the transformation
314::CODE;;(uses local widget space).
315::CODE;;`post_multiply`: bool, defaults to False.
316::CODE;;If True, the transform matrix is post multiplied
317::CODE;;(as if applied before the current transform).
318::CODE;;Usage example::
319::CODE;;from kivy.graphics.transformation import Matrix
320::CODE;;mat = Matrix().scale(3, 3, 3)
321::CODE;;scatter_instance.apply_transform(mat)
322::CODE;;'''
323::CODE;;t = Matrix().translate(anchor[0], anchor[1], 0)
324::CODE;;t = t.multiply(trans)
325::CODE;;t = t.multiply(Matrix().translate(-anchor[0], -anchor[1], 0))
326::CODE;;if post_multiply:
327::CODE;;self.transform = self.transform.multiply(t)
328::CODE;;else:
329::CODE;;self.transform = t.multiply(self.transform)
330::CODE;;def transform_with_touch(self, touch):
332::CODE;;changed = False
333::CODE;;if len(self._touches) == self.translation_touches:
336::CODE;;dx = (touch.x - self._last_touch_pos[touch][0]) \
337::CODE;;* self.do_translation_x
338::CODE;;dy = (touch.y - self._last_touch_pos[touch][1]) \
339::CODE;;* self.do_translation_y
340::CODE;;dx = dx / self.translation_touches
341::CODE;;dy = dy / self.translation_touches
342::CODE;;self.apply_transform(Matrix().translate(dx, dy, 0))
343::CODE;;changed = True
344::CODE;;if len(self._touches) == 1:
345::CODE;;return changed
347::CODE;;points = [Vector(self._last_touch_pos[t]) for t in self._touches
348::CODE;;if t is not touch]
350::CODE;;points.append(Vector(touch.pos))
354::CODE;;anchor = max(points[:-1], key=lambda p: p.distance(touch.pos))
357::CODE;;farthest = max(points, key=anchor.distance)
358::CODE;;if farthest is not points[-1]:
359::CODE;;return changed
362::CODE;;old_line = Vector(*touch.ppos) - anchor
363::CODE;;new_line = Vector(*touch.pos) - anchor
365::CODE;;return changed
366::CODE;;angle = radians(new_line.angle(old_line)) * self.do_rotation
367::CODE;;if angle:
368::CODE;;changed = True
369::CODE;;self.apply_transform(Matrix().rotate(angle, 0, 0, 1), anchor=anchor)
370::CODE;;if self.do_scale:
371::CODE;;scale = new_line.length() / old_line.length()
372::CODE;;new_scale = scale * self.scale
373::CODE;;if new_scale < self.scale_min:
374::CODE;;scale = self.scale_min / self.scale
375::CODE;;elif new_scale > self.scale_max:
376::CODE;;scale = self.scale_max / self.scale
377::CODE;;self.apply_transform(Matrix().scale(scale, scale, scale),
378::CODE;;anchor=anchor)
379::CODE;;changed = True
380::CODE;;return changed
381::CODE;;def _bring_to_front(self, touch):
383::CODE;;if self.auto_bring_to_front and self.parent:
384::CODE;;parent = self.parent
385::CODE;;if parent.children[0] is self:
386::CODE;;return

388::CODE;;parent.add_widget(self)
389::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_bring_to_front', touch)
390::CODE;;def on_motion(self, etype, me):
391::CODE;;if me.type_id in self.motion_filter and 'pos' in me.profile:
392::CODE;;me.push()
393::CODE;;me.apply_transform_2d(self.to_local)
394::CODE;;ret = super().on_motion(etype, me)
395::CODE;;me.pop()
396::CODE;;return ret
397::CODE;;return super().on_motion(etype, me)
398::CODE;;def on_touch_down(self, touch):
399::CODE;;x, y = touch.x, touch.y
401::CODE;;if not self.do_collide_after_children:
402::CODE;;if not self.collide_point(x, y):
403::CODE;;return False

408::CODE;;touch.pop()

410::CODE;;return True
411::CODE;;touch.pop()
414::CODE;;if not self.do_translation_x and \
415::CODE;;not self.do_translation_y and \
416::CODE;;not self.do_rotation and \
417::CODE;;not self.do_scale:
418::CODE;;return False
419::CODE;;if self.do_collide_after_children:
420::CODE;;if not self.collide_point(x, y):
421::CODE;;return False

423::CODE;;touch.multitouch_sim = True

427::CODE;;self._touches.append(touch)

429::CODE;;return True
430::CODE;;def on_touch_move(self, touch):
431::CODE;;x, y = touch.x, touch.y
433::CODE;;if self.collide_point(x, y) and not touch.grab_current == self:
434::CODE;;touch.push()
435::CODE;;touch.apply_transform_2d(self.to_local)
436::CODE;;if super(Scatter, self).on_touch_move(touch):
437::CODE;;touch.pop()
438::CODE;;return True
439::CODE;;touch.pop()
441::CODE;;if touch in self._touches and touch.grab_current == self:
442::CODE;;if self.transform_with_touch(touch):
443::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_transform_with_touch', touch)
444::CODE;;self._last_touch_pos[touch] = touch.pos
446::CODE;;if self.collide_point(x, y):
447::CODE;;return True

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Scatter Layout
3::CODE;;===============
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.6.0
5::CODE;;This layout behaves just like a
6::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.relativelayout.RelativeLayout`.
7::CODE;;When a widget is added with position = (0,0) to a :class:`ScatterLayout`,
8::CODE;;the child widget will also move when you change the position of the
9::CODE;;:class:`ScatterLayout`. The child widget's coordinates remain
10::CODE;;(0,0) as they are relative to the parent layout.
11::CODE;;However, since :class:`ScatterLayout` is implemented using a
12::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.scatter.Scatter`
13::CODE;;widget, you can also translate, rotate and scale the layout using touches
14::CODE;;or clicks, just like in the case of a normal Scatter widget, and the child
15::CODE;;widgets will behave as expected.
16::CODE;;In contrast to a Scatter, the Layout favors 'hint' properties, such as
17::CODE;;size_hint, size_hint_x, size_hint_y and pos_hint.
18::CODE;;.. note::
19::CODE;;The :class:`ScatterLayout` is implemented as a
20::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.floatlayout.FloatLayout`
21::CODE;;inside a :class:`~kivy.uix.scatter.Scatter`.
22::CODE;;.. warning::
23::CODE;;Since the actual :class:`ScatterLayout` is a
24::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.scatter.Scatter`, its
25::CODE;;add_widget and remove_widget functions are overridden to add children
26::CODE;;to the embedded :class:`~kivy.uix.floatlayout.FloatLayout` (accessible as
27::CODE;;the `content` property of :class:`~kivy.uix.scatter.Scatter`)
28::CODE;;automatically. So if you want to access the added child elements,
29::CODE;;you need self.content.children instead of self.children.
30::CODE;;.. warning::
31::CODE;;The :class:`ScatterLayout` was introduced in 1.7.0 and was called
32::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.relativelayout.RelativeLayout` in prior versions.
33::CODE;;The :class:`~kivy.uix.relativelayout.RelativeLayout` is now an optimized
34::CODE;;implementation that uses only a positional transform to avoid some of the
35::CODE;;heavier calculation involved for :class:`~kivy.uix.scatter.Scatter`.
36::CODE;;'''
37::CODE;;__all__ = ('ScatterLayout', 'ScatterPlaneLayout')
38::CODE;;from kivy.uix.floatlayout import FloatLayout
39::CODE;;from kivy.uix.scatter import Scatter, ScatterPlane
40::CODE;;from kivy.properties import ObjectProperty
41::CODE;;class ScatterLayout(Scatter):
42::CODE;;'''ScatterLayout class, see module documentation for more information.
43::CODE;;'''
44::CODE;;content = ObjectProperty()
45::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kw):
46::CODE;;self.content = FloatLayout()
47::CODE;;super(ScatterLayout, self).__init__(**kw)
48::CODE;;if self.content.size != self.size:
49::CODE;;self.content.size = self.size
50::CODE;;super(ScatterLayout, self).add_widget(self.content)
51::CODE;;self.fbind('size', self.update_size)
52::CODE;;def update_size(self, instance, size):
53::CODE;;self.content.size = size
54::CODE;;def add_widget(self, *args, **kwargs):
55::CODE;;self.content.add_widget(*args, **kwargs)
56::CODE;;def remove_widget(self, *args, **kwargs):
57::CODE;;self.content.remove_widget(*args, **kwargs)
58::CODE;;def clear_widgets(self, *args, **kwargs):
59::CODE;;self.content.clear_widgets(*args, **kwargs)

1::CODE;;'''Screen Manager
2::CODE;;==============
3::CODE;;.. image:: images/screenmanager.gif
4::CODE;;:align: right
5::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.4.0
6::CODE;;The screen manager is a widget dedicated to managing multiple screens for your
7::CODE;;application. The default :class:`ScreenManager` displays only one
8::CODE;;:class:`Screen` at a time and uses a :class:`TransitionBase` to switch from one
9::CODE;;Screen to another.
10::CODE;;Multiple transitions are supported based on changing the screen coordinates /
11::CODE;;scale or even performing fancy animation using custom shaders.
12::CODE;;Basic Usage
13::CODE;;-----------
14::CODE;;Let's construct a Screen Manager with 4 named screens. When you are creating
15::CODE;;a screen, **you absolutely need to give a name to it**::
16::CODE;;from kivy.uix.screenmanager import ScreenManager, Screen
18::CODE;;sm = ScreenManager()
20::CODE;;for i in range(4):
21::CODE;;screen = Screen(name='Title %d' % i)
22::CODE;;sm.add_widget(screen)
27::CODE;;sm.current = 'Title 2'
28::CODE;;The default :attr:`ScreenManager.transition` is a :class:`SlideTransition` with
29::CODE;;options :attr:`~SlideTransition.direction` and
30::CODE;;:attr:`~TransitionBase.duration`.
31::CODE;;Please note that by default, a :class:`Screen` displays nothing: it's just a
32::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.relativelayout.RelativeLayout`. You need to use that class as
33::CODE;;a root widget for your own screen, the best way being to subclass.
34::CODE;;.. warning::
35::CODE;;As :class:`Screen` is a :class:`~kivy.uix.relativelayout.RelativeLayout`,
36::CODE;;it is important to understand the
37::CODE;;:ref:`kivy-uix-relativelayout-common-pitfalls`.
38::CODE;;Here is an example with a 'Menu Screen' and a 'Settings Screen'::
39::CODE;;from kivy.app import App
40::CODE;;from kivy.lang import Builder
41::CODE;;from kivy.uix.screenmanager import ScreenManager, Screen
62::CODE;;class MenuScreen(Screen):
63::CODE;;pass
64::CODE;;class SettingsScreen(Screen):
65::CODE;;pass
66::CODE;;class TestApp(App):
67::CODE;;def build(self):
69::CODE;;sm = ScreenManager()
70::CODE;;sm.add_widget(MenuScreen(name='menu'))
71::CODE;;sm.add_widget(SettingsScreen(name='settings'))
72::CODE;;return sm
73::CODE;;if __name__ == '__main__':
74::CODE;;TestApp().run()
75::CODE;;Changing Direction
76::CODE;;------------------
77::CODE;;A common use case for :class:`ScreenManager` involves using a
78::CODE;;:class:`SlideTransition` which slides right to the next screen
79::CODE;;and slides left to the previous screen. Building on the previous
80::CODE;;example, this can be accomplished like so::
101::CODE;;Advanced Usage
102::CODE;;--------------
103::CODE;;From 1.8.0, you can now switch dynamically to a new screen, change the
104::CODE;;transition options and remove the previous one by using
105::CODE;;:meth:`~ScreenManager.switch_to`::
106::CODE;;sm = ScreenManager()
107::CODE;;screens = [Screen(name='Title {}'.format(i)) for i in range(4)]
108::CODE;;sm.switch_to(screens[0])
110::CODE;;sm.switch_to(screens[1], direction='right')
111::CODE;;Note that this method adds the screen to the :class:`ScreenManager` instance
112::CODE;;and should not be used if your screens have already been added to this
113::CODE;;instance. To switch to a screen which is already added, you should use the
114::CODE;;:attr:`~ScreenManager.current` property.
115::CODE;;Changing transitions
116::CODE;;--------------------
117::CODE;;You have multiple transitions available by default, such as:
118::CODE;;- :class:`NoTransition` - switches screens instantly with no animation
119::CODE;;- :class:`SlideTransition` - slide the screen in/out, from any direction
120::CODE;;- :class:`CardTransition` - new screen slides on the previous
121::CODE;;or the old one slides off the new one depending on the mode
122::CODE;;- :class:`SwapTransition` - implementation of the iOS swap transition
123::CODE;;- :class:`FadeTransition` - shader to fade the screen in/out
124::CODE;;- :class:`WipeTransition` - shader to wipe the screens from right to left
125::CODE;;- :class:`FallOutTransition` - shader where the old screen 'falls' and
126::CODE;;becomes transparent, revealing the new one behind it.
127::CODE;;- :class:`RiseInTransition` - shader where the new screen rises from the
128::CODE;;screen centre while fading from transparent to opaque.
129::CODE;;You can easily switch transitions by changing the
130::CODE;;:attr:`ScreenManager.transition` property::
131::CODE;;sm = ScreenManager(transition=FadeTransition())
132::CODE;;.. note::
133::CODE;;Currently, none of Shader based Transitions use
134::CODE;;anti-aliasing. This is because they use the FBO which doesn't have
135::CODE;;any logic to handle supersampling. This is a known issue and we
136::CODE;;are working on a transparent implementation that will give the
137::CODE;;same results as if it had been rendered on screen.
138::CODE;;To be more concrete, if you see sharp edged text during the animation, it's
139::CODE;;normal.
140::CODE;;'''
141::CODE;;__all__ = ('Screen', 'ScreenManager', 'ScreenManagerException',

269::CODE;;def start(self, manager):

359::CODE;;'''

389::CODE;;self.render_ctx.remove(instr)

391::CODE;;self.fbo_out = self.make_screen_fbo(self.screen_out)

609::CODE;;class FallOutTransition(ShaderTransition):
610::CODE;;'''Transition where the new screen 'falls' from the screen centre,
611::CODE;;becoming smaller and more transparent until it disappears, and
612::CODE;;revealing the new screen behind it. Mimics the popular/standard
613::CODE;;Android transition.
614::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.8.0
615::CODE;;'''
616::CODE;;duration = NumericProperty(0.15)
617::CODE;;'''Duration in seconds of the transition, replacing the default of
618::CODE;;:class:`TransitionBase`.
619::CODE;;:class:`duration` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
620::CODE;;defaults to .15 (= 150ms).
621::CODE;;'''
622::CODE;;FALLOUT_TRANSITION_FS = '''$HEADER$
623::CODE;;uniform float t;
624::CODE;;uniform sampler2D tex_in;
625::CODE;;uniform sampler2D tex_out;
626::CODE;;void main(void) {
627::CODE;;/* quantities for position and opacity calculation */
628::CODE;;float tr = 0.5*sin(t); /* 'real' time */
629::CODE;;vec2 diff = (tex_coord0.st - 0.5) * (1.0/(1.0-tr));
630::CODE;;vec2 dist = diff + 0.5;
631::CODE;;float max_dist = 1.0 - tr;
632::CODE;;/* in and out colors */
633::CODE;;vec4 cin = vec4(texture2D(tex_in, tex_coord0.st));
634::CODE;;vec4 cout = vec4(texture2D(tex_out, dist));
635::CODE;;/* opacities for in and out textures */
636::CODE;;float oin = clamp(1.0-cos(t), 0.0, 1.0);
637::CODE;;float oout = clamp(cos(t), 0.0, 1.0);
638::CODE;;bvec2 outside_bounds = bvec2(abs(tex_coord0.s - 0.5) > 0.5*max_dist,
639::CODE;;abs(tex_coord0.t - 0.5) > 0.5*max_dist);
640::CODE;;vec4 frag_col;
641::CODE;;if (any(outside_bounds) ){
642::CODE;;frag_col = vec4(cin.x, cin.y, cin.z, 1.0);
643::CODE;;}
644::CODE;;else {
645::CODE;;frag_col = vec4(oout*cout.x + oin*cin.x, oout*cout.y + oin*cin.y,
646::CODE;;oout*cout.z + oin*cin.z, 1.0);
647::CODE;;}
648::CODE;;gl_FragColor = frag_col;
649::CODE;;}
650::CODE;;'''
651::CODE;;fs = StringProperty(FALLOUT_TRANSITION_FS)
652::CODE;;class RiseInTransition(ShaderTransition):
653::CODE;;'''Transition where the new screen rises from the screen centre,
654::CODE;;becoming larger and changing from transparent to opaque until it
655::CODE;;fills the screen. Mimics the popular/standard Android transition.
656::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.8.0
657::CODE;;'''
658::CODE;;duration = NumericProperty(0.2)
659::CODE;;'''Duration in seconds of the transition, replacing the default of
660::CODE;;:class:`TransitionBase`.
661::CODE;;:class:`duration` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
662::CODE;;defaults to .2 (= 200ms).
663::CODE;;'''
664::CODE;;RISEIN_TRANSITION_FS = '''$HEADER$
665::CODE;;uniform float t;
666::CODE;;uniform sampler2D tex_in;
667::CODE;;uniform sampler2D tex_out;
668::CODE;;void main(void) {
669::CODE;;/* quantities for position and opacity calculation */
670::CODE;;float tr = 0.5 - 0.5*sqrt(sin(t)); /* 'real' time */
671::CODE;;vec2 diff = (tex_coord0.st - 0.5) * (1.0/(1.0-tr));
672::CODE;;vec2 dist = diff + 0.5;
673::CODE;;float max_dist = 1.0 - tr;
674::CODE;;/* in and out colors */
675::CODE;;vec4 cin = vec4(texture2D(tex_in, dist));
676::CODE;;vec4 cout = vec4(texture2D(tex_out, tex_coord0.st));
677::CODE;;/* opacities for in and out textures */
678::CODE;;float oin = clamp(sin(2.0*t), 0.0, 1.0);
679::CODE;;float oout = clamp(1.0 - sin(2.0*t), 0.0, 1.0);
680::CODE;;bvec2 outside_bounds = bvec2(abs(tex_coord0.s - 0.5) > 0.5*max_dist,
681::CODE;;abs(tex_coord0.t - 0.5) > 0.5*max_dist);
682::CODE;;vec4 frag_col;
683::CODE;;if (any(outside_bounds) ){
684::CODE;;frag_col = vec4(cout.x, cout.y, cout.z, 1.0);
685::CODE;;}
686::CODE;;else {
687::CODE;;frag_col = vec4(oout*cout.x + oin*cin.x, oout*cout.y + oin*cin.y,
688::CODE;;oout*cout.z + oin*cin.z, 1.0);
689::CODE;;}
690::CODE;;gl_FragColor = frag_col;
691::CODE;;}
692::CODE;;'''
693::CODE;;fs = StringProperty(RISEIN_TRANSITION_FS)

2::CODE;;Settings
3::CODE;;========
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.7
5::CODE;;This module provides a complete and extensible framework for adding a
6::CODE;;Settings interface to your application. By default, the interface uses
7::CODE;;a :class:`SettingsWithSpinner`, which consists of a
8::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.spinner.Spinner` (top) to switch between individual
9::CODE;;settings panels (bottom). See :ref:`differentlayouts` for some
10::CODE;;alternatives.
11::CODE;;.. image:: images/settingswithspinner_kivy.jpg
12::CODE;;:align: center
13::CODE;;A :class:`SettingsPanel` represents a group of configurable options. The
14::CODE;;:attr:`SettingsPanel.title` property is used by :class:`Settings` when a panel
15::CODE;;is added: it determines the name of the sidebar button. SettingsPanel controls
16::CODE;;a :class:`~kivy.config.ConfigParser` instance.
17::CODE;;The panel can be automatically constructed from a JSON definition file: you
18::CODE;;describe the settings you want and corresponding sections/keys in the
19::CODE;;ConfigParser instance... and you're done!
20::CODE;;Settings are also integrated into the :class:`~kivy.app.App` class. Use
21::CODE;;:meth:`Settings.add_kivy_panel` to configure the Kivy core settings in a panel.
22::CODE;;.. _settings_json:
23::CODE;;Create a panel from JSON
24::CODE;;------------------------
25::CODE;;To create a panel from a JSON-file, you need two things:
26::CODE;;* a :class:`~kivy.config.ConfigParser` instance with default values
27::CODE;;* a JSON file
28::CODE;;.. warning::
29::CODE;;The :class:`kivy.config.ConfigParser` is required. You cannot use the
30::CODE;;default ConfigParser from Python libraries.
31::CODE;;You must create and handle the :class:`~kivy.config.ConfigParser`
32::CODE;;object. SettingsPanel will read the values from the associated
33::CODE;;ConfigParser instance. Make sure you have set default values (using
34::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.config.ConfigParser.setdefaults`) for all the sections/keys
35::CODE;;in your JSON file!
36::CODE;;The JSON file contains structured information to describe the available
37::CODE;;settings. Here is an example::
38::CODE;;[
39::CODE;;{
40::CODE;;"type": "title",
41::CODE;;"title": "Windows"
42::CODE;;},
43::CODE;;{
44::CODE;;"type": "bool",
45::CODE;;"title": "Fullscreen",
46::CODE;;"desc": "Set the window in windowed or fullscreen",
47::CODE;;"section": "graphics",
48::CODE;;"key": "fullscreen"
49::CODE;;}
50::CODE;;]
51::CODE;;Each element in the root list represents a setting that the user can
52::CODE;;configure. Only the "type" key is mandatory: an instance of the associated
53::CODE;;class will be created and used for the setting - other keys are assigned to
54::CODE;;corresponding properties of that class.
55::CODE;;============== =================================================
56::CODE;;Type Associated class
57::CODE;;-------------- -------------------------------------------------
58::CODE;;title :class:`SettingTitle`
59::CODE;;bool :class:`SettingBoolean`
60::CODE;;numeric :class:`SettingNumeric`
61::CODE;;options :class:`SettingOptions`
62::CODE;;string :class:`SettingString`
63::CODE;;path :class:`SettingPath`
64::CODE;;color :class:`SettingColor`
65::CODE;;============== =================================================
66::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.1.0
67::CODE;;Added :attr:`SettingPath` type
68::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 2.1.0
69::CODE;;Added :attr:`SettingColor` type
70::CODE;;In the JSON example above, the first element is of type "title". It will create
71::CODE;;a new instance of :class:`SettingTitle` and apply the rest of the key-value
72::CODE;;pairs to the properties of that class, i.e. "title": "Windows" sets the
73::CODE;;:attr:`~SettingsPanel.title` property of the panel to "Windows".
74::CODE;;To load the JSON example to a :class:`Settings` instance, use the
75::CODE;;:meth:`Settings.add_json_panel` method. It will automatically instantiate a
76::CODE;;:class:`SettingsPanel` and add it to :class:`Settings`::
77::CODE;;from kivy.config import ConfigParser
78::CODE;;config = ConfigParser()
79::CODE;;config.read('myconfig.ini')
80::CODE;;s = Settings()
81::CODE;;s.add_json_panel('My custom panel', config, 'settings_custom.json')
82::CODE;;s.add_json_panel('Another panel', config, 'settings_test2.json')
84::CODE;;.. _differentlayouts:
85::CODE;;Different panel layouts
86::CODE;;-----------------------
87::CODE;;A kivy :class:`~kivy.app.App` can automatically create and display a
88::CODE;;:class:`Settings` instance. See the :attr:`~kivy.app.App.settings_cls`
89::CODE;;documentation for details on how to choose which settings class to
90::CODE;;display.
91::CODE;;Several pre-built settings widgets are available. All except
92::CODE;;:class:`SettingsWithNoMenu` include close buttons triggering the
93::CODE;;on_close event.
94::CODE;;- :class:`Settings`: Displays settings with a sidebar at the left to
95::CODE;;switch between json panels.
96::CODE;;- :class:`SettingsWithSidebar`: A trivial subclass of
97::CODE;;:class:`Settings`.
98::CODE;;- :class:`SettingsWithSpinner`: Displays settings with a spinner at
99::CODE;;the top, which can be used to switch between json panels. Uses
100::CODE;;:class:`InterfaceWithSpinner` as the
101::CODE;;:attr:`~Settings.interface_cls`. This is the default behavior from
102::CODE;;Kivy 1.8.0.
103::CODE;;- :class:`SettingsWithTabbedPanel`: Displays json panels as individual
104::CODE;;tabs in a :class:`~kivy.uix.tabbedpanel.TabbedPanel`. Uses
105::CODE;;:class:`InterfaceWithTabbedPanel` as the :attr:`~Settings.interface_cls`.
106::CODE;;- :class:`SettingsWithNoMenu`: Displays a single json panel, with no
107::CODE;;way to switch to other panels and no close button. This makes it
108::CODE;;impossible for the user to exit unless
109::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.app.App.close_settings` is overridden with a different
110::CODE;;close trigger! Uses :class:`InterfaceWithNoMenu` as the
111::CODE;;:attr:`~Settings.interface_cls`.
112::CODE;;You can construct your own settings panels with any layout you choose
113::CODE;;by setting :attr:`Settings.interface_cls`. This should be a widget
114::CODE;;that displays a json settings panel with some way to switch between
115::CODE;;panels. An instance will be automatically created by :class:`Settings`.
116::CODE;;Interface widgets may be anything you like, but *must* have a method
117::CODE;;add_panel that receives newly created json settings panels for the
118::CODE;;interface to display. See the documentation for
119::CODE;;:class:`InterfaceWithSidebar` for more information. They may
120::CODE;;optionally dispatch an on_close event, for instance if a close button
121::CODE;;is clicked. This event is used by :class:`Settings` to trigger its own
122::CODE;;on_close event.
123::CODE;;For a complete, working example, please see
124::CODE;;:file:`kivy/examples/settings/main.py`.
125::CODE;;'''

547::CODE;;if value is None:
548::CODE;;return

550::CODE;;raise Exception('Invalid config object, you must use a'
551::CODE;;'kivy.config.ConfigParser, not another one !')
552::CODE;;def get_value(self, section, key):
553::CODE;;'''Return the value of the section/key from the :attr:`config`
554::CODE;;ConfigParser instance. This function is used by :class:`SettingItem` to
555::CODE;;get the value for a given section/key.
556::CODE;;If you don't want to use a ConfigParser instance, you might want to
557::CODE;;override this function.

559::CODE;;config = self.config
560::CODE;;if not config:
561::CODE;;return

563::CODE;;def set_value(self, section, key, value):

33::CODE;;class Slider(Widget):
37::CODE;;value = NumericProperty(0.)
38::CODE;;'''Current value used for the slider.
39::CODE;;:attr:`value` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and defaults
40::CODE;;to 0.'''
41::CODE;;min = NumericProperty(0.)
42::CODE;;'''Minimum value allowed for :attr:`value`.
43::CODE;;:attr:`min` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and defaults to
44::CODE;;0.'''
45::CODE;;max = NumericProperty(100.)
46::CODE;;'''Maximum value allowed for :attr:`value`.
47::CODE;;:attr:`max` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and defaults to
48::CODE;;100.'''
49::CODE;;padding = NumericProperty('16sp')
50::CODE;;'''Padding of the slider. The padding is used for graphical representation
51::CODE;;and interaction. It prevents the cursor from going out of the bounds of the
52::CODE;;slider bounding box.
53::CODE;;By default, padding is 16sp. The range of the slider is reduced from
54::CODE;;padding \\*2 on the screen. It allows drawing the default cursor of 32sp
55::CODE;;width without having the cursor go out of the widget.
56::CODE;;:attr:`padding` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and defaults
57::CODE;;to 16sp.'''
58::CODE;;orientation = OptionProperty('horizontal', options=(
59::CODE;;'vertical', 'horizontal'))
60::CODE;;'''Orientation of the slider.
61::CODE;;:attr:`orientation` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.OptionProperty` and
62::CODE;;defaults to 'horizontal'. Can take a value of 'vertical' or 'horizontal'.
63::CODE;;'''
64::CODE;;range = ReferenceListProperty(min, max)
65::CODE;;'''Range of the slider in the format (minimum value, maximum value)::
66::CODE;;>>> slider = Slider(min=10, max=80)
67::CODE;;>>> slider.range
68::CODE;;[10, 80]
69::CODE;;>>> slider.range = (20, 100)
70::CODE;;>>> slider.min
71::CODE;;20
72::CODE;;>>> slider.max
73::CODE;;100
74::CODE;;:attr:`range` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.ReferenceListProperty` of
75::CODE;;(:attr:`min`, :attr:`max`) properties.
76::CODE;;'''
77::CODE;;step = BoundedNumericProperty(0, min=0)
78::CODE;;'''Step size of the slider.
79::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.4.0
80::CODE;;Determines the size of each interval or step the slider takes between
81::CODE;;:attr:`min` and :attr:`max`. If the value range can't be evenly
82::CODE;;divisible by step the last step will be capped by slider.max.
83::CODE;;A zero value will result in the smallest possible intervals/steps,
84::CODE;;calculated from the (pixel) position of the slider.
85::CODE;;:attr:`step` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and defaults
86::CODE;;to 0.'''
87::CODE;;background_horizontal = StringProperty(
88::CODE;;'atlas://data/images/defaulttheme/sliderh_background')
94::CODE;;background_disabled_horizontal = StringProperty(
95::CODE;;'atlas://data/images/defaulttheme/sliderh_background_disabled')
102::CODE;;background_vertical = StringProperty(
103::CODE;;'atlas://data/images/defaulttheme/sliderv_background')

110::CODE;;'atlas://data/images/defaulttheme/sliderv_background_disabled')

132::CODE;;'atlas://data/images/defaulttheme/slider_cursor_disabled')

190::CODE;;sensitivity = OptionProperty('all', options=('all', 'handle'))
200::CODE;;def on_min(self, *largs):
201::CODE;;self.value = min(self.max, max(self.min, self.value))
202::CODE;;def on_max(self, *largs):
203::CODE;;self.value = min(self.max, max(self.min, self.value))
204::CODE;;def get_norm_value(self):
205::CODE;;vmin = self.min
206::CODE;;d = self.max - vmin
207::CODE;;if d == 0:
208::CODE;;return 0
209::CODE;;return (self.value - vmin) / float(d)
210::CODE;;def set_norm_value(self, value):
211::CODE;;vmin = self.min
212::CODE;;vmax = self.max
213::CODE;;step = self.step
214::CODE;;val = min(value * (vmax - vmin) + vmin, vmax)
215::CODE;;if step == 0:
216::CODE;;self.value = val
217::CODE;;else:
218::CODE;;self.value = min(round((val - vmin) / step) * step + vmin,
219::CODE;;vmax)
220::CODE;;value_normalized = AliasProperty(get_norm_value, set_norm_value,
221::CODE;;bind=('value', 'min', 'max'),
222::CODE;;cache=True)
223::CODE;;'''Normalized value inside the :attr:`range` (min/max) to 0-1 range::
224::CODE;;>>> slider = Slider(value=50, min=0, max=100)
225::CODE;;>>> slider.value
226::CODE;;50
227::CODE;;>>> slider.value_normalized
228::CODE;;0.5
229::CODE;;>>> slider.value = 0
230::CODE;;>>> slider.value_normalized
231::CODE;;0
232::CODE;;>>> slider.value = 100
233::CODE;;>>> slider.value_normalized
234::CODE;;1
235::CODE;;You can also use it for setting the real value without knowing the minimum
236::CODE;;and maximum::
237::CODE;;>>> slider = Slider(min=0, max=200)
238::CODE;;>>> slider.value_normalized = .5
239::CODE;;>>> slider.value
240::CODE;;100
241::CODE;;>>> slider.value_normalized = 1.
242::CODE;;>>> slider.value
243::CODE;;200
244::CODE;;:attr:`value_normalized` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.AliasProperty`.
245::CODE;;'''
246::CODE;;def get_value_pos(self):
247::CODE;;padding = self.padding
248::CODE;;x = self.x
249::CODE;;y = self.y
250::CODE;;nval = self.value_normalized
251::CODE;;if self.orientation == 'horizontal':
252::CODE;;return (x + padding + nval * (self.width - 2 * padding), y)
253::CODE;;else:
254::CODE;;return (x, y + padding + nval * (self.height - 2 * padding))
255::CODE;;def set_value_pos(self, pos):
256::CODE;;padding = self.padding
257::CODE;;x = min(self.right - padding, max(pos[0], self.x + padding))
258::CODE;;y = min(self.top - padding, max(pos[1], self.y + padding))
259::CODE;;if self.orientation == 'horizontal':
260::CODE;;if self.width == 0:
261::CODE;;self.value_normalized = 0
262::CODE;;else:
263::CODE;;self.value_normalized = (x - self.x - padding
264::CODE;;) / float(self.width - 2 * padding)
265::CODE;;else:
266::CODE;;if self.height == 0:
267::CODE;;self.value_normalized = 0
268::CODE;;else:
269::CODE;;self.value_normalized = (y - self.y - padding
270::CODE;;) / float(self.height - 2 * padding)
271::CODE;;value_pos = AliasProperty(get_value_pos, set_value_pos,
272::CODE;;bind=('pos', 'size', 'min', 'max', 'padding',
273::CODE;;'value_normalized', 'orientation'),
274::CODE;;cache=True)
275::CODE;;'''Position of the internal cursor, based on the normalized value.
276::CODE;;:attr:`value_pos` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.AliasProperty`.
277::CODE;;'''
278::CODE;;def on_touch_down(self, touch):
279::CODE;;if self.disabled or not self.collide_point(*touch.pos):
280::CODE;;return
281::CODE;;if touch.is_mouse_scrolling:
282::CODE;;if 'down' in touch.button or 'left' in touch.button:
283::CODE;;if self.step:
284::CODE;;self.value = min(self.max, self.value + self.step)
285::CODE;;else:
286::CODE;;self.value = min(
287::CODE;;self.max,
288::CODE;;self.value + (self.max - self.min) / 20)
289::CODE;;if 'up' in touch.button or 'right' in touch.button:
290::CODE;;if self.step:
291::CODE;;self.value = max(self.min, self.value - self.step)
292::CODE;;else:
293::CODE;;self.value = max(
294::CODE;;self.min,
295::CODE;;self.value - (self.max - self.min) / 20)
296::CODE;;elif self.sensitivity == 'handle':
297::CODE;;if self.children[0].collide_point(*touch.pos):
298::CODE;;touch.grab(self)
299::CODE;;else:
300::CODE;;touch.grab(self)
301::CODE;;self.value_pos = touch.pos
302::CODE;;return True
303::CODE;;def on_touch_move(self, touch):
304::CODE;;if touch.grab_current == self:
305::CODE;;self.value_pos = touch.pos
306::CODE;;return True
307::CODE;;def on_touch_up(self, touch):
308::CODE;;if touch.grab_current == self:
309::CODE;;self.value_pos = touch.pos
310::CODE;;return True

2::CODE;;Spinner
3::CODE;;=======
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.4.0
5::CODE;;.. image:: images/spinner.jpg
6::CODE;;:align: right
7::CODE;;Spinner is a widget that provides a quick way to select one value from a set.
8::CODE;;In the default state, a spinner shows its currently selected value.
9::CODE;;Touching the spinner displays a dropdown menu with all the other available
10::CODE;;values from which the user can select a new one.
11::CODE;;Example::
12::CODE;;from kivy.base import runTouchApp
13::CODE;;from kivy.uix.spinner import Spinner
14::CODE;;spinner = Spinner(
16::CODE;;text='Home',
18::CODE;;values=('Home', 'Work', 'Other', 'Custom'),
20::CODE;;size_hint=(None, None),
21::CODE;;size=(100, 44),
22::CODE;;pos_hint={'center_x': .5, 'center_y': .5})
23::CODE;;def show_selected_value(spinner, text):
24::CODE;;print('The spinner', spinner, 'has text', text)
25::CODE;;spinner.bind(text=show_selected_value)
26::CODE;;runTouchApp(spinner)
27::CODE;;Kv Example::
28::CODE;;FloatLayout:
29::CODE;;Spinner:
30::CODE;;size_hint: None, None
31::CODE;;size: 100, 44
32::CODE;;pos_hint: {'center': (.5, .5)}

34::CODE;;values: 'Home', 'Work', 'Other', 'Custom'

36::CODE;;print("The spinner {} has text {}".format(self, self.text))

1::CODE;;'''Splitter
2::CODE;;======
3::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.5.0
4::CODE;;.. image:: images/splitter.jpg
5::CODE;;:align: right
6::CODE;;The :class:`Splitter` is a widget that helps you re-size its child
7::CODE;;widget/layout by letting you re-size it via dragging the boundary or
8::CODE;;double tapping the boundary. This widget is similar to the
9::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.scrollview.ScrollView` in that it allows only one
10::CODE;;child widget.
11::CODE;;Usage::
12::CODE;;splitter = Splitter(sizable_from = 'right')
13::CODE;;splitter.add_widget(layout_or_widget_instance)
14::CODE;;splitter.min_size = 100
15::CODE;;splitter.max_size = 250
16::CODE;;To change the size of the strip/border used for resizing::
17::CODE;;splitter.strip_size = '10pt'
18::CODE;;To change its appearance::
19::CODE;;splitter.strip_cls = your_custom_class
20::CODE;;You can also change the appearance of the `strip_cls`, which defaults to
21::CODE;;:class:`SplitterStrip`, by overriding the `kv` rule in your app:
22::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
23::CODE;;<SplitterStrip>:
24::CODE;;horizontal: True if self.parent and self.parent.sizable_from[0] \
25::CODE;;in ('t', 'b') else False
26::CODE;;background_normal: 'path to normal horizontal image' \
27::CODE;;if self.horizontal else 'path to vertical normal image'
28::CODE;;background_down: 'path to pressed horizontal image' \
29::CODE;;if self.horizontal else 'path to vertical pressed image'
30::CODE;;'''
31::CODE;;__all__ = ('Splitter', )

200::CODE;;def _rebind_parent(self, instance, new_parent):
201::CODE;;if self._bound_parent is not None:
202::CODE;;self._bound_parent.unbind(size=self.rescale_parent_proportion)
203::CODE;;if self.parent is not None:
204::CODE;;new_parent.bind(size=self.rescale_parent_proportion)
205::CODE;;self._bound_parent = new_parent
206::CODE;;self.rescale_parent_proportion()
207::CODE;;def rescale_parent_proportion(self, *args):
208::CODE;;if not self.parent:
209::CODE;;return
210::CODE;;if self.rescale_with_parent:
211::CODE;;parent_proportion = self._parent_proportion
212::CODE;;if self.sizable_from in ('top', 'bottom'):
213::CODE;;new_height = parent_proportion * self.parent.height
214::CODE;;self.height = max(self.min_size,
215::CODE;;min(new_height, self.max_size))
216::CODE;;else:
217::CODE;;new_width = parent_proportion * self.parent.width
218::CODE;;self.width = max(self.min_size, min(new_width, self.max_size))
219::CODE;;def _do_size(self, instance, value):
220::CODE;;if self.sizable_from[0] in ('l', 'r'):
221::CODE;;self.width = max(self.min_size, min(self.width, self.max_size))
222::CODE;;else:
223::CODE;;self.height = max(self.min_size, min(self.height, self.max_size))
224::CODE;;@staticmethod
225::CODE;;def _is_moving(sz_frm, diff, pos, minpos, maxpos):
226::CODE;;if sz_frm in ('l', 'b'):
227::CODE;;cmp = minpos
228::CODE;;else:
229::CODE;;cmp = maxpos
230::CODE;;if diff == 0:
231::CODE;;return False
232::CODE;;elif diff > 0 and pos <= cmp:
233::CODE;;return False
234::CODE;;elif diff < 0 and pos >= cmp:
235::CODE;;return False
236::CODE;;return True
237::CODE;;def strip_move(self, instance, touch):
238::CODE;;if touch.grab_current is not instance:
239::CODE;;return False
240::CODE;;max_size = self.max_size
241::CODE;;min_size = self.min_size
242::CODE;;sz_frm = self.sizable_from[0]
243::CODE;;if sz_frm in ('t', 'b'):
244::CODE;;diff_y = (touch.dy)
245::CODE;;self_y = self.y
246::CODE;;self_top = self.top
247::CODE;;if not self._is_moving(sz_frm, diff_y, touch.y, self_y, self_top):
248::CODE;;return
249::CODE;;if self.keep_within_parent:
250::CODE;;if sz_frm == 't' and (self_top + diff_y) > self.parent.top:
251::CODE;;diff_y = self.parent.top - self_top
252::CODE;;elif sz_frm == 'b' and (self_y + diff_y) < self.parent.y:
253::CODE;;diff_y = self.parent.y - self_y
254::CODE;;if sz_frm == 'b':
255::CODE;;diff_y *= -1
256::CODE;;if self.size_hint_y:
257::CODE;;self.size_hint_y = None
258::CODE;;if self.height > 0:
259::CODE;;self.height += diff_y
260::CODE;;else:
261::CODE;;self.height = 1
262::CODE;;height = self.height
263::CODE;;self.height = max(min_size, min(height, max_size))
264::CODE;;self._parent_proportion = self.height / self.parent.height
265::CODE;;else:
266::CODE;;diff_x = (touch.dx)
267::CODE;;self_x = self.x
268::CODE;;self_right = self.right
269::CODE;;if not self._is_moving(sz_frm, diff_x, touch.x, self_x, self_right):
270::CODE;;return
271::CODE;;if self.keep_within_parent:
272::CODE;;if sz_frm == 'l' and (self_x + diff_x) < self.parent.x:
273::CODE;;diff_x = self.parent.x - self_x
274::CODE;;elif (sz_frm == 'r' and
275::CODE;;(self_right + diff_x) > self.parent.right):
276::CODE;;diff_x = self.parent.right - self_right
277::CODE;;if sz_frm == 'l':
278::CODE;;diff_x *= -1
279::CODE;;if self.size_hint_x:
280::CODE;;self.size_hint_x = None
281::CODE;;if self.width > 0:
282::CODE;;self.width += diff_x
283::CODE;;else:
284::CODE;;self.width = 1
285::CODE;;width = self.width
286::CODE;;self.width = max(min_size, min(width, max_size))
287::CODE;;self._parent_proportion = self.width / self.parent.width
288::CODE;;def strip_up(self, instance, touch):
289::CODE;;if touch.grab_current is not instance:
290::CODE;;return
291::CODE;;if touch.is_double_tap:
292::CODE;;max_size = self.max_size
293::CODE;;min_size = self.min_size
294::CODE;;sz_frm = self.sizable_from[0]
295::CODE;;s = self.size
296::CODE;;if sz_frm in ('t', 'b'):
297::CODE;;if self.size_hint_y:
298::CODE;;self.size_hint_y = None
299::CODE;;if s[1] - min_size <= max_size - s[1]:
300::CODE;;self.height = max_size
301::CODE;;else:
302::CODE;;self.height = min_size
303::CODE;;else:
304::CODE;;if self.size_hint_x:
305::CODE;;self.size_hint_x = None
306::CODE;;if s[0] - min_size <= max_size - s[0]:
307::CODE;;self.width = max_size
308::CODE;;else:
309::CODE;;self.width = min_size
310::CODE;;touch.ungrab(instance)
311::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_release')
312::CODE;;def on_release(self):
313::CODE;;pass

2::CODE;;Stack Layout
3::CODE;;============
4::CODE;;.. only:: html
5::CODE;;.. image:: images/stacklayout.gif
6::CODE;;:align: right
7::CODE;;.. only:: latex
8::CODE;;.. image:: images/stacklayout.png
9::CODE;;:align: right
10::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.5
11::CODE;;The :class:`StackLayout` arranges children vertically or horizontally, as many
12::CODE;;as the layout can fit. The size of the individual children widgets do not
13::CODE;;have to be uniform.
14::CODE;;For example, to display widgets that get progressively larger in width::
15::CODE;;root = StackLayout()
16::CODE;;for i in range(25):
17::CODE;;btn = Button(text=str(i), width=40 + i * 5, size_hint=(None, 0.15))
18::CODE;;root.add_widget(btn)
19::CODE;;.. image:: images/stacklayout_sizing.png
20::CODE;;:align: left
21::CODE;;'''
22::CODE;;__all__ = ('StackLayout', )
23::CODE;;from kivy.uix.layout import Layout
24::CODE;;from kivy.properties import NumericProperty, OptionProperty, \
25::CODE;;ReferenceListProperty, VariableListProperty
26::CODE;;def _compute_size(c, available_size, idx):
27::CODE;;sh_min = c.size_hint_min[idx]
28::CODE;;sh_max = c.size_hint_max[idx]
29::CODE;;val = c.size_hint[idx] * available_size
30::CODE;;if sh_min is not None:
31::CODE;;if sh_max is not None:
32::CODE;;return max(min(sh_max, val), sh_min)
33::CODE;;return max(val, sh_min)
34::CODE;;if sh_max is not None:
35::CODE;;return min(sh_max, val)
36::CODE;;return val
37::CODE;;class StackLayout(Layout):
38::CODE;;'''Stack layout class. See module documentation for more information.
39::CODE;;'''
40::CODE;;spacing = VariableListProperty([0, 0], length=2)
41::CODE;;'''Spacing between children: [spacing_horizontal, spacing_vertical].
42::CODE;;spacing also accepts a single argument form [spacing].
43::CODE;;:attr:`spacing` is a
44::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.properties.VariableListProperty` and defaults to [0, 0].
45::CODE;;'''
46::CODE;;padding = VariableListProperty([0, 0, 0, 0])
47::CODE;;'''Padding between the layout box and it's children: [padding_left,
48::CODE;;padding_top, padding_right, padding_bottom].
49::CODE;;padding also accepts a two argument form [padding_horizontal,
50::CODE;;padding_vertical] and a single argument form [padding].
51::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.7.0
52::CODE;;Replaced the NumericProperty with a VariableListProperty.
53::CODE;;:attr:`padding` is a
54::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.properties.VariableListProperty` and defaults to
55::CODE;;[0, 0, 0, 0].
56::CODE;;'''
57::CODE;;orientation = OptionProperty('lr-tb', options=(
58::CODE;;'lr-tb', 'tb-lr', 'rl-tb', 'tb-rl', 'lr-bt', 'bt-lr', 'rl-bt',
59::CODE;;'bt-rl'))
60::CODE;;'''Orientation of the layout.
61::CODE;;:attr:`orientation` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.OptionProperty` and
62::CODE;;defaults to 'lr-tb'.
63::CODE;;Valid orientations are 'lr-tb', 'tb-lr', 'rl-tb', 'tb-rl', 'lr-bt',
64::CODE;;'bt-lr', 'rl-bt' and 'bt-rl'.
65::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.5.0
66::CODE;;:attr:`orientation` now correctly handles all valid combinations of
67::CODE;;'lr','rl','tb','bt'. Before this version only 'lr-tb' and
68::CODE;;'tb-lr' were supported, and 'tb-lr' was misnamed and placed
69::CODE;;widgets from bottom to top and from right to left (reversed compared
70::CODE;;to what was expected).
71::CODE;;.. note::
72::CODE;;'lr' means Left to Right.
73::CODE;;'rl' means Right to Left.
74::CODE;;'tb' means Top to Bottom.
75::CODE;;'bt' means Bottom to Top.
76::CODE;;'''
77::CODE;;minimum_width = NumericProperty(0)
78::CODE;;'''Minimum width needed to contain all children. It is automatically set
79::CODE;;by the layout.
80::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.8
81::CODE;;:attr:`minimum_width` is a :class:`kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
82::CODE;;defaults to 0.
83::CODE;;'''
84::CODE;;minimum_height = NumericProperty(0)
85::CODE;;'''Minimum height needed to contain all children. It is automatically set
86::CODE;;by the layout.
87::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.8
88::CODE;;:attr:`minimum_height` is a :class:`kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and
89::CODE;;defaults to 0.
90::CODE;;'''
91::CODE;;minimum_size = ReferenceListProperty(minimum_width, minimum_height)
92::CODE;;'''Minimum size needed to contain all children. It is automatically set
93::CODE;;by the layout.
94::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.8
95::CODE;;:attr:`minimum_size` is a
96::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.properties.ReferenceListProperty` of
97::CODE;;(:attr:`minimum_width`, :attr:`minimum_height`) properties.
98::CODE;;'''
99::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
100::CODE;;super(StackLayout, self).__init__(**kwargs)
101::CODE;;trigger = self._trigger_layout
102::CODE;;fbind = self.fbind
103::CODE;;fbind('padding', trigger)
104::CODE;;fbind('spacing', trigger)
105::CODE;;fbind('children', trigger)
106::CODE;;fbind('orientation', trigger)
107::CODE;;fbind('size', trigger)
108::CODE;;fbind('pos', trigger)
109::CODE;;def do_layout(self, *largs):
110::CODE;;if not self.children:
111::CODE;;self.minimum_size = (0., 0.)
112::CODE;;return
114::CODE;;selfpos = self.pos
115::CODE;;selfsize = self.size
116::CODE;;orientation = self.orientation.split('-')
117::CODE;;padding_left = self.padding[0]
118::CODE;;padding_top = self.padding[1]
119::CODE;;padding_right = self.padding[2]
120::CODE;;padding_bottom = self.padding[3]
121::CODE;;padding_x = padding_left + padding_right
122::CODE;;padding_y = padding_top + padding_bottom
123::CODE;;spacing_x, spacing_y = self.spacing
125::CODE;;posattr = [0] * 2
126::CODE;;posdelta = [0] * 2
127::CODE;;posstart = [0] * 2
128::CODE;;for i in (0, 1):
129::CODE;;posattr[i] = 1 * (orientation[i] in ('tb', 'bt'))
130::CODE;;k = posattr[i]
131::CODE;;if orientation[i] == 'lr':
133::CODE;;posdelta[i] = 1
134::CODE;;posstart[i] = selfpos[k] + padding_left
135::CODE;;elif orientation[i] == 'bt':
137::CODE;;posdelta[i] = 1
138::CODE;;posstart[i] = selfpos[k] + padding_bottom
139::CODE;;elif orientation[i] == 'rl':
141::CODE;;posdelta[i] = -1
142::CODE;;posstart[i] = selfpos[k] + selfsize[k] - padding_right
143::CODE;;else:
145::CODE;;posdelta[i] = -1
146::CODE;;posstart[i] = selfpos[k] + selfsize[k] - padding_top
147::CODE;;innerattr, outerattr = posattr
148::CODE;;ustart, vstart = posstart
149::CODE;;deltau, deltav = posdelta
150::CODE;;del posattr, posdelta, posstart
154::CODE;;if orientation[0] in ('lr', 'rl'):
157::CODE;;spacing_u = spacing_x
158::CODE;;spacing_v = spacing_y
159::CODE;;padding_u = padding_x
160::CODE;;padding_v = padding_y
161::CODE;;else:
164::CODE;;spacing_u = spacing_y
165::CODE;;spacing_v = spacing_x
166::CODE;;padding_u = padding_y
167::CODE;;padding_v = padding_x
169::CODE;;lv = 0
170::CODE;;urev = (deltau < 0)
171::CODE;;vrev = (deltav < 0)
172::CODE;;firstchild = self.children[0]
173::CODE;;sizes = []
174::CODE;;lc = []
175::CODE;;for c in reversed(self.children):
176::CODE;;if c.size_hint[outerattr] is not None:
177::CODE;;c.size[outerattr] = max(
178::CODE;;1, _compute_size(c, selfsize[outerattr] - padding_v,
179::CODE;;outerattr))
181::CODE;;ccount = len(lc)
182::CODE;;totalsize = availsize = max(
183::CODE;;0, selfsize[innerattr] - padding_u - spacing_u * ccount)
184::CODE;;if not lc:
185::CODE;;if c.size_hint[innerattr] is not None:
186::CODE;;childsize = max(1, _compute_size(c, totalsize, innerattr))
187::CODE;;else:
188::CODE;;childsize = max(0, c.size[innerattr])
189::CODE;;availsize = selfsize[innerattr] - padding_u - childsize
190::CODE;;testsizes = [childsize]
191::CODE;;else:
192::CODE;;testsizes = [0] * (ccount + 1)
193::CODE;;for i, child in enumerate(lc):
194::CODE;;if availsize <= 0:
196::CODE;;availsize = -1
197::CODE;;break
198::CODE;;if child.size_hint[innerattr] is not None:
199::CODE;;testsizes[i] = childsize = max(
200::CODE;;1, _compute_size(child, totalsize, innerattr))
201::CODE;;else:
202::CODE;;childsize = max(0, child.size[innerattr])
203::CODE;;testsizes[i] = childsize
204::CODE;;availsize -= childsize
205::CODE;;if c.size_hint[innerattr] is not None:
206::CODE;;testsizes[-1] = max(
207::CODE;;1, _compute_size(c, totalsize, innerattr))
208::CODE;;else:
209::CODE;;testsizes[-1] = max(0, c.size[innerattr])
210::CODE;;availsize -= testsizes[-1]
215::CODE;;if (availsize + 1e-10) >= 0 or not lc:
217::CODE;;lc.append(c)
218::CODE;;sizes = testsizes
219::CODE;;lv = max(lv, c.size[outerattr])
220::CODE;;continue
222::CODE;;for i, child in enumerate(lc):
223::CODE;;if child.size_hint[innerattr] is not None:
224::CODE;;child.size[innerattr] = sizes[i]
226::CODE;;sv += lv + spacing_v
227::CODE;;for c2 in lc:
228::CODE;;if urev:
229::CODE;;u -= c2.size[innerattr]
230::CODE;;c2.pos[innerattr] = u
231::CODE;;pos_outer = v
232::CODE;;if vrev:
236::CODE;;pos_outer -= c2.size[outerattr]
237::CODE;;c2.pos[outerattr] = pos_outer
238::CODE;;if urev:
239::CODE;;u -= spacing_u
240::CODE;;else:
241::CODE;;u += c2.size[innerattr] + spacing_u
242::CODE;;v += deltav * lv
243::CODE;;v += deltav * spacing_v
244::CODE;;lc = [c]
245::CODE;;lv = c.size[outerattr]
246::CODE;;if c.size_hint[innerattr] is not None:
247::CODE;;sizes = [
248::CODE;;max(1, _compute_size(c, selfsize[innerattr] - padding_u,
249::CODE;;innerattr))]
250::CODE;;else:
251::CODE;;sizes = [max(0, c.size[innerattr])]
252::CODE;;u = ustart
253::CODE;;if lc:
255::CODE;;for i, child in enumerate(lc):
256::CODE;;if child.size_hint[innerattr] is not None:
257::CODE;;child.size[innerattr] = sizes[i]
259::CODE;;sv += lv + spacing_v
260::CODE;;for c2 in lc:
261::CODE;;if urev:
262::CODE;;u -= c2.size[innerattr]
263::CODE;;c2.pos[innerattr] = u
264::CODE;;pos_outer = v
265::CODE;;if vrev:
266::CODE;;pos_outer -= c2.size[outerattr]
267::CODE;;c2.pos[outerattr] = pos_outer
268::CODE;;if urev:
269::CODE;;u -= spacing_u
270::CODE;;else:
271::CODE;;u += c2.size[innerattr] + spacing_u
272::CODE;;self.minimum_size[outerattr] = sv

2::CODE;;Stencil View
3::CODE;;============
4::CODE;;.. image:: images/stencilview.gif
5::CODE;;:align: right
6::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.4
7::CODE;;:class:`StencilView` limits the drawing of child widgets to the StencilView's
8::CODE;;bounding box. Any drawing outside the bounding box will be clipped (trashed).
9::CODE;;The StencilView uses the stencil graphics instructions under the hood. It
10::CODE;;provides an efficient way to clip the drawing area of children.
11::CODE;;.. note::
12::CODE;;As with the stencil graphics instructions, you cannot stack more than 128
13::CODE;;stencil-aware widgets.
14::CODE;;.. note::
15::CODE;;StencilView is not a layout. Consequently, you have to manage the size and
16::CODE;;position of its children directly. You can combine (subclass both)
17::CODE;;a StencilView and a Layout in order to achieve a layout's behavior.
18::CODE;;For example::
19::CODE;;class BoxStencil(BoxLayout, StencilView):
20::CODE;;pass
21::CODE;;'''
22::CODE;;__all__ = ('StencilView', )
23::CODE;;from kivy.uix.widget import Widget
24::CODE;;class StencilView(Widget):
25::CODE;;'''StencilView class. See module documentation for more information.
26::CODE;;'''
27::CODE;;pass
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Switch
3::CODE;;======
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.7
5::CODE;;.. image:: images/switch-on.jpg
6::CODE;;:align: right
7::CODE;;.. image:: images/switch-off.jpg
8::CODE;;:align: right
9::CODE;;The :class:`Switch` widget is active or inactive, like a mechanical light
10::CODE;;switch. The user can swipe to the left/right to activate/deactivate it::
11::CODE;;switch = Switch(active=True)
12::CODE;;To attach a callback that listens to the activation state::
13::CODE;;def callback(instance, value):
14::CODE;;print('the switch', instance, 'is', value)
15::CODE;;switch = Switch()
16::CODE;;switch.bind(active=callback)
17::CODE;;By default, the representation of the widget is static. The minimum size
18::CODE;;required is 83x32 pixels (defined by the background image). The image is
19::CODE;;centered within the widget.
20::CODE;;The entire widget is active, not just the part with graphics. As long as you
21::CODE;;swipe over the widget's bounding box, it will work.
22::CODE;;.. note::
23::CODE;;If you want to control the state with a single touch instead of a swipe,
24::CODE;;use the :class:`ToggleButton` instead.
25::CODE;;Kv Example::
26::CODE;;BoxLayout:
27::CODE;;Label:
28::CODE;;text: 'power up'
29::CODE;;Switch:
30::CODE;;id: switch
31::CODE;;Label:
32::CODE;;text: 'woooooooooooh' if switch.active else ''
33::CODE;;'''
34::CODE;;from kivy.uix.widget import Widget
35::CODE;;from kivy.animation import Animation
36::CODE;;from kivy.properties import BooleanProperty, ObjectProperty, NumericProperty
37::CODE;;class Switch(Widget):
38::CODE;;'''Switch class. See module documentation for more information.
39::CODE;;'''
40::CODE;;active = BooleanProperty(False)
41::CODE;;'''Indicate whether the switch is active or inactive.
42::CODE;;:attr:`active` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty` and defaults
43::CODE;;to False.
44::CODE;;'''
45::CODE;;touch_control = ObjectProperty(None, allownone=True)
46::CODE;;'''(internal) Contains the touch that currently interacts with the switch.
47::CODE;;:attr:`touch_control` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.ObjectProperty`
48::CODE;;and defaults to None.
49::CODE;;'''
50::CODE;;touch_distance = NumericProperty(0)
51::CODE;;'''(internal) Contains the distance between the initial position of the
52::CODE;;touch and the current position to determine if the swipe is from the left
53::CODE;;or right.
54::CODE;;:attr:`touch_distance` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty`
55::CODE;;and defaults to 0.
56::CODE;;'''
57::CODE;;active_norm_pos = NumericProperty(0)
58::CODE;;'''(internal) Contains the normalized position of the movable element
59::CODE;;inside the switch, in the 0-1 range.
60::CODE;;:attr:`active_norm_pos` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty`
61::CODE;;and defaults to 0.
62::CODE;;'''
63::CODE;;def on_touch_down(self, touch):
64::CODE;;if self.disabled or self.touch_control is not None:
65::CODE;;return
66::CODE;;if not self.collide_point(*touch.pos):
67::CODE;;return
68::CODE;;touch.grab(self)
69::CODE;;self.touch_distance = 0
70::CODE;;self.touch_control = touch
71::CODE;;return True
72::CODE;;def on_touch_move(self, touch):
73::CODE;;if touch.grab_current is not self:
74::CODE;;return
75::CODE;;self.touch_distance = touch.x - touch.ox
76::CODE;;return True
77::CODE;;def on_touch_up(self, touch):
78::CODE;;if touch.grab_current is not self:
79::CODE;;return
80::CODE;;touch.ungrab(self)
82::CODE;;if abs(touch.ox - touch.x) < 5:
83::CODE;;self.active = not self.active
84::CODE;;else:
85::CODE;;self.active = self.active_norm_pos > 0.5
86::CODE;;Animation(active_norm_pos=int(self.active), t='out_quad',
87::CODE;;d=.2).start(self)
88::CODE;;self.touch_control = None
89::CODE;;return True
90::CODE;;if __name__ == '__main__':
91::CODE;;from kivy.base import runTouchApp
92::CODE;;runTouchApp(Switch())
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;TabbedPanel
3::CODE;;===========
4::CODE;;.. image:: images/tabbed_panel.jpg
5::CODE;;:align: right
6::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.3.0
7::CODE;;The `TabbedPanel` widget manages different widgets in tabs, with a header area
8::CODE;;for the actual tab buttons and a content area for showing the current tab
9::CODE;;content.
10::CODE;;The :class:`TabbedPanel` provides one default tab.
11::CODE;;Simple example
12::CODE;;--------------
13::CODE;;.. include:: ../../examples/widgets/tabbedpanel.py
14::CODE;;:literal:
15::CODE;;.. note::
16::CODE;;A new class :class:`TabbedPanelItem` has been introduced in 1.5.0 for
17::CODE;;convenience. So now one can simply add a :class:`TabbedPanelItem` to a
18::CODE;;:class:`TabbedPanel` and `content` to the :class:`TabbedPanelItem`
19::CODE;;as in the example provided above.
20::CODE;;Customize the Tabbed Panel
21::CODE;;--------------------------
22::CODE;;You can choose the position in which the tabs are displayed::
23::CODE;;tab_pos = 'top_mid'
24::CODE;;An individual tab is called a TabbedPanelHeader. It is a special button
25::CODE;;containing a `content` property. You add the TabbedPanelHeader first, and set
26::CODE;;its `content` property separately::
27::CODE;;tp = TabbedPanel()
28::CODE;;th = TabbedPanelHeader(text='Tab2')
29::CODE;;tp.add_widget(th)
30::CODE;;An individual tab, represented by a TabbedPanelHeader, needs its content set.
31::CODE;;This content can be any widget. It could be a layout with a deep
32::CODE;;hierarchy of widgets, or it could be an individual widget, such as a label or a
33::CODE;;button::
34::CODE;;th.content = your_content_instance
35::CODE;;There is one "shared" main content area active at any given time, for all
36::CODE;;the tabs. Your app is responsible for adding the content of individual tabs
37::CODE;;and for managing them, but it's not responsible for content switching. The
38::CODE;;tabbed panel handles switching of the main content object as per user action.
39::CODE;;There is a default tab added when the tabbed panel is instantiated.
40::CODE;;Tabs that you add individually as above, are added in addition to the default
41::CODE;;tab. Thus, depending on your needs and design, you will want to customize the
42::CODE;;default tab::
43::CODE;;tp.default_tab_text = 'Something Specific To Your Use'
44::CODE;;The default tab machinery requires special consideration and management.
45::CODE;;Accordingly, an `on_default_tab` event is provided for associating a callback::
46::CODE;;tp.bind(default_tab = my_default_tab_callback)
47::CODE;;It's important to note that by default, :attr:`default_tab_cls` is of type
48::CODE;;:class:`TabbedPanelHeader` and thus has the same properties as other tabs.
49::CODE;;Since 1.5.0, it is now possible to disable the creation of the
50::CODE;;:attr:`default_tab` by setting :attr:`do_default_tab` to False.
51::CODE;;Tabs and content can be removed in several ways::
52::CODE;;tp.remove_widget(widget/tabbed_panel_header)
53::CODE;;or
55::CODE;;or
57::CODE;;To access the children of the tabbed panel, use content.children::
58::CODE;;tp.content.children
59::CODE;;To access the list of tabs::
60::CODE;;tp.tab_list
61::CODE;;To change the appearance of the main tabbed panel content::
63::CODE;;border = [0, 0, 0, 0]
64::CODE;;background_image = 'path/to/background/image'
65::CODE;;To change the background of a individual tab, use these two properties::
66::CODE;;tab_header_instance.background_normal = 'path/to/tab_head/img'
67::CODE;;tab_header_instance.background_down = 'path/to/tab_head/img_pressed'
68::CODE;;A TabbedPanelStrip contains the individual tab headers. To change the
69::CODE;;appearance of this tab strip, override the canvas of TabbedPanelStrip.
70::CODE;;For example, in the kv language:
71::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
72::CODE;;<TabbedPanelStrip>
73::CODE;;canvas:
74::CODE;;Color:
76::CODE;;Rectangle:
77::CODE;;size: self.size
78::CODE;;pos: self.pos
79::CODE;;By default the tabbed panel strip takes its background image and color from the
80::CODE;;tabbed panel's background_image and background_color.
81::CODE;;'''
