1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Text Input
3::CODE;;==========
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.4
5::CODE;;.. image:: images/textinput-mono.jpg
6::CODE;;.. image:: images/textinput-multi.jpg
7::CODE;;The :class:`TextInput` widget provides a box for editable plain text.
8::CODE;;Unicode, multiline, cursor navigation, selection and clipboard features
9::CODE;;are supported.
10::CODE;;The :class:`TextInput` uses two different coordinate systems:
11::CODE;;* (x, y) - coordinates in pixels, mostly used for rendering on screen.
12::CODE;;* (col, row) - cursor index in characters / lines, used for selection
13::CODE;;and cursor movement.
14::CODE;;Usage example
15::CODE;;-------------
16::CODE;;To create a multiline :class:`TextInput` (the 'enter' key adds a new line)::
17::CODE;;from kivy.uix.textinput import TextInput
18::CODE;;textinput = TextInput(text='Hello world')
19::CODE;;To create a singleline :class:`TextInput`, set the :class:`TextInput.multiline`
20::CODE;;property to False (the 'enter' key will defocus the TextInput and emit an
21::CODE;;:meth:`TextInput.on_text_validate` event)::
22::CODE;;def on_enter(instance, value):
23::CODE;;print('User pressed enter in', instance)
24::CODE;;textinput = TextInput(text='Hello world', multiline=False)
25::CODE;;textinput.bind(on_text_validate=on_enter)
26::CODE;;The textinput's text is stored in its :attr:`TextInput.text` property. To run a
27::CODE;;callback when the text changes::
28::CODE;;def on_text(instance, value):
29::CODE;;print('The widget', instance, 'have:', value)
30::CODE;;textinput = TextInput()
31::CODE;;textinput.bind(text=on_text)
32::CODE;;You can set the :class:`focus <kivy.uix.behaviors.FocusBehavior>` to a
33::CODE;;Textinput, meaning that the input box will be highlighted and keyboard focus
34::CODE;;will be requested::
35::CODE;;textinput = TextInput(focus=True)
36::CODE;;The textinput is defocused if the 'escape' key is pressed, or if another
37::CODE;;widget requests the keyboard. You can bind a callback to the focus property to
38::CODE;;get notified of focus changes::
39::CODE;;def on_focus(instance, value):
40::CODE;;if value:
41::CODE;;print('User focused', instance)
42::CODE;;else:
43::CODE;;print('User defocused', instance)
44::CODE;;textinput = TextInput()
45::CODE;;textinput.bind(focus=on_focus)
46::CODE;;See :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.FocusBehavior`, from which the
47::CODE;;:class:`TextInput` inherits, for more details.
48::CODE;;Selection
49::CODE;;---------
50::CODE;;The selection is automatically updated when the cursor position changes.
51::CODE;;You can get the currently selected text from the
52::CODE;;:attr:`TextInput.selection_text` property.
53::CODE;;Handles
54::CODE;;-------
55::CODE;;One can enable :attr:`TextInput.use_handles` property to enable or disable
56::CODE;;the usage of selection handles. This property is True by default on mobiles.
57::CODE;;Selection Handles uses the class :class:`Selector` as the base class for
58::CODE;;the selection handles. You can customize the color for selection handles
59::CODE;;like so ::
60::CODE;;<Selector>
61::CODE;;color: 0, 1, 0, 1
63::CODE;;TextInput instantiates the selection handles and stores it in the following
64::CODE;;properties. :attr:`TextInput._handle_middle`,
65::CODE;;:attr:`TextInput._handle_left`, :attr:`TextInput._handle_right`.
66::CODE;;You should set the selection template before the Instantiating TextInput,
67::CODE;;so as to get the selection handles to take the changes you set to apply.
68::CODE;;Filtering
69::CODE;;---------
70::CODE;;You can control which text can be added to the :class:`TextInput` by
71::CODE;;overwriting :meth:`TextInput.insert_text`. Every string that is typed, pasted
72::CODE;;or inserted by any other means into the :class:`TextInput` is passed through
73::CODE;;this function. By overwriting it you can reject or change unwanted characters.
74::CODE;;For example, to write only in capitalized characters::
75::CODE;;class CapitalInput(TextInput):
76::CODE;;def insert_text(self, substring, from_undo=False):
77::CODE;;s = substring.upper()
78::CODE;;return super().insert_text(s, from_undo=from_undo)
79::CODE;;Or to only allow floats (0 - 9 and a single period)::
80::CODE;;class FloatInput(TextInput):
81::CODE;;pat = re.compile('[^0-9]')
82::CODE;;def insert_text(self, substring, from_undo=False):
83::CODE;;pat = self.pat
84::CODE;;if '.' in self.text:
85::CODE;;s = re.sub(pat, '', substring)
86::CODE;;else:
87::CODE;;s = '.'.join(
88::CODE;;re.sub(pat, '', s)
89::CODE;;for s in substring.split('.', 1)
90::CODE;;)
91::CODE;;return super().insert_text(s, from_undo=from_undo)
92::CODE;;Default shortcuts
93::CODE;;-----------------
94::CODE;;=============== ========================================================
95::CODE;;Shortcuts Description
96::CODE;;--------------- --------------------------------------------------------
97::CODE;;Left Move cursor to left
98::CODE;;Right Move cursor to right
99::CODE;;Up Move cursor to up
100::CODE;;Down Move cursor to down
101::CODE;;Home Move cursor at the beginning of the line
102::CODE;;End Move cursor at the end of the line
103::CODE;;PageUp Move cursor to 3 lines before
104::CODE;;PageDown Move cursor to 3 lines after
105::CODE;;Backspace Delete the selection or character before the cursor
106::CODE;;Del Delete the selection of character after the cursor
107::CODE;;Shift + <dir> Start a text selection. Dir can be Up, Down, Left or
108::CODE;;Right
109::CODE;;Control + c Copy selection
110::CODE;;Control + x Cut selection
111::CODE;;Control + v Paste clipboard content
112::CODE;;Control + a Select all the content
113::CODE;;Control + z undo
114::CODE;;Control + r redo
115::CODE;;=============== ========================================================
116::CODE;;.. note::
117::CODE;;To enable Emacs-style keyboard shortcuts, you can use
118::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.emacs.EmacsBehavior`.
119::CODE;;'''

352::CODE;;class TextInput(FocusBehavior, Widget):
353::CODE;;'''TextInput class. See module documentation for more information.
354::CODE;;:Events:
355::CODE;;`on_text_validate`
356::CODE;;Fired only in multiline=False mode when the user hits 'enter'.
357::CODE;;This will also unfocus the textinput.
358::CODE;;`on_double_tap`
359::CODE;;Fired when a double tap happens in the text input. The default
360::CODE;;behavior selects the text around the cursor position. More info at
361::CODE;;:meth:`on_double_tap`.
362::CODE;;`on_triple_tap`
363::CODE;;Fired when a triple tap happens in the text input. The default
364::CODE;;behavior selects the line around the cursor position. More info at
365::CODE;;:meth:`on_triple_tap`.
366::CODE;;`on_quad_touch`
367::CODE;;Fired when four fingers are touching the text input. The default
368::CODE;;behavior selects the whole text. More info at
369::CODE;;:meth:`on_quad_touch`.
370::CODE;;.. warning::
371::CODE;;When changing a :class:`TextInput` property that requires re-drawing,
372::CODE;;e.g. modifying the :attr:`text`, the updates occur on the next
373::CODE;;clock cycle and not instantly. This might cause any changes to the
374::CODE;;:class:`TextInput` that occur between the modification and the next
375::CODE;;cycle to be ignored, or to use previous values. For example, after
376::CODE;;a update to the :attr:`text`, changing the cursor in the same clock
377::CODE;;frame will move it using the previous text and will likely end up in an
378::CODE;;incorrect position. The solution is to schedule any updates to occur
379::CODE;;on the next clock cycle using
380::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.clock.ClockBase.schedule_once`.
381::CODE;;.. Note::
382::CODE;;Selection is cancelled when TextInput is focused. If you need to
383::CODE;;show selection when TextInput is focused, you should delay
384::CODE;;(use Clock.schedule) the call to the functions for selecting
385::CODE;;text (select_all, select_text).
386::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.10.0
387::CODE;;`background_disabled_active` has been removed.
388::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.9.0
389::CODE;;:class:`TextInput` now inherits from
390::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.FocusBehavior`.
391::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.FocusBehavior.keyboard_mode`,
392::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.FocusBehavior.show_keyboard`,
393::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.FocusBehavior.hide_keyboard`,
394::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.FocusBehavior.focus`,
395::CODE;;and :attr:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.FocusBehavior.input_type`
396::CODE;;have been removed since they are now inherited
397::CODE;;from :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.FocusBehavior`.
398::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.7.0
399::CODE;;`on_double_tap`, `on_triple_tap` and `on_quad_touch` events added.
400::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 2.1.0
401::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.FocusBehavior.keyboard_suggestions`
402::CODE;;is now inherited from :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.FocusBehavior`.

1053::CODE;;def do_cursor_movement(self, action, control=False, alt=False):
1054::CODE;;'''Move the cursor relative to its current position.
1055::CODE;;Action can be one of :
1056::CODE;;- cursor_left: move the cursor to the left
1057::CODE;;- cursor_right: move the cursor to the right
1058::CODE;;- cursor_up: move the cursor on the previous line
1059::CODE;;- cursor_down: move the cursor on the next line
1060::CODE;;- cursor_home: move the cursor at the start of the current line
1061::CODE;;- cursor_end: move the cursor at the end of current line
1062::CODE;;- cursor_pgup: move one "page" before
1063::CODE;;- cursor_pgdown: move one "page" after
1064::CODE;;In addition, the behavior of certain actions can be modified:
1065::CODE;;- control + cursor_left: move the cursor one word to the left
1066::CODE;;- control + cursor_right: move the cursor one word to the right
1067::CODE;;- control + cursor_up: scroll up one line
1068::CODE;;- control + cursor_down: scroll down one line
1069::CODE;;- control + cursor_home: go to beginning of text
1070::CODE;;- control + cursor_end: go to end of text
1071::CODE;;- alt + cursor_up: shift line(s) up
1072::CODE;;- alt + cursor_down: shift line(s) down
1073::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.9.1
1074::CODE;;'''

1076::CODE;;return

1079::CODE;;result = self._move_cursor_up(col, row, control, alt)
1080::CODE;;if result:
1081::CODE;;col, row = result
1082::CODE;;else:
1083::CODE;;return
1084::CODE;;elif action == 'cursor_down':
1085::CODE;;result = self._move_cursor_down(col, row, control, alt)
1086::CODE;;if result:
1087::CODE;;col, row = result
1088::CODE;;else:
1089::CODE;;return

1100::CODE;;col = min(len(self._lines[row]), col)
1101::CODE;;elif action == 'cursor_pgdown':
1102::CODE;;row = min(row + self.pgmove_speed, len(self._lines) - 1)
1103::CODE;;col = min(len(self._lines[row]), col)

2::CODE;;Toggle button
3::CODE;;=============
4::CODE;;.. image:: images/togglebutton.jpg
5::CODE;;:align: right
6::CODE;;The :class:`ToggleButton` widget acts like a checkbox. When you touch or click
7::CODE;;it, the state toggles between 'normal' and 'down' (as opposed to a
8::CODE;;:class:`Button` that is only 'down' as long as it is pressed).
9::CODE;;Toggle buttons can also be grouped to make radio buttons - only one button in
10::CODE;;a group can be in a 'down' state. The group name can be a string or any other
11::CODE;;hashable Python object::
12::CODE;;btn1 = ToggleButton(text='Male', group='sex',)
13::CODE;;btn2 = ToggleButton(text='Female', group='sex', state='down')
14::CODE;;btn3 = ToggleButton(text='Mixed', group='sex')
15::CODE;;Only one of the buttons can be 'down'/checked at the same time.
16::CODE;;To configure the ToggleButton, you can use the same properties that you can use
17::CODE;;for a :class:`~kivy.uix.button.Button` class.
18::CODE;;'''
19::CODE;;__all__ = ('ToggleButton', )
20::CODE;;from kivy.uix.button import Button
21::CODE;;from kivy.uix.behaviors import ToggleButtonBehavior
22::CODE;;class ToggleButton(ToggleButtonBehavior, Button):
23::CODE;;'''Toggle button class, see module documentation for more information.
24::CODE;;'''

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Tree View
3::CODE;;=========
4::CODE;;.. image:: images/treeview.png
5::CODE;;:align: right
6::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.4
7::CODE;;:class:`TreeView` is a widget used to represent a tree structure. It is
8::CODE;;currently very basic, supporting a minimal feature set.
9::CODE;;Introduction
10::CODE;;------------
11::CODE;;A :class:`TreeView` is populated with :class:`TreeViewNode` instances, but you
12::CODE;;cannot use a :class:`TreeViewNode` directly. You must combine it with another
13::CODE;;widget, such as :class:`~kivy.uix.label.Label`,
14::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.button.Button` or even your own widget. The TreeView
15::CODE;;always creates a default root node, based on :class:`TreeViewLabel`.
16::CODE;;:class:`TreeViewNode` is a class object containing needed properties for
17::CODE;;serving as a tree node. Extend :class:`TreeViewNode` to create custom node
18::CODE;;types for use with a :class:`TreeView`.
19::CODE;;For constructing your own subclass, follow the pattern of TreeViewLabel which
20::CODE;;combines a Label and a TreeViewNode, producing a :class:`TreeViewLabel` for
21::CODE;;direct use in a TreeView instance.
22::CODE;;To use the TreeViewLabel class, you could create two nodes directly attached
23::CODE;;to root::
24::CODE;;tv = TreeView()
25::CODE;;tv.add_node(TreeViewLabel(text='My first item'))
26::CODE;;tv.add_node(TreeViewLabel(text='My second item'))
27::CODE;;Or, create two nodes attached to a first::
28::CODE;;tv = TreeView()
29::CODE;;n1 = tv.add_node(TreeViewLabel(text='Item 1'))
30::CODE;;tv.add_node(TreeViewLabel(text='SubItem 1'), n1)
31::CODE;;tv.add_node(TreeViewLabel(text='SubItem 2'), n1)
32::CODE;;If you have a large tree structure, perhaps you would need a utility function
33::CODE;;to populate the tree view::
34::CODE;;def populate_tree_view(tree_view, parent, node):
35::CODE;;if parent is None:
36::CODE;;tree_node = tree_view.add_node(TreeViewLabel(text=node['node_id'],
37::CODE;;is_open=True))
38::CODE;;else:
39::CODE;;tree_node = tree_view.add_node(TreeViewLabel(text=node['node_id'],
40::CODE;;is_open=True), parent)
41::CODE;;for child_node in node['children']:
42::CODE;;populate_tree_view(tree_view, tree_node, child_node)
43::CODE;;tree = {'node_id': '1',
44::CODE;;'children': [{'node_id': '1.1',
45::CODE;;'children': [{'node_id': '1.1.1',
46::CODE;;'children': [{'node_id': '1.1.1.1',
47::CODE;;'children': []}]},
48::CODE;;{'node_id': '1.1.2',
49::CODE;;'children': []},
50::CODE;;{'node_id': '1.1.3',
51::CODE;;'children': []}]},
52::CODE;;{'node_id': '1.2',
53::CODE;;'children': []}]}
54::CODE;;class TreeWidget(FloatLayout):
55::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
56::CODE;;super(TreeWidget, self).__init__(**kwargs)
57::CODE;;tv = TreeView(root_options=dict(text='Tree One'),
58::CODE;;hide_root=False,
59::CODE;;indent_level=4)
60::CODE;;populate_tree_view(tv, None, tree)
61::CODE;;self.add_widget(tv)
62::CODE;;The root widget in the tree view is opened by default and has text set as
63::CODE;;'Root'. If you want to change that, you can use the
64::CODE;;:attr:`TreeView.root_options`
65::CODE;;property. This will pass options to the root widget::
66::CODE;;tv = TreeView(root_options=dict(text='My root label'))
67::CODE;;Creating Your Own Node Widget
68::CODE;;-----------------------------
69::CODE;;For a button node type, combine a :class:`~kivy.uix.button.Button` and a
70::CODE;;:class:`TreeViewNode` as follows::
71::CODE;;class TreeViewButton(Button, TreeViewNode):
72::CODE;;pass
73::CODE;;You must know that, for a given node, only the
74::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.size_hint_x` will be honored. The allocated
75::CODE;;width for the node will depend of the current width of the TreeView and the
76::CODE;;level of the node. For example, if a node is at level 4, the width
77::CODE;;allocated will be:
78::CODE;;treeview.width - treeview.indent_start - treeview.indent_level * node.level
79::CODE;;You might have some trouble with that. It is the developer's responsibility to
80::CODE;;correctly handle adapting the graphical representation nodes, if needed.
81::CODE;;'''
82::CODE;;from kivy.clock import Clock

84::CODE;;from kivy.uix.widget import Widget

215::CODE;;def add_node(self, node, parent=None):
216::CODE;;'''Add a new node to the tree.
217::CODE;;:Parameters:
218::CODE;;`node`: instance of a :class:`TreeViewNode`
219::CODE;;Node to add into the tree
220::CODE;;`parent`: instance of a :class:`TreeViewNode`, defaults to None
221::CODE;;Parent node to attach the new node. If `None`, it is added to
222::CODE;;the :attr:`root` node.
223::CODE;;:returns:
224::CODE;;the node `node`.
225::CODE;;'''
227::CODE;;if not isinstance(node, TreeViewNode):
228::CODE;;raise TreeViewException(
229::CODE;;'The node must be a subclass of TreeViewNode')
231::CODE;;if parent is None and self._root:
232::CODE;;parent = self._root
233::CODE;;if parent:
234::CODE;;parent.is_leaf = False
235::CODE;;parent.nodes.append(node)
236::CODE;;node.parent_node = parent
237::CODE;;node.level = parent.level + 1
238::CODE;;node.fbind('size', self._trigger_layout)
239::CODE;;self._trigger_layout()
240::CODE;;return node
241::CODE;;def remove_node(self, node):
242::CODE;;'''Removes a node from the tree.
243::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.7
244::CODE;;:Parameters:
245::CODE;;`node`: instance of a :class:`TreeViewNode`
246::CODE;;Node to remove from the tree. If `node` is :attr:`root`, it is
247::CODE;;not removed.
248::CODE;;'''
250::CODE;;if not isinstance(node, TreeViewNode):
251::CODE;;raise TreeViewException(
252::CODE;;'The node must be a subclass of TreeViewNode')
253::CODE;;parent = node.parent_node
254::CODE;;if parent is not None:
255::CODE;;if node == self._selected_node:
256::CODE;;node.is_selected = False
257::CODE;;self._selected_node = None

259::CODE;;if node in nodes:

261::CODE;;parent.is_leaf = not bool(len(nodes))
262::CODE;;node.parent_node = None
263::CODE;;node.funbind('size', self._trigger_layout)
264::CODE;;self._trigger_layout()

285::CODE;;def toggle_node(self, node):
286::CODE;;'''Toggle the state of the node (open/collapsed).
287::CODE;;'''
288::CODE;;node.is_open = not node.is_open
289::CODE;;if node.is_open:
290::CODE;;if self.load_func and not node.is_loaded:
291::CODE;;self._do_node_load(node)
292::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_node_expand', node)
293::CODE;;else:
294::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_node_collapse', node)
295::CODE;;self._trigger_layout()
296::CODE;;def get_node_at_pos(self, pos):
297::CODE;;'''Get the node at the position (x, y).
298::CODE;;'''
299::CODE;;x, y = pos
300::CODE;;for node in self.iterate_open_nodes(self.root):
301::CODE;;if self.x <= x <= self.right and \
302::CODE;;node.y <= y <= node.top:
303::CODE;;return node
304::CODE;;def iterate_open_nodes(self, node=None):
305::CODE;;'''Generator to iterate over all the expended nodes starting from
306::CODE;;`node` and down. If `node` is `None`, the generator start with
307::CODE;;:attr:`root`.
308::CODE;;To get all the open nodes::
309::CODE;;treeview = TreeView()
311::CODE;;for node in treeview.iterate_open_nodes():
312::CODE;;print(node)
313::CODE;;'''
314::CODE;;if not node:
315::CODE;;node = self.root
316::CODE;;if self.hide_root and node is self.root:
317::CODE;;pass
318::CODE;;else:
319::CODE;;yield node
320::CODE;;if not node.is_open:
321::CODE;;return
322::CODE;;f = self.iterate_open_nodes
323::CODE;;for cnode in node.nodes:
324::CODE;;for ynode in f(cnode):
325::CODE;;yield ynode
326::CODE;;def iterate_all_nodes(self, node=None):
327::CODE;;'''Generator to iterate over all nodes from `node` and down whether
328::CODE;;expanded or not. If `node` is `None`, the generator start with
329::CODE;;:attr:`root`.
330::CODE;;'''
331::CODE;;if not node:
332::CODE;;node = self.root
333::CODE;;yield node
334::CODE;;f = self.iterate_all_nodes
335::CODE;;for cnode in node.nodes:
336::CODE;;for ynode in f(cnode):
337::CODE;;yield ynode
341::CODE;;def on_load_func(self, instance, value):
342::CODE;;if value:
343::CODE;;Clock.schedule_once(self._do_initial_load)
344::CODE;;def _do_initial_load(self, *largs):
345::CODE;;if not self.load_func:
346::CODE;;return

3::CODE;;=====

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Video player
3::CODE;;============
4::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.2.0
5::CODE;;The video player widget can be used to play video and let the user control the
6::CODE;;play/pausing, volume and position. The widget cannot be customized much because
7::CODE;;of the complex assembly of numerous base widgets.
8::CODE;;.. image:: images/videoplayer.jpg
9::CODE;;:align: center
10::CODE;;Annotations
11::CODE;;-----------
12::CODE;;If you want to display text at a specific time and for a certain duration,
13::CODE;;consider annotations. An annotation file has a ".jsa" extension. The player
14::CODE;;will automatically load the associated annotation file if it exists.
15::CODE;;An annotation file is JSON-based, providing a list of label dictionary items.
16::CODE;;The key and value must match one of the :class:`VideoPlayerAnnotation` items.
17::CODE;;For example, here is a short version of a jsa file that you can find in
18::CODE;;`examples/widgets/cityCC0.jsa`::
19::CODE;;[
20::CODE;;{"start": 0, "duration": 2,
21::CODE;;"text": "This is an example of annotation"},
22::CODE;;{"start": 2, "duration": 2,
23::CODE;;"bgcolor": [0.5, 0.2, 0.4, 0.5],
24::CODE;;"text": "You can change the background color"}
25::CODE;;]
26::CODE;;For our cityCC0.mpg example, the result will be:
27::CODE;;.. image:: images/videoplayer-annotation.jpg
28::CODE;;:align: center
29::CODE;;If you want to experiment with annotation files, test with::
30::CODE;;python -m kivy.uix.videoplayer examples/widgets/cityCC0.mpg
31::CODE;;Fullscreen
32::CODE;;----------
33::CODE;;The video player can play the video in fullscreen, if
34::CODE;;:attr:`VideoPlayer.allow_fullscreen` is activated by a double-tap on
35::CODE;;the video. By default, if the video is smaller than the Window, it will be not
36::CODE;;stretched.
37::CODE;;You can allow stretching by passing custom options to a
38::CODE;;:class:`VideoPlayer` instance::
39::CODE;;player = VideoPlayer(source='myvideo.avi', state='play',
40::CODE;;options={'fit_mode': 'contain'})
41::CODE;;End-of-stream behavior
42::CODE;;----------------------
43::CODE;;You can specify what happens when the video has finished playing by passing an
44::CODE;;`eos` (end of stream) directive to the underlying
45::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.core.video.VideoBase` class. `eos` can be one of 'stop', 'pause'
46::CODE;;or 'loop' and defaults to 'stop'. For example, in order to loop the video::
47::CODE;;player = VideoPlayer(source='myvideo.avi', state='play',
48::CODE;;options={'eos': 'loop'})
49::CODE;;.. note::
50::CODE;;The `eos` property of the VideoBase class is a string specifying the
51::CODE;;end-of-stream behavior. This property differs from the `eos`
52::CODE;;properties of the :class:`VideoPlayer` and
53::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.video.Video` classes, whose `eos`
54::CODE;;property is simply a boolean indicating that the end of the file has
55::CODE;;been reached.
56::CODE;;'''
57::CODE;;__all__ = ('VideoPlayer', 'VideoPlayerAnnotation')
58::CODE;;from json import load
59::CODE;;from os.path import exists
60::CODE;;from kivy.properties import ObjectProperty, StringProperty, BooleanProperty, \
61::CODE;;NumericProperty, DictProperty, OptionProperty

63::CODE;;from kivy.uix.gridlayout import GridLayout
64::CODE;;from kivy.uix.floatlayout import FloatLayout

76::CODE;;return False

80::CODE;;return True

83::CODE;;return

93::CODE;;return

96::CODE;;if dy < 10:

98::CODE;;self.video.volume = 0

100::CODE;;self.video.volume = 1.

1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;VKeyboard
3::CODE;;=========
4::CODE;;.. image:: images/vkeyboard.jpg
5::CODE;;:align: right
6::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.8
7::CODE;;VKeyboard is an onscreen keyboard for Kivy. Its operation is intended to be
8::CODE;;transparent to the user. Using the widget directly is NOT recommended. Read the
9::CODE;;section `Request keyboard`_ first.
10::CODE;;Modes
11::CODE;;-----
12::CODE;;This virtual keyboard has a docked and free mode:
13::CODE;;* docked mode (:attr:`VKeyboard.docked` = True)
14::CODE;;Generally used when only one person is using the computer, like a tablet or
15::CODE;;personal computer etc.
16::CODE;;* free mode: (:attr:`VKeyboard.docked` = False)
17::CODE;;Mostly for multitouch surfaces. This mode allows multiple virtual
18::CODE;;keyboards to be used on the screen.
19::CODE;;If the docked mode changes, you need to manually call
20::CODE;;:meth:`VKeyboard.setup_mode` otherwise the change will have no impact.
21::CODE;;During that call, the VKeyboard, implemented on top of a
22::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.uix.scatter.Scatter`, will change the
23::CODE;;behavior of the scatter and position the keyboard near the target (if target
24::CODE;;and docked mode is set).
25::CODE;;Layouts
26::CODE;;-------
27::CODE;;The virtual keyboard is able to load a custom layout. If you create a new
28::CODE;;layout and put the JSON in :file:`<kivy_data_dir>/keyboards/<layoutid>.json`,
29::CODE;;you can load it by setting :attr:`VKeyboard.layout` to your layoutid.
30::CODE;;The JSON must be structured like this::
31::CODE;;{
32::CODE;;"title": "Title of your layout",
33::CODE;;"description": "Description of your layout",
34::CODE;;"cols": 15,
35::CODE;;"rows": 5,
36::CODE;;...
37::CODE;;}
38::CODE;;Then, you need to describe the keys in each row, for either a "normal",
39::CODE;;"shift" or a "special" (added in version 1.9.0) mode. Keys for this row
40::CODE;;data must be named `normal_<row>`, `shift_<row>` and `special_<row>`.
41::CODE;;Replace `row` with the row number.
42::CODE;;Inside each row, you will describe the key. A key is a 4 element list in
43::CODE;;the format::
44::CODE;;[ <text displayed on the keyboard>, <text to put when the key is pressed>,
45::CODE;;<text that represents the keycode>, <size of cols> ]
46::CODE;;Here are example keys::
48::CODE;;["f", "f", "f", 1]
50::CODE;;["\u21B9", "\t", "tab", 1.5]
51::CODE;;Finally, complete the JSON::
52::CODE;;{
53::CODE;;...
54::CODE;;"normal_1": [
55::CODE;;["`", "`", "`", 1], ["1", "1", "1", 1], ["2", "2", "2", 1],
56::CODE;;["3", "3", "3", 1], ["4", "4", "4", 1], ["5", "5", "5", 1],
57::CODE;;["6", "6", "6", 1], ["7", "7", "7", 1], ["8", "8", "8", 1],
58::CODE;;["9", "9", "9", 1], ["0", "0", "0", 1], ["+", "+", "+", 1],
59::CODE;;["=", "=", "=", 1], ["\u232b", null, "backspace", 2]
60::CODE;;],
61::CODE;;"shift_1": [ ... ],
62::CODE;;"normal_2": [ ... ],
63::CODE;;"special_2": [ ... ],
64::CODE;;...
65::CODE;;}
66::CODE;;Request Keyboard
67::CODE;;----------------
68::CODE;;The instantiation of the virtual keyboard is controlled by the configuration.
69::CODE;;Check `keyboard_mode` and `keyboard_layout` in the :doc:`api-kivy.config`.
70::CODE;;If you intend to create a widget that requires a keyboard, do not use the
71::CODE;;virtual keyboard directly, but prefer to use the best method available on
72::CODE;;the platform. Check the :meth:`~kivy.core.window.WindowBase.request_keyboard`
73::CODE;;method in the :doc:`api-kivy.core.window`.
74::CODE;;If you want a specific layout when you request the keyboard, you should write
75::CODE;;something like this (from 1.8.0, numeric.json can be in the same directory as
76::CODE;;your main.py)::
77::CODE;;keyboard = Window.request_keyboard(
78::CODE;;self._keyboard_close, self)
79::CODE;;if keyboard.widget:
80::CODE;;vkeyboard = self._keyboard.widget
81::CODE;;vkeyboard.layout = 'numeric.json'
82::CODE;;'''
83::CODE;;__all__ = ('VKeyboard', )

101::CODE;;class VKeyboard(Scatter):
102::CODE;;'''
103::CODE;;VKeyboard is an onscreen keyboard with multitouch support.
104::CODE;;Its layout is entirely customizable and you can switch between available
105::CODE;;layouts using a button in the bottom right of the widget.
106::CODE;;:Events:
107::CODE;;`on_key_down`: keycode, internal, modifiers
108::CODE;;Fired when the keyboard received a key down event (key press).
109::CODE;;`on_key_up`: keycode, internal, modifiers
110::CODE;;Fired when the keyboard received a key up event (key release).
111::CODE;;'''
112::CODE;;target = ObjectProperty(None, allownone=True)
113::CODE;;'''Target widget associated with the VKeyboard. If set, it will be used to
114::CODE;;send keyboard events. If the VKeyboard mode is "free", it will also be used
115::CODE;;to set the initial position.
116::CODE;;:attr:`target` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.ObjectProperty` instance and
117::CODE;;defaults to None.
118::CODE;;'''
119::CODE;;callback = ObjectProperty(None, allownone=True)
120::CODE;;'''Callback can be set to a function that will be called if the
121::CODE;;VKeyboard is closed by the user.
122::CODE;;:attr:`target` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.ObjectProperty` instance and
123::CODE;;defaults to None.
124::CODE;;'''
125::CODE;;layout = StringProperty(None)
126::CODE;;'''Layout to use for the VKeyboard. By default, it will be the
127::CODE;;layout set in the configuration, according to the `keyboard_layout`
128::CODE;;in `[kivy]` section.
129::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.8.0
130::CODE;;If layout is a .json filename, it will loaded and added to the
131::CODE;;available_layouts.
132::CODE;;:attr:`layout` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.StringProperty` and defaults
133::CODE;;to None.
134::CODE;;'''
135::CODE;;layout_path = StringProperty(default_layout_path)
136::CODE;;'''Path from which layouts are read.
137::CODE;;:attr:`layout` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.StringProperty` and
138::CODE;;defaults to :file:`<kivy_data_dir>/keyboards/`
139::CODE;;'''
140::CODE;;available_layouts = DictProperty({})
141::CODE;;'''Dictionary of all available layouts. Keys are the layout ID, and the
142::CODE;;value is the JSON (translated into a Python object).
143::CODE;;:attr:`available_layouts` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.DictProperty` and
144::CODE;;defaults to {}.

686::CODE;;self._start_repeat_key, 0.5)
687::CODE;;self.repeat_touch = touch
688::CODE;;self.process_key_on(touch)
689::CODE;;touch.grab(self, exclusive=True)
690::CODE;;else:
691::CODE;;super(VKeyboard, self).on_touch_down(touch)
692::CODE;;return True
693::CODE;;def on_touch_up(self, touch):
694::CODE;;if touch.grab_current is self:
695::CODE;;self.process_key_up(touch)
696::CODE;;if self._start_repeat_key_ev is not None:
697::CODE;;self._start_repeat_key_ev.cancel()
698::CODE;;self._start_repeat_key_ev = None
699::CODE;;if touch == self.repeat_touch:
700::CODE;;if self._repeat_key_ev is not None:
701::CODE;;self._repeat_key_ev.cancel()
702::CODE;;self._repeat_key_ev = None
703::CODE;;self.repeat_touch = None
704::CODE;;return super(VKeyboard, self).on_touch_up(touch)
705::CODE;;if __name__ == '__main__':
706::CODE;;from kivy.base import runTouchApp
707::CODE;;vk = VKeyboard(layout='azerty')
708::CODE;;runTouchApp(vk)
1::CODE;;'''
2::CODE;;Widget class
3::CODE;;============
4::CODE;;The :class:`Widget` class is the base class required for creating Widgets.
5::CODE;;This widget class was designed with a couple of principles in mind:
6::CODE;;* *Event Driven*
7::CODE;;Widget interaction is built on top of events that occur. If a property
8::CODE;;changes, the widget can respond to the change in the 'on_<propname>'
9::CODE;;callback. If nothing changes, nothing will be done. That's the main
10::CODE;;goal of the :class:`~kivy.properties.Property` class.
11::CODE;;* *Separation Of Concerns (the widget and its graphical representation)*
12::CODE;;Widgets don't have a `draw()` method. This is done on purpose: The idea
13::CODE;;is to allow you to create your own graphical representation outside the
14::CODE;;widget class.
15::CODE;;Obviously you can still use all the available properties to do that, so
16::CODE;;that your representation properly reflects the widget's current state.
17::CODE;;Every widget has its own :class:`~kivy.graphics.Canvas` that you
18::CODE;;can use to draw. This separation allows Kivy to run your
19::CODE;;application in a very efficient manner.
20::CODE;;* *Bounding Box / Collision*
21::CODE;;Often you want to know if a certain point is within the bounds of your
22::CODE;;widget. An example would be a button widget where you only want to
23::CODE;;trigger an action when the button itself is actually touched.
24::CODE;;For this, you can use the :meth:`~Widget.collide_point` method, which
25::CODE;;will return True if the point you pass to it is inside the axis-aligned
26::CODE;;bounding box defined by the widget's position and size.
27::CODE;;If a simple AABB is not sufficient, you can override the method to
28::CODE;;perform the collision checks with more complex shapes, e.g. a polygon.
29::CODE;;You can also check if a widget collides with another widget with
30::CODE;;:meth:`~Widget.collide_widget`.
31::CODE;;We also have some default values and behaviors that you should be aware of:
32::CODE;;* A :class:`Widget` is not a :class:`~kivy.uix.layout.Layout`: it will not
33::CODE;;change the position or the size of its children. If you want control over
34::CODE;;positioning or sizing, use a :class:`~kivy.uix.layout.Layout`.
35::CODE;;* The default size of a widget is (100, 100). This is only changed if the
36::CODE;;parent is a :class:`~kivy.uix.layout.Layout`.
37::CODE;;For example, if you add a :class:`Label` inside a
38::CODE;;:class:`Button`, the label will not inherit the button's size or position
39::CODE;;because the button is not a *Layout*: it's just another *Widget*.
40::CODE;;* The default size_hint is (1, 1). If the parent is a :class:`Layout`, then the
41::CODE;;widget size will be the parent layout's size.
42::CODE;;* :meth:`~Widget.on_touch_down`, :meth:`~Widget.on_touch_move`,
43::CODE;;:meth:`~Widget.on_touch_up` don't do any sort of collisions. If you want to
44::CODE;;know if the touch is inside your widget, use :meth:`~Widget.collide_point`.
45::CODE;;Using Properties
46::CODE;;----------------
47::CODE;;When you read the documentation, all properties are described in the format::
48::CODE;;<name> is a <property class> and defaults to <default value>.
49::CODE;;e.g.
50::CODE;;:attr:`~kivy.uix.label.Label.text` is a
51::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.properties.StringProperty` and defaults to ''.
52::CODE;;If you want to be notified when the pos attribute changes, i.e. when the
53::CODE;;widget moves, you can bind your own callback function like this::
54::CODE;;def callback_pos(instance, value):
55::CODE;;print('The widget', instance, 'moved to', value)
56::CODE;;wid = Widget()
57::CODE;;wid.bind(pos=callback_pos)
58::CODE;;Read more about :doc:`/api-kivy.properties`.
59::CODE;;Basic drawing
60::CODE;;-------------
61::CODE;;Widgets support a range of drawing instructions that you can use to customize
62::CODE;;the look of your widgets and layouts. For example, to draw a background image
63::CODE;;for your widget, you can do the following:
64::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
65::CODE;;def redraw(self, args):
66::CODE;;self.bg_rect.size = self.size
67::CODE;;self.bg_rect.pos = self.pos
68::CODE;;widget = Widget()
69::CODE;;with widget.canvas:
70::CODE;;widget.bg_rect = Rectangle(source="cover.jpg", pos=self.pos, \
71::CODE;;size=self.size)
72::CODE;;widget.bind(pos=redraw, size=redraw)
73::CODE;;To draw a background in kv:
74::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
75::CODE;;Widget:
76::CODE;;canvas:
77::CODE;;Rectangle:
78::CODE;;source: "cover.jpg"
79::CODE;;size: self.size
80::CODE;;pos: self.pos
81::CODE;;These examples only scratch the surface. Please see the :mod:`kivy.graphics`
82::CODE;;documentation for more information.
83::CODE;;.. _widget-event-bubbling:
84::CODE;;Widget touch event bubbling
85::CODE;;---------------------------
86::CODE;;When you catch touch events between multiple widgets, you often
87::CODE;;need to be aware of the order in which these events are propagated. In Kivy,
88::CODE;;events bubble up from the first child upwards through the other children.
89::CODE;;If a widget has children, the event is passed through its children before
90::CODE;;being passed on to the widget after it.
91::CODE;;As the :meth:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.add_widget` method inserts widgets at
92::CODE;;index 0 by default, this means the event goes from the most recently added
93::CODE;;widget back to the first one added. Consider the following:
94::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
95::CODE;;box = BoxLayout()
96::CODE;;box.add_widget(Label(text="a"))
97::CODE;;box.add_widget(Label(text="b"))
98::CODE;;box.add_widget(Label(text="c"))
99::CODE;;The label with text "c" gets the event first, "b" second and "a" last. You can
100::CODE;;reverse this order by manually specifying the index:
101::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
102::CODE;;box = BoxLayout()
103::CODE;;box.add_widget(Label(text="a"), index=0)
104::CODE;;box.add_widget(Label(text="b"), index=1)
105::CODE;;box.add_widget(Label(text="c"), index=2)
106::CODE;;Now the order would be "a", "b" then "c". One thing to keep in mind when using
107::CODE;;kv is that declaring a widget uses the
108::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.add_widget` method for insertion. Hence, using
109::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
110::CODE;;BoxLayout:
111::CODE;;MyLabel:
112::CODE;;text: "a"
113::CODE;;MyLabel:
114::CODE;;text: "b"
115::CODE;;MyLabel:
116::CODE;;text: "c"
117::CODE;;would result in the event order "c", "b" then "a" as "c" was actually the last
118::CODE;;added widget. It thus has index 0, "b" index 1 and "a" index 2. Effectively,
119::CODE;;the child order is the reverse of its listed order.
120::CODE;;This ordering is the same for the :meth:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.on_touch_move`
121::CODE;;and :meth:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.on_touch_up` events.
122::CODE;;In order to stop this event bubbling, a method can return `True`. This tells
123::CODE;;Kivy the event has been handled and the event propagation stops. For example:
124::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
125::CODE;;class MyWidget(Widget):
126::CODE;;def on_touch_down(self, touch):
127::CODE;;If <some_condition>:
129::CODE;;return True
130::CODE;;else:
131::CODE;;return super(MyWidget, self).on_touch_down(touch)
132::CODE;;This approach gives you good control over exactly how events are dispatched
133::CODE;;and managed. Sometimes, however, you may wish to let the event be completely
134::CODE;;propagated before taking action. You can use the
135::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.clock.Clock` to help you here:
136::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
137::CODE;;class MyWidget(Label):
138::CODE;;def on_touch_down(self, touch, after=False):
139::CODE;;if after:
140::CODE;;print "Fired after the event has been dispatched!"
141::CODE;;else:
142::CODE;;Clock.schedule_once(lambda dt: self.on_touch_down(touch, True))
143::CODE;;return super(MyWidget, self).on_touch_down(touch)
144::CODE;;Usage of :attr:`Widget.center`, :attr:`Widget.right`, and :attr:`Widget.top`
145::CODE;;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
146::CODE;;A common mistake when using one of the computed properties such as
147::CODE;;:attr:`Widget.right` is to use it to make a widget follow its parent with a
148::CODE;;KV rule such as `right: self.parent.right`. Consider, for example:
149::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
150::CODE;;FloatLayout:
151::CODE;;id: layout
152::CODE;;width: 100
153::CODE;;Widget:
154::CODE;;id: wid
155::CODE;;right: layout.right
156::CODE;;The (mistaken) expectation is that this rule ensures that wid's right will
157::CODE;;always be whatever layout's right is - that is wid.right and layout.right will
158::CODE;;always be identical. In actual fact, this rule only says that "whenever
159::CODE;;layout's `right` changes, wid's right will be set to that value". The
160::CODE;;difference being that as long as `layout.right` doesn't change, `wid.right`
161::CODE;;could be anything, even a value that will make them different.
162::CODE;;Specifically, for the KV code above, consider the following example::
163::CODE;;>>> print(layout.right, wid.right)
164::CODE;;(100, 100)
165::CODE;;>>> wid.x = 200
166::CODE;;>>> print(layout.right, wid.right)
167::CODE;;(100, 300)
168::CODE;;As can be seen, initially they are in sync, however, when we change `wid.x`
169::CODE;;they go out of sync because `layout.right` is not changed and the rule is not
170::CODE;;triggered.
171::CODE;;The proper way to make the widget follow its parent's right is to use
172::CODE;;:attr:`Widget.pos_hint`. If instead of `right: layout.right` we did
173::CODE;;`pos_hint: {'right': 1}`, then the widgets right will always be set to be
174::CODE;;at the parent's right at each layout update.
175::CODE;;'''

220::CODE;;class Widget(WidgetBase):
221::CODE;;'''Widget class. See module documentation for more information.
222::CODE;;:Events:
223::CODE;;`on_touch_down`: `(touch, )`
224::CODE;;Fired when a new touch event occurs. `touch` is the touch object.
225::CODE;;`on_touch_move`: `(touch, )`
226::CODE;;Fired when an existing touch moves. `touch` is the touch object.
227::CODE;;`on_touch_up`: `(touch, )`
228::CODE;;Fired when an existing touch disappears. `touch` is the touch
229::CODE;;object.
230::CODE;;`on_kv_post`: `(base_widget, )`
231::CODE;;Fired after all the kv rules associated with the widget
232::CODE;;and all other widgets that are in any of those rules have had
233::CODE;;all their kv rules applied. `base_widget` is the base-most widget
234::CODE;;whose instantiation triggered the kv rules (i.e. the widget
235::CODE;;instantiated from Python, e.g. ``MyWidget()``).
236::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.11.0
237::CODE;;.. warning::
238::CODE;;Adding a `__del__` method to a class derived from Widget with Python
239::CODE;;prior to 3.4 will disable automatic garbage collection for instances
240::CODE;;of that class. This is because the Widget class creates reference
241::CODE;;cycles, thereby `preventing garbage collection
243::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.0.9
244::CODE;;Everything related to event properties has been moved to the
245::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.event.EventDispatcher`. Event properties can now be used
246::CODE;;when constructing a simple class without subclassing :class:`Widget`.
247::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.5.0
248::CODE;;The constructor now accepts on_* arguments to automatically bind
249::CODE;;callbacks to properties or events, as in the Kv language.
250::CODE;;'''
251::CODE;;__metaclass__ = WidgetMetaclass
252::CODE;;__events__ = (
253::CODE;;'on_motion', 'on_touch_down', 'on_touch_move', 'on_touch_up',
254::CODE;;'on_kv_post'
255::CODE;;)
256::CODE;;_proxy_ref = None
257::CODE;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
259::CODE;;EventLoop.ensure_window()
261::CODE;;if not hasattr(self, '_context'):
262::CODE;;self._context = get_current_context()
263::CODE;;no_builder = '__no_builder' in kwargs
264::CODE;;self._disabled_value = False
265::CODE;;if no_builder:
266::CODE;;del kwargs['__no_builder']
267::CODE;;on_args = {k: v for k, v in kwargs.items() if k[:3] == 'on_'}
268::CODE;;for key in on_args:
269::CODE;;del kwargs[key]
270::CODE;;self._disabled_count = 0
271::CODE;;super(Widget, self).__init__(**kwargs)
273::CODE;;if self.canvas is None:
274::CODE;;self.canvas = Canvas(opacity=self.opacity)
276::CODE;;if not no_builder:
277::CODE;;rule_children = []
278::CODE;;self.apply_class_lang_rules(
279::CODE;;ignored_consts=self._kwargs_applied_init,
280::CODE;;rule_children=rule_children)
281::CODE;;for widget in rule_children:
282::CODE;;widget.dispatch('on_kv_post', self)
283::CODE;;self.dispatch('on_kv_post', self)
285::CODE;;if on_args:
286::CODE;;self.bind(**on_args)
287::CODE;;@property
288::CODE;;def proxy_ref(self):
289::CODE;;'''Return a proxy reference to the widget, i.e. without creating a
290::CODE;;reference to the widget. See `weakref.proxy
291::CODE;;<http://docs.python.org/2/library/weakref.html?highlight\
293::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.7.2
294::CODE;;'''
295::CODE;;_proxy_ref = self._proxy_ref
296::CODE;;if _proxy_ref is not None:
297::CODE;;return _proxy_ref
298::CODE;;f = partial(_widget_destructor, self.uid)
299::CODE;;self._proxy_ref = _proxy_ref = WeakProxy(self, f)
303::CODE;;_widget_destructors[self.uid] = (f, _proxy_ref)
304::CODE;;return _proxy_ref
305::CODE;;def __hash__(self):
306::CODE;;return id(self)
307::CODE;;def apply_class_lang_rules(
308::CODE;;self, root=None, ignored_consts=set(), rule_children=None):
309::CODE;;'''
310::CODE;;Method that is called by kivy to apply the kv rules of this widget's
311::CODE;;class.
312::CODE;;:Parameters:
313::CODE;;`root`: :class:`Widget`
314::CODE;;The root widget that instantiated this widget in kv, if the
315::CODE;;widget was instantiated in kv, otherwise ``None``.
316::CODE;;`ignored_consts`: set
317::CODE;;(internal) See :meth:`~kivy.lang.builder.BuilderBase.apply`.
318::CODE;;`rule_children`: list
319::CODE;;(internal) See :meth:`~kivy.lang.builder.BuilderBase.apply`.
320::CODE;;This is useful to be able to execute code before/after the class kv
321::CODE;;rules are applied to the widget. E.g. if the kv code requires some
322::CODE;;properties to be initialized before it is used in a binding rule.
323::CODE;;If overwriting remember to call ``super``, otherwise the kv rules will
324::CODE;;not be applied.
325::CODE;;In the following example,
326::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
327::CODE;;class MyWidget(Widget):
328::CODE;;pass
329::CODE;;class OtherWidget(MyWidget):
330::CODE;;pass
331::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
332::CODE;;<MyWidget>:
333::CODE;;my_prop: some_value
334::CODE;;<OtherWidget>:
335::CODE;;other_prop: some_value
336::CODE;;When ``OtherWidget`` is instantiated with ``OtherWidget()``, the
337::CODE;;widget's :meth:`apply_class_lang_rules` is called and it applies the
338::CODE;;kv rules of this class - ``<MyWidget>`` and ``<OtherWidget>``.
339::CODE;;Similarly, when the widget is instantiated from kv, e.g.
340::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
341::CODE;;<MyBox@BoxLayout>:
342::CODE;;height: 55
343::CODE;;OtherWidget:
344::CODE;;width: 124
345::CODE;;``OtherWidget``'s :meth:`apply_class_lang_rules` is called and it
346::CODE;;applies the kv rules of this class - ``<MyWidget>`` and
347::CODE;;``<OtherWidget>``.
348::CODE;;.. note::
349::CODE;;It applies only the class rules not the instance rules. I.e. in the
350::CODE;;above kv example in the ``MyBox`` rule when ``OtherWidget`` is
351::CODE;;instantiated, its :meth:`apply_class_lang_rules` applies the
352::CODE;;``<MyWidget>`` and ``<OtherWidget>`` rules to it - it does not
353::CODE;;apply the ``width: 124`` rule. The ``width: 124`` rule is part of
354::CODE;;the ``MyBox`` rule and is applied by the ``MyBox``'s instance's
355::CODE;;:meth:`apply_class_lang_rules`.
356::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.11.0
357::CODE;;'''
358::CODE;;Builder.apply(
359::CODE;;self, ignored_consts=ignored_consts,
360::CODE;;rule_children=rule_children)
364::CODE;;def collide_point(self, x, y):
365::CODE;;'''
366::CODE;;Check if a point (x, y) is inside the widget's axis aligned bounding
367::CODE;;box.
368::CODE;;:Parameters:
369::CODE;;`x`: numeric
370::CODE;;x position of the point (in parent coordinates)
371::CODE;;`y`: numeric
372::CODE;;y position of the point (in parent coordinates)
373::CODE;;:Returns:
374::CODE;;A bool. True if the point is inside the bounding box, False
375::CODE;;otherwise.
376::CODE;;.. code-block:: python-console
377::CODE;;>>> Widget(pos=(10, 10), size=(50, 50)).collide_point(40, 40)
378::CODE;;True
379::CODE;;'''
380::CODE;;return self.x <= x <= self.right and self.y <= y <= self.top
381::CODE;;def collide_widget(self, wid):
382::CODE;;'''
383::CODE;;Check if another widget collides with this widget. This function
384::CODE;;performs an axis-aligned bounding box intersection test by default.
385::CODE;;:Parameters:
386::CODE;;`wid`: :class:`Widget` class
387::CODE;;Widget to test collision with.
388::CODE;;:Returns:
389::CODE;;bool. True if the other widget collides with this widget, False
390::CODE;;otherwise.
391::CODE;;.. code-block:: python-console
392::CODE;;>>> wid = Widget(size=(50, 50))
393::CODE;;>>> wid2 = Widget(size=(50, 50), pos=(25, 25))
394::CODE;;>>> wid.collide_widget(wid2)
395::CODE;;True
396::CODE;;>>> wid2.pos = (55, 55)
397::CODE;;>>> wid.collide_widget(wid2)
398::CODE;;False
399::CODE;;'''
400::CODE;;if self.right < wid.x:
401::CODE;;return False
402::CODE;;if self.x > wid.right:
403::CODE;;return False
404::CODE;;if self.top < wid.y:
405::CODE;;return False
406::CODE;;if self.y > wid.top:
407::CODE;;return False
408::CODE;;return True
409::CODE;;def on_motion(self, etype, me):
410::CODE;;'''Called when a motion event is received.
411::CODE;;:Parameters:
412::CODE;;`etype`: `str`
413::CODE;;Event type, one of "begin", "update" or "end"
414::CODE;;`me`: :class:`~kivy.input.motionevent.MotionEvent`
415::CODE;;Received motion event
416::CODE;;:Returns: `bool`
417::CODE;;`True` to stop event dispatching
418::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 2.1.0
419::CODE;;.. warning::
420::CODE;;This is an experimental method and it remains so while this warning
421::CODE;;is present.
422::CODE;;'''
423::CODE;;if self.disabled or me.dispatch_mode == MODE_DONT_DISPATCH:
424::CODE;;return
425::CODE;;if me.type_id not in self.motion_filter:
426::CODE;;return
427::CODE;;filtered = self.motion_filter[me.type_id]
428::CODE;;if filtered[0] is self and len(filtered) == 1:
429::CODE;;return
430::CODE;;if me.dispatch_mode == MODE_DEFAULT_DISPATCH:
431::CODE;;last_filtered = filtered[-1]
432::CODE;;for widget in self.children[:]:
433::CODE;;if widget.dispatch('on_motion', etype, me):
434::CODE;;return True
435::CODE;;if widget is last_filtered:
436::CODE;;return
437::CODE;;if me.dispatch_mode == MODE_FILTERED_DISPATCH:
438::CODE;;widgets = filtered[1:] if filtered[0] is self else filtered[:]
439::CODE;;for widget in widgets:
440::CODE;;if widget.dispatch('on_motion', etype, me):
441::CODE;;return True
445::CODE;;def on_touch_down(self, touch):
446::CODE;;'''Receive a touch down event.
447::CODE;;:Parameters:
448::CODE;;`touch`: :class:`~kivy.input.motionevent.MotionEvent` class
449::CODE;;Touch received. The touch is in parent coordinates. See
450::CODE;;:mod:`~kivy.uix.relativelayout` for a discussion on
451::CODE;;coordinate systems.
452::CODE;;:Returns: bool
453::CODE;;If True, the dispatching of the touch event will stop.
454::CODE;;If False, the event will continue to be dispatched to the rest
455::CODE;;of the widget tree.
456::CODE;;'''
457::CODE;;if self.disabled and self.collide_point(*touch.pos):
458::CODE;;return True
459::CODE;;for child in self.children[:]:
460::CODE;;if child.dispatch('on_touch_down', touch):
461::CODE;;return True
462::CODE;;def on_touch_move(self, touch):
463::CODE;;'''Receive a touch move event. The touch is in parent coordinates.
464::CODE;;See :meth:`on_touch_down` for more information.
465::CODE;;'''
466::CODE;;if self.disabled:
467::CODE;;return
468::CODE;;for child in self.children[:]:
469::CODE;;if child.dispatch('on_touch_move', touch):
470::CODE;;return True
471::CODE;;def on_touch_up(self, touch):
472::CODE;;'''Receive a touch up event. The touch is in parent coordinates.
473::CODE;;See :meth:`on_touch_down` for more information.
474::CODE;;'''
475::CODE;;if self.disabled:
476::CODE;;return
477::CODE;;for child in self.children[:]:
478::CODE;;if child.dispatch('on_touch_up', touch):
479::CODE;;return True
480::CODE;;def on_kv_post(self, base_widget):
481::CODE;;pass
485::CODE;;def add_widget(self, widget, index=0, canvas=None):
486::CODE;;'''Add a new widget as a child of this widget.
487::CODE;;:Parameters:
488::CODE;;`widget`: :class:`Widget`
489::CODE;;Widget to add to our list of children.
490::CODE;;`index`: int, defaults to 0
491::CODE;;Index to insert the widget in the list. Notice that the default
492::CODE;;of 0 means the widget is inserted at the beginning of the list
493::CODE;;and will thus be drawn on top of other sibling widgets. For a
494::CODE;;full discussion of the index and widget hierarchy, please see
495::CODE;;the :doc:`Widgets Programming Guide <guide/widgets>`.
496::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.5
497::CODE;;`canvas`: str, defaults to None
498::CODE;;Canvas to add widget's canvas to. Can be 'before', 'after' or
499::CODE;;None for the default canvas.
500::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.9.0
501::CODE;;.. code-block:: python-console
502::CODE;;>>> from kivy.uix.button import Button
503::CODE;;>>> from kivy.uix.slider import Slider
504::CODE;;>>> root = Widget()
505::CODE;;>>> root.add_widget(Button())
506::CODE;;>>> slider = Slider()
507::CODE;;>>> root.add_widget(slider)
508::CODE;;'''
509::CODE;;if not isinstance(widget, Widget):
510::CODE;;raise WidgetException(
511::CODE;;'add_widget() can be used only with instances'
512::CODE;;' of the Widget class.')
513::CODE;;widget = widget.__self__
514::CODE;;if widget is self:
515::CODE;;raise WidgetException(
516::CODE;;'Widget instances cannot be added to themselves.')
517::CODE;;parent = widget.parent
519::CODE;;if parent:
520::CODE;;raise WidgetException('Cannot add %r, it already has a parent %r'
521::CODE;;% (widget, parent))
522::CODE;;widget.parent = parent = self
524::CODE;;widget.inc_disabled(self._disabled_count)
525::CODE;;canvas = self.canvas.before if canvas == 'before' else \
526::CODE;;self.canvas.after if canvas == 'after' else self.canvas
527::CODE;;if index == 0 or len(self.children) == 0:
528::CODE;;self.children.insert(0, widget)
529::CODE;;canvas.add(widget.canvas)
530::CODE;;else:
531::CODE;;canvas = self.canvas
532::CODE;;children = self.children
533::CODE;;if index >= len(children):
534::CODE;;index = len(children)
535::CODE;;next_index = canvas.indexof(children[-1].canvas)
536::CODE;;else:
537::CODE;;next_child = children[index]
538::CODE;;next_index = canvas.indexof(next_child.canvas)
539::CODE;;if next_index == -1:
540::CODE;;next_index = canvas.length()
541::CODE;;else:
542::CODE;;next_index += 1
543::CODE;;children.insert(index, widget)
545::CODE;;if next_index == 0 and canvas.has_before:
546::CODE;;next_index = 1
547::CODE;;canvas.insert(next_index, widget.canvas)
548::CODE;;for type_id in widget.motion_filter:
549::CODE;;self.register_for_motion_event(type_id, widget)
550::CODE;;widget.fbind('motion_filter', self._update_motion_filter)
551::CODE;;def remove_widget(self, widget):
552::CODE;;'''Remove a widget from the children of this widget.
553::CODE;;:Parameters:
554::CODE;;`widget`: :class:`Widget`
555::CODE;;Widget to remove from our children list.
556::CODE;;.. code-block:: python-console
557::CODE;;>>> from kivy.uix.button import Button
558::CODE;;>>> root = Widget()
559::CODE;;>>> button = Button()
560::CODE;;>>> root.add_widget(button)
561::CODE;;>>> root.remove_widget(button)
562::CODE;;'''
563::CODE;;if widget not in self.children:
564::CODE;;return
565::CODE;;self.children.remove(widget)
566::CODE;;if widget.canvas in self.canvas.children:
567::CODE;;self.canvas.remove(widget.canvas)
568::CODE;;elif widget.canvas in self.canvas.after.children:
569::CODE;;self.canvas.after.remove(widget.canvas)
570::CODE;;elif widget.canvas in self.canvas.before.children:
571::CODE;;self.canvas.before.remove(widget.canvas)
572::CODE;;for type_id in widget.motion_filter:
573::CODE;;self.unregister_for_motion_event(type_id, widget)
574::CODE;;widget.funbind('motion_filter', self._update_motion_filter)
575::CODE;;widget.parent = None
576::CODE;;widget.dec_disabled(self._disabled_count)
577::CODE;;def clear_widgets(self, children=None):
578::CODE;;'''
579::CODE;;Remove all (or the specified) :attr:`~Widget.children` of this widget.
580::CODE;;If the 'children' argument is specified, it should be a list (or
581::CODE;;filtered list) of children of the current widget.
582::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.8.0
583::CODE;;The `children` argument can be used to specify the children you
584::CODE;;want to remove.
585::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 2.1.0
586::CODE;;Specifying an empty ``children`` list leaves the widgets unchanged.
587::CODE;;Previously it was treated like ``None`` and all children were
588::CODE;;removed.
589::CODE;;'''
590::CODE;;if children is None or children is self.children:
591::CODE;;children = self.children[:]
592::CODE;;remove_widget = self.remove_widget
593::CODE;;for child in children:
594::CODE;;remove_widget(child)
595::CODE;;def _update_motion_filter(self, child_widget, child_motion_filter):
596::CODE;;old_events = []
597::CODE;;for type_id, widgets in self.motion_filter.items():
598::CODE;;if child_widget in widgets:
599::CODE;;old_events.append(type_id)
600::CODE;;for type_id in old_events:
601::CODE;;if type_id not in child_motion_filter:
602::CODE;;self.unregister_for_motion_event(type_id, child_widget)
603::CODE;;for type_id in child_motion_filter:
604::CODE;;if type_id not in old_events:
605::CODE;;self.register_for_motion_event(type_id, child_widget)
606::CODE;;def _find_index_in_motion_filter(self, type_id, widget):
607::CODE;;if widget is self:
608::CODE;;return 0
609::CODE;;find_index = self.children.index
610::CODE;;max_index = find_index(widget) + 1
611::CODE;;motion_widgets = self.motion_filter[type_id]
612::CODE;;insert_index = 1 if motion_widgets[0] is self else 0
613::CODE;;for index in range(insert_index, len(motion_widgets)):
614::CODE;;if find_index(motion_widgets[index]) < max_index:
615::CODE;;insert_index += 1
616::CODE;;else:
617::CODE;;break
618::CODE;;return insert_index
619::CODE;;def register_for_motion_event(self, type_id, widget=None):
620::CODE;;'''Register to receive motion events of `type_id`.
621::CODE;;Override :meth:`on_motion` or bind to `on_motion` event to handle
622::CODE;;the incoming motion events.
623::CODE;;:Parameters:
624::CODE;;`type_id`: `str`
625::CODE;;Motion event type id (eg. "touch", "hover", etc.)
626::CODE;;`widget`: `Widget`
627::CODE;;Child widget or `self` if omitted
628::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 2.1.0
629::CODE;;.. note::
630::CODE;;Method can be called multiple times with the same arguments.
631::CODE;;.. warning::
632::CODE;;This is an experimental method and it remains so while this warning
633::CODE;;is present.
634::CODE;;'''
635::CODE;;a_widget = widget or self
636::CODE;;motion_filter = self.motion_filter
637::CODE;;if type_id not in motion_filter:
638::CODE;;motion_filter[type_id] = [a_widget]
639::CODE;;elif widget not in motion_filter[type_id]:
640::CODE;;index = self._find_index_in_motion_filter(type_id, a_widget)
641::CODE;;motion_filter[type_id].insert(index, a_widget)
642::CODE;;def unregister_for_motion_event(self, type_id, widget=None):
643::CODE;;'''Unregister to receive motion events of `type_id`.
644::CODE;;:Parameters:
645::CODE;;`type_id`: `str`
646::CODE;;Motion event type id (eg. "touch", "hover", etc.)
647::CODE;;`widget`: `Widget`
648::CODE;;Child widget or `self` if omitted
649::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 2.1.0
650::CODE;;.. note::
651::CODE;;Method can be called multiple times with the same arguments.
652::CODE;;.. warning::
653::CODE;;This is an experimental method and it remains so while this warning
654::CODE;;is present.
655::CODE;;'''
656::CODE;;a_widget = widget or self
657::CODE;;motion_filter = self.motion_filter
658::CODE;;if type_id in motion_filter:
659::CODE;;if a_widget in motion_filter[type_id]:
660::CODE;;motion_filter[type_id].remove(a_widget)
661::CODE;;if not motion_filter[type_id]:
662::CODE;;del motion_filter[type_id]
663::CODE;;def export_to_png(self, filename, *args, **kwargs):
664::CODE;;'''Saves an image of the widget and its children in png format at the
665::CODE;;specified filename. Works by removing the widget canvas from its
666::CODE;;parent, rendering to an :class:`~kivy.graphics.fbo.Fbo`, and calling
667::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.graphics.texture.Texture.save`.
668::CODE;;.. note::
669::CODE;;The image includes only this widget and its children. If you want
670::CODE;;to include widgets elsewhere in the tree, you must call
671::CODE;;:meth:`~Widget.export_to_png` from their common parent, or use
672::CODE;;:meth:`~kivy.core.window.WindowBase.screenshot` to capture the
673::CODE;;whole window.
674::CODE;;.. note::
675::CODE;;The image will be saved in png format, you should include the
676::CODE;;extension in your filename.
677::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.9.0
678::CODE;;:Parameters:
679::CODE;;`filename`: str
680::CODE;;The filename with which to save the png.
681::CODE;;`scale`: float
682::CODE;;The amount by which to scale the saved image, defaults to 1.
683::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.11.0
684::CODE;;'''
685::CODE;;self.export_as_image(*args, **kwargs).save(filename, flipped=False)
686::CODE;;def export_as_image(self, *args, **kwargs):
687::CODE;;'''Return an core :class:`~kivy.core.image.Image` of the actual
688::CODE;;widget.
689::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.11.0
690::CODE;;'''
691::CODE;;from kivy.core.image import Image
692::CODE;;scale = kwargs.get('scale', 1)
693::CODE;;if self.parent is not None:
694::CODE;;canvas_parent_index = self.parent.canvas.indexof(self.canvas)
695::CODE;;if canvas_parent_index > -1:
696::CODE;;self.parent.canvas.remove(self.canvas)
697::CODE;;fbo = Fbo(size=(self.width * scale, self.height * scale),
698::CODE;;with_stencilbuffer=True)
699::CODE;;with fbo:
700::CODE;;ClearColor(0, 0, 0, 0)
701::CODE;;ClearBuffers()
702::CODE;;Scale(1, -1, 1)
703::CODE;;Scale(scale, scale, 1)
704::CODE;;Translate(-self.x, -self.y - self.height, 0)
705::CODE;;fbo.add(self.canvas)
706::CODE;;fbo.draw()

708::CODE;;fbo.remove(self.canvas)
709::CODE;;if self.parent is not None and canvas_parent_index > -1:
710::CODE;;self.parent.canvas.insert(canvas_parent_index, self.canvas)
711::CODE;;return img

730::CODE;;def _walk(self, restrict=False, loopback=False, index=None):
733::CODE;;if index is None:
734::CODE;;index = len(self.children)
735::CODE;;yield self
736::CODE;;for child in reversed(self.children[:index]):
737::CODE;;for walk_child in child._walk(restrict=True):
738::CODE;;yield walk_child
740::CODE;;if not restrict:
741::CODE;;parent = self.parent
742::CODE;;try:
743::CODE;;if parent is None or not isinstance(parent, Widget):
744::CODE;;raise ValueError
745::CODE;;index = parent.children.index(self)
746::CODE;;except ValueError:
748::CODE;;if not loopback:
749::CODE;;return
753::CODE;;parent = self
754::CODE;;index = None
755::CODE;;for walk_child in parent._walk(loopback=loopback, index=index):
756::CODE;;yield walk_child
757::CODE;;def walk(self, restrict=False, loopback=False):
758::CODE;;''' Iterator that walks the widget tree starting with this widget and
759::CODE;;goes forward returning widgets in the order in which layouts display
760::CODE;;them.
761::CODE;;:Parameters:
762::CODE;;`restrict`: bool, defaults to False
763::CODE;;If True, it will only iterate through the widget and its
764::CODE;;children (or children of its children etc.). Defaults to False.
765::CODE;;`loopback`: bool, defaults to False
766::CODE;;If True, when the last widget in the tree is reached,
767::CODE;;it'll loop back to the uppermost root and start walking until
768::CODE;;we hit this widget again. Naturally, it can only loop back when
769::CODE;;`restrict` is False. Defaults to False.
770::CODE;;:return:
771::CODE;;A generator that walks the tree, returning widgets in the
772::CODE;;forward layout order.
773::CODE;;For example, given a tree with the following structure:
774::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
775::CODE;;GridLayout:
776::CODE;;Button
777::CODE;;BoxLayout:
778::CODE;;id: box
779::CODE;;Widget
780::CODE;;Button
781::CODE;;Widget
782::CODE;;walking this tree:
783::CODE;;.. code-block:: python-console
785::CODE;;>>> [type(widget) for widget in box.walk(loopback=True)]
786::CODE;;[<class 'BoxLayout'>, <class 'Widget'>, <class 'Button'>,
787::CODE;;<class 'Widget'>, <class 'GridLayout'>, <class 'Button'>]
789::CODE;;>>> [type(widget) for widget in box.walk()]
790::CODE;;[<class 'BoxLayout'>, <class 'Widget'>, <class 'Button'>,
791::CODE;;<class 'Widget'>]
793::CODE;;>>> [type(widget) for widget in box.walk(restrict=True)]
794::CODE;;[<class 'BoxLayout'>, <class 'Widget'>, <class 'Button'>]
795::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.9.0
796::CODE;;'''
797::CODE;;gen = self._walk(restrict, loopback)
798::CODE;;yield next(gen)
799::CODE;;for node in gen:
800::CODE;;if node is self:
801::CODE;;return
802::CODE;;yield node
803::CODE;;def _walk_reverse(self, loopback=False, go_up=False):
807::CODE;;root = self
808::CODE;;index = 0
810::CODE;;if go_up:
811::CODE;;root = self.parent
812::CODE;;try:
813::CODE;;if root is None or not isinstance(root, Widget):
814::CODE;;raise ValueError
815::CODE;;index = root.children.index(self) + 1
816::CODE;;except ValueError:
817::CODE;;if not loopback:
818::CODE;;return
819::CODE;;index = 0
820::CODE;;go_up = False
821::CODE;;root = self
823::CODE;;for child in islice(root.children, index, None):
824::CODE;;for walk_child in child._walk_reverse(loopback=loopback):
825::CODE;;yield walk_child
827::CODE;;yield root
829::CODE;;if go_up:
830::CODE;;for walk_child in root._walk_reverse(loopback=loopback,
831::CODE;;go_up=go_up):
832::CODE;;yield walk_child
833::CODE;;def walk_reverse(self, loopback=False):
834::CODE;;''' Iterator that walks the widget tree backwards starting with the
835::CODE;;widget before this, and going backwards returning widgets in the
836::CODE;;reverse order in which layouts display them.
837::CODE;;This walks in the opposite direction of :meth:`walk`, so a list of the
838::CODE;;tree generated with :meth:`walk` will be in reverse order compared
839::CODE;;to the list generated with this, provided `loopback` is True.
840::CODE;;:Parameters:
841::CODE;;`loopback`: bool, defaults to False
842::CODE;;If True, when the uppermost root in the tree is
843::CODE;;reached, it'll loop back to the last widget and start walking
844::CODE;;back until after we hit widget again. Defaults to False.
845::CODE;;:return:
846::CODE;;A generator that walks the tree, returning widgets in the
847::CODE;;reverse layout order.
848::CODE;;For example, given a tree with the following structure:
849::CODE;;.. code-block:: kv
850::CODE;;GridLayout:
851::CODE;;Button
852::CODE;;BoxLayout:
853::CODE;;id: box
854::CODE;;Widget
855::CODE;;Button
856::CODE;;Widget
857::CODE;;walking this tree:
858::CODE;;.. code-block:: python-console
860::CODE;;>>> [type(widget) for widget in box.walk_reverse(loopback=True)]
861::CODE;;[<class 'Button'>, <class 'GridLayout'>, <class 'Widget'>,
862::CODE;;<class 'Button'>, <class 'Widget'>, <class 'BoxLayout'>]
864::CODE;;>>> [type(widget) for widget in box.walk_reverse()]
865::CODE;;[<class 'Button'>, <class 'GridLayout'>]
866::CODE;;>>> forward = [w for w in box.walk(loopback=True)]
867::CODE;;>>> backward = [w for w in box.walk_reverse(loopback=True)]
868::CODE;;>>> forward == backward[::-1]
869::CODE;;True
870::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.9.0
871::CODE;;'''
872::CODE;;for node in self._walk_reverse(loopback=loopback, go_up=True):
873::CODE;;yield node
874::CODE;;if node is self:
875::CODE;;return

1049::CODE;;size_hint_x = NumericProperty(1, allownone=True)
1050::CODE;;'''x size hint. Represents how much space the widget should use in the
1051::CODE;;direction of the x axis relative to its parent's width.
1052::CODE;;Only the :class:`~kivy.uix.layout.Layout` and
1053::CODE;;:class:`~kivy.core.window.Window` classes make use of the hint.
1054::CODE;;The size_hint is used by layouts for two purposes:
1055::CODE;;- When the layout considers widgets on their own rather than in
1056::CODE;;relation to its other children, the size_hint_x is a direct proportion
1057::CODE;;of the parent width, normally between 0.0 and 1.0. For instance, a
1058::CODE;;widget with ``size_hint_x=0.5`` in
1059::CODE;;a vertical BoxLayout will take up half the BoxLayout's width, or
1060::CODE;;a widget in a FloatLayout with ``size_hint_x=0.2`` will take up 20%
1061::CODE;;of the FloatLayout width. If the size_hint is greater than 1, the
1062::CODE;;widget will be wider than the parent.
1063::CODE;;- When multiple widgets can share a row of a layout, such as in a
1064::CODE;;horizontal BoxLayout, their widths will be their size_hint_x as a
1065::CODE;;fraction of the sum of widget size_hints. For instance, if the
1066::CODE;;size_hint_xs are (0.5, 1.0, 0.5), the first widget will have a
1067::CODE;;width of 25% of the parent width.

1199::CODE;;opacity = NumericProperty(1.0)
1200::CODE;;'''Opacity of the widget and all its children.
1201::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.4.1
1202::CODE;;The opacity attribute controls the opacity of the widget and its children.
1203::CODE;;Be careful, it's a cumulative attribute: the value is multiplied by the
1204::CODE;;current global opacity and the result is applied to the current context
1205::CODE;;color.
1206::CODE;;For example, if the parent has an opacity of 0.5 and a child has an
1207::CODE;;opacity of 0.2, the real opacity of the child will be 0.5 * 0.2 = 0.1.
1208::CODE;;Then, the opacity is applied by the shader as:
1209::CODE;;.. code-block:: python
1210::CODE;;frag_color = color * vec4(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, opacity);
1211::CODE;;:attr:`opacity` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.NumericProperty` and defaults
1212::CODE;;to 1.0.
1213::CODE;;'''
1214::CODE;;def on_opacity(self, instance, value):

1216::CODE;;if canvas is not None:
1217::CODE;;canvas.opacity = value
1218::CODE;;canvas = None

1220::CODE;;The canvas is a graphics object that contains all the drawing instructions
1221::CODE;;for the graphical representation of the widget.

1223::CODE;;color, to keep the design simple and lean. Some derived classes, such as
1224::CODE;;Button, do add such convenience properties but generally the developer is
1225::CODE;;responsible for implementing the graphics representation for a custom
1226::CODE;;widget from the ground up. See the derived widget classes for patterns to
1227::CODE;;follow and extend.
1228::CODE;;See :class:`~kivy.graphics.Canvas` for more information about the usage.
1229::CODE;;'''

1235::CODE;;value = bool(value)
1236::CODE;;if value != self._disabled_value:
1237::CODE;;self._disabled_value = value
1238::CODE;;if value:
1239::CODE;;self.inc_disabled()
1240::CODE;;else:
1241::CODE;;self.dec_disabled()
1242::CODE;;return True
1243::CODE;;def inc_disabled(self, count=1):
1244::CODE;;self._disabled_count += count
1245::CODE;;if self._disabled_count - count < 1 <= self._disabled_count:
1246::CODE;;self.property('disabled').dispatch(self)
1247::CODE;;for c in self.children:
1248::CODE;;c.inc_disabled(count)
1249::CODE;;def dec_disabled(self, count=1):
1250::CODE;;self._disabled_count -= count
1251::CODE;;if self._disabled_count <= 0 < self._disabled_count + count:
1252::CODE;;self.property('disabled').dispatch(self)
1253::CODE;;for c in self.children:
1254::CODE;;c.dec_disabled(count)

46::CODE;;raise Exception('Invalid count of [ and ]')

51::CODE;;def rgba(s, *args):
52::CODE;;'''Return a Kivy color (4 value from 0-1 range) from either a hex string or
53::CODE;;a list of 0-255 values.
54::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.10.0
55::CODE;;'''
56::CODE;;if isinstance(s, str):
57::CODE;;return get_color_from_hex(s)
58::CODE;;if isinstance(s, (list, tuple)):
59::CODE;;s = [x / 255. for x in s]
60::CODE;;if len(s) == 3:
61::CODE;;s.append(1)
62::CODE;;return s
63::CODE;;if isinstance(s, (int, float)):
64::CODE;;s = [s / 255.]
65::CODE;;s.extend(x / 255. for x in args)
66::CODE;;if len(s) == 3:
67::CODE;;s.append(1)
68::CODE;;return s
69::CODE;;raise Exception('Invalid value (not a string / list / tuple)')

259::CODE;;def deprecated(func=None, msg=''):
260::CODE;;'''This is a decorator which can be used to mark functions
261::CODE;;as deprecated. It will result in a warning being emitted the first time
262::CODE;;the function is used.'''
263::CODE;;import inspect
264::CODE;;import functools
265::CODE;;if func is None:
266::CODE;;return functools.partial(deprecated, msg=msg)
267::CODE;;@functools.wraps(func)
268::CODE;;def new_func(*args, **kwargs):
269::CODE;;file, line, caller = inspect.stack()[1][1:4]
270::CODE;;caller_id = "%s:%s:%s" % (file, line, caller)
272::CODE;;if caller_id not in DEPRECATED_CALLERS:
273::CODE;;DEPRECATED_CALLERS.append(caller_id)
274::CODE;;warning = (
275::CODE;;'Call to deprecated function %s in %s line %d.'
276::CODE;;'Called from %s line %d'
277::CODE;;' by %s().' % (
278::CODE;;func.__name__,
279::CODE;;func.__code__.co_filename,
280::CODE;;func.__code__.co_firstlineno + 1,
281::CODE;;file, line, caller))
282::CODE;;if msg:
283::CODE;;warning = '{}: {}'.format(msg, warning)
284::CODE;;warning = 'Deprecated: ' + warning
285::CODE;;from kivy.logger import Logger
286::CODE;;Logger.warning(warning)
287::CODE;;if func.__doc__:
288::CODE;;Logger.warning(func.__doc__)
289::CODE;;return func(*args, **kwargs)
290::CODE;;return new_func
291::CODE;;@deprecated
292::CODE;;def interpolate(value_from, value_to, step=10):
293::CODE;;'''Interpolate between two values, by providing the
294::CODE;;reciprocal of the proportion between two points.
295::CODE;;.. deprecated:: 2.3.0
296::CODE;;For animations, consider using the
297::CODE;;`AnimationTransition.linear()` for a similar purpose.
298::CODE;;.. warning::
299::CODE;;These interpolations work only on lists/tuples/doubles with the same
300::CODE;;dimensions. No test is done to check the dimensions are the same.
301::CODE;;'''
302::CODE;;if type(value_from) in (list, tuple):
303::CODE;;out = []
304::CODE;;for x, y in zip(value_from, value_to):
305::CODE;;out.append(interpolate(x, y, step))
306::CODE;;return out
307::CODE;;else:
308::CODE;;return value_from + (value_to - value_from) / float(step)

342::CODE;;def format_bytes_to_human(size, precision=2):
343::CODE;;'''Format a byte value to a human readable representation (B, KB, MB...).
344::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.8
345::CODE;;:Parameters:
346::CODE;;`size`: int
347::CODE;;Number that represents the bytes value
348::CODE;;`precision`: int, defaults to 2
349::CODE;;Precision after the comma
350::CODE;;Examples::
351::CODE;;>>> format_bytes_to_human(6463)
352::CODE;;'6.31 KB'
353::CODE;;>>> format_bytes_to_human(646368746541)
354::CODE;;'601.98 GB'
355::CODE;;'''
356::CODE;;size = int(size)
357::CODE;;fmt = '%%1.%df %%s' % precision
358::CODE;;for unit in ['B', 'KB', 'MB', 'GB', 'TB']:
359::CODE;;if size < 1024.0:
360::CODE;;return fmt % (size, unit)
361::CODE;;size /= 1024.0
