1404::CODE;;class _IdentityRegressor(RegressorMixin, BaseEstimator):
1412::CODE;;We inherit from LinearClassifierMixin to get the proper shape for the
1413::CODE;;output `y`.
1421::CODE;;This class is not intended to be used directly. Use RidgeCV instead.
1422::CODE;;`_RidgeGCV` uses a Generalized Cross-Validation for model selection. It's an
1423::CODE;;efficient approximation of leave-one-out cross-validation (LOO-CV), where instead of
1424::CODE;;computing multiple models by excluding one data point at a time, it uses an
1425::CODE;;algebraic shortcut to approximate the LOO-CV error, making it faster and
1426::CODE;;computationally more efficient.
1427::CODE;;Using a naive grid-search approach with a leave-one-out cross-validation in contrast
1428::CODE;;requires to fit `n_samples` models to compute the prediction error for each sample
1429::CODE;;and then to repeat this process for each alpha in the grid.
1430::CODE;;Here, the prediction error for each sample is computed by solving a **single**
1431::CODE;;linear system (in other words a single model) via a matrix factorization (i.e.
1432::CODE;;eigendecomposition or SVD) solving the problem stated in the Notes section. Finally,
1433::CODE;;we need to repeat this process for each alpha in the grid. The detailed complexity
1434::CODE;;is further discussed in Sect. 4 in [1].
1435::CODE;;This algebraic approach is only applicable for regularized least squares
1436::CODE;;problems. It could potentially be extended to kernel ridge regression.
1437::CODE;;See the Notes section and references for more details regarding the formulation
1438::CODE;;and the linear system that is solved.
1439::CODE;;Notes
1440::CODE;;-----
1441::CODE;;We want to solve (K + alpha*Id)c = y,
1442::CODE;;where K = X X^T is the kernel matrix.
1443::CODE;;Let G = (K + alpha*Id).
1444::CODE;;Dual solution: c = G^-1y
1445::CODE;;Primal solution: w = X^T c
1446::CODE;;Compute eigendecomposition K = Q V Q^T.
1447::CODE;;Then G^-1 = Q (V + alpha*Id)^-1 Q^T,
1448::CODE;;where (V + alpha*Id) is diagonal.
1449::CODE;;It is thus inexpensive to inverse for many alphas.
1450::CODE;;Let loov be the vector of prediction values for each example
1451::CODE;;when the model was fitted with all examples but this example.
1452::CODE;;loov = (KG^-1Y - diag(KG^-1)Y) / diag(I-KG^-1)
1453::CODE;;Let looe be the vector of prediction errors for each example
1454::CODE;;when the model was fitted with all examples but this example.
1455::CODE;;looe = y - loov = c / diag(G^-1)
1456::CODE;;The best score (negative mean squared error or user-provided scoring) is
1457::CODE;;stored in the `best_score_` attribute, and the selected hyperparameter in
1458::CODE;;`alpha_`.
1459::CODE;;References
1460::CODE;;----------
1461::CODE;;[1] http://cbcl.mit.edu/publications/ps/MIT-CSAIL-TR-2007-025.pdf
1462::CODE;;[2] https://www.mit.edu/~9.520/spring07/Classes/rlsslides.pdf
1499::CODE;;Parameters
1500::CODE;;----------
1501::CODE;;X : {ndarray, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
1502::CODE;;The preprocessed design matrix.
1503::CODE;;sqrt_sw : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
1504::CODE;;square roots of sample weights
1505::CODE;;Returns
1506::CODE;;-------
1507::CODE;;gram : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_samples)
1508::CODE;;The Gram matrix.
1509::CODE;;X_mean : ndarray of shape (n_feature,)
1510::CODE;;The weighted mean of ``X`` for each feature.
1511::CODE;;Notes
1512::CODE;;-----
1513::CODE;;When X is dense the centering has been done in preprocessing
1514::CODE;;so the mean is 0 and we just compute XX^T.
1515::CODE;;When X is sparse it has not been centered in preprocessing, but it has
1516::CODE;;been scaled by sqrt(sample weights).
1517::CODE;;When self.fit_intercept is False no centering is done.
1518::CODE;;The centered X is never actually computed because centering would break
1519::CODE;;the sparsity of X.

1562::CODE;;the sparsity of X.
1585::CODE;;without explicitly centering X nor computing X.dot(A)

2196::CODE;;``scorer(estimator, X, y)``. See :ref:`scoring_callable` for details.
2197::CODE;;- `None`: negative :ref:`mean squared error <mean_squared_error>` if cv is
2198::CODE;;None (i.e. when using leave-one-out cross-validation), or
2199::CODE;;:ref:`coefficient of determination <r2_score>` (:math:`R^2`) otherwise.
2200::CODE;;cv : int, cross-validation generator or an iterable, default=None
2201::CODE;;Determines the cross-validation splitting strategy.
2202::CODE;;Possible inputs for cv are:
2203::CODE;;- None, to use the efficient Leave-One-Out cross-validation
2204::CODE;;- integer, to specify the number of folds.
2205::CODE;;- :term:`CV splitter`,
2206::CODE;;- An iterable yielding (train, test) splits as arrays of indices.
2207::CODE;;For integer/None inputs, if ``y`` is binary or multiclass,
2208::CODE;;:class:`~sklearn.model_selection.StratifiedKFold` is used, else,
2209::CODE;;:class:`~sklearn.model_selection.KFold` is used.
2210::CODE;;Refer :ref:`User Guide <cross_validation>` for the various
2211::CODE;;cross-validation strategies that can be used here.
2212::CODE;;gcv_mode : {'auto', 'svd', 'eigen'}, default='auto'
2213::CODE;;Flag indicating which strategy to use when performing
2214::CODE;;Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation. Options are::
2215::CODE;;'auto' : use 'svd' if n_samples > n_features, otherwise use 'eigen'
2216::CODE;;'svd' : force use of singular value decomposition of X when X is
2217::CODE;;dense, eigenvalue decomposition of X^T.X when X is sparse.
2218::CODE;;'eigen' : force computation via eigendecomposition of X.X^T
2219::CODE;;The 'auto' mode is the default and is intended to pick the cheaper
2220::CODE;;option of the two depending on the shape of the training data.
2221::CODE;;store_cv_results : bool, default=False

2224::CODE;;below). This flag is only compatible with ``cv=None`` (i.e. using
2225::CODE;;Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation).

2231::CODE;;settings: multiple prediction targets). When set to `True`, after
2232::CODE;;fitting, the `alpha_` attribute will contain a value for each target.
2233::CODE;;When set to `False`, a single alpha is used for all targets.

16::CODE;;The step size is set to 1 / (alpha_scaled + L + fit_intercept) where L is
17::CODE;;the max sum of squares for over all samples.
18::CODE;;Parameters
19::CODE;;----------
20::CODE;;max_squared_sum : float
21::CODE;;Maximum squared sum of X over samples.

26::CODE;;The loss function used in SAG solver.

29::CODE;;added to the decision function.

34::CODE;;algorithm.

37::CODE;;step_size : float
38::CODE;;Step size used in SAG solver.
39::CODE;;References
40::CODE;;----------
41::CODE;;Schmidt, M., Roux, N. L., & Bach, F. (2013).
42::CODE;;Minimizing finite sums with the stochastic average gradient
43::CODE;;https://hal.inria.fr/hal-00860051/document
44::CODE;;:arxiv:`Defazio, A., Bach F. & Lacoste-Julien S. (2014).
45::CODE;;"SAGA: A Fast Incremental Gradient Method With Support
46::CODE;;for Non-Strongly Convex Composite Objectives" <1407.0202>`
86::CODE;;SAG stands for Stochastic Average Gradient: the gradient of the loss is
87::CODE;;estimated each sample at a time and the model is updated along the way with
88::CODE;;a constant learning rate.
89::CODE;;IMPORTANT NOTE: 'sag' solver converges faster on columns that are on the
90::CODE;;same scale. You can normalize the data by using
91::CODE;;sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler on your data before passing it to the
92::CODE;;fit method.
93::CODE;;This implementation works with data represented as dense numpy arrays or
94::CODE;;sparse scipy arrays of floating point values for the features. It will
95::CODE;;fit the data according to squared loss or log loss.
96::CODE;;The regularizer is a penalty added to the loss function that shrinks model
97::CODE;;parameters towards the zero vector using the squared euclidean norm L2.
98::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.17
99::CODE;;Parameters
100::CODE;;----------
101::CODE;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
102::CODE;;Training data.
103::CODE;;y : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
104::CODE;;Target values. With loss='multinomial', y must be label encoded
105::CODE;;(see preprocessing.LabelEncoder). For loss='log' it must be in [0, 1].
106::CODE;;sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
107::CODE;;Weights applied to individual samples (1. for unweighted).
108::CODE;;loss : {'log', 'squared', 'multinomial'}, default='log'
109::CODE;;Loss function that will be optimized:
110::CODE;;-'log' is the binary logistic loss, as used in LogisticRegression.
111::CODE;;-'squared' is the squared loss, as used in Ridge.
112::CODE;;-'multinomial' is the multinomial logistic loss, as used in
113::CODE;;LogisticRegression.
114::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.18
115::CODE;;*loss='multinomial'*
116::CODE;;alpha : float, default=1.
117::CODE;;L2 regularization term in the objective function
118::CODE;;``(0.5 * alpha * || W ||_F^2)``.
119::CODE;;beta : float, default=0.
120::CODE;;L1 regularization term in the objective function
121::CODE;;``(beta * || W ||_1)``. Only applied if ``is_saga`` is set to True.
122::CODE;;max_iter : int, default=1000
123::CODE;;The max number of passes over the training data if the stopping
124::CODE;;criteria is not reached.
125::CODE;;tol : float, default=0.001
126::CODE;;The stopping criteria for the weights. The iterations will stop when
127::CODE;;max(change in weights) / max(weights) < tol.
128::CODE;;verbose : int, default=0
129::CODE;;The verbosity level.
130::CODE;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
131::CODE;;Used when shuffling the data. Pass an int for reproducible output
132::CODE;;across multiple function calls.
133::CODE;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
134::CODE;;check_input : bool, default=True
135::CODE;;If False, the input arrays X and y will not be checked.
136::CODE;;max_squared_sum : float, default=None
137::CODE;;Maximum squared sum of X over samples. If None, it will be computed,
138::CODE;;going through all the samples. The value should be precomputed
139::CODE;;to speed up cross validation.
140::CODE;;warm_start_mem : dict, default=None
141::CODE;;The initialization parameters used for warm starting. Warm starting is
142::CODE;;currently used in LogisticRegression but not in Ridge.
143::CODE;;It contains:
144::CODE;;- 'coef': the weight vector, with the intercept in last line
145::CODE;;if the intercept is fitted.
146::CODE;;- 'gradient_memory': the scalar gradient for all seen samples.
147::CODE;;- 'sum_gradient': the sum of gradient over all seen samples,
148::CODE;;for each feature.
149::CODE;;- 'intercept_sum_gradient': the sum of gradient over all seen
150::CODE;;samples, for the intercept.
151::CODE;;- 'seen': array of boolean describing the seen samples.
152::CODE;;- 'num_seen': the number of seen samples.
153::CODE;;is_saga : bool, default=False
154::CODE;;Whether to use the SAGA algorithm or the SAG algorithm. SAGA behaves
155::CODE;;better in the first epochs, and allow for l1 regularisation.
156::CODE;;Returns
157::CODE;;-------
158::CODE;;coef_ : ndarray of shape (n_features,)
159::CODE;;Weight vector.
160::CODE;;n_iter_ : int
161::CODE;;The number of full pass on all samples.
162::CODE;;warm_start_mem : dict
163::CODE;;Contains a 'coef' key with the fitted result, and possibly the
164::CODE;;fitted intercept at the end of the array. Contains also other keys
165::CODE;;used for warm starting.

167::CODE;;--------
168::CODE;;>>> import numpy as np
169::CODE;;>>> from sklearn import linear_model

661::CODE;;def _fit_binary(self, X, y, alpha, sample_weight, learning_rate, max_iter):
693::CODE;;Each binary classifier predicts one class versus all others. This
694::CODE;;strategy is called OvA (One versus All) or OvR (One versus Rest).
742::CODE;;Internally, this method uses ``max_iter = 1``. Therefore, it is not
743::CODE;;guaranteed that a minimum of the cost function is reached after calling
744::CODE;;it once. Matters such as objective convergence, early stopping, and
745::CODE;;learning rate adjustments should be handled by the user.
746::CODE;;Parameters
747::CODE;;----------
748::CODE;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix}, shape (n_samples, n_features)
749::CODE;;Subset of the training data.
750::CODE;;y : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
751::CODE;;Subset of the target values.
752::CODE;;classes : ndarray of shape (n_classes,), default=None
753::CODE;;Classes across all calls to partial_fit.
754::CODE;;Can be obtained by via `np.unique(y_all)`, where y_all is the
755::CODE;;target vector of the entire dataset.
756::CODE;;This argument is required for the first call to partial_fit
757::CODE;;and can be omitted in the subsequent calls.
758::CODE;;Note that y doesn't need to contain all labels in `classes`.
759::CODE;;sample_weight : array-like, shape (n_samples,), default=None
760::CODE;;Weights applied to individual samples.
761::CODE;;If not provided, uniform weights are assumed.
762::CODE;;Returns
763::CODE;;-------
764::CODE;;self : object
765::CODE;;Returns an instance of self.
796::CODE;;Parameters
797::CODE;;----------
798::CODE;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix}, shape (n_samples, n_features)
799::CODE;;Training data.
800::CODE;;y : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
801::CODE;;Target values.
802::CODE;;coef_init : ndarray of shape (n_classes, n_features), default=None
803::CODE;;The initial coefficients to warm-start the optimization.
804::CODE;;intercept_init : ndarray of shape (n_classes,), default=None
805::CODE;;The initial intercept to warm-start the optimization.
806::CODE;;sample_weight : array-like, shape (n_samples,), default=None
807::CODE;;Weights applied to individual samples.
808::CODE;;If not provided, uniform weights are assumed. These weights will
809::CODE;;be multiplied with class_weight (passed through the
810::CODE;;constructor) if class_weight is specified.
811::CODE;;Returns
812::CODE;;-------
813::CODE;;self : object
814::CODE;;Returns an instance of self.
833::CODE;;This estimator implements regularized linear models with stochastic
834::CODE;;gradient descent (SGD) learning: the gradient of the loss is estimated
835::CODE;;each sample at a time and the model is updated along the way with a
836::CODE;;decreasing strength schedule (aka learning rate). SGD allows minibatch
837::CODE;;(online/out-of-core) learning via the `partial_fit` method.
838::CODE;;For best results using the default learning rate schedule, the data should
839::CODE;;have zero mean and unit variance.
840::CODE;;This implementation works with data represented as dense or sparse arrays
841::CODE;;of floating point values for the features. The model it fits can be
842::CODE;;controlled with the loss parameter; by default, it fits a linear support
843::CODE;;vector machine (SVM).
844::CODE;;The regularizer is a penalty added to the loss function that shrinks model
845::CODE;;parameters towards the zero vector using either the squared euclidean norm
846::CODE;;L2 or the absolute norm L1 or a combination of both (Elastic Net). If the
847::CODE;;parameter update crosses the 0.0 value because of the regularizer, the
848::CODE;;update is truncated to 0.0 to allow for learning sparse models and achieve
849::CODE;;online feature selection.
850::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <sgd>`.
851::CODE;;Parameters
852::CODE;;----------
853::CODE;;loss : {'hinge', 'log_loss', 'modified_huber', 'squared_hinge',\
854::CODE;;'perceptron', 'squared_error', 'huber', 'epsilon_insensitive',\
855::CODE;;'squared_epsilon_insensitive'}, default='hinge'
856::CODE;;The loss function to be used.
857::CODE;;- 'hinge' gives a linear SVM.
858::CODE;;- 'log_loss' gives logistic regression, a probabilistic classifier.
859::CODE;;- 'modified_huber' is another smooth loss that brings tolerance to
860::CODE;;outliers as well as probability estimates.
861::CODE;;- 'squared_hinge' is like hinge but is quadratically penalized.
862::CODE;;- 'perceptron' is the linear loss used by the perceptron algorithm.
863::CODE;;- The other losses, 'squared_error', 'huber', 'epsilon_insensitive' and
864::CODE;;'squared_epsilon_insensitive' are designed for regression but can be useful
865::CODE;;in classification as well; see
866::CODE;;:class:`~sklearn.linear_model.SGDRegressor` for a description.
867::CODE;;More details about the losses formulas can be found in the :ref:`User Guide
868::CODE;;<sgd_mathematical_formulation>` and you can find a visualisation of the loss
869::CODE;;functions in
870::CODE;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_linear_model_plot_sgd_loss_functions.py`.
871::CODE;;penalty : {'l2', 'l1', 'elasticnet', None}, default='l2'
872::CODE;;The penalty (aka regularization term) to be used. Defaults to 'l2'
873::CODE;;which is the standard regularizer for linear SVM models. 'l1' and
874::CODE;;'elasticnet' might bring sparsity to the model (feature selection)
875::CODE;;not achievable with 'l2'. No penalty is added when set to `None`.
876::CODE;;You can see a visualisation of the penalties in
877::CODE;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_linear_model_plot_sgd_penalties.py`.
878::CODE;;alpha : float, default=0.0001
879::CODE;;Constant that multiplies the regularization term. The higher the
880::CODE;;value, the stronger the regularization. Also used to compute the
881::CODE;;learning rate when `learning_rate` is set to 'optimal'.
882::CODE;;Values must be in the range `[0.0, inf)`.
883::CODE;;l1_ratio : float, default=0.15
884::CODE;;The Elastic Net mixing parameter, with 0 <= l1_ratio <= 1.
885::CODE;;l1_ratio=0 corresponds to L2 penalty, l1_ratio=1 to L1.
886::CODE;;Only used if `penalty` is 'elasticnet'.
887::CODE;;Values must be in the range `[0.0, 1.0]` or can be `None` if
888::CODE;;`penalty` is not `elasticnet`.
889::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.7
890::CODE;;`l1_ratio` can be `None` when `penalty` is not "elasticnet".
891::CODE;;fit_intercept : bool, default=True
892::CODE;;Whether the intercept should be estimated or not. If False, the
893::CODE;;data is assumed to be already centered.
894::CODE;;max_iter : int, default=1000
895::CODE;;The maximum number of passes over the training data (aka epochs).
896::CODE;;It only impacts the behavior in the ``fit`` method, and not the
897::CODE;;:meth:`partial_fit` method.
898::CODE;;Values must be in the range `[1, inf)`.
899::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.19
900::CODE;;tol : float or None, default=1e-3
901::CODE;;The stopping criterion. If it is not None, training will stop
902::CODE;;when (loss > best_loss - tol) for ``n_iter_no_change`` consecutive
903::CODE;;epochs.
904::CODE;;Convergence is checked against the training loss or the
905::CODE;;validation loss depending on the `early_stopping` parameter.
906::CODE;;Values must be in the range `[0.0, inf)`.
907::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.19
908::CODE;;shuffle : bool, default=True
909::CODE;;Whether or not the training data should be shuffled after each epoch.
910::CODE;;verbose : int, default=0
911::CODE;;The verbosity level.
912::CODE;;Values must be in the range `[0, inf)`.
913::CODE;;epsilon : float, default=0.1
914::CODE;;Epsilon in the epsilon-insensitive loss functions; only if `loss` is
915::CODE;;'huber', 'epsilon_insensitive', or 'squared_epsilon_insensitive'.
916::CODE;;For 'huber', determines the threshold at which it becomes less
917::CODE;;important to get the prediction exactly right.
918::CODE;;For epsilon-insensitive, any differences between the current prediction
919::CODE;;and the correct label are ignored if they are less than this threshold.
920::CODE;;Values must be in the range `[0.0, inf)`.
921::CODE;;n_jobs : int, default=None
922::CODE;;The number of CPUs to use to do the OVA (One Versus All, for
923::CODE;;multi-class problems) computation.
924::CODE;;``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
925::CODE;;``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
926::CODE;;for more details.
927::CODE;;random_state : int, RandomState instance, default=None
928::CODE;;Used for shuffling the data, when ``shuffle`` is set to ``True``.
929::CODE;;Pass an int for reproducible output across multiple function calls.
930::CODE;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
931::CODE;;Integer values must be in the range `[0, 2**32 - 1]`.
932::CODE;;learning_rate : str, default='optimal'
933::CODE;;The learning rate schedule:
934::CODE;;- 'constant': `eta = eta0`
935::CODE;;- 'optimal': `eta = 1.0 / (alpha * (t + t0))`
936::CODE;;where `t0` is chosen by a heuristic proposed by Leon Bottou.
937::CODE;;- 'invscaling': `eta = eta0 / pow(t, power_t)`
938::CODE;;- 'adaptive': `eta = eta0`, as long as the training keeps decreasing.
939::CODE;;Each time n_iter_no_change consecutive epochs fail to decrease the
940::CODE;;training loss by tol or fail to increase validation score by tol if
941::CODE;;`early_stopping` is `True`, the current learning rate is divided by 5.
942::CODE;;- 'pa1': passive-aggressive algorithm 1, see [1]_. Only with `loss='hinge'`.
943::CODE;;Update is `w += eta y x` with `eta = min(eta0, loss/||x||**2)`.
944::CODE;;- 'pa2': passive-aggressive algorithm 2, see [1]_. Only with
945::CODE;;`loss='hinge'`.
946::CODE;;Update is `w += eta y x` with `eta = hinge_loss / (||x||**2 + 1/(2 eta0))`.
947::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.20
948::CODE;;Added 'adaptive' option.
949::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.8
950::CODE;;Added options 'pa1' and 'pa2'
951::CODE;;eta0 : float, default=0.01
952::CODE;;The initial learning rate for the 'constant', 'invscaling' or
953::CODE;;'adaptive' schedules. The default value is 0.01, but note that eta0 is not used
954::CODE;;by the default learning rate 'optimal'.
955::CODE;;Values must be in the range `(0.0, inf)`.
956::CODE;;For PA-1 (`learning_rate=pa1`) and PA-II (`pa2`), it specifies the
957::CODE;;aggressiveness parameter for the passive-agressive algorithm, see [1] where it
958::CODE;;is called C:
959::CODE;;- For PA-I it is the maximum step size.
960::CODE;;- For PA-II it regularizes the step size (the smaller `eta0` the more it
961::CODE;;regularizes).
962::CODE;;As a general rule-of-thumb for PA, `eta0` should be small when the data is
963::CODE;;noisy.
964::CODE;;power_t : float, default=0.5
965::CODE;;The exponent for inverse scaling learning rate.
966::CODE;;Values must be in the range `[0.0, inf)`.
967::CODE;;.. deprecated:: 1.8
968::CODE;;Negative values for `power_t` are deprecated in version 1.8 and will raise
969::CODE;;an error in 1.10. Use values in the range [0.0, inf) instead.
970::CODE;;early_stopping : bool, default=False
971::CODE;;Whether to use early stopping to terminate training when validation
972::CODE;;score is not improving. If set to `True`, it will automatically set aside
973::CODE;;a stratified fraction of training data as validation and terminate
974::CODE;;training when validation score returned by the `score` method is not
975::CODE;;improving by at least tol for n_iter_no_change consecutive epochs.
976::CODE;;See :ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_linear_model_plot_sgd_early_stopping.py` for an
977::CODE;;example of the effects of early stopping.
978::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.20
979::CODE;;Added 'early_stopping' option
980::CODE;;validation_fraction : float, default=0.1
981::CODE;;The proportion of training data to set aside as validation set for
982::CODE;;early stopping. Must be between 0 and 1.
983::CODE;;Only used if `early_stopping` is True.
984::CODE;;Values must be in the range `(0.0, 1.0)`.
985::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.20
986::CODE;;Added 'validation_fraction' option
987::CODE;;n_iter_no_change : int, default=5
988::CODE;;Number of iterations with no improvement to wait before stopping
989::CODE;;fitting.
990::CODE;;Convergence is checked against the training loss or the
991::CODE;;validation loss depending on the `early_stopping` parameter.
992::CODE;;Integer values must be in the range `[1, max_iter)`.
993::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.20
994::CODE;;Added 'n_iter_no_change' option
995::CODE;;class_weight : dict, {class_label: weight} or "balanced", default=None
996::CODE;;Preset for the class_weight fit parameter.
997::CODE;;Weights associated with classes. If not given, all classes
998::CODE;;are supposed to have weight one.
999::CODE;;The "balanced" mode uses the values of y to automatically adjust
1000::CODE;;weights inversely proportional to class frequencies in the input data
1001::CODE;;as ``n_samples / (n_classes * np.bincount(y))``.
1002::CODE;;warm_start : bool, default=False
1003::CODE;;When set to True, reuse the solution of the previous call to fit as
1004::CODE;;initialization, otherwise, just erase the previous solution.
1005::CODE;;See :term:`the Glossary <warm_start>`.
1006::CODE;;Repeatedly calling fit or partial_fit when warm_start is True can
1007::CODE;;result in a different solution than when calling fit a single time
1008::CODE;;because of the way the data is shuffled.
1009::CODE;;If a dynamic learning rate is used, the learning rate is adapted
1010::CODE;;depending on the number of samples already seen. Calling ``fit`` resets
1011::CODE;;this counter, while ``partial_fit`` will result in increasing the
1012::CODE;;existing counter.
1013::CODE;;average : bool or int, default=False
1014::CODE;;When set to `True`, computes the averaged SGD weights across all
1015::CODE;;updates and stores the result in the ``coef_`` attribute. If set to
1016::CODE;;an int greater than 1, averaging will begin once the total number of
1017::CODE;;samples seen reaches `average`. So ``average=10`` will begin
1018::CODE;;averaging after seeing 10 samples.
1019::CODE;;Integer values must be in the range `[1, n_samples]`.
1020::CODE;;Attributes
1021::CODE;;----------
1022::CODE;;coef_ : ndarray of shape (1, n_features) if n_classes == 2 else \
1023::CODE;;(n_classes, n_features)
1024::CODE;;Weights assigned to the features.
1025::CODE;;intercept_ : ndarray of shape (1,) if n_classes == 2 else (n_classes,)
1026::CODE;;Constants in decision function.
1027::CODE;;n_iter_ : int
1028::CODE;;The actual number of iterations before reaching the stopping criterion.
1029::CODE;;For multiclass fits, it is the maximum over every binary fit.
1030::CODE;;classes_ : array of shape (n_classes,)
1031::CODE;;t_ : int
1032::CODE;;Number of weight updates performed during training.
1033::CODE;;Same as ``(n_iter_ * n_samples + 1)``.
1034::CODE;;n_features_in_ : int
1035::CODE;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
1036::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
1037::CODE;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
1038::CODE;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
1039::CODE;;has feature names that are all strings.

1068::CODE;;[1]
1138::CODE;;This method is only available for log loss and modified Huber loss.
1139::CODE;;Multiclass probability estimates are derived from binary (one-vs.-rest)
1140::CODE;;estimates by simple normalization, as recommended by Zadrozny and
1141::CODE;;Elkan.
1142::CODE;;Binary probability estimates for loss="modified_huber" are given by
1143::CODE;;(clip(decision_function(X), -1, 1) + 1) / 2. For other loss functions
1144::CODE;;it is necessary to perform proper probability calibration by wrapping
1145::CODE;;the classifier with
1146::CODE;;:class:`~sklearn.calibration.CalibratedClassifierCV` instead.

1154::CODE;;Returns the probability of the sample for each class in the model,
1155::CODE;;where classes are ordered as they are in `self.classes_`.
1156::CODE;;References

1159::CODE;;probability estimates", SIGKDD'02,
1160::CODE;;https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/775047.775151
1161::CODE;;The justification for the formula in the loss="modified_huber"
1162::CODE;;case is in the appendix B in:
1163::CODE;;http://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/papers/volume2/zhang02c/zhang02c.pdf
1203::CODE;;This method is only available for log loss and modified Huber loss.
1204::CODE;;When loss="modified_huber", probability estimates may be hard zeros
1205::CODE;;and ones, so taking the logarithm is not possible.
1206::CODE;;See ``predict_proba`` for details.
1207::CODE;;Parameters
1208::CODE;;----------
1209::CODE;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
1210::CODE;;Input data for prediction.
1211::CODE;;Returns
1212::CODE;;-------
1213::CODE;;T : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_classes)
1214::CODE;;Returns the log-probability of the sample for each class in the
1215::CODE;;model, where classes are ordered as they are in
1216::CODE;;`self.classes_`.
1322::CODE;;Internally, this method uses ``max_iter = 1``. Therefore, it is not
1323::CODE;;guaranteed that a minimum of the cost function is reached after calling
1324::CODE;;it once. Matters such as objective convergence and early stopping
1325::CODE;;should be handled by the user.

1439::CODE;;Parameters
1440::CODE;;----------
1441::CODE;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix}, shape (n_samples, n_features)

1444::CODE;;ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
1445::CODE;;Predicted target values per element in X.
1453::CODE;;Parameters
1454::CODE;;----------
1455::CODE;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix}, shape (n_samples, n_features)
1456::CODE;;Input data.
1457::CODE;;Returns
1458::CODE;;-------
1459::CODE;;ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
1460::CODE;;Predicted target values per element in X.
1541::CODE;;SGD stands for Stochastic Gradient Descent: the gradient of the loss is
1542::CODE;;estimated each sample at a time and the model is updated along the way with
1543::CODE;;a decreasing strength schedule (aka learning rate).
1544::CODE;;The regularizer is a penalty added to the loss function that shrinks model
1545::CODE;;parameters towards the zero vector using either the squared euclidean norm
1546::CODE;;L2 or the absolute norm L1 or a combination of both (Elastic Net). If the
1547::CODE;;parameter update crosses the 0.0 value because of the regularizer, the
1548::CODE;;update is truncated to 0.0 to allow for learning sparse models and achieve
1549::CODE;;online feature selection.
1550::CODE;;This implementation works with data represented as dense numpy arrays of
1551::CODE;;floating point values for the features.
1552::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <sgd>`.
1553::CODE;;Parameters
1554::CODE;;----------
1555::CODE;;loss : str, default='squared_error'
1556::CODE;;The loss function to be used. The possible values are 'squared_error',
1557::CODE;;'huber', 'epsilon_insensitive', or 'squared_epsilon_insensitive'
1558::CODE;;The 'squared_error' refers to the ordinary least squares fit.
1559::CODE;;'huber' modifies 'squared_error' to focus less on getting outliers
1560::CODE;;correct by switching from squared to linear loss past a distance of
1561::CODE;;epsilon. 'epsilon_insensitive' ignores errors less than epsilon and is
1562::CODE;;linear past that; this is the loss function used in SVR.
1563::CODE;;'squared_epsilon_insensitive' is the same but becomes squared loss past
1564::CODE;;a tolerance of epsilon.
1565::CODE;;More details about the losses formulas can be found in the
1566::CODE;;:ref:`User Guide <sgd_mathematical_formulation>`.
1567::CODE;;penalty : {'l2', 'l1', 'elasticnet', None}, default='l2'
1568::CODE;;The penalty (aka regularization term) to be used. Defaults to 'l2'
1569::CODE;;which is the standard regularizer for linear SVM models. 'l1' and
1570::CODE;;'elasticnet' might bring sparsity to the model (feature selection)
1571::CODE;;not achievable with 'l2'. No penalty is added when set to `None`.
1572::CODE;;You can see a visualisation of the penalties in
1573::CODE;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_linear_model_plot_sgd_penalties.py`.
1574::CODE;;alpha : float, default=0.0001
1575::CODE;;Constant that multiplies the regularization term. The higher the
1576::CODE;;value, the stronger the regularization. Also used to compute the
1577::CODE;;learning rate when `learning_rate` is set to 'optimal'.
1578::CODE;;Values must be in the range `[0.0, inf)`.
1579::CODE;;l1_ratio : float, default=0.15
1580::CODE;;The Elastic Net mixing parameter, with 0 <= l1_ratio <= 1.
1581::CODE;;l1_ratio=0 corresponds to L2 penalty, l1_ratio=1 to L1.
1582::CODE;;Only used if `penalty` is 'elasticnet'.
1583::CODE;;Values must be in the range `[0.0, 1.0]` or can be `None` if
1584::CODE;;`penalty` is not `elasticnet`.
1585::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.7
1586::CODE;;`l1_ratio` can be `None` when `penalty` is not "elasticnet".
1587::CODE;;fit_intercept : bool, default=True
1588::CODE;;Whether the intercept should be estimated or not. If False, the
1589::CODE;;data is assumed to be already centered.
1590::CODE;;max_iter : int, default=1000
1591::CODE;;The maximum number of passes over the training data (aka epochs).
1592::CODE;;It only impacts the behavior in the ``fit`` method, and not the
1593::CODE;;:meth:`partial_fit` method.
1594::CODE;;Values must be in the range `[1, inf)`.
1595::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.19
1596::CODE;;tol : float or None, default=1e-3
1597::CODE;;The stopping criterion. If it is not None, training will stop
1598::CODE;;when (loss > best_loss - tol) for ``n_iter_no_change`` consecutive
1599::CODE;;epochs.
1600::CODE;;Convergence is checked against the training loss or the
1601::CODE;;validation loss depending on the `early_stopping` parameter.
1602::CODE;;Values must be in the range `[0.0, inf)`.

1604::CODE;;shuffle : bool, default=True
1605::CODE;;Whether or not the training data should be shuffled after each epoch.
1606::CODE;;verbose : int, default=0
1607::CODE;;The verbosity level.
1608::CODE;;Values must be in the range `[0, inf)`.
1609::CODE;;epsilon : float, default=0.1

1706::CODE;;intercept_ : ndarray of shape (1,)
1707::CODE;;The intercept term.
1708::CODE;;n_iter_ : int
1709::CODE;;The actual number of iterations before reaching the stopping criterion.
1710::CODE;;t_ : int
1711::CODE;;Number of weight updates performed during training.
1712::CODE;;Same as ``(n_iter_ * n_samples + 1)``.
1713::CODE;;n_features_in_ : int
1714::CODE;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
1715::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
1716::CODE;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
1717::CODE;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
1718::CODE;;has feature names that are all strings.
1719::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
1720::CODE;;See Also
1721::CODE;;--------
1722::CODE;;HuberRegressor : Linear regression model that is robust to outliers.
1723::CODE;;Lars : Least Angle Regression model.
1724::CODE;;Lasso : Linear Model trained with L1 prior as regularizer.
1725::CODE;;RANSACRegressor : RANSAC (RANdom SAmple Consensus) algorithm.
1726::CODE;;Ridge : Linear least squares with l2 regularization.
1727::CODE;;sklearn.svm.SVR : Epsilon-Support Vector Regression.
1728::CODE;;TheilSenRegressor : Theil-Sen Estimator robust multivariate regression model.
1729::CODE;;References
1730::CODE;;----------
1731::CODE;;.. [1] Online Passive-Aggressive Algorithms
1732::CODE;;<http://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/papers/volume7/crammer06a/crammer06a.pdf>
1733::CODE;;K. Crammer, O. Dekel, J. Keshat, S. Shalev-Shwartz, Y. Singer - JMLR (2006)
1734::CODE;;Examples
1735::CODE;;--------
1736::CODE;;>>> import numpy as np
1737::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.linear_model import SGDRegressor
1738::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
1739::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
1740::CODE;;>>> n_samples, n_features = 10, 5
1741::CODE;;>>> rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
1742::CODE;;>>> y = rng.randn(n_samples)
1743::CODE;;>>> X = rng.randn(n_samples, n_features)
1745::CODE;;>>> reg = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(),
1746::CODE;;... SGDRegressor(max_iter=1000, tol=1e-3))
1747::CODE;;>>> reg.fit(X, y)
1748::CODE;;Pipeline(steps=[('standardscaler', StandardScaler()),
1749::CODE;;('sgdregressor', SGDRegressor())])
1808::CODE;;This implementation is meant to be used with a kernel approximation
1809::CODE;;technique (e.g. `sklearn.kernel_approximation.Nystroem`) to obtain results
1810::CODE;;similar to `sklearn.svm.OneClassSVM` which uses a Gaussian kernel by
1811::CODE;;default.
1812::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <sgd_online_one_class_svm>`.
1813::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
1814::CODE;;Parameters
1815::CODE;;----------
1816::CODE;;nu : float, default=0.5
1817::CODE;;The nu parameter of the One Class SVM: an upper bound on the
1818::CODE;;fraction of training errors and a lower bound of the fraction of
1819::CODE;;support vectors. Should be in the interval (0, 1]. By default 0.5
1820::CODE;;will be taken.
1821::CODE;;fit_intercept : bool, default=True
1822::CODE;;Whether the intercept should be estimated or not. Defaults to True.
1823::CODE;;max_iter : int, default=1000
1824::CODE;;The maximum number of passes over the training data (aka epochs).
1825::CODE;;It only impacts the behavior in the ``fit`` method, and not the
1826::CODE;;`partial_fit`. Defaults to 1000.
1827::CODE;;Values must be in the range `[1, inf)`.
1828::CODE;;tol : float or None, default=1e-3
1829::CODE;;The stopping criterion. If it is not None, the iterations will stop
1830::CODE;;when (loss > previous_loss - tol). Defaults to 1e-3.
1831::CODE;;Values must be in the range `[0.0, inf)`.
1832::CODE;;shuffle : bool, default=True
1833::CODE;;Whether or not the training data should be shuffled after each epoch.
1834::CODE;;Defaults to True.
1835::CODE;;verbose : int, default=0
1836::CODE;;The verbosity level.
1837::CODE;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
1838::CODE;;The seed of the pseudo random number generator to use when shuffling
1839::CODE;;the data. If int, random_state is the seed used by the random number
1840::CODE;;generator; If RandomState instance, random_state is the random number
1841::CODE;;generator; If None, the random number generator is the RandomState
1842::CODE;;instance used by `np.random`.
1843::CODE;;learning_rate : {'constant', 'optimal', 'invscaling', 'adaptive'}, default='optimal'
1844::CODE;;The learning rate schedule to use with `fit`. (If using `partial_fit`,
1845::CODE;;learning rate must be controlled directly).
1846::CODE;;- 'constant': `eta = eta0`
1847::CODE;;- 'optimal': `eta = 1.0 / (alpha * (t + t0))`
1848::CODE;;where t0 is chosen by a heuristic proposed by Leon Bottou.
1849::CODE;;- 'invscaling': `eta = eta0 / pow(t, power_t)`
1850::CODE;;- 'adaptive': eta = eta0, as long as the training keeps decreasing.
1851::CODE;;Each time n_iter_no_change consecutive epochs fail to decrease the
1852::CODE;;training loss by tol or fail to increase validation score by tol if
1853::CODE;;early_stopping is True, the current learning rate is divided by 5.
1854::CODE;;eta0 : float, default=0.01
1855::CODE;;The initial learning rate for the 'constant', 'invscaling' or
1856::CODE;;'adaptive' schedules. The default value is 0.0, but note that eta0 is not used
1857::CODE;;by the default learning rate 'optimal'.
1858::CODE;;Values must be in the range `(0.0, inf)`.
1859::CODE;;power_t : float, default=0.5
1860::CODE;;The exponent for inverse scaling learning rate.
1861::CODE;;Values must be in the range `[0.0, inf)`.
1862::CODE;;.. deprecated:: 1.8
1863::CODE;;Negative values for `power_t` are deprecated in version 1.8 and will raise
1864::CODE;;an error in 1.10. Use values in the range [0.0, inf) instead.
1865::CODE;;warm_start : bool, default=False
1866::CODE;;When set to True, reuse the solution of the previous call to fit as
1867::CODE;;initialization, otherwise, just erase the previous solution.
1868::CODE;;See :term:`the Glossary <warm_start>`.
1869::CODE;;Repeatedly calling fit or partial_fit when warm_start is True can
1870::CODE;;result in a different solution than when calling fit a single time
1871::CODE;;because of the way the data is shuffled.
1872::CODE;;If a dynamic learning rate is used, the learning rate is adapted
1873::CODE;;depending on the number of samples already seen. Calling ``fit`` resets
1874::CODE;;this counter, while ``partial_fit`` will result in increasing the
1875::CODE;;existing counter.
1876::CODE;;average : bool or int, default=False
1877::CODE;;When set to True, computes the averaged SGD weights and stores the
1878::CODE;;result in the ``coef_`` attribute. If set to an int greater than 1,
1879::CODE;;averaging will begin once the total number of samples seen reaches
1880::CODE;;average. So ``average=10`` will begin averaging after seeing 10
1881::CODE;;samples.
1882::CODE;;Attributes
1883::CODE;;----------
1884::CODE;;coef_ : ndarray of shape (1, n_features)
1885::CODE;;Weights assigned to the features.
1886::CODE;;offset_ : ndarray of shape (1,)
1887::CODE;;Offset used to define the decision function from the raw scores.
1888::CODE;;We have the relation: decision_function = score_samples - offset.
1889::CODE;;n_iter_ : int
1890::CODE;;The actual number of iterations to reach the stopping criterion.
1891::CODE;;t_ : int
1892::CODE;;Number of weight updates performed during training.
1893::CODE;;Same as ``(n_iter_ * n_samples + 1)``.
1894::CODE;;n_features_in_ : int
1895::CODE;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
1896::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
1897::CODE;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
1898::CODE;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
1899::CODE;;has feature names that are all strings.
1900::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
1901::CODE;;See Also
1902::CODE;;--------
1903::CODE;;sklearn.svm.OneClassSVM : Unsupervised Outlier Detection.
1904::CODE;;Notes
1905::CODE;;-----
1906::CODE;;This estimator has a linear complexity in the number of training samples
1907::CODE;;and is thus better suited than the `sklearn.svm.OneClassSVM`
1908::CODE;;implementation for datasets with a large number of training samples (say
1909::CODE;;> 10,000).

22::CODE;;def _modified_weiszfeld_step(X, x_old):
44::CODE;;diff = X - x_old
45::CODE;;diff_norm = np.sqrt(np.sum(diff**2, axis=1))
46::CODE;;mask = diff_norm >= _EPSILON
48::CODE;;is_x_old_in_X = int(mask.sum() < X.shape[0])
49::CODE;;diff = diff[mask]
50::CODE;;diff_norm = diff_norm[mask][:, np.newaxis]
51::CODE;;quotient_norm = linalg.norm(np.sum(diff / diff_norm, axis=0))
53::CODE;;new_direction = np.sum(X[mask, :] / diff_norm, axis=0) / np.sum(
54::CODE;;1 / diff_norm, axis=0
55::CODE;;)
56::CODE;;else:
57::CODE;;new_direction = 1.0
58::CODE;;quotient_norm = 1.0
59::CODE;;return (
60::CODE;;max(0.0, 1.0 - is_x_old_in_X / quotient_norm) * new_direction
61::CODE;;+ min(1.0, is_x_old_in_X / quotient_norm) * x_old
62::CODE;;)

90::CODE;;if X.shape[1] == 1:
91::CODE;;return 1, np.median(X.ravel(), keepdims=True)
93::CODE;;spatial_median_old = np.mean(X, axis=0)
94::CODE;;for n_iter in range(max_iter):
95::CODE;;spatial_median = _modified_weiszfeld_step(X, spatial_median_old)
96::CODE;;if np.sum((spatial_median_old - spatial_median) ** 2) < tol:

130::CODE;;def _lstsq(X, y, indices, fit_intercept):
151::CODE;;fit_intercept = int(fit_intercept)
152::CODE;;n_features = X.shape[1] + fit_intercept
153::CODE;;n_subsamples = indices.shape[1]
154::CODE;;weights = np.empty((indices.shape[0], n_features))
155::CODE;;X_subpopulation = np.ones((n_subsamples, n_features))

304::CODE;;"".format(plus_1, n_dim, n_subsamples)
305::CODE;;)
307::CODE;;if n_subsamples != n_samples:
308::CODE;;raise ValueError(
309::CODE;;"Invalid parameter since n_subsamples != "
310::CODE;;"n_samples ({0} != {1}) while n_samples "
311::CODE;;"< n_features.".format(n_subsamples, n_samples)
312::CODE;;)
313::CODE;;else:
314::CODE;;n_subsamples = min(n_dim, n_samples)
315::CODE;;all_combinations = max(1, np.rint(binom(n_samples, n_subsamples)))
316::CODE;;n_subpopulation = int(min(self.max_subpopulation, all_combinations))
317::CODE;;return n_subsamples, n_subpopulation
318::CODE;;@_fit_context(prefer_skip_nested_validation=True)
319::CODE;;def fit(self, X, y):
332::CODE;;random_state = check_random_state(self.random_state)
333::CODE;;X, y = validate_data(self, X, y, y_numeric=True)
334::CODE;;n_samples, n_features = X.shape
335::CODE;;n_subsamples, self.n_subpopulation_ = self._check_subparams(
336::CODE;;n_samples, n_features
337::CODE;;)
338::CODE;;self.breakdown_ = _breakdown_point(n_samples, n_subsamples)
339::CODE;;if self.verbose:
340::CODE;;print("Breakdown point: {0}".format(self.breakdown_))
341::CODE;;print("Number of samples: {0}".format(n_samples))
342::CODE;;tol_outliers = int(self.breakdown_ * n_samples)
343::CODE;;print("Tolerable outliers: {0}".format(tol_outliers))
344::CODE;;print("Number of subpopulations: {0}".format(self.n_subpopulation_))
346::CODE;;if np.rint(binom(n_samples, n_subsamples)) <= self.max_subpopulation:
347::CODE;;indices = list(combinations(range(n_samples), n_subsamples))
348::CODE;;else:
349::CODE;;indices = [
350::CODE;;random_state.choice(n_samples, size=n_subsamples, replace=False)
351::CODE;;for _ in range(self.n_subpopulation_)
352::CODE;;]
353::CODE;;n_jobs = effective_n_jobs(self.n_jobs)
354::CODE;;index_list = np.array_split(indices, n_jobs)
355::CODE;;weights = Parallel(n_jobs=n_jobs, verbose=self.verbose)(
356::CODE;;delayed(_lstsq)(X, y, index_list[job], self.fit_intercept)
357::CODE;;for job in range(n_jobs)
358::CODE;;)
359::CODE;;weights = np.vstack(weights)
360::CODE;;self.n_iter_, coefs = _spatial_median(
361::CODE;;weights, max_iter=self.max_iter, tol=self.tol
362::CODE;;)
363::CODE;;if self.fit_intercept:
364::CODE;;self.intercept_ = coefs[0]
365::CODE;;self.coef_ = coefs[1:]
366::CODE;;else:
367::CODE;;self.intercept_ = 0.0
368::CODE;;self.coef_ = coefs
369::CODE;;return self

245::CODE;;def test_lasso_dual_gap():
250::CODE;;X, y, _, _ = build_dataset(n_samples=10, n_features=30)
251::CODE;;n_samples = len(y)
252::CODE;;alpha = 0.01 * np.max(np.abs(X.T @ y)) / n_samples
253::CODE;;clf = Lasso(alpha=alpha, fit_intercept=False).fit(X, y)
254::CODE;;w = clf.coef_
255::CODE;;R = y - X @ w
256::CODE;;primal = 0.5 * np.mean(R**2) + clf.alpha * np.sum(np.abs(w))
258::CODE;;R /= np.max(np.abs(X.T @ R) / (n_samples * alpha))
259::CODE;;dual = 0.5 * (np.mean(y**2) - np.mean((y - R) ** 2))
260::CODE;;assert_allclose(clf.dual_gap_, primal - dual)

28::CODE;;class MyPassiveAggressive(ClassifierMixin):
29::CODE;;def __init__(
30::CODE;;self,
31::CODE;;C=1.0,
32::CODE;;epsilon=DEFAULT_EPSILON,
33::CODE;;loss="hinge",
34::CODE;;fit_intercept=True,
35::CODE;;n_iter=1,
36::CODE;;random_state=None,
37::CODE;;):
38::CODE;;self.C = C
39::CODE;;self.epsilon = epsilon
40::CODE;;self.loss = loss
41::CODE;;self.fit_intercept = fit_intercept
42::CODE;;self.n_iter = n_iter
43::CODE;;def fit(self, X, y):
44::CODE;;n_samples, n_features = X.shape
45::CODE;;self.w = np.zeros(n_features, dtype=np.float64)
46::CODE;;self.b = 0.0
48::CODE;;intercept_decay = 1.0
49::CODE;;if issparse(X):
50::CODE;;intercept_decay = SPARSE_INTERCEPT_DECAY
51::CODE;;X = X.toarray()
52::CODE;;for t in range(self.n_iter):
53::CODE;;for i in range(n_samples):
54::CODE;;p = self.project(X[i])
55::CODE;;if self.loss in ("hinge", "squared_hinge"):
56::CODE;;loss = max(1 - y[i] * p, 0)
57::CODE;;else:
58::CODE;;loss = max(np.abs(p - y[i]) - self.epsilon, 0)
59::CODE;;sqnorm = np.dot(X[i], X[i])
60::CODE;;if self.loss in ("hinge", "epsilon_insensitive"):
61::CODE;;step = min(self.C, loss / sqnorm)
62::CODE;;elif self.loss in ("squared_hinge", "squared_epsilon_insensitive"):
63::CODE;;step = loss / (sqnorm + 1.0 / (2 * self.C))
64::CODE;;if self.loss in ("hinge", "squared_hinge"):
65::CODE;;step *= y[i]
66::CODE;;else:
67::CODE;;step *= np.sign(y[i] - p)
68::CODE;;self.w += step * X[i]
69::CODE;;if self.fit_intercept:
70::CODE;;self.b += intercept_decay * step
71::CODE;;def project(self, X):
72::CODE;;return np.dot(X, self.w) + self.b

595::CODE;;def _make_sparse_offset_regression(
596::CODE;;n_samples=100,
597::CODE;;n_features=100,
598::CODE;;proportion_nonzero=0.5,
599::CODE;;n_informative=10,
600::CODE;;n_targets=1,
601::CODE;;bias=13.0,
602::CODE;;X_offset=30.0,
603::CODE;;noise=30.0,
604::CODE;;shuffle=True,
605::CODE;;coef=False,
606::CODE;;positive=False,
607::CODE;;random_state=None,
608::CODE;;):
609::CODE;;X, y, c = make_regression(
610::CODE;;n_samples=n_samples,
611::CODE;;n_features=n_features,
612::CODE;;n_informative=n_informative,
613::CODE;;n_targets=n_targets,
614::CODE;;bias=bias,
615::CODE;;noise=noise,
616::CODE;;shuffle=shuffle,
617::CODE;;coef=True,
618::CODE;;random_state=random_state,
619::CODE;;)
620::CODE;;if n_features == 1:
621::CODE;;c = np.asarray([c])
622::CODE;;X += X_offset
623::CODE;;mask = (
624::CODE;;np.random.RandomState(random_state).binomial(1, proportion_nonzero, X.shape) > 0
625::CODE;;)
626::CODE;;removed_X = X.copy()
627::CODE;;X[~mask] = 0.0
628::CODE;;removed_X[mask] = 0.0
629::CODE;;y -= removed_X.dot(c)
630::CODE;;if positive:
631::CODE;;y += X.dot(np.abs(c) + 1 - c)
632::CODE;;c = np.abs(c) + 1
633::CODE;;if n_features == 1:
634::CODE;;c = c[0]
635::CODE;;if coef:
636::CODE;;return X, y, c
637::CODE;;return X, y

1830::CODE;;def test_lbfgs_solver_error():
1852::CODE;;Note that this test is stricter than the common test
1853::CODE;;check_sample_weight_equivalence alone.
1939::CODE;;The GCV approach works on scaled data: centered by an offset and scaled by the
1940::CODE;;square root of the sample weights. Thus, prior to computing scores, the
1941::CODE;;predictions need to be scaled back to the original scale. These predictions are
1942::CODE;;the ones stored in `cv_results_` in `RidgeCV`.
1943::CODE;;In this test, we check that the internal predictions stored in `cv_results_` are
1944::CODE;;equivalent to a naive LOO-CV grid search with a `Ridge` estimator.
1945::CODE;;Non-regression test for:
1946::CODE;;https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/issues/13998
1974::CODE;;when `scoring != None`.
1975::CODE;;We check the error reported by the RidgeCV is close to a naive LOO-CV using a
1976::CODE;;Ridge estimator.

1999::CODE;;if mean_errors.ndim == 1:
2001::CODE;;return -np.average(mean_errors, weights=[2, 1])

23::CODE;;def log_dloss(p, y):
24::CODE;;z = p * y
26::CODE;;if z > 18.0:
27::CODE;;return math.exp(-z) * -y
28::CODE;;if z < -18.0:
29::CODE;;return -y
30::CODE;;return -y / (math.exp(z) + 1.0)
31::CODE;;def log_loss(p, y):
32::CODE;;return np.mean(np.log(1.0 + np.exp(-y * p)))
34::CODE;;def squared_dloss(p, y):
35::CODE;;return p - y
36::CODE;;def squared_loss(p, y):
37::CODE;;return np.mean(0.5 * (p - y) * (p - y))
39::CODE;;def get_pobj(w, alpha, myX, myy, loss):
40::CODE;;w = w.ravel()
41::CODE;;pred = np.dot(myX, w)
42::CODE;;p = loss(pred, myy)
43::CODE;;p += alpha * w.dot(w) / 2.0
44::CODE;;return p
45::CODE;;def sag(
46::CODE;;X,
47::CODE;;y,
48::CODE;;step_size,
49::CODE;;alpha,
50::CODE;;n_iter=1,
51::CODE;;dloss=None,
52::CODE;;sparse=False,
53::CODE;;sample_weight=None,
54::CODE;;fit_intercept=True,
55::CODE;;saga=False,
56::CODE;;):
57::CODE;;n_samples, n_features = X.shape[0], X.shape[1]
58::CODE;;weights = np.zeros(X.shape[1])
59::CODE;;sum_gradient = np.zeros(X.shape[1])
60::CODE;;gradient_memory = np.zeros((n_samples, n_features))
61::CODE;;intercept = 0.0
62::CODE;;intercept_sum_gradient = 0.0
63::CODE;;intercept_gradient_memory = np.zeros(n_samples)
64::CODE;;rng = np.random.RandomState(77)
65::CODE;;decay = 1.0
66::CODE;;seen = set()
68::CODE;;if sparse:
69::CODE;;decay = 0.01
70::CODE;;for epoch in range(n_iter):
71::CODE;;for k in range(n_samples):
72::CODE;;idx = int(rng.rand() * n_samples)
74::CODE;;entry = X[idx]
75::CODE;;seen.add(idx)
76::CODE;;p = np.dot(entry, weights) + intercept
77::CODE;;gradient = dloss(p, y[idx])
78::CODE;;if sample_weight is not None:
79::CODE;;gradient *= sample_weight[idx]
80::CODE;;update = entry * gradient + alpha * weights
81::CODE;;gradient_correction = update - gradient_memory[idx]
82::CODE;;sum_gradient += gradient_correction
83::CODE;;gradient_memory[idx] = update
84::CODE;;if saga:
85::CODE;;weights -= gradient_correction * step_size * (1 - 1.0 / len(seen))
86::CODE;;if fit_intercept:
87::CODE;;gradient_correction = gradient - intercept_gradient_memory[idx]
88::CODE;;intercept_gradient_memory[idx] = gradient
89::CODE;;intercept_sum_gradient += gradient_correction
90::CODE;;gradient_correction *= step_size * (1.0 - 1.0 / len(seen))
91::CODE;;if saga:
92::CODE;;intercept -= (
93::CODE;;step_size * intercept_sum_gradient / len(seen) * decay
94::CODE;;) + gradient_correction
95::CODE;;else:
96::CODE;;intercept -= step_size * intercept_sum_gradient / len(seen) * decay
97::CODE;;weights -= step_size * sum_gradient / len(seen)
98::CODE;;return weights, intercept
99::CODE;;def sag_sparse(
100::CODE;;X,
101::CODE;;y,
102::CODE;;step_size,
103::CODE;;alpha,
104::CODE;;n_iter=1,
105::CODE;;dloss=None,
106::CODE;;sample_weight=None,
107::CODE;;sparse=False,
108::CODE;;fit_intercept=True,
109::CODE;;saga=False,
110::CODE;;random_state=0,
111::CODE;;):
112::CODE;;if step_size * alpha == 1.0:
113::CODE;;raise ZeroDivisionError(
114::CODE;;"Sparse sag does not handle the case step_size * alpha == 1"
115::CODE;;)
116::CODE;;n_samples, n_features = X.shape[0], X.shape[1]
117::CODE;;weights = np.zeros(n_features)
118::CODE;;sum_gradient = np.zeros(n_features)
119::CODE;;last_updated = np.zeros(n_features, dtype=int)
120::CODE;;gradient_memory = np.zeros(n_samples)
121::CODE;;rng = check_random_state(random_state)
122::CODE;;intercept = 0.0
123::CODE;;intercept_sum_gradient = 0.0
124::CODE;;wscale = 1.0
125::CODE;;decay = 1.0
126::CODE;;seen = set()
127::CODE;;c_sum = np.zeros(n_iter * n_samples)
129::CODE;;if sparse:
130::CODE;;decay = 0.01
131::CODE;;counter = 0
132::CODE;;for epoch in range(n_iter):
133::CODE;;for k in range(n_samples):
135::CODE;;idx = int(rng.rand() * n_samples)
136::CODE;;entry = X[idx]
137::CODE;;seen.add(idx)
138::CODE;;if counter >= 1:
139::CODE;;for j in range(n_features):
140::CODE;;if last_updated[j] == 0:
141::CODE;;weights[j] -= c_sum[counter - 1] * sum_gradient[j]
142::CODE;;else:
143::CODE;;weights[j] -= (
144::CODE;;c_sum[counter - 1] - c_sum[last_updated[j] - 1]
145::CODE;;) * sum_gradient[j]
146::CODE;;last_updated[j] = counter
147::CODE;;p = (wscale * np.dot(entry, weights)) + intercept
148::CODE;;gradient = dloss(p, y[idx])
149::CODE;;if sample_weight is not None:
150::CODE;;gradient *= sample_weight[idx]
151::CODE;;update = entry * gradient
152::CODE;;gradient_correction = update - (gradient_memory[idx] * entry)
153::CODE;;sum_gradient += gradient_correction
154::CODE;;if saga:
155::CODE;;for j in range(n_features):
156::CODE;;weights[j] -= (
157::CODE;;gradient_correction[j]
158::CODE;;* step_size
159::CODE;;* (1 - 1.0 / len(seen))
160::CODE;;/ wscale
161::CODE;;)
162::CODE;;if fit_intercept:
163::CODE;;gradient_correction = gradient - gradient_memory[idx]
164::CODE;;intercept_sum_gradient += gradient_correction
165::CODE;;gradient_correction *= step_size * (1.0 - 1.0 / len(seen))
166::CODE;;if saga:
167::CODE;;intercept -= (
168::CODE;;step_size * intercept_sum_gradient / len(seen) * decay
169::CODE;;) + gradient_correction
170::CODE;;else:
171::CODE;;intercept -= step_size * intercept_sum_gradient / len(seen) * decay
172::CODE;;gradient_memory[idx] = gradient
173::CODE;;wscale *= 1.0 - alpha * step_size
174::CODE;;if counter == 0:
175::CODE;;c_sum[0] = step_size / (wscale * len(seen))
176::CODE;;else:
177::CODE;;c_sum[counter] = c_sum[counter - 1] + step_size / (wscale * len(seen))
178::CODE;;if counter >= 1 and wscale < 1e-9:
179::CODE;;for j in range(n_features):
180::CODE;;if last_updated[j] == 0:
181::CODE;;weights[j] -= c_sum[counter] * sum_gradient[j]
182::CODE;;else:
183::CODE;;weights[j] -= (
184::CODE;;c_sum[counter] - c_sum[last_updated[j] - 1]
185::CODE;;) * sum_gradient[j]
186::CODE;;last_updated[j] = counter + 1
187::CODE;;c_sum[counter] = 0
188::CODE;;weights *= wscale
189::CODE;;wscale = 1.0
190::CODE;;counter += 1
191::CODE;;for j in range(n_features):
192::CODE;;if last_updated[j] == 0:
193::CODE;;weights[j] -= c_sum[counter - 1] * sum_gradient[j]
194::CODE;;else:
195::CODE;;weights[j] -= (
196::CODE;;c_sum[counter - 1] - c_sum[last_updated[j] - 1]
197::CODE;;) * sum_gradient[j]
198::CODE;;weights *= wscale
199::CODE;;return weights, intercept
200::CODE;;def get_step_size(X, alpha, fit_intercept, classification=True):
201::CODE;;if classification:
202::CODE;;return 4.0 / (np.max(np.sum(X * X, axis=1)) + fit_intercept + 4.0 * alpha)
203::CODE;;else:
204::CODE;;return 1.0 / (np.max(np.sum(X * X, axis=1)) + fit_intercept + alpha)

148::CODE;;def asgd(klass, X, y, eta, alpha, weight_init=None, intercept_init=0.0):
149::CODE;;if weight_init is None:
150::CODE;;weights = np.zeros(X.shape[1])
151::CODE;;else:
152::CODE;;weights = weight_init
153::CODE;;average_weights = np.zeros(X.shape[1])
154::CODE;;intercept = intercept_init
155::CODE;;average_intercept = 0.0
156::CODE;;decay = 1.0
158::CODE;;if klass in (SparseSGDClassifier, SparseSGDRegressor):
159::CODE;;decay = 0.01
160::CODE;;for i, entry in enumerate(X):
161::CODE;;p = np.dot(entry, weights)
162::CODE;;p += intercept
163::CODE;;gradient = p - y[i]
164::CODE;;weights *= 1.0 - (eta * alpha)
165::CODE;;weights += -(eta * gradient * entry)
166::CODE;;intercept += -(eta * gradient) * decay
167::CODE;;average_weights *= i
168::CODE;;average_weights += weights
169::CODE;;average_weights /= i + 1.0
170::CODE;;average_intercept *= i
171::CODE;;average_intercept += intercept
172::CODE;;average_intercept /= i + 1.0
173::CODE;;return average_weights, average_intercept

6::CODE;;from numbers import Integral
7::CODE;;import numpy as np
8::CODE;;from scipy import linalg
9::CODE;;from sklearn.base import BaseEstimator, _fit_context
10::CODE;;from sklearn.metrics import pairwise_distances
11::CODE;;from sklearn.utils import check_symmetric
12::CODE;;from sklearn.utils._param_validation import Interval
13::CODE;;from sklearn.utils.extmath import svd_flip
14::CODE;;from sklearn.utils.validation import validate_data
15::CODE;;class ClassicalMDS(BaseEstimator):
75::CODE;;_parameter_constraints: dict = {
76::CODE;;"n_components": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
77::CODE;;"metric": [str, callable],
78::CODE;;"metric_params": [dict, None],
79::CODE;;}
80::CODE;;def __init__(
81::CODE;;self,
82::CODE;;n_components=2,
83::CODE;;*,
84::CODE;;metric="euclidean",
85::CODE;;metric_params=None,
86::CODE;;):
87::CODE;;self.n_components = n_components
88::CODE;;self.metric = metric
89::CODE;;self.metric_params = metric_params
90::CODE;;def __sklearn_tags__(self):
91::CODE;;tags = super().__sklearn_tags__()
92::CODE;;tags.input_tags.pairwise = self.metric == "precomputed"
93::CODE;;return tags
94::CODE;;def fit(self, X, y=None):
110::CODE;;self.fit_transform(X)
111::CODE;;return self
112::CODE;;@_fit_context(prefer_skip_nested_validation=True)
113::CODE;;def fit_transform(self, X, y=None):
129::CODE;;X = validate_data(self, X)
130::CODE;;if self.metric == "precomputed":
131::CODE;;self.dissimilarity_matrix_ = X
132::CODE;;self.dissimilarity_matrix_ = check_symmetric(
133::CODE;;self.dissimilarity_matrix_, raise_exception=True
134::CODE;;)
135::CODE;;else:
136::CODE;;self.dissimilarity_matrix_ = pairwise_distances(
137::CODE;;X,
138::CODE;;metric=self.metric,
139::CODE;;**(self.metric_params if self.metric_params is not None else {}),
140::CODE;;)
142::CODE;;B = self.dissimilarity_matrix_**2
143::CODE;;B = B.astype(np.float64)
144::CODE;;B -= np.mean(B, axis=0)
145::CODE;;B -= np.mean(B, axis=1, keepdims=True)
146::CODE;;B *= -0.5
148::CODE;;w, U = linalg.eigh(B)
151::CODE;;w = w[::-1][: self.n_components]
152::CODE;;U = U[:, ::-1][:, : self.n_components]
154::CODE;;U, _ = svd_flip(U, None)
155::CODE;;self.embedding_ = np.sqrt(w) * U
156::CODE;;self.eigenvalues_ = w
157::CODE;;return self.embedding_
24::CODE;;Non-linear dimensionality reduction through Isometric Mapping
25::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <isomap>`.
26::CODE;;Parameters
27::CODE;;----------
28::CODE;;n_neighbors : int or None, default=5
29::CODE;;Number of neighbors to consider for each point. If `n_neighbors` is an int,
30::CODE;;then `radius` must be `None`.
31::CODE;;radius : float or None, default=None
32::CODE;;Limiting distance of neighbors to return. If `radius` is a float,
33::CODE;;then `n_neighbors` must be set to `None`.
34::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.1
35::CODE;;n_components : int, default=2
36::CODE;;Number of coordinates for the manifold.
37::CODE;;eigen_solver : {'auto', 'arpack', 'dense'}, default='auto'
38::CODE;;'auto' : Attempt to choose the most efficient solver
39::CODE;;for the given problem.
40::CODE;;'arpack' : Use Arnoldi decomposition to find the eigenvalues
41::CODE;;and eigenvectors.
42::CODE;;'dense' : Use a direct solver (i.e. LAPACK)
43::CODE;;for the eigenvalue decomposition.
44::CODE;;tol : float, default=0
45::CODE;;Convergence tolerance passed to arpack or lobpcg.
46::CODE;;not used if eigen_solver == 'dense'.
47::CODE;;max_iter : int, default=None
48::CODE;;Maximum number of iterations for the arpack solver.
49::CODE;;not used if eigen_solver == 'dense'.
50::CODE;;path_method : {'auto', 'FW', 'D'}, default='auto'
51::CODE;;Method to use in finding shortest path.
52::CODE;;'auto' : attempt to choose the best algorithm automatically.
53::CODE;;'FW' : Floyd-Warshall algorithm.
54::CODE;;'D' : Dijkstra's algorithm.
55::CODE;;neighbors_algorithm : {'auto', 'brute', 'kd_tree', 'ball_tree'}, \
56::CODE;;default='auto'
57::CODE;;Algorithm to use for nearest neighbors search,
58::CODE;;passed to neighbors.NearestNeighbors instance.
59::CODE;;n_jobs : int or None, default=None
60::CODE;;The number of parallel jobs to run.
61::CODE;;``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
62::CODE;;``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
63::CODE;;for more details.
64::CODE;;metric : str, or callable, default="minkowski"
65::CODE;;The metric to use when calculating distance between instances in a
66::CODE;;feature array. If metric is a string or callable, it must be one of
67::CODE;;the options allowed by :func:`sklearn.metrics.pairwise_distances` for
68::CODE;;its metric parameter.
69::CODE;;If metric is "precomputed", X is assumed to be a distance matrix and
70::CODE;;must be square. X may be a :term:`Glossary <sparse graph>`.
71::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.22
72::CODE;;p : float, default=2
73::CODE;;Parameter for the Minkowski metric from
74::CODE;;sklearn.metrics.pairwise.pairwise_distances. When p = 1, this is
75::CODE;;equivalent to using manhattan_distance (l1), and euclidean_distance
76::CODE;;(l2) for p = 2. For arbitrary p, minkowski_distance (l_p) is used.
77::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.22
78::CODE;;metric_params : dict, default=None
79::CODE;;Additional keyword arguments for the metric function.
80::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.22
81::CODE;;Attributes
82::CODE;;----------
83::CODE;;embedding_ : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_components)
84::CODE;;Stores the embedding vectors.
85::CODE;;kernel_pca_ : object
86::CODE;;:class:`~sklearn.decomposition.KernelPCA` object used to implement the
87::CODE;;embedding.
88::CODE;;nbrs_ : sklearn.neighbors.NearestNeighbors instance
89::CODE;;Stores nearest neighbors instance, including BallTree or KDtree
90::CODE;;if applicable.
91::CODE;;dist_matrix_ : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_samples)
92::CODE;;Stores the geodesic distance matrix of training data.
93::CODE;;n_features_in_ : int
94::CODE;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
95::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
96::CODE;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
97::CODE;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
98::CODE;;has feature names that are all strings.
99::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
100::CODE;;See Also
101::CODE;;--------
102::CODE;;sklearn.decomposition.PCA : Principal component analysis that is a linear
103::CODE;;dimensionality reduction method.
104::CODE;;sklearn.decomposition.KernelPCA : Non-linear dimensionality reduction using
105::CODE;;kernels and PCA.
106::CODE;;MDS : Manifold learning using multidimensional scaling.
107::CODE;;TSNE : T-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding.
108::CODE;;LocallyLinearEmbedding : Manifold learning using Locally Linear Embedding.
109::CODE;;SpectralEmbedding : Spectral embedding for non-linear dimensionality.
110::CODE;;References
111::CODE;;----------
112::CODE;;.. [1] Tenenbaum, J.B.; De Silva, V.; & Langford, J.C. A global geometric
113::CODE;;framework for nonlinear dimensionality reduction. Science 290 (5500)
114::CODE;;Examples
115::CODE;;--------
116::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.datasets import load_digits
117::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.manifold import Isomap
118::CODE;;>>> X, _ = load_digits(return_X_y=True)
119::CODE;;>>> X.shape
120::CODE;;(1797, 64)
121::CODE;;>>> embedding = Isomap(n_components=2)
122::CODE;;>>> X_transformed = embedding.fit_transform(X[:100])
123::CODE;;>>> X_transformed.shape
124::CODE;;(100, 2)
261::CODE;;Returns
262::CODE;;-------
263::CODE;;reconstruction_error : float
264::CODE;;Reconstruction error.
265::CODE;;Notes
266::CODE;;-----
267::CODE;;The cost function of an isomap embedding is
268::CODE;;``E = frobenius_norm[K(D) - K(D_fit)] / n_samples``
269::CODE;;Where D is the matrix of distances for the input data X,
270::CODE;;D_fit is the matrix of distances for the output embedding X_fit,
271::CODE;;and K is the isomap kernel:
272::CODE;;``K(D) = -0.5 * (I - 1/n_samples) * D^2 * (I - 1/n_samples)``
284::CODE;;Parameters
285::CODE;;----------
286::CODE;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix, BallTree, KDTree, NearestNeighbors}
287::CODE;;Sample data, shape = (n_samples, n_features), in the form of a
288::CODE;;numpy array, sparse matrix, precomputed tree, or NearestNeighbors
289::CODE;;object.
290::CODE;;y : Ignored
291::CODE;;Not used, present for API consistency by convention.
292::CODE;;Returns
293::CODE;;-------
294::CODE;;self : object
295::CODE;;Returns a fitted instance of self.
305::CODE;;Parameters
306::CODE;;----------
307::CODE;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix, BallTree, KDTree}
308::CODE;;Training vector, where `n_samples` is the number of samples
309::CODE;;and `n_features` is the number of features.
310::CODE;;y : Ignored
311::CODE;;Not used, present for API consistency by convention.
312::CODE;;Returns
313::CODE;;-------
314::CODE;;X_new : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_components)
315::CODE;;X transformed in the new space.
321::CODE;;This is implemented by linking the points X into the graph of geodesic
322::CODE;;distances of the training data. First the `n_neighbors` nearest
323::CODE;;neighbors of X are found in the training data, and from these the
324::CODE;;shortest geodesic distances from each point in X to each point in
325::CODE;;the training data are computed in order to construct the kernel.
326::CODE;;The embedding of X is the projection of this kernel onto the
327::CODE;;embedding vectors of the training set.
328::CODE;;Parameters
329::CODE;;----------
330::CODE;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix}, shape (n_queries, n_features)
331::CODE;;If neighbors_algorithm='precomputed', X is assumed to be a

6::CODE;;import warnings
7::CODE;;from numbers import Integral, Real
8::CODE;;import numpy as np
9::CODE;;from joblib import effective_n_jobs
10::CODE;;from sklearn.base import BaseEstimator, _fit_context
11::CODE;;from sklearn.isotonic import IsotonicRegression
12::CODE;;from sklearn.manifold import ClassicalMDS
13::CODE;;from sklearn.metrics import euclidean_distances, pairwise_distances
14::CODE;;from sklearn.utils import check_array, check_random_state, check_symmetric
15::CODE;;from sklearn.utils._param_validation import (
16::CODE;;Hidden,

21::CODE;;from sklearn.utils.parallel import Parallel, delayed

23::CODE;;def _smacof_single(
24::CODE;;dissimilarities,
25::CODE;;metric=True,
26::CODE;;n_components=2,
27::CODE;;init=None,
28::CODE;;max_iter=300,
29::CODE;;verbose=0,
30::CODE;;eps=1e-6,
31::CODE;;random_state=None,
32::CODE;;normalized_stress=False,
33::CODE;;):
92::CODE;;dissimilarities = check_symmetric(dissimilarities, raise_exception=True)
93::CODE;;n_samples = dissimilarities.shape[0]
94::CODE;;random_state = check_random_state(random_state)
95::CODE;;dissimilarities_flat = ((1 - np.tri(n_samples)) * dissimilarities).ravel()
96::CODE;;dissimilarities_flat_w = dissimilarities_flat[dissimilarities_flat != 0]
97::CODE;;if init is None:
99::CODE;;X = random_state.uniform(size=n_samples * n_components)
100::CODE;;X = X.reshape((n_samples, n_components))
101::CODE;;else:
103::CODE;;n_components = init.shape[1]
104::CODE;;if n_samples != init.shape[0]:
105::CODE;;raise ValueError(
106::CODE;;"init matrix should be of shape (%d, %d)" % (n_samples, n_components)
107::CODE;;)
108::CODE;;X = init
109::CODE;;distances = euclidean_distances(X)
113::CODE;;ir = IsotonicRegression(out_of_bounds="clip")
114::CODE;;old_stress = None
115::CODE;;for it in range(max_iter):
117::CODE;;if metric:
118::CODE;;disparities = dissimilarities
119::CODE;;else:
120::CODE;;distances_flat = distances.ravel()
122::CODE;;distances_flat_w = distances_flat[dissimilarities_flat != 0]
127::CODE;;if it < 1:
128::CODE;;disparities_flat = dissimilarities_flat_w
129::CODE;;else:
130::CODE;;disparities_flat = ir.fit_transform(
131::CODE;;dissimilarities_flat_w, distances_flat_w
132::CODE;;)
133::CODE;;disparities = np.zeros_like(distances_flat)
134::CODE;;disparities[dissimilarities_flat != 0] = disparities_flat
135::CODE;;disparities = disparities.reshape((n_samples, n_samples))
136::CODE;;disparities *= np.sqrt(
137::CODE;;(n_samples * (n_samples - 1) / 2) / (disparities**2).sum()
138::CODE;;)
139::CODE;;disparities = disparities + disparities.T
141::CODE;;distances[distances == 0] = 1e-5
142::CODE;;ratio = disparities / distances
143::CODE;;B = -ratio
144::CODE;;B[np.arange(len(B)), np.arange(len(B))] += ratio.sum(axis=1)
145::CODE;;X = 1.0 / n_samples * np.dot(B, X)
147::CODE;;distances = euclidean_distances(X)
148::CODE;;stress = ((distances.ravel() - disparities.ravel()) ** 2).sum() / 2
150::CODE;;print(f"Iteration {it}, stress {stress:.4f}")
151::CODE;;if old_stress is not None:
152::CODE;;sum_squared_distances = (distances.ravel() ** 2).sum()
153::CODE;;if ((old_stress - stress) / (sum_squared_distances / 2)) < eps:
155::CODE;;print(f"Convergence criterion reached (iteration {it}).")
156::CODE;;break
157::CODE;;old_stress = stress
158::CODE;;if normalized_stress:
159::CODE;;sum_squared_distances = (distances.ravel() ** 2).sum()
160::CODE;;stress = np.sqrt(stress / (sum_squared_distances / 2))
161::CODE;;return X, stress, it + 1
163::CODE;;@validate_params(
164::CODE;;{
165::CODE;;"dissimilarities": ["array-like"],
166::CODE;;"metric": ["boolean"],
167::CODE;;"n_components": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
168::CODE;;"init": ["array-like", None],
169::CODE;;"n_init": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left"), StrOptions({"warn"})],
170::CODE;;"n_jobs": [Integral, None],
171::CODE;;"max_iter": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
172::CODE;;"verbose": ["verbose"],

174::CODE;;"random_state": ["random_state"],
175::CODE;;"return_n_iter": ["boolean"],

178::CODE;;prefer_skip_nested_validation=True,

180::CODE;;def smacof(
181::CODE;;dissimilarities,
182::CODE;;*,
183::CODE;;metric=True,
184::CODE;;n_components=2,
185::CODE;;init=None,
186::CODE;;n_init="warn",
187::CODE;;n_jobs=None,
188::CODE;;max_iter=300,
189::CODE;;verbose=0,
190::CODE;;eps=1e-6,
191::CODE;;random_state=None,
192::CODE;;return_n_iter=False,
193::CODE;;normalized_stress="auto",
194::CODE;;):
301::CODE;;if n_init == "warn":
302::CODE;;warnings.warn(
303::CODE;;"The default value of `n_init` will change from 8 to 1 in 1.9.",
304::CODE;;FutureWarning,
305::CODE;;)
306::CODE;;n_init = 8
307::CODE;;dissimilarities = check_array(dissimilarities)
308::CODE;;random_state = check_random_state(random_state)
309::CODE;;if normalized_stress == "auto":
310::CODE;;normalized_stress = not metric
311::CODE;;if hasattr(init, "__array__"):
312::CODE;;init = np.asarray(init).copy()
313::CODE;;if not n_init == 1:
314::CODE;;warnings.warn(
315::CODE;;"Explicit initial positions passed: "
316::CODE;;"performing only one init of the MDS instead of %d" % n_init
317::CODE;;)
318::CODE;;n_init = 1
319::CODE;;best_pos, best_stress = None, None
320::CODE;;if effective_n_jobs(n_jobs) == 1:
321::CODE;;for it in range(n_init):
322::CODE;;pos, stress, n_iter_ = _smacof_single(
323::CODE;;dissimilarities,
324::CODE;;metric=metric,
325::CODE;;n_components=n_components,
326::CODE;;init=init,
327::CODE;;max_iter=max_iter,
328::CODE;;verbose=verbose,
329::CODE;;eps=eps,
330::CODE;;random_state=random_state,
331::CODE;;normalized_stress=normalized_stress,
332::CODE;;)
333::CODE;;if best_stress is None or stress < best_stress:
334::CODE;;best_stress = stress
335::CODE;;best_pos = pos.copy()
336::CODE;;best_iter = n_iter_
337::CODE;;else:
338::CODE;;seeds = random_state.randint(np.iinfo(np.int32).max, size=n_init)
339::CODE;;results = Parallel(n_jobs=n_jobs, verbose=max(verbose - 1, 0))(
340::CODE;;delayed(_smacof_single)(
341::CODE;;dissimilarities,
342::CODE;;metric=metric,
343::CODE;;n_components=n_components,
344::CODE;;init=init,
345::CODE;;max_iter=max_iter,
346::CODE;;verbose=verbose,
347::CODE;;eps=eps,
348::CODE;;random_state=seed,
349::CODE;;normalized_stress=normalized_stress,
350::CODE;;)
351::CODE;;for seed in seeds
352::CODE;;)
353::CODE;;positions, stress, n_iters = zip(*results)
354::CODE;;best = np.argmin(stress)
355::CODE;;best_stress = stress[best]
356::CODE;;best_pos = positions[best]
357::CODE;;best_iter = n_iters[best]
358::CODE;;if return_n_iter:
359::CODE;;return best_pos, best_stress, best_iter
360::CODE;;else:
361::CODE;;return best_pos, best_stress
366::CODE;;class MDS(BaseEstimator):

91::CODE;;sparse format well suited for eigenvalue decomposition.
92::CODE;;Parameters

100::CODE;;Returns
101::CODE;;-------
102::CODE;;laplacian : {array, sparse matrix}
103::CODE;;An array of matrix in a form that is well suited to fast
104::CODE;;eigenvalue decomposition, depending on the band width of the
105::CODE;;matrix.
152::CODE;;The adjacency matrix is used to compute a normalized graph Laplacian
153::CODE;;whose spectrum (especially the eigenvectors associated to the
154::CODE;;smallest eigenvalues) has an interpretation in terms of minimal
155::CODE;;number of cuts necessary to split the graph into comparably sized
156::CODE;;components.
157::CODE;;This embedding can also 'work' even if the ``adjacency`` variable is
158::CODE;;not strictly the adjacency matrix of a graph but more generally
159::CODE;;an affinity or similarity matrix between samples (for instance the
160::CODE;;heat kernel of a euclidean distance matrix or a k-NN matrix).
161::CODE;;However care must taken to always make the affinity matrix symmetric
162::CODE;;so that the eigenvector decomposition works as expected.
163::CODE;;Note : Laplacian Eigenmaps is the actual algorithm implemented here.
164::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <spectral_embedding>`.
165::CODE;;Parameters
166::CODE;;----------
167::CODE;;adjacency : {array-like, sparse graph} of shape (n_samples, n_samples)
168::CODE;;The adjacency matrix of the graph to embed.
169::CODE;;n_components : int, default=8
170::CODE;;The dimension of the projection subspace.
171::CODE;;eigen_solver : {'arpack', 'lobpcg', 'amg'}, default=None
172::CODE;;The eigenvalue decomposition strategy to use. AMG requires pyamg
173::CODE;;to be installed. It can be faster on very large, sparse problems,
174::CODE;;but may also lead to instabilities. If None, then ``'arpack'`` is
175::CODE;;used.
176::CODE;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
177::CODE;;A pseudo random number generator used for the initialization
178::CODE;;of the lobpcg eigen vectors decomposition when `eigen_solver ==
179::CODE;;'amg'`, and for the K-Means initialization. Use an int to make
180::CODE;;the results deterministic across calls (See
181::CODE;;:term:`Glossary <random_state>`).
182::CODE;;.. note::
183::CODE;;When using `eigen_solver == 'amg'`,
184::CODE;;it is necessary to also fix the global numpy seed with
185::CODE;;`np.random.seed(int)` to get deterministic results. See
186::CODE;;https://github.com/pyamg/pyamg/issues/139 for further
187::CODE;;information.
188::CODE;;eigen_tol : float, default="auto"
189::CODE;;Stopping criterion for eigendecomposition of the Laplacian matrix.
190::CODE;;If `eigen_tol="auto"` then the passed tolerance will depend on the
191::CODE;;`eigen_solver`:
192::CODE;;- If `eigen_solver="arpack"`, then `eigen_tol=0.0`;
193::CODE;;- If `eigen_solver="lobpcg"` or `eigen_solver="amg"`, then
194::CODE;;`eigen_tol=None` which configures the underlying `lobpcg` solver to
195::CODE;;automatically resolve the value according to their heuristics. See,
196::CODE;;:func:`scipy.sparse.linalg.lobpcg` for details.
197::CODE;;Note that when using `eigen_solver="amg"` values of `tol<1e-5` may lead
198::CODE;;to convergence issues and should be avoided.
199::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.2
200::CODE;;Added 'auto' option.
201::CODE;;norm_laplacian : bool, default=True
202::CODE;;If True, then compute symmetric normalized Laplacian.
203::CODE;;drop_first : bool, default=True
204::CODE;;Whether to drop the first eigenvector. For spectral embedding, this
205::CODE;;should be True as the first eigenvector should be constant vector for
206::CODE;;connected graph, but for spectral clustering, this should be kept as
207::CODE;;False to retain the first eigenvector.
208::CODE;;Returns
209::CODE;;-------
210::CODE;;embedding : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_components)
211::CODE;;The reduced samples.
212::CODE;;Notes
213::CODE;;-----
214::CODE;;Spectral Embedding (Laplacian Eigenmaps) is most useful when the graph
215::CODE;;has one connected component. If there graph has many components, the first
216::CODE;;few eigenvectors will simply uncover the connected components of the graph.
