104::CODE;;def _kl_divergence(
105::CODE;;params,
106::CODE;;P,
107::CODE;;degrees_of_freedom,
108::CODE;;n_samples,
109::CODE;;n_components,
110::CODE;;skip_num_points=0,
111::CODE;;compute_error=True,
112::CODE;;):
141::CODE;;X_embedded = params.reshape(n_samples, n_components)
143::CODE;;dist = pdist(X_embedded, "sqeuclidean")
144::CODE;;dist /= degrees_of_freedom
145::CODE;;dist += 1.0
146::CODE;;dist **= (degrees_of_freedom + 1.0) / -2.0
147::CODE;;Q = np.maximum(dist / (2.0 * np.sum(dist)), MACHINE_EPSILON)
151::CODE;;if compute_error:
152::CODE;;kl_divergence = 2.0 * np.dot(P, np.log(np.maximum(P, MACHINE_EPSILON) / Q))
153::CODE;;else:
154::CODE;;kl_divergence = np.nan
157::CODE;;grad = np.ndarray((n_samples, n_components), dtype=params.dtype)
158::CODE;;PQd = squareform((P - Q) * dist)
159::CODE;;for i in range(skip_num_points, n_samples):
160::CODE;;grad[i] = np.dot(np.ravel(PQd[i], order="K"), X_embedded[i] - X_embedded)
161::CODE;;grad = grad.ravel()
162::CODE;;c = 2.0 * (degrees_of_freedom + 1.0) / degrees_of_freedom
163::CODE;;grad *= c
164::CODE;;return kl_divergence, grad

315::CODE;;error = np.finfo(float).max
316::CODE;;best_error = np.finfo(float).max
317::CODE;;best_iter = i = it
318::CODE;;tic = time()
319::CODE;;for i in range(it, max_iter):
320::CODE;;check_convergence = (i + 1) % n_iter_check == 0
322::CODE;;kwargs["compute_error"] = check_convergence or i == max_iter - 1
323::CODE;;error, grad = objective(p, *args, **kwargs)
324::CODE;;inc = update * grad < 0.0
325::CODE;;dec = np.invert(inc)
326::CODE;;gains[inc] += 0.2
327::CODE;;gains[dec] *= 0.8
328::CODE;;np.clip(gains, min_gain, np.inf, out=gains)
329::CODE;;grad *= gains
330::CODE;;update = momentum * update - learning_rate * grad
331::CODE;;p += update
332::CODE;;if check_convergence:
333::CODE;;toc = time()
334::CODE;;duration = toc - tic
335::CODE;;tic = toc
336::CODE;;grad_norm = linalg.norm(grad)
337::CODE;;if verbose >= 2:
338::CODE;;print(
339::CODE;;"[t-SNE] Iteration %d: error = %.7f,"
340::CODE;;" gradient norm = %.7f"
341::CODE;;" (%s iterations in %0.3fs)"
342::CODE;;% (i + 1, error, grad_norm, n_iter_check, duration)
343::CODE;;)
344::CODE;;if error < best_error:
345::CODE;;best_error = error
346::CODE;;best_iter = i
347::CODE;;elif i - best_iter > n_iter_without_progress:
348::CODE;;if verbose >= 2:
349::CODE;;print(
350::CODE;;"[t-SNE] Iteration %d: did not make any progress "
351::CODE;;"during the last %d episodes. Finished."
352::CODE;;% (i + 1, n_iter_without_progress)
353::CODE;;)
354::CODE;;break
355::CODE;;if grad_norm <= min_grad_norm:
356::CODE;;if verbose >= 2:
357::CODE;;print(
358::CODE;;"[t-SNE] Iteration %d: gradient norm %f. Finished."
359::CODE;;% (i + 1, grad_norm)
360::CODE;;)
361::CODE;;break
362::CODE;;return p, error, i
363::CODE;;@validate_params(
364::CODE;;{
365::CODE;;"X": ["array-like", "sparse matrix"],
366::CODE;;"X_embedded": ["array-like", "sparse matrix"],
367::CODE;;"n_neighbors": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
368::CODE;;"metric": [StrOptions(set(_VALID_METRICS) | {"precomputed"}), callable],
369::CODE;;},
370::CODE;;prefer_skip_nested_validation=True,
371::CODE;;)
372::CODE;;def trustworthiness(X, X_embedded, *, n_neighbors=5, metric="euclidean"):
427::CODE;;n_samples = _num_samples(X)
428::CODE;;if n_neighbors >= n_samples / 2:
429::CODE;;raise ValueError(
430::CODE;;f"n_neighbors ({n_neighbors}) should be less than n_samples / 2"
431::CODE;;f" ({n_samples / 2})"
432::CODE;;)
433::CODE;;dist_X = pairwise_distances(X, metric=metric)
434::CODE;;if metric == "precomputed":
435::CODE;;dist_X = dist_X.copy()
438::CODE;;np.fill_diagonal(dist_X, np.inf)
439::CODE;;ind_X = np.argsort(dist_X, axis=1)
441::CODE;;ind_X_embedded = (
442::CODE;;NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=n_neighbors)
443::CODE;;.fit(X_embedded)
444::CODE;;.kneighbors(return_distance=False)
445::CODE;;)
449::CODE;;inverted_index = np.zeros((n_samples, n_samples), dtype=int)
450::CODE;;ordered_indices = np.arange(n_samples + 1)
451::CODE;;inverted_index[ordered_indices[:-1, np.newaxis], ind_X] = ordered_indices[1:]
452::CODE;;ranks = (
453::CODE;;inverted_index[ordered_indices[:-1, np.newaxis], ind_X_embedded] - n_neighbors
454::CODE;;)
455::CODE;;t = np.sum(ranks[ranks > 0])
456::CODE;;t = 1.0 - t * (
457::CODE;;2.0 / (n_samples * n_neighbors * (2.0 * n_samples - 3.0 * n_neighbors - 1.0))
458::CODE;;)
459::CODE;;return t

703::CODE;;def _fit(self, X, skip_num_points=0):
879::CODE;;params = X_embedded.ravel()
880::CODE;;opt_args = {
881::CODE;;"it": 0,
882::CODE;;"n_iter_check": self._N_ITER_CHECK,
883::CODE;;"min_grad_norm": self.min_grad_norm,
884::CODE;;"learning_rate": self.learning_rate_,
885::CODE;;"verbose": self.verbose,
886::CODE;;"kwargs": dict(skip_num_points=skip_num_points),
887::CODE;;"args": [P, degrees_of_freedom, n_samples, self.n_components],
888::CODE;;"n_iter_without_progress": self._EXPLORATION_MAX_ITER,
889::CODE;;"max_iter": self._EXPLORATION_MAX_ITER,
890::CODE;;"momentum": 0.5,
891::CODE;;}
892::CODE;;if self.method == "barnes_hut":
893::CODE;;obj_func = _kl_divergence_bh
894::CODE;;opt_args["kwargs"]["angle"] = self.angle
896::CODE;;opt_args["kwargs"]["verbose"] = self.verbose
899::CODE;;opt_args["kwargs"]["num_threads"] = _openmp_effective_n_threads()
900::CODE;;else:
901::CODE;;obj_func = _kl_divergence
904::CODE;;P *= self.early_exaggeration
905::CODE;;params, kl_divergence, it = _gradient_descent(obj_func, params, **opt_args)
906::CODE;;if self.verbose:
907::CODE;;print(
908::CODE;;"[t-SNE] KL divergence after %d iterations with early exaggeration: %f"
909::CODE;;% (it + 1, kl_divergence)
910::CODE;;)
913::CODE;;P /= self.early_exaggeration
914::CODE;;remaining = self.max_iter - self._EXPLORATION_MAX_ITER
915::CODE;;if it < self._EXPLORATION_MAX_ITER or remaining > 0:
916::CODE;;opt_args["max_iter"] = self.max_iter
917::CODE;;opt_args["it"] = it + 1
918::CODE;;opt_args["momentum"] = 0.8
919::CODE;;opt_args["n_iter_without_progress"] = self.n_iter_without_progress
920::CODE;;params, kl_divergence, it = _gradient_descent(obj_func, params, **opt_args)
922::CODE;;self.n_iter_ = it
923::CODE;;if self.verbose:
924::CODE;;print(
925::CODE;;"[t-SNE] KL divergence after %d iterations: %f"
926::CODE;;% (it + 1, kl_divergence)
927::CODE;;)
928::CODE;;X_embedded = params.reshape(n_samples, self.n_components)
929::CODE;;self.kl_divergence_ = kl_divergence
930::CODE;;return X_embedded

97::CODE;;def _average_multiclass_ovo_score(binary_metric, y_true, y_score, average="macro"):
131::CODE;;check_consistent_length(y_true, y_score)
132::CODE;;y_true_unique = np.unique(y_true)
133::CODE;;n_classes = y_true_unique.shape[0]
134::CODE;;n_pairs = n_classes * (n_classes - 1) // 2
135::CODE;;pair_scores = np.empty(n_pairs)
136::CODE;;is_weighted = average == "weighted"
137::CODE;;prevalence = np.empty(n_pairs) if is_weighted else None
140::CODE;;for ix, (a, b) in enumerate(combinations(y_true_unique, 2)):
141::CODE;;a_mask = y_true == a
142::CODE;;b_mask = y_true == b
143::CODE;;ab_mask = np.logical_or(a_mask, b_mask)
144::CODE;;if is_weighted:
145::CODE;;prevalence[ix] = np.average(ab_mask)
146::CODE;;a_true = a_mask[ab_mask]
147::CODE;;b_true = b_mask[ab_mask]
148::CODE;;a_true_score = binary_metric(a_true, y_score[ab_mask, a])
149::CODE;;b_true_score = binary_metric(b_true, y_score[ab_mask, b])
150::CODE;;pair_scores[ix] = (a_true_score + b_true_score) / 2
151::CODE;;return np.average(pair_scores, weights=prevalence)

372::CODE;;def confusion_matrix(
373::CODE;;y_true, y_pred, *, labels=None, sample_weight=None, normalize=None
374::CODE;;):
443::CODE;;xp, _, device_ = get_namespace_and_device(y_true, y_pred, labels, sample_weight)
444::CODE;;y_true = check_array(
445::CODE;;y_true,
446::CODE;;dtype=None,

450::CODE;;)

452::CODE;;y_pred,
453::CODE;;dtype=None,
454::CODE;;ensure_2d=False,
455::CODE;;ensure_all_finite=False,
456::CODE;;ensure_min_samples=0,
457::CODE;;)
463::CODE;;y_true = _convert_to_numpy(y_true, xp)
464::CODE;;y_pred = _convert_to_numpy(y_pred, xp)
465::CODE;;if sample_weight is None:
466::CODE;;sample_weight = np.ones(y_true.shape[0], dtype=np.int64)
467::CODE;;else:
468::CODE;;sample_weight = _convert_to_numpy(sample_weight, xp)
469::CODE;;if len(sample_weight) > 0:
470::CODE;;y_type, y_true, y_pred, sample_weight = _check_targets(
471::CODE;;y_true, y_pred, sample_weight
472::CODE;;)
473::CODE;;else:
479::CODE;;y_type, y_true, y_pred, _ = _check_targets(y_true, y_pred)
480::CODE;;y_true, y_pred = attach_unique(y_true, y_pred)
481::CODE;;if y_type not in ("binary", "multiclass"):
482::CODE;;raise ValueError("%s is not supported" % y_type)
483::CODE;;if labels is None:
484::CODE;;labels = unique_labels(y_true, y_pred)
485::CODE;;else:
486::CODE;;labels = _convert_to_numpy(labels, xp)
487::CODE;;n_labels = labels.size
488::CODE;;if n_labels == 0:
489::CODE;;raise ValueError("'labels' should contain at least one label.")
490::CODE;;elif y_true.size == 0:
491::CODE;;return np.zeros((n_labels, n_labels), dtype=int)
492::CODE;;elif len(np.intersect1d(y_true, labels)) == 0:
493::CODE;;raise ValueError("At least one label specified must be in y_true")
494::CODE;;n_labels = labels.size
497::CODE;;need_index_conversion = not (
498::CODE;;labels.dtype.kind in {"i", "u", "b"}
499::CODE;;and np.all(labels == np.arange(n_labels))
500::CODE;;and y_true.min() >= 0
501::CODE;;and y_pred.min() >= 0
502::CODE;;)
503::CODE;;if need_index_conversion:
504::CODE;;label_to_ind = {label: index for index, label in enumerate(labels)}
505::CODE;;y_pred = np.array([label_to_ind.get(label, n_labels + 1) for label in y_pred])
506::CODE;;y_true = np.array([label_to_ind.get(label, n_labels + 1) for label in y_true])
508::CODE;;ind = np.logical_and(y_pred < n_labels, y_true < n_labels)
509::CODE;;if not np.all(ind):
510::CODE;;y_pred = y_pred[ind]
511::CODE;;y_true = y_true[ind]
513::CODE;;sample_weight = sample_weight[ind]
515::CODE;;if sample_weight.dtype.kind in {"i", "u", "b"}:
516::CODE;;dtype = np.int64
517::CODE;;else:
518::CODE;;dtype = np.float32 if str(device_).startswith("mps") else np.float64
519::CODE;;cm = coo_matrix(
520::CODE;;(sample_weight, (y_true, y_pred)),
521::CODE;;shape=(n_labels, n_labels),
522::CODE;;dtype=dtype,
523::CODE;;).toarray()
524::CODE;;with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
525::CODE;;if normalize == "true":
526::CODE;;cm = cm / cm.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
527::CODE;;elif normalize == "pred":
528::CODE;;cm = cm / cm.sum(axis=0, keepdims=True)
529::CODE;;elif normalize == "all":
530::CODE;;cm = cm / cm.sum()
531::CODE;;cm = xpx.nan_to_num(cm)
532::CODE;;if cm.shape == (1, 1):
533::CODE;;warnings.warn(
534::CODE;;(
535::CODE;;"A single label was found in 'y_true' and 'y_pred'. For the confusion "
536::CODE;;"matrix to have the correct shape, use the 'labels' parameter to pass "
537::CODE;;"all known labels."
538::CODE;;),
539::CODE;;UserWarning,
540::CODE;;)
541::CODE;;return xp.asarray(cm, device=device_)
542::CODE;;@validate_params(
543::CODE;;{
544::CODE;;"y_true": ["array-like", "sparse matrix"],
545::CODE;;"y_pred": ["array-like", "sparse matrix"],
546::CODE;;"sample_weight": ["array-like", None],

548::CODE;;"samplewise": ["boolean"],
549::CODE;;},
550::CODE;;prefer_skip_nested_validation=True,

552::CODE;;def multilabel_confusion_matrix(
553::CODE;;y_true, y_pred, *, sample_weight=None, labels=None, samplewise=False
554::CODE;;):
637::CODE;;y_true, y_pred = attach_unique(y_true, y_pred)
638::CODE;;xp, _, device_ = get_namespace_and_device(y_true, y_pred, sample_weight)
639::CODE;;y_type, y_true, y_pred, sample_weight = _check_targets(
640::CODE;;y_true, y_pred, sample_weight
641::CODE;;)
642::CODE;;if y_type not in ("binary", "multiclass", "multilabel-indicator"):
643::CODE;;raise ValueError("%s is not supported" % y_type)
644::CODE;;present_labels = unique_labels(y_true, y_pred)
645::CODE;;if labels is None:
646::CODE;;labels = present_labels
647::CODE;;n_labels = None
648::CODE;;else:
649::CODE;;labels = xp.asarray(labels, device=device_)
650::CODE;;n_labels = labels.shape[0]
651::CODE;;labels = xp.concat(
652::CODE;;[labels, xpx.setdiff1d(present_labels, labels, assume_unique=True, xp=xp)],
653::CODE;;axis=-1,
654::CODE;;)
655::CODE;;if y_true.ndim == 1:
656::CODE;;if samplewise:
657::CODE;;raise ValueError(
658::CODE;;"Samplewise metrics are not available outside of "
659::CODE;;"multilabel classification."
660::CODE;;)
661::CODE;;le = LabelEncoder()
662::CODE;;le.fit(labels)
663::CODE;;y_true = le.transform(y_true)
664::CODE;;y_pred = le.transform(y_pred)
665::CODE;;sorted_labels = le.classes_
667::CODE;;tp = y_true == y_pred
668::CODE;;tp_bins = y_true[tp]
669::CODE;;if sample_weight is not None:
670::CODE;;tp_bins_weights = sample_weight[tp]
671::CODE;;else:
672::CODE;;tp_bins_weights = None
673::CODE;;if tp_bins.shape[0]:
674::CODE;;tp_sum = _bincount(
675::CODE;;tp_bins, weights=tp_bins_weights, minlength=labels.shape[0], xp=xp
676::CODE;;)
677::CODE;;else:
679::CODE;;true_sum = pred_sum = tp_sum = xp.zeros(labels.shape[0])
680::CODE;;if y_pred.shape[0]:
681::CODE;;pred_sum = _bincount(
682::CODE;;y_pred, weights=sample_weight, minlength=labels.shape[0], xp=xp
683::CODE;;)
684::CODE;;if y_true.shape[0]:
685::CODE;;true_sum = _bincount(
686::CODE;;y_true, weights=sample_weight, minlength=labels.shape[0], xp=xp
687::CODE;;)
689::CODE;;indices = xp.searchsorted(sorted_labels, labels[:n_labels])
690::CODE;;tp_sum = xp.take(tp_sum, indices, axis=0)
691::CODE;;true_sum = xp.take(true_sum, indices, axis=0)
692::CODE;;pred_sum = xp.take(pred_sum, indices, axis=0)
693::CODE;;else:
694::CODE;;sum_axis = 1 if samplewise else 0
697::CODE;;if labels.shape != present_labels.shape or xp.any(
698::CODE;;xp.not_equal(labels, present_labels)
699::CODE;;):
700::CODE;;if xp.max(labels) > xp.max(present_labels):
701::CODE;;raise ValueError(
702::CODE;;"All labels must be in [0, n labels) for "
703::CODE;;"multilabel targets. "
704::CODE;;"Got %d > %d" % (xp.max(labels), xp.max(present_labels))
705::CODE;;)
706::CODE;;if xp.min(labels) < 0:
707::CODE;;raise ValueError(
708::CODE;;"All labels must be in [0, n labels) for "
709::CODE;;"multilabel targets. "
710::CODE;;"Got %d < 0" % xp.min(labels)
711::CODE;;)
712::CODE;;if n_labels is not None:
713::CODE;;y_true = y_true[:, labels[:n_labels]]
714::CODE;;y_pred = y_pred[:, labels[:n_labels]]
715::CODE;;if issparse(y_true) or issparse(y_pred):
716::CODE;;true_and_pred = y_true.multiply(y_pred)
717::CODE;;else:
718::CODE;;true_and_pred = xp.multiply(y_true, y_pred)
720::CODE;;tp_sum = _count_nonzero(
721::CODE;;true_and_pred,
722::CODE;;axis=sum_axis,
723::CODE;;sample_weight=sample_weight,
724::CODE;;xp=xp,
725::CODE;;device=device_,
726::CODE;;)
727::CODE;;pred_sum = _count_nonzero(
728::CODE;;y_pred,
729::CODE;;axis=sum_axis,
730::CODE;;sample_weight=sample_weight,
731::CODE;;xp=xp,
732::CODE;;device=device_,
733::CODE;;)
734::CODE;;true_sum = _count_nonzero(
735::CODE;;y_true,
736::CODE;;axis=sum_axis,
737::CODE;;sample_weight=sample_weight,
738::CODE;;xp=xp,
739::CODE;;device=device_,
740::CODE;;)
741::CODE;;fp = pred_sum - tp_sum
742::CODE;;fn = true_sum - tp_sum
743::CODE;;tp = tp_sum
744::CODE;;if sample_weight is not None and samplewise:
745::CODE;;tp = xp.asarray(tp)
746::CODE;;fp = xp.asarray(fp)
747::CODE;;fn = xp.asarray(fn)
748::CODE;;tn = sample_weight * y_true.shape[1] - tp - fp - fn
749::CODE;;elif sample_weight is not None:
750::CODE;;tn = xp.sum(sample_weight) - tp - fp - fn
751::CODE;;elif samplewise:
752::CODE;;tn = y_true.shape[1] - tp - fp - fn
753::CODE;;else:
754::CODE;;tn = y_true.shape[0] - tp - fp - fn
755::CODE;;return xp.reshape(xp.stack([tn, fp, fn, tp]).T, (-1, 2, 2))
756::CODE;;@validate_params(
757::CODE;;{
758::CODE;;"y1": ["array-like"],
759::CODE;;"y2": ["array-like"],
760::CODE;;"labels": ["array-like", None],
761::CODE;;"weights": [StrOptions({"linear", "quadratic"}), None],
762::CODE;;"sample_weight": ["array-like", None],
763::CODE;;},
764::CODE;;prefer_skip_nested_validation=True,
765::CODE;;)
766::CODE;;def cohen_kappa_score(y1, y2, *, labels=None, weights=None, sample_weight=None):
820::CODE;;try:
821::CODE;;confusion = confusion_matrix(y1, y2, labels=labels, sample_weight=sample_weight)
822::CODE;;except ValueError as e:
823::CODE;;if "At least one label specified must be in y_true" in str(e):
824::CODE;;msg = (
825::CODE;;"At least one label in `labels` must be present in `y1` (even though "
826::CODE;;"`cohen_kappa_score` is otherwise agnostic to the order of `y1` and "
827::CODE;;"`y2`)."
828::CODE;;)
829::CODE;;raise ValueError(msg) from e
830::CODE;;raise
831::CODE;;xp, _, device_ = get_namespace_and_device(y1, y2)
832::CODE;;n_classes = confusion.shape[0]
837::CODE;;max_float_dtype = _max_precision_float_dtype(xp, device=device_)
838::CODE;;confusion = xp.astype(confusion, max_float_dtype, copy=False)
839::CODE;;sum0 = xp.sum(confusion, axis=0)
840::CODE;;sum1 = xp.sum(confusion, axis=1)
841::CODE;;expected = xp.linalg.outer(sum0, sum1) / xp.sum(sum0)
842::CODE;;if weights is None:
843::CODE;;w_mat = xp.ones([n_classes, n_classes], dtype=max_float_dtype, device=device_)
844::CODE;;_fill_diagonal(w_mat, 0, xp=xp)
846::CODE;;w_mat = xp.zeros([n_classes, n_classes], dtype=max_float_dtype, device=device_)
847::CODE;;w_mat += xp.arange(n_classes)
848::CODE;;if weights == "linear":
849::CODE;;w_mat = xp.abs(w_mat - w_mat.T)
850::CODE;;else:
851::CODE;;w_mat = (w_mat - w_mat.T) ** 2
852::CODE;;k = xp.sum(w_mat * confusion) / xp.sum(w_mat * expected)
853::CODE;;return float(1 - k)
854::CODE;;@validate_params(

867::CODE;;StrOptions({"warn"}),
868::CODE;;],
869::CODE;;},
870::CODE;;prefer_skip_nested_validation=True,
871::CODE;;)
872::CODE;;def jaccard_score(
873::CODE;;y_true,
874::CODE;;y_pred,
875::CODE;;*,
876::CODE;;labels=None,
877::CODE;;pos_label=1,
878::CODE;;average="binary",
879::CODE;;sample_weight=None,
880::CODE;;zero_division="warn",
881::CODE;;):
992::CODE;;labels = _check_set_wise_labels(y_true, y_pred, average, labels, pos_label)
993::CODE;;samplewise = average == "samples"
994::CODE;;MCM = multilabel_confusion_matrix(
995::CODE;;y_true,
996::CODE;;y_pred,
997::CODE;;sample_weight=sample_weight,
998::CODE;;labels=labels,
999::CODE;;samplewise=samplewise,
1000::CODE;;)

2902::CODE;;def _log_loss(transformed_labels, y_pred, *, normalize=True, sample_weight=None):
2922::CODE;;In binary class case, assuming labels in y_true are encoded with +1 and -1,
2923::CODE;;when a prediction mistake is made, ``margin = y_true * pred_decision`` is
2924::CODE;;always negative (since the signs disagree), implying ``1 - margin`` is
2925::CODE;;always greater than 1. The cumulated hinge loss is therefore an upper
2926::CODE;;bound of the number of mistakes made by the classifier.
2927::CODE;;In multiclass case, the function expects that either all the labels are
2928::CODE;;included in y_true or an optional labels argument is provided which
2929::CODE;;contains all the labels. The multilabel margin is calculated according
2930::CODE;;to Crammer-Singer's method. As in the binary case, the cumulated hinge loss
2931::CODE;;is an upper bound of the number of mistakes made by the classifier.
2932::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <hinge_loss>`.
2933::CODE;;Parameters
2934::CODE;;----------
2935::CODE;;y_true : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
2936::CODE;;True target, consisting of integers of two values. The positive label
2937::CODE;;must be greater than the negative label.
2938::CODE;;pred_decision : array-like of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_classes)
2939::CODE;;Predicted decisions, as output by decision_function (floats).
2940::CODE;;labels : array-like, default=None
2941::CODE;;Contains all the labels for the problem. Used in multiclass hinge loss.
2942::CODE;;sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
2943::CODE;;Sample weights.
2944::CODE;;Returns
2945::CODE;;-------
2946::CODE;;loss : float
2947::CODE;;Average hinge loss.
2948::CODE;;References
2949::CODE;;----------
2950::CODE;;.. [1] `Wikipedia entry on the Hinge loss
2951::CODE;;<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinge_loss>`_.
2952::CODE;;.. [2] Koby Crammer, Yoram Singer. On the Algorithmic
2953::CODE;;Implementation of Multiclass Kernel-based Vector
2954::CODE;;Machines. Journal of Machine Learning Research 2,
2955::CODE;;(2001), 265-292.
2956::CODE;;.. [3] `L1 AND L2 Regularization for Multiclass Hinge Loss Models
2957::CODE;;by Robert C. Moore, John DeNero
2958::CODE;;<https://storage.googleapis.com/pub-tools-public-publication-data/pdf/37362.pdf>`_.
2959::CODE;;Examples
2960::CODE;;--------
2961::CODE;;>>> from sklearn import svm
2962::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.metrics import hinge_loss
2963::CODE;;>>> X = [[0], [1]]
2964::CODE;;>>> y = [-1, 1]
2965::CODE;;>>> est = svm.LinearSVC(random_state=0)
2966::CODE;;>>> est.fit(X, y)
2967::CODE;;LinearSVC(random_state=0)
2968::CODE;;>>> pred_decision = est.decision_function([[-2], [3], [0.5]])
2969::CODE;;>>> pred_decision
2970::CODE;;array([-2.18, 2.36, 0.09])
2971::CODE;;>>> hinge_loss([-1, 1, 1], pred_decision)
2972::CODE;;0.30
2973::CODE;;In the multiclass case:
2974::CODE;;>>> import numpy as np
2975::CODE;;>>> X = np.array([[0], [1], [2], [3]])
2976::CODE;;>>> Y = np.array([0, 1, 2, 3])
2977::CODE;;>>> labels = np.array([0, 1, 2, 3])
2978::CODE;;>>> est = svm.LinearSVC()
2979::CODE;;>>> est.fit(X, Y)
2980::CODE;;LinearSVC()
2981::CODE;;>>> pred_decision = est.decision_function([[-1], [2], [3]])
2982::CODE;;>>> y_true = [0, 2, 3]
2983::CODE;;>>> hinge_loss(y_true, pred_decision, labels=labels)
2984::CODE;;0.56
3043::CODE;;the encoded array is placed on the target API namespace and device.

3054::CODE;;True labels.
3055::CODE;;y_prob : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
3056::CODE;;Probabilities of the positive class.
3057::CODE;;sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
3058::CODE;;Sample weights.
3059::CODE;;pos_label : int, float, bool or str, default=None
3060::CODE;;Label of the positive class. If None, `pos_label` will be inferred
3061::CODE;;in the following manner:
3062::CODE;;* if `y_true` in {-1, 1} or {0, 1}, `pos_label` defaults to 1;
3063::CODE;;* else if `y_true` contains string, an error will be raised and
3064::CODE;;`pos_label` should be explicitly specified;
3065::CODE;;* otherwise, `pos_label` defaults to the greater label,

3129::CODE;;The smaller the Brier score loss, the better, hence the naming with "loss".
3130::CODE;;The Brier score measures the mean squared difference between the predicted
3131::CODE;;probability and the actual outcome. The Brier score is a strictly proper scoring
3132::CODE;;rule.
3133::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <brier_score_loss>`.
3134::CODE;;Parameters
3135::CODE;;----------
3136::CODE;;y_true : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
3137::CODE;;True targets.
3138::CODE;;y_proba : array-like of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_classes)
3139::CODE;;Predicted probabilities. If `y_proba.shape = (n_samples,)`
3140::CODE;;the probabilities provided are assumed to be that of the
3141::CODE;;positive class. If `y_proba.shape = (n_samples, n_classes)`
3142::CODE;;the columns in `y_proba` are assumed to correspond to the
3143::CODE;;labels in alphabetical order, as done by
3144::CODE;;:class:`~sklearn.preprocessing.LabelBinarizer`.
3145::CODE;;sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
3146::CODE;;Sample weights.
3147::CODE;;pos_label : int, float, bool or str, default=None
3148::CODE;;Label of the positive class when `y_proba.shape = (n_samples,)`.
3149::CODE;;If not provided, `pos_label` will be inferred in the
3150::CODE;;following manner:
3151::CODE;;* if `y_true` in {-1, 1} or {0, 1}, `pos_label` defaults to 1;
3152::CODE;;* else if `y_true` contains string, an error will be raised and
3153::CODE;;`pos_label` should be explicitly specified;
3154::CODE;;* otherwise, `pos_label` defaults to the greater label,
3155::CODE;;i.e. `np.unique(y_true)[-1]`.
3156::CODE;;labels : array-like of shape (n_classes,), default=None
3157::CODE;;Class labels when `y_proba.shape = (n_samples, n_classes)`.
3158::CODE;;If not provided, labels will be inferred from `y_true`.
3159::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.7
3160::CODE;;scale_by_half : bool or "auto", default="auto"
3161::CODE;;When True, scale the Brier score by 1/2 to lie in the [0, 1] range instead
3162::CODE;;of the [0, 2] range. The default "auto" option implements the rescaling to
3163::CODE;;[0, 1] only for binary classification (as customary) but keeps the
3164::CODE;;original [0, 2] range for multiclass classification.
3165::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.7
3166::CODE;;Returns
3167::CODE;;-------
3168::CODE;;score : float
3169::CODE;;Brier score loss.
3170::CODE;;Notes
3171::CODE;;-----
3172::CODE;;For :math:`N` observations labeled from :math:`C` possible classes, the Brier
3173::CODE;;score is defined as:
3174::CODE;;.. math::
3175::CODE;;\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\sum_{c=1}^{C}(y_{ic} - \hat{p}_{ic})^{2}
3176::CODE;;where :math:`y_{ic}` is 1 if observation `i` belongs to class `c`,
3177::CODE;;otherwise 0 and :math:`\hat{p}_{ic}` is the predicted probability for
3178::CODE;;observation `i` to belong to class `c`.
3179::CODE;;The Brier score then ranges between :math:`[0, 2]`.
3180::CODE;;In binary classification tasks the Brier score is usually divided by
3181::CODE;;two and then ranges between :math:`[0, 1]`. It can be alternatively
3182::CODE;;written as:
3183::CODE;;.. math::
3184::CODE;;\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}(y_{i} - \hat{p}_{i})^{2}
3185::CODE;;where :math:`y_{i}` is the binary target and :math:`\hat{p}_{i}`
3186::CODE;;is the predicted probability of the positive class.
3187::CODE;;References
3188::CODE;;----------
3189::CODE;;.. [1] `Wikipedia entry for the Brier score
3190::CODE;;<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brier_score>`_.
3191::CODE;;Examples
3192::CODE;;--------
3193::CODE;;>>> import numpy as np
3194::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.metrics import brier_score_loss
3195::CODE;;>>> y_true = np.array([0, 1, 1, 0])
3196::CODE;;>>> y_true_categorical = np.array(["spam", "ham", "ham", "spam"])
3197::CODE;;>>> y_prob = np.array([0.1, 0.9, 0.8, 0.3])
3198::CODE;;>>> brier_score_loss(y_true, y_prob)
3199::CODE;;0.0375
3200::CODE;;>>> brier_score_loss(y_true, 1-y_prob, pos_label=0)
3201::CODE;;0.0375
3202::CODE;;>>> brier_score_loss(y_true_categorical, y_prob, pos_label="ham")
3203::CODE;;0.0375
3204::CODE;;>>> brier_score_loss(y_true, np.array(y_prob) > 0.5)
3205::CODE;;0.0
3206::CODE;;>>> brier_score_loss(y_true, y_prob, scale_by_half=False)
3207::CODE;;0.075
3208::CODE;;>>> brier_score_loss(
3209::CODE;;... ["eggs", "ham", "spam"],
3210::CODE;;... [[0.8, 0.1, 0.1], [0.2, 0.7, 0.1], [0.2, 0.2, 0.6]],
3211::CODE;;... labels=["eggs", "ham", "spam"]
3212::CODE;;... )
3213::CODE;;0.146
3249::CODE;;:math:`D^2` score function, fraction of log loss explained.
3250::CODE;;Best possible score is 1.0 and it can be negative (because the model can be
3251::CODE;;arbitrarily worse). A model that always predicts the per-class proportions
3252::CODE;;of `y_true`, disregarding the input features, gets a D^2 score of 0.0.

3280::CODE;;a quantity D).

3282::CODE;;value if n_samples is less than two.

3332::CODE;;be arbitrarily worse than the null model. The null model, also known as the
3333::CODE;;optimal intercept model, is a model that constantly predicts the per-class
3334::CODE;;proportions of `y_true`, disregarding the input features. The null model
3335::CODE;;gets a D^2 score of 0.0.

327::CODE;;thresholds = xp.astype(thresholds, _max_precision_float_dtype(xp, device))

364::CODE;;sl = slice(first_ind, last_ind)

371::CODE;;def _binary_roc_auc_score(y_true, y_score, sample_weight=None, max_fpr=None):
422::CODE;;from prediction scores.
423::CODE;;Note: this implementation can be used with :term:`binary`, :term:`multiclass` and
424::CODE;;:term:`multilabel` classification, but some restrictions apply (see Parameters).
425::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <roc_metrics>`.
426::CODE;;Parameters
427::CODE;;----------
428::CODE;;y_true : array-like of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_classes)
429::CODE;;True labels or binary label indicators. The binary and multiclass cases
430::CODE;;expect labels with shape (n_samples,) while the multilabel case expects
431::CODE;;binary label indicators with shape (n_samples, n_classes).
432::CODE;;y_score : array-like of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_classes)
433::CODE;;Target scores.
434::CODE;;* In the :term:`binary` case, it corresponds to an array of shape
435::CODE;;`(n_samples,)`. Both probability estimates and non-thresholded
436::CODE;;decision values can be provided. The probability estimates correspond
437::CODE;;to the **probability of the class with the greater label**,
438::CODE;;i.e. `estimator.classes_[1]` and thus
439::CODE;;`estimator.predict_proba(X, y)[:, 1]`. The decision values
440::CODE;;corresponds to the output of `estimator.decision_function(X, y)`.
441::CODE;;See more information in the :ref:`User guide <roc_auc_binary>`;
442::CODE;;* In the :term:`multiclass` case, it corresponds to an array of shape
443::CODE;;`(n_samples, n_classes)` of probability estimates provided by the
444::CODE;;`predict_proba` method. The probability estimates **must**
445::CODE;;sum to 1 across the possible classes. In addition, the order of the
446::CODE;;class scores must correspond to the order of ``labels``,
447::CODE;;if provided, or else to the numerical or lexicographical order of
448::CODE;;the labels in ``y_true``. See more information in the
449::CODE;;:ref:`User guide <roc_auc_multiclass>`;
450::CODE;;* In the :term:`multilabel` case, it corresponds to an array of shape
451::CODE;;`(n_samples, n_classes)`. Probability estimates are provided by the
452::CODE;;`predict_proba` method and the non-thresholded decision values by
453::CODE;;the `decision_function` method. The probability estimates correspond
454::CODE;;to the **probability of the class with the greater label for each
455::CODE;;output** of the classifier. See more information in the
456::CODE;;:ref:`User guide <roc_auc_multilabel>`.
457::CODE;;average : {'micro', 'macro', 'samples', 'weighted'} or None, \
458::CODE;;default='macro'
459::CODE;;If ``None``, the scores for each class are returned.
460::CODE;;Otherwise, this determines the type of averaging performed on the data.
461::CODE;;Note: multiclass ROC AUC currently only handles the 'macro' and
462::CODE;;'weighted' averages. For multiclass targets, `average=None` is only
463::CODE;;implemented for `multi_class='ovr'` and `average='micro'` is only
464::CODE;;implemented for `multi_class='ovr'`.
465::CODE;;``'micro'``:
466::CODE;;Calculate metrics globally by considering each element of the label
467::CODE;;indicator matrix as a label.
468::CODE;;``'macro'``:
469::CODE;;Calculate metrics for each label, and find their unweighted
470::CODE;;mean. This does not take label imbalance into account.
471::CODE;;``'weighted'``:
472::CODE;;Calculate metrics for each label, and find their average, weighted
473::CODE;;by support (the number of true instances for each label).
474::CODE;;``'samples'``:
475::CODE;;Calculate metrics for each instance, and find their average.
476::CODE;;Will be ignored when ``y_true`` is binary.
477::CODE;;sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
478::CODE;;Sample weights.
479::CODE;;max_fpr : float > 0 and <= 1, default=None
480::CODE;;If not ``None``, the standardized partial AUC [2]_ over the range
481::CODE;;[0, max_fpr] is returned. For the multiclass case, ``max_fpr``,
482::CODE;;should be either equal to ``None`` or ``1.0`` as AUC ROC partial
483::CODE;;computation currently is not supported for multiclass.
484::CODE;;multi_class : {'raise', 'ovr', 'ovo'}, default='raise'
485::CODE;;Only used for multiclass targets. Determines the type of configuration
486::CODE;;to use. The default value raises an error, so either
487::CODE;;``'ovr'`` or ``'ovo'`` must be passed explicitly.
488::CODE;;``'ovr'``:
489::CODE;;Stands for One-vs-rest. Computes the AUC of each class
490::CODE;;against the rest [3]_ [4]_. This
491::CODE;;treats the multiclass case in the same way as the multilabel case.
492::CODE;;Sensitive to class imbalance even when ``average == 'macro'``,
493::CODE;;because class imbalance affects the composition of each of the
494::CODE;;'rest' groupings.
495::CODE;;``'ovo'``:
496::CODE;;Stands for One-vs-one. Computes the average AUC of all
497::CODE;;possible pairwise combinations of classes [5]_.
498::CODE;;Insensitive to class imbalance when
499::CODE;;``average == 'macro'``.
500::CODE;;labels : array-like of shape (n_classes,), default=None
501::CODE;;Only used for multiclass targets. List of labels that index the
502::CODE;;classes in ``y_score``. If ``None``, the numerical or lexicographical
503::CODE;;order of the labels in ``y_true`` is used.
504::CODE;;Returns
505::CODE;;-------
506::CODE;;auc : float
507::CODE;;Area Under the Curve score.
508::CODE;;See Also
509::CODE;;--------
510::CODE;;average_precision_score : Area under the precision-recall curve.
511::CODE;;roc_curve : Compute Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve.
512::CODE;;RocCurveDisplay.from_estimator : Plot Receiver Operating Characteristic
513::CODE;;(ROC) curve given an estimator and some data.
514::CODE;;RocCurveDisplay.from_predictions : Plot Receiver Operating Characteristic
515::CODE;;(ROC) curve given the true and predicted values.
516::CODE;;Notes
517::CODE;;-----
518::CODE;;The Gini Coefficient is a summary measure of the ranking ability of binary
519::CODE;;classifiers. It is expressed using the area under of the ROC as follows:
520::CODE;;G = 2 * AUC - 1
521::CODE;;Where G is the Gini coefficient and AUC is the ROC-AUC score. This normalisation
522::CODE;;will ensure that random guessing will yield a score of 0 in expectation, and it is
523::CODE;;upper bounded by 1.
524::CODE;;References
525::CODE;;----------
526::CODE;;.. [1] `Wikipedia entry for the Receiver operating characteristic
527::CODE;;<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Receiver_operating_characteristic>`_
528::CODE;;.. [2] `Analyzing a portion of the ROC curve. McClish, 1989
529::CODE;;<https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/2668680>`_
530::CODE;;.. [3] Provost, F., Domingos, P. (2000). Well-trained PETs: Improving
531::CODE;;probability estimation trees (Section 6.2), CeDER Working Paper
533::CODE;;.. [4] `Fawcett, T. (2006). An introduction to ROC analysis. Pattern
534::CODE;;Recognition Letters, 27(8), 861-874.
535::CODE;;<https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S016786550500303X>`_
536::CODE;;.. [5] `Hand, D.J., Till, R.J. (2001). A Simple Generalisation of the Area
537::CODE;;Under the ROC Curve for Multiple Class Classification Problems.
538::CODE;;Machine Learning, 45(2), 171-186.
539::CODE;;<http://link.springer.com/article/10.1023/A:1010920819831>`_
540::CODE;;.. [6] `Wikipedia entry for the Gini coefficient
541::CODE;;<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gini_coefficient>`_

619::CODE;;Parameters
620::CODE;;----------
621::CODE;;y_true : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
622::CODE;;True multiclass labels.
623::CODE;;y_score : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_classes)
624::CODE;;Target scores corresponding to probability estimates of a sample
625::CODE;;belonging to a particular class
626::CODE;;labels : array-like of shape (n_classes,) or None
627::CODE;;List of labels to index ``y_score`` used for multiclass. If ``None``,
628::CODE;;the lexical order of ``y_true`` is used to index ``y_score``.
629::CODE;;multi_class : {'ovr', 'ovo'}
630::CODE;;Determines the type of multiclass configuration to use.
631::CODE;;``'ovr'``:
632::CODE;;Calculate metrics for the multiclass case using the one-vs-rest
633::CODE;;approach.
634::CODE;;``'ovo'``:
635::CODE;;Calculate metrics for the multiclass case using the one-vs-one
636::CODE;;approach.
637::CODE;;average : {'micro', 'macro', 'weighted'}
638::CODE;;Determines the type of averaging performed on the pairwise binary
639::CODE;;metric scores
640::CODE;;``'micro'``:
641::CODE;;Calculate metrics for the binarized-raveled classes. Only supported
642::CODE;;for `multi_class='ovr'`.
643::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.2
644::CODE;;``'macro'``:
645::CODE;;Calculate metrics for each label, and find their unweighted
646::CODE;;mean. This does not take label imbalance into account. Classes
647::CODE;;are assumed to be uniformly distributed.
648::CODE;;``'weighted'``:
649::CODE;;Calculate metrics for each label, taking into account the
650::CODE;;prevalence of the classes.
651::CODE;;sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,) or None
652::CODE;;Sample weights.
733::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <confusion_matrix>`.
734::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.8
735::CODE;;Parameters
736::CODE;;----------
737::CODE;;y_true : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
738::CODE;;True targets of binary classification.
739::CODE;;y_score : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
740::CODE;;Estimated probabilities or output of a decision function.
741::CODE;;pos_label : int, float, bool or str, default=None
742::CODE;;The label of the positive class.
743::CODE;;sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
744::CODE;;Sample weights.
745::CODE;;Returns
746::CODE;;-------
747::CODE;;tns : ndarray of shape (n_thresholds,)
748::CODE;;A count of true negatives, at index `i` being the number of negative
749::CODE;;samples assigned a `score < thresholds[i]`.
750::CODE;;fps : ndarray of shape (n_thresholds,)
751::CODE;;A count of false positives, at index `i` being the number of negative
752::CODE;;samples assigned a `score >= thresholds[i]`. The total number of
753::CODE;;negative samples is equal to `fps[-1]`.
754::CODE;;fns : ndarray of shape (n_thresholds,)
755::CODE;;A count of false negatives, at index `i` being the number of positive
756::CODE;;samples assigned a `score < thresholds[i]`.
757::CODE;;tps : ndarray of shape (n_thresholds,)
758::CODE;;An increasing count of true positives, at index `i` being the number
759::CODE;;of positive samples assigned a `score >= thresholds[i]`. The total
760::CODE;;number of positive samples is equal to `tps[-1]`.
761::CODE;;thresholds : ndarray of shape (n_thresholds,)
762::CODE;;Decreasing score values.
763::CODE;;See Also
764::CODE;;--------
765::CODE;;confusion_matrix : Compute classification matrix to evaluate the accuracy of a
766::CODE;;classifier.
767::CODE;;roc_curve : Compute Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve.
768::CODE;;precision_recall_curve : Compute precision-recall curve.
769::CODE;;det_curve : Compute Detection error tradeoff (DET) curve.
770::CODE;;Examples
771::CODE;;--------
772::CODE;;>>> import numpy as np
773::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.metrics import confusion_matrix_at_thresholds
774::CODE;;>>> y_true = np.array([0., 0., 1., 1.])
775::CODE;;>>> y_score = np.array([0.1, 0.4, 0.35, 0.8])
776::CODE;;>>> tns, fps, fns, tps, thresholds = confusion_matrix_at_thresholds(y_true, y_score)
777::CODE;;>>> tns
778::CODE;;array([2., 1., 1., 0.])
779::CODE;;>>> fps
780::CODE;;array([0., 1., 1., 2.])
781::CODE;;>>> fns
782::CODE;;array([1., 1., 0., 0.])
783::CODE;;>>> tps
784::CODE;;array([1., 1., 2., 2.])
785::CODE;;>>> thresholds
786::CODE;;array([0.8 , 0.4 , 0.35, 0.1 ])
862::CODE;;Note: Support beyond :term:`binary` classification tasks, via one-vs-rest or
863::CODE;;one-vs-one, is not implemented.
864::CODE;;The precision is the ratio ``tp / (tp + fp)`` where ``tp`` is the number of
865::CODE;;true positives and ``fp`` the number of false positives. The precision is
866::CODE;;intuitively the ability of the classifier not to label as positive a sample
867::CODE;;that is negative.
868::CODE;;The recall is the ratio ``tp / (tp + fn)`` where ``tp`` is the number of
869::CODE;;true positives and ``fn`` the number of false negatives. The recall is
870::CODE;;intuitively the ability of the classifier to find all the positive samples.
871::CODE;;The last precision and recall values are 1. and 0. respectively and do not
872::CODE;;have a corresponding threshold. This ensures that the graph starts on the
873::CODE;;y axis.
874::CODE;;The first precision and recall values are precision=class balance and recall=1.0
875::CODE;;which corresponds to a classifier that always predicts the positive class.
876::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <precision_recall_f_measure_metrics>`.
877::CODE;;Parameters
878::CODE;;----------
879::CODE;;y_true : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
880::CODE;;True binary labels. If labels are not either {-1, 1} or {0, 1}, then
881::CODE;;pos_label should be explicitly given.
882::CODE;;y_score : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
883::CODE;;Target scores, can either be probability estimates of the positive
884::CODE;;class, or non-thresholded measure of decisions (as returned by
885::CODE;;`decision_function` on some classifiers).
886::CODE;;For :term:`decision_function` scores, values greater than or equal to
887::CODE;;zero should indicate the positive class.
888::CODE;;pos_label : int, float, bool or str, default=None
889::CODE;;The label of the positive class.
890::CODE;;When ``pos_label=None``, if y_true is in {-1, 1} or {0, 1},
891::CODE;;``pos_label`` is set to 1, otherwise an error will be raised.
892::CODE;;sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
893::CODE;;Sample weights.
894::CODE;;drop_intermediate : bool, default=False
895::CODE;;Whether to drop some suboptimal thresholds which would not appear
896::CODE;;on a plotted precision-recall curve. This is useful in order to create
897::CODE;;lighter precision-recall curves.
898::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.3
899::CODE;;Returns
900::CODE;;-------
901::CODE;;precision : ndarray of shape (n_thresholds + 1,)
902::CODE;;Precision values such that element i is the precision of
903::CODE;;predictions with score >= thresholds[i] and the last element is 1.
904::CODE;;recall : ndarray of shape (n_thresholds + 1,)
905::CODE;;Decreasing recall values such that element i is the recall of
906::CODE;;predictions with score >= thresholds[i] and the last element is 0.
907::CODE;;thresholds : ndarray of shape (n_thresholds,)
908::CODE;;Increasing thresholds on the decision function used to compute
909::CODE;;precision and recall where `n_thresholds = len(np.unique(y_score))`.
910::CODE;;See Also
911::CODE;;--------
912::CODE;;PrecisionRecallDisplay.from_estimator : Plot Precision Recall Curve given
913::CODE;;a binary classifier.
914::CODE;;PrecisionRecallDisplay.from_predictions : Plot Precision Recall Curve
915::CODE;;using predictions from a binary classifier.
916::CODE;;average_precision_score : Compute average precision from prediction scores.
917::CODE;;det_curve: Compute error rates for different probability thresholds.
918::CODE;;roc_curve : Compute Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve.
919::CODE;;confusion_matrix_at_thresholds : For binary classification, compute true negative,
920::CODE;;false positive, false negative and true positive counts per threshold.
921::CODE;;Examples
922::CODE;;--------
923::CODE;;>>> import numpy as np
924::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.metrics import precision_recall_curve
925::CODE;;>>> y_true = np.array([0, 0, 1, 1])
926::CODE;;>>> y_scores = np.array([0.1, 0.4, 0.35, 0.8])
927::CODE;;>>> precision, recall, thresholds = precision_recall_curve(
928::CODE;;... y_true, y_scores)
929::CODE;;>>> precision
930::CODE;;array([0.5 , 0.66666667, 0.5 , 1. , 1. ])
931::CODE;;>>> recall
932::CODE;;array([1. , 1. , 0.5, 0.5, 0. ])
933::CODE;;>>> thresholds
934::CODE;;array([0.1 , 0.35, 0.4 , 0.8 ])
992::CODE;;Note: Support beyond :term:`binary` classification tasks, via one-vs-rest or
993::CODE;;one-vs-one, is not implemented.
994::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <roc_metrics>`.
995::CODE;;Parameters
996::CODE;;----------
997::CODE;;y_true : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
998::CODE;;True binary labels. If labels are not either {-1, 1} or {0, 1}, then
999::CODE;;pos_label should be explicitly given.
1000::CODE;;y_score : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
1001::CODE;;Target scores, can either be probability estimates of the positive
1002::CODE;;class, confidence values, or non-thresholded measure of decisions
1003::CODE;;(as returned by "decision_function" on some classifiers).
1004::CODE;;For :term:`decision_function` scores, values greater than or equal to
1005::CODE;;zero should indicate the positive class.
1006::CODE;;pos_label : int, float, bool or str, default=None
1007::CODE;;The label of the positive class.
1008::CODE;;When ``pos_label=None``, if `y_true` is in {-1, 1} or {0, 1},
1009::CODE;;``pos_label`` is set to 1, otherwise an error will be raised.
1010::CODE;;sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
1011::CODE;;Sample weights.
1012::CODE;;drop_intermediate : bool, default=True
1013::CODE;;Whether to drop thresholds where the resulting point is collinear with
1014::CODE;;its neighbors in ROC space. This has no effect on the ROC AUC or visual
1015::CODE;;shape of the curve, but reduces the number of plotted points.
1016::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.17
1017::CODE;;parameter *drop_intermediate*.
1018::CODE;;Returns
1019::CODE;;-------
1020::CODE;;fpr : ndarray of shape (>2,)
1021::CODE;;Increasing false positive rates such that element `i` is the false
1022::CODE;;positive rate of predictions with score >= `thresholds[i]`.
1023::CODE;;tpr : ndarray of shape (>2,)
1024::CODE;;Increasing true positive rates such that element `i` is the true
1025::CODE;;positive rate of predictions with score >= `thresholds[i]`.
1026::CODE;;thresholds : ndarray of shape (n_thresholds,)
1027::CODE;;Decreasing thresholds on the decision function used to compute
1028::CODE;;fpr and tpr. The first threshold is set to `np.inf`.
1029::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.3
1030::CODE;;An arbitrary threshold at infinity (stored in `thresholds[0]`) is
1031::CODE;;added to represent a classifier that always predicts the negative
1032::CODE;;class, i.e. `fpr=0` and `tpr=0`.
1033::CODE;;See Also
1034::CODE;;--------
1035::CODE;;RocCurveDisplay.from_estimator : Plot Receiver Operating Characteristic
1036::CODE;;(ROC) curve given an estimator and some data.
1037::CODE;;RocCurveDisplay.from_predictions : Plot Receiver Operating Characteristic
1038::CODE;;(ROC) curve given the true and predicted values.
1039::CODE;;RocCurveDisplay.from_cv_results : Plot multi-fold ROC curves given
1040::CODE;;cross-validation results.
1041::CODE;;det_curve: Compute error rates for different probability thresholds.
1042::CODE;;roc_auc_score : Compute the area under the ROC curve.
1043::CODE;;confusion_matrix_at_thresholds : For binary classification, compute true negative,
1044::CODE;;false positive, false negative and true positive counts per threshold.
1045::CODE;;Notes
1046::CODE;;-----
1047::CODE;;Since the thresholds are sorted from low to high values, they
1048::CODE;;are reversed upon returning them to ensure they correspond to both ``fpr``
1049::CODE;;and ``tpr``, which are sorted in reversed order during their calculation.
1050::CODE;;References

1130::CODE;;Label ranking average precision (LRAP) is the average over each ground
1131::CODE;;truth label assigned to each sample, of the ratio of true vs. total
1132::CODE;;labels with lower score.
1133::CODE;;This metric is used in multilabel ranking problem, where the goal
1134::CODE;;is to give better rank to the labels associated to each sample.
1135::CODE;;The obtained score is always strictly greater than 0 and
1136::CODE;;the best value is 1.
1137::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <label_ranking_average_precision>`.
1138::CODE;;Parameters

1143::CODE;;Target scores, can either be probability estimates of the positive
1144::CODE;;class, confidence values, or non-thresholded measure of decisions
1145::CODE;;(as returned by "decision_function" on some classifiers).
1146::CODE;;For :term:`decision_function` scores, values greater than or equal to
1147::CODE;;zero should indicate the positive class.
1148::CODE;;sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
1149::CODE;;Sample weights.
1150::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.20
1151::CODE;;Returns
1152::CODE;;-------
1153::CODE;;score : float
1154::CODE;;Ranking-based average precision score.

1161::CODE;;>>> label_ranking_average_precision_score(y_true, y_score)

1343::CODE;;Sum the true scores ranked in the order induced by the predicted scores,
1344::CODE;;after applying a logarithmic discount.
1345::CODE;;This ranking metric yields a high value if true labels are ranked high by
1346::CODE;;``y_score``.
1347::CODE;;Parameters
1348::CODE;;----------
1349::CODE;;y_true : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_labels)
1350::CODE;;True targets of multilabel classification, or true scores of entities
1351::CODE;;to be ranked.
1352::CODE;;y_score : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_labels)
1353::CODE;;Target scores, can either be probability estimates, confidence values,
1354::CODE;;or non-thresholded measure of decisions (as returned by
1355::CODE;;"decision_function" on some classifiers).
1356::CODE;;k : int, default=None
1357::CODE;;Only consider the highest k scores in the ranking. If `None`, use all
1358::CODE;;outputs.
1359::CODE;;log_base : float, default=2
1360::CODE;;Base of the logarithm used for the discount. A low value means a
1361::CODE;;sharper discount (top results are more important).
1362::CODE;;ignore_ties : bool, default=False
1363::CODE;;Assume that there are no ties in y_score (which is likely to be the
1364::CODE;;case if y_score is continuous) for efficiency gains.
1365::CODE;;Returns
1366::CODE;;-------
1367::CODE;;discounted_cumulative_gain : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
1368::CODE;;The DCG score for each sample.
1369::CODE;;See Also
1370::CODE;;--------
1371::CODE;;ndcg_score : The Discounted Cumulative Gain divided by the Ideal Discounted
1372::CODE;;Cumulative Gain (the DCG obtained for a perfect ranking), in order to
1373::CODE;;have a score between 0 and 1.
1392::CODE;;Compute DCG by averaging over possible permutations of ties.
1393::CODE;;The gain (`y_true`) of an index falling inside a tied group (in the order
1394::CODE;;induced by `y_score`) is replaced by the average gain within this group.
1395::CODE;;The discounted gain for a tied group is then the average `y_true` within
1396::CODE;;this group times the sum of discounts of the corresponding ranks.
1397::CODE;;This amounts to averaging scores for all possible orderings of the tied
1398::CODE;;groups.
1399::CODE;;(note in the case of dcg@k the discount is 0 after index k)
1400::CODE;;Parameters
1401::CODE;;----------
1402::CODE;;y_true : ndarray
1403::CODE;;The true relevance scores.
1404::CODE;;y_score : ndarray
1405::CODE;;Predicted scores.
1406::CODE;;discount_cumsum : ndarray
1407::CODE;;Precomputed cumulative sum of the discounts.
1408::CODE;;Returns
1409::CODE;;-------
1410::CODE;;discounted_cumulative_gain : float
1411::CODE;;The discounted cumulative gain.
1412::CODE;;References
1413::CODE;;----------
1414::CODE;;McSherry, F., & Najork, M. (2008, March). Computing information retrieval
1415::CODE;;performance measures efficiently in the presence of tied scores. In
1416::CODE;;European conference on information retrieval (pp. 414-421). Springer,
1417::CODE;;Berlin, Heidelberg.
1456::CODE;;Sum the true scores ranked in the order induced by the predicted scores,
1457::CODE;;after applying a logarithmic discount.
1458::CODE;;This ranking metric yields a high value if true labels are ranked high by
1459::CODE;;``y_score``.
1460::CODE;;Usually the Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG, computed by
1461::CODE;;ndcg_score) is preferred.

1465::CODE;;True targets of multilabel classification, or true scores of entities

1470::CODE;;"decision_function" on some classifiers).

1473::CODE;;outputs.
1474::CODE;;log_base : float, default=2

1476::CODE;;sharper discount (top results are more important).

1701::CODE;;This metric computes the number of times where the correct label is among
1702::CODE;;the top `k` labels predicted (ranked by predicted scores). Note that the
1703::CODE;;multilabel case isn't covered here.
1704::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <top_k_accuracy_score>`
1705::CODE;;Parameters
1706::CODE;;----------
1707::CODE;;y_true : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
1708::CODE;;True labels.
1709::CODE;;y_score : array-like of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_classes)
1710::CODE;;Target scores. These can be either probability estimates or
1711::CODE;;non-thresholded decision values (as returned by
1712::CODE;;:term:`decision_function` on some classifiers).
1713::CODE;;The binary case expects scores with shape (n_samples,) while the
1714::CODE;;multiclass case expects scores with shape (n_samples, n_classes).
1715::CODE;;In the multiclass case, the order of the class scores must
1716::CODE;;correspond to the order of ``labels``, if provided, or else to
1717::CODE;;the numerical or lexicographical order of the labels in ``y_true``.
1718::CODE;;If ``y_true`` does not contain all the labels, ``labels`` must be
1719::CODE;;provided.
1720::CODE;;k : int, default=2
1721::CODE;;Number of most likely outcomes considered to find the correct label.
1722::CODE;;normalize : bool, default=True
1723::CODE;;If `True`, return the fraction of correctly classified samples.
1724::CODE;;Otherwise, return the number of correctly classified samples.
1725::CODE;;sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
1726::CODE;;Sample weights. If `None`, all samples are given the same weight.
1727::CODE;;labels : array-like of shape (n_classes,), default=None
1728::CODE;;Multiclass only. List of labels that index the classes in ``y_score``.
1729::CODE;;If ``None``, the numerical or lexicographical order of the labels in
1730::CODE;;``y_true`` is used. If ``y_true`` does not contain all the labels,
1731::CODE;;``labels`` must be provided.
1732::CODE;;Returns
1733::CODE;;-------
1734::CODE;;score : float
1735::CODE;;The top-k accuracy score. The best performance is 1 with
1736::CODE;;`normalize == True` and the number of samples with
1737::CODE;;`normalize == False`.
1738::CODE;;See Also
1739::CODE;;--------
1740::CODE;;accuracy_score : Compute the accuracy score. By default, the function will
1741::CODE;;return the fraction of correct predictions divided by the total number
1742::CODE;;of predictions.
1743::CODE;;Notes
1744::CODE;;-----
1745::CODE;;In cases where two or more labels are assigned equal predicted scores,
1746::CODE;;the labels with the highest indices will be chosen first. This might
1747::CODE;;impact the result if the correct label falls after the threshold because
1748::CODE;;of that.
1749::CODE;;Examples
1750::CODE;;--------

769::CODE;;def _assemble_r2_explained_variance(
770::CODE;;numerator, denominator, n_outputs, multioutput, force_finite, xp, device
771::CODE;;):
833::CODE;;Best possible score is 1.0, lower values are worse.
834::CODE;;In the particular case when ``y_true`` is constant, the explained variance
835::CODE;;score is not finite: it is either ``NaN`` (perfect predictions) or
836::CODE;;``-Inf`` (imperfect predictions). To prevent such non-finite numbers to
837::CODE;;pollute higher-level experiments such as a grid search cross-validation,
838::CODE;;by default these cases are replaced with 1.0 (perfect predictions) or 0.0
839::CODE;;(imperfect predictions) respectively. If ``force_finite``
840::CODE;;is set to ``False``, this score falls back on the original :math:`R^2`
841::CODE;;definition.
842::CODE;;.. note::
843::CODE;;The Explained Variance score is similar to the :func:`R^2 score <r2_score>`,
844::CODE;;but the former does not account for systematic offsets in the prediction
845::CODE;;(such as the intercept in linear models, i.e. different intercepts give
846::CODE;;the same Explained Variance score). Most often the :func:`R^2 score
847::CODE;;<r2_score>` should be preferred.
848::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <explained_variance_score>`.
849::CODE;;Parameters
850::CODE;;----------
851::CODE;;y_true : array-like of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_outputs)
852::CODE;;Ground truth (correct) target values.
853::CODE;;y_pred : array-like of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_outputs)
854::CODE;;Estimated target values.
855::CODE;;sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
856::CODE;;Sample weights.
857::CODE;;multioutput : {'raw_values', 'uniform_average', 'variance_weighted'} or \
858::CODE;;array-like of shape (n_outputs,), default='uniform_average'
859::CODE;;Defines aggregating of multiple output scores.
860::CODE;;Array-like value defines weights used to average scores.
861::CODE;;'raw_values' :
862::CODE;;Returns a full set of scores in case of multioutput input.
863::CODE;;'uniform_average' :
864::CODE;;Scores of all outputs are averaged with uniform weight.
865::CODE;;'variance_weighted' :
866::CODE;;Scores of all outputs are averaged, weighted by the variances
867::CODE;;of each individual output.
868::CODE;;force_finite : bool, default=True
869::CODE;;Flag indicating if ``NaN`` and ``-Inf`` scores resulting from constant
870::CODE;;data should be replaced with real numbers (``1.0`` if prediction is
871::CODE;;perfect, ``0.0`` otherwise). Default is ``True``, a convenient setting
872::CODE;;for hyperparameters' search procedures (e.g. grid search
873::CODE;;cross-validation).
874::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.1
875::CODE;;Returns
876::CODE;;-------
877::CODE;;score : float or ndarray of floats
878::CODE;;The explained variance or ndarray if 'multioutput' is 'raw_values'.
879::CODE;;See Also
880::CODE;;--------
881::CODE;;r2_score :
882::CODE;;Similar metric, but accounting for systematic offsets in
883::CODE;;prediction.
884::CODE;;Notes
885::CODE;;-----
886::CODE;;This is not a symmetric function.
887::CODE;;Examples
888::CODE;;--------
889::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.metrics import explained_variance_score
890::CODE;;>>> y_true = [3, -0.5, 2, 7]
891::CODE;;>>> y_pred = [2.5, 0.0, 2, 8]
892::CODE;;>>> explained_variance_score(y_true, y_pred)
893::CODE;;0.957...
894::CODE;;>>> y_true = [[0.5, 1], [-1, 1], [7, -6]]
895::CODE;;>>> y_pred = [[0, 2], [-1, 2], [8, -5]]
896::CODE;;>>> explained_variance_score(y_true, y_pred, multioutput='uniform_average')
897::CODE;;0.983...
898::CODE;;>>> y_true = [-2, -2, -2]
899::CODE;;>>> y_pred = [-2, -2, -2]
900::CODE;;>>> explained_variance_score(y_true, y_pred)
901::CODE;;1.0
902::CODE;;>>> explained_variance_score(y_true, y_pred, force_finite=False)
903::CODE;;nan
904::CODE;;>>> y_true = [-2, -2, -2]
905::CODE;;>>> y_pred = [-2, -2, -2 + 1e-8]
906::CODE;;>>> explained_variance_score(y_true, y_pred)
907::CODE;;0.0
908::CODE;;>>> explained_variance_score(y_true, y_pred, force_finite=False)
909::CODE;;-inf
957::CODE;;Best possible score is 1.0 and it can be negative (because the
958::CODE;;model can be arbitrarily worse). In the general case when the true y is
959::CODE;;non-constant, a constant model that always predicts the average y
960::CODE;;disregarding the input features would get a :math:`R^2` score of 0.0.
961::CODE;;In the particular case when ``y_true`` is constant, the :math:`R^2` score
962::CODE;;is not finite: it is either ``NaN`` (perfect predictions) or ``-Inf``
963::CODE;;(imperfect predictions). To prevent such non-finite numbers to pollute
964::CODE;;higher-level experiments such as a grid search cross-validation, by default
965::CODE;;these cases are replaced with 1.0 (perfect predictions) or 0.0 (imperfect
966::CODE;;predictions) respectively. You can set ``force_finite`` to ``False`` to
967::CODE;;prevent this fix from happening.
968::CODE;;Note: when the prediction residuals have zero mean, the :math:`R^2` score
969::CODE;;is identical to the
970::CODE;;:func:`Explained Variance score <explained_variance_score>`.
971::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <r2_score>`.
972::CODE;;Parameters
973::CODE;;----------
974::CODE;;y_true : array-like of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_outputs)
975::CODE;;Ground truth (correct) target values.
976::CODE;;y_pred : array-like of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_outputs)
977::CODE;;Estimated target values.
978::CODE;;sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
979::CODE;;Sample weights.
980::CODE;;multioutput : {'raw_values', 'uniform_average', 'variance_weighted'}, \
981::CODE;;array-like of shape (n_outputs,) or None, default='uniform_average'
982::CODE;;Defines aggregating of multiple output scores.
983::CODE;;Array-like value defines weights used to average scores.
984::CODE;;Default is "uniform_average".
985::CODE;;'raw_values' :
986::CODE;;Returns a full set of scores in case of multioutput input.
987::CODE;;'uniform_average' :
988::CODE;;Scores of all outputs are averaged with uniform weight.
989::CODE;;'variance_weighted' :
990::CODE;;Scores of all outputs are averaged, weighted by the variances
991::CODE;;of each individual output.
992::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 0.19
993::CODE;;Default value of multioutput is 'uniform_average'.
994::CODE;;force_finite : bool, default=True
995::CODE;;Flag indicating if ``NaN`` and ``-Inf`` scores resulting from constant
996::CODE;;data should be replaced with real numbers (``1.0`` if prediction is
997::CODE;;perfect, ``0.0`` otherwise). Default is ``True``, a convenient setting
998::CODE;;for hyperparameters' search procedures (e.g. grid search
999::CODE;;cross-validation).
1000::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.1
1001::CODE;;Returns
1002::CODE;;-------
1003::CODE;;z : float or ndarray of floats
1004::CODE;;The :math:`R^2` score or ndarray of scores if 'multioutput' is
1005::CODE;;'raw_values'.
1006::CODE;;Notes
1007::CODE;;-----
1008::CODE;;This is not a symmetric function.
1009::CODE;;Unlike most other scores, :math:`R^2` score may be negative (it need not
1010::CODE;;actually be the square of a quantity R).
1011::CODE;;This metric is not well-defined for single samples and will return a NaN
1012::CODE;;value if n_samples is less than two.
1013::CODE;;References
1014::CODE;;----------
1015::CODE;;.. [1] `Wikipedia entry on the Coefficient of determination
1016::CODE;;<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coefficient_of_determination>`_
1017::CODE;;Examples
1018::CODE;;--------
1019::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.metrics import r2_score
1020::CODE;;>>> y_true = [3, -0.5, 2, 7]
1021::CODE;;>>> y_pred = [2.5, 0.0, 2, 8]
1022::CODE;;>>> r2_score(y_true, y_pred)
1023::CODE;;0.948...
1024::CODE;;>>> y_true = [[0.5, 1], [-1, 1], [7, -6]]
1025::CODE;;>>> y_pred = [[0, 2], [-1, 2], [8, -5]]
1026::CODE;;>>> r2_score(y_true, y_pred,
1027::CODE;;... multioutput='variance_weighted')
1028::CODE;;0.938...
1029::CODE;;>>> y_true = [1, 2, 3]
1030::CODE;;>>> y_pred = [1, 2, 3]
1031::CODE;;>>> r2_score(y_true, y_pred)
1032::CODE;;1.0
1033::CODE;;>>> y_true = [1, 2, 3]
1034::CODE;;>>> y_pred = [2, 2, 2]

1094::CODE;;The max_error metric calculates the maximum residual error.
1095::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <max_error>`.
1096::CODE;;Parameters
1097::CODE;;----------
1098::CODE;;y_true : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
1099::CODE;;Ground truth (correct) target values.
1100::CODE;;y_pred : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
1101::CODE;;Estimated target values.
1102::CODE;;Returns
1103::CODE;;-------
1104::CODE;;max_error : float
1105::CODE;;A positive floating point value (the best value is 0.0).
1106::CODE;;Examples
1107::CODE;;--------
1108::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.metrics import max_error
1109::CODE;;>>> y_true = [3, 2, 7, 1]
1110::CODE;;>>> y_pred = [4, 2, 7, 1]
1111::CODE;;>>> max_error(y_true, y_pred)
1112::CODE;;1.0
1123::CODE;;xp, _ = get_namespace(y_true, y_pred)
1124::CODE;;p = power
1125::CODE;;if p < 0:
1127::CODE;;dev = 2 * (
1128::CODE;;xp.pow(
1129::CODE;;xp.where(y_true > 0, y_true, 0.0),
1130::CODE;;2 - p,
1131::CODE;;)
1132::CODE;;/ ((1 - p) * (2 - p))
1133::CODE;;- y_true * xp.pow(y_pred, 1 - p) / (1 - p)
1134::CODE;;+ xp.pow(y_pred, 2 - p) / (2 - p)
1135::CODE;;)
1136::CODE;;elif p == 0:
1138::CODE;;dev = (y_true - y_pred) ** 2
1139::CODE;;elif p == 1:
1141::CODE;;dev = 2 * (xlogy(y_true, y_true / y_pred) - y_true + y_pred)
1142::CODE;;elif p == 2:
1144::CODE;;dev = 2 * (xp.log(y_pred / y_true) + y_true / y_pred - 1)
1145::CODE;;else:
1146::CODE;;dev = 2 * (
1147::CODE;;xp.pow(y_true, 2 - p) / ((1 - p) * (2 - p))
1148::CODE;;- y_true * xp.pow(y_pred, 1 - p) / (1 - p)
1149::CODE;;+ xp.pow(y_pred, 2 - p) / (2 - p)
1150::CODE;;)
1151::CODE;;return float(_average(dev, weights=sample_weight, xp=xp))

8::CODE;;def _check_rows_and_columns(a, b):
18::CODE;;intersection = (a_rows * b_rows).sum() * (a_cols * b_cols).sum()
19::CODE;;a_size = a_rows.sum() * a_cols.sum()
20::CODE;;b_size = b_rows.sum() * b_cols.sum()
21::CODE;;return intersection / (a_size + b_size - intersection)
22::CODE;;def _pairwise_similarity(a, b, similarity):
27::CODE;;a_rows, a_cols, b_rows, b_cols = _check_rows_and_columns(a, b)
28::CODE;;n_a = a_rows.shape[0]
29::CODE;;n_b = b_rows.shape[0]
30::CODE;;result = np.array(
31::CODE;;[
32::CODE;;[similarity(a_rows[i], a_cols[i], b_rows[j], b_cols[j]) for j in range(n_b)]
33::CODE;;for i in range(n_a)
34::CODE;;]
35::CODE;;)
36::CODE;;return result
37::CODE;;@validate_params(
38::CODE;;{
39::CODE;;"a": [tuple],
40::CODE;;"b": [tuple],
41::CODE;;"similarity": [callable, StrOptions({"jaccard"})],
42::CODE;;},
43::CODE;;prefer_skip_nested_validation=True,
44::CODE;;)
45::CODE;;def consensus_score(a, b, *, similarity="jaccard"):
84::CODE;;if similarity == "jaccard":
85::CODE;;similarity = _jaccard
86::CODE;;matrix = _pairwise_similarity(a, b, similarity)
87::CODE;;row_indices, col_indices = linear_sum_assignment(1.0 - matrix)
88::CODE;;n_a = len(a[0])
89::CODE;;n_b = len(b[0])
90::CODE;;return float(matrix[row_indices, col_indices].sum() / max(n_a, n_b))
