1350::CODE;;def _run_search(self, evaluate_candidates):
1355::CODE;;RandomizedSearchCV implements a "fit" and a "score" method.
1356::CODE;;It also implements "score_samples", "predict", "predict_proba",
1357::CODE;;"decision_function", "transform" and "inverse_transform" if they are
1358::CODE;;implemented in the estimator used.
1359::CODE;;The parameters of the estimator used to apply these methods are optimized
1360::CODE;;by cross-validated search over parameter settings.
1361::CODE;;In contrast to GridSearchCV, not all parameter values are tried out, but
1362::CODE;;rather a fixed number of parameter settings is sampled from the specified
1363::CODE;;distributions. The number of parameter settings that are tried is
1364::CODE;;given by n_iter.
1365::CODE;;If all parameters are presented as a list,
1366::CODE;;sampling without replacement is performed. If at least one parameter
1367::CODE;;is given as a distribution, sampling with replacement is used.
1368::CODE;;It is highly recommended to use continuous distributions for continuous
1369::CODE;;parameters.
1370::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <randomized_parameter_search>`.
1371::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.14
1372::CODE;;Parameters
1373::CODE;;----------
1374::CODE;;estimator : estimator object
1375::CODE;;An object of that type is instantiated for each grid point.
1376::CODE;;This is assumed to implement the scikit-learn estimator interface.
1377::CODE;;Either estimator needs to provide a ``score`` function,
1378::CODE;;or ``scoring`` must be passed.
1379::CODE;;param_distributions : dict or list of dicts
1380::CODE;;Dictionary with parameters names (`str`) as keys and distributions
1381::CODE;;or lists of parameters to try. Distributions must provide a ``rvs``
1382::CODE;;method for sampling (such as those from scipy.stats.distributions).
1383::CODE;;If a list is given, it is sampled uniformly.
1384::CODE;;If a list of dicts is given, first a dict is sampled uniformly, and
1385::CODE;;then a parameter is sampled using that dict as above.
1386::CODE;;n_iter : int, default=10
1387::CODE;;Number of parameter settings that are sampled. n_iter trades
1388::CODE;;off runtime vs quality of the solution.
1389::CODE;;scoring : str, callable, list, tuple or dict, default=None
1390::CODE;;Strategy to evaluate the performance of the cross-validated model on
1391::CODE;;the test set.
1392::CODE;;If `scoring` represents a single score, one can use:
1393::CODE;;- a single string (see :ref:`scoring_string_names`);
1394::CODE;;- a callable (see :ref:`scoring_callable`) that returns a single value;
1395::CODE;;- `None`, the `estimator`'s
1396::CODE;;:ref:`default evaluation criterion <scoring_api_overview>` is used.
1397::CODE;;If `scoring` represents multiple scores, one can use:
1398::CODE;;- a list or tuple of unique strings;
1399::CODE;;- a callable returning a dictionary where the keys are the metric
1400::CODE;;names and the values are the metric scores;
1401::CODE;;- a dictionary with metric names as keys and callables as values.
1402::CODE;;See :ref:`multimetric_grid_search` for an example.
1403::CODE;;If None, the estimator's score method is used.
1404::CODE;;n_jobs : int, default=None
1405::CODE;;Number of jobs to run in parallel.
1406::CODE;;``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
1407::CODE;;``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
1408::CODE;;for more details.
1409::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: v0.20
1410::CODE;;`n_jobs` default changed from 1 to None
1411::CODE;;refit : bool, str, or callable, default=True
1412::CODE;;Refit an estimator using the best found parameters on the whole
1413::CODE;;dataset.
1414::CODE;;For multiple metric evaluation, this needs to be a `str` denoting the
1415::CODE;;scorer that would be used to find the best parameters for refitting
1416::CODE;;the estimator at the end.
1417::CODE;;Where there are considerations other than maximum score in
1418::CODE;;choosing a best estimator, ``refit`` can be set to a function which
1419::CODE;;returns the selected ``best_index_`` given the ``cv_results_``. In that
1420::CODE;;case, the ``best_estimator_`` and ``best_params_`` will be set
1421::CODE;;according to the returned ``best_index_`` while the ``best_score_``
1422::CODE;;attribute will not be available.
1423::CODE;;The refitted estimator is made available at the ``best_estimator_``
1424::CODE;;attribute and permits using ``predict`` directly on this
1425::CODE;;``RandomizedSearchCV`` instance.
1426::CODE;;Also for multiple metric evaluation, the attributes ``best_index_``,
1427::CODE;;``best_score_`` and ``best_params_`` will only be available if
1428::CODE;;``refit`` is set and all of them will be determined w.r.t this specific
1429::CODE;;scorer.
1430::CODE;;See ``scoring`` parameter to know more about multiple metric
1431::CODE;;evaluation.
1432::CODE;;See :ref:`this example
1433::CODE;;<sphx_glr_auto_examples_model_selection_plot_grid_search_refit_callable.py>`
1434::CODE;;for an example of how to use ``refit=callable`` to balance model
1435::CODE;;complexity and cross-validated score.
1436::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 0.20
1437::CODE;;Support for callable added.
1438::CODE;;cv : int, cross-validation generator or an iterable, default=None
1439::CODE;;Determines the cross-validation splitting strategy.
1440::CODE;;Possible inputs for cv are:
1441::CODE;;- None, to use the default 5-fold cross validation,
1442::CODE;;- integer, to specify the number of folds in a `(Stratified)KFold`,
1443::CODE;;- :term:`CV splitter`,
1444::CODE;;- An iterable yielding (train, test) splits as arrays of indices.
1445::CODE;;For integer/None inputs, if the estimator is a classifier and ``y`` is
1446::CODE;;either binary or multiclass, :class:`StratifiedKFold` is used. In all
1447::CODE;;other cases, :class:`KFold` is used. These splitters are instantiated
1448::CODE;;with `shuffle=False` so the splits will be the same across calls.
1449::CODE;;Refer :ref:`User Guide <cross_validation>` for the various
1450::CODE;;cross-validation strategies that can be used here.
1451::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 0.22
1452::CODE;;``cv`` default value if None changed from 3-fold to 5-fold.
1453::CODE;;verbose : int
1454::CODE;;Controls the verbosity: the higher, the more messages.
1455::CODE;;- >1 : the computation time for each fold and parameter candidate is
1456::CODE;;displayed;
1457::CODE;;- >2 : the score is also displayed;
1458::CODE;;- >3 : the fold and candidate parameter indexes are also displayed
1459::CODE;;together with the starting time of the computation.
1460::CODE;;pre_dispatch : int, or str, default='2*n_jobs'
1461::CODE;;Controls the number of jobs that get dispatched during parallel
1462::CODE;;execution. Reducing this number can be useful to avoid an
1463::CODE;;explosion of memory consumption when more jobs get dispatched
1464::CODE;;than CPUs can process. This parameter can be:
1465::CODE;;- None, in which case all the jobs are immediately created and spawned. Use
1466::CODE;;this for lightweight and fast-running jobs, to avoid delays due to on-demand
1467::CODE;;spawning of the jobs
1468::CODE;;- An int, giving the exact number of total jobs that are spawned
1469::CODE;;- A str, giving an expression as a function of n_jobs, as in '2*n_jobs'
1470::CODE;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
1471::CODE;;Pseudo random number generator state used for random uniform sampling
1472::CODE;;from lists of possible values instead of scipy.stats distributions.
1473::CODE;;Pass an int for reproducible output across multiple
1474::CODE;;function calls.
1475::CODE;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
1476::CODE;;error_score : 'raise' or numeric, default=np.nan
1477::CODE;;Value to assign to the score if an error occurs in estimator fitting.
1478::CODE;;If set to 'raise', the error is raised. If a numeric value is given,
1479::CODE;;FitFailedWarning is raised. This parameter does not affect the refit
1480::CODE;;step, which will always raise the error.
1481::CODE;;return_train_score : bool, default=False
1482::CODE;;If ``False``, the ``cv_results_`` attribute will not include training
1483::CODE;;scores.
1484::CODE;;Computing training scores is used to get insights on how different
1485::CODE;;parameter settings impact the overfitting/underfitting trade-off.
1486::CODE;;However computing the scores on the training set can be computationally
1487::CODE;;expensive and is not strictly required to select the parameters that
1488::CODE;;yield the best generalization performance.
1489::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.19
1490::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 0.21
1491::CODE;;Default value was changed from ``True`` to ``False``
1492::CODE;;Attributes
1493::CODE;;----------
1494::CODE;;cv_results_ : dict of numpy (masked) ndarrays
1495::CODE;;A dict with keys as column headers and values as columns, that can be
1496::CODE;;imported into a pandas ``DataFrame``.
1497::CODE;;For instance the below given table
1498::CODE;;+--------------+-------------+-------------------+---+---------------+

1512::CODE;;'split0_test_score' : [0.80, 0.84, 0.70],
1513::CODE;;'split1_test_score' : [0.82, 0.50, 0.70],
1514::CODE;;'mean_test_score' : [0.81, 0.67, 0.70],
1515::CODE;;'std_test_score' : [0.01, 0.24, 0.00],
1516::CODE;;'rank_test_score' : [1, 3, 2],
1517::CODE;;'split0_train_score' : [0.80, 0.92, 0.70],
1518::CODE;;'split1_train_score' : [0.82, 0.55, 0.70],

1524::CODE;;'std_score_time' : [0.00, 0.00, 0.00],
1525::CODE;;'params' : [{'kernel' : 'rbf', 'gamma' : 0.1}, ...],
1526::CODE;;}
1527::CODE;;For an example of analysing ``cv_results_``,
1528::CODE;;see :ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_model_selection_plot_grid_search_stats.py`.
1529::CODE;;NOTE
1530::CODE;;The key ``'params'`` is used to store a list of parameter
1531::CODE;;settings dicts for all the parameter candidates.
1532::CODE;;The ``mean_fit_time``, ``std_fit_time``, ``mean_score_time`` and
1533::CODE;;``std_score_time`` are all in seconds.
1534::CODE;;For multi-metric evaluation, the scores for all the scorers are
1535::CODE;;available in the ``cv_results_`` dict at the keys ending with that
1536::CODE;;scorer's name (``'_<scorer_name>'``) instead of ``'_score'`` shown
1537::CODE;;above. ('split0_test_precision', 'mean_train_precision' etc.)
1538::CODE;;best_estimator_ : estimator
1539::CODE;;Estimator that was chosen by the search, i.e. estimator
1540::CODE;;which gave highest score (or smallest loss if specified)
1541::CODE;;on the left out data. Not available if ``refit=False``.
1542::CODE;;For multi-metric evaluation, this attribute is present only if
1543::CODE;;``refit`` is specified.
1544::CODE;;See ``refit`` parameter for more information on allowed values.
1545::CODE;;best_score_ : float
1546::CODE;;Mean cross-validated score of the best_estimator.

1548::CODE;;``False``. See ``refit`` parameter for more information.
1549::CODE;;This attribute is not available if ``refit`` is a function.
1550::CODE;;best_params_ : dict
1551::CODE;;Parameter setting that gave the best results on the hold out data.
1552::CODE;;For multi-metric evaluation, this is not available if ``refit`` is
1553::CODE;;``False``. See ``refit`` parameter for more information.
1554::CODE;;best_index_ : int
1555::CODE;;The index (of the ``cv_results_`` arrays) which corresponds to the best
1556::CODE;;candidate parameter setting.
1557::CODE;;The dict at ``search.cv_results_['params'][search.best_index_]`` gives
1558::CODE;;the parameter setting for the best model, that gives the highest
1559::CODE;;mean score (``search.best_score_``).
1560::CODE;;For multi-metric evaluation, this is not available if ``refit`` is
1561::CODE;;``False``. See ``refit`` parameter for more information.
1562::CODE;;scorer_ : function or a dict
1563::CODE;;Scorer function used on the held out data to choose the best
1564::CODE;;parameters for the model.
1565::CODE;;For multi-metric evaluation, this attribute holds the validated
1566::CODE;;``scoring`` dict which maps the scorer key to the scorer callable.
1567::CODE;;n_splits_ : int
1568::CODE;;The number of cross-validation splits (folds/iterations).
1569::CODE;;refit_time_ : float

1571::CODE;;This is present only if ``refit`` is not False.
1572::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.20
1573::CODE;;multimetric_ : bool

1575::CODE;;classes_ : ndarray of shape (n_classes,)

1578::CODE;;n_features_in_ : int
1579::CODE;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`. Only defined if
1580::CODE;;`best_estimator_` is defined (see the documentation for the `refit`
1581::CODE;;parameter for more details) and that `best_estimator_` exposes
1582::CODE;;`n_features_in_` when fit.
1583::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
1584::CODE;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
1585::CODE;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Only defined if
1586::CODE;;`best_estimator_` is defined (see the documentation for the `refit`
1587::CODE;;parameter for more details) and that `best_estimator_` exposes
1588::CODE;;`feature_names_in_` when fit.

1590::CODE;;See Also
1591::CODE;;--------
1592::CODE;;GridSearchCV : Does exhaustive search over a grid of parameters.
1593::CODE;;ParameterSampler : A generator over parameter settings, constructed from
1594::CODE;;param_distributions.
1595::CODE;;Notes
1596::CODE;;-----
1597::CODE;;The parameters selected are those that maximize the score of the held-out
1598::CODE;;data, according to the scoring parameter.
1599::CODE;;If `n_jobs` was set to a value higher than one, the data is copied for each
1600::CODE;;parameter setting(and not `n_jobs` times). This is done for efficiency
1601::CODE;;reasons if individual jobs take very little time, but may raise errors if
1602::CODE;;the dataset is large and not enough memory is available. A workaround in
1603::CODE;;this case is to set `pre_dispatch`. Then, the memory is copied only
1604::CODE;;`pre_dispatch` many times. A reasonable value for `pre_dispatch` is `2 *
1605::CODE;;n_jobs`.

1607::CODE;;--------
1608::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
1609::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
1610::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.model_selection import RandomizedSearchCV
1611::CODE;;>>> from scipy.stats import uniform
1612::CODE;;>>> iris = load_iris()
1613::CODE;;>>> logistic = LogisticRegression(solver='saga', tol=1e-2, max_iter=200,
1614::CODE;;... random_state=0)
1615::CODE;;>>> distributions = dict(C=uniform(loc=0, scale=4),
1616::CODE;;... penalty=['l2', 'l1'])
1617::CODE;;>>> clf = RandomizedSearchCV(logistic, distributions, random_state=0)
1618::CODE;;>>> search = clf.fit(iris.data, iris.target)
1619::CODE;;>>> search.best_params_
1620::CODE;;{'C': np.float64(2.195...), 'penalty': 'l1'}

17::CODE;;class _SubsampleMetaSplitter:
55::CODE;;Ref:
56::CODE;;Almost optimal exploration in multi-armed bandits, ICML 13
57::CODE;;Zohar Karnin, Tomer Koren, Oren Somekh
172::CODE;;We want the best candidate out of the last iteration. By default
173::CODE;;BaseSearchCV would return the best candidate out of all iterations.
174::CODE;;Currently, we only support for a single metric thus `refit` and
175::CODE;;`refit_metric` are not required.
193::CODE;;Parameters
194::CODE;;----------
195::CODE;;X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
196::CODE;;Training vector, where `n_samples` is the number of samples and
197::CODE;;`n_features` is the number of features.
198::CODE;;y : array-like, shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_output), optional
199::CODE;;Target relative to X for classification or regression;
200::CODE;;None for unsupervised learning.
201::CODE;;**params : dict of string -> object
202::CODE;;Parameters passed to the ``fit`` method of the estimator.
203::CODE;;Returns
204::CODE;;-------
205::CODE;;self : object
206::CODE;;Instance of fitted estimator.
316::CODE;;The search strategy starts evaluating all the candidates with a small
317::CODE;;amount of resources and iteratively selects the best candidates, using
318::CODE;;more and more resources.
319::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User guide <successive_halving_user_guide>`.
320::CODE;;.. note::
321::CODE;;This estimator is still **experimental** for now: the predictions
322::CODE;;and the API might change without any deprecation cycle. To use it,
323::CODE;;you need to explicitly import ``enable_halving_search_cv``::
327::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.model_selection import HalvingGridSearchCV
328::CODE;;Parameters
329::CODE;;----------
330::CODE;;estimator : estimator object
331::CODE;;This is assumed to implement the scikit-learn estimator interface.
332::CODE;;Either estimator needs to provide a ``score`` function,
333::CODE;;or ``scoring`` must be passed.
334::CODE;;param_grid : dict or list of dictionaries
335::CODE;;Dictionary with parameters names (string) as keys and lists of
336::CODE;;parameter settings to try as values, or a list of such
337::CODE;;dictionaries, in which case the grids spanned by each dictionary
338::CODE;;in the list are explored. This enables searching over any sequence
339::CODE;;of parameter settings.
340::CODE;;factor : int or float, default=3
341::CODE;;The 'halving' parameter, which determines the proportion of candidates
342::CODE;;that are selected for each subsequent iteration. For example,
343::CODE;;``factor=3`` means that only one third of the candidates are selected.
344::CODE;;resource : ``'n_samples'`` or str, default='n_samples'
345::CODE;;Defines the resource that increases with each iteration. By default,
346::CODE;;the resource is the number of samples. It can also be set to any
347::CODE;;parameter of the base estimator that accepts positive integer
348::CODE;;values, e.g. 'n_iterations' or 'n_estimators' for a gradient
349::CODE;;boosting estimator. In this case ``max_resources`` cannot be 'auto'
350::CODE;;and must be set explicitly.
351::CODE;;max_resources : int, default='auto'
352::CODE;;The maximum amount of resource that any candidate is allowed to use
353::CODE;;for a given iteration. By default, this is set to ``n_samples`` when
354::CODE;;``resource='n_samples'`` (default), else an error is raised.
355::CODE;;min_resources : {'exhaust', 'smallest'} or int, default='exhaust'
356::CODE;;The minimum amount of resource that any candidate is allowed to use
357::CODE;;for a given iteration. Equivalently, this defines the amount of
358::CODE;;resources `r0` that are allocated for each candidate at the first
359::CODE;;iteration.
360::CODE;;- 'smallest' is a heuristic that sets `r0` to a small value:
361::CODE;;- ``n_splits * 2`` when ``resource='n_samples'`` for a regression problem
362::CODE;;- ``n_classes * n_splits * 2`` when ``resource='n_samples'`` for a
363::CODE;;classification problem
364::CODE;;- ``1`` when ``resource != 'n_samples'``
365::CODE;;- 'exhaust' will set `r0` such that the **last** iteration uses as
366::CODE;;much resources as possible. Namely, the last iteration will use the
367::CODE;;highest value smaller than ``max_resources`` that is a multiple of
368::CODE;;both ``min_resources`` and ``factor``. In general, using 'exhaust'
369::CODE;;leads to a more accurate estimator, but is slightly more time
370::CODE;;consuming.
371::CODE;;Note that the amount of resources used at each iteration is always a
372::CODE;;multiple of ``min_resources``.
373::CODE;;aggressive_elimination : bool, default=False
374::CODE;;This is only relevant in cases where there isn't enough resources to
375::CODE;;reduce the remaining candidates to at most `factor` after the last
376::CODE;;iteration. If ``True``, then the search process will 'replay' the
377::CODE;;first iteration for as long as needed until the number of candidates
378::CODE;;is small enough. This is ``False`` by default, which means that the
379::CODE;;last iteration may evaluate more than ``factor`` candidates. See
380::CODE;;:ref:`aggressive_elimination` for more details.
381::CODE;;cv : int, cross-validation generator or iterable, default=5
382::CODE;;Determines the cross-validation splitting strategy.
383::CODE;;Possible inputs for cv are:
384::CODE;;- integer, to specify the number of folds in a `(Stratified)KFold`,
385::CODE;;- :term:`CV splitter`,
386::CODE;;- An iterable yielding (train, test) splits as arrays of indices.
387::CODE;;For integer/None inputs, if the estimator is a classifier and ``y`` is
388::CODE;;either binary or multiclass, :class:`StratifiedKFold` is used. In all
389::CODE;;other cases, :class:`KFold` is used. These splitters are instantiated
390::CODE;;with `shuffle=False` so the splits will be the same across calls.
391::CODE;;Refer :ref:`User Guide <cross_validation>` for the various
392::CODE;;cross-validation strategies that can be used here.
393::CODE;;.. note::
394::CODE;;Due to implementation details, the folds produced by `cv` must be
395::CODE;;the same across multiple calls to `cv.split()`. For
396::CODE;;built-in `scikit-learn` iterators, this can be achieved by
397::CODE;;deactivating shuffling (`shuffle=False`), or by setting the
398::CODE;;`cv`'s `random_state` parameter to an integer.
399::CODE;;scoring : str or callable, default=None
400::CODE;;Scoring method to use to evaluate the predictions on the test set.
401::CODE;;- str: see :ref:`scoring_string_names` for options.
402::CODE;;- callable: a scorer callable object (e.g., function) with signature
403::CODE;;``scorer(estimator, X, y)``. See :ref:`scoring_callable` for details.
404::CODE;;- `None`: the `estimator`'s
405::CODE;;:ref:`default evaluation criterion <scoring_api_overview>` is used.
406::CODE;;refit : bool or callable, default=True
407::CODE;;Refit an estimator using the best found parameters on the whole
408::CODE;;dataset.
409::CODE;;Where there are considerations other than maximum score in
410::CODE;;choosing a best estimator, ``refit`` can be set to a function which
411::CODE;;returns the selected ``best_index_`` given ``cv_results_``. In that
412::CODE;;case, the ``best_estimator_`` and ``best_params_`` will be set
413::CODE;;according to the returned ``best_index_`` while the ``best_score_``
414::CODE;;attribute will not be available.
415::CODE;;The refitted estimator is made available at the ``best_estimator_``
416::CODE;;attribute and permits using ``predict`` directly on this
417::CODE;;``HalvingGridSearchCV`` instance.
418::CODE;;See :ref:`this example
419::CODE;;<sphx_glr_auto_examples_model_selection_plot_grid_search_refit_callable.py>`
420::CODE;;for an example of how to use ``refit=callable`` to balance model
421::CODE;;complexity and cross-validated score.
422::CODE;;error_score : 'raise' or numeric
423::CODE;;Value to assign to the score if an error occurs in estimator fitting.
424::CODE;;If set to 'raise', the error is raised. If a numeric value is given,
425::CODE;;FitFailedWarning is raised. This parameter does not affect the refit
426::CODE;;step, which will always raise the error. Default is ``np.nan``.
427::CODE;;return_train_score : bool, default=False
428::CODE;;If ``False``, the ``cv_results_`` attribute will not include training
429::CODE;;scores.
430::CODE;;Computing training scores is used to get insights on how different
431::CODE;;parameter settings impact the overfitting/underfitting trade-off.
432::CODE;;However computing the scores on the training set can be computationally
433::CODE;;expensive and is not strictly required to select the parameters that
434::CODE;;yield the best generalization performance.
435::CODE;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
436::CODE;;Pseudo random number generator state used for subsampling the dataset
437::CODE;;when `resources != 'n_samples'`. Ignored otherwise.
438::CODE;;Pass an int for reproducible output across multiple function calls.
439::CODE;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
440::CODE;;n_jobs : int or None, default=None
441::CODE;;Number of jobs to run in parallel.
442::CODE;;``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
443::CODE;;``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
444::CODE;;for more details.
445::CODE;;verbose : int
446::CODE;;Controls the verbosity: the higher, the more messages.
447::CODE;;Attributes
448::CODE;;----------
449::CODE;;n_resources_ : list of int
450::CODE;;The amount of resources used at each iteration.
451::CODE;;n_candidates_ : list of int
452::CODE;;The number of candidate parameters that were evaluated at each
453::CODE;;iteration.
454::CODE;;n_remaining_candidates_ : int
455::CODE;;The number of candidate parameters that are left after the last
456::CODE;;iteration. It corresponds to `ceil(n_candidates[-1] / factor)`
457::CODE;;max_resources_ : int
458::CODE;;The maximum number of resources that any candidate is allowed to use
459::CODE;;for a given iteration. Note that since the number of resources used
460::CODE;;at each iteration must be a multiple of ``min_resources_``, the
461::CODE;;actual number of resources used at the last iteration may be smaller
462::CODE;;than ``max_resources_``.
463::CODE;;min_resources_ : int
464::CODE;;The amount of resources that are allocated for each candidate at the
465::CODE;;first iteration.
466::CODE;;n_iterations_ : int
467::CODE;;The actual number of iterations that were run. This is equal to
468::CODE;;``n_required_iterations_`` if ``aggressive_elimination`` is ``True``.
469::CODE;;Else, this is equal to ``min(n_possible_iterations_,
470::CODE;;n_required_iterations_)``.
471::CODE;;n_possible_iterations_ : int
472::CODE;;The number of iterations that are possible starting with
473::CODE;;``min_resources_`` resources and without exceeding
474::CODE;;``max_resources_``.
475::CODE;;n_required_iterations_ : int
476::CODE;;The number of iterations that are required to end up with less than
477::CODE;;``factor`` candidates at the last iteration, starting with
478::CODE;;``min_resources_`` resources. This will be smaller than
479::CODE;;``n_possible_iterations_`` when there isn't enough resources.
480::CODE;;cv_results_ : dict of numpy (masked) ndarrays
481::CODE;;A dict with keys as column headers and values as columns, that can be
482::CODE;;imported into a pandas ``DataFrame``. It contains lots of information
483::CODE;;for analysing the results of a search.
484::CODE;;Please refer to the :ref:`User guide<successive_halving_cv_results>`
485::CODE;;for details.
486::CODE;;For an example of analysing ``cv_results_``,
487::CODE;;see :ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_model_selection_plot_grid_search_stats.py`.
488::CODE;;best_estimator_ : estimator or dict
489::CODE;;Estimator that was chosen by the search, i.e. estimator
490::CODE;;which gave highest score (or smallest loss if specified)
491::CODE;;on the left out data. Not available if ``refit=False``.
492::CODE;;best_score_ : float
493::CODE;;Mean cross-validated score of the best_estimator.
494::CODE;;best_params_ : dict
495::CODE;;Parameter setting that gave the best results on the hold out data.
496::CODE;;best_index_ : int
497::CODE;;The index (of the ``cv_results_`` arrays) which corresponds to the best
498::CODE;;candidate parameter setting.
499::CODE;;The dict at ``search.cv_results_['params'][search.best_index_]`` gives
500::CODE;;the parameter setting for the best model, that gives the highest
501::CODE;;mean score (``search.best_score_``).
502::CODE;;scorer_ : function or a dict
503::CODE;;Scorer function used on the held out data to choose the best
504::CODE;;parameters for the model.
505::CODE;;n_splits_ : int
506::CODE;;The number of cross-validation splits (folds/iterations).
507::CODE;;refit_time_ : float
508::CODE;;Seconds used for refitting the best model on the whole dataset.
509::CODE;;This is present only if ``refit`` is not False.
510::CODE;;multimetric_ : bool
511::CODE;;Whether or not the scorers compute several metrics.
512::CODE;;classes_ : ndarray of shape (n_classes,)
513::CODE;;The classes labels. This is present only if ``refit`` is specified and
514::CODE;;the underlying estimator is a classifier.
515::CODE;;n_features_in_ : int
516::CODE;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`. Only defined if
517::CODE;;`best_estimator_` is defined (see the documentation for the `refit`
518::CODE;;parameter for more details) and that `best_estimator_` exposes
519::CODE;;`n_features_in_` when fit.
520::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
521::CODE;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
522::CODE;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Only defined if
523::CODE;;`best_estimator_` is defined (see the documentation for the `refit`
524::CODE;;parameter for more details) and that `best_estimator_` exposes
525::CODE;;`feature_names_in_` when fit.
526::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
527::CODE;;See Also
528::CODE;;--------
529::CODE;;:class:`HalvingRandomSearchCV`:
530::CODE;;Random search over a set of parameters using successive halving.
531::CODE;;Notes
532::CODE;;-----
533::CODE;;The parameters selected are those that maximize the score of the held-out
534::CODE;;data, according to the scoring parameter.
535::CODE;;All parameter combinations scored with a NaN will share the lowest rank.
536::CODE;;Examples
537::CODE;;--------
538::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
539::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
541::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.model_selection import HalvingGridSearchCV
542::CODE;;...
543::CODE;;>>> X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True)
544::CODE;;>>> clf = RandomForestClassifier(random_state=0)
545::CODE;;...
546::CODE;;>>> param_grid = {"max_depth": [3, None],
547::CODE;;... "min_samples_split": [5, 10]}
548::CODE;;>>> search = HalvingGridSearchCV(clf, param_grid, resource='n_estimators',
549::CODE;;... max_resources=10,
550::CODE;;... random_state=0).fit(X, y)
552::CODE;;{'max_depth': None, 'min_samples_split': 10, 'n_estimators': 9}
598::CODE;;The search strategy starts evaluating all the candidates with a small
599::CODE;;amount of resources and iteratively selects the best candidates, using more
600::CODE;;and more resources.
601::CODE;;The candidates are sampled at random from the parameter space and the
602::CODE;;number of sampled candidates is determined by ``n_candidates``.
603::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User guide<successive_halving_user_guide>`.
604::CODE;;.. note::
605::CODE;;This estimator is still **experimental** for now: the predictions
606::CODE;;and the API might change without any deprecation cycle. To use it,
607::CODE;;you need to explicitly import ``enable_halving_search_cv``::
611::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.model_selection import HalvingRandomSearchCV
612::CODE;;Parameters
613::CODE;;----------
614::CODE;;estimator : estimator object
615::CODE;;This is assumed to implement the scikit-learn estimator interface.
616::CODE;;Either estimator needs to provide a ``score`` function,
617::CODE;;or ``scoring`` must be passed.
618::CODE;;param_distributions : dict or list of dicts
619::CODE;;Dictionary with parameters names (`str`) as keys and distributions
620::CODE;;or lists of parameters to try. Distributions must provide a ``rvs``
621::CODE;;method for sampling (such as those from scipy.stats.distributions).
622::CODE;;If a list is given, it is sampled uniformly.
623::CODE;;If a list of dicts is given, first a dict is sampled uniformly, and
624::CODE;;then a parameter is sampled using that dict as above.
625::CODE;;n_candidates : "exhaust" or int, default="exhaust"
626::CODE;;The number of candidate parameters to sample, at the first
627::CODE;;iteration. Using 'exhaust' will sample enough candidates so that the
628::CODE;;last iteration uses as many resources as possible, based on
629::CODE;;`min_resources`, `max_resources` and `factor`. In this case,
630::CODE;;`min_resources` cannot be 'exhaust'.
631::CODE;;factor : int or float, default=3
632::CODE;;The 'halving' parameter, which determines the proportion of candidates
633::CODE;;that are selected for each subsequent iteration. For example,
634::CODE;;``factor=3`` means that only one third of the candidates are selected.
635::CODE;;resource : ``'n_samples'`` or str, default='n_samples'
636::CODE;;Defines the resource that increases with each iteration. By default,
637::CODE;;the resource is the number of samples. It can also be set to any
638::CODE;;parameter of the base estimator that accepts positive integer
639::CODE;;values, e.g. 'n_iterations' or 'n_estimators' for a gradient
640::CODE;;boosting estimator. In this case ``max_resources`` cannot be 'auto'
641::CODE;;and must be set explicitly.
642::CODE;;max_resources : int, default='auto'
643::CODE;;The maximum number of resources that any candidate is allowed to use
644::CODE;;for a given iteration. By default, this is set ``n_samples`` when
645::CODE;;``resource='n_samples'`` (default), else an error is raised.
646::CODE;;min_resources : {'exhaust', 'smallest'} or int, default='smallest'
647::CODE;;The minimum amount of resource that any candidate is allowed to use
648::CODE;;for a given iteration. Equivalently, this defines the amount of
649::CODE;;resources `r0` that are allocated for each candidate at the first
650::CODE;;iteration.
651::CODE;;- 'smallest' is a heuristic that sets `r0` to a small value:
652::CODE;;- ``n_splits * 2`` when ``resource='n_samples'`` for a regression problem
653::CODE;;- ``n_classes * n_splits * 2`` when ``resource='n_samples'`` for a
654::CODE;;classification problem
655::CODE;;- ``1`` when ``resource != 'n_samples'``
656::CODE;;- 'exhaust' will set `r0` such that the **last** iteration uses as
657::CODE;;much resources as possible. Namely, the last iteration will use the
658::CODE;;highest value smaller than ``max_resources`` that is a multiple of
659::CODE;;both ``min_resources`` and ``factor``. In general, using 'exhaust'
660::CODE;;leads to a more accurate estimator, but is slightly more time
661::CODE;;consuming. 'exhaust' isn't available when `n_candidates='exhaust'`.
662::CODE;;Note that the amount of resources used at each iteration is always a
663::CODE;;multiple of ``min_resources``.
664::CODE;;aggressive_elimination : bool, default=False
665::CODE;;This is only relevant in cases where there isn't enough resources to
666::CODE;;reduce the remaining candidates to at most `factor` after the last
667::CODE;;iteration. If ``True``, then the search process will 'replay' the
668::CODE;;first iteration for as long as needed until the number of candidates
669::CODE;;is small enough. This is ``False`` by default, which means that the
670::CODE;;last iteration may evaluate more than ``factor`` candidates. See
671::CODE;;:ref:`aggressive_elimination` for more details.
672::CODE;;cv : int, cross-validation generator or an iterable, default=5
673::CODE;;Determines the cross-validation splitting strategy.
674::CODE;;Possible inputs for cv are:
675::CODE;;- integer, to specify the number of folds in a `(Stratified)KFold`,
676::CODE;;- :term:`CV splitter`,
677::CODE;;- An iterable yielding (train, test) splits as arrays of indices.
678::CODE;;For integer/None inputs, if the estimator is a classifier and ``y`` is
679::CODE;;either binary or multiclass, :class:`StratifiedKFold` is used. In all
680::CODE;;other cases, :class:`KFold` is used. These splitters are instantiated
681::CODE;;with `shuffle=False` so the splits will be the same across calls.
682::CODE;;Refer :ref:`User Guide <cross_validation>` for the various
683::CODE;;cross-validation strategies that can be used here.
684::CODE;;.. note::
685::CODE;;Due to implementation details, the folds produced by `cv` must be
686::CODE;;the same across multiple calls to `cv.split()`. For
687::CODE;;built-in `scikit-learn` iterators, this can be achieved by
688::CODE;;deactivating shuffling (`shuffle=False`), or by setting the
689::CODE;;`cv`'s `random_state` parameter to an integer.
690::CODE;;scoring : str or callable, default=None
691::CODE;;Scoring method to use to evaluate the predictions on the test set.
692::CODE;;- str: see :ref:`scoring_string_names` for options.
693::CODE;;- callable: a scorer callable object (e.g., function) with signature
694::CODE;;``scorer(estimator, X, y)``. See :ref:`scoring_callable` for details.
695::CODE;;- `None`: the `estimator`'s
696::CODE;;:ref:`default evaluation criterion <scoring_api_overview>` is used.
697::CODE;;refit : bool or callable, default=True
698::CODE;;Refit an estimator using the best found parameters on the whole
699::CODE;;dataset.
700::CODE;;Where there are considerations other than maximum score in
701::CODE;;choosing a best estimator, ``refit`` can be set to a function which
702::CODE;;returns the selected ``best_index_`` given ``cv_results_``. In that
703::CODE;;case, the ``best_estimator_`` and ``best_params_`` will be set
704::CODE;;according to the returned ``best_index_`` while the ``best_score_``
705::CODE;;attribute will not be available.
706::CODE;;The refitted estimator is made available at the ``best_estimator_``
707::CODE;;attribute and permits using ``predict`` directly on this
708::CODE;;``HalvingRandomSearchCV`` instance.
709::CODE;;See :ref:`this example
710::CODE;;<sphx_glr_auto_examples_model_selection_plot_grid_search_refit_callable.py>`
711::CODE;;for an example of how to use ``refit=callable`` to balance model
712::CODE;;complexity and cross-validated score.
713::CODE;;error_score : 'raise' or numeric
714::CODE;;Value to assign to the score if an error occurs in estimator fitting.
715::CODE;;If set to 'raise', the error is raised. If a numeric value is given,
716::CODE;;FitFailedWarning is raised. This parameter does not affect the refit
717::CODE;;step, which will always raise the error. Default is ``np.nan``.
718::CODE;;return_train_score : bool, default=False
719::CODE;;If ``False``, the ``cv_results_`` attribute will not include training
720::CODE;;scores.
721::CODE;;Computing training scores is used to get insights on how different
722::CODE;;parameter settings impact the overfitting/underfitting trade-off.
723::CODE;;However computing the scores on the training set can be computationally
724::CODE;;expensive and is not strictly required to select the parameters that
725::CODE;;yield the best generalization performance.
726::CODE;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
727::CODE;;Pseudo random number generator state used for subsampling the dataset
728::CODE;;when `resources != 'n_samples'`. Also used for random uniform
729::CODE;;sampling from lists of possible values instead of scipy.stats
730::CODE;;distributions.
731::CODE;;Pass an int for reproducible output across multiple function calls.
732::CODE;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
733::CODE;;n_jobs : int or None, default=None
734::CODE;;Number of jobs to run in parallel.
735::CODE;;``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
736::CODE;;``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
737::CODE;;for more details.
738::CODE;;verbose : int
739::CODE;;Controls the verbosity: the higher, the more messages.
740::CODE;;Attributes

743::CODE;;The amount of resources used at each iteration.

132::CODE;;@abstractmethod
133::CODE;;def get_n_splits(self, X=None, y=None, groups=None):
139::CODE;;Provides train/test indices to split data in train/test sets. Each
140::CODE;;sample is used once as a test set (singleton) while the remaining
141::CODE;;samples form the training set.
142::CODE;;Note: ``LeaveOneOut()`` is equivalent to ``KFold(n_splits=n)`` and
143::CODE;;``LeavePOut(p=1)`` where ``n`` is the number of samples.
144::CODE;;Due to the high number of test sets (which is the same as the
145::CODE;;number of samples) this cross-validation method can be very costly.
146::CODE;;For large datasets one should favor :class:`KFold`, :class:`ShuffleSplit`
147::CODE;;or :class:`StratifiedKFold`.
148::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <leave_one_out>`.
149::CODE;;Examples
150::CODE;;--------
151::CODE;;>>> import numpy as np
152::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.model_selection import LeaveOneOut
153::CODE;;>>> X = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
154::CODE;;>>> y = np.array([1, 2])
155::CODE;;>>> loo = LeaveOneOut()
156::CODE;;>>> loo.get_n_splits(X)
157::CODE;;2
158::CODE;;>>> print(loo)
159::CODE;;LeaveOneOut()
160::CODE;;>>> for i, (train_index, test_index) in enumerate(loo.split(X)):
161::CODE;;... print(f"Fold {i}:")
162::CODE;;... print(f" Train: index={train_index}")
163::CODE;;... print(f" Test: index={test_index}")
164::CODE;;Fold 0:
165::CODE;;Train: index=[1]
166::CODE;;Test: index=[0]
167::CODE;;Fold 1:
168::CODE;;Train: index=[0]
169::CODE;;Test: index=[1]
170::CODE;;See Also
171::CODE;;--------
172::CODE;;LeaveOneGroupOut : For splitting the data according to explicit,
173::CODE;;domain-specific stratification of the dataset.
174::CODE;;GroupKFold : K-fold iterator variant with non-overlapping groups.
185::CODE;;Parameters
186::CODE;;----------
187::CODE;;X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
188::CODE;;Training data, where `n_samples` is the number of samples
189::CODE;;and `n_features` is the number of features.
190::CODE;;y : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
191::CODE;;Always ignored, exists for API compatibility.
192::CODE;;groups : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
193::CODE;;Always ignored, exists for API compatibility.
194::CODE;;Returns
195::CODE;;-------
196::CODE;;n_splits : int
197::CODE;;Returns the number of splitting iterations in the cross-validator.
204::CODE;;Provides train/test indices to split data in train/test sets. This results
205::CODE;;in testing on all distinct samples of size p, while the remaining n - p
206::CODE;;samples form the training set in each iteration.
207::CODE;;Note: ``LeavePOut(p)`` is NOT equivalent to
208::CODE;;``KFold(n_splits=n_samples // p)`` which creates non-overlapping test sets.
209::CODE;;Due to the high number of iterations which grows combinatorically with the
210::CODE;;number of samples this cross-validation method can be very costly. For
211::CODE;;large datasets one should favor :class:`KFold`, :class:`StratifiedKFold`
212::CODE;;or :class:`ShuffleSplit`.
213::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <leave_p_out>`.
214::CODE;;Parameters
215::CODE;;----------
216::CODE;;p : int
217::CODE;;Size of the test sets. Must be strictly less than the number of
218::CODE;;samples.
219::CODE;;Examples
220::CODE;;--------
221::CODE;;>>> import numpy as np
222::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.model_selection import LeavePOut
223::CODE;;>>> X = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6], [7, 8]])
224::CODE;;>>> y = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4])
225::CODE;;>>> lpo = LeavePOut(2)
226::CODE;;>>> lpo.get_n_splits(X)
227::CODE;;6
228::CODE;;>>> print(lpo)

231::CODE;;... print(f"Fold {i}:")
232::CODE;;... print(f" Train: index={train_index}")
233::CODE;;... print(f" Test: index={test_index}")
234::CODE;;Fold 0:
235::CODE;;Train: index=[2 3]
236::CODE;;Test: index=[0 1]
237::CODE;;Fold 1:
238::CODE;;Train: index=[1 3]
239::CODE;;Test: index=[0 2]
240::CODE;;Fold 2:
241::CODE;;Train: index=[1 2]
242::CODE;;Test: index=[0 3]

251::CODE;;Test: index=[2 3]

1720::CODE;;Provides randomized train/test indices to split data according to a
1721::CODE;;third-party provided group. This group information can be used to encode
1722::CODE;;arbitrary domain specific stratifications of the samples as integers.
1723::CODE;;For instance the groups could be the year of collection of the samples
1724::CODE;;and thus allow for cross-validation against time-based splits.
1725::CODE;;The difference between :class:`LeavePGroupsOut` and ``GroupShuffleSplit`` is that
1726::CODE;;the former generates splits using all subsets of size ``p`` unique groups,
1727::CODE;;whereas ``GroupShuffleSplit`` generates a user-determined number of random
1728::CODE;;test splits, each with a user-determined fraction of unique groups.
1729::CODE;;For example, a less computationally intensive alternative to
1730::CODE;;``LeavePGroupsOut(p=10)`` would be
1731::CODE;;``GroupShuffleSplit(test_size=10, n_splits=100)``.
1732::CODE;;Contrary to other cross-validation strategies, the random splits
1733::CODE;;do not guarantee that test sets across all folds will be mutually exclusive,
1734::CODE;;and might include overlapping samples. However, this is still very likely for
1735::CODE;;sizeable datasets.
1736::CODE;;Note: The parameters ``test_size`` and ``train_size`` refer to groups, and
1737::CODE;;not to samples as in :class:`ShuffleSplit`.
1738::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <group_shuffle_split>`.
1739::CODE;;For visualisation of cross-validation behaviour and
1740::CODE;;comparison between common scikit-learn split methods
1741::CODE;;refer to :ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_model_selection_plot_cv_indices.py`
1742::CODE;;Parameters
1743::CODE;;----------
1744::CODE;;n_splits : int, default=5
1745::CODE;;Number of re-shuffling & splitting iterations.
1746::CODE;;test_size : float, int, default=None
1747::CODE;;If float, should be between 0.0 and 1.0 and represent the proportion
1748::CODE;;of groups to include in the test split (rounded up). If int,
1749::CODE;;represents the absolute number of test groups. If None, the value is
1750::CODE;;set to the complement of the train size. If ``train_size`` is also None,
1751::CODE;;it will be set to 0.2.
1752::CODE;;train_size : float or int, default=None
1753::CODE;;If float, should be between 0.0 and 1.0 and represent the
1754::CODE;;proportion of the groups to include in the train split. If
1755::CODE;;int, represents the absolute number of train groups. If None,
1756::CODE;;the value is automatically set to the complement of the test size.
1757::CODE;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
1758::CODE;;Controls the randomness of the training and testing indices produced.
1759::CODE;;Pass an int for reproducible output across multiple function calls.
1760::CODE;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
1761::CODE;;Examples
1762::CODE;;--------
1763::CODE;;>>> import numpy as np
1764::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.model_selection import GroupShuffleSplit
1765::CODE;;>>> X = np.ones(shape=(8, 2))
1766::CODE;;>>> y = np.ones(shape=(8, 1))
1767::CODE;;>>> groups = np.array([1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3])
1768::CODE;;>>> print(groups.shape)
1769::CODE;;(8,)
1770::CODE;;>>> gss = GroupShuffleSplit(n_splits=2, train_size=.7, random_state=42)
1771::CODE;;>>> gss.get_n_splits()
1772::CODE;;2
1773::CODE;;>>> print(gss)
1774::CODE;;GroupShuffleSplit(n_splits=2, random_state=42, test_size=None, train_size=0.7)

1776::CODE;;... print(f"Fold {i}:")

1838::CODE;;Provides train/test indices to split data in train/test sets.
1839::CODE;;This cross-validation object is a merge of :class:`StratifiedKFold` and
1840::CODE;;:class:`ShuffleSplit`, which returns stratified randomized folds. The folds
1841::CODE;;are made by preserving the percentage of samples for each class in `y` in a
1842::CODE;;binary or multiclass classification setting.
1843::CODE;;Note: like the :class:`ShuffleSplit` strategy, stratified random splits
1844::CODE;;do not guarantee that test sets across all folds will be mutually exclusive,

2314::CODE;;the value is automatically set to the complement of the test size.
2315::CODE;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
2316::CODE;;Controls the shuffling applied to the data before applying the split.
2317::CODE;;Pass an int for reproducible output across multiple function calls.
2318::CODE;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
2319::CODE;;shuffle : bool, default=True
2320::CODE;;Whether or not to shuffle the data before splitting. If shuffle=False
2321::CODE;;then stratify must be None.
2322::CODE;;stratify : array-like, default=None
2323::CODE;;If not None, data is split in a stratified fashion, using this as
2324::CODE;;the class labels.
2325::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <stratification>`.
2326::CODE;;Returns
2327::CODE;;-------
2328::CODE;;splitting : list, length=2 * len(arrays)
2329::CODE;;List containing train-test split of inputs.
2330::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.16
2331::CODE;;If the input is sparse, the output will be a
2332::CODE;;``scipy.sparse.csr_matrix``. Else, output type is the same as the
2333::CODE;;input type.

58::CODE;;def _check_groups_routing_disabled(groups):
59::CODE;;if groups is not None and _routing_enabled():
60::CODE;;raise ValueError(
61::CODE;;"`groups` can only be passed if metadata routing is not enabled via"
62::CODE;;" `sklearn.set_config(enable_metadata_routing=True)`. When routing is"
63::CODE;;" enabled, pass `groups` alongside other metadata via the `params` argument"
64::CODE;;" instead."
65::CODE;;)
66::CODE;;@validate_params(
67::CODE;;{
68::CODE;;"estimator": [HasMethods("fit")],

92::CODE;;def cross_validate(
93::CODE;;estimator,
94::CODE;;X,
95::CODE;;y=None,
96::CODE;;*,
97::CODE;;groups=None,
98::CODE;;scoring=None,
99::CODE;;cv=None,
100::CODE;;n_jobs=None,
101::CODE;;verbose=0,
102::CODE;;params=None,
103::CODE;;pre_dispatch="2*n_jobs",
104::CODE;;return_train_score=False,
105::CODE;;return_estimator=False,
106::CODE;;return_indices=False,
107::CODE;;error_score=np.nan,
108::CODE;;):
264::CODE;;_check_groups_routing_disabled(groups)
265::CODE;;X, y = indexable(X, y)
266::CODE;;params = {} if params is None else params
267::CODE;;cv = check_cv(cv, y, classifier=is_classifier(estimator))
268::CODE;;scorers = check_scoring(
269::CODE;;estimator, scoring=scoring, raise_exc=(error_score == "raise")
270::CODE;;)
271::CODE;;if _routing_enabled():
275::CODE;;router = (
276::CODE;;MetadataRouter(owner="cross_validate")
277::CODE;;.add(
278::CODE;;splitter=cv,
279::CODE;;method_mapping=MethodMapping().add(caller="fit", callee="split"),
280::CODE;;)
281::CODE;;.add(
282::CODE;;estimator=estimator,
285::CODE;;method_mapping=MethodMapping().add(caller="fit", callee="fit"),
286::CODE;;)
287::CODE;;.add(
288::CODE;;scorer=scorers,
289::CODE;;method_mapping=MethodMapping().add(caller="fit", callee="score"),
290::CODE;;)
291::CODE;;)
292::CODE;;try:
293::CODE;;routed_params = process_routing(router, "fit", **params)
294::CODE;;except UnsetMetadataPassedError as e:
299::CODE;;raise UnsetMetadataPassedError(
300::CODE;;message=str(e).replace("cross_validate.fit", "cross_validate"),
301::CODE;;unrequested_params=e.unrequested_params,
302::CODE;;routed_params=e.routed_params,
303::CODE;;)
304::CODE;;else:
305::CODE;;routed_params = Bunch()
306::CODE;;routed_params.splitter = Bunch(split={"groups": groups})
307::CODE;;routed_params.estimator = Bunch(fit=params)
308::CODE;;routed_params.scorer = Bunch(score={})
309::CODE;;indices = cv.split(X, y, **routed_params.splitter.split)
310::CODE;;if return_indices:
312::CODE;;indices = list(indices)
315::CODE;;parallel = Parallel(n_jobs=n_jobs, verbose=verbose, pre_dispatch=pre_dispatch)
316::CODE;;results = parallel(
317::CODE;;delayed(_fit_and_score)(
318::CODE;;clone(estimator),
319::CODE;;X,
320::CODE;;y,
321::CODE;;scorer=scorers,
322::CODE;;train=train,
323::CODE;;test=test,
324::CODE;;verbose=verbose,
325::CODE;;parameters=None,
326::CODE;;fit_params=routed_params.estimator.fit,
327::CODE;;score_params=routed_params.scorer.score,
328::CODE;;return_train_score=return_train_score,
329::CODE;;return_times=True,
330::CODE;;return_estimator=return_estimator,
331::CODE;;error_score=error_score,
332::CODE;;)
333::CODE;;for train, test in indices
334::CODE;;)
335::CODE;;_warn_or_raise_about_fit_failures(results, error_score)
339::CODE;;if callable(scoring):
340::CODE;;_insert_error_scores(results, error_score)
341::CODE;;results = _aggregate_score_dicts(results)
342::CODE;;ret = {}
343::CODE;;ret["fit_time"] = results["fit_time"]
344::CODE;;ret["score_time"] = results["score_time"]
345::CODE;;if return_estimator:
346::CODE;;ret["estimator"] = results["estimator"]
347::CODE;;if return_indices:
348::CODE;;ret["indices"] = {}
349::CODE;;ret["indices"]["train"], ret["indices"]["test"] = zip(*indices)
350::CODE;;test_scores_dict = _normalize_score_results(results["test_scores"])
351::CODE;;if return_train_score:
352::CODE;;train_scores_dict = _normalize_score_results(results["train_scores"])
353::CODE;;for name in test_scores_dict:
354::CODE;;ret["test_%s" % name] = test_scores_dict[name]
355::CODE;;if return_train_score:
356::CODE;;key = "train_%s" % name
357::CODE;;ret[key] = train_scores_dict[name]
358::CODE;;return ret
359::CODE;;def _insert_error_scores(results, error_score):
364::CODE;;successful_score = None
365::CODE;;failed_indices = []
366::CODE;;for i, result in enumerate(results):
367::CODE;;if result["fit_error"] is not None:
368::CODE;;failed_indices.append(i)
369::CODE;;elif successful_score is None:
370::CODE;;successful_score = result["test_scores"]
371::CODE;;if isinstance(successful_score, dict):
372::CODE;;formatted_error = {name: error_score for name in successful_score}
373::CODE;;for i in failed_indices:
374::CODE;;results[i]["test_scores"] = formatted_error.copy()
375::CODE;;if "train_scores" in results[i]:
376::CODE;;results[i]["train_scores"] = formatted_error.copy()
377::CODE;;def _normalize_score_results(scores, scaler_score_key="score"):
446::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <cross_validation>`.
447::CODE;;Parameters
448::CODE;;----------
449::CODE;;estimator : estimator object implementing 'fit'
450::CODE;;The object to use to fit the data.
451::CODE;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
452::CODE;;The data to fit. Can be for example a list, or an array.
453::CODE;;y : array-like of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_outputs), \
454::CODE;;default=None
455::CODE;;The target variable to try to predict in the case of
456::CODE;;supervised learning.
457::CODE;;groups : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
458::CODE;;Group labels for the samples used while splitting the dataset into
459::CODE;;train/test set. Only used in conjunction with a "Group" :term:`cv`
460::CODE;;instance (e.g., :class:`GroupKFold`).
461::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.4
462::CODE;;``groups`` can only be passed if metadata routing is not enabled
463::CODE;;via ``sklearn.set_config(enable_metadata_routing=True)``. When routing
464::CODE;;is enabled, pass ``groups`` alongside other metadata via the ``params``
465::CODE;;argument instead. E.g.:
466::CODE;;``cross_val_score(..., params={'groups': groups})``.
467::CODE;;scoring : str or callable, default=None
468::CODE;;Strategy to evaluate the performance of the `estimator` across cross-validation
469::CODE;;splits.
470::CODE;;- str: see :ref:`scoring_string_names` for options.
471::CODE;;- callable: a scorer callable object (e.g., function) with signature
472::CODE;;``scorer(estimator, X, y)``, which should return only a single value.
473::CODE;;See :ref:`scoring_callable` for details.
474::CODE;;- `None`: the `estimator`'s
475::CODE;;:ref:`default evaluation criterion <scoring_api_overview>` is used.
476::CODE;;Similar to the use of `scoring` in :func:`cross_validate` but only a
477::CODE;;single metric is permitted.
478::CODE;;cv : int, cross-validation generator or an iterable, default=None
479::CODE;;Determines the cross-validation splitting strategy.
480::CODE;;Possible inputs for cv are:
481::CODE;;- `None`, to use the default 5-fold cross validation,
482::CODE;;- int, to specify the number of folds in a `(Stratified)KFold`,
483::CODE;;- :term:`CV splitter`,
484::CODE;;- An iterable that generates (train, test) splits as arrays of indices.
485::CODE;;For `int`/`None` inputs, if the estimator is a classifier and `y` is
486::CODE;;either binary or multiclass, :class:`StratifiedKFold` is used. In all
487::CODE;;other cases, :class:`KFold` is used. These splitters are instantiated
488::CODE;;with `shuffle=False` so the splits will be the same across calls.
489::CODE;;Refer :ref:`User Guide <cross_validation>` for the various
490::CODE;;cross-validation strategies that can be used here.
491::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 0.22
492::CODE;;`cv` default value if `None` changed from 3-fold to 5-fold.
493::CODE;;n_jobs : int, default=None
494::CODE;;Number of jobs to run in parallel. Training the estimator and computing
495::CODE;;the score are parallelized over the cross-validation splits.
496::CODE;;``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
497::CODE;;``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
498::CODE;;for more details.
499::CODE;;verbose : int, default=0
500::CODE;;The verbosity level.
501::CODE;;params : dict, default=None
502::CODE;;Parameters to pass to the underlying estimator's ``fit``, the scorer,
503::CODE;;and the CV splitter.
504::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.4
505::CODE;;pre_dispatch : int or str, default='2*n_jobs'
506::CODE;;Controls the number of jobs that get dispatched during parallel
507::CODE;;execution. Reducing this number can be useful to avoid an
508::CODE;;explosion of memory consumption when more jobs get dispatched
509::CODE;;than CPUs can process. This parameter can be:
510::CODE;;- ``None``, in which case all the jobs are immediately created and spawned. Use
511::CODE;;this for lightweight and fast-running jobs, to avoid delays due to on-demand
512::CODE;;spawning of the jobs
513::CODE;;- An int, giving the exact number of total jobs that are spawned
514::CODE;;- A str, giving an expression as a function of n_jobs, as in '2*n_jobs'
515::CODE;;error_score : 'raise' or numeric, default=np.nan
516::CODE;;Value to assign to the score if an error occurs in estimator fitting.
517::CODE;;If set to 'raise', the error is raised.
518::CODE;;If a numeric value is given, FitFailedWarning is raised.
519::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.20
520::CODE;;Returns
521::CODE;;-------
522::CODE;;scores : ndarray of float of shape=(len(list(cv)),)
523::CODE;;Array of scores of the estimator for each run of the cross validation.
524::CODE;;See Also
525::CODE;;--------
526::CODE;;cross_validate : To run cross-validation on multiple metrics and also to
527::CODE;;return train scores, fit times and score times.
528::CODE;;cross_val_predict : Get predictions from each split of cross-validation for
529::CODE;;diagnostic purposes.
530::CODE;;sklearn.metrics.make_scorer : Make a scorer from a performance metric or
531::CODE;;loss function.
532::CODE;;Examples
533::CODE;;--------
534::CODE;;>>> from sklearn import datasets, linear_model
535::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score
536::CODE;;>>> diabetes = datasets.load_diabetes()
537::CODE;;>>> X = diabetes.data[:150]
538::CODE;;>>> y = diabetes.target[:150]
539::CODE;;>>> lasso = linear_model.Lasso()
540::CODE;;>>> print(cross_val_score(lasso, X, y, cv=3))
541::CODE;;[0.3315057 0.08022103 0.03531816]
581::CODE;;Parameters
582::CODE;;----------
583::CODE;;estimator : estimator object implementing 'fit'
584::CODE;;The object to use to fit the data.
585::CODE;;X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
586::CODE;;The data to fit.
587::CODE;;y : array-like of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_outputs) or None
588::CODE;;The target variable to try to predict in the case of
589::CODE;;supervised learning.
590::CODE;;scorer : A single callable or dict mapping scorer name to the callable
591::CODE;;If it is a single callable, the return value for ``train_scores`` and
592::CODE;;``test_scores`` is a single float.
593::CODE;;For a dict, it should be one mapping the scorer name to the scorer
594::CODE;;callable object / function.
595::CODE;;The callable object / fn should have signature
596::CODE;;``scorer(estimator, X, y)``.
597::CODE;;train : array-like of shape (n_train_samples,)
598::CODE;;Indices of training samples.
599::CODE;;test : array-like of shape (n_test_samples,)
600::CODE;;Indices of test samples.
601::CODE;;verbose : int
602::CODE;;The verbosity level.
603::CODE;;error_score : 'raise' or numeric, default=np.nan
604::CODE;;Value to assign to the score if an error occurs in estimator fitting.
605::CODE;;If set to 'raise', the error is raised.
606::CODE;;If a numeric value is given, FitFailedWarning is raised.
607::CODE;;parameters : dict or None
608::CODE;;Parameters to be set on the estimator.
609::CODE;;fit_params : dict or None
610::CODE;;Parameters that will be passed to ``estimator.fit``.
611::CODE;;score_params : dict or None
612::CODE;;Parameters that will be passed to the scorer.
613::CODE;;return_train_score : bool, default=False
614::CODE;;Compute and return score on training set.
615::CODE;;return_parameters : bool, default=False
616::CODE;;Return parameters that has been used for the estimator.
617::CODE;;split_progress : {list, tuple} of int, default=None
618::CODE;;A list or tuple of format (<current_split_id>, <total_num_of_splits>).
619::CODE;;candidate_progress : {list, tuple} of int, default=None
620::CODE;;A list or tuple of format
621::CODE;;(<current_candidate_id>, <total_number_of_candidates>).
622::CODE;;return_n_test_samples : bool, default=False
623::CODE;;Whether to return the ``n_test_samples``.
624::CODE;;return_times : bool, default=False
625::CODE;;Whether to return the fit/score times.
626::CODE;;return_estimator : bool, default=False
627::CODE;;Whether to return the fitted estimator.
628::CODE;;Returns
629::CODE;;-------
630::CODE;;result : dict with the following attributes
631::CODE;;train_scores : dict of scorer name -> float
632::CODE;;Score on training set (for all the scorers),
633::CODE;;returned only if `return_train_score` is `True`.
634::CODE;;test_scores : dict of scorer name -> float
635::CODE;;Score on testing set (for all the scorers).
636::CODE;;n_test_samples : int
637::CODE;;Number of test samples.
638::CODE;;fit_time : float
639::CODE;;Time spent for fitting in seconds.
640::CODE;;score_time : float
641::CODE;;Time spent for scoring in seconds.
642::CODE;;parameters : dict or None
643::CODE;;The parameters that have been evaluated.
644::CODE;;estimator : estimator object
645::CODE;;The fitted estimator.
646::CODE;;fit_error : str or None
647::CODE;;Traceback str if the fit failed, None if the fit succeeded.
761::CODE;;Will return a dict of floats if `scorer` is a _MultiMetricScorer, otherwise a single
762::CODE;;float is returned.
861::CODE;;The data is split according to the cv parameter. Each sample belongs
862::CODE;;to exactly one test set, and its prediction is computed with an
863::CODE;;estimator fitted on the corresponding training set.
864::CODE;;Passing these predictions into an evaluation metric may not be a valid
865::CODE;;way to measure generalization performance. Results can differ from
866::CODE;;:func:`cross_validate` and :func:`cross_val_score` unless all tests sets
867::CODE;;have equal size and the metric decomposes over samples.
868::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <cross_validation>`.
869::CODE;;Parameters
870::CODE;;----------
871::CODE;;estimator : estimator
872::CODE;;The estimator instance to use to fit the data. It must implement a `fit`
873::CODE;;method and the method given by the `method` parameter.
874::CODE;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
875::CODE;;The data to fit. Can be, for example a list, or an array at least 2d.
876::CODE;;y : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_outputs), \
877::CODE;;default=None
878::CODE;;The target variable to try to predict in the case of
879::CODE;;supervised learning.
880::CODE;;groups : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
881::CODE;;Group labels for the samples used while splitting the dataset into
882::CODE;;train/test set. Only used in conjunction with a "Group" :term:`cv`
883::CODE;;instance (e.g., :class:`GroupKFold`).
884::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.4
885::CODE;;``groups`` can only be passed if metadata routing is not enabled
886::CODE;;via ``sklearn.set_config(enable_metadata_routing=True)``. When routing
887::CODE;;is enabled, pass ``groups`` alongside other metadata via the ``params``
888::CODE;;argument instead. E.g.:
889::CODE;;``cross_val_predict(..., params={'groups': groups})``.
890::CODE;;cv : int, cross-validation generator or an iterable, default=None
891::CODE;;Determines the cross-validation splitting strategy.
892::CODE;;Possible inputs for cv are:
893::CODE;;- None, to use the default 5-fold cross validation,
894::CODE;;- int, to specify the number of folds in a `(Stratified)KFold`,
895::CODE;;- :term:`CV splitter`,
896::CODE;;- An iterable that generates (train, test) splits as arrays of indices.
897::CODE;;For int/None inputs, if the estimator is a classifier and ``y`` is
898::CODE;;either binary or multiclass, :class:`StratifiedKFold` is used. In all
899::CODE;;other cases, :class:`KFold` is used. These splitters are instantiated
900::CODE;;with `shuffle=False` so the splits will be the same across calls.
901::CODE;;Refer :ref:`User Guide <cross_validation>` for the various
902::CODE;;cross-validation strategies that can be used here.
903::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 0.22
904::CODE;;``cv`` default value if None changed from 3-fold to 5-fold.
905::CODE;;n_jobs : int, default=None
906::CODE;;Number of jobs to run in parallel. Training the estimator and
907::CODE;;predicting are parallelized over the cross-validation splits.
908::CODE;;``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
909::CODE;;``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
910::CODE;;for more details.
911::CODE;;verbose : int, default=0
912::CODE;;The verbosity level.
913::CODE;;params : dict, default=None
914::CODE;;Parameters to pass to the underlying estimator's ``fit`` and the CV
915::CODE;;splitter.
916::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.4
917::CODE;;pre_dispatch : int or str, default='2*n_jobs'
918::CODE;;Controls the number of jobs that get dispatched during parallel
919::CODE;;execution. Reducing this number can be useful to avoid an
920::CODE;;explosion of memory consumption when more jobs get dispatched
921::CODE;;than CPUs can process. This parameter can be:
922::CODE;;- None, in which case all the jobs are immediately created and spawned. Use
923::CODE;;this for lightweight and fast-running jobs, to avoid delays due to on-demand
924::CODE;;spawning of the jobs
925::CODE;;- An int, giving the exact number of total jobs that are spawned
926::CODE;;- A str, giving an expression as a function of n_jobs, as in '2*n_jobs'
927::CODE;;method : {'predict', 'predict_proba', 'predict_log_proba', \
928::CODE;;'decision_function'}, default='predict'
929::CODE;;The method to be invoked by `estimator`.
930::CODE;;Returns
931::CODE;;-------
932::CODE;;predictions : ndarray
933::CODE;;This is the result of calling `method`. Shape:
934::CODE;;- When `method` is 'predict' and in special case where `method` is
935::CODE;;'decision_function' and the target is binary: (n_samples,)
936::CODE;;- When `method` is one of {'predict_proba', 'predict_log_proba',
937::CODE;;'decision_function'} (unless special case above):
938::CODE;;(n_samples, n_classes)
939::CODE;;- If `estimator` is :term:`multioutput`, an extra dimension
940::CODE;;'n_outputs' is added to the end of each shape above.
941::CODE;;See Also
942::CODE;;--------
943::CODE;;cross_val_score : Calculate score for each CV split.
944::CODE;;cross_validate : Calculate one or more scores and timings for each CV
945::CODE;;split.
946::CODE;;Notes
947::CODE;;-----
948::CODE;;In the case that one or more classes are absent in a training portion, a
949::CODE;;default score needs to be assigned to all instances for that class if
950::CODE;;``method`` produces columns per class, as in {'decision_function',
951::CODE;;'predict_proba', 'predict_log_proba'}. For ``predict_proba`` this value is
952::CODE;;0. In order to ensure finite output, we approximate negative infinity by
953::CODE;;the minimum finite float value for the dtype in other cases.

1244::CODE;;Permutes targets to generate 'randomized data' and compute the empirical
1245::CODE;;p-value against the null hypothesis that features and targets are
1246::CODE;;independent.
1247::CODE;;The p-value represents the fraction of randomized data sets where the
1248::CODE;;estimator performed as well or better than on the original data. A small
1249::CODE;;p-value suggests that there is a real dependency between features and
1250::CODE;;targets which has been used by the estimator to give good predictions.
1251::CODE;;A large p-value may be due to lack of real dependency between features
1252::CODE;;and targets or the estimator was not able to use the dependency to
1253::CODE;;give good predictions.
1254::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <permutation_test_score>`.
1255::CODE;;Parameters
1256::CODE;;----------
1257::CODE;;estimator : estimator object implementing 'fit'
1258::CODE;;The object to use to fit the data.
1259::CODE;;X : array-like of shape at least 2D
1260::CODE;;The data to fit.
1261::CODE;;y : array-like of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_outputs) or None
1262::CODE;;The target variable to try to predict in the case of
1263::CODE;;supervised learning.
1264::CODE;;groups : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
1265::CODE;;Labels to constrain permutation within groups, i.e. ``y`` values
1266::CODE;;are permuted among samples with the same group identifier.
1267::CODE;;When not specified, ``y`` values are permuted among all samples.
1268::CODE;;When a grouped cross-validator is used, the group labels are
1269::CODE;;also passed on to the ``split`` method of the cross-validator. The
1270::CODE;;cross-validator uses them for grouping the samples while splitting
1271::CODE;;the dataset into train/test set.
1272::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.6
1273::CODE;;``groups`` can only be passed if metadata routing is not enabled
1274::CODE;;via ``sklearn.set_config(enable_metadata_routing=True)``. When routing
1275::CODE;;is enabled, pass ``groups`` alongside other metadata via the ``params``
1276::CODE;;argument instead. E.g.:
1277::CODE;;``permutation_test_score(..., params={'groups': groups})``.
1278::CODE;;cv : int, cross-validation generator or an iterable, default=None
1279::CODE;;Determines the cross-validation splitting strategy.
1280::CODE;;Possible inputs for cv are:
1281::CODE;;- `None`, to use the default 5-fold cross validation,
1282::CODE;;- int, to specify the number of folds in a `(Stratified)KFold`,
1283::CODE;;- :term:`CV splitter`,
1284::CODE;;- An iterable yielding (train, test) splits as arrays of indices.
1285::CODE;;For `int`/`None` inputs, if the estimator is a classifier and `y` is
1286::CODE;;either binary or multiclass, :class:`StratifiedKFold` is used. In all
1287::CODE;;other cases, :class:`KFold` is used. These splitters are instantiated
1288::CODE;;with `shuffle=False` so the splits will be the same across calls.
1289::CODE;;Refer :ref:`User Guide <cross_validation>` for the various
1290::CODE;;cross-validation strategies that can be used here.
1291::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 0.22
1292::CODE;;`cv` default value if `None` changed from 3-fold to 5-fold.
1293::CODE;;n_permutations : int, default=100
1294::CODE;;Number of times to permute ``y``.
1295::CODE;;n_jobs : int, default=None
1296::CODE;;Number of jobs to run in parallel. Training the estimator and computing
1297::CODE;;the cross-validated score are parallelized over the permutations.
1298::CODE;;``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
1299::CODE;;``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
1300::CODE;;for more details.
1301::CODE;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=0
1302::CODE;;Pass an int for reproducible output for permutation of
1303::CODE;;``y`` values among samples. See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
1304::CODE;;verbose : int, default=0
1305::CODE;;The verbosity level.
1306::CODE;;scoring : str or callable, default=None
1307::CODE;;Scoring method to use to evaluate the predictions on the validation set.
1308::CODE;;- str: see :ref:`scoring_string_names` for options.
1309::CODE;;- callable: a scorer callable object (e.g., function) with signature
1310::CODE;;``scorer(estimator, X, y)``, which should return only a single value.
1311::CODE;;See :ref:`scoring_callable` for details.
1312::CODE;;- `None`: the `estimator`'s
1313::CODE;;:ref:`default evaluation criterion <scoring_api_overview>` is used.
1314::CODE;;params : dict, default=None
1315::CODE;;Parameters to pass to the `fit` method of the estimator, the scorer
1316::CODE;;and the cv splitter.
1317::CODE;;- If `enable_metadata_routing=False` (default): Parameters directly passed to
1318::CODE;;the `fit` method of the estimator.
1319::CODE;;- If `enable_metadata_routing=True`: Parameters safely routed to the `fit`
1320::CODE;;method of the estimator, `cv` object and `scorer`. See :ref:`Metadata Routing
1321::CODE;;User Guide <metadata_routing>` for more details.
1322::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.6
1323::CODE;;Returns
1324::CODE;;-------
1325::CODE;;score : float
1326::CODE;;The true score without permuting targets.
1327::CODE;;permutation_scores : array of shape (n_permutations,)
1328::CODE;;The scores obtained for each permutations.
1329::CODE;;pvalue : float
1330::CODE;;The p-value, which approximates the probability that the score would
1331::CODE;;be obtained by chance. This is calculated as:
1332::CODE;;`(C + 1) / (n_permutations + 1)`
1333::CODE;;Where C is the number of permutations whose score >= the true score.
1334::CODE;;The best possible p-value is 1/(n_permutations + 1), the worst is 1.0.
1335::CODE;;Notes
1336::CODE;;-----
1337::CODE;;This function implements Test 1 in:
1338::CODE;;Ojala and Garriga. `Permutation Tests for Studying Classifier Performance
1339::CODE;;<http://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume11/ojala10a/ojala10a.pdf>`_. The
1340::CODE;;Journal of Machine Learning Research (2010) vol. 11

1355::CODE;;... f"{permutation_scores.std():.3f}"
1356::CODE;;... )
1357::CODE;;Permutation Scores: 0.505 +/- 0.057
1358::CODE;;>>> print(f"P-value: {pvalue:.3f}")
1359::CODE;;P-value: 0.010
