258::CODE;;output : ndarray of shape (n_infrequent_categories,) or None
259::CODE;;If there are infrequent categories, indices of infrequent
260::CODE;;categories. Otherwise None.
288::CODE;;Defines the private attribute: `_default_to_infrequent_mappings`. For
289::CODE;;feature `i`, `_default_to_infrequent_mappings[i]` defines the mapping
290::CODE;;from the integer encoding returned by `super().transform()` into
291::CODE;;infrequent categories. If `_default_to_infrequent_mappings[i]` is None,
292::CODE;;there were no infrequent categories in the training set.
293::CODE;;For example if categories 0, 2 and 4 were frequent, while categories
294::CODE;;1, 3, 5 were infrequent for feature 7, then these categories are mapped
295::CODE;;to a single output:
296::CODE;;`_default_to_infrequent_mappings[7] = array([0, 3, 1, 3, 2, 3])`
297::CODE;;Defines private attribute: `_infrequent_indices`. `_infrequent_indices[i]`
298::CODE;;is an array of indices such that
299::CODE;;`categories_[i][_infrequent_indices[i]]` are all the infrequent category
300::CODE;;labels. If the feature `i` has no infrequent categories
301::CODE;;`_infrequent_indices[i]` is None.
302::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.1
303::CODE;;Parameters
304::CODE;;----------
305::CODE;;n_samples : int
306::CODE;;Number of samples in training set.
307::CODE;;category_counts: list of ndarray
308::CODE;;`category_counts[i]` is the category counts corresponding to
309::CODE;;`self.categories_[i]`.
310::CODE;;missing_indices : dict
311::CODE;;Dict mapping from feature_idx to category index with a missing value.
354::CODE;;This modifies X_int in-place. Values that were invalid based on `X_mask`
355::CODE;;are mapped to the infrequent category if there was an infrequent
356::CODE;;category for that feature.
357::CODE;;Parameters
358::CODE;;----------
359::CODE;;X_int: ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_features)
360::CODE;;Integer encoded categories.
361::CODE;;X_mask: ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_features)
362::CODE;;Bool mask for valid values in `X_int`.
363::CODE;;ignore_category_indices : dict
364::CODE;;Dictionary mapping from feature_idx to category index to ignore.
365::CODE;;Ignored indexes will not be grouped and the original ordinal encoding
366::CODE;;will remain.
400::CODE;;Encode categorical features as a one-hot numeric array.
401::CODE;;The input to this transformer should be an array-like of integers or
402::CODE;;strings, denoting the values taken on by categorical (discrete) features.
403::CODE;;The features are encoded using a one-hot (aka 'one-of-K' or 'dummy')
404::CODE;;encoding scheme. This creates a binary column for each category and
405::CODE;;returns a sparse matrix or dense array (depending on the ``sparse_output``
406::CODE;;parameter).
407::CODE;;By default, the encoder derives the categories based on the unique values
408::CODE;;in each feature. Alternatively, you can also specify the `categories`
409::CODE;;manually.
410::CODE;;This encoding is needed for feeding categorical data to many scikit-learn
411::CODE;;estimators, notably linear models and SVMs with the standard kernels.
412::CODE;;Note: a one-hot encoding of y labels should use a LabelBinarizer
413::CODE;;instead.
414::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <preprocessing_categorical_features>`.
415::CODE;;For a comparison of different encoders, refer to:
416::CODE;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_preprocessing_plot_target_encoder.py`.
417::CODE;;Parameters
418::CODE;;----------
419::CODE;;categories : 'auto' or a list of array-like, default='auto'
420::CODE;;Categories (unique values) per feature:
421::CODE;;- 'auto' : Determine categories automatically from the training data.
422::CODE;;- list : ``categories[i]`` holds the categories expected in the ith
423::CODE;;column. The passed categories should not mix strings and numeric
424::CODE;;values within a single feature, and should be sorted in case of
425::CODE;;numeric values.
426::CODE;;The used categories can be found in the ``categories_`` attribute.
427::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.20
428::CODE;;drop : {'first', 'if_binary'} or an array-like of shape (n_features,), \
429::CODE;;default=None
430::CODE;;Specifies a methodology to use to drop one of the categories per
431::CODE;;feature. This is useful in situations where perfectly collinear
432::CODE;;features cause problems, such as when feeding the resulting data
433::CODE;;into an unregularized linear regression model.
434::CODE;;However, dropping one category breaks the symmetry of the original
435::CODE;;representation and can therefore induce a bias in downstream models,
436::CODE;;for instance for penalized linear classification or regression models.
437::CODE;;- None : retain all features (the default).
438::CODE;;- 'first' : drop the first category in each feature. If only one
439::CODE;;category is present, the feature will be dropped entirely.
440::CODE;;- 'if_binary' : drop the first category in each feature with two
441::CODE;;categories. Features with 1 or more than 2 categories are
442::CODE;;left intact.
443::CODE;;- array : ``drop[i]`` is the category in feature ``X[:, i]`` that
444::CODE;;should be dropped.
445::CODE;;When `max_categories` or `min_frequency` is configured to group
446::CODE;;infrequent categories, the dropping behavior is handled after the
447::CODE;;grouping.
448::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.21
449::CODE;;The parameter `drop` was added in 0.21.
450::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 0.23
451::CODE;;The option `drop='if_binary'` was added in 0.23.
452::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.1
453::CODE;;Support for dropping infrequent categories.
454::CODE;;sparse_output : bool, default=True
455::CODE;;When ``True``, it returns a :class:`scipy.sparse.csr_matrix`,
456::CODE;;i.e. a sparse matrix in "Compressed Sparse Row" (CSR) format.
457::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.2
458::CODE;;`sparse` was renamed to `sparse_output`
459::CODE;;dtype : number type, default=np.float64
460::CODE;;Desired dtype of output.
461::CODE;;handle_unknown : {'error', 'ignore', 'infrequent_if_exist', 'warn'}, \
462::CODE;;default='error'
463::CODE;;Specifies the way unknown categories are handled during :meth:`transform`.
464::CODE;;- 'error' : Raise an error if an unknown category is present during transform.
465::CODE;;- 'ignore' : When an unknown category is encountered during
466::CODE;;transform, the resulting one-hot encoded columns for this feature
467::CODE;;will be all zeros. In the inverse transform, an unknown category
468::CODE;;will be denoted as None.
469::CODE;;- 'infrequent_if_exist' : When an unknown category is encountered
470::CODE;;during transform, the resulting one-hot encoded columns for this
471::CODE;;feature will map to the infrequent category if it exists. The
472::CODE;;infrequent category will be mapped to the last position in the
473::CODE;;encoding. During inverse transform, an unknown category will be
474::CODE;;mapped to the category denoted `'infrequent'` if it exists. If the
475::CODE;;`'infrequent'` category does not exist, then :meth:`transform` and
476::CODE;;:meth:`inverse_transform` will handle an unknown category as with
477::CODE;;`handle_unknown='ignore'`. Infrequent categories exist based on
478::CODE;;`min_frequency` and `max_categories`. Read more in the
479::CODE;;:ref:`User Guide <encoder_infrequent_categories>`.
480::CODE;;- 'warn' : When an unknown category is encountered during transform
481::CODE;;a warning is issued, and the encoding then proceeds as described for
482::CODE;;`handle_unknown="infrequent_if_exist"`.
483::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.1
484::CODE;;`'infrequent_if_exist'` was added to automatically handle unknown
485::CODE;;categories and infrequent categories.
486::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.6
487::CODE;;The option `"warn"` was added in 1.6.
488::CODE;;min_frequency : int or float, default=None
489::CODE;;Specifies the minimum frequency below which a category will be
490::CODE;;considered infrequent.
491::CODE;;- If `int`, categories with a smaller cardinality will be considered
492::CODE;;infrequent.
493::CODE;;- If `float`, categories with a smaller cardinality than
494::CODE;;`min_frequency * n_samples` will be considered infrequent.
495::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.1
496::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <encoder_infrequent_categories>`.
497::CODE;;max_categories : int, default=None
498::CODE;;Specifies an upper limit to the number of output features for each input
499::CODE;;feature when considering infrequent categories. If there are infrequent
500::CODE;;categories, `max_categories` includes the category representing the
501::CODE;;infrequent categories along with the frequent categories. If `None`,
502::CODE;;there is no limit to the number of output features.
503::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.1
504::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <encoder_infrequent_categories>`.
505::CODE;;feature_name_combiner : "concat" or callable, default="concat"
506::CODE;;Callable with signature `def callable(input_feature, category)` that returns a
507::CODE;;string. This is used to create feature names to be returned by
508::CODE;;:meth:`get_feature_names_out`.
509::CODE;;`"concat"` concatenates encoded feature name and category with
510::CODE;;`feature + "_" + str(category)`.E.g. feature X with values 1, 6, 7 create
511::CODE;;feature names `X_1, X_6, X_7`.
512::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.3
513::CODE;;Attributes
514::CODE;;----------
515::CODE;;categories_ : list of arrays
516::CODE;;The categories of each feature determined during fitting
517::CODE;;(in order of the features in X and corresponding with the output
518::CODE;;of ``transform``). This includes the category specified in ``drop``
519::CODE;;(if any).
520::CODE;;drop_idx_ : array of shape (n_features,)
521::CODE;;- ``drop_idx_[i]`` is the index in ``categories_[i]`` of the category
522::CODE;;to be dropped for each feature.
523::CODE;;- ``drop_idx_[i] = None`` if no category is to be dropped from the
524::CODE;;feature with index ``i``, e.g. when `drop='if_binary'` and the
525::CODE;;feature isn't binary.
526::CODE;;- ``drop_idx_ = None`` if all the transformed features will be
527::CODE;;retained.
528::CODE;;If infrequent categories are enabled by setting `min_frequency` or
529::CODE;;`max_categories` to a non-default value and `drop_idx[i]` corresponds
530::CODE;;to an infrequent category, then the entire infrequent category is
531::CODE;;dropped.
532::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 0.23
533::CODE;;Added the possibility to contain `None` values.
534::CODE;;infrequent_categories_ : list of ndarray
535::CODE;;Defined only if infrequent categories are enabled by setting
536::CODE;;`min_frequency` or `max_categories` to a non-default value.
537::CODE;;`infrequent_categories_[i]` are the infrequent categories for feature
538::CODE;;`i`. If the feature `i` has no infrequent categories
539::CODE;;`infrequent_categories_[i]` is None.
540::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.1
541::CODE;;n_features_in_ : int
542::CODE;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
543::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
544::CODE;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
545::CODE;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
546::CODE;;has feature names that are all strings.
547::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
548::CODE;;feature_name_combiner : callable or None
549::CODE;;Callable with signature `def callable(input_feature, category)` that returns a
550::CODE;;string. This is used to create feature names to be returned by
551::CODE;;:meth:`get_feature_names_out`.
552::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.3
553::CODE;;See Also
554::CODE;;--------
555::CODE;;OrdinalEncoder : Performs an ordinal (integer)
556::CODE;;encoding of the categorical features.
557::CODE;;TargetEncoder : Encodes categorical features using the target.
558::CODE;;sklearn.feature_extraction.DictVectorizer : Performs a one-hot encoding of
559::CODE;;dictionary items (also handles string-valued features).
560::CODE;;sklearn.feature_extraction.FeatureHasher : Performs an approximate one-hot
561::CODE;;encoding of dictionary items or strings.
562::CODE;;LabelBinarizer : Binarizes labels in a one-vs-all
563::CODE;;fashion.
564::CODE;;MultiLabelBinarizer : Transforms between iterable of
565::CODE;;iterables and a multilabel format, e.g. a (samples x classes) binary
566::CODE;;matrix indicating the presence of a class label.
567::CODE;;Examples
568::CODE;;--------
569::CODE;;Given a dataset with two features, we let the encoder find the unique
570::CODE;;values per feature and transform the data to a binary one-hot encoding.
571::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder
572::CODE;;One can discard categories not seen during `fit`:
573::CODE;;>>> enc = OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore')
574::CODE;;>>> X = [['Male', 1], ['Female', 3], ['Female', 2]]
575::CODE;;>>> enc.fit(X)
576::CODE;;OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore')
577::CODE;;>>> enc.categories_
578::CODE;;[array(['Female', 'Male'], dtype=object), array([1, 2, 3], dtype=object)]
579::CODE;;>>> enc.transform([['Female', 1], ['Male', 4]]).toarray()
580::CODE;;array([[1., 0., 1., 0., 0.],
581::CODE;;[0., 1., 0., 0., 0.]])
582::CODE;;>>> enc.inverse_transform([[0, 1, 1, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0, 1, 0]])
583::CODE;;array([['Male', 1],
584::CODE;;[None, 2]], dtype=object)
585::CODE;;>>> enc.get_feature_names_out(['gender', 'group'])
586::CODE;;array(['gender_Female', 'gender_Male', 'group_1', 'group_2', 'group_3'], ...)
587::CODE;;One can always drop the first column for each feature:
588::CODE;;>>> drop_enc = OneHotEncoder(drop='first').fit(X)
589::CODE;;>>> drop_enc.categories_
590::CODE;;[array(['Female', 'Male'], dtype=object), array([1, 2, 3], dtype=object)]
591::CODE;;>>> drop_enc.transform([['Female', 1], ['Male', 2]]).toarray()
592::CODE;;array([[0., 0., 0.],
593::CODE;;[1., 1., 0.]])
594::CODE;;Or drop a column for feature only having 2 categories:
595::CODE;;>>> drop_binary_enc = OneHotEncoder(drop='if_binary').fit(X)
596::CODE;;>>> drop_binary_enc.transform([['Female', 1], ['Male', 2]]).toarray()
597::CODE;;array([[0., 1., 0., 0.],
598::CODE;;[1., 0., 1., 0.]])
599::CODE;;One can change the way feature names are created.
600::CODE;;>>> def custom_combiner(feature, category):
601::CODE;;... return str(feature) + "_" + type(category).__name__ + "_" + str(category)
602::CODE;;>>> custom_fnames_enc = OneHotEncoder(feature_name_combiner=custom_combiner).fit(X)
603::CODE;;>>> custom_fnames_enc.get_feature_names_out()
604::CODE;;array(['x0_str_Female', 'x0_str_Male', 'x1_int_1', 'x1_int_2', 'x1_int_3'],
605::CODE;;dtype=object)
606::CODE;;Infrequent categories are enabled by setting `max_categories` or `min_frequency`.
607::CODE;;>>> import numpy as np
608::CODE;;>>> X = np.array([["a"] * 5 + ["b"] * 20 + ["c"] * 10 + ["d"] * 3], dtype=object).T
609::CODE;;>>> ohe = OneHotEncoder(max_categories=3, sparse_output=False).fit(X)
610::CODE;;>>> ohe.infrequent_categories_
611::CODE;;[array(['a', 'd'], dtype=object)]
612::CODE;;>>> ohe.transform([["a"], ["b"]])
613::CODE;;array([[0., 0., 1.],
614::CODE;;[1., 0., 0.]])
654::CODE;;If there are no infrequent categories, then `drop_idx` is
655::CODE;;returned. This method is called in `_set_drop_idx` when the `drop`
656::CODE;;parameter is an array-like.
674::CODE;;If `self.drop` is:
675::CODE;;- `None`, No categories have been dropped.
676::CODE;;- `'first'`, All zeros to drop the first category.
677::CODE;;- `'if_binary'`, All zeros if the category is binary and `None`
678::CODE;;otherwise.
679::CODE;;- array-like, The indices of the categories that match the
680::CODE;;categories in `self.drop`. If the dropped category is an infrequent
681::CODE;;category, then the index for the infrequent category is used. This
682::CODE;;means that the entire infrequent category is dropped.
683::CODE;;This methods defines a public `drop_idx_` and a private
684::CODE;;`_drop_idx_after_grouping`.
685::CODE;;- `drop_idx_`: Public facing API that references the drop category in
686::CODE;;`self.categories_`.
687::CODE;;- `_drop_idx_after_grouping`: Used internally to drop categories *after* the
688::CODE;;infrequent categories are grouped together.
689::CODE;;If there are no infrequent categories or drop is `None`, then
690::CODE;;`drop_idx_=_drop_idx_after_grouping`.
776::CODE;;1. If there are infrequent categories, the category is named
777::CODE;;'infrequent_sklearn'.
778::CODE;;2. Dropped columns are removed when remove_dropped=True.
795::CODE;;if (
796::CODE;;self._drop_idx_after_grouping is not None
797::CODE;;and self._drop_idx_after_grouping[i] is not None
798::CODE;;):
799::CODE;;return np.delete(categories, self._drop_idx_after_grouping[i])
800::CODE;;return categories

845::CODE;;:class:`scipy.sparse._csr.csr_matrix` (CSR format).

856::CODE;;(n_samples, n_encoded_features)
857::CODE;;Transformed input. If `sparse_output=True`, a sparse matrix will be
858::CODE;;returned.
918::CODE;;Convert the data back to the original representation.
919::CODE;;When unknown categories are encountered (all zeros in the
920::CODE;;one-hot encoding), ``None`` is used to represent this category. If the
921::CODE;;feature with the unknown category has a dropped category, the dropped
922::CODE;;category will be its inverse.
923::CODE;;For a given input feature, if there is an infrequent category,
924::CODE;;'infrequent_sklearn' will be used to represent the infrequent category.
925::CODE;;Parameters
926::CODE;;----------

928::CODE;;(n_samples, n_encoded_features)
929::CODE;;The transformed data.
930::CODE;;Returns
931::CODE;;-------
932::CODE;;X_original : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_features)
933::CODE;;Inverse transformed array.
1018::CODE;;Parameters
1019::CODE;;----------
1020::CODE;;input_features : array-like of str or None, default=None
1021::CODE;;Input features.
1022::CODE;;- If `input_features` is `None`, then `feature_names_in_` is
1023::CODE;;used as feature names in. If `feature_names_in_` is not defined,

1025::CODE;;`["x0", "x1", ..., "x(n_features_in_ - 1)"]`.
1026::CODE;;- If `input_features` is an array-like, then `input_features` must

1029::CODE;;-------
1030::CODE;;feature_names_out : ndarray of str objects
1031::CODE;;Transformed feature names.
1058::CODE;;Encode categorical features as an integer array.
1059::CODE;;The input to this transformer should be an array-like of integers or
1060::CODE;;strings, denoting the values taken on by categorical (discrete) features.
1061::CODE;;The features are converted to ordinal integers. This results in
1062::CODE;;a single column of integers (0 to n_categories - 1) per feature.
1063::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <preprocessing_categorical_features>`.
1064::CODE;;For a comparison of different encoders, refer to:
1065::CODE;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_preprocessing_plot_target_encoder.py`.
1066::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.20
1067::CODE;;Parameters
1068::CODE;;----------
1069::CODE;;categories : 'auto' or a list of array-like, default='auto'
1070::CODE;;Categories (unique values) per feature:
1071::CODE;;- 'auto' : Determine categories automatically from the training data.
1072::CODE;;- list : ``categories[i]`` holds the categories expected in the ith
1073::CODE;;column. The passed categories should not mix strings and numeric
1074::CODE;;values, and should be sorted in case of numeric values.
1075::CODE;;The used categories can be found in the ``categories_`` attribute.
1076::CODE;;dtype : number type, default=np.float64
1077::CODE;;Desired dtype of output.
1078::CODE;;handle_unknown : {'error', 'use_encoded_value'}, default='error'
1079::CODE;;When set to 'error' an error will be raised in case an unknown
1080::CODE;;categorical feature is present during transform. When set to
1081::CODE;;'use_encoded_value', the encoded value of unknown categories will be
1082::CODE;;set to the value given for the parameter `unknown_value`. In
1083::CODE;;:meth:`inverse_transform`, an unknown category will be denoted as None.
1084::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
1085::CODE;;unknown_value : int or np.nan, default=None
1086::CODE;;When the parameter handle_unknown is set to 'use_encoded_value', this
1087::CODE;;parameter is required and will set the encoded value of unknown
1088::CODE;;categories. It has to be distinct from the values used to encode any of
1089::CODE;;the categories in `fit`. If set to np.nan, the `dtype` parameter must
1090::CODE;;be a float dtype.
1091::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
1092::CODE;;encoded_missing_value : int or np.nan, default=np.nan
1093::CODE;;Encoded value of missing categories. If set to `np.nan`, then the `dtype`
1094::CODE;;parameter must be a float dtype.
1095::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.1
1096::CODE;;min_frequency : int or float, default=None
1097::CODE;;Specifies the minimum frequency below which a category will be
1098::CODE;;considered infrequent.
1099::CODE;;- If `int`, categories with a smaller cardinality will be considered
1100::CODE;;infrequent.
1101::CODE;;- If `float`, categories with a smaller cardinality than
1102::CODE;;`min_frequency * n_samples` will be considered infrequent.
1103::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.3
1104::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <encoder_infrequent_categories>`.
1105::CODE;;max_categories : int, default=None
1106::CODE;;Specifies an upper limit to the number of output categories for each input
1107::CODE;;feature when considering infrequent categories. If there are infrequent
1108::CODE;;categories, `max_categories` includes the category representing the
1109::CODE;;infrequent categories along with the frequent categories. If `None`,
1110::CODE;;there is no limit to the number of output features.
1111::CODE;;`max_categories` do **not** take into account missing or unknown
1112::CODE;;categories. Setting `unknown_value` or `encoded_missing_value` to an
1113::CODE;;integer will increase the number of unique integer codes by one each.
1114::CODE;;This can result in up to `max_categories + 2` integer codes.
1115::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.3
1116::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <encoder_infrequent_categories>`.
1117::CODE;;Attributes
1118::CODE;;----------
1119::CODE;;categories_ : list of arrays
1120::CODE;;The categories of each feature determined during ``fit`` (in order of
1121::CODE;;the features in X and corresponding with the output of ``transform``).
1122::CODE;;This does not include categories that weren't seen during ``fit``.
1123::CODE;;n_features_in_ : int
1124::CODE;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
1125::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
1126::CODE;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
1127::CODE;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
1128::CODE;;has feature names that are all strings.
1129::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
1130::CODE;;infrequent_categories_ : list of ndarray

1132::CODE;;`min_frequency` or `max_categories` to a non-default value.
1133::CODE;;`infrequent_categories_[i]` are the infrequent categories for feature
1134::CODE;;`i`. If the feature `i` has no infrequent categories
1135::CODE;;`infrequent_categories_[i]` is None.
1136::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.3
1137::CODE;;See Also
1138::CODE;;--------
1139::CODE;;OneHotEncoder : Performs a one-hot encoding of categorical features. This encoding
1140::CODE;;is suitable for low to medium cardinality categorical variables, both in
1141::CODE;;supervised and unsupervised settings.
1142::CODE;;TargetEncoder : Encodes categorical features using supervised signal
1143::CODE;;in a classification or regression pipeline. This encoding is typically
1144::CODE;;suitable for high cardinality categorical variables.
1145::CODE;;LabelEncoder : Encodes target labels with values between 0 and
1146::CODE;;``n_classes-1``.
1147::CODE;;Examples
1148::CODE;;--------
1149::CODE;;Given a dataset with two features, we let the encoder find the unique
1150::CODE;;values per feature and transform the data to an ordinal encoding.
1151::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.preprocessing import OrdinalEncoder
1152::CODE;;>>> enc = OrdinalEncoder()
1153::CODE;;>>> X = [['Male', 1], ['Female', 3], ['Female', 2]]
1154::CODE;;>>> enc.fit(X)
1155::CODE;;OrdinalEncoder()
1156::CODE;;>>> enc.categories_
1157::CODE;;[array(['Female', 'Male'], dtype=object), array([1, 2, 3], dtype=object)]
1158::CODE;;>>> enc.transform([['Female', 3], ['Male', 1]])
1159::CODE;;array([[0., 2.],
1160::CODE;;[1., 0.]])
1161::CODE;;>>> enc.inverse_transform([[1, 0], [0, 1]])
1162::CODE;;array([['Male', 1],
1163::CODE;;['Female', 2]], dtype=object)
1164::CODE;;By default, :class:`OrdinalEncoder` is lenient towards missing values by
1165::CODE;;propagating them.
1166::CODE;;>>> import numpy as np
1167::CODE;;>>> X = [['Male', 1], ['Female', 3], ['Female', np.nan]]
1168::CODE;;>>> enc.fit_transform(X)
1169::CODE;;array([[ 1., 0.],

20::CODE;;def _identity(X):
25::CODE;;A FunctionTransformer forwards its X (and optionally y) arguments to a
26::CODE;;user-defined function or function object and returns the result of this
27::CODE;;function. This is useful for stateless transformations such as taking the
28::CODE;;log of frequencies, doing custom scaling, etc.
29::CODE;;Note: If a lambda is used as the function, then the resulting
30::CODE;;transformer will not be pickleable.
31::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.17
32::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <function_transformer>`.
33::CODE;;Parameters
34::CODE;;----------
35::CODE;;func : callable, default=None
36::CODE;;The callable to use for the transformation. This will be passed
37::CODE;;the same arguments as transform, with args and kwargs forwarded.
38::CODE;;If func is None, then func will be the identity function.
39::CODE;;inverse_func : callable, default=None
40::CODE;;The callable to use for the inverse transformation. This will be
41::CODE;;passed the same arguments as inverse transform, with args and
42::CODE;;kwargs forwarded. If inverse_func is None, then inverse_func
43::CODE;;will be the identity function.
44::CODE;;validate : bool, default=False
45::CODE;;Indicate that the input X array should be checked before calling
46::CODE;;``func``. The possibilities are:
47::CODE;;- If False, there is no input validation.
48::CODE;;- If True, then X will be converted to a 2-dimensional NumPy array or
49::CODE;;sparse matrix. If the conversion is not possible an exception is
50::CODE;;raised.
51::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 0.22
52::CODE;;The default of ``validate`` changed from True to False.
53::CODE;;accept_sparse : bool, default=False
54::CODE;;Indicate that func accepts a sparse matrix as input. If validate is
55::CODE;;False, this has no effect. Otherwise, if accept_sparse is false,
56::CODE;;sparse matrix inputs will cause an exception to be raised.
57::CODE;;check_inverse : bool, default=True
58::CODE;;Whether to check that or ``func`` followed by ``inverse_func`` leads to
59::CODE;;the original inputs. It can be used for a sanity check, raising a
60::CODE;;warning when the condition is not fulfilled.
61::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.20
62::CODE;;feature_names_out : callable, 'one-to-one' or None, default=None
63::CODE;;Determines the list of feature names that will be returned by the
64::CODE;;`get_feature_names_out` method. If it is 'one-to-one', then the output
65::CODE;;feature names will be equal to the input feature names. If it is a
66::CODE;;callable, then it must take two positional arguments: this
67::CODE;;`FunctionTransformer` (`self`) and an array-like of input feature names
68::CODE;;(`input_features`). It must return an array-like of output feature
69::CODE;;names. The `get_feature_names_out` method is only defined if
70::CODE;;`feature_names_out` is not None.
71::CODE;;See ``get_feature_names_out`` for more details.
72::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.1
73::CODE;;kw_args : dict, default=None
74::CODE;;Dictionary of additional keyword arguments to pass to func.
75::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.18

77::CODE;;Dictionary of additional keyword arguments to pass to inverse_func.
78::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.18

88::CODE;;See Also
89::CODE;;--------
90::CODE;;MaxAbsScaler : Scale each feature by its maximum absolute value.
91::CODE;;StandardScaler : Standardize features by removing the mean and

40::CODE;;def _create_expansion(X, interaction_only, deg, n_features, cumulative_size=0):
80::CODE;;Generate a new feature matrix consisting of all polynomial combinations
81::CODE;;of the features with degree less than or equal to the specified degree.
82::CODE;;For example, if an input sample is two dimensional and of the form
83::CODE;;[a, b], the degree-2 polynomial features are [1, a, b, a^2, ab, b^2].
84::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <polynomial_features>`.
85::CODE;;Parameters
86::CODE;;----------
87::CODE;;degree : int or tuple (min_degree, max_degree), default=2
88::CODE;;If a single int is given, it specifies the maximal degree of the
89::CODE;;polynomial features. If a tuple `(min_degree, max_degree)` is passed,
90::CODE;;then `min_degree` is the minimum and `max_degree` is the maximum
91::CODE;;polynomial degree of the generated features. Note that `min_degree=0`
92::CODE;;and `min_degree=1` are equivalent as outputting the degree zero term is
93::CODE;;determined by `include_bias`.
94::CODE;;interaction_only : bool, default=False
95::CODE;;If `True`, only interaction features are produced: features that are
96::CODE;;products of at most `degree` *distinct* input features, i.e. terms with
97::CODE;;power of 2 or higher of the same input feature are excluded:
98::CODE;;- included: `x[0]`, `x[1]`, `x[0] * x[1]`, etc.
99::CODE;;- excluded: `x[0] ** 2`, `x[0] ** 2 * x[1]`, etc.
100::CODE;;include_bias : bool, default=True
101::CODE;;If `True` (default), then include a bias column, the feature in which
102::CODE;;all polynomial powers are zero (i.e. a column of ones - acts as an
103::CODE;;intercept term in a linear model).
104::CODE;;order : {'C', 'F'}, default='C'
105::CODE;;Order of output array in the dense case. `'F'` order is faster to
106::CODE;;compute, but may slow down subsequent estimators.
107::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.21
108::CODE;;Attributes
109::CODE;;----------
110::CODE;;powers_ : ndarray of shape (`n_output_features_`, `n_features_in_`)
111::CODE;;`powers_[i, j]` is the exponent of the jth input in the ith output.
112::CODE;;n_features_in_ : int
113::CODE;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
114::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
115::CODE;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
116::CODE;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
117::CODE;;has feature names that are all strings.
118::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
119::CODE;;n_output_features_ : int
120::CODE;;The total number of polynomial output features. The number of output
121::CODE;;features is computed by iterating over all suitably sized combinations
122::CODE;;of input features.
123::CODE;;See Also
124::CODE;;--------
125::CODE;;SplineTransformer : Transformer that generates univariate B-spline bases
126::CODE;;for features.
127::CODE;;Notes
128::CODE;;-----
129::CODE;;Be aware that the number of features in the output array scales
130::CODE;;polynomially in the number of features of the input array, and
131::CODE;;exponentially in the degree. High degrees can cause overfitting.
132::CODE;;See :ref:`examples/linear_model/plot_polynomial_interpolation.py
133::CODE;;<sphx_glr_auto_examples_linear_model_plot_polynomial_interpolation.py>`
134::CODE;;Examples
135::CODE;;--------
136::CODE;;>>> import numpy as np
137::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.preprocessing import PolynomialFeatures
138::CODE;;>>> X = np.arange(6).reshape(3, 2)
139::CODE;;>>> X
140::CODE;;array([[0, 1],
141::CODE;;[2, 3],
142::CODE;;[4, 5]])
143::CODE;;>>> poly = PolynomialFeatures(2)
144::CODE;;>>> poly.fit_transform(X)
145::CODE;;array([[ 1., 0., 1., 0., 0., 1.],
146::CODE;;[ 1., 2., 3., 4., 6., 9.],
147::CODE;;[ 1., 4., 5., 16., 20., 25.]])
148::CODE;;>>> poly = PolynomialFeatures(interaction_only=True)
149::CODE;;>>> poly.fit_transform(X)
150::CODE;;array([[ 1., 0., 1., 0.],
151::CODE;;[ 1., 2., 3., 6.],
152::CODE;;[ 1., 4., 5., 20.]])
184::CODE;;This should be equivalent to counting the number of terms returned by
185::CODE;;_combinations(...) but much faster.
205::CODE;;check_is_fitted(self)
206::CODE;;combinations = self._combinations(
207::CODE;;n_features=self.n_features_in_,
208::CODE;;min_degree=self._min_degree,
209::CODE;;max_degree=self._max_degree,
210::CODE;;interaction_only=self.interaction_only,
211::CODE;;include_bias=self.include_bias,
212::CODE;;)
213::CODE;;return np.vstack(
214::CODE;;[np.bincount(c, minlength=self.n_features_in_) for c in combinations]

340::CODE;;def transform(self, X):
365::CODE;;check_is_fitted(self)
366::CODE;;xp, _, device_ = get_namespace_and_device(X)
367::CODE;;X = validate_data(
368::CODE;;self,
369::CODE;;X,
370::CODE;;order="F",
371::CODE;;dtype=supported_float_dtypes(xp=xp, device=device_),
372::CODE;;reset=False,
373::CODE;;accept_sparse=("csr", "csc"),
374::CODE;;)
375::CODE;;n_samples, n_features = X.shape
376::CODE;;max_int32 = xp.iinfo(xp.int32).max
377::CODE;;if sparse.issparse(X) and X.format == "csr":
378::CODE;;if self._max_degree > 3:
379::CODE;;return self.transform(X.tocsc()).tocsr()
380::CODE;;to_stack = []
381::CODE;;if self.include_bias:
382::CODE;;to_stack.append(
383::CODE;;sparse.csr_matrix(np.ones(shape=(n_samples, 1), dtype=X.dtype))
384::CODE;;)
385::CODE;;if self._min_degree <= 1 and self._max_degree > 0:
386::CODE;;to_stack.append(X)
387::CODE;;cumulative_size = sum(mat.shape[1] for mat in to_stack)
388::CODE;;for deg in range(max(2, self._min_degree), self._max_degree + 1):
389::CODE;;expanded = _create_expansion(
390::CODE;;X=X,
391::CODE;;interaction_only=self.interaction_only,
392::CODE;;deg=deg,
393::CODE;;n_features=n_features,
394::CODE;;cumulative_size=cumulative_size,
395::CODE;;)
396::CODE;;if expanded is not None:
397::CODE;;to_stack.append(expanded)
398::CODE;;cumulative_size += expanded.shape[1]
399::CODE;;if len(to_stack) == 0:
401::CODE;;XP = sparse.csr_matrix((n_samples, 0), dtype=X.dtype)
402::CODE;;else:
403::CODE;;XP = sparse.hstack(to_stack, dtype=X.dtype, format="csr")
404::CODE;;elif sparse.issparse(X) and X.format == "csc" and self._max_degree < 4:
405::CODE;;return self.transform(X.tocsr()).tocsc()
406::CODE;;elif sparse.issparse(X):
407::CODE;;combinations = self._combinations(
408::CODE;;n_features=n_features,
409::CODE;;min_degree=self._min_degree,
410::CODE;;max_degree=self._max_degree,
411::CODE;;interaction_only=self.interaction_only,
412::CODE;;include_bias=self.include_bias,
413::CODE;;)
414::CODE;;columns = []
415::CODE;;for combi in combinations:
416::CODE;;if combi:
417::CODE;;out_col = 1
418::CODE;;for col_idx in combi:
419::CODE;;out_col = X[:, [col_idx]].multiply(out_col)
420::CODE;;columns.append(out_col)
421::CODE;;else:
422::CODE;;bias = sparse.csc_matrix(np.ones((X.shape[0], 1)))
423::CODE;;columns.append(bias)
424::CODE;;XP = sparse.hstack(columns, dtype=X.dtype).tocsc()
425::CODE;;else:
428::CODE;;order_kwargs = {}
429::CODE;;if _is_numpy_namespace(xp=xp):
430::CODE;;order_kwargs["order"] = self.order
431::CODE;;elif self.order == "F":
432::CODE;;raise ValueError(
433::CODE;;"PolynomialFeatures does not support order='F' for non-numpy arrays"
434::CODE;;)
435::CODE;;XP = xp.empty(
436::CODE;;shape=(n_samples, self._n_out_full),
437::CODE;;dtype=X.dtype,
438::CODE;;device=device_,
439::CODE;;**order_kwargs,
440::CODE;;)
454::CODE;;if self.include_bias:
455::CODE;;XP[:, 0] = 1
456::CODE;;current_col = 1
457::CODE;;else:
458::CODE;;current_col = 0
459::CODE;;if self._max_degree == 0:
460::CODE;;return XP
462::CODE;;XP[:, current_col : current_col + n_features] = X
463::CODE;;index = list(range(current_col, current_col + n_features))
464::CODE;;current_col += n_features
465::CODE;;index.append(current_col)
467::CODE;;for _ in range(2, self._max_degree + 1):
468::CODE;;new_index = []
469::CODE;;end = index[-1]
470::CODE;;for feature_idx in range(n_features):
471::CODE;;start = index[feature_idx]
472::CODE;;new_index.append(current_col)
473::CODE;;if self.interaction_only:
474::CODE;;start += index[feature_idx + 1] - index[feature_idx]
475::CODE;;next_col = current_col + end - start
476::CODE;;if next_col <= current_col:
477::CODE;;break
480::CODE;;if _is_numpy_namespace(xp):
482::CODE;;np.multiply(
483::CODE;;XP[:, start:end],
484::CODE;;X[:, feature_idx : feature_idx + 1],
485::CODE;;out=XP[:, current_col:next_col],
486::CODE;;casting="no",
487::CODE;;)
488::CODE;;else:
489::CODE;;XP[:, current_col:next_col] = xp.multiply(
490::CODE;;XP[:, start:end], X[:, feature_idx : feature_idx + 1]
491::CODE;;)
492::CODE;;current_col = next_col
493::CODE;;new_index.append(current_col)
494::CODE;;index = new_index
495::CODE;;if self._min_degree > 1:
496::CODE;;n_XP, n_Xout = self._n_out_full, self.n_output_features_
497::CODE;;if self.include_bias:
498::CODE;;Xout = xp.empty(
499::CODE;;shape=(n_samples, n_Xout),
500::CODE;;dtype=XP.dtype,
501::CODE;;device=device_,
502::CODE;;**order_kwargs,
503::CODE;;)
504::CODE;;Xout[:, 0] = 1
505::CODE;;Xout[:, 1:] = XP[:, n_XP - n_Xout + 1 :]
506::CODE;;else:
507::CODE;;Xout = xp.asarray(XP[:, n_XP - n_Xout :], copy=True)
508::CODE;;XP = Xout
509::CODE;;return XP

655::CODE;;@staticmethod
656::CODE;;def _get_base_knot_positions(X, n_knots=10, knots="uniform", sample_weight=None):
666::CODE;;if knots == "quantile":
667::CODE;;percentile_ranks = 100 * np.linspace(
668::CODE;;start=0, stop=1, num=n_knots, dtype=np.float64
669::CODE;;)
670::CODE;;if sample_weight is None:
671::CODE;;knots = np.nanpercentile(X, percentile_ranks, axis=0)
672::CODE;;else:
673::CODE;;knots = _weighted_percentile(X, sample_weight, percentile_ranks).T
674::CODE;;else:
679::CODE;;mask = slice(None, None, 1) if sample_weight is None else sample_weight > 0
680::CODE;;x_min = np.zeros(X.shape[1], dtype=np.float64)
681::CODE;;x_max = np.zeros(X.shape[1], dtype=np.float64)
682::CODE;;for feature_idx in range(X.shape[1]):
683::CODE;;x = X[mask, feature_idx]
684::CODE;;if np.all(np.isnan(x)):
685::CODE;;continue
686::CODE;;else:
687::CODE;;x_min[feature_idx] = np.nanmin(x)
688::CODE;;x_max[feature_idx] = np.nanmax(x)
689::CODE;;knots = np.linspace(
690::CODE;;start=x_min,
691::CODE;;stop=x_max,
692::CODE;;num=n_knots,
693::CODE;;endpoint=True,
694::CODE;;dtype=np.float64,
695::CODE;;)
696::CODE;;return knots
697::CODE;;def get_feature_names_out(self, input_features=None):
714::CODE;;check_is_fitted(self, "n_features_in_")
715::CODE;;n_splines = self.bsplines_[0].c.shape[1]
716::CODE;;input_features = _check_feature_names_in(self, input_features)
717::CODE;;feature_names = []
718::CODE;;for i in range(self.n_features_in_):
719::CODE;;for j in range(n_splines - 1 + self.include_bias):
720::CODE;;feature_names.append(f"{input_features[i]}_sp_{j}")

723::CODE;;def fit(self, X, y=None, sample_weight=None):
740::CODE;;try:
741::CODE;;X = validate_data(
742::CODE;;self,
743::CODE;;X,

745::CODE;;accept_sparse=False,

748::CODE;;ensure_all_finite=(self.handle_missing != "zeros"),

752::CODE;;raise ValueError(

754::CODE;;"to error in this case (handle_missing='error'). To avoid this "
755::CODE;;"error, set handle_missing='zeros' to encode missing values as "
756::CODE;;"splines with value 0 or ensure no missing values in X."

758::CODE;;raise e

760::CODE;;sample_weight = _check_sample_weight(sample_weight, X, dtype=X.dtype)

762::CODE;;if isinstance(self.knots, str):
763::CODE;;base_knots = self._get_base_knot_positions(
764::CODE;;X,

767::CODE;;sample_weight=sample_weight,

771::CODE;;if base_knots.shape[0] < 2:
772::CODE;;raise ValueError("Number of knots, knots.shape[0], must be >= 2.")
773::CODE;;elif base_knots.shape[1] != n_features:
774::CODE;;raise ValueError("knots.shape[1] == n_features is violated.")
775::CODE;;elif not np.all(np.diff(base_knots, axis=0) > 0):
776::CODE;;raise ValueError("knots must be sorted without duplicates.")
778::CODE;;n_knots = base_knots.shape[0]
779::CODE;;if self.extrapolation == "periodic" and n_knots <= self.degree:
780::CODE;;raise ValueError(
781::CODE;;"Periodic splines require degree < n_knots. Got n_knots="
782::CODE;;f"{n_knots} and degree={self.degree}."
783::CODE;;)

786::CODE;;n_splines = n_knots + self.degree - 1
787::CODE;;else:
789::CODE;;n_splines = n_knots - 1
790::CODE;;degree = self.degree
791::CODE;;n_out = n_features * n_splines
794::CODE;;if self.extrapolation == "periodic":
798::CODE;;period = base_knots[-1] - base_knots[0]
799::CODE;;knots = np.r_[
800::CODE;;base_knots[-(degree + 1) : -1] - period,
801::CODE;;base_knots,
802::CODE;;base_knots[1 : (degree + 1)] + period,
803::CODE;;]
804::CODE;;else:
817::CODE;;dist_min = base_knots[1] - base_knots[0]
818::CODE;;dist_max = base_knots[-1] - base_knots[-2]
819::CODE;;knots = np.r_[
820::CODE;;np.linspace(
821::CODE;;base_knots[0] - degree * dist_min,
822::CODE;;base_knots[0] - dist_min,
823::CODE;;num=degree,
824::CODE;;),
825::CODE;;base_knots,
826::CODE;;np.linspace(
827::CODE;;base_knots[-1] + dist_max,
828::CODE;;base_knots[-1] + degree * dist_max,
829::CODE;;num=degree,
830::CODE;;),
831::CODE;;]
835::CODE;;coef = np.eye(n_splines, dtype=np.float64)
836::CODE;;if self.extrapolation == "periodic":
837::CODE;;coef = np.concatenate((coef, coef[:degree, :]))
838::CODE;;extrapolate = self.extrapolation in ["periodic", "continue"]
839::CODE;;bsplines = [
840::CODE;;BSpline.construct_fast(
841::CODE;;knots[:, i], coef, self.degree, extrapolate=extrapolate
842::CODE;;)
843::CODE;;for i in range(n_features)

845::CODE;;self.bsplines_ = bsplines
846::CODE;;self.n_features_out_ = n_out - n_features * (1 - self.include_bias)
847::CODE;;return self
848::CODE;;def transform(self, X):
860::CODE;;check_is_fitted(self)
861::CODE;;X = validate_data(
862::CODE;;self,
863::CODE;;X,
864::CODE;;reset=False,
865::CODE;;accept_sparse=False,
866::CODE;;ensure_2d=True,
867::CODE;;ensure_all_finite=(self.handle_missing != "zeros"),
868::CODE;;)

871::CODE;;degree = self.degree
874::CODE;;n_out = self.n_features_out_ + n_features * (1 - self.include_bias)
875::CODE;;if X.dtype in FLOAT_DTYPES:

879::CODE;;if self.sparse_output:
880::CODE;;output_list = []

884::CODE;;spl = self.bsplines_[feature_idx]
886::CODE;;nan_row_indices = np.flatnonzero(_get_mask(X[:, feature_idx], np.nan))
887::CODE;;if self.extrapolation in ("continue", "error", "periodic"):
888::CODE;;if self.extrapolation == "periodic":
893::CODE;;n = spl.t.size - spl.k - 1
894::CODE;;if spl.t[n] - spl.t[spl.k] > 0:
896::CODE;;x = spl.t[spl.k] + (X[:, feature_idx] - spl.t[spl.k]) % (
897::CODE;;spl.t[n] - spl.t[spl.k]
898::CODE;;)

904::CODE;;x = X[:, feature_idx]
905::CODE;;if self.sparse_output:

924::CODE;;elif nan_row_indices.shape[0] > 0:

930::CODE;;x, spl.t, spl.k, self.bsplines_[0].extrapolate
931::CODE;;)

937::CODE;;XBS_sparse = XBS_sparse.tolil()
938::CODE;;XBS_sparse[:, :degree] += XBS_sparse[:, -degree:]
939::CODE;;XBS_sparse = XBS_sparse[:, :-degree]

943::CODE;;else:
944::CODE;;XBS[
945::CODE;;:, (feature_idx * n_splines) : ((feature_idx + 1) * n_splines)

953::CODE;;] = 0

959::CODE;;f_min, f_max = spl(xmin), spl(xmax)

963::CODE;;X[:, feature_idx] <= xmax

985::CODE;;] = spl(X[inside_range_mask, feature_idx])

1001::CODE;;if has_nan_output_values:

1004::CODE;;)
1005::CODE;;elif self.extrapolation == "constant":

312::CODE;;eps = np.finfo(np.float64).eps

890::CODE;;interaction_only, include_bias, csr_container
891::CODE;;):

900::CODE;;if interaction_only:
901::CODE;;return d * i - (i**2 + 3 * i) // 2 - 1 + j
902::CODE;;else:
903::CODE;;return d * i - (i**2 + i) // 2 + j
904::CODE;;n_samples = 13
905::CODE;;n_features = 120001
906::CODE;;data_dtype = np.float32
907::CODE;;data = np.arange(1, 5, dtype=np.int64)
908::CODE;;row = np.array([n_samples - 2, n_samples - 2, n_samples - 1, n_samples - 1])
911::CODE;;col = np.array(
912::CODE;;[n_features - 2, n_features - 1, n_features - 2, n_features - 1], dtype=np.int64
913::CODE;;)
914::CODE;;X = csr_container(
915::CODE;;(data, (row, col)),

160::CODE;;def _sparse_random_matrix(n_components, n_features, density="auto", random_state=None):
205::CODE;;_check_input_size(n_components, n_features)
206::CODE;;density = _check_density(density, n_features)
207::CODE;;rng = check_random_state(random_state)
208::CODE;;if density == 1:
210::CODE;;components = rng.binomial(1, 0.5, (n_components, n_features)) * 2 - 1
211::CODE;;return 1 / np.sqrt(n_components) * components
212::CODE;;else:
214::CODE;;indices = []
215::CODE;;offset = 0
216::CODE;;indptr = [offset]
217::CODE;;for _ in range(n_components):
219::CODE;;n_nonzero_i = rng.binomial(n_features, density)
220::CODE;;indices_i = sample_without_replacement(
221::CODE;;n_features, n_nonzero_i, random_state=rng
222::CODE;;)
223::CODE;;indices.append(indices_i)
224::CODE;;offset += n_nonzero_i
225::CODE;;indptr.append(offset)
226::CODE;;indices = np.concatenate(indices)
228::CODE;;data = rng.binomial(1, 0.5, size=np.size(indices)) * 2 - 1
230::CODE;;components = sp.csr_matrix(
231::CODE;;(data, indices, indptr), shape=(n_components, n_features)
232::CODE;;)
233::CODE;;return np.sqrt(1 / density) / np.sqrt(n_components) * components

467::CODE;;Projected array.
480::CODE;;Sparse random matrix is an alternative to dense random
481::CODE;;projection matrix that guarantees similar embedding quality while being
482::CODE;;much more memory efficient and allowing faster computation of the
483::CODE;;projected data.
484::CODE;;If we note `s = 1 / density` the components of the random matrix are
485::CODE;;drawn from:
486::CODE;;.. code-block:: text
487::CODE;;-sqrt(s) / sqrt(n_components) with probability 1 / 2s
488::CODE;;0 with probability 1 - 1 / s
489::CODE;;+sqrt(s) / sqrt(n_components) with probability 1 / 2s
490::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <sparse_random_matrix>`.
491::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.13
492::CODE;;Parameters
493::CODE;;----------
494::CODE;;n_components : int or 'auto', default='auto'
495::CODE;;Dimensionality of the target projection space.
496::CODE;;n_components can be automatically adjusted according to the
497::CODE;;number of samples in the dataset and the bound given by the
498::CODE;;Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma. In that case the quality of the
499::CODE;;embedding is controlled by the ``eps`` parameter.
500::CODE;;It should be noted that Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma can yield
501::CODE;;very conservative estimated of the required number of components
502::CODE;;as it makes no assumption on the structure of the dataset.
503::CODE;;density : float or 'auto', default='auto'
504::CODE;;Ratio in the range (0, 1] of non-zero component in the random
505::CODE;;projection matrix.
506::CODE;;If density = 'auto', the value is set to the minimum density
507::CODE;;as recommended by Ping Li et al.: 1 / sqrt(n_features).
508::CODE;;Use density = 1 / 3.0 if you want to reproduce the results from
509::CODE;;Achlioptas, 2001.
510::CODE;;eps : float, default=0.1
511::CODE;;Parameter to control the quality of the embedding according to
512::CODE;;the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma when n_components is set to
513::CODE;;'auto'. This value should be strictly positive.
514::CODE;;Smaller values lead to better embedding and higher number of
515::CODE;;dimensions (n_components) in the target projection space.
516::CODE;;dense_output : bool, default=False
517::CODE;;If True, ensure that the output of the random projection is a
518::CODE;;dense numpy array even if the input and random projection matrix
519::CODE;;are both sparse. In practice, if the number of components is
520::CODE;;small the number of zero components in the projected data will
521::CODE;;be very small and it will be more CPU and memory efficient to
522::CODE;;use a dense representation.
523::CODE;;If False, the projected data uses a sparse representation if
524::CODE;;the input is sparse.
525::CODE;;compute_inverse_components : bool, default=False
526::CODE;;Learn the inverse transform by computing the pseudo-inverse of the
527::CODE;;components during fit. Note that the pseudo-inverse is always a dense
528::CODE;;array, even if the training data was sparse. This means that it might be
529::CODE;;necessary to call `inverse_transform` on a small batch of samples at a
530::CODE;;time to avoid exhausting the available memory on the host. Moreover,
531::CODE;;computing the pseudo-inverse does not scale well to large matrices.
532::CODE;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
533::CODE;;Controls the pseudo random number generator used to generate the
534::CODE;;projection matrix at fit time.
535::CODE;;Pass an int for reproducible output across multiple function calls.
536::CODE;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
537::CODE;;Attributes
538::CODE;;----------
539::CODE;;n_components_ : int
540::CODE;;Concrete number of components computed when n_components="auto".
541::CODE;;components_ : sparse matrix of shape (n_components, n_features)
542::CODE;;Random matrix used for the projection. Sparse matrix will be of CSR
543::CODE;;format.
544::CODE;;inverse_components_ : ndarray of shape (n_features, n_components)
545::CODE;;Pseudo-inverse of the components, only computed if
546::CODE;;`compute_inverse_components` is True.
547::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.1
548::CODE;;density_ : float in range 0.0 - 1.0
549::CODE;;Concrete density computed from when density = "auto".
550::CODE;;n_features_in_ : int
551::CODE;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
552::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
553::CODE;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
554::CODE;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
555::CODE;;has feature names that are all strings.
556::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0

241::CODE;;for label in classes:

397::CODE;;Parameters
398::CODE;;----------
399::CODE;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
400::CODE;;Training data, where `n_samples` is the number of samples
401::CODE;;and `n_features` is the number of features.
402::CODE;;y : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
403::CODE;;Target class values with unlabeled points marked as -1.
404::CODE;;All unlabeled samples will be transductively assigned labels
405::CODE;;internally, which are stored in `transduction_`.
406::CODE;;Returns
407::CODE;;-------
408::CODE;;self : object
409::CODE;;Returns the instance itself.
414::CODE;;This model is similar to the basic Label Propagation algorithm,
415::CODE;;but uses affinity matrix based on the normalized graph Laplacian
416::CODE;;and soft clamping across the labels.
417::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <label_propagation>`.
418::CODE;;Parameters
419::CODE;;----------
420::CODE;;kernel : {'knn', 'rbf'} or callable, default='rbf'
421::CODE;;String identifier for kernel function to use or the kernel function
422::CODE;;itself. Only 'rbf' and 'knn' strings are valid inputs. The function
423::CODE;;passed should take two inputs, each of shape (n_samples, n_features),
424::CODE;;and return a (n_samples, n_samples) shaped weight matrix.
425::CODE;;gamma : float, default=20
426::CODE;;Parameter for rbf kernel.
427::CODE;;n_neighbors : int, default=7
428::CODE;;Parameter for knn kernel which is a strictly positive integer.
429::CODE;;alpha : float, default=0.2
430::CODE;;Clamping factor. A value in (0, 1) that specifies the relative amount
431::CODE;;that an instance should adopt the information from its neighbors as
432::CODE;;opposed to its initial label.
433::CODE;;alpha=0 means keeping the initial label information; alpha=1 means
434::CODE;;replacing all initial information.
435::CODE;;max_iter : int, default=30
436::CODE;;Maximum number of iterations allowed.
437::CODE;;tol : float, default=1e-3
438::CODE;;Convergence tolerance: threshold to consider the system at steady
439::CODE;;state.
440::CODE;;n_jobs : int, default=None
441::CODE;;The number of parallel jobs to run.
442::CODE;;``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
443::CODE;;``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
444::CODE;;for more details.
445::CODE;;Attributes
446::CODE;;----------
447::CODE;;X_ : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_features)
448::CODE;;Input array.
449::CODE;;classes_ : ndarray of shape (n_classes,)
450::CODE;;The distinct labels used in classifying instances.
451::CODE;;label_distributions_ : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_classes)
452::CODE;;Categorical distribution for each item.
453::CODE;;transduction_ : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
454::CODE;;Label assigned to each item during :term:`fit`.
455::CODE;;n_features_in_ : int
456::CODE;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
457::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
458::CODE;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
459::CODE;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
460::CODE;;has feature names that are all strings.
461::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
462::CODE;;n_iter_ : int
463::CODE;;Number of iterations run.
464::CODE;;See Also
465::CODE;;--------
466::CODE;;LabelPropagation : Unregularized graph based semi-supervised learning.
467::CODE;;References
468::CODE;;----------
469::CODE;;`Dengyong Zhou, Olivier Bousquet, Thomas Navin Lal, Jason Weston,
470::CODE;;Bernhard Schoelkopf. Learning with local and global consistency (2004)
471::CODE;;<https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/doc_view/pid/d74c37aabf2d5cae663007cbd8718175466aea8c>`_

480::CODE;;>>> random_unlabeled_points = rng.rand(len(iris.target)) < 0.3
481::CODE;;>>> labels = np.copy(iris.target)
482::CODE;;>>> labels[random_unlabeled_points] = -1
483::CODE;;>>> label_prop_model.fit(iris.data, labels)

25::CODE;;class SelfTrainingClassifier(ClassifierMixin, MetaEstimatorMixin, BaseEstimator):
120::CODE;;_parameter_constraints: dict = {
123::CODE;;"estimator": [HasMethods(["fit"])],
124::CODE;;"threshold": [Interval(Real, 0.0, 1.0, closed="left")],
125::CODE;;"criterion": [StrOptions({"threshold", "k_best"})],
126::CODE;;"k_best": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
127::CODE;;"max_iter": [Interval(Integral, 0, None, closed="left"), None],
128::CODE;;"verbose": ["verbose"],
129::CODE;;}
130::CODE;;def __init__(
131::CODE;;self,
132::CODE;;estimator=None,
133::CODE;;threshold=0.75,
134::CODE;;criterion="threshold",
135::CODE;;k_best=10,
136::CODE;;max_iter=10,
137::CODE;;verbose=False,
138::CODE;;):
139::CODE;;self.estimator = estimator
140::CODE;;self.threshold = threshold
141::CODE;;self.criterion = criterion
142::CODE;;self.k_best = k_best
143::CODE;;self.max_iter = max_iter
144::CODE;;self.verbose = verbose
145::CODE;;def _get_estimator(self):
152::CODE;;return clone(self.estimator)
153::CODE;;@_fit_context(
155::CODE;;prefer_skip_nested_validation=False
156::CODE;;)
157::CODE;;def fit(self, X, y, **params):
180::CODE;;_raise_for_params(params, self, "fit")
181::CODE;;self.estimator_ = self._get_estimator()
184::CODE;;X, y = validate_data(
185::CODE;;self,
186::CODE;;X,
187::CODE;;y,
188::CODE;;accept_sparse=["csr", "csc", "lil", "dok"],
189::CODE;;ensure_all_finite=False,
190::CODE;;)
191::CODE;;if y.dtype.kind in ["U", "S"]:
192::CODE;;raise ValueError(
193::CODE;;"y has dtype string. If you wish to predict on "
194::CODE;;"string targets, use dtype object, and use -1"
195::CODE;;" as the label for unlabeled samples."
196::CODE;;)
197::CODE;;has_label = y != -1
198::CODE;;if np.all(has_label):
199::CODE;;warnings.warn("y contains no unlabeled samples", UserWarning)
200::CODE;;if self.criterion == "k_best" and (
201::CODE;;self.k_best > X.shape[0] - np.sum(has_label)
202::CODE;;):
203::CODE;;warnings.warn(
204::CODE;;(
205::CODE;;"k_best is larger than the amount of unlabeled "
206::CODE;;"samples. All unlabeled samples will be labeled in "
207::CODE;;"the first iteration"
208::CODE;;),
209::CODE;;UserWarning,
210::CODE;;)
211::CODE;;if _routing_enabled():
212::CODE;;routed_params = process_routing(self, "fit", **params)
213::CODE;;else:
214::CODE;;routed_params = Bunch(estimator=Bunch(fit={}))
215::CODE;;self.transduction_ = np.copy(y)
216::CODE;;self.labeled_iter_ = np.full_like(y, -1)
217::CODE;;self.labeled_iter_[has_label] = 0
218::CODE;;self.n_iter_ = 0
219::CODE;;while not np.all(has_label) and (
220::CODE;;self.max_iter is None or self.n_iter_ < self.max_iter
221::CODE;;):
222::CODE;;self.n_iter_ += 1
223::CODE;;self.estimator_.fit(
224::CODE;;X[safe_mask(X, has_label)],
225::CODE;;self.transduction_[has_label],
226::CODE;;**routed_params.estimator.fit,
227::CODE;;)
229::CODE;;prob = self.estimator_.predict_proba(X[safe_mask(X, ~has_label)])
230::CODE;;pred = self.estimator_.classes_[np.argmax(prob, axis=1)]
231::CODE;;max_proba = np.max(prob, axis=1)
233::CODE;;if self.criterion == "threshold":
234::CODE;;selected = max_proba > self.threshold
235::CODE;;else:
236::CODE;;n_to_select = min(self.k_best, max_proba.shape[0])
237::CODE;;if n_to_select == max_proba.shape[0]:
238::CODE;;selected = np.ones_like(max_proba, dtype=bool)
239::CODE;;else:
241::CODE;;selected = np.argpartition(-max_proba, n_to_select)[:n_to_select]
243::CODE;;selected_full = np.nonzero(~has_label)[0][selected]
245::CODE;;self.transduction_[selected_full] = pred[selected]
246::CODE;;has_label[selected_full] = True
247::CODE;;self.labeled_iter_[selected_full] = self.n_iter_
248::CODE;;if selected_full.shape[0] == 0:
250::CODE;;self.termination_condition_ = "no_change"
251::CODE;;break
252::CODE;;if self.verbose:
253::CODE;;print(
254::CODE;;f"End of iteration {self.n_iter_},"
255::CODE;;f" added {selected_full.shape[0]} new labels."
256::CODE;;)
257::CODE;;if self.n_iter_ == self.max_iter:
258::CODE;;self.termination_condition_ = "max_iter"
259::CODE;;if np.all(has_label):
260::CODE;;self.termination_condition_ = "all_labeled"
261::CODE;;self.estimator_.fit(
262::CODE;;X[safe_mask(X, has_label)],
263::CODE;;self.transduction_[has_label],
264::CODE;;**routed_params.estimator.fit,
265::CODE;;)
266::CODE;;self.classes_ = self.estimator_.classes_
267::CODE;;return self

296::CODE;;self,

299::CODE;;ensure_all_finite=False,
300::CODE;;reset=False,
301::CODE;;)

604::CODE;;class BaseSVC(ClassifierMixin, BaseLibSVM, metaclass=ABCMeta):
666::CODE;;Parameters
667::CODE;;----------
668::CODE;;X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
669::CODE;;The input samples.
670::CODE;;Returns
671::CODE;;-------
672::CODE;;X : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_classes * (n_classes-1) / 2)
673::CODE;;Returns the decision function of the sample for each class
674::CODE;;in the model.
675::CODE;;If decision_function_shape='ovr', the shape is (n_samples,
676::CODE;;n_classes).
677::CODE;;Notes
678::CODE;;-----
679::CODE;;If decision_function_shape='ovo', the function values are proportional
680::CODE;;to the distance of the samples X to the separating hyperplane. If the
681::CODE;;exact distances are required, divide the function values by the norm of
682::CODE;;the weight vector (``coef_``). See also `this question
683::CODE;;<https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/14876/
684::CODE;;interpreting-distance-from-hyperplane-in-svm>`_ for further details.
685::CODE;;If decision_function_shape='ovr', the decision function is a monotonic
686::CODE;;transformation of ovo decision function.
694::CODE;;For a one-class model, +1 or -1 is returned.
695::CODE;;Parameters
696::CODE;;----------
697::CODE;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features) or \
698::CODE;;(n_samples_test, n_samples_train)
699::CODE;;For kernel="precomputed", the expected shape of X is
700::CODE;;(n_samples_test, n_samples_train).
701::CODE;;Returns
702::CODE;;-------
703::CODE;;y_pred : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
704::CODE;;Class labels for samples in X.
735::CODE;;The model needs to have probability information computed at training
736::CODE;;time: fit with attribute `probability` set to True.
737::CODE;;Parameters
738::CODE;;----------
739::CODE;;X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
740::CODE;;For kernel="precomputed", the expected shape of X is
741::CODE;;(n_samples_test, n_samples_train).
742::CODE;;Returns
743::CODE;;-------
744::CODE;;T : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_classes)
745::CODE;;Returns the probability of the sample for each class in
746::CODE;;the model. The columns correspond to the classes in sorted
747::CODE;;order, as they appear in the attribute :term:`classes_`.
748::CODE;;Notes
749::CODE;;-----
750::CODE;;The probability model is created using cross validation, so
751::CODE;;the results can be slightly different than those obtained by
752::CODE;;predict. Also, it will produce meaningless results on very small
753::CODE;;datasets.
767::CODE;;The model need to have probability information computed at training
768::CODE;;time: fit with attribute `probability` set to True.
769::CODE;;Parameters
770::CODE;;----------
771::CODE;;X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features) or \
772::CODE;;(n_samples_test, n_samples_train)
773::CODE;;For kernel="precomputed", the expected shape of X is
774::CODE;;(n_samples_test, n_samples_train).
775::CODE;;Returns
776::CODE;;-------
777::CODE;;T : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_classes)
778::CODE;;Returns the log-probabilities of the sample for each class in
779::CODE;;the model. The columns correspond to the classes in sorted
780::CODE;;order, as they appear in the attribute :term:`classes_`.
781::CODE;;Notes
782::CODE;;-----
783::CODE;;The probability model is created using cross validation, so
784::CODE;;the results can be slightly different than those obtained by
785::CODE;;predict. Also, it will produce meaningless results on very small
786::CODE;;datasets.
860::CODE;;Returns
861::CODE;;-------
862::CODE;;ndarray of shape (n_classes * (n_classes - 1) / 2)
868::CODE;;Returns
869::CODE;;-------
870::CODE;;ndarray of shape (n_classes * (n_classes - 1) / 2)
879::CODE;;This number depends on the values of the following attributes:
880::CODE;;- multi_class
881::CODE;;- penalty
882::CODE;;- loss
883::CODE;;- dual
884::CODE;;The same number is also internally used by LibLinear to determine
885::CODE;;which solver to use.
947::CODE;;Preprocessing is done in this function before supplying it to liblinear.
948::CODE;;Parameters
949::CODE;;----------
950::CODE;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
951::CODE;;Training vector, where `n_samples` is the number of samples and
952::CODE;;`n_features` is the number of features.
953::CODE;;y : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
954::CODE;;Target vector relative to X
955::CODE;;C : float
956::CODE;;Inverse of cross-validation parameter. The lower the C, the higher
957::CODE;;the penalization.
958::CODE;;fit_intercept : bool
959::CODE;;Whether or not to fit an intercept. If set to True, the feature vector
960::CODE;;is extended to include an intercept term: ``[x_1, ..., x_n, 1]``, where
961::CODE;;1 corresponds to the intercept. If set to False, no intercept will be
962::CODE;;used in calculations (i.e. data is expected to be already centered).
963::CODE;;intercept_scaling : float
964::CODE;;Liblinear internally penalizes the intercept, treating it like any
965::CODE;;other term in the feature vector. To reduce the impact of the
966::CODE;;regularization on the intercept, the `intercept_scaling` parameter can
967::CODE;;be set to a value greater than 1; the higher the value of
968::CODE;;`intercept_scaling`, the lower the impact of regularization on it.
969::CODE;;Then, the weights become `[w_x_1, ..., w_x_n,
970::CODE;;w_intercept*intercept_scaling]`, where `w_x_1, ..., w_x_n` represent
971::CODE;;the feature weights and the intercept weight is scaled by
972::CODE;;`intercept_scaling`. This scaling allows the intercept term to have a
973::CODE;;different regularization behavior compared to the other features.
974::CODE;;class_weight : dict or 'balanced', default=None
975::CODE;;Weights associated with classes in the form ``{class_label: weight}``.
976::CODE;;If not given, all classes are supposed to have weight one. For
977::CODE;;multi-output problems, a list of dicts can be provided in the same
978::CODE;;order as the columns of y.
979::CODE;;The "balanced" mode uses the values of y to automatically adjust
980::CODE;;weights inversely proportional to class frequencies in the input data
981::CODE;;as ``n_samples / (n_classes * np.bincount(y))``
982::CODE;;penalty : {'l1', 'l2'}
983::CODE;;The norm of the penalty used in regularization.
984::CODE;;dual : bool
985::CODE;;Dual or primal formulation,
986::CODE;;verbose : int
987::CODE;;Set verbose to any positive number for verbosity.
988::CODE;;max_iter : int
989::CODE;;Number of iterations.
990::CODE;;tol : float
991::CODE;;Stopping condition.
992::CODE;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
993::CODE;;Controls the pseudo random number generation for shuffling the data.
994::CODE;;Pass an int for reproducible output across multiple function calls.
995::CODE;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
996::CODE;;multi_class : {'ovr', 'crammer_singer'}, default='ovr'
997::CODE;;`ovr` trains n_classes one-vs-rest classifiers, while `crammer_singer`
998::CODE;;optimizes a joint objective over all classes.
999::CODE;;While `crammer_singer` is interesting from a theoretical perspective
1000::CODE;;as it is consistent it is seldom used in practice and rarely leads to
1001::CODE;;better accuracy and is more expensive to compute.
1002::CODE;;If `crammer_singer` is chosen, the options loss, penalty and dual will
1003::CODE;;be ignored.
1004::CODE;;loss : {'logistic_regression', 'hinge', 'squared_hinge', \
1005::CODE;;'epsilon_insensitive', 'squared_epsilon_insensitive}, \
1006::CODE;;default='logistic_regression'
1007::CODE;;The loss function used to fit the model.
1008::CODE;;epsilon : float, default=0.1
1009::CODE;;Epsilon parameter in the epsilon-insensitive loss function. Note
1010::CODE;;that the value of this parameter depends on the scale of the target
1011::CODE;;variable y. If unsure, set epsilon=0.
1012::CODE;;sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
1013::CODE;;Weights assigned to each sample.
1014::CODE;;Returns
1015::CODE;;-------
1016::CODE;;coef_ : ndarray of shape (n_features, n_features + 1)
1017::CODE;;The coefficient vector got by minimizing the objective function.
1018::CODE;;intercept_ : float
1019::CODE;;The intercept term added to the vector.
1020::CODE;;n_iter_ : array of int
1021::CODE;;Number of iterations run across for each class.
22::CODE;;The lower bound for `C` is computed such that for `C` in `(l1_min_C, infinity)`
23::CODE;;the model is guaranteed not to be empty. This applies to l1 penalized
24::CODE;;classifiers, such as :class:`sklearn.svm.LinearSVC` with penalty='l1' and
25::CODE;;:class:`sklearn.linear_model.LogisticRegression` with penalty='l1'.
26::CODE;;This value is valid if `class_weight` parameter in `fit()` is not set.
27::CODE;;For an example of how to use this function, see
28::CODE;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_linear_model_plot_logistic_path.py`.

30::CODE;;----------
31::CODE;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
32::CODE;;Training vector, where `n_samples` is the number of samples and
33::CODE;;`n_features` is the number of features.
34::CODE;;y : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
35::CODE;;Target vector relative to X.
36::CODE;;loss : {'squared_hinge', 'log'}, default='squared_hinge'
37::CODE;;Specifies the loss function.
38::CODE;;With 'squared_hinge' it is the squared hinge loss (a.k.a. L2 loss).
39::CODE;;With 'log' it is the loss of logistic regression models.
40::CODE;;fit_intercept : bool, default=True
41::CODE;;Specifies if the intercept should be fitted by the model.
42::CODE;;It must match the fit() method parameter.
43::CODE;;intercept_scaling : float, default=1.0
44::CODE;;When fit_intercept is True, instance vector x becomes
45::CODE;;[x, intercept_scaling],
46::CODE;;i.e. a "synthetic" feature with constant value equals to
47::CODE;;intercept_scaling is appended to the instance vector.
48::CODE;;It must match the fit() method parameter.
49::CODE;;Returns
50::CODE;;-------
51::CODE;;l1_min_c : float
52::CODE;;Minimum value for C.

39::CODE;;Similar to SVC with parameter kernel='linear', but implemented in terms of
40::CODE;;liblinear rather than libsvm, so it has more flexibility in the choice of
41::CODE;;penalties and loss functions and should scale better to large numbers of
42::CODE;;samples.
43::CODE;;The main differences between :class:`~sklearn.svm.LinearSVC` and
44::CODE;;:class:`~sklearn.svm.SVC` lie in the loss function used by default, and in
45::CODE;;the handling of intercept regularization between those two implementations.
46::CODE;;This class supports both dense and sparse input and the multiclass support
47::CODE;;is handled according to a one-vs-the-rest scheme.
48::CODE;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <svm_classification>`.
49::CODE;;Parameters
50::CODE;;----------
51::CODE;;penalty : {'l1', 'l2'}, default='l2'
52::CODE;;Specifies the norm used in the penalization. The 'l2'
53::CODE;;penalty is the standard used in SVC. The 'l1' leads to ``coef_``
54::CODE;;vectors that are sparse.
55::CODE;;loss : {'hinge', 'squared_hinge'}, default='squared_hinge'
56::CODE;;Specifies the loss function. 'hinge' is the standard SVM loss
57::CODE;;(used e.g. by the SVC class) while 'squared_hinge' is the
58::CODE;;square of the hinge loss. The combination of ``penalty='l1'``
59::CODE;;and ``loss='hinge'`` is not supported.
60::CODE;;dual : "auto" or bool, default="auto"
61::CODE;;Select the algorithm to either solve the dual or primal
62::CODE;;optimization problem. Prefer dual=False when n_samples > n_features.
63::CODE;;`dual="auto"` will choose the value of the parameter automatically,
64::CODE;;based on the values of `n_samples`, `n_features`, `loss`, `multi_class`
65::CODE;;and `penalty`. If `n_samples` < `n_features` and optimizer supports
66::CODE;;chosen `loss`, `multi_class` and `penalty`, then dual will be set to True,
67::CODE;;otherwise it will be set to False.
68::CODE;;.. versionchanged:: 1.3
69::CODE;;The `"auto"` option is added in version 1.3 and will be the default
70::CODE;;in version 1.5.
71::CODE;;tol : float, default=1e-4
72::CODE;;Tolerance for stopping criteria.
73::CODE;;C : float, default=1.0
74::CODE;;Regularization parameter. The strength of the regularization is
75::CODE;;inversely proportional to C. Must be strictly positive.
76::CODE;;For an intuitive visualization of the effects of scaling
77::CODE;;the regularization parameter C, see
78::CODE;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_svm_plot_svm_scale_c.py`.
79::CODE;;multi_class : {'ovr', 'crammer_singer'}, default='ovr'
80::CODE;;Determines the multi-class strategy if `y` contains more than
81::CODE;;two classes.
82::CODE;;``"ovr"`` trains n_classes one-vs-rest classifiers, while
83::CODE;;``"crammer_singer"`` optimizes a joint objective over all classes.
84::CODE;;While `crammer_singer` is interesting from a theoretical perspective
85::CODE;;as it is consistent, it is seldom used in practice as it rarely leads
86::CODE;;to better accuracy and is more expensive to compute.
87::CODE;;If ``"crammer_singer"`` is chosen, the options loss, penalty and dual
88::CODE;;will be ignored.
89::CODE;;fit_intercept : bool, default=True
90::CODE;;Whether or not to fit an intercept. If set to True, the feature vector
91::CODE;;is extended to include an intercept term: `[x_1, ..., x_n, 1]`, where
92::CODE;;1 corresponds to the intercept. If set to False, no intercept will be
93::CODE;;used in calculations (i.e. data is expected to be already centered).
94::CODE;;intercept_scaling : float, default=1.0
95::CODE;;When `fit_intercept` is True, the instance vector x becomes ``[x_1,
96::CODE;;..., x_n, intercept_scaling]``, i.e. a "synthetic" feature with a
97::CODE;;constant value equal to `intercept_scaling` is appended to the instance
98::CODE;;vector. The intercept becomes intercept_scaling * synthetic feature
99::CODE;;weight. Note that liblinear internally penalizes the intercept,
100::CODE;;treating it like any other term in the feature vector. To reduce the
101::CODE;;impact of the regularization on the intercept, the `intercept_scaling`
102::CODE;;parameter can be set to a value greater than 1; the higher the value of
103::CODE;;`intercept_scaling`, the lower the impact of regularization on it.
104::CODE;;Then, the weights become `[w_x_1, ..., w_x_n,
105::CODE;;w_intercept*intercept_scaling]`, where `w_x_1, ..., w_x_n` represent
106::CODE;;the feature weights and the intercept weight is scaled by
107::CODE;;`intercept_scaling`. This scaling allows the intercept term to have a
108::CODE;;different regularization behavior compared to the other features.
109::CODE;;class_weight : dict or 'balanced', default=None
110::CODE;;Set the parameter C of class i to ``class_weight[i]*C`` for
111::CODE;;SVC. If not given, all classes are supposed to have
112::CODE;;weight one.
113::CODE;;The "balanced" mode uses the values of y to automatically adjust
114::CODE;;weights inversely proportional to class frequencies in the input data
115::CODE;;as ``n_samples / (n_classes * np.bincount(y))``.
116::CODE;;verbose : int, default=0
117::CODE;;Enable verbose output. Note that this setting takes advantage of a
118::CODE;;per-process runtime setting in liblinear that, if enabled, may not work
119::CODE;;properly in a multithreaded context.
120::CODE;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
121::CODE;;Controls the pseudo random number generation for shuffling the data for
122::CODE;;the dual coordinate descent (if ``dual=True``). When ``dual=False`` the
123::CODE;;underlying implementation of :class:`LinearSVC` is not random and
124::CODE;;``random_state`` has no effect on the results.
125::CODE;;Pass an int for reproducible output across multiple function calls.
126::CODE;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
127::CODE;;max_iter : int, default=1000
128::CODE;;The maximum number of iterations to be run.
129::CODE;;Attributes
130::CODE;;----------
131::CODE;;coef_ : ndarray of shape (1, n_features) if n_classes == 2 \
132::CODE;;else (n_classes, n_features)
133::CODE;;Weights assigned to the features (coefficients in the primal
134::CODE;;problem).
135::CODE;;``coef_`` is a readonly property derived from ``raw_coef_`` that
136::CODE;;follows the internal memory layout of liblinear.
137::CODE;;intercept_ : ndarray of shape (1,) if n_classes == 2 else (n_classes,)
138::CODE;;Constants in decision function.
139::CODE;;classes_ : ndarray of shape (n_classes,)
140::CODE;;The unique classes labels.
141::CODE;;n_features_in_ : int
142::CODE;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
143::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
144::CODE;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
145::CODE;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
146::CODE;;has feature names that are all strings.
147::CODE;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
148::CODE;;n_iter_ : int
149::CODE;;Maximum number of iterations run across all classes.
150::CODE;;See Also
151::CODE;;--------
152::CODE;;SVC : Implementation of Support Vector Machine classifier using libsvm:
153::CODE;;the kernel can be non-linear but its SMO algorithm does not
154::CODE;;scale to large number of samples as LinearSVC does.
155::CODE;;Furthermore SVC multi-class mode is implemented using one
156::CODE;;vs one scheme while LinearSVC uses one vs the rest. It is
157::CODE;;possible to implement one vs the rest with SVC by using the
158::CODE;;:class:`~sklearn.multiclass.OneVsRestClassifier` wrapper.
159::CODE;;Finally SVC can fit dense data without memory copy if the input
160::CODE;;is C-contiguous. Sparse data will still incur memory copy though.
161::CODE;;sklearn.linear_model.SGDClassifier : SGDClassifier can optimize the same
162::CODE;;cost function as LinearSVC
163::CODE;;by adjusting the penalty and loss parameters. In addition it requires
164::CODE;;less memory, allows incremental (online) learning, and implements
165::CODE;;various loss functions and regularization regimes.
166::CODE;;Notes
167::CODE;;-----
168::CODE;;The underlying C implementation uses a random number generator to
169::CODE;;select features when fitting the model. It is thus not uncommon
170::CODE;;to have slightly different results for the same input data. If
171::CODE;;that happens, try with a smaller ``tol`` parameter.
172::CODE;;The underlying implementation, liblinear, uses a sparse internal
173::CODE;;representation for the data that will incur a memory copy.
174::CODE;;Predict output may not match that of standalone liblinear in certain
175::CODE;;cases. See :ref:`differences from liblinear <liblinear_differences>`
176::CODE;;in the narrative documentation.
177::CODE;;References
178::CODE;;----------
179::CODE;;`LIBLINEAR: A Library for Large Linear Classification
180::CODE;;<https://www.csie.ntu.edu.tw/~cjlin/liblinear/>`__
181::CODE;;Examples
182::CODE;;--------
183::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.svm import LinearSVC
184::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
185::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
186::CODE;;>>> from sklearn.datasets import make_classification
187::CODE;;>>> X, y = make_classification(n_features=4, random_state=0)

193::CODE;;>>> print(clf.named_steps['linearsvc'].coef_)
194::CODE;;[[0.141 0.526 0.679 0.493]]
195::CODE;;>>> print(clf.named_steps['linearsvc'].intercept_)
196::CODE;;[0.1693]
